For individual pious persons are bound to promote the edification of the Church. But as for the fact that the Corinthians said, I am of Paul, I of Apollo, I of Cephas, he undoubtedly looked to this, that everyone chose for himself a sort of individual author and Master of a sect: Which Christ most severely prohibited. Do not be called Masters: For one is your Master, Christ: All the Apostles and Prophets received doctrine from Christ: And certain commands. When everyone chooses for himself a peculiar Master of a sect, not only are dissensions and distractions generated, but also new dogmas are fashioned, and men depart from Christ the only mediator. Therefore, the names of sects ought to be most alien from the Church: And individual believers ought to profess the Christian name: The huge multitude of diverse monastic orders fights diametrically with the command of Christ and the rebuke of the Apostle, and it is a great argument that Monks have departed from the doctrine of Christ and the Apostles.

Latin:

Significatum enim est mihi de vobis, per eos qui sunt ex familia Chloe, quòd contentiones inter vos sint: Dico autem hac de re, quòd quisque vestrum dicit, Ego sum Pauli, Ego sum Apollo, Ego sum Caephae: Ego sum Christi.

Exponit Paulus occasionem, & causam, cur tanta diligentia hortetur Ecclesiam Corinthiorum ad concordiam: Quia intellexerit in ea esse dissidia & factiones: Ac ne suspicentur Paulum ex incertis rumoribus hoc habere, scribit unde hoc cognoverit, nimirum ex familia Chloae. Sanctum enim officium praestitit familia Chloae, quòd hoc vulnus Ecclesiae indicavit Apostolo, ut tempestivum adhiberetur remedium. Singuli enim pii obstricti sunt ad promovendam Ecclesiae aedificationem. Quòd verò Corinthii dixerunt, Ego sum Pauli, Ego Apollo, Ego Caephae, Haud dubiè eò spectavit, quòd quilibet sibi elegit singularem quasi sectae authorem & Magistrum: Quod Christus severissimè prohibuit. Nolite vocari Magistri: Unus est enim Magister vester Christus: Apostoli & Prophetae omnes à Christo acceperunt doctrinam: Et certa mandata. Cum quilibet sibi peculiarem eligit sectae Magistrum, non tantum dissidia & distractiones generantur, sed etiam nova dogmata finguntur, & discedunt homines à Christo unico mediatore. Sectarum igitur appellationes ab Ecclesia debent esse alienissimae: Et singuli fideles Christianum nomen profiteri debent: Ingens multitudo diversorum ordinum monasticorum ex diametro pugnat cum mandato Christi & repraehensione Apostoli & Argumentum magnum est quòd Monachi discesserint à doctrina Christi & Apostolorum.

## 1:13-15
Is Christ divided in you?

The first argument by which he proves that schisms are not to be made: As Christ is one, one head of the Church, Messiah, King and pontiff, who cannot be divided: So it is necessary that the Church be one and undivided, which is the only bride and body of one Christ. But those who are eager for diverse sects do nothing else than tear the members of the body of Christ from one another, and then as it were cut Christ himself into parts. It is therefore a wicked and greatest crime to foster discords in the Church, and to be eager for factions. The Holy Spirit warns that it is not enough if we embrace one or another particle of the Christian religion: But that it must be embraced whole and entire: Because Christ cannot be divided. He also teaches that there ought to be the highest unity in the Church: For the reason that we are members of one body, we have one head: we are led by one Spirit: we have been initiated by one Baptism: we all feed on one bread: one faith may shine in us: And we may be sustained by one hope of eternal life. Let sectarians attend in this place to how great a crime they commit when they rend the Church, that they undoubtedly attempt to divide Christ himself and to lacerate his body: Just as did Marcion, Manes, Valentinus, Arrius, Eutyches: And in our time Schwenckfeldius, Servetus, Zwinglius, Osiander, Micron, the new Manichaeans, and infinite others: Who gave their effort rather to join disciples and followers to themselves than to Christ.

Was Paul crucified for you?

The second argument from the efficient cause of redemption: We ought to profess his name, and

We are obligated to him alone, who liberated us from the power of Satan by his own blood: and who is the foundation and cause of our entire religion: but Jesus Christ alone was crucified for us and by his own blood merited for us righteousness and life: Neither Paul, nor Peter, nor any Apostle or Prophet was crucified for your sins and for your redemption: Therefore we ought to profess the name of Jesus Christ alone, and be obligated to him alone, not to Paul, not to Peter, not to a Prophet, nor to an Apostle. Here Paul shows what a grave crime men commit when, inflated with ambition and pride, they strive to attach disciples to themselves rather than to Christ, or beget new dogmas, or stir up unnecessary dissensions: because, forsooth, they attempt to transfer to themselves, with the greatest wickedness, the entire benefit and merit of Jesus Christ, who poured out his blood for us, and was made a curse for us on the cross. He also rebukes those who, while they too much esteem and admire their own teachers, slip into such a state that they plainly forget Jesus Christ who was crucified for them, inasmuch as they tenaciously defend that which they have drawn from their own teachers: nor can they be moved from it even if they hear the contrary demonstrated by clear testimonies of Jesus Christ. But most evidently here the Apostle Paul refutes the blasphemous error of the papists: who imagine that even the Apostles and martyrs have shed their blood for the Church: And they teach that by the merit and passion of the saints the wrath of God is appeased, and our sins are expiated: And therefore that one must trust in them: But Paul constantly denies that either he, Paul, or any Apostle was crucified for the Church; But only Jesus Christ: Who also says in the Prophet, I alone have trodden the winepress: And there is no one with me: Iesai: 62. Item: I, even I, blot out your sins and your transgressions, and that for my own name's sake. Iesa: 43.

Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

The third argument by which he proves that factions have no place in the Church, is taken from the covenant of Baptism: We ought to profess the name of him, to adhere to him, and to acknowledge and follow him alone as master, in whose name we have been baptized: But we have been baptized in the name of no Apostle or Prophet: but only in the name of Jesus Christ: Therefore we ought not to profess the name of Paul or Peter, nor hold them as authors of a sect. This is also a most weighty argument: inasmuch as it reminds Christians to whom they gave their faith in Baptism, what kind of covenant they have entered into with Christ. By the merit, righteousness, obedience, passion, and death of Jesus Christ alone we have been redeemed from the wrath of God, liberated from the curse of the law, and snatched from the power of Satan, of sin, and of death. Also, by the resurrection and efficacy of Christ alone are we transferred into the kingdom of light, of justice, and of life: he alone reconciled us to the Father: he alone merited for us eternal joy and salvation: he alone is the one who obtains the Holy Spirit from the Father, and pours him out upon all believers: he alone is the perpetual guardian and defender of the Church, who is present with it everywhere, protects it, nourishes it, governs it, consoles it, and saves it: For Jesus Christ alone, God and man, was appointed by the Father as mediator and savior. Therefore, he alone enters into a covenant with us in Baptism, that he wishes to be our defender and savior, and binds himself to us: but in turn we ourselves give our faith, and bind ourselves, that we wish to place all our trust in him, and to adhere to him alone. Therefore, he who is eager for factions, and chooses for himself other masters or teachers besides Christ, he breaks the holy covenant of Baptism.

This passage is to be observed with singular diligence and attention: For Paul teaches what is the force and meaning of the words of Baptism: Going, Baptize in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit: that they surely contain the whole of religion in themselves. I baptize you in the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. That is, the same eternal and true God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, who is the author of Baptism, and is present in this action, in this washing he receives you, the baptized, into grace, washes and remits to you all your sins on account of the death of the mediator Jesus Christ, pronounces you righteous, regenerates and sanctifies you by the Holy Spirit poured out into you, adopts you as a son and establishes you as an heir of eternal life and of all eternal goods: all of which he seals for you by this very action as a pledge: now this God, who is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, strikes a covenant with you, that he wills to be your God, to nourish, cherish, govern you, to deliver you from death and the power of Satan: and you in turn bind yourself, that you will acknowledge, invoke, celebrate this God alone who is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, worship him with all obedience, place all trust in him, and believe his entire word. Paul teaches that this power is in these words of Baptism, when he says, Were you baptized in the name of Paul? For he shows that the authority of no Apostle nor creature is so great that Christians ought to be baptized in his name. For the name signifies the acknowledgment, command, religion, invocation, trust, worship, obligation, and celebration of the true God. And in Baptism he teaches that such goods are offered, promised, and distributed to us as cannot be given by a creature, namely, the remission of sins, justification, the gift of the Holy Spirit, vivification, divine protection, nourishment, deliverance from death and Satan, and defense. in all dangers, guidance, and the inheritance of eternal life. Neither an Apostle nor an Angel can bestow these such great spiritual and indeed bodily goods upon the Church: Therefore we cannot be baptized in the name of any Apostle. And from this Apostolic interpretation it is now manifest that the divinity of the Son and of the Holy Spirit is most powerfully demonstrated from the words of Baptism: For because Christ commands that we be baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit: And it is not right that we be baptized in the name of a creature: but equal honor of divinity is deferred to the Son and to the Holy Spirit: both of whom in Baptism remit sins for us, grant righteousness and life, free us from death and Satan, and bestow the inheritance of eternal life: it is necessary that both the Son and the Holy Spirit be of the same divinity as the eternal Father. The Apostle also warns that this faith is required in a pious teacher of the Church, that he may join all hearers to Christ, and strive for the honor of Christ alone, and amplify his kingdom. It is characteristic of all sectarians that they do not seek the propagation of the kingdom of Christ so much as the amplitude of their own honor and the authority of their name: And so they are entirely occupied with this, that by whatever arts and new dogmas they can, they may attract hearers to themselves and excite admiration for themselves: but they slander faithful and sincere teachers, so that they alone may stand out; Samosatenus did this with great zeal, Marcion, Manes, Arius, Nestorius, Pelagius, Osiander, Calvin, Beza: Who are entirely in this, that they might be suspected by their own, and might stand out in the world by the celebrity of their name. But Paul teaches that there ought to be another mind and zeal in a faithful minister, namely that he should not seek his own glory or reputation; but that of Jesus Christ: and that he should not render his hearers addicted to himself but to Christ. For He acquired the Church for Himself with His own blood: thus John, when his disciples admired him too much, and held him for the Messiah, sends them away to Christ, and adds: You yourselves are my witnesses that I said I am not the Christ: He who has the bride is the bridegroom, but the friend of the bridegroom hears his voice and rejoices greatly because of the voice of the bridegroom.

I give thanks to God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius, lest anyone should say that I baptized in my own name: I baptized also the household of Stephanas, besides I do not know whether I baptized any other.

Because the false apostles boasted in this, that they had baptized many disciples, and they abused the ministry of Baptism, so that they might join disciples to themselves, Paul boasts against himself and the Church that he baptized few, so that the occasion might be taken away from the Corinthians of boasting in the name of Paul, or of placing any trust in Paul. It is so dangerous when men admire the heralds of the word and the dispensers of the sacraments, and do not distinguish between our Lord Jesus Christ, who purchased salvation for us with his blood, and who is effective in the ministry through the Holy Spirit, and the ministers, who cannot bestow or effect salvation: whence John the Baptist says: I baptize with water: but after me comes he who is before me, he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire: so that Paul congratulates himself that he did not baptize many. Let there be mention of Crispus the ruler of the synagogue Acts 18. Let there be mention of Gaius of Derbe, a companion of Paul Acts 19 and 20 and Romans 16 where Paul names him his host.

For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the Gospel.

Paul here shows what was the principal part of his ministry: He says not to baptize men, which could also be dispatched by other ministers of the Church who were not equal to Paul in gifts: But to announce the Gospel and to expound the mysteries of the divine word. The command of baptizing men was indeed enjoined upon the individual Apostles and Paul: Go, says Christ, Baptize all men: Nor are the administration of the sacraments and the preaching of the Gospel to be torn apart: For the sacraments are the sealing of the promise: But the most important account must be held of the preaching and exposition of the word: For without the preaching of the word the sacraments would be empty spectacles, which would lack all fruit. And it is of much greater industry and labor to teach the people about God and the benefits of the mediator, than to administer the sacraments. Since therefore there are many ministers in the Church, and one cannot perform all things: And Paul is adorned by God with a singular gift of instructing the Church and illuminating the holy scripture, he indicates that he was sent by God not so much to Baptize, as to preach: Not that he esteems the administration of Baptism as vile or of small moment: But because that part of the ministry is both more necessary and of greater work.

Not in wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ be made empty: For the word of the cross is to those who are perishing foolishness: but to us who are being saved, it is the power of God. For it is written I will destroy the wisdom of the wise: And I will abolish the intelligence of the prudent: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe?

Latin:

Divisus ne est in vobis Christus?

Primum argumentum quo probat non esse facienda schismata: Ut unus est Christus, unum Ecclesiae caput, Messias, Rex & pontifex, qui dividi non potest: Ita necesse est unam & indivisam esse Ecclesiam, quae est unius Christi unica sponsa, & corpus. At qui diversis sectis student nihil aliud agunt, quàm ut corporis Christi membra divellant a se invicem, tùm ut ipsum Christum quasi in partes secent. Est ergò scelus nefarium & maximum discordias fovere in Ecclesia, & factionibus studere. Monet Spiritus sanctus non satis esse si unam & alteram particulam religionis Christianae amplectamur: Sed totam & integram amplectendam esse: Quia Christus dividi non potest. Docet etiam summam oportere esse unitatem in Ecclesia: Eò quòd unius corporis simus membra, unum habeamus caput: uno ducamur Spiritu: uno simus initiati Baptismo: uno pane omnes vescamur: una fides in nobis luceat: Et una spe vitae aeternae sustentemur. Attendant hoc loco sectarii quantum scelus committant cum scindunt Ecclesiam, quòd nimirum ipsum Christum conentur dividere & eius lacerare corpus: Quemadmodum fecerunt, Marcion, Manes, Valentinus, Arrius, Eutyches: Et nostro tempore Schwenckfeldius, Servetus, Zwinglius, Osiander, Micron, Novi Manichaei, & infiniti alii: Qui hoc potius dederunt operam ut sibi adiungerent discipulos & sectatores quàm Christo.

Num Paulus pro vobis est crucifixus:

Secundum argumentum à causa efficiente redemptionis: Eius nomen profiteri debemus, &

illi soli obligati sumus, qui suo sanguine nos à potestate Satanae liberavit: & qui universae nostrae religionis est fundamentum & causa: sed solus Iesus Christus pro nobis est crucifixus & suo sanguine meruit nobis iustitiam et vitam: Nec Paulus, nec Petrus, nec ullus Apostolus vel Propheta pro vestris peccatis & in vestram redemptionem est crucifixus: Ergò solius Iesu Christi nomen profiteri debemus, et illi soli obligati esse, non Paulo, non Petro, non Prophetae, neque Apostolo. Hîc ostendit Paulus quam grave crimen committant homines cum inflati ambitione & superbia discipulos sibi magis quàm Christo adiungere student, aut gignunt nova dogmata, aut movent non necessaria dissidia: quòd nimirum totum beneficium & meritum Iesu Christi, qui suum sanguinem pro nobis effudit, & factus est maledictum pro nobis in cruce, in se cum summo scelere transferre conentur. Repraehendit etiam eos, qui dum suos praeceptores nimium suspiciunt & admirantur, eò delabuntur, ut Iesu Christi qui pro ipsis crucifixus est planè obliviscantur, siquidem id mordicus defendunt, quod à suis hauserunt praeceptoribus: neque ab eo dimoveri possunt etiam si perspicuis testimoniis Iesu Christi contrarium demonstari audiant. Evidentissimè autem refellit hic Apostolus Paulus blasphemum errorem pontificiorum: qui fingunt etiam Apostolos & martyres sanguinem suum pro Ecclesia effudisse: Ac docent merito & passioné sanctorum esse placatam iram Dei, & expiata nostra peccata: Ideoque iis fidendum esse: Paulus verò constanter negat vel se Paulum, vel ullum Apostolum esse crucifixum pro Ecclesia; Sed solum Iesum Christum: Qui & in Propheta inquit, ego solus calcavi torcular: Et nemo est mecum: Iesai: 62. Item: Ego ego deleo peccata tua & transgressiones tuas, idque propter nomen meum. Iesa: 43.

Aut in nomen Pauli Baptizati estis?

Tertium argumentum quo probat factiones in Ecclesia non habere locum, sumptum à faedere Baptismi: Eius nomen profiteri, illi adhaerere, eumque solum magistrum agnoscere & sequi debemus, in cuius nomine Baptizati sumus: Sed in nullius Apostoli vel Prophetae nomine Baptizati sumus: sed tantum in nomine Iesu Christi: Ergò neque Pauli neque Petri nomen profiteri, aut eos veluti sectae authores habere debemus. Gravissimum etiam hoc est argumentum: siquidem monet Christianos, cui fidem in Baptismo dederunt, quale faedus cum Christo iniverint. Solius Iesu Christi merito, institia, obedientia, passione, & morte redempti sumus ab ira Dei, liberati à maledictione legis, & erepti ex potestate Satanae, peccati, et mortis. Solius etiam Christi resurrectione, & efficacia transferimur in regnum lucis, iustitiae & vitae: solus ille placavit nos patri: solus meruit nobis aeternam laeticiam & salutem: solus est qui impetrat à patre Spiritum sanctum, & effundit illum in omnes credentes: solus est perpetuus Ecclesiae custos et defensor, qui ubique ei adest, eam tuetur, nutrit, gubernat, consolatur, & salvat: Solus enim Iesus Christus Deus & homo constitutus est à patre mediator et salvator. Itaque solus ille init nobiscum foedus in Baptismo, quod noster velit esse defensor & salvator, & sese obligat nobis: vicissim autem nos ipsi fidem damus, & obstringimus, quòd omnem fiduciam in ipsum collocare, & ipsi soli adhaerere velimus. Qui ergò factionibus studet, & alios sibi eligit magistros, vel praeceptores praeter Christum, is frangit sanctum Baptismi foedus.

Singulari diligentia & attentione observandus est hic locus: Docet enim Paulus quae sit vis & significatio verborum Baptismi: Euntes Baptizate in nomine patris, & filii & Spiritus sancti: quòd nimirum universam religionem in se contineant. Baptiso te in nomine patris, filii, & Spiritus sancti. Id est, Ipse aeternus et verus Deus pater, filius & Spiritus sanctus, qui est author Baptismi, & praesens est in hac actione, hoc lavacro te Baptizatum recipit in gratiam, abluit & remittit tibi omnia tua peccata propter mortem mediatoris Iesu Christi, pronunciat te iustum, regenerat & sanctificat te effuso in te Spiritu sancto, adoptat te in filium & statuit te haeredem vitae aeternae & omnium aeternorum bonorum: quae omnia hac ipsa actione tanquam pignore tibi obsignat: ferit iàm te cum foedus hic Deus qui est pater, filius & Spiritus sanctus, quòd velit esse Deus tuus, te nutrire, fovere, gubernare, te liberare ex morte & potentia Satanae: & tu vicissim obligas te, quòd hunc solum Deum qui est pater, filius & Spiritus sanctus velis agnoscere, invocare, celebrare, omni obedientia ipsum colere, omnem fiduciam in ipsum collocare, & universo eius verbo credere. Hanc vim in esse his verbis Baptismi docet Paulus, cum inquit, An in nomine Pauli Baptizati estis? Ostendit enim nullius Apostoli neque creaturae tantam esse authoritatem, ut in eius nomine Christiani Baptizari debeant. Nomen enim significat agnitionem, mandatum, religionem, invocationem, fiduciam, cultum, obligationem, celebrationem veri Dei. Et in Baptismo docet offerri, promitti ac distribui nobis talia bona, quae à creatura donari non possint, vide licet remissionem peccatorum, iustificationem, donationem Spiritus sancti, vivificationem, divinam protectionem, nutricationem, liberationem à morte & Satana, desensionem in omnibus periculis, gubernationem, & haereditatem vitae aeternae. Haec tanta bona spiritualia nimirum & corporalia non potest nec Apostolus nec Angelus largiri Ecclesiae: Idcirco in nullius Apostoli nomen Baptizari possumus. Atque ex hac Apostolica interpretatione iam manifestum est, ex verbis Baptismi validissimè demonstrari divinitatem Filii & Spiritus sancti: Quia enim iubet Christus ut Baptizemur in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti: Et fas non sit Baptizari nos in nomine creaturae: aequalis verò honor divinitatis defertur filio & Spiritui sancto: qui uterque nobis in Baptismo remittit peccata, donat iustitiam & vitam, liberat à morte & Satana, & largitur haereditatem vitae aeternae: necesse est, & filium & Spiritum sanctum eiusdem esse divinitatis cum aeterno patre. Monet etiam Apostolus hanc fidem in pio doctore Ecclesiae requiri, ut omnes auditores adiungat Christo, & solius Christi honori studeat, & eius regnum amplificet. Proprium hoc est omnium sectariorum ut non tàm quaerant propagationem regni Christi, quàm sui honoris amplitudinem, & nominis authoritatem: Itaque in hoc toti sunt, ut quibuscunque artibus, & novis dogmatibus possunt ad se alliciant auditores & sui admirationem excitent: fideles verò & synceros doctores calumniantur, ut ipsi soli emineant; Hoc magno studio egerunt Samosatenus, Martion, Manes, Arrius, Nestorius, Pelagius, Osiander, Calvinus, Baeza: Qui in hoc toti sunt ut à suis suspiciantur, & in mundo emineant nominis celebritate. Paulus verò docet aliam oportere mentem & studium esse in fideli ministro, nimirum ut non suam gloriam vel existimationem quaerat; sed Iesu Christi: utque non sibi sed Christo reddat addictos auditores. Is enim suo sanguine sibi acquisivit Ecclesiam: sic Iohannes cum discipuli eum nimium admirarentur, & pro Messia haberent ablegat eos ad Christum, & addit: Vos testes mei estis quòd dixerim non sum Christus: Qui sponsam habet hic sponsus est, amicus autem sponsi audit vocem eius & vehementer laetatur ob vocem sponsi.

Gratias ago Deo quòd neminem vestrum Baptizavi nisi Crispum & Caium, ne quis dicat quòd in meum nomen Baptizavi: Baptizavi autem & Stephanae familiam, Praeterea non scio num ullum alium Baptizaverim.

Quia pseudoapostoli in hoc gloriabantur, quòd multos discipulos Baptizassent, & abutebantur ministerio Baptismi, ut sibi adiungerent discipulos, Paulus contra sibi & Ecclesiae gloriatur quòd paucos Baptizavit, ut Corinthiis sit erepta occasio de nomine Pauli gloriandi, aut in Paulum ullam fiduciam collocandi. Adeo periculosum est cum homines nimirum admirantur verbi praecones & sacramentorum dispensatores, & non distinguunt inter dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, qui sanguine suo nobis comparavit salutem, & qui per Spiritum sanctum est efficax in ministerio & inter ministros, qui non possunt largiri vel efficere salutem: unde Iohannes Baptista inquit: Ego Baptizo aqua: sed post me venit qui prior me est, is vos Baptizabit Spiritu & igne: ut Paulus sibi gratuletur quòd non Baptizaverit multos. Crispi Archisynagogi sit mentio act: 18. Caii Derbei comitis Pauli sit mentio act: 19. & 20: & Roma: 16. ubi Paulus nominat eum hospitem suum.

Non enim misit me Christus ad Baptizandum, sed ad Evangelizandum.

Paulus hic ostendit quae fuerit praecipua pars sui ministerii: Inquit non Baptizare homines, quod etiam per alios Ecclesiae ministros qui donis Paulo non erant pares, expediri poterat: Sed annunciare Evangelion & exponere mysteria verbi divini. Mandatum Baptizandi homines fuit sanè iniunctum singulis Apostolis & Paulo: Euntes inquit Christus, Baptizate omnes homines: Nec divellenda sunt administratio sacramentorum & praedicatio Evangelii: Nam sacramenta sunt obsignatio promissionis: Potissima autem ratio haberi debet praedicationis, & expositionis verbi: Nam sine praedicatione verbi sacramenta essent inania spectacula, quae omni fructu carerent. Ac multò maioris industriae, & laboris est docere populum de Deo & de beneficiis mediatoris, quàm administrare sacramenta. Cum ergò plures sint in Ecclesia ministri, nec unus omnia praestare possit: Et Paulus singulari dono erudiendi Ecclesiam, & illustrandi sacram scripturam sit ornatus à Deo, indicat se non tàm ad Baptizandum, quàm ad praedicandum à Deo missum esse: Non quòd vilem vel exigui momenti aestimet Baptismi administrationem: Sed quod illa pars ministerii & magis necessaria, & maioris sit operae.

Non in sapientia sermonis, ne inanis reddatur crux Christi: Sermo enim crucis his qui pereunt stultitia est: nobis verò qui salvamur, potentia Dei est. Scriptum est enim perdam sapientiam sapientum: Et intelligentiam prudentum abolebo: Ubi sapiens: Ubi scriba?

## 1:20
Where is the disputer of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?

The root and source of all dissensions and contentions in the Church, and of horrible errors and impieties in the world, is the self-confidence and pride of human wit. For however much reason may be blind in divine matters, yet it arrogates to itself the understanding of spiritual things, and takes upon itself judgment. The human mind does not acknowledge its own sad darkness, nor does it feel its own infirmity, but trusts that it will investigate by the sharpness of its own wit who and what kind of being God is, and what His will is toward us. Therefore it wanders in its thoughts, and fashions various things, both idols and religions, and is wonderfully pleased with its own inventions and figments. It defends these tenaciously and attempts to force them upon everyone; individual men also labor under pride, and exalt themselves by their own gifts. Hence, therefore, it is necessary that contentions exist in the Church, and horrendous impieties in the world. Therefore, so that Paul may pluck out this poisonous root of dissensions, he leads the Church to the acknowledgment of its own weakness and the densest darkness by which the human mind is oppressed, and he shows how huge the difference is between human wisdom and the Gospel of the cross, and he warns that God is opposed to human wisdom, which exalts itself against the word. To Adam after the fall into sin, certain small sparks of human reason remained in man: By which man could discern between the honorable and the base, understand discipline, and in some way govern this life. The knowledge that there is a God remained in man; conscience remained, either excusing him in deeds rightly done, or accusing him in crimes: But that spiritual light, which shows the true God and His divine will toward us, was utterly extinguished in the first fall.

For man was dead in sins, and is only darkness and flesh. And so it is impossible for man by his own powers to acknowledge the true God: Rather, he carves foul idols for himself with his own thoughts: As the Greeks fashioned Jupiter, Mars, Pallas, Priapus: The Egyptians worshipped garlic, cats, crocodiles: The Romans cultivated fever, Paleness, Victory, and similar portents: But just as human reason cannot find the true God, so it can in no way understand and investigate His will toward us, and especially His counsel concerning the redemption of the human race and the gathering of the Church. Therefore, while human reason wanders in its own errors and figments, and devises various religions: The nations repeatedly devise new divinities: Heretics invent new dogmas: Samosatenus feigns that λόγον in John signifies a purpose in the Father: Marcion devises two different divinities: Arius denies the divinity of Christ: Nestorius attacks the personal union of the two natures in Christ: Mahomet invents a religion pleasing to the flesh, removes from the midst articles conflicting with reason, grants a multitude of wives: and for the sake of the Jews retains circumcision: And in sum the whole world horribly plays with opinions about God and His will: by which it inflicts extreme insult upon the true God, and attacks His word. Rightly therefore is it judged an enemy of God: just as Paul testifies: the mind of the flesh, says Paul, is enmity against God: Ro. 8. Concerning this misery and darkness of the human mind this Paul preaches: he admonishes the Church of its weakness, so that it may utterly extinguish the plague of pride; and he teaches that the doctrine of the Gospel concerning the cross of Jesus Christ is most diverse from all human wisdom. Reason itself and human wisdom is indeed a notable gift of God: If it could contain itself within its own limits, and only govern earthly things which it understands, such as economy and politics: But because it exceeds its own limits, and wishes to dominate in spiritual matters which it is entirely ignorant of; it becomes an enemy of God, and with all its strength opposes itself to God.

For God wishes to be acknowledged just as He reveals Himself. But human wisdom wishes to carve divinities for itself: God binds us to the word: And He wishes mercy, faith, worship, and all obedience to be governed by a certain word, but human wisdom attempts to worship God outside the word according to its own judgment; God judges that the cross and afflictions are profitable to the Church: And He is delighted by this kind of exercise of the pious; But human wisdom utterly abhors and detests every misery and cross. God demands that we hang entirely upon Him, and trust in Him alone, but human wisdom attempts to consult for itself, and seeks human protections, and means which it understands, upon which it hangs entirely. God requires a confession of the truth, and wishes it to be valued more than all the comforts of this life: But human wisdom commands that peace, possessions, spouse, children, and life be preferred before religion, and God. God wishes His Church to be ruled by the express word: And the ministry to be dispensed according to His own command without respect of persons: But human wisdom also wishes the Church to obey its own commands and counsels: And the ministry of the word and sacraments to be accommodated to the judgment of the powerful and the governors. In sum, in all spiritual matters or affairs, human wisdom is utterly opposed to the will of God which He has revealed in the word. Hence it is that there are no more bitter enemies of the Church and the word than the wise of this world: And in turn God resists with all His might the wise of this world: Christ says, I thank thee O heavenly Father, that thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent of this world: And you have revealed them to little ones, and in this place from Isaiah ch. 29. Paul cites the divine threat against the wise of this world: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise: And the intelligence of the prudent: Doubtless because they oppose themselves to God and His most wise word. By this grave condemnation of human wisdom he calls the Corinthians away from the admiration of it, and leads them to the word of the cross of Christ: He says therefore, Christ sent me to preach the Gospel not in wisdom of speech: that is, not in the persuasive words of human wisdom: Not that I might show off singular wisdom in speech, just as the false apostles do.

Lest the cross of Christ be made void: Human reason admires flourishing fortune, seeks glory in the world, and with great zeal pursues great wealth, luxurious days, and the favor of men: And it proclaims this to be the highest happiness: By which false judgment it condemns the Cross of Jesus Christ, who was the most despised of all in the world, and was made a curse for us, to extreme foolishness. Truly therefore he makes void the cross of Jesus Christ, through which salvation was brought to the world, whoever conforms himself to human wisdom, and thus destroys the entire doctrine of Christ, while he transforms it into Philosophy and the inventions of reason. And he who strives for this, that on account of wisdom and eloquence he may be in admiration among the world: He completely enervates the doctrine concerning the cross of Christ: because by his example he teaches that the cross is rather to be cast away and fled from, than to be taken up according to the precept of Christ. And he who abominates the cross, how can he believe that salvation has been procured for us through the cross, and that the eternal Father truly loved the Son hanging on the cross and raised him up: For the word of the cross is foolishness, says Paul, to those who are perishing: This is, the world not only abhors all hardships and especially the cross, so foul a kind of death: but also judges it to be extreme foolishness to bring upon oneself such great calamities for the sake of religion and confession, and to undergo so shameful a kind of punishment: to strive in vain (he says) and by fatiguing oneself to seek nothing but hatred, is of extreme madness. He also considers it most foolishly believed that by the punishment of one most miserable and most calamitous man, who was condemned by the judgment of the wise, and was numbered with wicked thieves, justice and salvation were procured for the world: and that in such a miserable man fixed to the cross as a blasphemer and seditious person, all confidence is to be placed: he thinks that a judgment of this kind differs nothing from extreme madness. But Paul says that those who are perishing and are destined for eternal damnation, hold such a judgment concerning the cross of Christ: which is not surprising: because they are not ruled by the light of the word, and the guidance of the Holy Spirit.

But to us who are being saved it is the power of God: We, he says, who have a certain hope of salvation, called We are through the Gospel and illuminated by the Holy Spirit: the word of the cross is the power of God. For from the Gospel concerning the cross of Christ we understand that through Christ the power of sin and death is broken, and the whole kingdom of Satan is destroyed: From the Gospel we learn that God is effective in us through the Holy Spirit, to renew in us the image of God, to restore the lost light, righteousness, life, and eternal joy: Which could be effected by the power of no man or creature: And through Christ crucified we acknowledge the infinite power of God, by which He both can and wills to succor us in all dangers, to snatch us from every necessity, to bestow all good things, and to provide more and greater things than we are able either to ask or to understand. Nor indeed do we learn the infinite power of God in Jesus Christ only from the word of God: but we also experience it, if indeed through the word of the cross itself God is effective, He draws us back from the jaws of death and hell, regenerates us through the Holy Spirit, and constitutes us heirs of eternal life. While meanwhile those who despise the word of the cross, neither understand nor believe the power of God: And in whatever calamity, deserted by all creatures, they rush into desperation and destruction. For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise. The Apostle Paul proves that the word of the cross yields foolishness and destruction to those who are perishing: Because God has threatened that He will destroy the wise and prudent of this age; What therefore [will they do] with their counsels they accomplished or gained by things so prudently and acutely devised, except that they provoked the wrath of God against themselves, and precipitated themselves into eternal destruction. An example is Pharaoh, who with his counselors devised various frauds by which he might oppress the people of Israel: But he at last perished most miserably with his own in the sea. Sennacherib boasted of his own wisdom: And at last he is slaughtered by his own sons in the temple of his idol. In Aurelian, Decius, Diocletian, there was great wisdom and singular talent: But this very wisdom destroyed them. For the reason that they thought the dignity and power of the Roman Empire could not be restored unless they first blotted out the Christian name. While therefore they wage war against Christ, they plunge themselves into extreme calamities and eternal destruction.

And all histories testify that wise men for the most part meet with most sad fates. The cause is that the excellent gift of wisdom, which they ought to contribute to the glory of God and the edification of the Church, they for the most part convert to the contumely of God and the oppression of the Church and the truth. How sad was the end of Achitophel, whose wisdom is celebrated even by the testimony of scripture? Likewise, the wisdom of Socrates, Themistocles, Palamedes, Pericles, Demades, Demosthenes, Hyperides, Cicero, Theramenes, and Cato, and of very many others is highly praised in history: But all these perished most miserably, and most of them plunged themselves into tragic calamities by their own counsels. Therefore, the history of the whole world testifies that God destroys the wisdom of the wise.

Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer? From another chapter, indeed 33. Iesa, he cites these words: But in the same sense: For the Prophet, having a discourse concerning the admirable state of the Church, says that it will come to pass that the pious will exclaim with astonishment: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? As if they were saying: There are not many wise men, there are not many learned men in our assembly: And yet we are the people of God and are miraculously defended by God. It would be impossible for worldly kingdoms to consist and be able to be defended without wise and learned men. But the Church of God both consists and is propagated and is defended even without wise counselors.

Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? By those things through which one sins, by the same is one also punished. The wise especially harm the glory of God while they fashion idols and false religions with their own wits and attack the doctrine of the Gospel with their own counsels: Therefore God makes them foolish, and delivers them into a reprobate mind. Ahithophel is so insane that he cuts off his life with a noose. Nebuchadnezzar, exalting himself too much in wisdom, is turned into madness. Nor are those endowed with a sounder mind who spurn the benefits of the mediator, pursue the doctrine of the Gospel with insults, and attack the Church. For thus to themselves they block the way to eternal life and all happiness. Therefore, let all wise men see to it that they learn to fear the Lord and submit themselves to His word, and let them not despise the cross of Jesus Christ.

Latin:

Ubi disputator huius seculi? Nonne infatuavit Deus sapientiam mundi huius?

Radix & scaturigo omnium dissidiorum & contentionum in Ecclesia, & horribilium errorum et impietatum in mundo, est humani ingenii considentia, & superbia. Quantumvis enim caecutiat ratio in rebus divinis: Tamen arrogat sibi spiritualium rerum intelligentiam, & sumit sibi iudicium. Non agnoscit mens humana suam tristem caliginem: Nec sentit suam infirmitatem: Sed confidit se proprio ingenii acumine investigaturam quis & qualis sit Deus, & quae eius sit erga nos voluntas. Vagatur igitur cogitationibus, & varia fingit cùm Idola, tùm religiones: Et mirè sibi placet in suis inventis & figmentis. Ea mordicus tuetur & omnibus obtrudere conatur: Singuli etiam homines superbia laborant, & efferunt sese donis suis. Hinc ergò necesse est existere contentiones in Ecclesia, & horrendas impietates in mundo. Ut igitur Paulus hanc venenatam dissidiorum radicem evellat, deducit Ecclesiam ad agnitionem propriae imbecillitatis, & densissimae caliginis, qua oppressa est mens humana: Et ostendit quàm ingens sit discrimen inter humanam sapientiam, & Evangelion crucis: Et monet Deum adversari humanae sapientiae, quae se contra verbum effert. Adamo lapso in peccatum igniculi quidam humanae rationis manserunt in homine: Quibus potuit homo discernere inter honestum & turpe, disciplinam intelligere, & hanc vitam aliquomodo regere. Mansit in homine noticia quòd sit Deus; Mansit conscientia sese vel excusans in rectè factis: Vel arguens in sceleribus: At lux ista spiritualis, quae monstrat verum Deum eiusque divinam erga nos voluntatem, prorsus est extincta in primo lapsu.

Homo enim in peccatis fuit mortuus, & tantum est tenebrae, & caro. Itaque impossibile est homini propriis viribus agnoscere verum Deum: Quin tetra idola sibi sculpit suis cogitationibus: Ut Graeci Iovem, Martem, Palladem, Priapum finxerunt: Aegyptii allium, feles, Crocodilos adorarunt: Romani febrem, Pallorem, Victoriam, & similia portenta coluerunt: Ut autem humana ratio verum Deum invenire non potest, ita nec voluntatem eius erga nos & inprimis consilium eius de redemptione generis humani, & de colligenda Ecclesia intelligere & pervestigare nullo modo potest. Dum ergò suis erroribus & figmentis vagatur humana ratio, & varias excogitat religiones: Gentes subinde excogitant nova numina: Haeretica singunt nova dogmata: Samosatenus fingit λόγον in Ioanne significare propositum in patre: Marcion excogitat duo diversa numina: Arrius negat divinitatem Christi: Nestorius oppugnat personalem unionem duarum naturarum in Christo: Mahometh fingit religionem carni gratam, articulos pugnantes cum ratione aufert è medio, concedit uxorum multitudinem: & in gratiam Iudaeorum retinet circumcisionem: Et in summa totus mundus horribiliter ludit opinionibus de Deo & eius voluntate: quibus verum Deum extrema contumelia adficit, & eius verbum oppugnat. Iure igitur censetur hostis Dei: quemadmodum Paulus testatur: sensus carnis, inquit Paulus, est immicitia adversus Deum: Ro. 8. De hac miseria & caligine humanae mentis concionatur hic Paulus: admonet Ecclesiam suae infirmitatis, ut pestem superbiae prorsus extinguat; ac docet diversissimam esse doctrinam Evangelii de cruce Iesu Christi, à tota sapientia humana. Est quidem ratio ipsa et humana sapientia insigne Dei donum: Si se intra suos limites continere posset, & tantum terrena regeret quae intelligit, ut Oeconomiam & politiam: Quia verò excedit suos limites, & in spiritualibus quae prorsus ignorat vult dominari; Fit hostis Dei, & totis viribus sese Deo opponit.

Deus enim vult agnosci sicut se patefacite Sed humana sapientia vult sibi sculpere numina: Deus alligat nos ad verbum: Et misericordiam, fidem, cultum, & omnem obedientiam vult regi certo verbo, sed humana sapientîa conatur colere Deum extra verbum pro suo arbitratu; Deus crucem & adflictiones iudicat conducere Ecclesiae: Et huiusmodi exercitio piorum delectatur; Sed humana sapientia prorsus ab omni miseria & cruce abhorret & eam detestatur. Deus postulat ut ab ipso toti pendeamus, & ipsi soli fidamus, sed humana sapientia sibi ipsa consulere conatur, & quaerit humana praesidia, & media quae intelligit, à quibus tota pendet. Deus confessionem requirit veritatis, eamque pluris vult fieri quàm omnia commoda huius vitae: Sed humana sapientia iubet pacem, facultates, coniugem, liberos, vitam anteferri religioni, & Deo. Deus Ecclesiam suam vult regi expresso verbo: Et ministerium iuxta ipsius mandatum sine respectu personarum dispensari: Sed humana sapientia suis mandatis & consiliis quoque vult parere Ecclesiam: Et ministerium verbi & sacramentorum accommodari ad potentum & gubernatorum arbitrium. In summa in omnibus rebus aut negociis spiritualibus prorsus adversatur humana sapientia Dei voluntati quam in verbo patefecit. Hinc est quòd nulli sint acerbiores hostes Ecclesiae & verbi, quàm sapientes huius mundi: Et vicissim Deus totis viribus resistit huius mundi sapientibus: Christus inquit, Gratias tibi ago pater coelestis, quòd haec abscondisti à sapientibus & prudentibus huius mundi: Et revelasti ea parvulis, & hoc loco ex Iesa; cap: 29. Citat Paulus comminationem divinam contra sapientes huius mundi: Perdam sapientiam sapientum: Et intelligentiam prudentum: Nimirum quia sese Deo & eius sapientissimo verbo opponunt. Hac gravi condemnatione humanae sapientiae avocat Corinthios ab admiratione eius, & ad verbum crucis Christi deducit: Dicit igitur, Christus me misit ad Evangelizandum non in sapientia sermonis: hoc est, non in persuasoriis humanae sapientiae verbis: Non ut ostentarem singularem sapientiam in sermone, quemadmodum pseudoapostoli faciunt.

Ne inanis reddatur crux Christi: Humana ratio florentem fortunam admiratur, gloriam in mundo expetit, magnas opes, lautos dies, & hominum favorem magno studio quaerit: Et hanc summam praedicat foelicitatem: Quo falso iudicio Crucem Iesu Christi, qui fuit omnium despectissimus in mundo, & factus est maledictum pro nobis, extremae stultitiae condemnat. Verè igitur inanem reddit Iesu Christi crucem, per quam parta est mundo salus, quisquis humanae sapientiae sese conformat, atque ita delet universam Christi doctrinam, dum eam in Philosophiam & rationis commenta transformat. Ac qui hoc studet ut propter sapientiam & eloquentiam sit in admirationê apud mundum: Is enervat prorsus doctrinam de cruce Christi: quia exemplo suo docet abiiciendani potius & fugiendam esse crucem, quàm iuxta Christi praeceptum tollendam. Et qui crucem abominatur, quomodo is credere potest quòd nobis per crucem parta sit salus, et quòd pater aeternus in cruce pendentem filium verè dilexerit eumque resuscitaverit: Sermo enim crucis stultitia est, inquit Paulus, his qui pereunt: Hoc est, mundus non tantum abhorret omnes aerumnas et inprimis crucem tàm foedum genus mortis: verum etiam iudicat extremam esse stultitiam propter religionem & confessionem tantas sibi accersere calamitates, & tàm probrosum genus supplicii subire: frustra niti (inquit) & sese fatigando nihil nisi odium quaerere, extremae dementiae est. Stultissimè etiam credi ex stimat, quòd unius miserrimi & calamitosissimi hominis supplicio, qui sapientum iudicio condemnatus, & sceleratis latronibus annumeratus fuit, mundo parta sit iustitia & salus: & quòd in tàm miserum hominem cruci adfixum tanquam blasphemum, & seditiosum, omnis fiducia sit collocanda: huiusmodi sententiam nihil ab extrema dementia differre putat. Sed Paulus inquit eos qui pereunt & ad aeternam damnationem destinati sunt, tale ferre iudicium de cruce Christi: quod mirum non est: quia luce verbi, & Spiritus sancti ductu non reguntur.

Nobis vero qui salvamur est potentia Dei: Nos, inquit, qui certam salutis spem habemus, vocati sumus per Evangelium & illuminati per Spiritum sanctum: sermo crucis est potentia Dei. Ex Evangelio enim de cruce Christi intelligimus quòd per Christum frangatur potentia peccati & mortis, & destruatur totum regnum Satanae: Ex Evangelio discimus Deum in nobis efficacem esse per Spiritum sanctum, renovare in nobis imaginem Dei, restituere amissam lucem, iusticiam, vitam & laeticiam aeternam: Quae nullius hominis vel creaturae vi effici poterant: Ac per Christum crucifixum agnoscimus infinitam Dei potentiam, qua nobis in omnibus periculis succurrere, ex omni necessitate eripere, omnia bona largiri, & plura atque maiora praestare & possit & velit, quam nos vel petere vel intelligere possimus. Nec verò tantum ex verbo Dei potentiam Dei infinitam addiscimus in Iesu Christo: sed etiam experimur, si quidem per ipsum sermonem crucis efficax est Deus, retrahit nos ex faucibus mortis & inferni, regenerat nos per Spiritum sanctum, & constituit nos haeredes vitae aeternae. Cum interea illi qui contemnunt sermonem crucis, nec intelligant nec credant Dei potentiam: Et in quacunque calamitate deserti ab omnibus creaturis ruant in desperationem & interitum. Scriptum est enim: perdam sapientiam sapientum. Probat Apost: Paulus sermonem crucis iis qui pereunt cedere instultitiam & interitum: Quia Deus minatus sit, se perditurum sapientes et prudentes huius seculi; Quid ergò suis consiliis tàm prudenter & acutè excogitatis effecerunt aut lucrati sunt, nisi quod iram Dei in se provocarunt, & se in aeternum exitium praecipitaverunt. Exemplo est Pharao qui cum suis consiliariis varias excogitavit fraudes, quibus opprimeret populum Israel: Sed ille tandem miserrimè cum suis in mari periit. Sennacherib de sua sapientia gloriabatur: Et tandem à propriis filiis in templo sui idoli trucidatur. In Aureliano, Decio, Diocletiano, magna fuit sapientia, & singulare ingenium: Sedhaec ipsa sapientia perdidit eos. Eò quòd existimarunt dignitatem & potentiam Romani Imperii restitui non posse misi prius nomen Christianum delerent. Dum igitur Christo bellum inferunt, se in extremas calamitates & aeternum exitium demergunt.

Ac omnes historiae testantur sapientes homines plerumque tristissimos sortiri casus. In causa est, quòd praeclarum sapientiae donum, quod ad Dei gloriam & aedificationem Ecclesiae conferre debebant, ut plurimum ad Dei contumeliam & oppressionem Ecclesiae & veritatis convertunt. Quàm tristis fuit exitus Achitophelis cuius sapientia etiam scripturae testimonio celebratur? Item, Socratis, Themistoclis, Palamedis, Periclis, Demadis, Demosthenis, Hyperidae, Ciceronis, Theramenis, & Catonis, & plurimorum aliorum sapientia valde praedicatur in historia: Verum hi omnes miserrimè perierunt, ac plerique suis consiliis sese in tragicas calamitates praecipitarunt. Totius igitur mundi historia testatur quò perdit Deus sapientiam sapientum.

Ubi sapiens? Ubi scriba? Ubi disputator? Ex alio capite nimirum 33. Iesa, haec verba allegat: Sed eodem sensu: Propheta enim concionem habens de admirabili statu Ecclesiae, dicit futurum, ut pii cum stupore exclament: Ubi sapiens? Ubi scriba? Quasi dicant: Non multi sapientes, non multi eruditi sunt in nostro caetu: Et tamen sumus populus Dei & mirabiliter à Deo defendimur. Impossibile esset regna mundana consistere & defendi posse sine viris sapientibus & eruditis. Verum Ecclesia Dei etiam sine sapientibus consiliariis & consistit & propgatur, & defenditur.

Nunquid infatuavit Deus sapientiam seculi huius? Per quae quis peccat, per eadem etiam punitur. Sapientes inprimis laedunt gloriam Dei dum ingeniis suis fingunt idola & falsas religiones & oppugnant doctrinam Evangelii suis consiliis: Infatuat igitur eos Deus, & tradit eos in reprobam mentem. Achitophel adeò insanit, ut laqueo vitam abrumpat. Nabuchdonosor nimium efferens sese sapientia, vertitur in furorem. Nec saniore mente praediti sunt qui beneficia mediatoris aspernantur, doctrinam Evangelii conviciis insectantur, & Ecclesiam oppugnant. Ita enim sibi viam ad vitam aeternam & omnem foelicitatem praecludunt. Videant ergò omnes sapientes, ut discant timere dominum & se submittant eius verbo, ac ne Iesu Christi crucem adspernentur.

## 1:21-22
For after that in the wisdom of God, the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe, seeing that both the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom.

This is a notable sentence, in which Paul explains what moved God to reveal a doctrine so foreign to human wisdom. It is surely because the world, from the most wise works of creation, sustenance, and the governing of all things, did not recognize God by the light of nature, nor did it celebrate Him as God: but rather it treated Him with extreme insult, repeatedly by inventing new deities. Therefore, in order that He might confound the wisdom of human intellect, and also punish with blindness and stupidity those wandering in their own thoughts and treating God with insult: Then, in order that He might demonstrate His infinite wisdom, and that the elect might recognize that they do not arrive at the admirable light of the knowledge of Christ by the powers of free will, but that it is a mere gratuitous gift of God, a new light shedding into our heart through the Holy Spirit: for this reason He instituted the ministry of the word, which seems most absurd and foolish to human reason, and which the world hates and execrates worse than a snake. After the world, he says, in the wisdom of God: that is, through the works of creation and the sustaining of all things, in each of which the most evident traces of the wisdom and omnipotence of God are impressed, did not know God through wisdom. That is, through the light of nature, and the powers of the mind: For they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the corruptible man, of birds and of reptiles: and they worshipped the creature instead of the creator: Therefore it pleased God to save through foolish preaching; which, of course, the world judges to be extreme foolishness, when it is divine and heavenly wisdom, which we shall admire in all eternity.

For the Jews seek a sign: And the Greeks seek wisdom: From the preposterous judgment and curiosity of the world he proves that the preaching of the Gospel is held for foolishness. For the Jews did not assent either to Christ or to the Apostles, even if these demonstrated their doctrine both by the testimonies of the Prophets and by admirable miracles and signs: but with impious curiosity they demanded signs from heaven: such as they themselves wished to prescribe to God; Therefore, from their own ingenuity they attempted to form God; and His counsels to govern: Thus they attempted to make God the creator a slave to their own curiosity and petulance. But because God did not wish to serve their impious desire, they spurned him with the whole Gospel, all the benefits of the mediator, and the entire kingdom of the Messiah. The Greeks struggled against the Gospel with similar impiety: for they demanded such a doctrine as would, like philosophy, agree with human reason, and whose demonstrations they could understand and perceive in nature itself, and also in which they could exercise and display the sharpness of their wit. But because the Apostles demanded faith, which must be applied to divine oracles, and also true exercises of repentance: and proposed articles clearly at variance with philosophy, they proudly despised this kind of Apostolic doctrine: The other peoples, such as the Chaldeans, Egyptians, Persians, Romans, and others, did not have sounder judgments about the Gospel: but he makes mention only of the Jews and Greeks, because the former seemed to excel most in religion, the latter in wisdom and doctrine.

Therefore, the Apostle again inculcates here that the whole doctrine of the Gospel concerning the kingdom of Jesus Christ is most different from the wisdom and counsels of human reason: Whence it follows that the Gospel cannot be perceived by the powers of free will, nor can the true God be known. Therefore, it is falsely asserted by the Synergists that there are three causes concurring in the conversion of man; the Spirit holy, the word of God, and the mind and will. Indeed, the whole mind is blind, and considers the preaching of the Gospel concerning the kingdom of Christ as foolishness. Hence it is also clear that all Philosophy must be distinguished from the doctrine of the Church, which is a heavenly mystery. Paul also warns that it is impious to seek signs and miracles from God, and to wish to prescribe to Him the manner in which He ought to deal with us. Through the Prophets, Christ, and the Apostles, God brought forth admirable and stupendous signs and miracles: By which He demonstrated His doctrine. By these miracles He wishes us to apply faith: And He does not wish to be tempted by us; But to be adored with fear: He Himself knows when there is a need for signs and miracles; And He is never wanting to the infirmity and necessity of the Church: The wicked curiosity of men could never be satisfied. Therefore, all the miracles and signs which God brought forth in the Church must be weighed as diligently as possible: But one must take care lest we tempt God by the petition of new miracles: for this is a grave sin fighting against the first commandment, and entirely contrary to faith.

Latin:

Postquam enim in sapientia Dei, mundus non cognovit per sapientiam Deum, placuit Deo per stultam praedicationem salvos facere credentes, Post aequam & Iudaei signum petunt, & Graeci sapientiam quaerunt.

Insignis haec est sententia, in qua Paulus exponit, quid moverit Deum, ut doctrinam tàm alienam á sapientia humana patefaceret. Nimirum quia mundus ex sapientissimis operibus creationis, sustentationis, & gubernationis omnium rerum luce naturae non agnovit Deum neque ut Deum celebravit: Sed eum potius extrema contumelia adfecit, subinde fingendo nova numina. Ut igitur confunderet humani ingenii sapientiam, atque etiam, caecitate & stupore puniret suis cogitationibus vagantes & Deum contumelia adficientes: Tum ut infinitam suam sapientiam demonstraret, & electi agnoscerent se non viribus liberi arbitrii pervenire ad admirandum lumen cognitionis Christi, sed merum esse gratuitum donum Dei, novam lucem per Spiritum sanctum in cor nostrum spargentis: id circo ministerium verbi instituit, quod rationi humanae absurdissimum & stultissimum videtur, quodque mundus peius angue odit & execratur. Postquam mundus inquit, in sapientia Dei: hoc est, per opera creationis & sustentationis omnium rerum, in quibus singulis evidentissima vestigia sapientiae & omnipotentiae Dei impressa sunt, non cognovit Deum per sapientiam. Id est, per lucem naturae, & viribus mentis: Mutaverunt enim gloriam incorruptibilis Dei in similitudinem corruptibilis hominis, volatilium & reptilium: & coluerunt creaturam pro creatore: Idcirco placuit Deo salvos facere per stultam praedicationem; quam scilicet mundus iudicat extremam esse stultitiam, cum sit divina & coelestis sapientia, quàm in omni aeternitate admirabimur.

Siquidem Iudaei signum petunt: Et graeci sapientiam quaerunt: Ex praepostero mundi Iudicio & curiositate probat praedicationem Evangelii haberi pro stultitia. Iudaei enim non adsentiebantur neque Christo neque Apostolis, etiamsi hi doctrinam suam & testimoniis Prophetarum & admirandis miraculis et signis demonstrarent: sed impia curiositate postulabant signa de coelo: qualia ipsi vellent Deo praescribere; Ex suo igitur ingenio conabantur Deum formare; & eius consilia gubernare: Ita ex conditore Deo conabantur facere mancipium suae curiositatis & petulantiae. Quia verò Deus noluit servire ipsorum impiae cupiditati, spreverunt eum cum toto Evangelio, omnibus beneficiis mediatoris, & universo regno Messiae. Graeci simili impietate obluctati sunt Evangelio: talem enim doctrinam postularunt, quae veluti Philosophia congrueret cum ratione humana, & cuius demonstrationes in ipsa natura intelligere & sentire possent, atque etiam in qua ingenii acumen exercere & ostentare possent. Quia verò. Apostoli postularunt fidem, quae adhibenda sit divinis oraculis, atque etiam vera paenitentiae exercitia: & proposuerunt articulos plane discrepantes à Philosophia, superbè hoc genus doctrinae Apostolicae contempserunt: Caeteri populi ut Chaldei, Aegyptii, Persae, Romani, & alii, non habebant saniora de Evangelio iudicia: tantum autem Iudaeorum et Graecorum facit mentionem, quòd illi religione, hi sapientia & doctrina videbantur maximè excellere.

Rursus ergò inculcat hîc Apostolus totam doctrinam Evangelii de regno Iesu Christi diversissimam esse ab humanae rationis sapientia & consiliis: Unde sequitur Viribus liberi arbitrii non posse percipt Evangelion, neque cognosci verum Deum. Falso ergò adseritur à Synergistis tres esse causas concurrentes in conversione hominis; Spiritum sanctum, verbum Dei, & mentem ac voluntatem. Imò tota mens caeca est, & praedicationem Evangelii de Christi regno pro stultitia habet. Hinc etiam patet totam Philosophiam distinguendam esse à doctrina Ecclesiae, quae est coeleste mysterium. Monet etiam Paulus impium esse petere signa & miracula à Deo, & ipsi velle praescribere modum quo nobiscum agere debeat. Per Prophetas, Christum & Apostolos edidit Deus admiranda & stupenda signa & miracula: Quibus doctrinam suam demonstravit. His miraculis vult nos adhibere fidem: Et non vult à nobis tentari; Sed cum timore adorari: Ipse novit quando opus sit signis & miraculis; Et nunquam de est infirmitati & necessitati Ecclesiae: Sceleratae curiositati hominum nunquam satisfieri posset. Universa itaque miracula & signa quae edidit Deus in Eccle: quam diligentissimè expendenda sunt: Sed cavendum est ne Deum petitione novorum miraculorum tentemus: hoc enim grave peccatum est pugnans cum primo praecepto, & prorsus contrarium fidei.

## 1:23-24
We, however, preach Christ crucified, to the Jews indeed a stumbling block, but to the Greeks foolishness: But to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God. For that which is foolish of God is wiser than men, and what is weak of God is stronger than men.

He shows the head of the preaching of the Gospel, in which the whole world stumbles: namely, that we preach Jesus Christ crucified to be the salvation of the world: The world shrinks from this sad spectacle: The Jews are most grievously offended, because they must acknowledge as the Messiah (of whom they had boasted so much) a man most calamitous in the whole world and fixed to a cross. The Greeks consider it extreme foolishness that they teach. The Apostles teach that we have righteousness, life, and eternal salvation in Jesus Christ crucified: and that he is the lord of the whole world. Such are the profane and sacrilegious judgments of the wise concerning the Gospel at all times. And therefore we ought not to be troubled as often as we hear our doctrine and ministry most atrociously condemned in the world: For the natural man does not perceive the things that are of the Spirit of God; but we ought to regard, esteem, and confirm ourselves by the judgment of the Holy Spirit alone; just as Paul says. But to those who are called, we preach Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God: By the called he understands those called by a holy calling. That is, illuminated by the word and the Holy Spirit: These understand in Christ and experience divine power and wisdom.

For they believe and experience that through Christ the works and the whole kingdom of Satan and of death are destroyed, and life and righteousness are restored: They also understand the most wise counsels of God revealed in the Law and the Gospel, what is the chief end of man: why He sent His only-begotten Son: why He instituted the ministry of the Spirit: why He exercises the Church with the cross: why He allows the wicked to rage for a time: what He has decreed concerning the gathering of the Church, concerning the end of the world, and concerning the final judgment. This most ample and heavenly wisdom, unknown to human reason, is revealed to those called and illuminated through Christ.

Latin:

Nos autem praedicamus Christum crucifixum, Iudaeis quidem scandalum, Graecis verò stultitiam: Ipsis verò vocatis Iudaeis & Graecis Christum Dei potentiam & sapientiam. Nam quod stultum est Dei, sapientius est quàm homines & quod infirmum est Dei, robustius est quàm homines.

Caput praedicationis Evangelii, in quo totus mundus impingit, ostendit: videlicet quòd Iesum Christum crucifixum praedicamus salutem esse mundi: Ab hoc tristi spectaculo abhorret mundus: Iudaei offenduntur granissimè, quod hominem in toto orbe calamitosissimum & cruci adfixum pro Messia, (de quo adeò gloriati fuerant) agnoscere debeant. Graeci pro extrema stultitia habent, quòd docent. Apostoli in Iesu Christo crucifixo nos habere iustitiam, vitam & aeternam salutem: eumque totius mundi dominum esse. Huiusmodi profana et sacrilega sunt sapientum iudicia de Evangelio omnibus temporibus. Ideoque non oportet nos turbari quoties in mundo audimus doctrinam & ministerium nostrum atrocissimè condemnari: Animalis enim homo non percipit ea quae sunt Spiritus Dei; solius autem Spiritus sancti iudicium respicere, magnifacere & eo nos confirmare debemus; quemadmodum Paulus inquit. Ipsis veró vocatis praedicamus Christum Dei potentiam & sapientiam: Vocatos intelligit vocatos sancta vocatione. Hoc est, illuminatos per verbum & Spiritum sanctum: Hi intelligunt in Christo & experiuntur divinam potentiam & sapientiam.

Credunt enim & experiuntur per Christum destrui opera & totum regnum Satanae, et mortis, & restitui vitam & iustitiam: Intelligunt etiam sapientissima Dei consilia in lege & Evangelio patefacta, Quis sit praecipuus finis hominis: cur miserit unigenitum filium: Quare ministerium Spiritus instituerit: cur exerceat Ecclesiam cruce: cur Impios aliquandiu sinat grassari: quid decreverit de collectione Ecclesiae, de fine mundi, & de extremo iudicio. Haec amplissima & coelestis sapientia ignota rationi humanae patefit vocatis & illuminatis per Christum.

## 1:25
For that which is foolish of God, is wiser than men: He illustrates the amplitude of the divine wisdom which is communicated to us in Christ by a comparison of most dissimilar things: For that which is foolish of God: that is, that which seems to us absurd, inept, and foolish concerning God: as that God commanded that Abraham, being ninety years old, should circumcise the flesh of his foreskin: that God commanded Ezekiel to eat human dung: that God commanded Moses to enter the desert and the sea with the people: that He cast Joseph into a pit, drove him into exile, thrust him into prison when He had determined to make him Lord of Egypt: that He chooses fishermen, plebeian, rude, and poor men as Apostles, so that through them He might call the world to repentance: that in establishing His kingdom, having passed over the wise and the powerful, He chooses the lame, the deaf, the blind, the lepers, the poor: Because He commanded His only-begotten Son to undergo the death of the cross. These and countless other things seem both absurd and foolish to our reason: But in these very things God has used a singular wisdom, which far exceeds the entire wisdom of human intellect. For in all these things both the justice, and the wisdom, and the omnipotence of God are seen: Because He understands and can do more than our intellect can grasp. Reason criticizes almost all the works and commands of God like another Momus: But in the end the outcome teaches that God orders, disposes, and perfects all things most wisely: Therefore we ought not to delay for the judgment of reason, but always look to the word and command of God. Thus what is the weakness of God; that is, what seems to us to be the greatest weakness in God: As that God is beaten with rods, is fastened to a cross, dies and is buried, seems to us a huge weakness: That the Church in the time of Hezekiah is surrounded by a siege, and is reduced to the greatest straits, seems to us the extreme weakness of God, as one who cannot rescue His people from the violence of tyrants; But what seems to us weakness, this surpasses the strength and powers of all men: For through the scourges, the cross, the death, the burial of Christ the Son of God, God broke the entire power of Satan, blotted out sin, swallowed up death, took away the curse of the law, conquered the world, established, redeemed, saved. the whole Church: Which could not be effected by the powers of all creatures. Truly, therefore, that which is weak of God is more robust than all men. Let us not, therefore, be offended or troubled when the liberation, building up, and defense of the Church seems impossible to us. For infinite is the wisdom as well as the power of God.

For see your calling, brethren, that not many wise according to the flesh, not many powerful, not many noble, but God chose the foolish things of the world, that He might put to shame the wise: and the weak things of the world that He might put to shame those things which are strong: And the ignoble things of the world, and those which are most of all for contempt, God chose, and those things which are not, that He might abolish those things which are, so that no flesh may glory before God.

That we may consider the admirable counsel and wisdom of God, which is entirely different from human judgment, and that God makes of nothing all the wisdom, power, and whatever is great and sublime before men, He commands us to look upon the admirable gathering of the Church: Which is in great part from the poorest of all men, the most vile, the most abject, from the deaf, the blind, the lame, the lepers, and sinners. To establish and propagate the empires of the world, it is customary to choose the wisest, the strongest, the most noble, those endowed with the highest virtues, the wealthiest, the most skilled, and the most beautiful of all men, who are most suitable for conducting affairs, and who adorn empires with their own dignity and beauty. But the eternal Father, for establishing, propagating, and preserving the eternal and spiritual kingdom of his son Jesus Christ, enters upon a completely different method: he chooses the most abject and the most vile of all, so much so that the Church, because of its poverty, squalor, and infirmity, is a cause of astonishment to the judgment of reason. But by what counsel the eternal Father does this, Paul teaches, namely that he might confound and abolish the wisdom, power, and nobility of men, and whatever is sublime in the world. For men abuse the gifts of wisdom, power, and nobility, and exalt themselves above and against the Lord and his Messiah. Therefore, so that God may make it testified to the world that human wisdom which opposes itself to God is mere foolishness: and that trust in one's own virtue is the highest sacrilege, and that all power, nobility, splendor, wealth, glory, and honor of the entire creature is nothing before God, passing over the wise and the powerful, he chooses into the Church the most abject of all. So that at last all glory of wisdom, justice, and power may return to God alone.

Hence, therefore, it is clear in how great an error they are involved who, seeking the Church, look only to the judgments of the powerful, the decrees of councils, the opinions of the learned, and the consensus of the nobles, and without examination and investigation of the foundations in matters and controversies of religion, swear by the words of magnates, learned men, and councils.

These things, however, are not to be taken as if no one of the rich, the powerful, the wise, or the noble could be saved: Nay, the holy scripture gives a distinguished testimony to certain wise and powerful men, that they were true citizens of the Church. There was exceptional wisdom in Joseph, who taught the counselors of Pharaoh wisdom: in Daniel, who governed the Chaldean and Persian empire with his counsels: in David, Hushai, Bezalel, Benaiah, Moses: who are illustrious citizens of the Church.

Great and powerful were Pharaoh, the host of the family of Jacob, David, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, Nebuchadnezzar, Darius the Mede, Cyrus, Constantine the Great, Theodosius, Marcian: and they were called to the society of the Church: Abraham, Isaac, David, Jehoshaphat, Charlemagne, Esther were rich, and yet they have a part in the kingdom of Christ.

Of noble birth were Isaiah, Daniel, Josiah, Hezekiah, Zadok, Joseph: And yet they have the testimony of the Holy Spirit that they were enrolled as heirs of eternal life. Therefore God did not reject all the wise, the powerful, the rich, and the noble, but only those who trust in their own wisdom, power, and nobility, and stubbornly resist the Gospel of Jesus Christ. Daniel was wise, but he, in the fear of God and true humility, attributes everything to God, and confesses that there is no counsel in him, unless God has enlightened him with His Spirit. Therefore, whoever is adorned by God with the gift of talent, wisdom, or nobility, let him humble himself all the more and not boast, lest he provoke the wrath of God and exclude himself from the fellowship of the Church. This sentence of Paul warns us not to be offended by the abject appearance of the Church: For thus it pleased God to choose those things which are abject and vile in the world, so that His power and glory might have a place. This sentence also consoles miserable and calamitous men, and those placed in the lowest lot, that they should not suspect that they are therefore neglected or less cared for because they are miserable, but rather let them conclude that the more calamitous and miserable any of the faithful is in the world, the greater is the care God has for him. Thirdly, the Apostle teaches that all boasting belongs to the only wise and omnipotent God: And that the entire human race ought to abstain completely from all boasting.

Latin:

Nàm quod stultum est Dei, sapientius est hominibus: Amplitudinem sapientiae divinae quae nobis in Christo communicatur illustrat collatione rerum dissimilimarum: Nàm quod stultum est Dei: hoc est, quod nobis de Deo absurdum, ineptum & stultum videtur: ut quòd Deus iussit ut Abraham nonagenarius circumcideret carnem praeputii sui: quòd iussit Deus Ezechielem vescistercore humano: quòd iussit Deus Mosem cum populo ingredi desertum & mare: quòd Iosephum coniecit in foveam, pepulit in exilium, detrusit in carcerem cum statuisset eum facere Dominum Aegypti: quòd piscatores, homines plebeios, & rudes, & pauperes eligit in Apostolos, ut mundum per hos vocet ad paenitentiam: quò in constituendo regno suo praeteritis sapientibus & potentibus eligit claudos, surdos, caecos, leprosos, pauperes: Quod iussit unigenitum filium subire mortem crucis. Haec & alia innumera rationi nostrae & absurda & stulta videntur: At in his ipsis Deus singulari sapientia est usus, quae universam humani ingenii sapientiam longissimè excedit. In his omnibus enim & iustitia, & sapîentia, & omnipotentia Dei conspicitur: Quòd plus intelligat & possit quàm ingenium nostrum capere possit. Ratio omnia fere opera & mandata Dei carpit veluti alter momus: Sed tandem eventus docet, Deum omnia sapientissimè ordinare, disponere, & perficere: Nihil ergò rationis iudicium morari debemus, sed semper ad verbum & mandatum Dei respicere. Sic quod est infirmum Dei; hoc est, quod nobis videtur summa esse in Deo infirmitas: Ut quòd Deus caeditur virgis, adfigitur cruci, moritur & sepelitur, ingens infirmitas nobis videtur: Quòd Ecclesia tempore Hiskia cingitur obsidione, & in summas redigitur angustias, extrema nobis Dei infirmitas videtur, ut qui non possit populum suum eripere ex tyrannorum violentia; Sed quae nobis videtur infirmitas, haec superat omnium hominum robur & vires: Nam per flagra, crucem, mortem, sepulturam Christi filii Dei Deus fregit universam Satanae potentiam, delevit peccatum, absorpsit mortem, sustulit legis maledictionem, vicit mundum, constituit, redemit, salvavit totam Ecclesiam: Quod universae creaturae viribus effici non poterat. Verè igitur quod infirmum est Dei, robustius est omnibus hominibus. Non ergò offendamur aut turbemur, cum Ecclesiae liberatio, aedificatio & defensio nobis videtur impossibilis. Infinita enim est Dei cum sapientia tum potentia.

Videte enim vocationem vestram fratres, quòd non multi sapientes secundum carnem, non multi potentes, non multi nobiles, sed stulta mundi elegit Deus, ut sapientes pudefaceret: & infirma mundi ut ea quae valida sunt pudefaceret: Et ignobila mundi, & quae maximè sunt contemptui, elegit Deus, & ea quae non sunt ut ea quae sunt aboleret, ne coram Deo ulla caro glorietur.

Ut consideremus admirandum Dei consilium & sapientiam prorsus diversam à iudicio humano, & quòd Deus nihili faciat universam hominum sapientiam, potentiam, & quidquid magnum & sublime est coràm hominibus, iubet nos intueri admirabilem collectionem Ecclesiae: Quae magna ex parte ex omnium hominum pauperrimis, vilissimis, abiectissimis, ex surdis, caecis, claudis, leprosis, Et peccatoribus consistit. Ad constituenda & propaganda imperia mundi eligi solent omnium hominum sapientissimi, fortissimi, nobilissimi, summis virtutibus praediti, ditissimi, peritissimi, & pulcherrimi, qui ad res gerendas maximè sunt idonei, & imperia suo decore & pulchritudine ornant. At pater aeternus ad constituendum, propagandum, & conservandum aeternum & spirituale regnum sui filii Iesu Christi, prorsus diversam init rationem: eligit abiectissimum, & vilissimum quenque adeò ut Ecclesia prae paupertate, squalore, & infirmitate stupori sit iudicio rationis. Quo autem consilio hoc faciat pater aeternus docet Paulus, nimirum ut sapientiam, potentiam, nobilitatem hominum, & quidquid sublime est in mundo confundat & aboleat. Abutuntur enim homines sapientiae potentiae, & nobilitatis donis, & sese supra & contra dominum & Messiam eius efferunt. Ut ergò Deus testatum faciat mundo, humanam sapientiam quae se Deo opponit meram esse stultitiam: & fiduciam propriae virtutis summum esse sacrilegium, omnemque otentiam, nobilitatem, splendorem, opes, gloriam et decus universae creaturae nihil esse apud Deum, praeteritis sapientibus & potentibus eligit in Ecclesiam omnium abiectissimos. Ut ta tandem omnis gloria sapientiae iustitiae, & potentiae ad solum Deum redeat.

Hinc ergò liquet in quanto versentur errore qui Ecclesiam quaerentes tantum adiudicia potentum, decreta conciliorum, sententias eruditorum, & consensum Nobilium respiciunt, & sine examine & investigatione fundamentorum in negotiis & controversiis religionis iurant in verba magnatum, eruditorum hominum, & conciliorum.

Haec autem ita accipienda non sunt quasi nemo divitum, potentum, sapientum, nobilium salvari possit: Imò scriptura sacra quibusdam sapientibus & potentibus praeclarum dat testimonium, quòd fuerint veri cives Ecclesiae. Eximia fuit sapientia in Iosepho, qui consiliarios Pharaonis docuit sapientiam: in Daniele qui imperium Chaldaicum & Persicum gubernavit consiliis: in Davide, Chusai, Bezaleel, Benaia, Mose: qui sunt illustres Ecclesiae cives.

Magni & potentes fuerunt Pharao hospes familiae Iacob, David, Iosaphat, Hiskia, Nebucadnezar, Darius Medus, Cyrus, Constantinus Magnus, Theodosius, Marcianus: & vocati sunt ad societatem Ecclesiae: Dives fuit Abraham, Isaac, David, Iosaphath, Carolus Magnus, Esther & tamen partem habent in regno Christi.
