Because they are spiritually judged: He shows the reason why the natural man cannot perceive or know the things which are of the Spirit: Because they are to be judged spiritually: That is, there is need of spiritual light, a reborn mind, knowledge of the word, and the help of the Holy Spirit to judge the doctrine of the Holy Spirit. The carnal man savors only carnal things; as Nicodemus, being carnal, understands only natural generation, and what the powers of free will can accomplish: he understands absolutely nothing about spiritual regeneration and the benefits of the mediator.

Latin:

Animalis verò homo non percipit ea quae sunt Spiritus: stultitia enim sunt ei: Nec potest intelligere: Quia spiritualiter diiudicantur.

Hic est ille celeberrimus locus, qui evidentissimè dirimit totam controversiam, quae omnibus temporibus de viribus liberi arbitrii in Ecsia agitata fuit. Disertissimè enim pronunciat Apostolus Paulus Spiritus sancti instinctu: Hominem animalem adeò nihil intelligere eorum quae sunt Spiritus Dei, & ad aeternam pertinent salutem, ut ea omnia pro stultitia habeat. Nunc liberi arbitrii patrone & synergiae defensor, & contra Paulum adstrue esse aliquid in homine non renato, vel modiculum, vel exiguam facultatulam, vel scintillulam, vel nutum saltem, quo possit se homo adplicare ad gratiam, vel adsentiri oblatae veritati Evangelii. Quid posset manifestius atque etiam gravius contra synergiam dici? Sed verborum pondera nobis expendenda sunt.

Animalem hominem nominat Paulus totum hominem, animam & corpus, cum omnibus viribus mentis, voluntatis, & cordis, quatenus naturaliter à parentibus est genitus: Nec dum per Spiritum sanctum est renatus. Animalem enim spirituali opponit. De eo igitur loquitur qui in puris relictus est naturalibus: Quales non tantùm sunt Ethnici & omnes extra Ecclesiam, sed omnes etiam intra Ecclesiam qui per Spiritum sanctum non sunt conversi. Quantavis igitur quis polleat vel sapientia, vel eruditione, vel ingenio, vel virtute, vel rerum peritia: Nisi quis per Spiritum sanctum sit regeneratus, & illuminatus, est animalis et nihil percipit eorum quae sunt Spiritus. Eodem sensu sacra scriptura alibi vocat carnem, quem hoc loco animalem hominem nominat Paulus, ut Ioan: 3. Quidquid ex carne natum est, caro est: Et Matth: 16. Caro & sanguis haec tibi non revelarunt. Iesa: 40. Omnis caro faenum. In his locis caro significat totum hominem, animam & corpus cum omnibus viribus & potentiis, quemadmodum à parentibus genitus est: Luce autem Spiritus sancti non est illustratus. Animales sunt Ethnici quantacunque sapientia praediti Temistocles, Solon, Plato, Xenophon, Scipio, Lelius, Augustus: Animales sunt Gamaliel, Nicodemus antè conversionem Pharisaei, & omnes qui Spiritus sancti luce destituuntur. Cum Christus inquit: Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua & Spiritu, non videbit regnum Dei, prorsus idem docet quod hic Paulus, hominem videlicet animalem seu carnalem, qui per Spiritum sanctum renatus non est, ea quae ad regnum Dei coeleste pertinent & sunt Spiritus sancti, videre non posse.

Haec enim sunt Spiritus, quae sine illuminatione Spiritus sancti intelligi non possunt, ut est doctrina de vera agnitione Dei. Nemo potest Iesum vocare dominum (inquit Paulus) nisi in Spiritu sancto. Et nemo novit patrem nisi filius. Deinde quàm sublime sit iudicium Dei iuxta legem, ratio humana non intelligit: Lex, inquit Paulus, est spiritualis: Ego autem carnalis, Rom: 7. Praeterea Spiritus est universa doctrina Evangelii de mediatore Deo & homine, de ipsius morte & resurrectione, de ipsius beneficiis, de spirituali ipsius regno, in quo sedens ad dexteram aeterni patris verbo & Spiritu colligit & regit Ecclesiam, distribuit iustitiam & vitam aeternam. Haec omnia quae ad regnum Christi pertinent & de coelo sunt patefacta, in cor autem hominis sine revelatione Spiritus sancti non adscenderunt, sunt Spiritus Dei. Adfirmat ergò nunc Paulus Animalem hominem nihil eorum percipere quae sunt Spiritus Dei. Necesse est igitur extinctum esse liberum arbitrium, quò ad spiritualia: Necesse est emortuas esse vires hominis in spiritualibus: siquidem animalis homó nihil eorum percipit, quae sunt Spiritus Dei. Quae igitur impudentia est Pelagianorum & Syner gistarum contra tàm manifestam Spiritus sancti sententiam, quod audent adserere, in homine animali nondum renato aliquam restare vim liberi arbitrii, qua se ad gratiam adplicare, vel praedicationi Evangelii adsentiri, vel tractioni patris ex sese annuere possit.

I. Observent igitur studiosi hoc insigne testimonium Spiritus sancti, quod luce meridiana clarius est, & nulla Sophistica infringi potest: quòd testatur nullum esse in homine liberum arbitrium in spiritualibus: Et addantur hîc alia similia testimonia ut Ioan: 3. Quidquid ex carne natum est, caro est, Item. Rom: 8. Sensus carnis est inimicitia adversus Deum. Item: Ioan: 6. Nemo venit ad me nisi pater meus traxerit eum. Falsa igitur & impia doctrina est, quòd scriptores adfirmant tres esse causas concurrentes in conversione, Spiritum sanctum, verbum Dei, & mentem ac voluntatem. Cum solus Spiritus sanctus per verbum in ipsa caeca mente, & perversa voluntate operetur conversionem ad Deum.

II. Multa praeterea doctrinae capita ex hoc dicto peti possunt, ut quod omnes homines natura sunt peccatores & filii irae. Ita enim conditus erat homo ut verum Deum agnosceret & celebraret: Sed adeò corruptus est, ut ea quae Spiritus sunt, nempe quis sit verus Deus, videre non possit. Et cum homo animalis non intelligat spirituale legis iudicium, manifestum est eum non praestare integram obedientiam.

III. Tertiò patet ex hoc dicto Ethnicos, quantavis virtute, sapientia & doctrina praediti fuerint, non tamen fuisse membra Eccle: Dei, nec spem ullam habuisse consequendi vitam aeternam. Prorsus enim ignari fuerunt doctrinae Spiritus sancti.

IIII. Quartò docet Paulus sine Spiritus & verbi ministerio neminem pervenire ad agnitionem Mediatoris Iesu Christi: Animalis enim homo licet summo ingenio sit praeditus & mille annos speculetur, tamen non percipit ea quae sunt Spiritus.

V. Quintò monet hoc dictum, Ecclesiam non esse regendam humanis consiliis: Sed expressum Dei verbum esse sequendum.

VI. Sextò monet Paulus ut hic captivemus rationem & omnes cogitationes de Deo & vita aeterna in obsequium Iesu Christi: Ratio enim nihil eorum percipit quae sunt Spiritus. Non igitur Philosophia miscenda est cum Theologia: Neque articuli fidei ex Philosophia exponendi aut formandi sunt, sed vera sententia articulorum fidei ex revelatione Spiritus sancti, quae Propheticis & Apostolicis literis consignata est, semper est petenda.

Stultia enim sunt ei: Ea scilicet quae sunt Spiritus. Tristissima est oratio, quòd dixit Paulus, hominem animalem non percipere ea quae sunt Spiritus, sed multò gravius est quòd dixit animalem hominem consilia & doctrinam Dei & Spiritus sancti stultitiae condemnare. Est ergò contumeliosa in Deum & hostis Dei. Qui ergò fieri posset ut huismodi blasphemus Dei hostis in conversione sui ad Deum Spiritui sancto adsentiendo doctrinae, quam pro stultitia habet, cooperaretur? Necesse est igitur horribiliter corruptam esse humanam naturam. Manifestum est etiam omnes esse natura filios irae & obnoxios morti.

Et non potest cognoscere: Ne quid relinquat dubitationis, sed ut omnes Sophismatum rimas obstruat, addit Animalem hominem non posse ea cognoscere quae sunt Spiritus. In spiritualibus ergò prorsus emortuum est liberum arbitrium & omni vi seu efficacia destituitur. Sic ad Rom: 8. Paulus: Sensus carnis legi Dei non subiicitur: Nec enim potest. Et Christus inquit. Iohan: 6: Nemo potest ad me venire nisi pater meus traxerit eum.

Quia spiritualiter diiudicantur: Rationem ostendit, quare animalis homo non possit ea quae sunt Spirittus percipere aut cognoscere: Quia spiritualiter diiudicentur: Hoc est, spirituali luce, renata mente, cognitione verbi, auxilio Spiritus sancti opus est ad diiudicandam Spiritus sancti doctrinam. Carnalis tantùm carnalia sapit, Ut Nicodemus carnalis tantùm intelligit naturalem generationem, & quid vires liberi arbitrii praestatare possint: De spirituali regeneratione & de beneficiis mediatoris prorsus nihil intelligit.

## 2:15
But the spiritual man judges all things: yet he himself is judged by no one.

As above he named him the animal man who is destitute of the light of the Holy Spirit and follows only the affections of the flesh: So here he names the spiritual man as one reborn through the Holy Spirit, and endowed with a new light, namely the recognition of the true God, and the understanding of the benefits of Christ: Who is called by Paul elsewhere the new man and a new creature in Christ. He says this spiritual man judges all things: Namely, those things which have been divinely revealed through the Holy Spirit and pertain to our salvation. For Paul is not speaking about the controversies of the civil forum, or the disputes of private individuals, about the affairs of this life, or about the disciplines of human philosophy: But about spiritual things; in which our salvation consists. The spiritual man understands, sees, perceives, and judges all these spiritual things: let them be pious men and those fearing the Lord in the most serious controversies often judge more correctly than trained theologians who are further removed from piety. The spiritual man easily judges the controversy concerning the presence of the body of Christ in the supper: for he simply acquiesces to the word of Christ: he easily understands that good works are not necessary for salvation: That there is no cooperation of the Holy Spirit in the conversion of man to God: That original sin is not a substance: Because in these and all similar things he follows the express word of God: and the Holy Spirit directs him into all truth. He himself however is judged by no one. For his whole doctrine, confession, labors, life, hope, and struggles are spiritual: Therefore they cannot be judged by the flesh. Hence it is that when the pious sound forth most wholesome doctrine, they are accused of lying by the world: when they issue a pious confession, they are accused of blasphemy: when they sustain holy labors, they are held as crimes: when they live piously, they are reckoned as the most wicked of men: when they sustain necessary struggles for defending the truth, they are called the torches of wars and of all disturbances. So impossible is it for the spiritual man to be judged by carnal men. Peter, about to give counsel to Christ that He should not suffer, hears: get behind me Satan: for you do not savor the things that are of God, but the things that are of man. For this counsel had proceeded from the impatience of the flesh, not from the judgment of the Spirit.

For who has known the mind of the Lord?

Or who has given him counsel? We, however, hold the mind of Christ.

With the testimony of the Prophet Isaiah brought forward from 40. cap: he proves the previous opinion that spiritual things cannot be judged by carnal men. For the Prophet testifies that the secret counsels of God concerning the gathering of the Church and the government of the world are known to no man without heavenly revelation. Therefore, the animal man, not illuminated by the light of the Holy Spirit, cannot judge concerning the mystery of the Gospel, which contains the secret counsels of God concerning the gathering of the Church. We, however, Christians, who have been reconciled to God through faith and gifted with the Holy Spirit, hold the mind of Christ: that is, we understand the counsel and will of the eternal God, which He decreed concerning the redemption of the human race through His Son: we understand the counsel of Jesus Christ, according to which He gathers the Church: we know who God is and how He wishes to be worshipped: we know that God in the law severely accuses the sins of all men: we know that in the Gospel the remission of sins, righteousness, the Holy Spirit, and eternal life are freely offered to all who do penance: we know for what counsel Christ underwent the cross: and why He subjected the Church to the cross: we know how He wishes to be invoked, and that He will surely give eternal life to those who believe.

We hold this mind of Christ and the whole counsel of God the Father concerning the redemption of the human race: Because the Holy Spirit has revealed it to us in the ministry of the Gospel. And the Apostle speaks not only of the ministers of the Church, or teachers, but universally of all the faithful: for the Holy Spirit reveals the mind of Christ to individuals, to each one according to his measure.

Doctrinal topics.

I. The first topic in this second Chapter is, That the knowledge of Jesus Christ crucified is the sum of all wisdom, which can befall a man in this life. For Paul, such a great Apostle, boasts that he knows nothing except Jesus crucified.

II. The second is concerning the immense terror and infirmity of the Apostles: Paul confesses that he taught among the Corinthians in fear and trembling. Therefore, let no one imagine that the Apostles were perfect, and immune from all infirmity.

III. The third is concerning the solid foundation of faith: that it ought to and can rely not on the words of human wisdom: but on the demonstration of the Spirit and of the power of God: that is, the manifest word of God, and miracles proper to the divine and omnipotent nature.

IIII. The fourth, That the doctrine of the Gospel is a hidden mystery, unknown to reason and to all the princes of the world.

V. The fifth topic is concerning the communication of idioms; that it is rightly said, on account of the personal union of the two natures in Christ, that the Lord of glory was crucified, that God suffered, that God died.

VI. The sixth is concerning the servile free will of man: That the animal man does not see, nor understand the counsels of God, and perceives nothing of those things which are of the Spirit of God. There is therefore no free will in man regarding spiritual things.

VII. The seventh topic: Concerning the eternal divinity of the Holy Spirit. Paul testifies that the Holy Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God: His wisdom is therefore immense, and He is the eternal God. He also testifies that the Holy Spirit is from God: whence it follows that He is of the same essence with the eternal God: for God is Spirit or spiritual essence. Therefore the Spirit from God is of divine essence.

VIII. The eighth concerning the office and benefit of the Holy Spirit, that through the ministry of the Gospel He reveals to us the secret counsels of God, and kindles an admirable light in us, and dwells in us.

IX. The ninth: Concerning the distinction between the form of speech of human wisdom: And the form of speech which the Holy Spirit teaches.

X. The tenth concerning original sin: That the nature of men is so corrupted, that not only does he not understand the counsels of God from himself, but dares even to condemn them as extreme folly.

Latin:

Spiritualis verò diiudicat omnia: ipse verò à nemine iudicatur.

Ut supra Animalem nominavit eum qui luce spiritus sancti destituitur & tantùm adfectus carnis sequitur: Ita hic spiritualem nominat hominem renatum per Spiritum sanctum, & nova luce, nimirum agnitione veri Dei, & intellectu beneficiorum Christi donatum: Qui Paulo alias dicitur novus homo et nova creatura in Christo. Hunc spiritualem dicit omnia diiudicare: Scilicet quae divinitus per Spiritum sanctum sunt revelata & ad nostram pertinent salutem. Non enim loquitur Paulus de controversiis fori civilis, aut litibus privatorum, de huius vitae rebus, aut de Philosophiae humanae disciplinis: Sed de spiritualibus; in quibus nostra consistit salus. Haec spiritualia omnia intelligit, videt, percipit, iudicat spiritualis: sit homines pii & timentes dominum in gravissimis controversiis saepe rectius iudicant, quàm exercitati theologi qui longius absunt à pietate. Spiritualis facilè diiudicat controversiam de praesentia corporis Christi in caena: simpliciter enim acquiescit verbo Christi: facile intelligit quòd bona opera non sunt necessaria ad salutem: Quòd nulla sit cooperatio Spiritus sancti in conversione hominis ad Deum: Quòd peccatum originis non sit substantia: Quia in his et similibus omnibus sequitur expressum Dei verbum: & Spiritus sanctus dirigit eum in omnem veritatem. Ipse tamen â nemine diiudicatur. Nam tota eius doctrina, confessio, labores, vita, spes, certamina sunt spiritualia: Ideo à carne diiudicari non possunt. Hinc est quod cum pii doctrinam sonant saluberrimam, mendacii à mundo arguuntur: quando confessionem piam edunt, blasphemiae accusantur: cum sanctos labores sustinent, pro piaculis habentur: cum piè vivunt, pro sceleratissimis hominibus accensentur: cum necessaria pro veritate tuenda sustinent certamina, vocantur faces bellorum & omnium turbarum. Adeò impossibile est hominem Spiritualem à carnalibus diiudicari. Petrus daturus Christo consilium, ne pateretur, audit: abi post me Satanas: non enim quae Dei, sed quae hominis sunt, sapis. Ex carnis enim impatientia, non ex iudicio Spiritus profectum erat hoc consilium.

Quis enim novit mentem domini?

aut quis daturus est ei consilium? Nos aut mentem Christi tenemus.

Testimonio Iesaiae Prophetae adducto ex 40. cap: probat superiorem sententiam spiritualia à carnalibus hominibus diiudicari non posse. Propheta enim testatur arcana Dei consilia de collectione Ecclesiae & gubernatione mundi, sine coelesti patefactione nemini hominum nota esse. Ergò animalis homo non illustratus luce Spiritus sancti, de mysterio Evangelii, quod continet arcana Dei consilia de collectione Ecclesiae diiudicare non potest. Nos verò Christiani, qui per fidem Deo reconciliati, & Spiritu sancto donati sumus, tenemus mentem Christi: hoc est, intelligimus consilium & voluntatem aeterni Dei, quam de redemptione generis humani per filium decrevit: intelligimus consilium Iesu Christi, iuxta quod colligit Ecclesiam: scimus quis sit Deus & quomodo coli velit: scimus Deum in lege severè accusare omnium hominum peccata: scimus in Evangelio omnibus agentibus paenitentiam gratis offerri remissionem peccatorum, iustitiam, Spiritum sanctum, & vitam aeternam: scimus quo consilio Christus subierit crucem: & quare Ecclesiam subiecerit cruci: scimus quomodo invocari velit, & quòd certò credentibus vitam aeternam daturus sit.

Hanc mentem Christi & totum consilium Dei patris de redemptione generis humani, tenemus: Quia Spiritus sanctus illud nobis in ministerio Evangelii revelavit. Ac loquitur Apostolus non tantum de ministris Ecclesiae, sive doctoribus, sed in universum de omnibus fidelibus: singulis enim revelat Spiritus sanctus mentem Christi, unicuique iuxta mensuram suam.

Loci doctrinae.

I. Primus locus in hoc secundo Capite est, Quòd noticia Iesu Christi crucifixi sit omnium summa sapientia, quae possit homini in hac vita contingere. Paulus enim tantus Apostolus gloriatur se nihil scire nisi Iesum crucifixum.

II. Secundus est de ingenti terrore & infirmitate Apostolorum: Paulus fatetur se in timore & tremore docuisse apud Corinthios. Nemo ergò imaginetur Apostolos fuisse perfectos, & ab omni infirmitate immunes.

III. Tertius de solido fidei fundamento: quòd ea niti debeat & possit non humanae sapientiae sermonibus: sed demonstratione Spiritus & virtutis Dei: hoc est, manifesto Dei verbo, & miraculis propriis divinae & omnipotentis naturae.

IIII. Quartus, Quòd doctrina Evangelii sit mysterium absconditum, ignotum rationi & omnibus mundi principibus.

V. Quintus locus est de communicatione Idiomatum; Quòd rectè dicatur propter unionem personalem duarum naturarum in Christo, Dominum gloriae esse crucifixum, Deum esse passum, Deum esse mortuum.

VI. Sextus est de servo hominis arbitrio: Quòd animalis homo non videat, nec intelligat consilia Dei, & nihil eorum percipiat quae sunt Spiritus Dei. Nullum est igitur liberum arbitrium in homine quò ad spiritualia.

VII. Septimus locus: De Spiritus sancti aeterna divinitate. Paulus testatur Spiritum sanctum omnia scrutari, etiam profunda Dei: Est igitur immensa eius sapientia, atque aeternus Deus. Testatur etiam Spiritum sanctum esse ex Deo: unde sequitur eiusdem eum esse essentiae cum Deo aeterno: Deus enim est Spiritus seu spiritualis essentia. Ergò Spiritus ex Deo est divinae essentiae.

VIII. Octavus de officio & beneficio Spiritus sancti, quòd per ministerium Evangelii revelet nobis arcana Dei consilia, & admirandam lucem in nobis accendat, & in nobis habitet.

IX. Nonus: De discrimine inter formam sermonis humanae sapientiae: Et formam sermonis quam docet Spiritus sanctus.

X. Decimus de peccato originis: Quod hominum natura in tantum sit corrupta, ut non solum non intelligat ex sese consilia Dei, sed ea etiam extremae stulticiae condemnare audeat.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

## 3:1-7
And I brethren could not speak to you as unto spiritual: but as unto carnal: as unto little ones in Christ: I gave you milk to drink, and not meat to eat: for you were not able: but neither are you able as yet. For you are yet carnal. For whereas there is among you envying, and contention, and dissensions, are you not carnal, and walk according to man? For when one saith, I indeed am of Paul: and another, I am of Apollo: are you not carnal?

By the example of the Corinthians he teaches that the carnal or animal man does not perceive the things that are of the Spirit. For not even the Corinthians themselves, however endowed with either wisdom or erudition, were able to perceive the spiritual doctrine of Paul immediately at the beginning, but it was necessary for Paul to accommodate himself to their weakness. Therefore they ought not to assume high spirits, but be mindful of their own ignorance and infirmity.

Paul warns that we should never exalt ourselves proudly, that we must always recall what kind of people we were before our conversion, what the beginnings of our conversion were, how mercifully God illuminated our minds, and how much darkness and weakness of the flesh still clings to us: Therefore we ought both to fear God and to think modestly of ourselves. Thus Paul criticizes the false apostles who preached their sermons magnificently and splendidly, and looked down upon Paul's doctrine as childish from on high: And at the same time he taxes both the levity and arrogance of the hearers, because they hunt for the praise of wisdom and eloquence from the knowledge of the Gospel. That he says he fed the Corinthians with milk as if they were infants, and did not immediately nourish them with solid food, signifies that he did not at once propose to them the sublime mysteries of heavenly doctrine: But that he delivered the first rudiments and articles of faith until they should grow up in the knowledge of Christ. Therefore a pious and faithful doctor of the Church should not show off his own erudition or wisdom: But he should primarily have regard for his hearers, and aim at this, that he may build up the Church.

Nor indeed does he only admonish them as to what kind of people they were before their conversion, but also as to what kind they still are, namely carnal: since they are eager for factions and dissensions, which depraved affection proceeds not from the Spirit, but from the flesh. This infirmity of the Corinthians testifies that the Church of Christ on earth is not entirely lacking every stain: but carrying around much infirmity and filth. For he addresses those whom a little later he says have been washed, justified, and sanctified. The Apostle also warns with great zeal that empty contentions and unnecessary dissensions are to be avoided.

Who then is Paul? and who is Apollos? but ministers by whom you have believed; even as the Lord gave to every man. I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase. So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.

Because the Corinthians were contending about the glory and authority of teachers in the Church, as to which one should be preferred over the other, when nevertheless the doctrine was the same, he leads them to the author of the ministry, who alone through it is efficacious and works salvation: and he shows the distinction between God the lord and author of the word, and the Apostles the ministers. I and Apollos, he says, are not authors of the word, or lords of the Church, or effectors of salvation: but only: ministers sent by God so that through our voice you might believe. We indeed sound forth the heavenly doctrine which we have received from God: but neither to instill faith into your hearts, nor can we communicate the Holy Spirit to you, nor turn your minds and wills to God. But it is God who kindles faith, converts hearts, communicates the Holy Spirit, and increases his gifts in you. Therefore, all things must be referred to the glory of God, and thanks must be given to him. Thus also John the Baptist says: I indeed baptize you with water: but he who is before me comes after me, he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. Therefore, let the illustrious distinctions by which Jesus Christ and the Apostles or other saints differ among themselves always be in sight.

1.

Christ is almighty God and man. The Apostles are weak human creatures.

2.

Christ is invoked by the Church in every necessity. It is a sin to invoke an Apostle.

3.

Jesus Christ is without any sin. The Apostles and all the saints are sinners, conceived and born in sins.

4.

Christ is the mediator, redeemer, savior, and lord of the Church. But the Apostles are not redeemers, but they themselves are in need of redemption, and are ministers of the Church.

5.

Christ is effective through the word, He illuminates minds, converts wills, bends hearts, inspires faith, and works life and consolation. The Apostles are only ministers of the word and of the sacraments.

6.

Christ pours out and gives the Holy Spirit. The Apostles only baptize with water.

7.

Christ is present everywhere and always to His Church and to individual members. The Apostles only served some members of the Church in one place at a certain time, until they finished their course.

Latin:

Et ego fratres non potui vobis loqui, tanquam spiritualibus: Sed tanquam carnalibus: Tanquam infantibus in Christo: Lacte vos potavi, & non cibo vos alui: Non enim eratis capaces: Sed neque etiamnum capaces estis. Adhuc enim carnales estis. Cum enim in vobis sint aemulatio, contentio, dissidia nunquid carnales estis, & secundum hominem ambulatis? Quando enim dicit quis, Ego quidem sum Pauli: Alius autem dicit Ego sum Apollo: Nonne carnales estis?

Corinthiorum exemplo docet carnalem seu animalem hominem non percipere ea quae sunt Spiritus. Nam ne ipsi quidem Corinthii quantavis praediti vel sapientia vel eruditione, statim initiò percipere potuerunt spiritualem Pauli doctrinam, quin oportuit Paulum sese accommodare ipsorum imbecillitati. Non igitur altos Spiritus sumere debent, sed memores esse suae inscitiae & infirmitatis.

Monet Paulus ne unquam superbè nos efferamus, semper memoria repetendum esse quales ante conversionem extiterimus, quae fuerint initiae nostrae conversionis, quàm clementer Deus mentes nostras illuminaverit, quanta etiamnum in nobis haereat & caligo & imbecillitas carnis: Quare & Deum timere & de nobis modestè sentire debemus. Perstringit ita Paul: Pseudoapostolos qui magnificè & splendide suas praedicabant conciones, & Pauli doctrinam ut puerilem ex alto despiciebant: Et simul auditorum & levitatem & arrogantiam taxat, quòd ex cognitione Evangelii laudem sapientiae & eloquentiae venentur. Quòd dicit lacte se potasse Corinthios tanquam infantes, non mox solido aluisse cibo, significat se non statim sublimia mysteria doctrinae coelestis ipsis proposuisse: Sed prima rudimenta & articulos fidei tradidisse donec in cognitione Christi adolescerent. Pius ergò ac fidelis doctor Ecclesiae non ostentet suam eruditionem vel sapientiam: Sed inprimis habeat suorum auditorum rationem, & hoc spectet ut aedificet Ecclesiam.

Nec verò tantum admonet eos quales ante conversionem fuerint, sed etiam quales etiamnum sint, nimirum carnales: siquidem factionibus & dissidiis studeant, qui pravus adfectus non à Spiritu, sed à carne proficiscitur. Haec Corinthiorum infirmitas testatur, Ecclesiam Christi in terris non prorsus omni labe carere: sed multum infirmitatis et sordium circumferre. Eos enim alloquitur quos paulò post dicit ablutos, iustificatos & sanctificatos esse. Monet etiam Apostolus magno studio inanes contentiones, & dissidia non necessaria vitanda esse.

Quis igitur est Paulus? quis autem Apollo? nisi ministri per quos credidistis? ut cuique Deus dedit. Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit, sed Deus incrementum dedit. Itaque neque qui plantat est aliquid, neque qui rigat: sed qui incrementum dedit Deus.

Quia Corinthii certabant de gloria & authoritate doctorum in Ecclesia, uter utri praeferendus esset, cum eadem tamen doctrina esset, deducit eos ad authorem ministerii, qui per illud solus est efficax & operatur salutem: & discrimen monstrat inter Deum dominum & authorem verbi, & Apostolos ministros. Ego & Apollo, inquit, non sumus authores verbi, aut domini Ecclesiae aut effectores salutis: sed tantum: ministri missi à Deo ut per nostram vocem crederetis. Nos quidem sonamus doctrinam caelestem quam à Deo accepimus: sed nec fidem vestris cordibus instillare, nec Spiritum sanctum vobis communicare, nec mentes & voluntates vestras ad Deum convertere possumus. Deus autem est qui fidem accendit, corda convertit, Spiritum sanctum communicat & dona sua in vobis auget. Ad Dei ergò gloriam omnia sunt referenda, & illi gratiae agendae. Sic & Ioannes Baptista inquit: Ego quidem Baptizo vos aqua: sed post me venit, qui prior me est, is vos Baptizabit Spiritu & igne. Illustria igitur discrimina quibus Iesus Christus & Apostoli vel alii sancti inter se differunt, semper sint in conspectu.

1.

Christus est Deus omnipotens & homo. Apostoli sunt homines creaturae imbecilles.

2.

Christus invocatur ab Ecclesia in omni necessitate. Apostolum invocare nefas est.

3.

Iesus Christus est sine omni peccato. Apostoli & sancti omnes sunt peccatores, in peccatis concepti & nati.

4.

Christus est mediator, redemptor, salvator, & dominus Ecclesiae. At Apostoli non sunt redemptores, sedipsimet egent redemptione, & sunt ministri Ecclesiae.

5.

Christus est efficax per verbum, illustrat mentes, convertit voluntates, flectit corda, inspirat fidem et operatur vitam et consolationem. Apostoli tantum sunt ministri verbi & sacramentorum.

6.

Christus effundit & donat Spiritum sanctum. Apostoli tantum aqua Baptizant.

7.

Christus ubique et semper adest suae Ecclesiae et singulis membris. Apostoli tantum uno in loco certo tempore aliquot membris Ecclesiae servierunt, donec cursum absolverunt.

## 3:8
He who plants and he who waters are one: but each one will receive his own reward, according to his own labor.

This is, whether someone first teaches the ignorant the Gospel of Jesus Christ: or whether someone further instructs, consoles, and admonishes those already established in the doctrine of Christ, they are ministers of the same condition and sustain the same office commended to them by Christ: Timothy or Titus is as much a saving minister of the Church as the Apostle Paul. And each one shall receive his reward for his labor. Let pious preachers fix this most ample promise in their souls. Great and difficult are the labors which pious pastors sustain in the ministry. And the world is not only ungrateful for them, but even malicious, and repays good with many evils. And in such great security of men, pastors often fear lest all their labors, and studies, and contentions, and temptations be in vain. But here Paul affirms that God, according to the norm of His justice, will render to each one a reward according to his labor. For there is no good work so small that, performed in faith and the acknowledgment of the mediator, it is not compensated with a most ample reward, both in this life and in the future. Christ being witness, Matth: 10. He who shall have given a drink of cold water to one of these least ones in my name, amen I say to you, he shall not lose his reward. The Apostle also teaches that the efficacy of the ministry does not depend upon the dignity of the ministers, but upon the efficacy of Christ, just as it is all the same from what material the king's seal is made, whether from gold or steel, it nevertheless expresses the same image in the wax: so it is all the same whether a learned man, or an unlearned man, or an Apostle, or a Deacon, or a pious man, or a hypocrite sounds the sincere word of God, and administers the sacraments to us, if only we believe in the word of Christ, without doubt it will be truly efficacious in us for salvation.

Latin:

Qui plantat & qui rigat unum sunt: Unusquisque autem propriam suam mercedem accipiet, iuxta proprium suum laborem.

Hoc est, sive quis primum ignaros doceat Evangelion Iesu Christi: Sive quis institutos in doctrina Christi amplius erudiat, consoletur & admoneat, eiusdem conditionis sunt ministri & idem munus sustinent à Christo ipsis commendatum: tàm Timotheus, vel Titus est salutaris Eccle: minister, quàm Apost; Paulus. Et unusquisque suam accipiet pro labore suo mercedem. Hanc amplissimam promissionem infigant animis pii concionatores. Magni & difficiles sunt labores quos sustinent pii pastores in ministerio. Et mundus pro iis non solum est ingratus, sed etiam maleficus, & bonum rependit multis malis. Et in tanta hominum securitate metuunt saepe pastores, ne omnes illorum & labores & studia, & contentiones, & tentationes sint inanes. Sed hic adfirmat Paulus Deum secundum normam suae iustitiae unicuique iuxta suum laborem redditurum mercedem. Nullum est enim bonum opus tam exiguum quod praestitum in fide & agnitione mediatoris non compensetur amplissima mercede cum in hac, tum in futura vita. Teste Christo, Matth: 10. Qui dederit potum aquae frigidae uni ex minimis his in nomine meo, amen dico vobis non amittet mercedem suam. Docet etiam Apostolus ministerii efficaciam non pendere à dignitate ministrorum, sed ab efficacia Christi, sicuti perinde est ex qua materia factum sit sigillum regis, ex auro, vel Chalibe, eandem tamen exprimit imaginem in cera: ita perinde est sive doctus, sive indoctus, sive Apostolus, sive Diaconus, sive pius, sive hypocrita sonet syncerum Dei verbum, & sacramenta nobis administret, si modò nos verbo Christi credimus, sine dubio erit innobis verè efficax ad salutem.

## 3:9-17
For we are God's fellow workers: you are God's tillage, God's building.

He compares the gathering of the Church to tillage and building: which metaphors are most customary to the Prophets. And he urges that the Apostles and other teachers of the Church are nothing but ministers: but that God Himself is the Lord of the Church: that He is the effector of faith, and the teacher of salvation. We are fellow workers of God, namely by sounding the doctrine of the Gospel, and by administering the Sacraments: we scatter the seed of the word into the field of the Lord: but it is God's to grant that it may bear fruit. Therefore, one must not look to the Apostles or pastors, but always to God. The Apostle does not say that they are Synergi in conversion to God: for this is the work of the Holy Spirit alone: in which work we are a merely passive subject: but in the ministry of the word, and in the building of the house of the Lord, we are fellow workers.

According to the grace which is given to me, as a wise architect I have laid the foundation: but another builds upon it: let each one see how he builds upon it.

After he showed the distinction between God the author of the ministry, who alone is effective through the word, and the heralds of the word, so that all salvation may be attributed to God: He now warns what the distinction is between ministers: And what must be especially regarded by a minister. And because he intends to preach his Apostolic office, he begins from the commendation of the grace of God, to which he ascribes all things, lest anyone suspect him of boasting about his own wisdom or erudition. God (he says) called me by a singular counsel and immense mercy to this office, that I might be an Apostle of Jesus Christ, and that I might lay the foundations of religion, that is, that I might clearly expound the articles of faith: And as a wise Architect I laid the foundations. As in the erecting of buildings it matters a great deal that solid foundations be wisely placed: So in religion it is the first and greatest thing that the articles of faith, upon which our salvation rests, be explicitly and clearly explained and properly fortified. Therefore Paul signifies: that this was his primary concern, that the articles of faith be faithfully and perspicuously delivered in the Church. Paul was not occupied with childish declamations, he did not pursue subtle disputes, he did not burden the Churches with many ceremonies: He did not introduce new and unusual exercises of an austere life, with which things many great men were occupied more than was fitting: But he was entirely intent upon this, that he might clearly deliver the foundations of Christian doctrine. Every one of Paul's Epistles testifies to this, especially those which were written to the Romans: And to the Galatians: And to the Ephesians. In which, since the principal he explains the heads of heavenly doctrine most clearly. And in the first place, he narrates with such perspicuity the doctrine concerning the acknowledgment of the true God, concerning the two natures in Christ, concerning the office of the law, concerning the corruption of human nature, concerning the gratuitous remission of sins, concerning the benefits of the mediator, concerning good works, concerning the Church, and concerning the future judgment, that nothing can be said more lucidly. Thus, therefore, as a distinguished craftsman and wise architect, he rightly laid the foundation of the Church: for he depicted Christ crucified and resurrected before the eyes of the Church. Another builds upon it, that is, pastors, Bishops, and doctors who come after the Apostles explain the Apostolic doctrine more broadly, illustrate it with examples, repeat and inculcate it: and thus they gather the Church: but it is not permitted for them to depart from the doctrine of the Apostles: but upon the foundation laid by the Apostles the remaining structure of the Church is to be adorned. This is, the articles of faith, which the Apostles handed down to us, are to be retained.

From this place, therefore, must first be learned the sublime authority of the Apostolic vocation: and how great a difference there is between an Apostle and another, whether a Bishop or a doctor in the Church. The Apostle has this duty, that he may lay the foundations of religion: that is, that he may hand down the articles of faith, that he may teach who God is: what kind of person Christ is: why the son was sent by the father: why the law was promulgated: for what purpose it was again abrogated: that he might testify concerning the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ: that he might announce the remission of sins to all believing in Christ; and might clearly expound all the articles of faith. For he was called immediately by Christ, adorned with the visible gift of the Holy Spirit, and instructed with the gift of performing miracles, so that it may be certain that he does not err in the faith. Other Evangelists, pastors, bishops, presbyters, however much they may excel in gifts, are nevertheless inferior to the Apostles in vocation: For they do not lay new foundations of religion, but are bound to the articles handed down by the Apostles: they ought to build upon it, that is, to repeat, sound forth, inculcate, illustrate, and assiduously urge this very doctrine of the Prophets and Apostles, and according to it gather the Church. A distinction must also be observed here between the dogmas of the Church. For some pertain to the foundation: as are all the articles of faith, which are learnedly comprised in the Apostolic symbol, in the doctrine of the decalogue and of the sacraments. He who departs from this foundation does not build the Church of Christ, but constructs houses for idols. Other dogmas are built upon the foundation. In these, one proposes things more useful, better, and firmer than another: Here, if anyone hallucinates or errs, provided he does not depart from the foundation, he does not on that account fall from grace, nor is he removed from the society of the Church.

Victor of Rome: while he too austerely urges the celebration of the day of Easter, he indeed errs, but because he does not depart from the foundation, this infirmity is pardoned in him.

For no other foundation can anyone lay, besides that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

The universal salvation of the human race consists in our Lord Jesus Christ, whom God has set forth as a propitiation in his blood through faith: Ro: 3. To him all the prophets bear witness that all who believe in him receive remission of sins in his name, Act: 10. For thus it pleased God through this only-begotten son to reconcile things which are in heaven and which are on earth. Nor is there salvation in any other, nor is there any other name given to men under heaven, in which we must be saved. This foundation, therefore, must be retained. When, however, he names Jesus Christ, he embraces the whole doctrine of the Church concerning the acknowledgment of the true God, concerning the person and office of the Mediator, the law and the Gospel. Those who depart from this foundation have nothing in common with the Church of Christ which is the house of God. Mahomet attempts to overturn this foundation entirely: For he denies that Jesus Christ is the eternal God: He denies that he is the savior of the world. Therefore he does not build, but destroys the Church. The Roman Pontiffs deny that righteousness and salvation come to us through the blood of Jesus Christ alone: And they contend that they merit eternal life by their works. Therefore they depart from the foundation, and show themselves to be enemies of the Church. The Calvinists remove the body and blood of Jesus Christ from the holy supper, and pervert the testament of the son of God. Therefore they attempt to undermine the foundation, and by this very fact they declare themselves to be aliens from the society of the true Church. Thus in all controversies of religion it must be seen whether anyone faithfully retains or casts away the foundation of our salvation. Arius, Photinus, Samosatenus, Macedonius, Nestorius, Eutyches, Montanus, Origen, Pelagius, the Monks, and those similar to them overturned the foundation of religion: Therefore by the right judgment of the Church they were condemned. Now Matthias Flacius Illyricus overturns the foundation of faith: Because he pertinaciously asserts that original sin is a substance: That original sin is from God; that Satan is the creator of the old man.

Si quis but if anyone builds upon this foundation, gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble: the work of each one will become manifest. For the day will reveal it, when it will be revealed in fire. For what sort of work each one's is, the fire will prove. If any man's work abide, which he hath built thereupon: he shall receive a reward: if any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved, yet so as by fire.

This passage of Paul is variously explained by interpreters: for some explain it concerning works, others concerning hearers, others concerning doctrine. And indeed, since the whole discourse is figurative, it can be explained in various ways: but it must be seen to it that the exposition is analogous to the faith. Papist writers who interpret gold and silver as the works of monks, alms, prayers, and vows of chastity: but hay, stubble, and wood as economic and civil works, and then from this attempt to construct purgatorial fire, depart from the analogy of the faith: therefore they are not to be heard.

Johannes Brentius explains it concerning hearers in this way. There is one foundation; all ministers are bound to preach Christ and the incorrupt doctrine of the Gospel: but another builds upon it gold, silver, gems: That is, he has hearers who are pious, faithful, constant, and diligent in the study of good works: who in the very heat of persecution persist in the confession of the truth. The work of these abides, and these receive an ample reward. But other ministers, although they teach Christ purely, do not nevertheless obtain among their hearers that they cultivate true piety; these build wood, stubble, and hay upon the foundation: for these hearers fail from the truth in the time of persecution and are consumed. These, therefore, suffer loss in their hearers: yet they themselves are saved through the fire of various tribulations. Since this exposition is analogous to the faith, it is not to be rejected. But another interpretation is much more elegant and agrees more with the text, which is of this kind.

For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ, This is, whoever performs the ministry of teaching in the Church, must always look to this goal, that he may set forth Jesus Christ with all his benefits and his whole kingdom to his hearers, that he may clearly hand down all the articles of faith, that he may not corrupt nor tear down the articles in which our salvation consists: if anyone denies either the divinity or the human nature of Christ or appoints other mediators, he attempts to lay another foundation. Therefore he does not build a temple for God: but he prepares a den of thieves for his idol. Origen departed from the foundation, because he corrupted the doctrine of the law and the Gospel, he taught men to be righteous by works: he asserted free will: he denied the resurrection of the flesh.

Nestorius and Eutyches departed from the foundation because the former tore apart the natures in Christ: the latter indeed confounded them. Therefore they taught a different Christ than the holy scriptures set forth to us. Thus Pelagius: Thus the Roman pontiffs, the Monks, and the Anabaptists depart from the foundation, while they corrupt the principal articles of faith. Athanasius, however, Augustine, Ambrose, and Luther retain the foundation. For they rightly preach Jesus Christ as the savior of the world.

If anyone, he says, builds upon this foundation: that is, upon the saving doctrine concerning Jesus Christ, handed down by the Apostles, he builds gold, silver, precious stones: wood, hay, stubble: the work of each one will be made manifest. The doctrine which is built upon the foundation is not to be understood as concerning the inventions of men: as if it were permitted to any teacher to bring his own dreams into the Church: but as the explanations of the Prophetic and Apostolic sermons: admonitions, exhortations, counsels, exercises, the administration of the sacraments, and whatever pertains to the ministry. In these, however, there are great differences, just as the gifts of the Holy Spirit are most diverse. Athanasius builds gold and silver upon the foundation, while he constantly defends, and demonstrates from the testimonies of scripture, that the son of God is eternal and almighty God: when he urges the doctrine concerning the incarnation of the son, and faithfully expounds scripture. Jerome, however, while he so extols Virginity that he heaps insult upon marriage: and condemns second nuptials, he too much extols monasticism, hay and stubble he built upon the foundation: Which did not bear the fire of temptation, but were consumed. Thus also Augustine has his own stubble and wood: In that he denies that the Baptism of John conferred the remission of sins: In that he often confuses renewal with justification: In Cyprian, Jerome, and others, much stubble occurs. And so, ecclesiastical writers must be read with judgment. For it is of great prudence, as Jerome says, to gather gold in the mud.

The day, says Paul, will declare what each one's work is like, because it is revealed by fire. Senseless Papists have twisted this passage to their own figment about purgatorial fire, when the mind of Paul is far different. The whole fabrication about purgatorial fire is overturned by the saying of Christ: He who believes in the Son is not judged: But he who does not believe is already judged. John 3. Rightly, therefore, Cyprian: When one has departed from here, there is no place for repentance. Here life is either lost or held. Paul, therefore, speaks of the fire of persecution and temptation, and looks back at the saying Psalm 12. The words of the Lord are pure words: Silver examined by fire, purified seven times in an earthen vessel. And this is the mind of the Apostle. Saving and necessary doctrine, which is built up from the firm testimonies of the Prophets and Apostles, is similar to gold and silver, which is not consumed, but endures in the fire, and subsequently appears purer and brighter. For the saving doctrine endures in every persecution and temptation, it provides firm consolations, nor can it be overwhelmed or destroyed by the deceits of Satan. But doctrine invented by human ingenuity concerning arduous exercises, ceremonies, vows, and similar things, does not endure in the fire of persecution but, like wood, hay, and stubble, burns up. For it does not stand against the deceits of Satan: but vanishes. This in persecution raises up the heart or provides joy. Bernard lived most harshly and kept the laws of the monastery most strictly: But he has nothing of consolation from this, in the agony of death, the fire of temptation and the magnitude of the wrath of God consumes all those stubbles. Therefore he cries out: I have lived lost: All my righteousnesses are as a menstruous cloth. And he is compelled to turn himself to the foundation: Just as he confesses that Christ possesses the kingdom by a double right. In this way the fire tests the excellence and firmness of doctrines.

If any man's work abide (he says) he shall receive a reward. This is, if anyone has handed down useful and necessary doctrine to the Church, has diligently exhorted all to repentance, has illustrated the articles of faith, has diligently refuted errors, he shall receive an ample reward. The work of Athanasius and Augustine which they built upon the foundation, remains to this very day, and will remain hereafter. Rightly did both illustrate the principal articles of faith. Athanasius: piously and constantly refuted both the Arians, and the Macedonians: and the Apollinarists. Augustine illustrated the doctrine concerning original sin, refuted Pelagius and the Celestians, and the Donatists, and instructed the Church with useful writings; thus also Luther purged the Church, explained Scripture, translated the Bibles, refuted very many sects, restored true worship, and revealed the Antichrist, the son of perdition. This work remains perpetually in the Church: He shall therefore receive a most ample reward. For those who instruct others unto righteousness shall shine like the sun. Dan: 12.

If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss, but he himself shall be saved. These things are not to be understood concerning impious teachers or heretics, who corrupt the foundation and depart from the articles of faith: For to these remains no hope of salvation: Since there is no salvation in any other than in our Lord Jesus Christ. But they are to be understood concerning those who, while they teach rightly concerning Christ and retain the foundation of faith, nevertheless mix in certain things which do not subsist in the fire of persecutions, as Gregory and Bernard indeed retain the foundation, that the passion of Christ is our righteousness: But they mix in much hay and stubble, as concerning monastic vows, fasts of God, the sacrifice of the mass, prayer for the dead, the invocation of saints, and the merit of good works: Which stubble in the agony of death and great dangers is undoubtedly consumed.

Bernard in the temptation of conscience at last discovers that all confidence which is placed in the merit of works is vain: whence he cries out, it suffices for merit to know that merit does not suffice. I do not want a merit that excludes grace. With these straws consumed, he indeed suffers loss: For all labor which was spent in delivering such doctrines of men perishes. Yet he himself shall be saved: Namely, if he retains the foundation and does not allow himself to be torn away from it.

Yet so (he says) as through fire: He does not speak of purgatorial fire, nor of natural fire, but metaphorically of persecution, temptation, and the testing of faith. For through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God: The very temptation and testing shows who retains the foundation by true faith. Cyprian, rebaptizing, built straw upon the foundation, which in time was consumed and refuted by Augustine: Yet he himself, undergoing death for the name of Christ, retained the foundation: therefore, through the fire of tribulations he was saved. Paul here clearly shows the distinction between heresy and error: For those who depart from the foundation he condemns as heretics, according to the saying, if anyone has taught another Gospel than I have taught, let him be ἀνάθημα. Gal: 1: Therefore, this is a heretic, who overturns the foundation. For heresy is a mortal sin, as is evident from 5. Chapter: to the Galatians: But he who errs or is hallucinating in something, and yet retains the foundation, nor does he obstinately defend his opinion against the manifest authority of scripture, he is not immediately to be called a heretic; for many infirmities and ignorances cling even to the saints. The Apostle Peter, having received the Holy Spirit, did not know that it was permitted for him to associate with the Gentiles, and that nothing was common: Yet he did not depart from the foundation. Augustine errs in that he says that concupiscence or original sin remaining in the saints after Baptism is not truly sin. He errs also in that he says that the Baptism of John did not confer the remission of sins: He errs in that he says that infants are saved not by their own faith, but by the faith of another, namely of their parents and of the Church: But yet he did not depart from the foundation. Therefore, error in the reborn and believers is a venial sin. That he adds that the faithful are saved through fire: He warns that the heart must be prepared for various temptations and afflictions, and that the solid foundations of faith must be sought, upon which we may safely lean in every kind of persecution and temptation. For thus God has ordained that it behooves us all to be made conformable to the image of the Son of God. Therefore, heavenly doctrine is not to be looked upon only drowsily, nor is any doctrine to be embraced without examination. But the solid and perpetual truth, which can bear the fire of temptations, is to be learned with great zeal.

Do you not know that you are the temple of God you are: and the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him. For the temple of God is holy, which you are.

By an argument taken from the excellent dignity of the saints, and the authority of the Holy Spirit, and the horrible divine punishment, he dissuades the Corinthians from disturbing the Church of God with empty boasting of wisdom or gifts, or with any contention, but rather that they should cherish, console, edify, and promote the Church with true humility and sincere zeal for concord. The sacrosanct temple of the most high God ought not to be destroyed, disturbed, nor profaned, but built up and kept holy. Even idolatrous nations and those ignorant of God thought the temples of their idols were to be religiously cultivated: and they judged that despoilers of temples were punished by the divine: but the Jews, by the command of God, defended the Jerusalem temple with great zeal, and did not suffer it to be polluted. It was not even permitted for an uncircumcised Gentile to enter the temple. With much greater religion must the spiritual temple of God be cultivated, in which God himself dwells. For he does not dwell in a temple made by hands. But you, holy and elect, are the temple of the most high God. For he said: I will dwell in you. Therefore, it is a grave sacrilege for this sacrosanct temple to be disturbed by pride or to disturb with contentions, or to pollute. For the temple is corrupted and destroyed by contentions: because minds are torn apart from one another by dissensions, an occasion is provided for new dogmas, and the weak are scandalized so that they return to their former errors.

The Holy Spirit, he says, dwells in you. This is a most evident argument of the most ardent love of God toward us, that He pours out of His Spirit through the Son into our hearts, so that He may most closely join us to Himself, dwell in us, impart justice and eternal life to us, and kindle in us motions that are in harmony with God, the fear of God, love, joy, chastity, humility, clemency, and virtues of every kind, and also make us partakers of the divine nature. The immense magnitude of this divine benefit, and the glory of the Church, cannot be explained by any human voice. Therefore, one must think reverently about all the saints: and one must take the greatest care lest we offend or grieve the Holy Spirit in the pious by contentions or vain boasting, or profane or disturb His most holy lodging. Wherever, however, the Holy Spirit dwells, there also is the eternal Father and the only-begotten Son. If anyone loves me, says Christ, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him. Ioan: 14.

And this indwelling of God differs greatly from the general presence of God, by which God is present to all creatures. For by His general presence God indeed sustains creatures, and preserves them for judgment. But He does not impart to them righteousness and life; however, indwelling signifies that God through the Holy Spirit occupies the hearts of men, and purges them from sin, frees them from death and the power of Satan: and imparts to them life, righteousness, joy, and eternal blessedness. Therefore, let us celebrate this immense benefit of God with a grateful heart, and let us take care with zeal lest by security, or by sins against conscience, we drive away such a guest from us.

If anyone, he says, destroys the temple of God: God will destroy him. He adds most grave threats here, so that he may move us all the more vehemently, that we may take care for ourselves against scandals and contentions disturbing the Church. If anyone violates with his crime the hall of some great prince or emperor, he is afflicted with a most grave punishment. Thus let him know that he will pay most grave penalties to God, who has violated the most sacred temple of the eternal God. Men only kill the body, they cannot kill the soul. But God, when He has decreed to destroy a man, casts body and soul into eternal fire. This most grave of all punishments ought to move all the pious lest anyone disturb the Church.

Let no one deceive himself. If anyone

Latin:

Dei enim sumus cooperatores: Dei agricolatio, Dei aedificatio estis.

Collectionem Ecclesiae confert agriculturae & aedificationi: Quae metaphorae Prophetis sunt usitatissimae. Et urget Apostolos & alios Ecclesiae doctores nihil esse praeterque ministros: Ipsum autem Deum esse Dominum Ecclesiae: Ipsum esse effectorem fidei, & doctorem salutis. Cooperatores Dei sumus, scilicet sonando doctrinam Evangelii, & administrando Sacramenta: Semen verbi nos spargimus in agrum domini: Sed Dei est dare ut fructum ferat. Non ergò ad Apostolos seu pastores, sed ad Deum semper est respiciendum. Non dicit Apostolus quòd sint Synergi in conversione ad Deum: Nam hoc est solius Spiritus sancti opus: In quo opere nos sumus subiectum merè patiens: sed in ministerio verbi, & in aedificatione domus domini sumus cooperatores.

Secundum gratiam quae data est mihi tanquam sapiens architectus fundamentum posui: Alius autem super aedificat: Videat unusquisque quomodo super aedificet.

Postquam discrimen monstravit inter Deum authorem ministerii, qui solus est efficax per verbum & inter praecones verbi, ut omnis salus Deo feratur accepta: Monet nunc quod sit discrimen inter ministros: Et quid ministro praecipuè spectanctandum sit. Ac quia munus suum Apostolicum praedicare instituit, à commendatione gratiae Dei, cui omnia adscribit, orditur, ne quis suspicetur eum de sua sapientia vel eruditione gloriari. Deus (inquit) me singulari consilio & immensa misericordia ad hoc munus vocavit, ut Apostolus essem Iesu Christi, & fundamenta religionis ponerem, hoc est, articulos fidei dilucidè exponerem: Et ut sapiens Architectus fundamenta ieci. Ut in aedificiis extruendis plurimum refert solida fundamenta sapienter collocari: Ita in religione primum & maximum est articulos fidei, quibus innititur nostra salus, disertè atque dilucidè explicari et probe muniri. Significat ergò Paul: sibi hoc in primis curae fuisse, ut articuli fidei fideliter & perspicuè in Ecclesia traderentur. Non fuit Paulus occupatus puerilibus declamationibus, non sectatus est argutas disputationes, non oneravit Ecclesias ceremoniis multis: Non introduxit nova & inusitata exercitia austerae vitae, quibus rebus multi magni viri occupati fuerunt plus quàm par fuit: Sed totus in hoc incubuit ut fundamenta doctrinae Christianae perspicuè traderet. Testantur id singulae Pauli Epistolae, in primis illae, quae ad Ro: Et Gal: Et ad Ephesios scriptae sunt. In quibus cum praecipua capita doctrinae caelestis clarissimè exponit. Et in primis doctrinam de agnitione veri Dei, de duabus naturis in Christo, de officio legis, de corruptione humanae naturae, de gratuit a remissione peccatorum, de beneficiis mediatoris, de bonis operibus, de Ecclesia, de iudicio futuro tanta perspicuitate enarrat, ut nihil dici possit dilucidius. Sic ergò ut insignis artifex & sapiens architectus rectè collocavit fundamentum Ecclesiae: Christum enim crucifixum & resuscitatum depinxit Ecclesiae ob oculos. Alius super aedificat, hoc est, pasiores, Episcopi & doctores qui veniunt post Apostolos latius exponunt Apostolicam doctrinam, illustrant eam exemplis, repetunt & in culcant eam: & sic colligunt Ecclesiam: sed non licet illis discedere à doctrina Apostolorum: sed super fundamentum ab Apostolis positum reliqua Ecclesiae structura adornanda est. Hoc est, articuli fidei, quos nobis Apostoli tradiderunt, retinendi sunt.

Ex hoc ergò loco primum discenda est sublimis authoritas Apostolicae vocationis: & quantum discrimen sit inter Apostolum & alium, vel Episcopum, vel doctorem in Ecclesia. Apostolus hoc munus habet ut fundamenta religionis iaciat: hoc est, fidei articulos tradat, ut doceat quis sit Deus: qualis persona sit Christus: quare filius missus sit à patre: quare lex promulgata sit: quo consilio rursus abrogata sit: ut testetur de morte & resurrectione Iesu Christi: ut annunciet remissionem peccatorum omnibus in Christum credentibus; & omnes articulos fidei dilucidè exponat. Idcirco enim immediatè à Christo vocatus, visibili donatione Spiritus sancti ornatus, & dono edendi miracula instructus est, ut constet eum in fide non errare. Alii Evangelistae, pastores, episcopi, presbyteri, quantumvis excellant donis, tamen inferiores sunt Apostolis vocatione: Non enim collocant nova fundamenta religionis, sed alligati sunt ad articulos ab Apostolis traditos: super aedificare debent, hoc est, hanc ipsam doctrinam Prophetarum & Apostolorum repetere, sonare, inculcare, illustrare, adsiduè urgere & iuxta illam Ecclesiam colligere. Discrimen etiam hic observandum est inter dogmata Ecclesiae. Alia enim ad fundamentum pertinent: ut sunt omnes articuli fidei, qui in symbolo Apostolico eruditè compraehensi sunt, In doctrina decalogi & sacramentorum. Ab hoc fundamento qui discedit, non aedificat Christi Ecclesiam, sed idolis extruit aedes. Alia dogmata supra fundamentum construuntur. In his alius alio utiliora, meliora, firmiora proponit: Hîc si quis hallucinetur vel erret, modo non discedat à fundamento non propterea excidit gratia, nec removetur à societate Ecclesiae.

Victor Roma: dum nimis austerè urget celebrationem diei pascatos, errat quidem, sed quia non discedit à fundamento, condonatur illi haec infirmitas.

Fundamentum enim aliud nemo potest ponere, praeter id quod positum est, qui est Iesus Christus.

Universa salus generis humani consistit in domino nostro Iesu Christo, quem proposuit Deus propiciatorium in sanguine ipsius per fidem: Ro: 3. Huic omnes Prophetae testimonium perhibent accipere remissionem peccatorum in nomine ipsius, omnes qui credunt in ipsum, Act: 10. Sic enim placuit Deo per hunc unigenitum filium reconciliare quae in coelis & quae in terris sunt. Neque est in alio salus, nec aliud nomen datum hominibus sub coelo, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri. Hoc ergò fundamentum retineri necesse est. Cum autem Iesum Christum nominat, complectitur totam Ecclesiae doctrinam de agnitione veri Dei, de persona & officio Mediatoris, legem & Evangelion. Ab hoc fundamento qui recedunt nihil commune habent cum Ecclesia Christi quae est domus Dei. Mahometh prorsus evertere conatur hoc fundamentum: Negat enim Iesum Christum esse aeternum Deum: Negat eum esse salvatorem mundi. Non ergò aedificat, sed destruit Ecclesiam. Pontifices Romani negant per solum sanguinem Iesu Christi nobis contingere iustitiam & salutem: Et contendunt se operibus mereri vitam aeternam. A fundamento igitur recedunt, & ostendunt se esse hostes Ecclesiae. Calvinistae corpus & sanguinem Iesu Christi removent è sacra coena, & pervertunt testamentum filii Dei. Fundamentum igitur subruere conantur, & hoc ipso declarant se alienos esse à societate verae Ecclesiae. Sic in omnibus controversiis religionis videndum est, num quis fideliter retineat vel abiiciat fundamentum nostrae salutis. Arrius, Photinus, Samosatenus, Macedonius, Nestorius, Eutyches, Montanus, Origenes, Pelagius, Monachi, et horum similes fundamentum religionis everterunt: Recto ergò iudicio Eccle: damnati sunt. Nunc Matthias Flacius Illyricus evertit fundamentum fidei: Quia pertinaciter adserit peccatum originis esse substantiam: Peccatum originis esse à Deo; Satanam esse conditorem veteris hominis.

Si quis verò supra hoc fundamentum aedificat, aurum, argentum, lapides preciosos, Ligna, faenum, stipulas: uniuscuiusque opus manifestum fiet. Dies enim revelabit, quando in igne revelabitur. Quale enim cuiusque opus sit, ignis probabit. Si cuius opus manet, quod superaedificavit: mercedem accipiet: si cuius opus exustum fuerit, damnum patietur: ipse verò salvus fiet, sed sic tanquam per ignem.

Hic Pauli locus ab interpretibus variè exponitur: alii enim de operibus: alii de auditoribus, alii de doctrina exponunt. Et quidem cum tota oratio figurata sit, varie potest exponi: sed videndum est ut expositio sit analoga fidei. Pontificii scriptores qui aurum & argentum interpretantur opera monachorum, eleemosynas, precationes, & vota castitatis: foenum verò stipulas & ligna opera Oeconomica & civilia, & deinde hinc ignem purgatorium extruere conantur ab analogia fidei recedunt: Ideò audiendi non sunt.

Ioannes Brentius de auditoribus exponit hoc modo. Unum est fundamentum omnes ministri tenentur praedicare Christum & incorruptam Evangelii doctrinam: sedalius super aedificat aurum, argentum, gemmas: Id est, habet pios, fideles, constantes & in studio bonorum operum diligentes auditores: qui in ipso persecutionis ardore persistunt in confessione veritatis. Horum opus manet, et hi accipiunt amplam mercedem. Verum alii ministri licet purè doceant Christum, non tamen apud auditores suos obtinent ut veram pietatem colant, hi lignum, stipulam, et foenum aedificant super fundamentum: nam hi auditores tempore persecutionis deficiunt à veritate & consumuntur. Hi ergò in suis auditoribus damnum accipiunt: ipsi tamen salvi fiunt per ignem variarum tribulationum. Haec ex positio cum sit analoga fidei, reiicienda non est. Verum alia interpretatio est multò concinnior & magis congruit textui, quae est huiusmodi.

Fundamentum aliud poni non potest, praeter id quod positum est, quod est Iesus Christus, Hoc est, quis quis fungitur in Ecclesia ministerio docendi, in hunc scopum semper respicere debet ut Iesum Christum cum omnibus suis beneficiis & toto regno auditoribus suis proponat, omnes articulos fidei dilucide tradat, non corrumpat nec convellat articulos in quibus nostra salus consistit: si quis vel divinitatem vel humanam naturam Christi negat velalios constituit mediatores, is aliud conatur ponere fundamentum. Ideò non aedificat templum Deo: sed latronum speluncam parat idolo suo. Origenes recessit à fundamento, quia corrupit doctrinam legis et Evangelii, docuit homines operibus iustos esse: adseruit liberum arbitrium: negavit carnis resurrectionem.

Nestorius & Eutyches discesserunt à fundamento quia ille divulsit in Christo naturas: hic verò confudit eas. Alium ergò Christum docuerunt, quàm sacrae scripturae nobis proponunt. Sic Pelagius: Sic Romani pontifices, Monachi, Anabaptistae recedunt à fundamento, dum articulos fidei praecipuos corrumpunt. Athanasius verò, Augustinus, Ambrosius, Lutherus, retinent fundamentum. Rectè enim praedicant Iesum Christum mundi salvatorem.

Si quis, inquit, super hoc fundamento: hoc est, super salutari doctrina de Iesu Christo, ab Apostolis tradita aedificat aurum, argentum, lapides praeciosos: ligna, foenum, stipulam: uniuscuiusque opus manifestum fiet. Doctrina quae super fundamento aedificatur non intelligenda est de commentis hominum: quasi liceat cuivis doctori sua adferre somnia in Ecclesiam: sed explicationes Propheticarum & Apostolorum concionum: commonefactiones, adhortationes, consilia, exercitia, sacramentorum administratio & quaecunque ad ministerium pertinent. In his verò magnae sunt dissimilitudines, ut dona Spiritus sancti sunt diversissima. Athanasius aurum & argentum aedificat super fundamentum, dum constanter defendit, & ex testimoniis scripturae demonstrat filium Dei esse aeternum & omnipotentem Deum: Cum urget doctrinam de incarnatione filii, & fideliter enarrat scripturam. Hieronymus verò dum ita extollit Virginitatem ut contumelia adficiat coniugium: & damnat secundas nuptias, nimium extollit monasticen, foenum & stipulas aedificavit super fundamento: Quae ignem tentationis non tulerunt, sed consumpta sunt. Sic & Augustinus habet suas stipulas & ligna: Ut quòd negat Baptismum Iohan: non contulisse peccatorum remissionem: Quòd renovationem saepe; cum iustificatione confundit: In Cypriano, Hieronymo, & aliis stipulae multae occurrunt. Itaque cum iudicio legendi sunt scriptores Ecclesiastici. Grandis enim prudentiae est, ut Hieronymus inquit, aurum in luto legere.

Dies, inquit Paulus, viniuscuisque opus quale sit declarabit, quia per ignem revelatur. Hunc locum insulsi Papistae ad figmentum suum de purgatorio igne contorserunt cum longè alia sit mens Pauli. Totum commentum de purgatorio igne evertit Christi dictum: Qui credit in filium non iudicatur: Qui verò non credit iam iudicatus est. Ioan: 3. Rectè ergò Cypria: Quando isthinc excessum est, poenitentiae nullus est locus. Hic vita velamittitur veltenetur. Paulus ergò de igne persecutionis & tentationis loquitur, & respicit addictum Psal: 12. Eloquia domini eloquia munda: Argentum igne examinatum in vase testaceo purgatum septies. Estque haec Apostoli mens. Doctrina salutaris & necessaria, quae ex firmis testimoniis Prophetarum & Apostolorum extruitur, similis est auro & argento, quod non ab sumitur, sed; durat in igne, & subinde purius & nitidius apparet. Perdurat enim doctrina salutaris in omni persecutione & tentatione, praebet firmas consolationes, nec potest obrui aut deleri praestigiis Sathanae. Sed doctrina ab ingenio humano inventa de arduis exercitiis, ceremoniis, votis, & similibus rebus, non perdurat in igne per secutionis sed veluti lignum, foenum & stipula conflagrat. Non enim consistit contra praestigias Sathanae: sed evanescit. Haec in persecutione erigit cor aut praebet laeticiam. Bernhardus vixit durissime & leges monasterii servavit strictissime: Sed nihil hinc habet consolationis, in agone mortis, ignis tentationis & magnitudo irae Dei omnes illas stipulas consumit. Clamitat igitur: perdite vixi: Omnes iustitiae meae tanquam pannus menstruatae. Ac convertere se cogitur ad fundamentum: Sicuti fatetur Christum duplici iure possidere regnum. Hoc modo ignis probat doctrinarum praestantiam & firmitatem.

Si cuius opus manet (inquit) mercedem accipiet. Hoc est si quis utilem & necessariam doctrinam tradiderit Ecclesiae, sedulo omnes ad paenitentiam fuerit hortatus, articulos fidei illustrarit, errores diligenter confutarit amplam accipiet mercedem. Athanasii et Augustini opus quod aedificarunt super fundamento, manet in hunc usque diem, et deinceps manebit. Rectè uterque illustravit praecipuos fidei articulos. Athana: piè & constanter refutavit cum Arrianos, tùm Macedoni: tum Apollinaristas. Augustinus illustravit doctrinam de peccato Originis refutavit Pelagium & caelestium, & Donatistas, & utilibus scriptis erudivit Ecclesiam, sic & Lutherus repurgavit Ecclesiam, explicavit scripturam, Vertit Biblia, refutavit plurimas sectas, restituit verum cultum, revelavit Antichristum filium perditionis. Hoc opus manet perpetuò in Ecclesia: Accipiet igitur mercedem amplissimam. Qui enim alios erudiunt ad iustitiam fulgebunt sicuti sol. Dan: 12.

Si cuius opus consumetur damnum accipiet, ipse autem salvabitur. Haec non de impiis doctoribus vel haereticis intelligenda sunt, qui fundamentum corrumpunt & ab articulis fidei discedunt: His enim nulla restat salutis spes: Cum non sit in alio salus quam in domino nostro Iesu Christo. Sed de iis accipienda sunt qui cum recte de Christo docent & fundamentum fidei retinent, admiscent tamen quaedam quae in igne persecutionum non subsistunt, ut Gregorius & Bernhardus fundamentum quidem retinent, quod passio Christi nostra sit iustitia: Sed plurimum foeni, & stipularum admiscent, ut de votis monasticis, Dei ieuniis, de missarum sacrificio, de precatione pro mortuis, de invocatione sanctorum, de meritò bonorum operum: Quae stipulae in agone mortis & magnis periculis haud dubiè sunt consumptae.

Bernhardus in tentatione conscientiae tandem depraehendit vanam esse omnem fiduciam, quae in merito operum collocatur: unde clamitat sufficit ad meritum scire quod non sufficiat meritum. Nolo meritum quod gratiam excludat. His stipulis consumptis ipse quidem damnum accipit: Perit enim omnis labor qui insumptus est tradendis huiusmodi doctrinis hominum. Ipse tamen salvus fiet: Videlicet si retinet fundamentum & non patitur se ab illo divelli.

Sic tamen (inquit) tanquam per ignem: Non loquitur de igne purgatorio, neque de igne naturali, sed per metaphoram de persecutione, tentatione, probatione fidei. Per multas enim tribulationes oportet nos ingredi in regnum Dei: Ipsa tentatio & probatio ostendit quis vera fide retineat fundamentum. Cyprianus anabaptizans, stipulas aedificavit supra fundamentum, quae tempopore consumptae & ab Aug: sunt refutatae: Ipse tamen pro nomine Christi subiens mortem, retinuit fundamentum: per ignem igitur tribulationum ipse salvatus est. Paulus hic disertè ostendit discrimen inter haeresin & errorem: Eos enim qui à fundamento discedunt tanquam haereticos condemnat, iuxta dictum, si quis aliud Evangelion docuerit quàm ego docui sit ἀνάθημα.Gal: 1: Hic ergò est haereticus, qui fundamentum evertit. Haeresis enim est peccatum mortale, ut patet ex 5. Capit: ad Galat: Qui autem errat vel hallucinatur in aliquo, & tamen fundamentum retinet, nec suam opinionem contra manifestam scripturae authoritatem pertinaciter defendit, non statim est dicendus haereticus; multae enim infirmitates & ignorantiae haerent etiam in sanctis. Nescivit Petrus Apostolus accepto Spiritu sancto, licere sibi versari cum gentibus, & nihil esse commune: Non tamen discessit à fundamento. Errat Augustinus in eo, quòd dicit concupiscentiam seu peccatum Originis post Baptismum manens in sanctis non esse verè peccatum. Errat & in eo quòd dicit Ioannis Baptisma non contulisse remissionem peccatorum: Errat in eo quòd dicit infantes fide non propria, sed aliena, parentum nimirum & Ecclesiae salvatos esse: Sed tamen à fundamento non discessit. Error ergò in renatis & credentibus peccatum est veniale. Quòd addit per ignem salvari fideles: Monet praeparandum esse cor ad varias tentationes & adflictiones, & solida fidei fundamenta inquirenda esse, quibus tutò inniti possimus in omnigenere persecutionum & tentationum. Sic enim ordinavit Deus ut oporteat nos omnes fieri conformes imagini Filii Dei. Non igitur oscitanter adspicienda est tantum doctrina coelestis, nec quaevis doctrina amplectenda est sine exploratione. Sed veritas solida & perpetua, quae ignem tentationum ferre possit, magno studio est discenda.

An nescitis quòd templum Dei estis: & Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis? Si quis templum Dei corrumpit, corrumpet eum Deus. Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos.

Argumento sumpto ab excellenti dignitate sanctorum, & authoritate Spiritus sancti, atque horribili poena divina dehortatur Corinthios ne inani iactantia sapientiae vel donorum, vel ulla contentione turbent Ecclesiam Dei, sed vera humilitate, & syncero studio concordiae foveant, consolentur, aedificent, & promoveant Ecclesiam. Templum sacrosanctum altissimi Dei non debet destrui, turbari, nec prophanari, sed aedificari & sanctum custodiri. Etiam gentes Idolatrae & ignari Dei suorum Idolorum templa religiose colenda putaverunt: & iudicarunt spoliatores templorum divinitus puniri: Iudaei verò ex mandato Dei templum Hierosolymitanum magno zelo defenderunt, nec passi sunt pollui. Ne ingredi quidem licebat Ethnico non circumciso templum. Multo maiore religione colendum est spirituale Dei templum, in quo ipse Deus habitat. Non enim habitat in templo manufacto. Vos autem sancti & electi templum estis altissimi Dei. Ille enim dixit: Ego habitabo in vobis. Grave igitur sacrilegium est hoc sacrosanctum templum vel superbia, vel contentionibus turbare, vel polluere. Corrumpitur autem & destruitur templum contentionibus: quia dissidiis divelluntur à se animi, praebetur occasio, novorum dogmatum, imbecilles scandalizantur ut redeant ad pristinos errores.

Spiritus sanctus inquit habitat in vobis. Hoc evidentissimum est argumentum ardentissimi amoris Dei ergà nos, quod de Spiritu suo effundit per filium in corda nostra, ut nos arctissimè sibi copulet, in nobis habitet, iustitiam & vitam aeternam nobis impertiat, & innobis accendat motus qui congruant cum Deo, timorem Dei, dilectionem, laetitiam, castitatem, humilitatem, clementiam, & omnis generis virtutes, faciat etiam nos consortes divinae naturae. Immensa magnitudo huius beneficii divini, & gloria Ecclesiae nulla humana voce exponi potest. Reverenter igitur de omnibus sanctis sentiendum est: & summo studio cavendum ne contentionibus aut inani iactantia Spiritum sanctum in piis offendamus, aut contristemus, aut sacrosanctum eius hospicium prophanemus aut turbemus. Ubicunque autem habitat Spiritus sanctus, ibi simul est & pater aeternus, & filius unigenitus. Si quis diligit me inquit Christus sermonem meum servabit, & pater meus diliget eum, & veniemus ad eum & mansionem apud eum faciemus. Ioan: 14.

Atque haec inhabitatio Dei plurimum differt à generali Dei praesentia, qua adest Deus omnibus creaturis. Generali enim praesentia Deus sustentat quidem creaturas, easque conservat ad tudicium.
