Primùm reprehendit Paulus quòd, civiles controversias non potius inter sese placidè transigant & componant, quàm eas deferant ad Magistratum politicum, eumque alienum ab Ecclesia: Turpe est enim Christianos, qui vinculo mutuae dilectionis inter se colligati esse debebant, lites & contentiones inter sese exercere: Hinc enim gentes capiunt occasionem blasphemandi nomen Dei & Ecclesiam Christi. Deinde stultum est ad homines impios & iniustos deferre controversiae tuae cognitionem, cum pios possis habere arbitros in Ecclesia inter fratres. Nam in sanctis magna lux est verae sapientiae: Timor domini est initium sapientiae: Et sancti illuminantur per Spiritum sanctum: Et in conspectu habent verbum, quod est lucerna pedibus eorum: Est etiam verùm & non simulatum studium iustitiae, veritatis & concordiae in sanctis. At impii extra Ecclesiam variis agitantur erroribus, ut non semper videant quid iustum sit: gravissimè dixit Hilarius lib: 5. ac Tri: Nihil sanè in se habet sapientiae impietas, & Dei timor, qui sapientiae initium est, ubi deest, aufert secum omne exordium prudentiae: nec in illis existit verùm iustitiae & concordiae studium: Sed ducuntur pravis adfectibus, ardent pleonexia, & in omnibus suo lucro & honori student, & ex hominum discordia saepè voluptatem capiunt.

Magna igitur inscitia est controversias ad homines extra Ecclesiam deferre, cum pii & sancti arbitri in Ecclesia haberi possint. Sanctos vocat credentes, qui etsi habent multiplices infirmitates & peccata, tamen quia perfidem abluti sunt sanguine Iesu Christi, imputatur illis filii Dei obedientia, & sanctificati sunt Spiritu sancto, qui novos, sanctos & legi quodammodo congruentes motus in eis accendit, verè coram Deo sunt sancti cum imputatione tùm inchoatione. Impios verò extra Ecclesiam vocat iniustos: ut qui in peccatis adhuc submersi sint, & qui iniustitiae studeant. Nec verò tantum scelerati ut Harpalus, Demosthenes, Catilina, Verres, iniusti sunt, sed etiam qui studium iustitiae simularunt ut Aristides, Conon, Solon, Fabricius, Camillus, Cicero, verè iniusti fuerunt: sua enim emolumenta potius quaesiverunt, quàm Dei gloriam, & utilitatem proximi. Nec est quod veram iustitiam apud eos qui non reguntur ductu Spiritus sancti quaeramus, cum sint mancipia Satanae & impurorum adfectuum. Hanc ob causam nominat eos Paulus contemptos in Ecclesia, quasi dicat: Etsi extra Ecclesiam propter sapientiam & iustitiam aliqui Ethnici laudibus in coelum usque evehantur, ut Aristides, Socrates, Xenophon, Solon. Temistocles, Laelius, Cato: Tamen Ecclesia Dei non habet eos eo loco: Quia destituuntur luce verbi divini, & non reguntur ductu Spiritus sancti.

Adiungit Paùlus suae repraehensioni duas gravissimas rationes, à collatione maiorum. ( Sancti mundum iudicabunt, inquit) Quantò magis idonei sunt ad componendas controversias de terrenis bonis: sancti etiam angelos, immundos Spiritus iudicabunt: Cur non ergò iudicarent de corporalibus bonis controversias. Quod sancti cum Christo futuri sint iudices mundi & Satanae, patet ex dicto Christi. Matth: 19. Sedebitis super sedes iudicantes duodecim tribus Israel. Item: Ut recipiant vos in aeterna tabernacula. Item: Veniet filius hominis cum multitudine angelorum & electorum. Summus quidem mundi iudex est Christus. Sancti verò adstabunt Christo & iuxta verbum Dei damnabunt impios homines & impuros Spiritus.

Insignis igitur erit rerum vicissitudo. Nam in mundo sancti sunt omnium hominum abiectissimi, & miserrimi, qui ut homines pessimi ab impiis crudeli sententia ad omnis generis supplicia damnantur. At in extremo iudicio vicissim sancti occupabunt sedes, iudicium, & gravissima sententia ad aeternum interitum condemnabunt mundum. Decius crudeli sententia damnavit Laurentium ad ignem: At extemo iudicio Laurentius Christo iudici adstabit à latere, & feret sententiam damnationis aeternae in Deum. Hac ergò insigni consolatione confirment sese pii, praesertim cum ad tribunalia potentum trahuntur, & diris sententiis, ad mortem damnantur.

Alterum argumentum est, quòd sancti Satanam cum omnibus suis angelis iudicaturi sunt: servantur enim ad iudicium: & Christus Satanam tradet sub pedibus nostris. Multò ergò magis sancti iudicare poterint controversias de rebus terrenis & ad hanc vitam pertinentibus.

Secundò repraehendit Apostolus in Corinthiis, quòd contentionis sint studiosiores, quàm deceat Christianos. Potius Christianus iniuriam pati ac dissimulare & condonare debet, quàm cum ignominia & detrimento religionis nostrae litigare in foro & quidem coràm Magistratu seu iudice, qui adversarius est nostrae religioni. Non ergò prohibet vel improbat civilia officia Paulus, nec vetat omninò, ne causas ad legittimum Magistratum deferamus. Si enim res tuas legittimè tibi repetere licet, & commodus iudex tibi datur, non debes tuos fraudare tua negligentia, vel superstitione. Nec hominum maliciam confirmare debet nimia tua indulgentia. Sed Paulus iubet ut prudenter consideremus, quando sit necesse compellare iudicem politicum, quando non sit necesse, propter res leves non debemus vel nobis vel aliis facessere negocia. Cùm iudex est hostis tuae religionis, magna stultitia est ad eum deferre litem, ut tibi maius crees periculum. Cùm etiam tibi controversia est, non cum Epicureo vel Ethnico, sed cum fratre, qui tecum eundem profitetur Christum, religioni parcendum est, ne ea propter nostras contentiones malè audiat.

Ad erubescentiam vestram dico: Adeò non est inter vos sapiens? ne unus quidem, qui possit diiudicare inter fratrem suum & fratrem? Sed frater cum fratre litigat, & hoc coram infidelibus. Itaque iam quidem omninò defectus est in vobis, quòd lites habetis inter vos invicem. Cur non magis iniuriam patimini? Cur non potius damnum accipitis? Sed vos iniuriam facitis & damno adficitis, idque fratres.

Acriter obiurgat litigantes coram politico magistratu, quòd non potius arbitros constituant ex fratribus eiusdem religionis, ut clàm, & sine contumelia nominis Christiani controversia componatur. Inprimis autem authores iniuriarum & controversiarum graviter perstringit, & monet eos, ut abstineant ab iniuriis, & ne proximo damnum inferant, ne excidant gratia & haereditate vitae aeternae priventur: Nam iniustitia manifesta cum fide stare non potest. Potius inquit decebat vos pati iniuriam, eamque dissimulare, & Deo vindictam committere: Hoc enim poscit Christiana religio. Vos autem infertis aliis iniuriam & adficitis alios damno. Id pugnat cum 5. & 7. praeceptis. Et tantò gravius est hoc vestrum peccatum: Quòd fratres adficitis iniuria, quos omni officio iuvare debebatis. Qui enim minimum fratrem laedit, ipsum Christum laedit. Quemadmodum filius Dei testatur: Quidquid sive boni, sive mali uni ex minimis his feceritis, mihi fecistis. Nullus quidem hominum iniuria est adficiendus, sed qui fratrem laedit, gravius peccat, quàm qui in Ethnicum vel Turcam est iniurius: Licet & hic peccet.

## 6:9-10
Do you not know that the unjust will not possess the kingdom of God? Do not err, neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor those who lie with males, nor thieves, nor the covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners will inherit the kingdom of God.

This is the second part of this chapter, in which he transfers the correction from the species to the genus, and shows the final cause on account of which one must abstain not only from contentions and injury, but plainly from all crimes, namely, lest from the grace of God we may be cut off, and deprived of the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven. For it is impossible that faith, apprehending the benefits of the mediator, should shine in him who defiles himself with crimes that devastate the conscience: Faith is a consolation, says Bernard, he does not need consolation who rejoices when he has done evil, and exults in the worst things: but without faith no one can please God. Therefore, he who rushes into crimes against conscience can cherish no hope of obtaining the inheritance of eternal life. The Prophets and Apostles often repeat this sentiment, lest we deceive ourselves, and lest we imagine that we shall be partakers of the kingdom of heaven, even if we sin against conscience, as libertines impudently pretend. John says: He who commits sin is of the Devil: And Paul Rom. 8 If you live according to the flesh, you shall die: Likewise, the mind of the flesh is death. Likewise, Gal. 5 The works of the flesh are manifest, such as fornication, adultery, Idolatry, etc. Those who do such things cannot possess the Kingdom of God. Zech. 8 Do not love a lie, etc. These are the things which I hate, says the Lord. Therefore, let this most grave threat always be in sight, lest we fall into sins against conscience.

First, let the doctrine be observed here that a man defiling himself with external crimes is not a living member of the Church: Nor does he have a part in the kingdom of God. David, contaminating himself with adultery and murder, is not a son of God, but is liable to eternal damnation, thus Judas the incestuous, Joab the murderer, Achan the thief, are not living members of Christ: Next, a distinction must be observed between sins which remain in the saints and sins which cast out faith. Sins are manifold in the saints, and yet they retain faith, are pleasing to God, and are heirs of eternal life. But those who have reigning sins and live according to the flesh are not heirs of life, but are liable to eternal damnation. Therefore, the sin that is forgiven or covered in the saints and believers is original sin, and every kind of vicious affection which is born in the mind and will and heart from original sin: Furthermore, many omissions of duty, futility in speech, lapses in deliberation, sins of ignorance, impure affections, self-admiration, pride, envy, desire for gain, grief of rejection, desire for vengeance, and the like, which evils the pious deplore, resist them as much as possible with the Holy Spirit helping, and constantly seek their forgiveness from God. It is of these infirmities that it was said: For this shall every saint pray unto thee Psalm: 32. Item: If we say that we have no sin we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us. 1. Ioan: 1.

But mortal sin: It is first every original and actual sin in one not converted to God: Next, it is a lapse against conscience, when he, who had been reborn, with the Holy Spirit cast out, perfects the desires of the flesh in deed, and in external crimes falls, or when someone stubbornly defends an error which fights against the foundation of our religion, as when Macedonius denies that the Holy Spirit is eternal and almighty God. Paul is speaking here of this kind of sin.

Thirdly, it must be learned from this for what purpose one must abstain from crimes and do good works, namely, that we may not fall from the grace which we have obtained through faith, and that we may not be deprived of the inheritance of eternal life. Here the other final causes of good works may be added.

Latin:

An ignoratis quod iniusti regnum Dei non possidebunt? Ne erretis, neque scortatores, neque Idolatrae, neque adulteri, neque molles, neque qui concumbunt cum masculis, neque fures, neque avari, neque ebriosi, neque maledici, neque praedones regnum Dei haereditate capient.

Secunda est haec pars huius capitis, in qua correptionem transfert à specie adgenus, & causam finalem monstrat propter quam non solum à contentionibus & iniuria, sed planè ab omnibus sceleribus sit abstinendum, videlicet ne gratia Dei excidamus, & haereditate regni coelorum privemur. Impossibile est enim ut in eo luceat fides adpraehendens beneficia mediatoris, qui se polluit sceleribus vastantibus conscientiam: Fides solatium est, inquit Bernhardus, non eget ille solatio, qui gaudet cum malefecerit, & exultat in rebus pessimis: sine fide autem nemo Deo placere potest. Qui ergò in scelera contra conscientiam ruit, nullam spem fovere potest adipiscendi aeternae vitae hareditatem. Hanc sententiam saepè repetunt Prophetae & Apostoli, ne imponamus nobis, & ne imaginemur fore nos participes regni coelorum, etiamsi peccemus contra conscientiam, ut libertini impudenter fingunt. Ioannes inquit: Qui facit peccatum ex Diabolo est: Et Paulus Roma: 8. Si secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini: Item, sensus carnis mors est. Item, Galat: 5. Manifesta sunt opera carnis, ut scortatio, adulterium, Idolatria, &c. Qui talia faciunt, Regnum Dei possidere non possunt. Zach: 8. Mendacium ne diligatis, &c. Haec sunt quae odi, dicit dominus. Semper igitur haec gravissima comminatio sit in conspectu ne in peccata contra conscientiam labamur.

Primùm hic doctrina observetur quòd homo polluens se externis sceleribus non sit vivum Ecclesiae membrum: Nec partem habeat in regno Dei. David contaminans se adulterio & caede non est filius Dei, sed est obnoxius aeternae damnationi, sic Iudas incestus, Ioab homicida, Achan fur, non sunt viva membra Christi: Deinde discrimen observetur inter peccata, quae remanent in sanctis et peccata, quae excutiunt fidem. Multiplicia sunt in sanctis peccata, & tamen retinent fidem, placent Deo, & sunt haeredes vitae aeternae. At qui peccata habent regnantia & secundum carnem vivunt non sunt haeredes vitae, sed obnoxii sunt aeternae damnationi. Peccatum ergo remissum seu tectum est in sanctis & credentibus peccatum originis, & omnis generis viciosi adfectus, qui in mente & voluntate & corde nascuntur ex peccato originis: Praeterea multae omissiones officii, futilitas in sermone, lapsus in deliberatione, peccata ignorantiae, impuri adfectus, admiratio sui, superbia, invidia, cupiditas lucri, dolor repulsae, cupiditas vindictae, & similia, quae mala deplorant pii, repugnant iis quantum fieri potest auxiliante Spiritu sancto, & eorum veniam adsiduè à Deo petunt. De his infirmitatibus dictum est. Pro hac orabit ad te omnis sanctus Psalm: 32. Item: Si dixerimus quod peccatum non habemus decipimus nos ipsos & veritas non est in nobis. 1. Ioan: 1.

Peccatum autem mortale: Est primùm omne peccatum originale & actuale in non converso ad Deum: Deinde est lapsus contra conscientiam, cumis, qui renatus fuit, excusso Spiritu sancto cupiditates carnis opere perficit, et in externa ruit scelera, aut cùm quis errorem, qui cum fundamento nostrae religionis pugnat pertinaciter defendit, ut cum Macedonius negat Spiritum sanctum esse aeternum & omnipotentem Deum. De hoc genere peccatorum hic loquitur Paulus.

Tertiò hinc discendum est, quo fine sit abstinendum à sceleribus, & bene operandum, nimirum ne excidamus gratia, quam perfidem adepti sumus, & ne haereditate vitae aeternae privemur. Hîc caeterae causae finales bonorum operum addantur.

## 6:11
And such were some of you: But you are washed, but you are sanctified, but you are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.

By apostolic custom, Paul intersperses evangelical consolation with his castigation and severe admonition. For this is the duty of an Apostle, not only to tax sins severely according to the judgment of the law, but also to illustrate and explain the benefits of the mediator, and to show a certain remedy against sin and the terrors of the conscience. Therefore, when he had testified that those who pollute themselves with crimes would not be participants in the kingdom of Christ, and the Corinthians were conscious of such crimes in themselves, lest they should fall into desperation, he adds the consolation that they have been washed and sanctified. For the blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin. John 1.

I accept the terms of washing, sanctification, and justification here concerning the whole benefit of Christ, namely, concerning the remission of sins and renewal. For Christ washes away filth when he imputes his obedience and righteousness to us through faith: Christ also washes away our filth when through the Holy Spirit he wipes out the poison of sin from our nature and kindles righteousness in it. Thus also we are sanctified first by imputation, then by renewal and vivification, in which a new life is begun in us. I accept the term of justification here similarly for the whole benefit of Christ, namely, for the remission of sins or reconciliation with God and for the gift of the Holy Spirit. But in the Epistle to the Romans, where it is asked by what thing we please God, it is accepted specifically, namely, for the gratuitous remission of sins and the imputation of the righteousness of the mediator, and it does not include vivification. That he says in the name of the Lord Jesus, he shows that we are justified and sanctified by the merit and efficacy of Jesus Christ: that he adds in the Spirit of our God: he shows the efficient cause of our vivification, sanctification, and renewal.

Latin:

Et haec eratis aliqui: Sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed iustificati estis per nomen Domini Iesu, & in Spiritu Dei nostri.

Apostolica consuetudine inter spargit Paulus castigationi & severae admonitioni Evangelicam consolationem. Hoc enim Apostoli est munus, non solum iuxta legis sententiam severè taxare peccata, sed etiam beneficia mediatoris illustrare & exponere, & monstrare certum remedium adversus peccatum & conscientiae terrores. Cùm ergò testatus esset eos, qui se polluunt sceleribus, non fore participes regni Christi, & Corinthii sibi de eiusmodi sceleribus essent conscii, ne ruerent in desperationem, addit consolationem eos ablutos & sanctificatos esse. Sanguis enim Iesu Christi mundat nos ab omni peccato. Ioan: 1.

Vocabula ablutionis, sanctificationis, iustificationis hic de toto beneficio Christi accipio, nimirum de remissione peccatorum & renovatione. Abluit enim Christus sordes dum nobis per fidem imputat suam obedientiam & iustitiam: Eluit etiam Christus nostras sordes dum per Spiritum sanctum extergit venenum peccati ex nostra natura & in ea iustitiam accendit. Sic etiam sanctificamur primùm imputatione, deinde renovatione & vivificatione, in qua nova vita in nobis inchoatur. Vocabulum iustificationis hic similiter pro toto Christi beneficio accipio, scilicet pro remissione peccatorum seu reconciliatione cum Deo & pro donatione Spiritus sancti. Verum in Epistola ad Roma: ubi quaeritur qua re coram Deo placeamus speciatim accipitur, nimirum pro gratuita remissione peccatorum & imputatione iustitiae mediatoris, & non complectitur vivificationem. Quòd dicit in nomine domini Iesu, ostendit nos merito & efficacia Iesu Christi iustificari & sanctificari: quòd addit in Spiritu Dei nostri: Causam efficientem monstrat nostrae vivificationis, sanctificationis & renovationis.

## 6:12
All things are lawful for me: but not all things are expedient. All things are lawful for me: but I will not be brought under the power of any.

Latin:

Omnia mihi licent: sed non omnia exepdiunt. Omnia mihi licent: at ego non redigar sub ullius potestatem.

## 6:12
All things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any: This is, liberty is not to be so abused that the desires of the flesh bring us into servitude. Rather, we ought to use the Spiritual liberty which Christ has procured for us in such a way that we curb and repress the desires of the flesh, and give ourselves into servitude, that we may serve Christ and gain our neighbor. For the highest liberty is to serve Jesus Christ and his spouse the Church. Paul therefore teaches here that that is true Spiritual liberty which always dominates the desires and affections of the flesh.

Latin:

Omnia mihi licent, verum non redigar sub ullius potestatem: Hoc est, libertate non ita est abutendum, ut cupiditates carnis redigant nos in servitutem. Potius Spirituali libertate, quam Christus nobis comparavit, sic uti de bemus, ut frenemus & reprimamus carnis cupiditates, & nos in servitutem dedamus, ut Christo serviamus & proximum lucremur. Summa enim libertas est servire Iesu Christo & eius sponsae Ecclesiae. Docet ergò hîc Paulus eam veram esse Spiritualem libertatem, quae cupiditatibus & adfectibus carnis semper dominatur.

## 6:13-14
Foods are destined for the belly and the belly for foods. But God will destroy both this and those. The body, however, is not for fornication, but for the Lord: and the Lord for the body. But God both raised the Lord, and will raise us up through his power.

This is the third part of this chapter, by which he refutes the false persuasion of those who, under the pretext of Christian liberty, contended that it was permitted for them to commit fornication with impunity. And thus they reasoned, just as it is permitted for a Christian to use any food, according to the doctrine of the Apostles; for all things are clean to the clean: So also it is permitted to commit fornication with impunity, and to seek similar bodily pleasures. He refutes this impious opinion and error concerning Christian liberty, and primarily teaches that one must abstain from fornication, and he adds most weighty arguments.

All things are lawful for me: Thus, indeed, the Corinthian fornicators and those abusing liberty boasted: and they interpreted it not only concerning indifferent things as the Apostles had taught: but they even transferred it to sins. Therefore Paul restricts it. But not all things are expedient. Not only what is lawful, but also what is expedient, what contributes to the illustration of the glory of God, and the edification of the Church must be seen and considered. First concerning indifferent things and

it must be accepted that it is entirely lawful for us in indifferent matters: Then, not only what is granted to us, but what the use of the Church demands, must be attended to. It was lawful for Paul to omit the circumcision of Timothy, but it was not expedient for the Church: Therefore he circumcised him.

Latin:

Escae ventri destinatae sunt & venter escis. Deus autem & hunc & illas abolebit. Corpus verò non scortationi, sed Domino: & dominus corpori. Deus autem & dominum suscitavit, & nos suscitabit per potentiam suam.

Tertia est haec pars huius capitis, qua refellit falsam eorum persuasionem, qui praetextu libertatis Christianae contendebant licere sibi impunè scortari. Ac sic colligebant, sicut Christianò licet quovis cibo uti, secundum doctrinam Apostolorum; omnia enim sunt munda mundis: It à etiam licet impunè scortari, & similes quaerere corporis voluptates. Hanc impiam opinionem; & errorem de libertate Christiana refellit, & imprimis docet abstinendum esse à scortatione, et argumenta adiungit gravissima.

Omnia mihi licent: It à nimirum Corinthii scortatores & abutentes libertate iactitabant: & non tantum de rebus mediis interpretabantur ut Apostoli docuerant: sed etiam ad peccata transferebant. Restringit igitur Paulus. Sed non omnia expediunt. Non solum quid liceat, sed etiamquid expediat, quid faciat ad illustrationem gloriae Dei, & aedificationem Ecclesiae videndum & considerandum est. Primùm de rebus mediis &

indifferentibus est accipiendum omninò nobis licere: Deinde non solùm quid nobis concessum sit, sed quid postulet usus Ecclesiae, attendendum est. Licebat Paulo omittere circumcisionem Timothei, sed non expediebat Ecclesiae: Ergò circumcidit eum.

## 6:13
Food for the belly, and the belly for foods: it easily appears that the Corinthians argued thus from a similarity, just as it is free for us Christians to eat any kind of food, because food is destined for the belly: so what will prevent it from being lawful to commit fornication: Paul therefore refutes that impious consequence, showing that there is a huge difference. Food, he says, is owed to the belly: and the belly is destined for food. God ordained and granted that we should use food and drink in this life. Nor did he prohibit any foods. It is therefore an Adiaphoron or a middle thing, with which kind of food you wish to eat.

But God will destroy both food and the belly: This is, in the future life, we will neither eat, nor drink, but we will be as the angels. God will not destroy the members; for the very bodies themselves will rise again, and will be conformed to the glorious body of Jesus Christ. But the Lord will destroy the use of the members, which serves for the sustenance of this life.

The body, however, is not for fornication, but for the Lord: and the Lord for the body. There is a distinction, he says, between the use of food and fornication. The former God ordained and granted: the latter He most severely prohibited, commandment 6, Thou shalt not commit adultery. The body, therefore, is not destined for fornication: but it is the will of God that we possess our vessel in sanctification. The body, he says, is destined for the Lord: that is, for this reason we were created and redeemed through Christ; for this reason we are sanctified through the Holy Spirit, that our bodies might become members of the body of Christ, and be temples in which God Himself dwells. And the Lord for the body, namely, is destined. For the Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, for this reason assumed human nature and is Immanuel, that He might liberate our bodies, which were slaves of Satan, and wash them with His blood, and through the Holy Spirit endow them with life and righteousness, and most closely join us to Himself. And so, not only in this life are our bodies cherished, defended, and preserved by God, but also after this life they will be raised to eternal glory by God, who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead.

Therefore our bodies are not to be defiled by fornication, but are to be kept holy and clean, and to be surrendered to the ministry of Jesus Christ.

Do you not know that your bodies are members of Jesus Christ? Shall I therefore take away the members of Christ, and make them the members of a harlot? God forbid. Do you not know that he who is joined to a harlot, is one body? For they shall be (he says) two in one flesh. But he who is joined to the Lord, is one Spirit.

Paul adds arguments of the gravest weight to his exhortation. For the Corinthians could with difficulty be led away from their accustomed vices. And this first argument is taken from the supreme injustice and indignity of the matter. It is the height of iniquity and injustice to take away members from Jesus Christ, and to make them members of a harlot. The fornicator, who previously gave his name to Christ, tears a member away from the body of Jesus Christ: For by sinning against conscience he falls from grace, and expels the Holy Spirit: And he becomes one flesh with the harlot: Therefore he involves himself in the greatest wickedness. Paul warns by this argument that they should consider how great a glory it is to be a member of the body of Christ, which is the Church:

That our head is the omnipotent and eternal Son of God: That we are enlivened and led by the Holy Spirit, who flows down from Christ the head into all the members. We ought to value this heavenly glory and happiness highly. Then he warns how great the baseness is in fornication; since a fornicator is a member of an impure harlot, which is the dwelling place of Satan. Paul brings forward a testimony from Genesis. And they shall be two in one flesh: Which saying speaks of the most intimate and indissoluble covenant of husband and wife. But Paul transfers it thus to fornication, so that he may warn that the fornicator becomes one flesh with the harlot. And therefore this crime is to be abhorred by Christians. If anyone asks whether a husband cohabiting with his wife tears his body away from Christ, it must be answered that a Christian and faithful husband does not tear his body away from Christ even if he renders due benevolence to his wife. For marriage is honorable in all: And the cohabitation of male and female is divinely ordained. When, therefore, with a good conscience spouses apply themselves to procreating children according to God's ordinance, they do not expel the Holy Spirit, nor are they torn away from the spiritual body of Christ.

Latin:

Esca ventri, & venter escis: facilè adparet Corinthios sic argumentatos esse à simili, sicut liberum est nobis Christianis vesci quovis genere ciborum, quia esca ventriest destinata: ita quid prohibebit quò minus liceat scortari: Paulus ergòrefellit impiam illam consecutionem, monstrans ingens esse discrimen. Esca inquit debetur ventri: & venter destinatus est escae. Deus ordinavit & concessit ut cibo & potu in hac vita uteremur. Neque ullos cibos prohibuit. Est igitur Adiaphoron seu res media, quo genere cibi vesci voles.

Deus autem & escam & ventrem abolebit: Hoc est, in futura vita, nec edemus, nec bibemus, sed erimus sicuti angeli. Membra non abolebit Deus; Ipsa enim corpora nos ira resurgent, & conformabuntur glorioso corpori Iesu Christi. Usum autem membrorum, qui servit huius vita sustentationi, abolebit dominus.

Corpus autem non scortationi, sed domino: & dominus corpori. Discrimen est, inquit, inter usum cibi, & scortationem. Illum ordinavit & concessit Deus: Hanc severissimè prohibuit, praecept: 6, Non maechaberis. Corpus ergò non est destinatum scortationi: Sed voluntas Dei est, ut vas nostrum in sanctificatione possideamus. Corpus, inquit, Domino est destinatum: hoc est, ideò conditi & per Christum redempti sumus; ideò per Spiritum sanctum sanctificamur, ut corpora nostra fiant membra corporis Christi, & sint templa in quibus ipse Deus habitet. Et Dominus corpori, scilicet destinatus est. Nam filius Dei dominus noster Iesus Christus idcircò adsumpsit humanam naturam et est Immanuel, ut corpora nostra, quae erant mancipia Satanae, liberaret, & suo sanguine ablueret, & per Spiritum sanctum vita & iustitia donaret, & nos sibi arctissimè copularet. Itaque non tantum in hac vita corpora nostra foventur, defenduntur et servantur à Deo, sed etiam post hanc vitam suscitabuntur ad aeternam gloriamà Deo, qui dominum nostrum Iesum Christum à mortuis suscitavit.

Non ergò corpora nostra polluenda sunt scortatione, sed sancta & munda custodienda, & ministerio Iesu Christi mancipanda.

An nescitis quòd corpora vestra membra sunt Iesu Christi. An ergò avellens membra Christi, faciam ea membra scorti? Absit. An nescitis quòd qui adglutinatur scorto, unum corpus est? Erunt enim (inquit) duo in carnem unam. At qui adglutinatur domino, unus Spiritus est.

Argumenta gravissimi ponderis adiungit Paulus suae adhortationi. Difficulter enim Corinthii à consuetis viciis abduci poterant. Estque hoc primum argumentum sumptum à summainiustitiaet indignitate rei. Summa est iniquitas & iniustitia auferre membra Iesu Christo, eaque facere membra meretricis. Scortator, qui antea nomen Christo dedit, avellit membrum à corpore Iesu Christi: Nam peccato contra conscientiam excidit gratia, & expellit Spiritum sanctum: Ac fit una caro cum scorto: Summo ergò scelere sese involvit. Admonet Paulus hoc argumento ut cogitent quanta sit gloria esse membrum corporis Christi, quod est Ecclesia:

Quod caput nostrum sit omnipotens & aeternus Dei filius: Quod vegetamur & ducimur Spiritu sancto, qui de capite Christo in omnia membra dimanat. Hanc coelestem gloriam & foelicitatem magni facere debemus. Deinde monet quanta sit in scortatione turpitudo; Siquidem scortator sit membrum impuri scorti, quod est Satanae domicilium. Adducit Paulus testimonium ex Genesi. Et erunt duo in carnem unam: Quod dictum loquitur de arctissimo & indissolubili foedere mariti & coniugis. Paulus veròita transfert ad scortationem ut moneat scortatorem cum scorto unam fieri carnem. Ideoque Christianis abominandum esse hoc scelus. Si quis rogat num maritus coniugi cohabitans corpus suum avellat à Christo, respondendum est, maritum Christianum & fidelem non avellere corpus a Christo etiamsi debitam benevolentiam praestet coniugi. Honorabile est enim coniugium in omnibus: Et cohabitatio maris & foeminae divinitus est ordinata. Cum ergò bona conscientia coniuges operam dent procreandis liberis iuxta Dei ordinationem, non expellunt Spiritum sanctum, nec avelluntur à spirituali corpore Christi.

## 6:17
He who is joined to the Lord is one Spirit. He shows how we are made and are members of the body of Christ, namely through the Holy Spirit whom the Son of God pours into us, and whom we receive through faith, so that it may join us most closely with God, and kindle in us righteousness, the love of God, life, and eternal joy. One highest Spirit, that is, one spiritual body, and we are all led and sanctified by one Spirit.

Latin:

Qui domino adglutinatur, unus est Spiritus. Ostendit quomodo efficiamur & simus membra corporis Christi, nimirum per Spiritum sanctum quem filius Dei in nos effundit, & quem nos per fidem accipimus, ut nos arctissimè cum Deo copulet, & in nobis iustitiam, amorem Dei, vitam et laeticiam aeternam accendat. Unus summus Spiritus, id est, unum spirituale corpus & omnes uno Spiritu ducimur & sanctificamur.

## 6:18
Flee fornication, every sin that a man does is without the body. But he who commits fornication sins against his own body.

The second argument is taken from a comparison of sins. Sins by which we afflict our bodies with ignominy are graver than those which are committed outside the body: for he who treats his body with contumely is injurious not only to God, but also to himself. God, however, strictly commands that each one should take care of his own body, and show it honor as the lodging of God. But fornication treats one's own body with contumely; for it makes it a member of a harlot. Therefore, the pious must abstain from so foul a crime. That he says all other sins are committed outside the body, he speaks of most external and common misdeeds: theft, rapine, murder, injury to a neighbor, lying, calumny, are committed outside the body, that is, they have another object, namely, the neighbor. But fornication treats one's own body with contumely.

If anyone brings death upon himself, he is injurious to his own body: but those examples are more rare. Drunkenness also contaminates the body. But when Paul commands to flee fornication, he embraces all neighboring crimes, such as drunkenness, lasciviousness, adulteries, and incest. By other crimes also, such as murder, perjury, and theft, the members are contaminated: Your hands are polluted with blood, says the prophet. But Paul warns that there is a singular foulness of lusts, which affects bodies with a hideous ignominy: Whence also God is accustomed to punish this crime with various kinds of diseases in the body.

Latin:

Fugite scortationem, omne peccatum, quod facit homo, extra corpus est. Qui verò scortatur in proprium corpus peccat.

Secundum argumentum sumptum à collatione peccatorum. Graviora sunt peccata quibus nostra corpora ignominia adficimus, quàm quae extra corpus fiunt: nam qui corpus contumelia adficit, non solum in Deum, sed in seipsum quoque est iniurius. Deus autem severè praecipit ut quisque proprii corporis curam agat, eique ut hospicio Dei honorem exhibeat. At scortatio proprium corpus contumelia adficit; facit enim illud membrum meretricis. Abstinendum est igitur piis à tàm foedo scelere. Quòd dicit omnia alia peccata fieri extra corpus, de plerisque externis & usitatis facinoribus loquitur: furtum, rapina, caedes, laesio proximi, mendacium, calumnia, extra corpus fiunt, id est, aliud habent obiectum, videlicet proximum. Sed scortatio proprium corpus contumelia adficit.

Si quis sibi consciscat mortem, in proprium corpus est iniurius: sed rariora sunt illa exempla. Ebrietas etiam contaminat corpus. Sed Paulus cùm iubet fugere scortationem, omnia vicina scelera, ut ebrietatem, lasciviam, adulteria & incestum complectitur. Aliis etiam sceleribus, ut caede, periurio, furto contaminantur membra: Manus vestrae pollutae sunt sanguine, inquit propheta. Sed Paulus monet singularem esse turpitudincm libidinum, quae tetra ignominia adficiat corpora: Urde & Deus hoc scelus variis generibus morborum in corpore punire solet.

## 6:19
Do you not know that your bodies are the temple of the Holy Spirit, who exists in you and whom you have from God?

This is the third argument taken from the majesty of the Holy Spirit. The temple in which the Holy Spirit himself dwells is not to be contaminated with foul lusts, but the bodies of the faithful, having been sanctified, are into temples of the Holy Spirit, who through faith dwells in our hearts. Therefore, the bodies of the faithful are by no means to be polluted with lusts.

This argument is most grave and full of majesty; For it explains with what purpose and end we are created and redeemed. He shows with what immense benefit the eternal and most merciful Father affects us: That He not only snatches us from the tyranny of Satan and forgives us all our sins, but also pours the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from the essence of the Father and the Son, into our hearts, so that He may kindle in them light and heavenly life, and make us partakers of the divine nature. What greater thing could God give us than Himself? Who can attain to the most ample glory of the saints with words, when Scripture testifies that they are the dwellings of the Holy Spirit? For He is not an idle guest, but brings with Him the ornaments and the highest of all gifts. Therefore, those men labor under extreme madness who expel such a guest and master and despoil themselves of the highest glory: By fornication and lusts, they make of themselves impure pigsties for unclean spirits.

Latin:

An nescitis quòd corpora vestra templum sunt Spiritus sancti, qui in vobis existit & quem habetis à Deo?

Tertium est hoc argumentum sumptum à maiestate Spiritus sancti. Templum in quo ipse Spiritus sanctus habitat, non est contaminandum foedis libidinibus, sed corpora fidelium sanctificata, sunt in templa Spiritus sancti, qui per fidem habitat in cordibus nostris. Ergò corpora fidelium nequaquam sunt polluenda libidinibus.

Gravissimum & plenum maiestatis est hoc argumentum; Exponit enim quo consilio & fine conditi & redempti simus. Ostendit quàm immenso beneficio adficiat nos aeternus & clementissimus pater: Quod non solum eripiat nos ex Tyrannide Satanae & condonet nobis omnia peccata, sed etiam Spiritum sanctum, qui procedit de essentia patris & filii, effundat in corda nostra, ut in eis lucém & vitam coelestem accendat, & faciat nos participes divinae naturae. Quid posset nobis Deus maius dare se ipso? Quis potest amplissimam gloriam sanctorum verbis adsequi, cum scripturatestetur eos esse domicilia Spiritus sancti? Non est enim ille hospes ociosus, sed ornamenta & dona omnium summa secum adfert. Extremo igitur furere laborant homines qui tantum hospitem & dominum expellunt & sese spoliant summa gloria: Per scortationem autem & libidines, faciunt ex sese impuras haras immundorum Spirituum.

## 6:20
You are not your own (right:) You have been bought with a price. Glorify therefore God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.

This is the fourth argument from correlatives. No one ought to usurp those things which are of another's right for his own lust and transfer them to nefarious uses. Our bodies are not of our own right or power, but they are God's: for God redeemed them with a price, namely the blood of his only-begotten Son. Therefore it is not permitted for us to abuse our bodies by our own will, but they ought to serve the will and glory of God. The Apostle admonishes many things here. For he recalls to our memory at what price we have been redeemed: namely, by the precious blood of Jesus Christ. Therefore we ought to value our bodies highly also and show honor to them. He also admonishes us that we are not our own masters. In every action and endeavor, therefore, we ought to look to the will of the almighty God. There is also great consolation in the fact that he says that almighty God is glorified both by our spirit and by our body, when we use them according to the will of God. Therefore, the labors and sweats of the saints in whatever calling are pleasing sacrifices to God, whatever works we perform according to the word of God in faith, whether you plow, or dig, or chop wood, or sweep a house: you glorify God by laboring with your body according to your calling: It is a most pleasing sacrifice when we expose our bodies to dangers and the tyranny of the wicked for the truth and glory of God, when necessity demands it.

Latin:

Non estis vestri (iuris:) Empti estis precio. Glorificate iam Deum in corpore vestro, & Spiritu vestro, quae Dei sunt.

Quartum est hoc argumentum à correlativis. Nemo ea, quae alieni iuris sunt pro sua libidine usurpare & ad usus nefarios transferre debet. Corpora nostra non sunt nostri iuris aut potestatis, sed sunt Dei: Deus enim precio nimirum sanguine unigeniti sui filii redemit ea. Ergò non licet nobis nostro arbitrio abuti nostris corporibus, sed servire ea debent voluntati & gloriae Dei. Multa hîe monet Apostolus. Revocat enim nobis in memoriam quanto precio redemptisimus: Nimirum precioso sanguine Iesu Christi. Magni ergò facere debemus etiam corpora nostra & eis honorem exhibere. Monet etiam nos non esse nostri iuris. In omni igitur actione & conatu ad voluntatem omnipotentis Dei respicere debemus, Magna etiam est consolatio, quod dicit & Spiritu nostro & corpore nostro glorificari omnipotentem Deum, cum eo utimur iuxta Dei voluntatem. Grata ergò sunt sacrificia Deo, labores & sudores sanctorum in quacunque vocatione, qualescunque operas praestemus iuxta verbum Dei in fide, sive ares, sive fodias, sive ligna caedas, sive domum verras: Glorificas Deum laborans corpore iuxta vocationem: Gratissimum est sacrificium cùm corpora nostra pro veritate & gloria Dei obiicimus periculis & tyrannidi, impiorum poscente id necessitate.

## 6:20 Doctrines of the Places
Doctrines of the Places.

1. The first is concerning the distinguished glory of the saints, that they are to judge the angels and the world with Christ.

2. Second, that the impious and enemies of the truth, however much they may excel in gifts, are of no value in the eyes of the true Church. For he who is an enemy of Jesus Christ the Son of God is deservedly not only despised by the Church, but is also held in hatred.

3. Third, that as much as possible one must abstain from contentions and lawsuits, and take care lest by litigating with a brother before a pagan magistrate, we disfigure our religion and profession.

4. That arbitrators are to be chosen from the assembly of the saints, who may peacefully settle controversies, and that an injury is rather to be overlooked than to litigate with a brother when necessity does not demand it.

5. A notable passage is to be observed, that those who defile themselves with external crimes, such as injustice, theft, robbery, fornication, adultery, avarice, and drunkenness, are excluded by the severe judgment of God from participation in the kingdom of heaven.

6. Concerning the benefits of the Mediator Jesus Christ: that He washes away and forgives the sins of those who are penitent and approach Him by faith, that He freely justifies and sanctifies us: and that He gives us His Holy Spirit, so that He may renew in us the image of God.

7. Concerning true Christian liberty, which does not consist in the license of the flesh, but rather in the restraint of desires and in a pious zeal for building up the Church.

8. It shows the distinction between indifferent things or adiaphora, such as the use of food and drink, and prohibited things, such as fornication and adultery.

9. On the resurrection of our bodies.

10. Concerning the necessity for all pious persons to flee fornication, and concerning the magnitude of that crime.

11. Of the spiritual communion of the saints with Christ, that we all are members of Christ, and are enlivened by His Spirit.

12. On the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in the faithful

13. Concerning the redemption of the human race, which was accomplished through the blood of Jesus Christ.

14. For what end good works are to be done, namely that we may glorify the eternal and omnipotent God, whose servants we all are: then that we may not by sins against conscience cast out the Holy Spirit: that we may not afflict our bodies with disgrace, and that we may not be deprived of the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven.

Latin:

Loci Doctrinae.

1. Primus est de insigni gloria sanctorum, quod angelos & mundum cum Christo sint iudicaturi.

2. Secundus, quòd impii & veritatis hostes, quantiscunque donis excellant, in nullo sint precio apud veram Ecclesiam. Qui enim hostis est Iesu Christi filii Dei, meritò non solùm ab Ecclesia contemnitur, sed etiam odio habetur.

3. Tertius, quantum fieri potest, à contentionibus & litibus abstinendum esse, & cavendum ne litigando cum fratre coram Ethnico magistratu, religionem & professionem nostram deformemus.

4. Ex coetu sanctorum eligendos esse arbitros, qui placidè componant controversias, & potius dissimulandam esse iniuriam, quam litigandum cum fratre non poscente necessitate.

5. Insignis locus observandus est, quòd polluentes sese externis sceleribus, ut iniustitia, furto, rapina, scortatione, adulterio, avartitia, ebrietate, exclusi sint severo Dei iudicio à participatione regni coelorum.

6. De beneficiis Mediatoris Iesu Christi: quòd paenitentium & fide ad eum accedentium abluat & remittat peccata, quòd gratis iustificet & sanctificet nos: quodque donet nobis Spiritum suum sanctum, ut is renovet in nobis imaginem Dei.

7. De vera libertate Christiana, quae non consistit in licentia carnis, sed potius in cohibitione cupiditatum et in pio studio aedificandi Ecclesiam.

8. Discrimen monstrat inter res medias seu adiaphoras, ut cibi & potus usum, & inter res prohibitas ut scortationem & adulteria.

9. De resurrectione nostrorum corporum.

10. De fugienda omnibus piis scortatione, & de magnitudine eius sceleris.

11. De Spirituali communione sanctorum cum Christo, quòd omnes simus membra Christi, & Spiritu ipsius vegetemur.

12. De inhabitatione Spiritus Sancti in fidelibus

13. De redemptione generis humani, quae per sanguinem Iesu Christi facta est.

14. Quo fine facienda sint bona opera, nimirum ut aeternum & omnipotentem Deum, cuius servi omnes sumus, glorificemus: tum ne peccatis contra conscientiam excutiamus Spiritum sanctum: ne corpora nostra contumelia adficiamus, et ne haereditate regni coelorum privemur.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII.

Latin:

CAPUT VII.

## 7:1-2
Now concerning the things whereof you wrote to me, It is good for a man not to touch a woman. But for fear of fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband.

The Corinthians had proposed various questions concerning marriage to the Apostle Paul. For the hearers in the doctrine of Christ not sufficiently grounded and well-fortified dispute many things with themselves, and in many things they stick, anxious and doubtful, fearing lest they wound their conscience. Therefore, Paul responds to the proposed questions, and if any other things could disturb the conscience.

The first question was whether it was permitted to be celibate, or whether it was truly necessary to become married; they saw Paul abstaining from marriage. And they noticed that those imitating this example were falling into adulteries and fornications. Therefore, they were stuck. Paul responds. It is entirely convenient, especially with so many impending dangers and miseries, to abstain from marriage and to remain celibate. For exiles and departures can be borne with less trouble. Jerome wickedly contaminated this saying, against Jovinian, where he argues thus: It is good for a man not to touch a woman: Therefore it is evil to touch a woman. But Jerome did violence to the Apostolic sentence. For the Apostle in this place does not oppose good to evil: But he speaks of a middle thing, and an Adiaphoron. It is good, that is, it is permitted: also in some respect and in a certain way it is convenient and useful, especially with persecution and exiles encroaching. And for those who are instructed with the gift of continence. Therefore, Jerome sinned gravely because he twisted the oracle of the Holy Spirit to impugn marriage. And in this, the furies of the Manichaeans and Encratites Jerome did not help a little, because he dared to assert that it is evil to touch a wife: as if they polluted their conscience with sin, who are joined in matrimony according to the ordinance of God: which madness Paul calls a doctrine of demons. Therefore, the mind of Paul is, It is good not to touch a wife: That is, it is a lawful thing and not prohibited in itself, namely, for those who have the gift of continence.

But someone might say, Does Paul's statement conflict with the opinion of God? who in Gene: Cap: 6. says. It is not good for man to be alone: I answer, The sentences are of the same Holy Spirit, nor do they conflict among themselves. For God in Genesis speaks generally, concerning the whole human race, and looks to the propagation of men. In this respect it is not good for a man to be alone. And it is a greater good and more convenient to nature to live in society than in perpetual solitude. But Paul speaks specifically concerning the pious, namely those who are exposed in the world to various injuries, and who have the gift of continence, or who consecrate themselves entirely to the ministry of the Gospel; and with respect to corrupt nature and various miseries it is indeed good, That is, it is lawful and is a certain convenience to lack a spouse. For there are fewer temptations, fewer complaints, fewer troubles: Nor indeed is it to be thought that applies to individual persons either of Christians, or of teachers in the Church. Paul's statement: For it sometimes happens that pious and holy matrons provide remarkable consolation to their husbands who are in exile for the sake of the truth and are enduring various miseries, lift them up with a word, serve them with a prompt and faithful spirit, exhort them to constant patience, and help them with earnest prayer to God. Therefore, he only wishes to say this, that it is a lawful thing if anyone wishes to abstain from marriage; just as Christ says, there are those who castrate themselves for the sake of the kingdom of heaven; Matth: 19.

But as becoming a spouse or abstaining from marriage is in itself a lawful thing: so, on account of the corruption of nature, for those who do not have the gift of continence, it is necessary. To avoid fornication, let each one have his own spouse.

The principal final causes of the institution of marriage are, first, that the human race might be propagated by the conjunction of male and female in legitimate order and chastity: Second, that man might live in society, and have a companion and helper in all cares, endeavors, and labors. Paul adds a third here, to avoid lusts. For after man fell into sin, and his nature was corrupted, marriage is in place of a remedy, so that they might be able to provide continence and guard the purity of conscience: therefore it is lawful for those to contract marriage who, on account of old age, cannot have the hope of offspring.

Let the husband render to the wife due benevolence: Similarly also the wife to the husband, the wife does not have power over her own body, but the husband: Similarly also the husband does not have power over his own body, but the wife: do not defraud one another, unless perhaps sometimes by the consent of both for a time, that you may be free for fasting and prayer. And again come together into one lest Satan tempt you because of your incontinence. But I speak this by permission, not by commandment: For I wish all men to be, just as I also am. But each one has his own gift from God: This one indeed of this kind, but that one truly another.

Without doubt the question of the Corinthians was, whether it was permitted to a spouse to render due benevolence to his wife and to give effort to begetting children. For fanatical men were condemning marriages entirely, as an evil thing, and were execrating the conjugal custom, as a foul work. And because the saints feel in themselves impure motions, and

The Corinthians doubted whether the work of generation is contaminated by the evil of lust, and whether spouses ought to abstain entirely from conjugal intimacy. Therefore, Paul teaches that it is lawful for the saints to apply themselves to the procreation of children, and that marriage is a thing founded and ordained by God. And although infirmity also approaches in the saints, nevertheless they do not fall from grace, but that infirmity is covered by the shelter of the Mediator. That which he says, the husband does not have power over his own body, nor the wife over her own body, warns how tightly spouses are bound together by a covenant, and that one spouse cannot, according to their own will, make a vow concerning their own body, or dissolve the covenant of marriage: But just as they entered into matrimony by the consent of both, so neither has the right to decide anything concerning their own body, except by the consent of both. This sentiment should be understood not only concerning due benevolence and vows, but also concerning adultery and desertion. It is not lawful for a spouse to give power over their own body to anyone against the bond of marriage: It is also not lawful to wander here and there according to one's own will, without the consent of the other. That which he says, that the husband does not have power over his own body, but the wife, teaches that the covenant is mutual: And that the husband is just as bound to the spouse: As the wife is bound to the husband.

Latin:

De quibus verò scripsistis mihi, Bonum est homini uxorem non tangere. Sed ad vitandas scortationes unusquisque propriam habeat coniugem & unaquaeque proprium habeat maritum.

Varias quaestiones de coniugio proposuerant Corinthii Apostolo Paulo. Auditores enim in doctrina Christi non satis fundati, & probè muniti multa secum disputant, & in multis haerent anxii & dubii, metuentes ne vulnerent conscientiam. Respondet ergò Paulus ad propositas quaestiones, & si qua alia conscientiam turbare poterant.

Prima quaestio erat an liceret esse coelibem, an verò necesse esset fieri coniugem, videbant Paulum abstinere à coniugio: Et animadvertebant imitantes hoc exemplum labi in adulteria & scortationes. Haerebant ergò. Respondet Paulus. Commodum omninò esse praesertim tot impendentibus periculis & miseriis, abstinere à coniugio & manere coelibem. Exilia enim & profectiones minore molestia ferri possunt. Nefariè contaminavit hoc dictum Hieronymus, adversus Iovinianum, ubi sic disputat: Bonum est homini uxorem non tangere: Ergò malum est uxorem tangere. Sed vim fecit Apostolicae sententiae Hieronymus. Apostolus enim hoc loco non opponit bonum malo: Sed de re media, & Adiaphoro loquitur. Bonum est, Id est, licet: etiam aliquo respectu & quodammodo est commodum & utile, praesertim ingruente persecutione & exiliis. Et iis qui dono continentiae instructi sunt. Graviter ergò peccavit Hieronymus quòd Spiritus sancti oraculum ad impugnandum coniugium contorsit. Atque in hoc Manicheorum & Encratitarum furores non parum iuvit Hieronymus, quòd ausus fuit adserere malum esse tangere uxorem: quasi conscientiam polluerent peccato, qui iuxta Dei ordinationem matrimonio copulantur: quem furorem Paulus nominat doctrinam daemoniorum. Pauli ergò mens est, Bonum esse non tangere uxorem: Id est, rem esse licitam & per se non prohibitam, scilicet, iis qui donum habent continentiae.

Sed dicat aliquis, Pugnat ne Pauli dictum cum sententia Dei? qui in Gene: Cap: 6. inquit. Non est bonum homini esse solo: Respondeo, Eiusdem Spiritus sancti sunt sententiae, nec pugnant inter se. Nám Deus in Genesi generatim loquitur, de toto genere humano, & respicit propagationem hominum. Hoc respectu non est bonum hominem esse solum. Et maius bonum & naturae convenientius est vivere in societate quàm in perpetua solitudine. Paulus verò speciatim loquitur de piis, nimirum qui in mundo sunt expositi variis iniuriis, & qui donum continentiae habent, aut qui sese totos ministerio Evangelii consecrant; & respectu corruptae naturae & variarum miseriarum est quidem bonum, Id est, licet & est quaedam commoditas carere coniuge. Minus enim est tentationum, minus querelarum, minus molestiarum: Nec verò putandum est ad singulas personas vel Christianorum, vel doctorum in Ecclesia congruere Pauli dictum: Aliquando enim contingit ut piae & sanctae matronae suis maritis exulantibus propter veritatem, et varias miserias sustinentibus, insignem praebeant consolationem, erigant eos verbo, ministrent eis prompto & fideli animo, hortentur eos ad constantem patientiam, & iuvent eos seria precatione ad Deum. Tantum igitur hoc vult dicere, esse rem licitam, si quis abstinere velit à coniugio; Quemadmodum Christus inquit sunt qui castrant sese propter regnum, coelorum; Matth: 19.

Ut autem fieri coniugem, vel abstinere à matrimonio per se est res licita: Ita propter naturae corruptionem, illis qui donum continentiae non habent, est necessaria. Ad vitandas scortationes unusquisque propriam habeat coniugem.

Praecipuae causae finales instituti coniugii sunt, prima, ut coniunctione maris & faminae legittimo ordine & castitate propagaretur genus humanum: Secunda, ut homo viveret in societate, haberet sociam & adiutricem omnium curarum, conatuum & laborum. Tertiam hic addit Paulus ad vitandas libidines. Post quàm enim lapsus est homo in peccatum, & natura eius corrupta est, toco remedii est coniugium, ut continentiam praestare, & puritatem conscientiae tueri possint: licet igitur eos contrahere matrimonium, qui ob senectutem spem prolis habere non possunt.

Vir mulieri debitam benevolentiam praestet: Similiter & mulier viro, mulier proprii corporis potestatem non habet, sed vir: Similiter & vir proprii corporis potestatem non habet, sed mulier: non defraudetis vos invicem, nisi fortassis aliquando ex consensu utriusque ad tempus, ut vacetis ieiunio & orationi. Et rursus in unum convenite ne Satanas vos tentet propter vestram incontinentiam. Hoc autem ex venia, non ex mandato loquor: Volo enim omnes homines esse, quemadmodum & ego sum. Sed uniusquisque proprium donum habet ex Deo: Hic quidem huiusmodi, ille verò aliud.

Haud dubiè secunda Corinthiorum quaestio fuit, an coniugi liceret praestare uxori debitam benevolentiam & operam dare procreandis liberis. Fanatici enim homines prorsus damnabant coniugia, ut rem malam, & consuetudinem coniugalem, tanquam foedum opus execrabantur. Et quia sancti sentiunt in se impuros motus, &

opus generationis contaminari malo libidinis, dubitabant Corinthii coniuges, num ipsis prorsus à consuetudine coniugali abstinendum sit. Docet ergò Paulus licere sanctis operam dare procreandis liberis, & coniugium esse rem à Deo conditam & ordinatam. Et licet in sanctis quoque accedat infirmitas, tamen eos non excidere gratia, sed tegi illam infirmitatem umbraculo Mediatore. Quod dicit vir non habet potestatem sui corporis, neque mulier sui corporis, monet quàm arcto foedere coniuge inter sese sint devincti, & coniugum alterutrum non pro suo arbitrio de suo corpore vovere, aut foedus coniugii dissolvere posse: Sed sicuti matrimonium consensu utriusque inierunt, ita neuter de suo corpore quidquam statuere habet, nisi de utriusque consensu. Haec sententia non tantum de debita benevolentia, & votis, sed etiam de adulterio & desertione intelligatur. Non licet coniugi potestatem sui corporis alicui facere contra vinculum matrimonii: Non licet etiam pro suo arbitrio hinc inde vagari, sine alterius consensu. Quod dicit virum non habere sui corporis potestatem, sed uxorem, docet foedus esse mutuum: Et tam maritum devinctum esse coniugi: Atque uxor devincta est marito.

## 7:5
Unless perhaps by consent for a time: He encourages pious spouses to abstain at times from conjugal intimacy, but by the consent of both, A husband should not pretend a religion of continence with danger to the modesty of his spouse: And conversely, a wife should not defraud her husband of the debt of benevolence with danger to his own: But the consent of both should intervene when it pleases them to abstain: Then let this exercise last for a time, not as was done in the Church with growing superstition: For many renounced their wives, hid themselves in monasteries, and vowed perpetual chastity. These, against the command of Christ, broke the bond of matrimony. Paul therefore adds for a time, for some days, for some weeks, abstain yourselves.

That you may be free for fasting and prayer: Indeed, pious spouses must always live soberly and invoke God seriously every single day. But here he speaks of certain exercises, that the body must sometimes be chastised by fasting, lest it grow wanton, and so that more ardent prayers may be made, especially when some necessity, whether public or private, presses. The profane voice of Jerome is, I do not fulfill the duty of a Christian while I fulfill the duty of a husband. Nay, the holy matron Leah, while she gives effort to procreating children and ardently invokes God, is heard for her offspring.

And come together again, lest Satan tempt you: He does not want those exercises of fasting and more ardent prayer to last always. For Satan knows how great our weakness is, and he lies in wait for us assiduously: We must therefore take care, lest under the appearance of continence we may fall into the snares of the devil. Therefore, the remedy must be used which God has mercifully granted to the infirmity of the flesh.

I say this by way of concession, he says, not by way of command. God has granted the conjugal custom, although it is not without sin. For God did not wish to take away His work on account of sin: but He blessed His work, although it is contaminated by infirmity. The life of spouses is therefore under indulgence, if they believe in the Son of God.

Each one has his own gift, this is a most grave admonition, by which the Apostle exhorts that individuals should diligently weigh what kind of gifts they have received from God, and institute their life according to the reason of the gifts. Let him who is adorned with the gift of continence use it for the glory of God and the edification of the Church. Let him who is destitute of this gift consult his own infirmity with a legitimate remedy and not rashly expose himself to danger.

David was instructed by God with singular fortitude: Solomon was adorned with an admirable gift of wisdom. Therefore, let everyone observe what kind of gift he has received from God, and use it wisely. The monks are a foolish race of men, if indeed, having no regard for age, health, or gifts, they require similar exercises from all, when there is the greatest diversity of men.

I say to those who are outside of marriage and to widows: it is good for them if they remain as I also am: but if they do not contain themselves, let them marry: For it is better to marry than to burn.

He repeats the previous sentiment, that it is a good and lawful thing to remain outside of marriage, if anyone has the gift of continence. There is no reason for widows to fear that they might sin if they abstain from marriage. For this is permitted; they are not compelled by a command to marry. But their nature must be examined to see whether it is adorned with the gift of continence, so that if widows feel themselves to be destitute of it, they may marry again. For it is better to marry than to burn: that is. Although many afflictions and troubles happen to those who are married: nevertheless, those can be tolerated with a better conscience than if someone is constantly struggling with the flames of lust, and vows continence while nature fights against it. For that heat does not depart without pollutions and a wound to the conscience. Innumerable examples teach how unhappily the counsel of monks and nuns has turned out, who vowed perpetual chastity while spurning this counsel of Paul: And indeed not only those who, overcome by the flesh, have fallen into foul lusts, but also those who have abstained from all fornication and adultery, have felt the sad bites of conscience, while they could not repress the ardor of lust. Therefore, this counsel of Paul is salutary, that it is better to marry and enter into matrimony, as nature demands it, than to commit oneself to the constant flames of lust: especially since neither constant labors nor heavy hardships occupy them in such a way that they can extinguish them. At the same time, however, Paul answers the third question here, namely that second marriages are lawful. For he grants to widows that they may marry again. Tertullian, therefore, and others who condemned second marriages, have gravely hallucinated in that: And they have contradicted the doctrine of the Holy Spirit. From this passage it is usually gathered that Paul indeed had a spouse before, but that she having died, he remained in widowhood so that he might serve the kingdom of Christ more expeditiously: Because he numbers himself among the widows in this place, and wishes that others could imitate him.

But to the married I command, not I, but the Lord, that the wife should not separate herself from her husband: But if indeed she is separated, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband. And let the husband not dismiss his wife.

Fourthly, the Corinthians asked about divorces, whether it was lawful for wives to depart from their husbands, and whether it was lawful for a husband to give a bill of divorce to his wife; The Gentiles observed the laws of marriage less religiously, and most frequent were divorces among them: for they thought it was placed in their own judgment to dissolve the bond of marriage: or to preserve it. And without doubt, having been converted to Christ, they pretended the Mosaic custom concerning the giving of a bill of divorce. Therefore Paul renews the law of marriage, and forbids that a wife should desert her husband: and that a husband should expel his spouse. And so that this precept might have more weight in the Church, he says it is not his own command, but that of the Son of God, Jesus Christ. Without doubt Paul looked to the words of Christ. What God has joined, let man not separate. Matth: 19. And Christ expressly teaches that a spouse cannot be dismissed, except on account of fornication. As to what Paul adds, that if she is separated, she should remain unmarried: without doubt it is to be understood concerning that case when a wife complains of the immense cruelty of her husband, as often happens, and pretends this cause, why she cannot remain with her husband: in this case the Apostle commands that the woman departing from her spouse should not marry another, but that she should remain unmarried. This opinion also agrees with the saying of Christ: he who marries a separated woman, namely one who separated herself of her own accord from her husband, commits adultery. For thus in Mark the words of Christ are expounded.

Latin:

Nisi fortè ex consensu ad tempus: Hortatur pios coniuges ut aliquando abstineant à consuetudine coniugali, sed ex consensu utriusque, maritus non praetendat religionem continentiae cum periculo pudicitiae coniugis: Et vicissim uxor non defraudet maritum debita benevolentiae cum ipsius periculo: Sed utriusque consensus interveniat cum placet continere: Deinde ad tempus duret hoc exercitium, non ut crescente superstitione in Ecclesia factum est: Multi enim renunciarunt suis uxoribus, abdiderunt sese in monasteriae & voverunt perpetuam castitatem. Hi contra mandatum Christi solverunt matrimonii vinculum. Paulus igitur addit ad tempus, aliquot diebus, aliquot septimanis, vos continete.

Ut vacetis ieiunio & orationi: Semper quidem & singulis diebus & sobriè vivendum & seriò invocandum est piis coniugibus. Sed hîc de certis exercitiis loquitur, aliquando castigandum esse corpus ieiunio, ne luxuriet, & ut ardentiores preces fieri possint praesertim premente aliquae necessitate vel publica vel privata. Prophana vox est Hieronymi, Non impleo officium Christiani, dum impleo officium mariti. Imò Lea sancta matrona dum operam dat procreandis liberis, & ardenter invocat Deum, pro sobole exauditur.

Et simul convenite, ne vos tentet Satanas: Non vult semper durare illa exercitia ieiuniorum, & ardentioris precationis. Satanas enim novit quanta sit nostra imbecillitas, & adsiduè nobis insidiatur: Cavendum est igitur, ne sub specie continentiae in laqueos diaboli incidamus. Remedio igitur utendum quòd Deus infirmitati carnis clementer concessit.

Secundum veniam inquit hoc dico, non iuxta praeceptum. Consuetudinem coniugalem concessit Deus licet non sit absque peccato. Non enim voluit Deus auferre opus suum propter peccatum: sed operi suo benedixit, licet infirmitate sit contaminatum. Sub venia est igitur vita coniugum, si credant in filium Dei.

Unusquisque proprium donum habet, gravissima est haec admonitio, qua Apostolus hortatur ut singuli diligenter expendant, cuiusmodi dona à Deo acceperint, & vitam suam pro ratione donorum institutant. Continentiae dono ornatus, utatur eo ad gloriam Dei & aedificationem Ecclesiae. Hoc dono destitutus consulat suae infirmitati legittimo remedio & non temerè sese exponat periculo.

David singulari fortitudine instructus fuit à Deo: Salomon admirando sapientiae dono fuit ornatus. Observet ergò qui libet, cuiusmodi donum à Deo acceperit, & eo sapienter utatur. Monachi stolidum genus hominum est, si quidem nulla habita ratione aetatis, valetudinis, donorum, similia exercitia ab omnibus requirunt, cùm hominum summa sit diversitas.

Dico autem iis, qui sunt extra coniugium & viduis: bonum ipsis est, si manserint sicuti & ego: si autem non continent sese, nubant: Melius est enim nubere, quàm uri.

Repetit superiorem sententiam, quòd sit res bona & licita, manere extra coniugium, si quis donum continentiae habeat. Non est, quod metuant viduae, ne peccent, si abstineant à coniugio. Hoc enim licet, non coguntur mádato ad coniugium. Sed natura examinanda est num ornata sit dono continentiae, quò si destitui se sentiant viduae, nubant rursus. Melius enim est nubere, quàm uri: hoc est. Etsi multae adflictiones et molestiae eveniunt coniugibus: tamen meliore conscientia illae tolerari possunt quàm si quis adsiduè conflictetur cumflammis libidinis, et voveat continentiam natura re pugnante. Non enim abit ille aestus absque pollutionibus & vulnere conscientiae. Innumera exempla docent quàm infaeliciter cesserit consilium monachorum & monialium, qui perpetuam castitatem voverunt spreto hoc Pauli consilio: Nec verò tantum illi, qui superati à carne, in foedas libidines sunt prolapsi, sed etiam qui ab omni scortatione & adulterio abstinuerunt, tristes conscientiae morsus senserunt, dum libidinis ardorem reprimere non potuerunt. Salutare igitur est hoc consilium Pauli, potius esse nubendum & matrimonium ineundum, natura id poscente, quàm adsiduis libidinis flammis sese committendum: praesertim cum nec labores adsidui, nec graves aerumnae ita eos occupant ut eas possint restinguere. Simul autem Paulus ad tertiam quaestionem hîc respondet, quòd nimirum secundae nuptiae sint licitae. Viduis enim concedit ut denuò nubant. Tertullianus igitur & alii qui secundas damnarunt nuptias, graviter in eo sunt hallucinati: Et doctrinae Spiritus sancti contradixerunt. Ex hoc loco colligi solet Paulum habuisse quidem prius coniugem, sed ea mortua in viduitate ut expeditius regno Christi servire posset, mansisse: Quia sese hoc loco viduis annumerat, & optat ut caeteri eum imitari possent.

Coniugatis autem mando non ego, sed dominus, ne uxor separet se à viro: Quod si verò separatur innupta maneat, aut marito reconcilietur. Et maritus uxorem non dimittat.

Quartò interrogarunt Corinthii de divortiis, an liceret uxoribus discedere à maritis, & num marito liceret dare libellum repudii uxori; Gentes minus religiosè colebant leges coniugii, et frequentissima erant apud illas divortia: putabant enim in ipsorum arbitrio positum esse dissolvere vinculum coniugii: vel illud conservare. Et haud dubiè ad Christum conversi consuetudinem Mosaicam de dando libello repudii praetenderunt. Paulus ergò renovat legem coniugii, & vetat, ne uxor deserat maritum: & ne maritus expellat coniugem. Utque hoc praeceptum plus ponderis habeat in Ecclesia, dicit non suum, sed filii Dei Iesu Christi esse mandatum. Haud dubiè respexit Paulus ad verba Christi. Quos Deus coniunxit, homo ne separet. Matth: 19. Ac Christus expressè docet, non posse dimitti coniugem, nisi propter fornicationem. Quòd Paulus addit, quòd siseparetur, maneat innupta: Haud dubiè de eo casu accipiendum est, quando uxor de immani mariti saevitia conqueritur, ut saepè accidit, & hanc praetendit causam, cur non possit manere apud maritum: in hoc casu praecipit Apostolus, ne mulier discedens à coniuge, alteri nubat, sed ut maneat innupta. Congruit & haec sententia cum dicto Christi: qui separatam ducit, scilicet quae se sponte à marito separavit, adulterium committit. Sic enim in Marco verbae Christi exponuntur.

## 7:12
But to the rest I say, not the Lord, if any brother has an unbelieving wife,

Latin:

Reliquis verò ego dico, non dominus, si quis frater uxorem habet infidelem,

## 7:13-14
and she consents to dwell with him, let her not leave him: And the woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he is pleased to dwell with her, let her not leave him. For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the woman: And the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the husband, otherwise your children would be unclean: But now they are holy.

First, it must be noted with what modesty and fear such a great Apostle conducts himself in his ministry. Concerning those things for which he has certain and express commands from Christ, he commands them διαρρηδὴν, and demands them with great severity. For the Lord must be obeyed without any hesitation. But those things which the Lord has not commanded in express words, he does not wish to put forward in the person of the Lord: Yet he explains what he himself thinks, as a faithful Apostle of Jesus Christ. And cases often arise in the Church, concerning which the will of the Lord is not precisely and specifically determined; yet a pious and faithful pastor, who looks only to the glory of God, the edification of the Church, and the salvation of men, and directs his counsels to the norm of the divine word, can give wholesome counsel.

When therefore the Corinthians had asked in the fifth place, whether on account of the diversity of religion it was lawful to make divorces, and since undoubtedly dissension in religion, and contentions between spouses, and desertions have produced many things, Paul shows what his opinion is. Namely, that on account of dissension in religion a spouse is not to be dismissed, nor deserted, provided that she herself wishes to remain. For a diverse religion does not dissolve the covenant of marriage: which God wills to be perpetual and indissoluble. This precept of the Apostle must therefore be observed, so that no one, under the pretext of religion, either expels or deserts a spouse. And lest he leave scruples in the conscience, he teaches faithful husbands or wives that they are not contaminated by the association and cohabitation of infidel wives or husbands. An infidel husband, he says, is sanctified in a faithful wife. Sanctification cannot in this place be taken for reconciliation and renewal through the Holy Spirit: for an infidel is not sanctified in this sense through a faithful one. For the just shall live by his own faith. And in that day there will be two in one bed, one shall be taken, the other shall be left. It is necessary, therefore, that these words be understood concerning legal or civil sanctification: An infidel wife is sanctified, that is, the marriage is nonetheless legitimate, even if one of the spouses is an infidel: It is permitted for a faithful one without injury to the conscience to dwell with an infidel, nor is there any reason that he should fear, nor is he contaminated by the infidel. For to the clean all things are clean; And through the word and prayer all creatures are sanctified to the faithful: This is, the use of them becomes licit and holy.

He proves this opinion from the effect, because the children of those spouses who dissent in religion are holy. If marriage were impure on account of dissent in religion: The children also would be unclean, that is, not legitimate. But children are held to be holy or legitimately born: Therefore, the marriage of such persons is also legitimate and holy. It is manifest, therefore, that Paul in this place calls holy that which is lawful, legitimate, pure, and permitted, just as in the laws things were called holy which were permitted by law: But those things were called unclean and common which were prohibited by law. Calvin violently corrupts these words of Paul; since he interprets them concerning spiritual sanctification and the abolition of the curse. And he contends that the children of the faithful are holy from the womb, that is, exempt from the curse: Because the children of the saints have a peculiar prerogative from the promise, I will be the God of your seed. But this interpretation is foreign to the mind of Paul, nor is it ἀνάλογα of faith. For the universal Holy Scripture testifies that all children, as much of the saints as of the impious, are born subject to sin and the curse of the law. We were all, says Paul, by nature children of wrath: And John 3 Unless one is born again of water and the Spirit, he shall not enter into the kingdom of God. And the Baptist says, do not say we have Abraham as our father: For God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham. Likewise, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man but are born of God. And David, born of most holy parents, says of himself: Behold, I was conceived in iniquities, and in sins my mother conceived me. Therefore, the promise, 'I will be your God and the God of your seed,' does not mean this: That the children of the saints are holy from the womb: But God promises all good things to Abraham and to his entire posterity, but in such a way that they apply this promise to themselves by faith. Nor could Isaac himself have boasted of this promise if he had remained uncircumcised. It must also be considered that there is a twofold seed of Abraham, one carnal, the other spiritual. The spiritual seed of Abraham are those who are reborn through the Holy Spirit and imitate the footsteps of the faith of Abraham. The promise looks especially to these, and offers them the goods of eternal and present life. The other is the carnal seed, which draws its origin from the flesh of Abraham, such as Esau, Absalom, Annas, Caiaphas, and all the Jews. And God indeed did good to these, and adorned them with great benefits on account of Abraham, but on account of the prerogative of the flesh, he numbered no one among the saints, but rather demanded faith from each individual. Therefore, Calvin's interpretation is foreign to Paul's passage.

But if the unbeliever departs: Let him depart: A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases.

He now instructs consciences concerning the other case, if the unbelieving party, on account of religion, does not wish to cohabit with the faithful spouse, that he should depart and dissolve the marriage: what then must be done by the faithful and innocent party? Paul answers, the brother or sister in this case is not brought into bondage, as if he were saying: Let not the faithful party cast away religion on that account: nor let him fear for his conscience, as if it were held captive in this case: for the liberty, into which Christ has vindicated us, can by no case be snatched away from the faithful. Therefore the deserted party is without fault, and if there is need of marriage for the sake of conscience, it is permitted to the innocent and faithful party to contract another marriage.
