When therefore the Roman pontiff attempts to bind and burden the consciences of men by the distinction of foods, the prohibition of marriage, and the obligation of vows, and by works of satisfaction, these ropes must be broken, and Christian liberty must be recalled to memory, because to the pure all things are pure. Paul embraces all these degrees of liberty at once when he says, I being free from all: He does not, however, speak of a license to sin: for this primarily fights against liberty from sin, and the readiness of the Spirit to serve God. Nor does he speak of immunity from civil burdens. As the seditious peasants contended, that a Christian man is free. Therefore, that tributes and taxes are not to be paid to princes: Nor is obedience to be rendered. For this civil obedience pertains to the second degree of liberty. Whence Paul says. Rom: 13. To whom honor, honor; to whom tribute, tribute; to whom tax, tax. And so Paul says in this place, he has delivered himself into servitude to all: That is, he has accommodated himself to the weakness of all and served them with a prompt and spontaneous Spirit, seeking the salvation of his neighbor. To the Jews, he says, I became I became as a Jew. This is: Even if through Christ I am free from all Mosaic ceremonies, and I could enjoy this liberty, caring nothing for the distinction of clean and unclean animals, feast days, Circumcision and the like: Yet lest I should offend the weak Jews, who did not yet have that understanding of liberty which I have, I abstained, and so conducted myself, as if I were still bound by the Mosaic laws, and lived in the Jewish manner. Under the law, he calls those Jews, who although they had perceived and embraced the beginnings of the doctrine of the Gospel, yet did not yet understand the doctrine concerning Christian liberty, and maintained that the observation of the Mosaic laws was altogether necessary, and that without this righteousness before God could consist for no one. To these Paul served for a time, at the same time observing the law, as if he were still under the law, and did not understand the doctrine concerning liberty.

Latin:

Ego tamen nullo horum usus sum: inquit. Repetit suum institutum: quòd nimirum abstinuerit ab usu libertatis, cùm multa aequissimo iure petere, facere, usurpare potuisset, ut hoc suo exemplo invitet Corinthios ad imitationem, ut scilicet libenter cedant de suo iure propter Ecclesiae aedificationem.

Non autem haec scripsi, ut sic fiat mecum. Mori enim malim, quàm pati, ut quis gloriationem meam inanem reddat. Etenim si Evangelium annunciem, non est quòd glorier. Necessitas enim mihi incumbit. Vae autem mihi si non Evangelizem. Si enim volens hoc facio, mercedem habeo: si invitus, dispensatio mihi concredita est.

Occupatio est, qua occurrit tacitè suspicioni Corinthiorum. Quia enim Paulus adeò prolixè & multis allatis gravissimis argumentis docuit aequissimo iure servientibus Evangelio deberi alimenta & stipendia, suspicari poterant Corinthii Paulum obliquè perstrinxisse Corinthios, quòd erga ipsum minus grati essent, & quòd sub aliorum persona poscat ab eis stipendium. Ut ergò hanc sinistram suspicionem antevertat, excipit Paulus, se hoc consilio haec non scripsisse: Sed potius aliorum ministrorum & totius Ecclesiae causa: ne pastores et ministri praetextu exempli Pauli defraudentur debita mercede & stipendiis, & ne auditores Evangelii sese ingratos praebeant aut difficiles erga praecones verbi. Ac ut omnem tollat suspicionem, commemorat quanti faciat hanc gloriationem, quòd gratis praedicet Evangelium, Satius esset me mori quàm pati ut infringeretur mea gloriatio. Quasi dicat: hanc gloriationem, quod sine stipendio & gratuitò annuncio Evangelion, pluris facio quàm hanc meam vitam. Videt enim Paulus copiosam sibi mercedem in coelis esse repositam, qua haec ipsius fidelitas pensabitur. Si inquit, Evangelizem non est quòd glorier, necessitas mihi incumbit: Et vae mihi si non Evangelizem. Hic necessitatem sui muneris ex ponit: Quod divino mandato ipsi sit iniunctum & severè impositum ut doctrinam Evangelii sonet in mundo. Haud dubiè respicit ad historiam suae conversionis, ubi Christus de coelo eum est allocutus, Acto: 9. Et disertè ad Anamam dixit: Hic mihi est vas electum, ut portet nomen meum coram gentibus, regibus & filiis Israel: Et raptus in tertium coelum haud dubiè mandatum severum praedicandi Evangelion accepit. Ideò dicit sibi incumbere necessitatem, & vae sibi nisi praedicet: Hoc est, gravissimae poenae ipsi essent expectandae si praedicationem omitteret. Ex hoc loco manifestum est, sanam esse formam verborum, cum dicitur, Bona opera divinitus mandata sunt necessaria. Necesse est ut obtemperemus Deo: severa enim Dei mandata nequaquam sunt vel negligenda, vel in dubio ponenda. Sed illa appendix Maioristica, ad salutem esse necessaria, impia & falsa est. Sola enim gratia Dei, solum meritum Iesu Christi, & sola fides necessaria est ad salutem. Necessaria autem sunt bona opera ratione mandati divini, & sunt necessaria ad illustrandam Dei gloriam in terris, & ad testificationem nostrae fidei.

Si volens, inquit, facio, mercedem habeo: Omnes piorum laberes in fide susceptos, copiosa mercede rependit filius Dei: Inprimis verò docentibus Evangelion reposuit in coelis immarcessibilem gloriae coronam. 2. Timoth: 4. Daniel inquit, qui alios erudiunt ad iustitiam, tanquam sol fulgebunt in firmamento coeli: Cap: 12.Si invitus facio, dispensatio mihi concredita est: Etiamsi non essem prompto animo ad docendum Evangelium, ut saepè caro obluctatur spiritui, & aversatur odia, exilia, pericula, quae semper ut comites individui sequuntur Evangelii praedicationem: Tamen non possem omittere vocationem: Dispensatio, id est, ministerium praedicandi Evangelion mihi concreditum & commissum est. Id circo sive prompto sive invito id praestem animo, omninò oportet me parêre Dei mandato, & impositae vocationi.

Quae igitur est merces mea? Ut dum praedico Evangelion gratuitum & sine sumptu efficiam Evangelion Christi:

Ne abutar potestate mea in Evangèlio.

Ipsa Evangelii praedicatio mandata fuit Paulo divinitus: Ut autem gratis & sine stipendio praedicaret, non fuit ei mandatum. De hac igitur fidelitate & promptitudine sua gloriatur. Et hanc ipsam gloriationem vocat suam mercedem et praemium, quasi dicat: Mercedem à vobis non posco. Insigne praemium mihi est, quòd mihi licet gloriari contra falsos doctores & calumniatores, quòd Ecclesia propter Evangelion nullos in me sumptus fecerit, & quòd gratis laboraverim in ministerio. Repetit deinde causam finalem huius consilii sui, nimirum, ne abuteretur sua potestate in Evangelio, ne ullo modo cursum Evangelii impediret, aut ulli homini offendiculum poneret.

Liber enim cùm sim ab omnibus, omnibus meipsum in servitutem tradidi: Quò plures lucrifaciam. Iudaeis factus sum tanquàm Iudaeus: ut Iudaeos lucrer. His qui sub lege sunt, tanquàm sub lege essem, ut eos qui sub lege sunt, lucrer.

Hic tandem redit Apostolus ad principalem scopum huius capitis. Suum enim exemplum toti proponit Ecclesiae, quòd cum in Iesu Christo sit liberrimus, iudicet sibi omnia munda esse, nulli homini sit devinctus in conscientia sua, Apostolico Spiritu intelligat doctrinam de libertate Christiana, nullis legibus Mosaicis, nullis hominum traditionibus sit adstrictus. Tamen quasi in servitutem sese redegerit, ut eò plures Christo lucrifaceret, quod suum exemplum toti Ecclesiae proponit imitandum. Quia vero Libertini, & Epicurei alieni ab alacritate confessionis hoc Pauli testimonio sceleratè abuti solent, quasi doceat hic Paulus cum omnium sectarum hominibus colludere, & ad omnia scelera connivere, omnino necesse est refutari falsam & impiam dicti Paulini interpretationem, & sanam Spiritus sancti monstrari sententiam. Primùm in conspectu sit integra doctrina de libertate Christiana, quae non est barbarica licentia peccandi, aut quidvis faciendi, & nullis legibus neque divinis neque humanis parendi. Hanc ferociam & petulantiam per furorem mundus nominat libertatem, cum sit omnium foedissima servitus. Qui enim suas tantum sequitur impuras cupiditates, miserrimum est mancipium Satanae & peccati, quod tandem sponte ruit in aeternum exitium. Quemadmodum dominus docet. Qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati. Vera autem libertas Christiana est excellens illa felicitas & gloriae quod per dominum nostrum Iesum Christum liberati sumus à peccato ab ira Dei, à maledictione legis, à morte, & à tyrannide Satanae, quoque donati sumus Spiritu sancto qui novam lucem, iustitiam, & vitam in nobis accendit, & amissas vires restituit ut Spiritu spontaneo & libero Deo servire possimus iuxta ipsius verbum, tum quòd nulla lex Mosaica, nec ullae traditiones hominum quod ad religionem conscientiam nostram coram Deo constringere potest, sed quòd omnia sint munda mundis, & quòd omnis creatura Dei bona sit, ad usurpandum cum gratiarum actione. De hac libertate spirituali loquitur Christus Ioan: 8. Si vos filius liberavit verè liberi eritis, & Paul: Gal: 5. In libertate ergò in quam Christus vos vocavit state, & 1. Cor: 7. Magno precio redempti estis, nolite fieri servi hominum, & Iesa: 52. Gratis venundati estis, gratis redimemini: Ac docendi causa rectè ponuntur quatuor gradus libertatis.

Primùs gradus est liberatio à peccato, ab ira Dei, à maledictione legis, à peccato, à morte, à tyrannide Diaboli, & tota servitute infernali: Et contra, imputatio iustitiae filii Dei & reconciliatio cum aeterno patre. Haec libertas maius bonum est quàm multis mundis imperare, & omnium rerum copia abundare. Hanc libertatem passim inculcat scriptura ut Rom: 6. Non estis sub lege sed sub gratia: Item, Rom: 8. Lex Spiritus vitae in Christo Iesu liberavit me à lege peccati & mortis.

Secundus gradus est donatio Spiritus sancti & ipsa renovatio virium, quas nova vi & libertate instruit Spiritus sanctus ut non amplius ex legis coactione repugnante natura, sed prompto & spontaneo Spiritu agnoscamus, invocemus, metuamus & diligamus Deum. De hoc gradu Paulus loquitur ad Rom: 8. Non enim accepistis Spiritum servitutis rursum ad timorem, sed accepistis Spiritum adoptionis filiorum, in quo clamamus abba pater, & 2. Cor: 3. Ubi Spiritus est ibi est libertas: Nos vero omnes retecta facie gloriam domini speculantes in eandem imaginem transformamur à gloria in gloriam, tanquam à domini Spiritu.

Tertius gradus est liberatio à legibus Mosaicis forensibus, & ceremonialibus. Post quam enim exhibitus est Messias, & militia Hierusalem completa: Totalex Mosis abrogata est neque amplius obstringit natos ex semine Abrahae. De hac libertate Paulus loquitur Coloss: 2. Nemo vos iudicet in cibo aut potu, aut vicibus dierum festorum aut Sabbathis, quae sunt umbra futurorum: Corpus autem hoc totum quod Christi est & ad spirituale eius regnum pertinet.

Quartus gradus est, quod nullae traditiones hominum quò ad religionem conscientiam nostram coram Deo obstringere possunt. De hoc gradu Paulus loquitur Coloss: 2. Si ergò mortui estis cum Christo ab elementis mundi, quid tanquam viventes in mundo decretis tenemini? Ne tetigeris, ne gustaveris, ne attrectaveris, quae omnia ipso usu consumuntur & pereunt, utpote praecepta & doctrinae hominum. Cum ergò Roma: pontifex distinctione ciborum, prohibitione, coniugii, obligatine votorum, operibus satisfactionum conscientias hominum adstringere & gravare conatur, rumpendi sunt isti funes, & libertas Christiana repetenda memoria, quòd omnia mundis sint munda. Omnes hos gradus libertatis simul complectitur Paulus cum inquit, liber cum sim abomnibus: Nequaquam autem loquitur de licentia peccandi: Haec enim inprimis pugnat cum libertate à peccato, & promptitudine Spiritus serviendi Deo. Nec loquitur de immunitate ab oneribus civilibus. Ut seditiosirustici contendebant, hominem Christianum esse liberum. Ideo principibus non esse pendenda tributa & vectigalia: Nec praestandam esse obedientiam. Haec enim civilis obedientia pertinet ad secundum gradum libertatis. Unde Paulus inquit. Rom: 13. Cui honorem, honorem, cui tributum, tributum, cui vectigal vectigal. Atque ita Paulus hoc loco dicit, tradidisse sese in servitutem omnibus: Id est, omnium se imbecillitati sese accommodasse & inservisse prompto & spontaneo Spiritu quaerendo salutem proximi. Iudaeis, inquit, factus sum tanquam Iudaeus. Hoc est: Et si per Christum liber sim ab omnibus ceremoniis Mosaicis, & hac libertate frui possem, nihil curans distinctionem animalium mundorum & immundorum, dierum festorum, Circumcisionem & similia: Tamen ne infirmos Iudaeos, qui nondum habebant eum intellectum libertatis quem ego habeo, offenderem, abstinui, & ita me gessi, ac si Mosaicis legibus adhuc essem obstrictus, & Iudaico more viverem. Sub lege, Iudaeos vocat, qui etsi initia doctrinae Evangelii perceperant & amplexi erant, tamen doctrinam de libertate Christiana nondum intelligebant, & statuebant legum Mosaicarum observationem prorsus necessariam esse, & sine hac iustitiam coram Deo nemini constare posse. His ad tempus servivit Paulus, simul legem observans, ac si adhuc sub lege esset, & doctrinam de libertate non intelligeret.

## 9:21-23
To them that are without law as without law: Whereas I am not without the law of God: But am in the law of Christ, that I might gain them that are without law, I became to the weak as weak, that I might gain the weak. I became all things to all men, that I might by all means save some. And I do this for the gospel's sake, that I may be made partaker thereof.

Just as he accommodated himself to the weak Jews converted to the faith, so also he accommodated himself to the Gentiles who were without the Mosaic law, that he might save some. And if Paul was a Jew by nation, nourished by Mosaic ceremonies, Paul did not however morosely urge ancestral customs among the Gentiles, but accommodated himself to the infirmity of the Gentiles, and lived with them as if he were held by no Mosaic law, for he knew that the entire Mosaic polity had already been abrogated. Ανομος here does not signify unjust, but one who is not held by the law, and he speaks of ceremonial and forensic laws. The exception which is interposed (not being without law to God, but in the law to Christ:) is inserted to refute the Antinomians, lest anyone think that Paul had abolished the entire law, and together with the Gentiles had contaminated himself with crimes against the law of God, as if he cared for no law. To God, he says, that is, before God in conscience I was not without law, I did not despise the judgment of God, I did not loosen the reins to desires, I did not live in crimes. But in the law to Christ I was: This is, redeemed through Christ and gifted with the Spirit, I live holily and piously according to the law, and I prove my faith and obedience to Christ. Therefore, that which he says: I have become all things to all men: Is not to be understood concerning the omission of necessary confession, and the preaching of the Gospel, or other necessary duties: for concerning this kind Paul says, I believed, therefore I have spoken: And Woe to me unless I shall have evangelized, nor concerning the commission of manifest crimes. For concerning these Paul expressly says, that those who do such things shall not possess the kingdom of God. But concerning those things which are neither commanded nor prohibited divinely, but are ἀδιάφορα that is, indifferent, he says that he has become all things to all men. That is, that he has accommodated himself to the grasp of all, so that he might at least gain some for Christ and convert them to God.

Therefore, let actions be diligently distinguished; some are commanded by the express word of God, in these it is not permitted for us to dispense by our own judgment. For the rule is immovable: What I command you, this only you shall do, you shall add nothing, nor take away, you shall not turn aside either to the right or to the left. Others are prohibited by divine law, which must all necessarily be avoided and admitted for the sake of no one. For the rule is immovable: The soul that shall have done these abominations shall be eradicated. Likewise, Cursed is he who does not remain in all things which are written in the book of this law.

The third kind of actions comprises adiaphora or middle things, which are neither commanded nor prohibited: in these he teaches us to become all things to all men, so that we may spontaneously yield from our own right, accommodate ourselves to the infirmity of others, bear weaknesses, and always look to this one thing, that we may gain many for Christ.

Because of the Gospel, says Paul, I do this so that I may become a partaker of it. This is, so that I may spread it as widely as possible and, lest by the abuse of liberty, I fall away from the communion of the Gospel, which is the highest happiness of all.

Latin:

His qui sunt sine lege tanquam sine lege: Cum non sim sine lege Deo: Sed in lege Christo, ut eos qui sunt sine lege lucrer, factus sum infirmis, tanqum infirmus ut infirmos lucrarer. Omnibus omnia factus sum, ut omnibus modis aliquos salvos faciam. Hoc autem facio propter Evangelium, ut eius particeps fiam.

Ut Iudaeis infirmis ad fidem conversis sese accommodavit, ita & gentibus quae erant sine lege Mosaica sese accommodavit, ut aliquos salvos faceret. Et si natione Iudaeus erat Paulus ceremoniis Mosaicis enutritus, non tamen morose ursit Paulus apud gentes patrios mores, sed accommodavit se infirmitati gentium, & ita vixit cum eis ac si nulla lege Mosaica teneretur, sciebat enim totam politiam Mosaicam iam abrogatam esse. Ανομος hic non significat iniustum, sed qui lege non tenetur, & loquitur de legibus ceremonialibus & forensibus. Exceptio quae interponitur ( non existens sine lege Deo, sed in lege Christo:) Inserta est ad refutandos Antinomos, ne quis existimet Paulum totam legem sustulisse, & unà cum gentibus contra Dei legem sceleribus se contaminasse, quasi nullam curaret legem. Deo inquit, id est, coram Deo in conscientia non fui sine lege, non sprevi iudicium Dei, non laxavi frena cupiditatibus, non vixi in sceleribus. Sed in lege Christo fui: Hoc est per Christum redemptus & Spiritu donatus sanctè & piè vivo iuxta legem, & Christo probo fidem & obedientiam meam. Quòd ergo dicit: Omnia se factum esse omnibus: Non est intelligendum de omissione necessariae confessionis, & praedicationis Evangelii, aut aliorum necessariorum officiorum: de hoc enim genere Paulus dicit, Credidi propter quod locutus sum: Et Vae mihi nisi Evangelizavero, neque de commissione manifestorum scelerum. Nam de his Paulus expresse dicit, qui talia faciunt regnum Dei non possidebunt. De iis autem quae nec mandata, neque prohibita sunt divinitus, Sed sunt ἀδιάφορα Id est, indifferentia, dicit se omnibus omnia factum esse. Id est, se omnium captui sese accommodasse, ut aliquos saltem lucrifaceret Christo & ad Deum converteret.

Diligenter ergò discernantur actiones, aliae sunt mandatae expresso Dei verbo, in his non licet nobis nostro arbitrio dispensare. Regula enim immota est: Quod ego praecipio tibi hoc tantum facies, nihil addes, neque detrahes, non declinabis neque ad dexteram neque ad sinistram. Aliae sunt prohibitae lege divina quae omnes necessariò sunt cavendae & in nullius; gratiam, admittendae. Regula enim immota est: Anima quae fecerit abominationes istas eradicabitur. Item, Maledictus qui non permanet in omnibus quae scripta sunt in libro legis huius.

Tertium genus actionum adiaphora seu res medias complectitur, quae nec sunt mandatae, nec sunt prohibitae: in his docet nos omnibus omnia fieri, ita ut de nostro iure sponte cedamus, infirmitati aliorum nos accommodemus, imbecillitates feramus, & hoc unum semper spectemus ut Christo multos lucrifaciamus.

Propter Evangelion, inquit Paulus, hoc facio ut eius fiam particeps. Hoc est, ut quàm latissimè illud spargam & ne abusu libertatis, excidam communione Evangelii, quae omnium summa est felicitas.

## 9:24-25
Do you not know that those who run in a race, all indeed run, but one receives the prize, that is, the reward. So run that you may obtain (the palm). Everyone who competes, endures all things: they indeed, therefore, that they may receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible one.

He transfers the admonition concerning the use of liberty to a general exhortation concerning the showing of diligence and serious study of true piety, lest either stumbling by error, or overtaken by desire, or failing in the contest, we be frustrated of our hope: and he depicts the contest of piety with similitudes. Those who run in a race do not all receive the prize, but the one who has conquered the others. Thus many approach the Gospel, they enter the contest of piety, but they either wander in the middle of the course, or are hindered, or are broken. Asa was running excellently in the beginning, but he collapsed in the very course, and did not obtain the prize of eternal life.

Thus Jeroboam, Saul, Amaziah, Uzziah, Joash. Thus Arius, Nestorius, Samosatenus, Pelagius strayed from the mark, because they embraced errors instead of the truth. Therefore Paul warns that we should run in such a way that we may obtain the prize. This is what Christ says: he who will have persevered until the end, will be saved. One must therefore remain in the word, in faith, in piety, in patience, in diligence, in constancy.

Everyone who competes endures all things: and restrains himself. That is, whatever he understands will be an impediment to him so that he might be less able to obtain the palm, this he avoids: He does not indulge in luxury, sleep, or sluggishness, but is of an awakened spirit, and even endures blows, only so that he may obtain the crown, which is nevertheless corruptible. How much more ought we in this spiritual stadium and wrestling school to sustain, endure, and tolerate all things, since we know that an unfading crown, namely heavenly and eternal glory and joy, is set before us. This comparison contains a most grave castigation of our time and sloth, that with such great rewards set before us in the kingdom of Christ we are so negligent. Similar is the discourse of Christ Luke 16. The children of this world are wiser than the children of light in their generation.

I therefore run in such a way, not as with a blind impulse: I exercise the contest of boxers in such a way as one who does not beat the air. But I buffet my body and bring it into subjection, lest while I preach to others I myself should be a castaway.

In this whole chapter he has set forth his own example to the Church, first in particular how liberty is to be used: then in general, how for the sake of Christ's glory and the edification of the Church all things are to be endured. Now by the commemoration of his own exercises he concludes the chapter, and exhorts individuals that they should imitate his sincerity, prudence, piety, abstinence, tolerance, and zeal.

I, he says: so run, not as with uncertain impulse, not with blind zeal. Paul calls that an uncertain and blind impulse when someone has not laid the solid foundations of his faith, does not look forward to the certain end of his labors and struggles, does not understand the legitimate means, nor has determined with himself to endure all things, so that he may obtain eternal salvation. Very many such are in the Church who embrace the doctrine of the Church; they undertake the labors of the ministry, they subject themselves to grave dangers, and they sustain great miseries, when nevertheless they neither seriously inquire into the foundations of doctrine, nor rightly gaze upon the goal of eternal life, nor use legitimate means: And thus they often suffer the hardest things in vain and without fruit.

Ἀδήλως the Baalites were running: For they did not understand the foundations of doctrine, they did not join themselves to the Church, they did not listen to the Prophets, but they served in the worship of idols: And they sought only the comforts of the belly. Ἀδήλως the Pharisees were running, to whom Paul gives testimony that they had a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge, for they were fervent with a study of religion, but they did not understand the goal of scripture, they were bewitched by errors, they were ignorant of the benefits of the Messiah, and they endured all things in vain. Thus all heretics Ἀδήλως, that is, are carried by a blind impulse, not looking at a certain end, not founded on solid doctrine, not using legitimate means. Meletius was a great man, and suffered many things for the sake of the Gospel, Ἀδήλως yet he ran, because he attributed more to his own stubbornness and moroseness than to the sound doctrine of the Gospel: while he denies repentance to the lapsed.

The Audians endured dangers and hardships with great patience for the sake of confession: and yet they ran Ἀδήλως, while with excessive stubbornness they defended that the passover ought to be observed by the rite of the Jews, and without cause they troubled the Church.

Acesius was a great man, and he constantly confessed the truth of the Gospel, and refuted the Arians: But while through error, he stubbornly defended the delirium of the Novatians, Ἀδήλως he runs, it neither rests upon a certain foundation, nor looks toward a goal, nor prudently chooses means. Manifestly wicked men do not run ἀδήλως, for they sin against conscience, such as Arius, Nestorius, Macedonius, Pelagius, Aëtius, Monearius, the Roman pontiffs, the King of Münster, John of Leiden. These know that they are attacking the truth. But Paul here censures those who join themselves to the Church, and show some zeal, and yet do not seek the truth, do not rely upon a solid foundation, do not direct all things to the glory of God and the salvation of the Church. These are suddenly and easily cast down from their purpose of piety by some chance. Therefore Paul warns by this example of his, that those who pursue piety should take care, lest they be carried by a blind impulse, like the Anabaptists, or fanatical men, or the ignorant mob: But that they should inquire into the solid foundations of their doctrine, have a certain goal proposed, namely the glory of God, the edification of the Church, and their own salvation: Let them also see to it that they choose legitimate means, and the way shown in the word of God, in the fear of God, lest they run into uncertainty, or beat the air. For it is most sad that a man should undertake great labors, and sustain hardships, and miseries, and yet beat the air, that is, to profit neither himself nor others. Origen sustained most harsh labors, and many miseries, and yet he beat the air. For he profited neither himself nor others, but much more harmed the Church. Pelagius led an austere life, and has suffered much, but he beat the air; he profited neither himself nor the Church, but rather harmed it. Such people are always very numerous in the Church, as now Illyricus who recalls Manichaeism from the underworld. He has indeed labored and suffered much, but because he stubbornly defends error, he beats the air with all his struggling. Therefore Paul warns that we should struggle in such a way that we do not go astray. This will happen if we firmly grasp the foundations of doctrine, always perform penance, undertake all things in the fear of God, avoid all errors, and assiduously call upon God in every endeavor. Paul signifies his ardent zeal and the assiduous struggles of piety when he says that he chastises his body: ὑπώπια signifies the swellings and welts arisen on the face from a blow. And Paul signifies that he suppresses, curbs, and restrains the affections of the flesh with great zeal, lest while he calls others to penance, he himself gives way to security, or is entangled in the snares of Satan: such as many are in the ministry, who, while they vigorously tax the vices of others and rightly show the way of salvation, they themselves nevertheless indulge in security and do not attain eternal life. However, the Apostle does not speak here of the hypocrisy of the Encratites, or the exercises of Monks, or Hermits, or fanatical men: but of the necessary repression of the affections of the flesh.

Latin:

An ignoratis quòd qui in stadio currunt, omnes quidem currunt, sed unus bravium, Id est, praemium accipit. Sic currite ut obtineatis (palmam). Omnis qui certat, omnia sustinet: illi quidem igitur, ut corruptibilem coronam accipiant, nos autem incorruptibilem.

Admonitionem de usu libertatis transfert ad generalem adhortationem de praestanda diligentia & serio studio verae pietatis, ne vel errore impingentes, vel cupiditate praeventi, vel in certamine deficientes spe nostra frustremur: & similitudinibus pingit pietatis certamen. Qui in stadio currunt non omnes accipiunt bravium, sed unus qui caeteros vicit. Ita multi accedunt ad Evangelion, ingrediuntur certamen pietatis, sed vel aberrant in medio cursu, vel impediuntur, vel franguntur. Assa praeclarè currebat initio, sed concidit in ipso cursu, nec obtinuit bravium vitae aeternae.

Sic Ierobeam, Saul, Amaza, Uzia, Ioas. Sic Arrius, Nestorius, Samosatenus, Pelagius aberrarunt à scopo, quia errores pro veritate sunt amplexi. Monet ergò Paulus, ut sic curramus, ut bravium obtineamus. Hoc est, quòd Christus dicit: qui per severaverit usque ad finem, salvus erit. Manendum est ergò in verbo, in fide, in pietate, in pacientia, in diligentia, in constantia.

Omnis qui certat omnia tolerat: & continet se. Id est, quidquid intelligit sibi impedimento fore quò minus palmam obtinere possit, hoc cavet: Non indulget luxui, somno, torpori, sed excitato est animo, & plagas etiam perfert, tantum ut coronam, quae tamen corruptibilis est, obtineat. Quantò magis nos in hoc spirituali stadio & palaestra omnia sustinere, perferre & tolerare debemus, cum sciamus coronam immarcessibilem, nimirum gloriam & laeticiam coelestem & aeternam nobis esse propositam. Haec comparatio gravissimam continet castigationem nostri temporis & ignaviae, quòd tantis propositis praemiis in regno Christi adeò simus negligentes. Similis est Christi concio Lucae 16. Filii huius seculi prudentiores sunt filiis lucis in sua generatione.

Ego igitur sic curro, tanquam non caeco impetu: Sic pugilum certamen exerceo ut qui non verberem aerem. Sed lividum facio corpus meum & in servi tutem illud redigo, ne dum aliis praedico ipse sim reprobus.

In hoc toto capite exemplum suum proposuit Ecclesiae, primùm in specie quomodo sit utendum libertate: deinde in genere, quomodo propter Christi gloriam & Ecclesiae aedificationem omnia sint sustinenda. Nunc commemoratione suorum exercitiorum concludit caput, & hortatur singulos, ut ipsius synceritatem, prudentiam, pietatem, abstinentiam, tolerantiam & zelum imitentur.

Ego inquit: Sic curro tanquam non incerto impetu, non coeco studio. Insertum & coecum im petum nominat Paulus cum quis non solida iecit fidei suae fundamenta, non prospicit certum finem suorum laborum & certaminum, non intelligit media legitima, nec apud se constituit omnia sustinere, ut aeternam obtineat salutem. Plurimi tales sunt in Ecclesia qui doctrinam Ecclesiae amplectuntur; labores ministerii suscipiunt, gravibus periculis sese subiictunt, & magnas sustinent aerumnas, cum tamen nec fundamenta doctrinae seriò inquirant, nec vitae aeternae scopum rectè intueantur, nec mediis utantur legitimis: Atque ita saepè frustrà & sine fructu durissima patiantur.

Ἀδήλως currebant Baaelitae: Non enim intelligebant doctrinae fundamenta, non iungebant se Ecclesiae, non audiebant Prophetas, sed in cultu idolorum servebant: Et tantum commoda ventris quaerebant. Ἀδήλως currebant Pharisaei, quibus Paulus dat testimonium quod habuerint zelum Dei, sed non secundum scientiam, fervebant enim studio religionis, sed non intelligebant scopum scripturae, erant fascinati erroribus, ignorabant Messiae beneficia, & omnia frustrà sustinebant. Sic omnes haeretici Ἀδήλως, id est, caeco impetu feruntur, non intuentes finem certum, non fundati solida doctrina, non utentes legitimis mediis. Meletius vir magnus fuit, & multa passus propter Evangelium, Ἀδήλως tamen cucurrit, quia pertinatiae suae & morositati plus tribuit, quam sanae doctrinae Evangelii: dum lapsis negat poenitentiam.

Audiani magna patientia sustinuerunt pericula & aerumnas propter confessionem: & tamen cucurrerunt Ἀδήλως, dum nimia pertinacia defenderunt pascha Iudaeorum ritu esse observandum, & sine causa turbarunt Ecclesiam.

Acesius magnus vir fuit, & constanter confessus est veritatem Evangelii, & refutavit Arrianos: Sed dum per errorem, pertinaciter defendit delirium Novatianorum, Ἀδήλως currit, nec certo fundamento innititur, nec metam prospicit, nec media prudenter eligit. Manifestè scelerati non currunt ἀδήλως, peccant enim contra conscientiam, ut Arrius, Nestorius, Macedonius, Pelagius, Aëtius, Monearius, pontifices Romani, Rex monasteriensis, Ioannes leidensis, Hi sciunt se oppugnare veritatem. Sed eos taxat hic Paulus qui adiungunt se Ecclesiae, & zelum aliquem ostendunt, & tamen non quaerunt veritatem, non nituntur solido fundamento, non omnia dirigunt ad gloriam Dei & salutem Ecclesiae. Hi subito aliquo casu facilè deiiciuntur à suo proposito pietatis. Monet ergò Paulus hoc suo exemplo, ut qui pietatem sectantur dent operam, ne ferantur caeco impetu, ut Anabaptistae, aut fanatici homines, aut vulgus imperitum: Sed ut inquirant fundamenta solida suae doctrinae, habeant propositam certam metam, videlicet gloriam Dei, aedificationem Ecclesiae, et propriam salutem: Videant etiam ut legitima media, & viam monstratam in verbo Dei, in timore Dei eligant, ne in incertum currant, aut verberent aërem. Est enim tristissimum, hominem su scipere magnos labores, & sustinere aerumnas, & miserias, & tamen verberare aërem, hoc est, nec sibi nec aliis prodesse. Origenes labores sustinuit durissimos, & miserias multas, & tamen aërem verberavit. Nam nec sibi nec aliis profuit, sed multò magis obfuit Ecclesiae. Pelagius austeram duxit vitam, & multa est perpessus, sed aërem verberavit, Nec sibi nec Ecclesiae profuit, sed magis obfuit. Tales plurimi semper sunt in Ecclesia, ut nunc Illyricus qui Manichaeismum revocat ab inseris. Plurima quidem & laboravit & perpessus est, sed quia errorem pertinaciter defendit, aërem verberat omni suo certamine. Monet ergò Paulus ut ita certemus, ne aberremus. Hoc fiet si fundamenta doctrinae solidè percipiemus, semper poenitentiam agemus, omnia in timore Dei susciptemus, omnes errores vitabimus, & adsiduè in omni conatu Deum invocabimus. Ardens suum studium, & adsidua pietatis certamina significat Paulus, cum inquit se castigare corpus suum: ὑπώπια significant tumores vibices ortas in facie ex plaga. Et significat Paulus se magno studio reprimere, frenare & coërcere carnis adfectus, ne dum alios vocat ad poenitentiam, ipse sese dedat securitati, aut laqueis Satanae implicetur: Quales multi sunt in ministerio, qui cum aliorum vitia strenuè taxent, & viam salutis rectè monstrent, ipsi tamen securitati indulgent & vitam aeternam non adipiscuntur. Non autem loquitur hîc Apostolus de hypocrisi Encratitarum, aut exercitiis Monachorum, vel Eremitarum vel fanaticorum hominum: sed de necessaria repressione adfectuum carnis.

## 9:25 Places of Doctrine
Places of Doctrine.

1. The first is concerning Christian liberty and its legitimate use, which ought to be governed by love of neighbor and for the glory of the divine name, for the illustration of the Gospel, and the edification of the Church.

2. A notable testimony concerning the resurrection of Jesus Christ, inasmuch as Paul saw the Lord Jesus after his ascension into heaven.

3. Concerning the efficacy of the Evangelical ministry, that the labor of those teaching may not depart without fruit, but through it a holy Church may be gathered to God.

4. What is the best method of all for refuting adversaries, namely that we send them back to the Church of God gathered and confirmed by our labor and ministry.

5. Concerning the marriage of priests or ministers of the Gospel, that the Apostles Peter and the other brothers of the Lord were married, from which it is manifest that the law of the Roman pontiffs concerning the celibacy of priests is a doctrine of demons.

6. In this chapter is, as it were, the seat of the doctrine that ministers of the Church and their families ought to be nourished and cherished by the Church with honest stipends: for the Apostle treats this place at length, and with many most weighty arguments teaches that food and the necessities of this life are altogether owed to those who faithfully teach and serve the Church. And first of all, it is most worthy of note what he says, that our Lord Jesus Christ so ordained, that those who serve the Gospel, should live from the Gospel.

7. That good works are necessary: for Paul says, necessity is laid upon me, namely of obeying the command of God. And yet they ought to be done with the freedom of the Spirit, and by spontaneous motion.

8. Concerning the horrible punishment of those who, on account of the hatreds or persecutions of men, cast away the labors of teaching the Gospel. Woe to me, says Paul, if I do not preach the Gospel.

9. Concerning the third use of the law in the regenerate, since Paul testifies that he was not without law to God: But lived with great zeal according to the law.

10. Concerning the assiduous exercises of the pious, by which they ought to repress the affections of the flesh, and to excite and increase an ardent zeal for piety, and zeal according to knowledge.

11. Concerning the eternal rewards of the labors and struggles, which the pious sustain in the ministry and in their whole life.

12. That the teachers of the Church ought to shine before the flock of the Lord with an illustrious example of piety. For as Lactantius truly said, Those who give precepts, but do not do them, faith is absent from them.

Latin:

Loci Doctrinae.

1. Primus est de libertate Christiana & de legitimo eius usu, qui regi debet dilectione proximi & ad gloriam divini nominis, ad illustrationem Evangelii, & aedificationem Ecclesiae.

2. Insigne testimonium de resurrectione Iesu Christi, siquidem Paulus dominum Iesum post adscensionem in coelum vidit.

3. De efficacia ministerii Evangelici, quod docentium labor non abeat absque fructis, Sed per eum colligatur Deo sancta Ecclesia.

4. Quae sit omnium optima ratio refutandi adversarios, nimirum ut eos remittamus ad Ecclesiam Dei nostro labore & ministerio collectam, & confirmatam.

5. De coniugio sacerdotum seu ministrorum Evangelii, quòd Apostoli Petrus, & fratres domini alii fuerint coniuges, unde manifestum est legem pontificum Rom: de coelibatu sacerdotum esse doctrinam Daemoniorum.

6. In hoc capite quasi sedes est doctrinae, quod ministri Ecclesiae & eorum familiae honestis stipendiis ab Ecclesia nutriri & foveri debeant: Prolixè enim hunc locum tractat Apostolics, & multis gravissimis argumentis docet alimenta & huius vitae necessaria omninò deberi fideliter docentibus & servientibus Ecclesiae. Ac inprimis notatu dignissimum est, quod inquit dominum nostrum Iesum Christum sic ordinasse, ut hi qui serviunt Evangelio, de Evangelio vivant.

7. Quod bona opera sint necessaria: Paulus enim inquit, necessitas mihi incumbit scilicet obediendi mandato Dei. Et tamen fieri debent libertate Spiritus, & motu spontaneo.

8. De horribili poena eorum qui propter hominum odia aut persecutiones abiiciunt docendi Evangelion labores. Vae mihi inquit Paulus, nisi Evangeliza vero.

9. De tertio legis usu in renatis, siquidem Paulus testatur se non fuisse sine lege Deo: Sed magno studio iuxta legem vixisse.

10. De adsiduis exercitiis piorum, quibus adfectus carnis reprimere, & ardens pietatis studium, & zelum secundum scientiam excitare & augere debent.

11. De aeternis praemiis laborum & certaminum, quae sustinent pii in ministerio & tota vita.

12. Quòd doctores Ecclesiae illustri exemplo pietatis praelucere debeant gregi domini. Nam ut verè dixit Lactantius, Qui praecipiunt, nec faciunt, abest ab iis fides.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X.

The doctrine having been set forth concerning the avoiding of the abuse of liberty, and what true Christian liberty is, namely that all things are pure to the pure, lest anyone should receive this most wholesome and most full-of-consolation doctrine wrongly, and should abuse it for the excuse of idolatry or other impieties, Paul meets the false interpretations of his doctrine, and because there were many blemishes and lapses in the Corinthian Church, Paul preaches concerning the necessity of good works according to the decalogue, with examples proposed by which in the Old Testament God testified to His wrath against the disobedient. And the Apostle looks primarily to this in this chapter, that the Corinthians, on account of the title of Church, the glory of the ministry, and the use of the sacraments, might not grow proud and give themselves over to carnal security, but might live in perpetual fear of the Lord and seriously exercise piety: since the title of Church and the ministry of Moses and the presence of Christ and the use of sacraments and miracles did not help the secure and impious Israelites, so that the wrath of God would not overwhelm them: therefore God is always to be feared and security is to be avoided, and it is to be sought that we be confirmed in faith. He mixes, however, in this place, in the Apostolic manner, a notable consolation, that God does not desert His own, nor does He present more grievous temptations than we can bear, lest the pious, looking upon the lapses of many, be completely broken in spirit and cast away the exercise of faith. Then with a peculiar zeal he advises that they should beware of idolatry and depart from idols, since they should have no commerce with the impious sacrifices of idols. For God wills that His Church be separated from the worshippers of idols. Finally, he teaches to what extent it is permitted for a Christian to attend the banquets of gentile friends, and how the consciences of the weak are to be spared in such a case. Lastly, he advises that we should refer all things to the glory of God and the benefit of the Church.

Latin:

CAPUT X.

Exposita doctrina de vitando abusu libertatis, & quae sit vera libertas Christiana, quòd nimirum omnia sint munda mundis, ne quis hanc saluberrimam & consolationis plenissimam doctrinam sinistrè acciperet, & ad excusationem Idolatriae, vel aliarum impietatum ea abuteretur, occurrit Paulus falsis interpretationibus suae doctrinae, & quia multi naevi, & lapsus erant in Ecclesia Corinthiaca, concionatur Paulus de necessitate bonorum operum iuxta decalogum, propositis exemplis quibus in veteri testamento Deus iram suam adversus inobedientes testatus est. Atque huc inprimis respicit Apostolus in hoc capite, Ne Corinthii propter titulum Ecclesiae, gloriam ministerii, & usum sacramentorum superbiant & sese dedant securitati carnali, sed in perpetuo timore domini vivant & pietatem seriò exerceant: siquidem titulus Ecclesiae & ministerium Mosis & praesentia Christi, & usus sacramentorum & miraculorum nihil iuvit securos & impios Israëlitas, quò minus ira Dei ipsos obrueret: semper itaque timendum esse Deum & vitandam securitatem, & petendum ut in fide confirmemur. Miscet autem hoc loco more Apostolico insignem consolationem, quòd Deus non deserat suos, nec obiiciat graviores tentationes quam ferre possimus, ne pii plurimorum lapsus intuentes planè frangantur animo & abiiciant fidei exercitium. Deinde peculiari studio monet, ut caveant idolatriam & ab idolis discedant, cum impiis idolorum sacrificiis nihil habeant commertii. Vult enim Deus Ecclesiam suam seiunctam esse à cultoribus idolorum. Tandem quatenus liceat Christiano ad gentilium amicorum convivia accedere, & quomodo infirmorum conscientiae in tali casu parcendum sit, docet. Postremò monet, ut omnia ad Dei gloriam & emolumentum Ecclesiae referamus.

## 10:1-4
I would not have you ignorant brethren, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea, and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them. And the rock was Christ.

About to exhort the Corinthians that they should beware of carnal security and foolish presumption on account of the title of Church, he places before their eyes a very illustrious example of the Church in the Old Testament, namely the Israelites, whom Moses led out of Egypt through the desert. And first their glory, then their fall, thirdly he sets forth the punishments: That the Corinthians, warned by this illustrious example, may learn to fear the Lord. Our fathers, he says, were all under the cloud: That is, Great and excellent was the glory of the people of Israel whom Moses led out of Egypt. For they saw assiduously the presence of God, who by day in a pillar of cloud, and by night in a pillar of fire, both went before and covered, and illuminated the camps of the Israelites. Nothing similar is read in the whole history of the world, that God has so testified his presence every single day: and in this army he did it. The history which exists in Exo: 14. and Nume: 9. must be repeated here. Moreover, this is the nature of Paul's argumentation. Although the glory of the people of Israel whom Moses led out of Egypt was huge, so much so that they had God present daily, and were protected by the pillar of cloud by which God testified his presence, nevertheless this glory did not save them, nor did it make them immune from punishments, but nonetheless, when they sinned securely, and provoked the wrath of God, God punished them most gravely, and cast away very many. Thus, although now your glory also may be great, because you are the Church of God, because you have been liberated from the idols of the nations, you have been gifted with the visible effusion of the Holy Spirit: You speak in various tongues, you have the ministry of the Gospel, and the use of the Sacraments, by which Christ testifies his presence, nevertheless you ought not from this promise security to yourselves, as if punishments could not reach you, even if you you have defiled with crimes: But you must establish it altogether certainly, just as God did not spare that people, whom He had adorned with such great glory, nor will He spare you, secure and unrepentant, on account of the title. This is the scope of Paul's argumentation. That he says all were baptized into Moses under the cloud and through the sea, he signifies that that Church was gathered by the ministry of Moses, and that huge miracles were performed in it through Moses, so that the Church was certain of the will of God, of religion and worship, and of divine revelations. But because they abused this such great glory and such great benefits of God for security, they did not bear this with impunity, but paid heavy penalties, from which we can take an example of how it will turn out for us if we are secure in such great benefits of God. The pious reader must be altogether admonished here of the notable corruption of this Pauline passage which Calvin has petulantly attempted to foist upon the Church of God. For because Paul says that all the Israelites ate the same spiritual food, Calvin explains this as if Paul were comparing the Church of the Old Testament with the Church of the New Testament: And were saying that the Israelites ate the same spiritual food in the desert that we eat in the holy supper of the Lord. And from this he attempts to gather further that we in the New Testament and in the supper of the Lord do not eat the flesh of Christ otherwise than the fathers ate it in the desert, namely through faith. But this is a manifest and petulant depravation of the Pauline text.

For Paul does not compare the Israelites in the desert with us, but among themselves: he does not say that the Israelites ate the same spiritual food that we eat, for he speaks of the eating of Manna, which we have never seen, much less tasted. It is therefore a remarkable and manifest imposture, because τὸ ἀυτὸ βρῶμα does not refer to the Church of the new testament, but only to all those whom Moses led out of Egypt. Although all these ate Manna and the bread of angels, yet they did not bear their impiety and crimes with impunity, just as if you were to say that all who were in the ark of Noah in the flood were saved, and yet not all pleased God.

Furthermore, that Paul names spiritual food, he does not speak of the spiritual eating of the body of Christ which is done through faith, but of the eating of Manna, which was a corporal food nourishing the bodies of the Israelites: Therefore Paul calls Manna spiritual food, and the water flowing from the rock spiritual drink, because that food and drink was not given by the common law of nature, but miraculously from heaven, and through the power of Christ who was present ruling that army. Ambrose could have warned Calvin about this exposition, who explains the words of Paul most clearly in this manner: He calls these, Manna and the water which flowed from the rock, spiritual: Because they were not prepared by the law of the world, but by the power of God without the mixture of elements, to a time created, having in themselves the figure of the future mystery, which we now take in commemoration of Christ the Lord. Ambrose explicitly says that they are therefore called spiritual by Paul, because they were not created by the law of the world: From this, therefore, no argument can be drawn concerning the presence or absence of the body of Jesus Christ in the holy supper.

They drank, he says, from the spiritual one, the rock accompanying them: but the rock was Christ. In order to illustrate the immense glory of the Israelite people, he shows the efficient cause of the miraculous food and drink. Jesus Christ, he says, the eternal and omnipotent God, the perpetual guardian of his Church, the truly spiritual rock, which is the immovable foundation of the whole house of God, which is the Church, was always accompanying that army, ruling and protecting it, bestowing immense benefits upon it, and adorning it with excellent glory: Which the Israelites ought to have received with a grateful mind and cultivated piety with so much greater zeal: But they abused so many innumerable benefits for carnal security: And so they were punished. This passage is very remarkable: For it is in place of a narration of the four books of Moses. For Paul, with an apostolic spirit, testifies that Moses speaks of Jesus Christ, as often as he reports in Exodus and the following books that the Lord Jehovah was present in that people, had given commands through Moses, had led the people, had performed miracles, had shown his glory, had repressed and finally destroyed enemies, to have punished the secure, and the rebellious: to have promulgated the law, to have instituted the priesthood, and to have founded that whole polity. Therefore, Paul provides us with very many testimonies and arguments that Jesus Christ, crucified and resurrected for us, is the eternal and omnipotent God.

But with most of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness. Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.

By the examples of the Israelite people he now teaches that external glory of the Church helps nothing unless you pursue piety from the heart. The history which he mentions here exists in Num. 11. where the people burned with the desire of eating meat, and Jesus Christ indeed gave them meat: but while the meat was still between their teeth, the wrath of the Lord was kindled and He struck the people with a very great slaughter. Therefore, we in the Church must take care that we do not indulge our desires: lest we also provoke the grave wrath of God, and bring great punishments upon ourselves.

Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written:

Latin:

Nolim autem vos ignorare fratres, quòd patres nostri omnes sub nube erant, & omnes per mare transierunt, & omnes in Mosen Baptizati sunt in nube & in mari, & omnes eandem escam spiritualem comedebant, & omnes potum spiritualem bibebant. Bibebant enim de spirituali, quae eos comitabatur, petra. Petra verò fuit Christus.

Adhortaturus Corinthios, ut sibi caveant à carnali securitate, & stulta praesumptione propter titulum Ecclesiae, ponit eis ob oculos exemplum Ecclesiae in veteri testamento valdè illustre, nimirum Israelitas, quos Moses duxit, ex Aegypto per desertum. Ac primùm ipsorum gloriam, deinde lapsus, tertiò poenas exponit: Ut hoc exemplo illustri admoniti Corinthii discant timere Dominum. Patres nostri inquit, sub nube omnes erant: Id est, Magna et excellens fuit gloria populi Israel quem Moses duxit ex Aegypto. Adsiduè enim videbant praesentiam Dei, qui interdiu in columna nubis, noctu columna ignis & praecedebat & tegebat, & illuminabat castra Israelitarum. Nihil simile legitur in tota mundi historia, quòd Deus ita singulis diebus praesentiam suam sit testatus: atque in hoc exercitu fecit. Repetenda hic est historia quae extat Exo: 14. & Nume: 9. Est autem huiusmodi Pauli argumentatio. Etsi ingens fuit gloria populi Israel quem Moses eduxit ex Aegypto, adeò ut quotidie Deum habuerint praesentem, & columna nubis qua Deus praesentiam suam testabatur protegebantur, haec tamen gloria non salvavit eos, nec fecit eos immunes à poenis, sed nihilominus, cum securè peccarent, & iram Dei provocarent, gravissimè eos punivit Deus, & plurimos abiecit. Ita etsi nunc & vestra gloria magna sit, quòd sitis Ecclesia Dei, quòd liberati estis ab idolis gentium, donati estis visibili effusione Spiritus sancti: Loquimini variis linguis, habetis ministerium Evangelii, & usum Sacramentorum, quibus Christus suam testatur praesentiam, non tamen hinc securitatem vobis promittere debetis, quasi poenae non possint vos attingere, etiamsi vos contaminaveritis sceleribus: Sed omninò certò statuere debetis, sicut Deus non pepercit isti populo, quem tanta gloria ornaverat, nec vobis securis & impoenitentibus propter titulum parsurum esse. Hic est scopus argumentationis Pauli. Quòd dicit omnes sub nube, & per mare in Mosen baptizatos esse, significat istam Ecclesiam ministerio Mosis collectam, & in ea ingentia miracula per Mosen edita esse, ita ut Ecclesia certa fuerit de voluntate Dei, de religione & cultu, & de divinis patefactionibus. Quia verò hac tanta gloria & tantis Dei beneficiis ad securitatem abutebantur, non tulerunt hoc impunè, sed graves dederunt poenas, unde exemplum sumere possumus, quomodo nobis cessurum sit si securi in tantis Dei beneficiis fuerimus. Omnino admonendus hic est pius lector de insigni corruptela huius loci Paulini quam Calvinus petulanter Ecclesiae Dei obtrudere conatus est. Quia enim Paulus dicit omnes Israelitas eandem escam spiritualem manducasse, Calvinus hoc sic enarrat, ac si Paulus Ecclesiam veteris testamenti cum Ecclesia novi testamenti conferret: Et diceret Israelitas eandem escam spiritualem comedisse in deserto, quam nos comedimus in sacra coena domini. Et hinc amplius colligere conatur nos in novo testamento & in coena domini non aliter manducare carnem Christi, quam eam patres in deserto manducarunt, nimirum per fidem. Verum haec manifesta & petulans est depravatio textus Paulini.

Paulus enim non confert in Israelitas in deserto nobiscum, sed inter se: non dicit Israelitas eandem escam spiritualem comedissè quam nos edimus, loquitur enim de manducatione Manna, quod nos nunquam vidimus, nedum gustavimus. Insignis igitur & manifesta impostura est, quia τὸ ἀυτὸ βρῶμα non respicit Ecclesiam novi testamenti, sed tantum eos omnes quos Moses ex Aegypto eduxit. Hi licet omnes comederint Manna & panem angelorum, tamen impietatem & scelera non tulerunt impunè, ut si dicas omnes qui fuerunt in arca Nohe in diluvio sunt servati, & tamen non omnes placuerunt Deo.

Deinde quòd Paulus nominat escam spiritualem, non loquitur de manducatione corporis Christi spirituali quae fit per fidem, sed de manducatione Manna, quae fuit corporalis esca nutriens corpora Israelitarum: Idcircò autem Paulus nominat Manna escam spiritualem, & aquam fluentem è petra potum spiritualem, quòd cibus ille & potus non fuerit communi lege naturae datus, sed miraculosè de coelo, & per virtutem Christi qui praesens regebat istum exercitum. De hac expositione Calvinum monere potuisset Ambrosius, qui in hunc modum verba Pauli planissimè exponit: Manna & aquam quae fluxit de petra, haec dicit spiritualia: Quia non mundi lege parata sunt, sed Dei virtute sine elementorum commixtione, ad tempus creata, habentia in se figuram futuri mysterii, quod nunc sumimus in commemorationem Christi domini. Disertè dicit Ambrosius ideò dici à Paulo spiritualia, quia non sint mundi lege creata: Hinc ergò de praesentia vel absentia corporis Iesu Christi in sacra coena nullum argumentum sumi potest.

Bibebant inquit ex spirituali, comitante eos petra: Petra autem erat Christus. Ut illustret ingentem gloriam populi Israelitici, causam ostendit efficientem miraculosi cibi & potus. Iesus Christus inquit aeternus & omnipotens Deus, perpetuus custos suae Ecclesiae, verè spiritualis petra, quae immotum fundamentum est totius domus Dei, quae est Ecclesia, semper comitabatur istum exercitum, regebat & tuebatur eum, immensis beneficiis adficiebat, & excellenti gloria ornabat eum: Quae Israelitae grato animo debuissent accipere & tanto maiore studio colere pietatem: Verùm abusi sunt tot innumeris beneficiis ad carnalem securitatem: Itaque sunt puniti. Hic locus insignis est admodum: Est enim vice enarrationis in quatuor libros Mosis. Paulus enim Apostolico spiritu testatur, Mosen de Iesu Christo loqui, quoties in Exodo & libris sequentibus refert Dominum Iehovae fuisse in isto populo praesentem, mandata dedisse per Mosen, duxisse populum, edidisse miracula, ostendisse suam gloriam, repressisse & tandem delevisse hostes, punivisse securos, & rebelles: promulgasse legem, instituisse sacerdotium, & totam istam condidissè politiam. Plurima igitur testimonia, & argumenta suppeditat nobis Paulus, quòd Iesus Christus pro nobis crucifixus & resuscitatus sit aeternus & omnipotens Deus.

Verum plerique ipsorum non placuerunt Deo: prostrati enim sunt in deserto. Haec autem figurae nobis fuerunt, ne nos simus concupiscentes rerum malarum quemadmodum & illi concupiverunt.

Exemplis populi Israelitici nunc docet, nihil iuvare externam gloriam Ecclesiae nisi ex animo secteris pietatem. Historia cuius hic meminit extat Nume: 11. ubi populus flagravit desiderio edendi carnes, & Iesus Christus dedit quidem carnes: sed dum caro adhuc inter dentes versaretur, exarsit ira domini & percussit populum clade admodum magna. Nos ergò in Ecclesia cavere debemus, ne cupiditatibus nostris indulgeamus: ne & nos gravem Dei iram provocemus, & magnas poenas nobis accersamus.

Neque idolatrae sitis, sicuti quidam illorum, quemadmodum scriptum est:

## 10:7
The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

By another example of the people of Israel, he exhorts us that we should avoid idolatry: lest we incur the indignation of God and be severely punished. For in one day 3000 of the Israelites were slain. The history exists Exod: 32:

Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and fell in one day 23000 men:

This history exists Numbers: 25. And by this example Paul severely warns that Christians should avoid lusts and all prohibited mixtures.

Latin:

Sedit populus ut ederet & biberet, & surrexerunt, ad ludendum.

Alio exemplo populi Israel nos hortatur ut vitemus Idolatriam: ne incurramus in Dei indignationem & graviter puniamur. Uno die enim 3000. Israelitarum intersecta sunt. Historia extat Exod: 32:

Neque scortemur, quemadmodum quidam illorum scortati sunt, & ceciderunt una die 23000 hominum:

Haec historia extat Numeri: 25. Et hoc exemplo severè monet Paulus, ut Christiani vitent libidines & omnes prohibitas commixtiones.

## 10:9
Neither let us tempt Christ as some of them tempted, and were destroyed by serpents.

Because he says that Christ is not to be tempted, just as the Israelites tempted Christ, by that he provides us light into the whole of Moses; for with an Apostolic Spirit he warns that whatever Moses writes concerning Jehovah who accompanied the camps of the Israelites, and performed huge miracles among this people, this is to be understood of our Lord Jesus Christ, the perpetual guardian of the Church is to be understood. To tempt Christ is to depart from the doctrine of Christ, to undertake things outside of one's calling, not to believe in the miracles performed by Christ, to demand miracles from Christ out of caprice and curiosity, and to attempt great and dangerous things out of presumption and without a command from God, and without faith in Christ. The history exists Exo: 17. Is the Lord in our midst? they say. By which voice they openly testified that they had applied faith neither to the ministry of Moses nor to so many divine miracles.

Neither murmur, as some of them murmured, and were destroyed by the destroyer.

The Israelites murmured very often against the Lord, as Exod: 16.Nu: 11.Numeri: 14. and elsewhere. But because he mentions the destroyer here, there is no doubt that he refers to the history of Numeri: 16. Where Moses relates how the opening of the earth swallowed up Core and Datan, the faction of the seditious: and on the following day the people murmured against Moses, as if he had destroyed the people of God. And the anger of God flared up and He sent fire from heaven, which devoured 14700 Israelites in the army. It is to be observed in this place, that those who murmur against faithful pastors and ministers, murmur against the son of God Jesus Christ, and by that very murmuring show their impatience, diffidence and hatred against Christ, and bring heavy punishments upon themselves.

Now all these things happened to them as figures: but they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come. Wherefore he that thinketh himself to stand, let him take heed lest he fall.

He now applies the Examples of the ancient Church to the Corinthians and to individual Christians. All these things happened to the Israelites in the desert, that they might be types; That is, examples of the wrath of God against the secure and the impious in every age of the Church. For that time of the leading of the people out of Egypt was very illustrious: Therefore, if God did not spare that people so glorious and adorned with so many miracles, but punished them most severely: it can easily be gathered that God will spare no one on account of an external title and the glory of the Church. We therefore ought often to repeat the histories of the whole Church and of the world: and by the consideration of the examples of the wrath of God to kindle ourselves to the fear of God and piety. God did not spare Jerusalem, the most flourishing city, which was the one seat of doctrine, and the dwelling of God on earth among men: but He horribly laid it waste on account of the contempt of the word and the slaughter of the Son: God did not spare the most flourishing kingdoms and nations: He did not spare Asia, He did not spare Greece, He did not spare Egypt, He did not spare Africa, He did not spare Antioch, He did not spare Ephesus, He did not spare Corinth, He did not spare Constantinople, He did not spare Rome. Therefore, let no one flatter himself in security or contempt of the word of God, as if God were going to spare him on account of the title of Church or the dignity of office: but let him rather conclude this, that by how much greater gifts he is endowed by God, and by how much more honorable a place he occupies in the Church, by so much heavier penalties he is going to pay, if he has provoked the wrath of God by security and impiety.

That he says that the things which happened to them were types, teaches that those things which happened to the people of the old testament shadow forth many things for us, and figuratively signify what is to be expected by us in similar cases. And he warns that we should always look upon the history of the whole Church. He also shows the use of the whole of holy scripture, he says all things were written for our sake, so that the examples of the wrath of God might warn us, and might excite in us serious piety, fear, and love of God.

Upon whom the ends of the ages have come: this particle warns that the end of the world is not far off: And because Christ has been exhibited, and all promises have been fulfilled, and the Mosaic polity has been abolished, the Gospel has been scattered into the whole world by the ministry of the Apostles, and the nations have been co-opted into the society of the Church, there is no reason why we should expect either the restoration of the Mosaic polity, or a new state of the Church or new sacraments, or new prophecies, but we ought to expect with certain confidence and hope the end of the world which is at the doors and the joyful coming of Jesus Christ from heaven in the clouds. For the world will not last forever, as the philosophers have trifled: but heaven and earth will perish by fire, and indeed that last day of the world is not far off. Lord Jesus Christ, only-begotten Son of God, sitting at the right hand of the eternal Father, enlighten, strengthen, and rule us with your Holy Spirit, that we may constantly persist in the true knowledge of you and in the confidence of your merits, and may receive your glorious coming from the heavens with great joy of heart, and may live with you in all eternity. Amen.

He who stands, let him see that he does not fall: This is the sum of the whole exhortation. That one must not be proud on account of gifts, not presumptuous on account of the title of the Church, not live securely, but must live perpetually in the fear of God, and take heed by prayer and diligence lest we be overturned by Satan. Great men have fallen. Aaron, Gideon, Saul, David. Absalom, Asa, Joash, Judas: many of whom perished. And we can suffer something human. Therefore let us not be proud but let us assiduously pray to the Lord that his good Spirit may lead us into the right way Psal: 143.

Latin:

Nec tentemus Christum quemadmodum quidam illorum tentarunt, & à serpentibus extincti sunt.

Quòd dicit Christum non esse tentandum, quemadmodum Israelitae Christum tentarunt, eo lumen nobis praebet in totum Mosem Apostolico enim Spiritu monet, quidquid Moses de Iehovae qui comitatus est castra Israelitarum, & ingentia miracula in hoc populo edidit, scribit, hoc de domino nostro Iesu Christo perpetuo custode Ecclesiae intelligendum esse. Tentare Christum, est discedere à doctrina Christi, suscipere res extra vocationem, non credere miraculis à Christo editis, poscere miracula à Christo, pro libidine & curiositate, Et tentare res magnas & periculosas ex praesumtione & sine mandato Dei, & sine fide in Christum. Historia extat Exo: 17. Est ne dominus in medio nostri? inquiunt. Qua voce palam testati sunt se nec ministerio Mosis, nec tot divinis miraculis fidem adhibuisse.

Nec murmurate, sicut quidam illorum murmuraverunt, & interempti sunt à vastatore.

Saepissimè murmurarunt Israelitae contra Dominum, ut Exod: 16.Nu: 11.Numeri: 14. & alias. Sed quia hic vastatoris meminit non est dubium quin respiciat ad historiam Numeri: 16. Ubi Moses refert quomodo hiatus terrae absorbsit Core & Datan, factionem seditiosorum: & postero die populus murmuravit contra Mosen, quasi is populum Dei deleverit. Et ira Dei excanduit & misit ignem de coelo, qui devoravit in exercitu 14700. Israelitas. Observandum est hoc in loco, quòd qui murmurant contra fideles pastores & ministros, contra filium Dei Iesum Christum murmurent, & ipso murmure suam impatientiam, diffidentiam et odium adversus Christum demonstrent, & poenas graves sibi accersant.

Haec autem omnia figurae contigerunt illis: scripta verò sunt propter admonitionem nostri, in quos termini aetatum inciderunt. Qua propter qui stare videtur, videat ne cadat.

Accommodat nunc Exempla veteris Ecclesiae, ad Corinthios & singulos Christianos. Ista omnia evenerunt Israelitis in deserto, ut essent typi; Id est, exemplaria irae Dei adversus securos & impios omni tempore Ecclesiae. Illud enim tempus eductionis populi ex Aegypto fuit admodum illustre: Quòd si ergò Deus non pepercit isti populo tam glorioso & tot miraculis ornato, sed punivit eos severissimè: colligi facilè potest Deum nemini parsurum esse propter externum titulum & gloriam Ecclesiae. Nos ergò saepè repetere debemus totius Ecclesiae & mundi historias: & consideratione exemplorum irae Dei nos ad timorem Dei & pietatem accendere. Non pepercit Deus Hierosolymis florentissimae urbi, quae una erat sedes doctrinae, & domicilium Dei in terris apud homines: sed horribiliter eam vastavit propter contemptum verbi & necem filii: Non pepercit Deus florentissimis regnis & nationibus: Non Asiae, non Graeciae, non Aegypto, non Africae, non pepercit Antiochiae, Non Epheso, Non Corintho, non Constantinapoli, non Romae. Nemo ergò blandiatur sibi in securitate, vel contemptu verbi Dei, quasi Deus illi sit parsurus, propter titulum Ecclesiae vel officii dignitatem: sed hoc potius statuat, quò maioribus donis à Deo est adfectus, quò honestiorem locum in Ecclesia obtinet, hoc graviores poenas est daturus, si securitate & impietate provocaverit iram Dei.

Quòd dicit typos fuisse, quae illis evenerunt, docet ea quae acciderunt populo veteris testamenti multa nobis adumbrare, & figuratè significare quid nobis in similibus casibus sit expectandum. Ac monet ut semper intueamur totius Ecclesiae historiam. Usum etiam totius sacrae scripturaeostendit, omnia inquit nostra causa scripta sunt, ut exempla irae Dei nos admonerent, et in nobis seriam pietatem, timorem & dilectionem Dei excitarent.

In quos finis seculorum incidit: haec particula monet finem mundi non procul abesse: Ac quia Christus exhibitus est, & omnes promissiones impletae, & abolita politia Mosaica, Evangelium ministerio Apostolorum in totum orbem sparsum, & gentes in societatem Ecclesiae cooptatae sunt, non est quod expectemus vel restitutionem politiae Mosaicae, vel novum statum Ecclesiae aut nova sacramenta, aut nova vaticima, sed omninò finem mundi qui est prae foribus & laetum Iesu Christi adventum de coelo in nubibus certa fiducia & spe expectare debemus. Non enim perpetuò durabit mundus, ut philosophi nugati sunt: sed coelum & terra peribunt igni, & quidem ultimus ille mundi dies non procul abest. Domine Iesu Christe unigenite fili Dei, sedens ad dexteram aeterni patris illumina, confirma & rege nos Spiritutuo sancto, ut in vera agnitione tui, & fiducia tuorum meritorum constanter persistamus, & gloriosum tuum de coelis adventum ingenti laeticia cordis excipiamus, & tecum in omni aeternitate vivamus. Amen.

Qui stat videat ne cadat: Haec summa est totius adhortationis. Non superbiendum esse propter dona, non praesumendum propter titulum Ecclesiae, non securè vivendum esse, sed perpetuò in timore Dei vivendum, & oratione et diligentia cavendum ne à Satana evertamur. Magni viri lapsi sunt. Aaron, Gideon, Saul, David. Absolon, Assa, Ioas, Iudas: quorum multi perierunt. Et nos humani aliquid pati possumus. Non ergò superbiamus sed adsiduè oremus dominum ut bonus Spiritus eius deducat nos in viam rectam Psal: 143.

## 10:13
No temptation has taken you except what is human, but God is faithful who He will not suffer you to be tempted above that you are able: But will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that you may be able to bear it.

The pious must be fortified on both sides: Both that they may not slip into carnal security, elated by confidence in gifts: And that they may not be submerged in desperation, while they contemplate both their own immense weakness, and the most severe wrath of God. Therefore, after Paul, having recited many examples of divine wrath, deterred the Corinthians from security and presumption, lest the weaker and more timid, contemplating the most grave falls of the Jewish people, and the most severe examples of divine wrath, and at the same time weighing their own immense weakness, should cast down their spirit and despair of obtaining salvation, he raises them up with a signal consolation. Provided they seriously and without hypocrisy pursue piety, and seek salvation, God will not be wanting to them with His aid, nor will He suffer them to be oppressed by the magnitude of temptations. There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man, that is, Although God has hitherto exercised your faith with temptations: Yet He so tempers and moderates them, that you may be able to endure and overcome them by the aid of the Holy Spirit, provided you are willing to struggle against the affections of the flesh with the Spirit, faith, and invocation. A human temptation is that which proceeds from one's own unclean and corrupt flesh, and which is accustomed to exercise the human race. And the Apostle signifies there are other more serious temptations, Diabolical, which utterly overthrow men and so entangle them, that they cannot return to God: it was a Diabolical temptation that Saul cast away all trust in God, feared only for his own glory, and at length sought help from Satan. Thus the temptation of Achitophel was Diabolical, and of Judas, who, despairing of pardon from God, strangled themselves. It was a Diabolical temptation that Nestorius was the author of a new dogma, nor could he be brought back to a sounder mind. It was a Diabolical temptation that Franciscus Spira denied the truth, and thereafter admitted no consolation, but cried out that he was being accused before the Eternal Father by the Son. Likewise, that Latomus confessed that he had attacked the acknowledged truth against his conscience, and therefore that he was damned and could not obtain pardon. This is the horrible power of Satan by which he dementates the reprobate, so that they cannot return to repentance, and God permits such examples, that the Church may learn to fear the snares and power of Satan.

Other temptations are milder, which the Apostle here calls human: namely, when men either out of the weakness of their own flesh fall into sins against conscience, or are even driven by Satan, being incautious, into sins, or are vexed by persecutions on account of the truth. In these falls, or even persecutions, while the mind is not hardened by an Epicurean contempt of God, nor inflamed by the hatred of God and the fury of Satan, there is hope of returning to salutary repentance, especially when we are called through the word of God. There is certainly no temptation so light or small that it cannot cast us down from the degree of faith and precipitate us into eternal destruction, if we rely only on our own strengths, but since we are led by the Holy Spirit to repentance, we are raised up and confirmed by the help of God, we can overcome temptations.

There are indeed innumerable temptations that exercise the Church, some are spiritual, others are corporal. They are spiritual when we doubt about God, about providence, whether we are in the number of the elect, we are tempted concerning the will of God toward us, when the pious fall into sins against conscience, when they doubt about perseverance, when they fear the curse of the law: When they feel constant terrors of conscience, and fear eternal rejection. Others are corporal when the pious are anxious about food, about lodging, about defense: When they sustain exiles, miseries, hardships, diseases, prisons, on account of the profession of the truth. But of whatever kind the temptations may be, it must be known that certain help is promised to us, if anyone has fallen into sin against conscience, God promises forgiveness, As I live I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he may be converted and live Ezech: 33. And Christ says: Come to me all you who labor and are burdened and I will refresh you. Matt: 11. If our immense weakness and the monstrous power of Satan terrify us, the promise of Christ ought to raise us up: John: 10. No one shall snatch my sheep from my hand. If we are tempted concerning food and things necessary for this life, the saying is at hand: Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God. Matt: 4. In sum, there is no temptation so savage that the word of God does not supply us with most efficacious consolations in it. And in this place, the notable promise which offers us help in every temptation must be diligently observed and fixed in the depths of our hearts: God is faithful toward all and each, who does not allow us to be tempted beyond our strength, but grants such an outcome of the temptation, he so moderates them, that we may be able to endure.

Therefore my beloved, flee from idolatry: I speak as to sensible people: Judge for yourselves what I say.

At the beginning of this chapter, he exhorted the Corinthians that, warned by the example of the ancient Church, they should beware of various crimes, lest they provoke the wrath of God and draw punishments upon themselves: But because it was difficult to lead away those accustomed to idolatry throughout their whole life, he repeats with peculiar zeal the commandment concerning fleeing from idolatry and preaches at length about it, having shown the causes which ought to warn us to flee idolatry, and the whole address of the Apostle pertains to the first commandment of the decalogue. For idolatry is a sin against the first commandment, by which some divinity is fashioned besides the true God the father of our Lord Jesus Christ, and trust is placed either in a creature of God, or in a figment of men, and the honors which are owed to God alone are attributed to a fictitious divinity.

Paul calls the citizens of the Church prudent: For true prudence is only in the Church of Christ: In which the Holy Spirit illuminates the minds of men, and the word of God, the fountain of all wisdom, shines. Hilary spoke gravely and piously in De Trinitate, book 5: Impiety has nothing of wisdom in itself: And, the fear of God which is the beginning of wisdom, where it is lacking, takes away with it every beginning of prudence.

The Apostle Paul defers the judgment concerning his doctrine to the Church: Therefore it is permitted to the whole Church of Christ, and to individual hearers, as well laymen as they are called, as clerics, as well unlearned persons, as the highest Bishops, to inquire into the doctrine of their pastors, and to pass judgment concerning controversies. Just as Christ also teaches, Beware of false prophets. Matth: 7.

Latin:

Tentatio vos non adprehendit nisi humana, fidelis autem est Deus qui non sinet vos tentari, supra vires: Sed faciet ut tentatio eum sortiatur exitum, Ut ferre possitis.

Utrinque muniendi sunt pii: Et ne labantur in securitatem carnalem elati fiducia donorum: Et ne mergantur in desperationem, dum intuentur & suam ingentem imbecillitatem, & severissimam Dei iram. Post quam ergò Paulus recitatis multis exempliis irae divinae à securitate & praesumptione Corinthios deterruit, ne imbecilliores & timidiores, intuentes gravissimos lapsus populi Iudaici, & severissima exempla irae divinae & simul expendentes ingentem suam imbecillitatem abiiciant animum, & de salute adipiscenda desperent, erigit eos insigni consolatione. Modò seriò & sine hypocrisi sectentur pietatem, & expetant salutem, Deum non defuturum ipsis suo auxilio, nec passurum ut tentationum magnitudine opprimantur.
