Tantum humana tentatio vos adprehendit, id est, Etsi Deus hactenus exercuit vestram fidem tentationibus: Tamen eas ita temperat & moderatur, ut sufferre & auxilio Spiritus sancti superare possitis, modò Spiritu, fide & invocatione luctari velitis contra carnis adfectus. Tentatio humana est, quae à propria carne immunda & corrupta proficiscitur, & quae genus humanum exercere solet. Et significat Apostolus esse alias graviores tentationes, Diabolicas, quae prorsus evertunt homines & ita implicant, ut redire non possint ad Deum: Diabolica fuit tentatio, quòd Saul omnem fiduciam in Deum abiecit, tantum suae gloriae metuit, & tandem a Satana opem petivit. Sic Diabolica fuit tentatio Achitophelis, & Iudae, qui desperantes de venia apud Deum seipsos strangularunt. Diabolica fuit tentatio quòd Nestorius novi dogmatis fuit author, nec potuit reduci ad saniorem mentem. Diabolica fuit tentatio, quòd Franciscus Spira abengavit veritatem, & deinde nullam admisit consolationem, sed clamavit, se coram Aeterno patre à filio accusari. Item, Quòd Latomus fassus est se agnitam veritatem contra conscientiam oppugnasse, atque ideò se damnatum esse nec posse consequi veniam. Haec est horribilis potentia Satanae qua dementat reprobos, ut non possint redire ad poenitentiam, ac permittit Deus eiusmodi exempla, ut discat Ecclesia metuere insidias & potentiam Satanae.

Aliae tentationes leniores sunt, quas hümanas hic vocat Apostolus: vide licet cum homines vel ex propria carnis imbecillitate, labuntur in peccata contra conscientiam, vel etiam à Satana incauti impelluntur in peccata, aut persecutionibus vexantur propter veritatem. In his lapsibus, vel etiam persecutionibus, dum animus non est confirmatus Epicureo contemptu Dei, nec odio Dei & furore Satanae inflammatus, spes est redeundi ad salutarem poenitentiam, praesertim cum vocamur per verbum Dei. Nulla sanè est tam levis, vel exigua tentatio quin possit nos deiicere de gradu fidei, & in aeternum exitium praecipitare, si tantum nostris viribus nitamur, sed quoniam Spiritu sancto ducimur ad poenitentiam, erigimur & confirmamur auxilio Dei, vincere possumus tentationes.

Sunt sanè innumerae tentationes quae exercent Ecclesiam, aliae sunt spirituales, aliae corporales. Spirituales sunt, cum dubitamus de Deo, de providentia, num simus in numero electorum, de voluntate Dei erga nos tentamur, cum labuntur pii in peccata contra conscientiam, cum dubitant de perseverantia, cum metuunt legis male dictionem: Cum terrores conscientiae adsiduos sentiunt, & metuunt aeternam abiectionem. Aliae sunt corporales cum soliciti sunt pii de victu, de hospitio, de defensione: Cum sustinent exilia, miserias, aerumnas, morbos, carceres, propter veritatis professionem. Cuiuscunque autem generis sint tentationes, sciendum est certum auxilium nobis promissum esse, si quis in peccatum contra conscientiam prolapsus est, promittit Deus veniam, Vivo ego nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur & vivat Ezech: 33. Et Christus inquit: Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis & onerati estis ego reficiam vos. Matth: 11. Si terret nos ingens nostra infirmitas & immanis potentia Satanae, erigere nos debet promissio Christi: Ioan: 10. Nomo rapiet oves meas de manu mea si de victu, & rebus ad hanc vitam necessariis tentamur, in promptu est dictum: Non in solo pane vivit homo, sed ex omni verbo quod procedit ex ore Dei. Matth: 4. In summa nulla est tam saeva tentatio, quin in ea verbum Dei suppeditet nobis consolationes efficacissimas. Atque hoc loco promissio insignis quae in omni tentatione offert nobis auxilium, diligenter observanda & imis pectoribus est infigenda, fidelis est Deus erga omnes & singulos, qui non sinit nos tentari supra vires, sed talem largitur exitum tentationis, ita moderatur eas, ut nos sufferre possimus.

Quapropter dilecti mei, fugite idolatriam: Tanquam prudentibus loquor: Iudicate vos quod dico.

Initio huius capitis hortatus est Corinthios, ut admoniti exemplo veteris Ecclesiae caverent varia scelera, ne provocarent iram Dei & poenas sibi attraherent: Quia verò difficile erat adsuetos per totam vitam idolatriae, ab ea abducere, peculiari studio repetit praeceptum de fugienda idolatria & de eo prolixè concionatur monstratis causis, quae nos ad fugiendam idolatriam praemonere debent, & tota Apostoli concio ad primum praeceptum decalogi pertinet. Est enim idolatria peccatum contra primum praeceptum, quo fingitur aliquod numen praeter verum Deum patrem domini nostri Iesu Christi, & vel in creaturam Dei, vel in figmentum hominum collocatur fiducia, & honores qui soli Deo debentur fictitio numini tribuuntur.

Prudentes appellat Paulus cives Ecclesiae: Vera enim prudentia tantum est in Ecclesia Christi: In qua Spiritus sanctus illuminat hominum mentes, & lucet verbum Dei fons omnis sapientiae. Graviter & piè dixit Hilarius de Trini: lib: 5. Nihil in se habet sapientiae impietas: Et, Dei timor qui est initium sapientiae, ubi deest, aufert secum omne exordium prudentiae.

Apostolus Paulus defert iudicium de sua doctrina Ecclesiae: Licet ergò toti Ecclesiae Christi, & singulis auditoribus tam laicis ut vocant, quam clericis, tam idiotis, quam summis Episcopis inquirere in doctrinam suorum pastorum, & de controversiis ferre sententiam. Quemadmodum & Christus docet, Cavete vobis à falsis Prophetis. Matth: 7.

## 10:16-17
The cup of blessing, which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? And the bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.

This is the first argument taken from contraries, by which he teaches that idolatry must be fled. He who is a partaker of the body and blood of Christ ought to have nothing in common with idols. Christians become partakers of the body and blood of Jesus Christ: Therefore they ought to have nothing in common with idols. For there is no communion of Christ and Belial: this passage is very significant, if indeed it clearly explains the controversy concerning the presence of the body of Christ in the sacred supper, and most powerfully fortifies the true opinion against the deceptions of the Calvinists, who shamefully pervert the words of Paul. Calvin contends that there is a figure in these words of Paul, and explains it thus. The bread is the communion of the body of Christ, That is, a symbol of the communion of the body of Christ. Others pervert it thus. The bread is that by which fellowship with Christ is made. Bullinger explains it thus, that he says the body of Christ, here allegorically signifies the Church: And one twists the words of Paul one way, another another, but all Calvinists do this, that they may drive out and exterminate the body and blood of Jesus Christ from the sacred supper.

Therefore, we must labor so much the more that we may defend this most precious treasure, and retain the truth of the Apostolic doctrine.

Therefore, as far as the words are concerned, it is certain that κοινωνίαν signifies not society, but communication and participation, which finally even Calvin, convinced by the evidence of the matter, conceded. For Paul explains the term κοινωνίαν by the word μετοχὴν. And Theophyl: He says that κοινωνίαν signifies something more excellent than μετοχὴ,, namely, the highest union with Christ.

The term (body) does not signify in this place the Church, which by allegory is called the body of Christ, but it signifies the very substance of the body of Jesus Christ, which hung for us on the cross, and rose from the dead. For it cannot be denied that Paul is dealing here with the Eucharist, and with the body and blood of Jesus Christ, for he says the cup of blessing, which we bless. And Bullinger's interpretation is inept and violent, when he says the body of Christ here signifies the Church. For since Paul says the cup is the communication of the blood of Christ, this must necessarily be understood not of the Church, but of the true participation of the blood of Christ. Therefore, the words of the Apostle are to be taken properly without figures.

And because it is disputed, whether Paul is speaking of spiritual communication, association, and ingrafting of the saints in Christ, or whether he speaks of a corporal participation: Item, whether it is evident from these words that the body of Jesus Christ is truly present in the holy supper, and is eaten and received by the unworthy and the worthy alike, or not, let us weigh, examine, and ponder the very words of the Holy Spirit.

First, therefore, let the pious reader who is studious of the truth attend to what is the scope of the Pauline disputation, and what the Apostle endeavors to teach. Paul exhorts the Corinthians to flee idolatry and Gentile sacrifices, and in order to persuade the Corinthians to comply, he draws an argument from the doctrine concerning the supper of the Lord: Those who become participants of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, these ought not to become participants of demons. You Corinthians, in the use of the supper of the Lord, are participants of the body and blood of Jesus Christ. Therefore, you ought to flee every fellowship of idols: And to abstain from Gentile sacrifices: that this is Paul's argumentation, both the words themselves, the following arguments, and the whole series of the discourse teach.

From this argumentation, however, it is clear that Paul spoke not figuratively, but properly. For if Paul had meant this, that the bread of the Eucharist is only a sign of the communication of the body of Christ, this argument would have done little to deter the Corinthians from the sacrifices of idols. Nor does Paul understand a spiritual participation of the body of Christ when he says: the bread is the communion of the body of Christ: because he is not treating here only of the faithful and penitent, who approach the holy synaxis with pious motions of the heart, but he is also addressing the impenitent and secure Corinthians, who were contaminating themselves with idolatry and the fellowship of Gentile sacrifices. Since, therefore, he testifies that even those who are secure, and devoid of true faith, communicate in the body and blood of Jesus Christ, as often as they eat of the blessed bread and wine, it is manifest: that Paul is not treating here of the spiritual and salutary participation of the body and blood of Jesus Christ: which the pious, in whom true repentance exists, and faith shines, and who abstain from idolatry and other sins that devastate the conscience, alone perceive: but of another, namely the corporal, which is common as much to the unworthy as to the worthy.

Secondly, to a sound and sensible man it cannot and ought not to be a doubt, but that the Apostle Paul, weaving an argument from the institution of the Lord's supper, looked to the words of Jesus Christ and weighed them, and from these as from a fountain drew his argumentation. Whence it is certainly clear, that it must be that the mind of the words of Paul is the same: is not the bread which we bless the communion of the body of Jesus Christ: which is that of the words of Christ, This is my body. It is manifest, however, from the declaration of Christ, that this is the sense of the words of Christ, This is my body mine: That is, the bread of the Eucharist is the true body of Jesus Christ, because Christ adds: which is given for you. The bread is not a symbol or sign of the body: For the sign of the body was not given for us unto death, but the body of Christ itself, which hung upon the cross. Therefore it is necessary that the sense of Paul's words be the same. Namely, the bread which we bless is the communion of the body of Jesus Christ: That is, it is the body of Jesus Christ itself, of which all become partakers who use the sacred synaxis. These things cannot be overturned by any sophistry. But those who contend that Paul spoke figuratively: that the bread is a sign of the communion of the body of Christ, these do manifest injury to the Apostle Paul, and violently twist the words of the Holy Spirit, and overturn the very words of the institution of the supper. For if the bread of the Eucharist is only a sign of the communion of the body of Christ, it would follow that the words of the supper must also be accepted in this way: namely, that the bread of the Eucharist is a sign of the body: and that the sign of the body was given unto death for our sins. But who does not see with what great impiety those things would be said? Therefore, without any figure, Paul spoke properly, the bread which we bless is the communion of the body of Jesus Christ, That is, the bread of blessing is the body of Jesus Christ itself, of which all become partakers who eat of this bread.

Thirdly, Paul distinctly pronounces the cup of blessing to be the communion of the blood: that the bread of blessing is the communion of the body of Jesus Christ: Therefore the Apostle teaches that in the chalice the blood of Christ itself, and in the bread the body of Christ itself, is communicated to us. For the Apostle looked to the very institution of Christ. To drink the blood of Christ figuratively, and to eat his flesh, is one and the same thing, namely to become a participant in the benefits of Christ through faith: But Paul here attributes the communion of the blood to the chalice of blessing, and attributes the communion of the body to the bread of the Eucharist. Therefore he is not speaking of spiritual communion.

Fourthly, if Paul had wished to signify spiritual participation, he would rather have said that the Spirit, or faith, or the vivification itself is the communion of the body and blood of Christ: for faith is the medium by which Christ is applied to individuals, and Christ lives in us by the Spirit: but Paul says that the chalice is the communion of the blood, and the bread of blessing is the communion of the body. Therefore it is necessary that he is speaking of the corporal communion of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, which all who eat of this bread and drink from this chalice receive, as well the unworthy and the secure, as the penitent and those approaching the Holy Supper with confidence in God:

Fifthly, the proof which the Apostle adds testifies that this is the mind of Paul: for thus he proves that the bread is the communion of the body of Christ: Because the bread is one, and we being many are one body: for we all partake of the one bread. From the fact that in the holy supper we all partake of one bread, the Apostle Paul proves that the bread of blessing is the communion of the body of Jesus Christ: This argument of Paul would not hold, if the mind of Paul were that the bread was a sign of the communion of the body of Christ, and the Apostle had spoken only of spiritual participation.

For it does not follow from that, because we partake of one bread, that we all become partakers of the benefits, merits, Spirit, and efficacy of Christ: for many approach the synaxis through hypocrisy, and take judgment upon themselves, so far are they from becoming partakers of the benefits and Spirit of Christ. It is necessary, therefore, that this be the mind of the words of Paul, that by the bread itself the body of Christ is communicated to all, to the worthy for salvation, to the unworthy for judgment.

Therefore a better exposition of the words of Paul cannot be given than through the words of Jesus Christ: The cup of blessing is the communion of the blood of Jesus Christ, that is, the wine of blessing is the very blood of Jesus Christ, poured out for the remission of our sins, and all who drink from this cup, worthy and

unworthy, become participants of the blood of Jesus Christ: And the bread of the Eucharist is the communication of the body of Jesus Christ, that is, the blessed Bread is the very body of Jesus Christ, which is delivered for us, and all who eat this bread of the Eucharist, become participants of the body of Jesus Christ, as well the unworthy as the worthy.

Let us therefore defend this sound and native meaning of the words of Paul, against the deceptions of the Calvinists. Because the adversaries urge the voice of Paul, we being many are one Body, in that they are not helped at all. For Paul calls the body one congregation, one assembly, one society, as citizens of one city are as it were one body: so those who are gathered in the Church to participate in the Eucharist are one body, one congregation. From that fact, however, that the whole assembly communicates of one bread, he gathers that the Eucharist is a participation of the body of Christ. Nor is it therefore the case that the body of Christ itself is truly distributed in the supper, not only to the worthy, but also to the unworthy, since even the unworthy participate of one bread.

Latin:

Calix benedictionis, cui benedicimus, annon est communicatio sanguinis Christi? & panis quem frangimus numquid est communicatio corporis Christi? siquidem unus panis, unus Corpus multi sumus. Omnes enim de uno pane participamus.

Primum hoc est argumentum sumptum à contrariis, quo docet fugiendam esse Idolatriam. Qui particeps est corporis & sanguinis Christi, nihil commune habere debet cum Idolis. Christiani fiunt participes corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi: Ergò cum Idolis nihil commune habere debent. Nulla enim communicatio est Christi & Belial: locus hic valdè insignis est, si quidem perspicuè explicat controver siam de praesentia corporis Christi in sacra coena, & validissimè munit veram sententiam contra praestigia Calvinistarum, qui Pauli verba flagicio se depravant. Calvinus contendit inesse figuram his verbis Pauli, & sic enarrat. Panis est communicatio corporis Christi, Id est, symbolum communicationis corporis Christi. Alii sic depravant. Panis est id quo fit societas cum Christo. Bullingerus sic enarrat, ut dicat corpus Christi, hîc allegoricè significare Ecclesiam: Atque alius aliter contorquet verba Pauli, omnes verò Calvinistae hoc agunt, ut corpus & sanguinem Iesu Christi è Sàcra coena proturbent & exterminent.

Nobis ergò tantò magis laborandum est, ut Thesaurum hunc preciosissimum tueamur, & veritatem doctrinae Apostolicae retineamus.

Quòd ergò ad voces attinet, certum est κοινωνίαν significare non societatem, sed communicationem & participationem, quod tandem etiam Calvinus convictus rei evidentia concessit. Paulus enim vocabulum κοινωνίαν per vocem μετοχὴν exponit. Et Theophyl: Dicit κοινωνίαν aliquid excellentius significare, quàm μετοχὴ, summam nimirum unionem cum Christo.

Vocabulum (corpus) non significat hoc loco Ecclesiam, quae per allegoriam corpus Christi dicitur, sed significat ipsam substantiam corporis Iesu Christi, quae pro nobis in cruce pependit, & ex mortuis resurrexit. Negari enim non potest Paulum hîc de Eucharistia, et de corpore et sanguine Iesu Christi agere, dicit enim calix benedictionis, cui benedicimus. Et inepta & violenta est Bullingeri interpretatio, cùm dicit corpus Christi hîc significare Ecclesiam. Cum enim dicat Paulus calicem esse communicationem sanguinis Christi, hoc necesse est, non de Ecclesiae, sed sanguinis Christi vera participatione intelligi. Verba igitur Apostoli propriè sine figuris accipienda sunt.

Ac quia controvertitur, num Paulus de spirituali communicatione, consociatione, & insitione sanctorum in Christo, an verò de corporali participatione, loquatur: Item, num ex his verbis pateat, quòd corpus Iesu Christi in sacra coena verè sit praesens, edatur & percipiatur ab indignis & dignis simul, nec ne, ipsa verba Spiritus sancti ponderemus, examinemus, & perpendamus.

Primùm ergò attendat pius & veritatis studiosus lector, quis sit scopus disputationis Paulinae, & quid docere conetur Apostolus. Adhortatur Paulus Corinthios, ut fugiant idolatriam, et Ethnica sacrificia, utque Corinthios ad obtemperandum persuadeat, argumentum ducit ex doctrina de coena domini: Qui participes fiunt corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi, hi non debent fieri participes Daemonum. Vos Corinthii in usu coenae domini estis participes corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi. Ergò fugere debetis omne consortium idolorum: Et abstinere à sacrificiis Ethnicis: hanc esse Pauli argumentationem, cùm verba ipsa, tum sequentia argumenta, & tota orationis series docet.

Ex hac autem argumentatione liquet, Paulum non figuratè, sed propriè locutum esse. Si enim hoc sensisset Paulus, panem Eucharistiae tantum esse signum communicationis corporis Christi, parùm fecisset hoc argumentum, ad deterrendos Corinthios à sacrificiis idolorum. Nec spiritualem participationem corporis Christi intelligit Paulus, cum dicit: panis est communicatio corporis Christi: quia non agit hîc tantum de fidelibus & poenitentibus, qui piis motibus cordis ad sacram synaxim accedunt, sed etiam impoenitentes, & securos Corinthios alloquitur, qui se idolatria & consortio sacrificiorum Ethnicorum contaminabant. Cùm ergo testetur, etiam eos qui securi sunt, & verae fidei expertes, communicare corpori & sanguini Iesu Christi, quoties vescuntur pane & vino benedicto, manifestum est: Paulum non de spirituali & salutari participatione corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi hîc agere: quam pii, in quibus vera existit poenitentia, & lucet fides, & qui abstinent ab Idolatria & aliis peccatis vastantibus conscientiam, tantum percipiunt: sed de alia, nimirum corporali, quae communis est tam indignis quam dignis.

Secundò, homini sano & cordato dubium esse non potest nec debet, quin Paulus Apostolus texens argumentum ex institutione caenae dominicae respexerit ad verba Iesu Christi eaque ponderaverit, & ex his veluti fonte hauserit suam argumentationem. Unde certò patet, oportere eandem esse mentem verborum Pauli: panis cui benedicimus est ne communicatio corporis Iesu Christi: quae est verborum Christi, Hoc est corpus meum. Manifestum est autem ex declaratione Christi, hunc esse sensum verborum Christi, Hoc est corpus meum: Id est, panis eucharistiae est verum corpus Iesu Christi, quia addit Christus: quod pro vobis traditur. Panis non est symbolum vel signum corporis: Nam signum corporis non est pro nobis datum in mortem, sed ipsum corpus Christi, quod in cruce pependit. Ergò & verborum Pauli sensum necesse est eundem esse. Vide licet panis cui benedicimus, est communicatio corporis Iesu Christi: Hoc est, est ipsum corpus Iesu Christi, cuius omnes fiunt participes, qui sacra synaxi utuntur. Haec nulla sophistica everti possunt. Qui verò contendunt, Paulum figuratè locutum esse: quod panis sit signum communicationis corporis Christi, hi Apostolo Paulo manifestam faciunt iniuriam, & verba Spiritus sancti violenter contorquent, & ipsa etiam verba institutionis caenae evertunt. Si enim panis Eucharistiae est tantum signum communicationis corporis Christi, sequeretur, & verba caenae sic oportere accipi: videlicet, panem eucharistiae esse signum corporis: & signum corporis pro nostris peccatis in mortem esse traditum. Quis verò non videt quanta impietate ista dicerentur? Absque omni igitur figura Paulus propriè locutus est, panis cui benedicimus est communicatio corporis Iesu Christi, Id est, panis benedictionis est ipsum corpus Iesu Christi, cuius omnes fiunt participes, qui de hoc pane edunt.

Tertiò, distinctè pronunciat Paulus calicem benedictionis esse communicationem sanguinis: panem benedictionis esse communicationem corporis Iesu Christi: Docet ergò Apostolus, in calice ipsum sanguinem Christi, in pane ipsum corpus Christi nobis communicari. Ad ipsam enim institutionem Christi respexit Apostolus. Figuratè bibere sanguinem Christi, & edere carnem eius, unum & idem est, nimirum per fidem fieri participem beneficiorum Christi: Verùm Paulus communicationem sanguinis tribuit hîc calici benedictionis, communicationem corporis pani Eucharistiae tribuit. Ergò non loquitur de spirituali communicatione.

Quartò, si Paulus voluisset significare spiritualem participationem, potiùs dixisset Spiritum, aut fidem, aut ipsam vivificationem esse communicationem corporis & sanguinis Christi: fides enim est medium, quo adplicatur singulis Christus, & Spiritu vivit in nobis Christus: sed Paulus dicit calicem esse communicationem sanguinis, & panem benedictionis esse communicationem corporis. Ergò necesse est eum de corporali communicatione corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi loqui, quam omnes, qui de hoc pane edunt, & ex hoc calice bibunt, praecipiunt, tam indigni & securi, quàm poenitentes, & cum fiducia in Deum ad Sacram coenam accedentes:

Quintò, probatio, quam attexit Apostolus testatur, hanc esse mentem Pauli: sic enim probat, quòd panis sit communicatio corporis Christi: Quia unus est panis, & unum corpus multi sumus: omnes enim ex uno pane participamus. Ex eo, quod in sacra caena ex uno pane omnes participamus probat Apostolus Paulus, panem benedictionis esse communicationem corporis Iesu Christi: Haec ratio Pauli non consisteret, simens Pauli esset, quòd panis esset signum communicationis corporis Christi, & tantum de spirituali participatione locutus esset Apostolus.

Non enim ex eo sequitur, quia ex uno pane participamus, fieri nos omnes participes beneficiorum, meritorum, Spiritus & efficatiae Christi: multi enim per hypocrisin accedunt ad synaxin, & iudicium sibi sumunt, tantum abest, ut fiant participes beneficiorum & Spiritus Christi. Necesse est igitur hanc esse mentem verborum Pauli, quòd ipso pane communicetur omnibus corpus Christi, dignis ad salutem, indignis ad iudicium.

Ergò melior expositio verborum Pauli dari non potest, quàm per verba Iesu Christi: Calix benedictionis est communicatio sanguinis Iesu Christi, id est, Vinum benedictionis est ipse sanguis Iesu Christi, in remissionem nostrorum peccatorum effusus, & omnes, qui ex hoc calice bibunt digni &

indigni, participes fiunt sanguinis Iesu Christi: Et panis Eucharistiae est communicatio corporis Iesu Christi, id est, Panis benedictus est ipsum corpus Iesu Christi, quod pro nobis est traditum, & omnes qui manducant hunc panem Eucharistiae, fiunt participes corporis Iesu Christi, tam indigni quam digni.

Hanc ergò sanam & nativam verborum Pauli sententiam tueamur, contra Calvinistarum praestigias. Quod urgent adversarii vocem Pauli, unum Corpus multi sumus, in eo nihil iuvantur. Corpus enim vocat Paulus unam congregationem, unum coetum, unam societatem, ut cives unius civitatis sunt quasi unum corpus: sic qui congregantur in Ecclesia ad participandum de Eucharistia sunt unum corpus una congregatio. Ex eo autem quod totus coetus communicat de uno pane colligit, Eucharistiam esse participationem corporis Christi. Nec esse est igitur ipsum corpus Christi verè distribui in coena, non tantum dignis, sed & indignis, siquidem & indigni de uno pane participant.

## 10:18
Behold Israel after the flesh, are not they who eat the sacrifices participants of the altar?

The declaration is of the prior argument from a likeness: when the Israelites offer, and then eat the sacrifices, individuals become participants of the offering. So also Christians, when they offer bread and wine, and eat and drink the body and blood of Christ, all become participants of the body and blood of Christ. This argument both declares and confirms the opinion shown above. For if the unworthy participated in nothing of the body and blood of Christ, as the delirium of the Calvinists holds, Paul would have untimely brought forward this argument taken from the sacrifices of the Israelites, especially when he was speaking about the participation of the body of Christ.

Latin:

Videte Israelem secundum carnem, numquid qui comedunt sacrificia participes fiunt altaris?

Declaratio est argumenti prioris à simili: quando Israelitae offerunt, et deinde commedunt sacrificia, Singuli fiunt participes oblationis. Sic etiam Christiani, quando offerunt panem & vinum, & commedunt & bibunt corpus & sanguinem Christi omens fiunt participes corporis & sanguinis Christi. Hoc argumentum & declarat & confirmat superius monstratam sententiam. Si enim indigni nihil paticiparent de corpore & sanguine Christi, sicuti Calvinistarum habet delirium, imtempestivè adduxisset Paulus hoc argumentum sumptum à sacrificiis Israelitarum, praesertim cum de participatione corporis Christi loqueretur.

## 10:19-20
What therefore do I say? That an idol is anything? Or that what is sacrificed to idols is anything? Nay, I say this, that what the nations sacrifice, they sacrifice to Devils, and not to God. Moreover, I do not want you to become participants of Demons.

Paul shows what he urges in his argument taken from the Lord's Supper and the participation of the body of Christ: Namely, that the Corinthians should abstain from the sacrifices of idols, lest they become participants of Devils: Idols indeed, he says, are nothing, nor is anything sacrificed to idols: These things by themselves could neither help nor harm us, but because what is offered to idols is offered to Devils, who impel men to the worship of idols, therefore one must abstain, so that men do not communicate with Demons. Here now the Calvinists shout out, Behold, is not the communication with Demons spiritual? Therefore, is the communication of the body of Christ, which is opposed to it, also spiritual? I answer, Paul is not speaking of a spiritual society with Devils, but of an external and bodily participation: Namely, that those of the Christians who approached the sacrifices of idols, even if they abhorred in their mind the society of Demons, nevertheless by eating the Idolothytes would bodily communicate with Demons: because they would eat the foods offered to Demons, that is, in worship, and thus in a certain way would testify that they had society with Demons, and would horribly contaminate themselves. Therefore, Paul prohibits not only internal and spiritual society with Devils, but also external and bodily communication with Devils, which was done by the participation of food that had been offered to Devils. Therefore, the Calvinists violently twist this text against the mind of Paul: Who teaches that in the supper a participation of the true body of Christ takes place: In the sacrifices of idols men communicate with Devils. And therefore all idols must be completely fled.

Latin:

Quid igitur dico? Quod idolon aliquid sit? Aut quod idolis sacrificatum aliquid sit? Imò hoc dico, quod quae gentes sacrificant, Diabolis, & non Deo sacrificant. Nolo autem vos participes fieri Daemoniorum.

Ostendit Paulus quid urgeat in suo argumento sumpto à coena domini & participatione corporis Christi: Nimirum ut Corinthii abstineant à sacrificiis idolorum, ne participes fiant Diabolorum: Idola quidem inquit nihil sunt, neque sacrificatum idolis quidquam est: Haec per se nec iuvare nec laedere nos possent, sed quia quae offeruntur idolis, Diabolis offeruntur, qui impellunt homines ad cultus idolorum, idcircò abstinendum est, ne communicent homines Daemonibus. Hîc iam vociferantur Calvinistae, Ecce an non communicatio cum Daemonibus est spiritualis? Ergo & communicatio corporis Christi, quae illi opponitur, est spiritualis? Respondeo, Paulus non loquitur de spirituali societate cum Diabolis, sed de externa & corporali participatione: Quòd videlicet qui ex Christianis accedebant ad sacrificia idolorum, et si animo abhorrerent à societate Daemonum, tamen vesoendo Idolothytis corporaliter communicarent Daemonibus: quia cibos Daemonibus scilicet in cultu oblatis vescerentur, & sic quodammodo testarentur, quòd societatem cum Daemonibus haberent, & horribiliter sese contaminarent. Prohibet ergò Paulus non solùm internam & spiritualem societatem cum Diabolis, sed etiam externam et corporalem communicationem cum Diabolis, quae fiebat participatione cibi, qui erat oblatus Diabolis. Violenter itaque contorquent hunc textum Calvinistae contra mentem Pauli: Qui docet, in coena participationem veri corporis Christi fieri: In sacrificiis idolorum homines communicare Diabolis. Ideoque prorsus fugienda esse omnia idola.

## 10:21
You cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of Demons: You cannot become partakers of the table of the Lord, and of the table of demons: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

Here, because he posits the major premise of his argument. Christians cannot simultaneously become participants of the table of the Lord and the table of the Devils: But in the holy supper Christians become participants of the body of Christ: In the sacrifices of idols men communicate with Devils. Therefore Christians ought to abstain entirely from the sacrifices of idols. The Apostle Paul tends toward this. If a Calvinist should object: If Paul spoke of the corporal participation of the body of Christ, which is common to the worthy and the unworthy, one can simultaneously participate in the body of the Lord and become a participant of the table of Demons: But Paul denies that this can happen: Therefore he spoke of spiritual participation. It must be answered that Paul intends this: It cannot be done with the salvation of the soul: You cannot simultaneously be participants of the table of the Lord, and of the table of the Devils with the salvation of your soul.

For he who eats the body of the Lord unworthily, becomes guilty of the body of Christ: And he who participates in the table of Demons, contaminates himself with foul idolatry. We must therefore take care, lest we provoke the wrath of God.

And thus Paul shows also in this opinion, that he spoke concerning the corporal participation of the body of Christ and the corporal participation of the blood of Christ, which is common to the worthy and the unworthy. For he warns and terrifies the Corinthians, lest they eat the body of the Lord unto judgment. If he had spoken only of spiritual communication: there would have been no need to terrify them lest they provoke the wrath of God by participation in the body of Christ: For no one abuses the spiritual participation of the body and blood of Christ. Therefore he says, Or shall we provoke the Lord to indignation? as if he were to say: Beware lest you provoke our Lord Jesus Christ to wrath, while you approach the Eucharist ferociously without serious repentance, participating in his body and yet remaining secure while approaching nonetheless the sacrifices of idols. Are we stronger than he? that is, shall we securely hope that we will escape the punishment of such a crime? do you not know that the Lord is omnipotent, who in a light moment can afflict us with the most grave punishment. Let us therefore fear his wrath, let us abstain from all worship of idols, but let us always approach the supper of the Lord with serious repentance.

Latin:

Non potestis calicem domini bibere, & calicem Daemoniorum: Non potestis participes fieri mensae domini, & mensae Daemoniorum: An verò ad indignationem provocabimus nos dominum? Num fortiores eo sumus?

Hîc quia si maiorem ponit sui argumenti. Christiani non possunt simul & mensae domini et mensae Diabolorum fieri participes: Sed in sacra caena fiunt Christiani participes corporis Christi: In sacrificiis idolorum homines communicant Diabolis. Ergò Christiani ab idolorum sacrificiis prorsus abstinere debent. Huc tendit Apostolus Paulus. Si obiiciat quis Calvinista. Si Paulus de corporali participatione corporis Christi locutus est, quae communis est dignis & indignis, Potest quis simul & de corpore domini participare & mensae Daemonum fieri particeps: Sed Paulus negat hoc fieri posse: Ergò de spirituali participatione est locutus. Respondendum est, Paulum hoc velle: Non posse id fieri cum salute animae: Non potestis simul esse participes mensae domini, & mensae Diabolorum cum animae vestrae salute.

Nam qui indignè edit corpus domini, reus fit corporis Christi: Et qui mensae Daemonum participat, contaminat se foeda idolatria. Cavendum est igitur, ne iram Dei provocemus.

Atque ita ostendit Paulus etiam in hac sententia, quod de corporali participatione corporis Christi & corporali participatione sanguinis Christi sit locutus, quae dignis & indignis est communis. Monet enim & terret Corinthios, ne corpus domini ad iudicium edant. Si tantum de spirituali communicatione locutus fuisset: nihil opus fuisset eos terrere ne participatione corporis Christi iram Dei provocarent: Nam spirituali participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi nemo abutitur. Ideò inquit, An verò ad indignationem provocabimus dominum? quasi dicat: Cavete ne ad iram provocetis dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, dum ferociter sine poenitentia seria acceditis ad Eucharistiam, participantes de corpore ipsius & tamen securi manetis accedentes nihilominus ad sacrificia Idolorum. An potentiores illo sumus? hoc est, an securi sperabimus nos evasuros poenam tanti sceleris? an nescitis Dominum esse omnipotentem qui levi momento gravissimo potest nos adficere supplicio. Metuamus ergò eius iram, abstineamus ab omni cultu Idolorum, ad coenam verò domini semper cum seria poenitentia accedamus.

## 10:22
All things are lawful for me: but all things are not expedient: All things are lawful for me: but all things do not edify. Let no man seek what is his own, but each one what is another's.

Again here he dilutes the objection of those who had not rightly perceived the doctrine concerning Christian liberty, and were abusing pious sentiments as a pretext for their own impiety and collusion: whom he had also repressed above in Chapter 6. The Corinthians had heard that to the pure all things are pure: and that the earth is the Lord's: Therefore it is permitted to Christians to do all things: Hence they gathered that it was permitted even to them to be present at the rites of Idols. The Apostle therefore refutes this sinister opinion, and teaches that the meaning of the doctrine concerning Christian liberty is far different. And first it must be known that works prohibited by the express word of God are not included in this saying. It is by no means permitted to the pious to worship Idols, to swear falsely, to spread false dogmas, to stir up seditions, to commit fornication, to steal, to lie: those who do such things, says Paul, shall not possess the kingdom of God. 1 Cor: 6. But the saying is to be understood concerning middle things and adiaphora: that indeed nothing is unclean to those who are pure in heart: Titus: 1. that Christians are not bound to the ceremonial laws of Moses, nor to the statutes or decrees of Bishops. For Christians have been endowed with liberty in Christ Jesus: And the earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof. Therefore it is permitted to the pious to use individual things with thanksgiving. We are not bound to a certain kind of food, nor to certain feast days, nor to a certain form of polity, nor to a certain kind of vestments, nor to certain ceremonies: but all things are lawful to the pious, namely in these indifferent things. For if anyone should ferociously sin against the decalogue, he is no longer pious, but an impious contemner of God: to whom all things are unclean, as much the mind as the conscience Titus 1. Furthermore, although to a Christian in indifferent things all things are lawful. For his conscience through faith in the word is free from all things: yet he ought not to abuse this liberty to the fraud or detriment of anyone. For we ought to have regard not only for ourselves, but also for the Church and our neighbor. Wherefore if an untimely use of liberty seems about to hinder the edification of the Church, and to be about to produce scandal to a neighbor, I ought rather to yield from my right, and abstain from the use of liberty. Paul was free, and could have omitted the circumcision of Timothy: But because he judges it expedient for the Church that he be circumcised, lest the Jews abhor him, he circumcised him. Paul was free, and could have sought a salary from the Churches which he was instructing: Yet he abstained, because he saw this to make for the edification of the Church. Thus the pious ought not only to see what is lawful to them by a good conscience in itself: but also what is expedient, what may edify the Church, what may instruct and confirm a brother in the truth. Let no one seek what is his own, that is, let no one indulge his own affections and desires, but let each one seek what are another's: according to the commandment. You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

Latin:

Omnia mihi licent: sed non omnia expediunt: Omnia mihi licent: sed non omnia aedificant. Nemo quaerat quod suum est, sed unusquisque quod est alterius.

Rursus hîc diluit obiectionem eorum qui doctrinam de libertate Christiana non rectè perceperant, & piis sententiis ad praetextum suae impietatis & collusionis abutebantur: quos & supra Cap: 6 represserat. Audiverant Corinthii, Mundis omnia esse munda: & Domini esse terram: Ergò licere Christianis omnia: Hinc colligebant licere etiam ipsis inter esse sacris Idolorum. Refellit ergo Apostolus hanc sinistram opinionem, & docet longè aliam esse sententiam doctrinae de libertate Christiana. Ac primò sciendum est, hoc dicto non includi opera expresso Dei verbo prohibita. Nequaquam licet piis colere Idola, peierare, falsa dogmata spargere, seditiones movere, scortari, furari, mentiri: qui talia faciunt inquit Paulus regnum Dei non possidebunt. 1. Cor: 6. Sed de rebus mediis & adiaphoris intelligendum est dictum: quod nimirum nihil sit immundum mundis corde: Titum: 1. quod Christiani non sint adstricti ad leges ceremoniales Mosi, nec ad statuta vel decreta Episcoporum. Donati enim sunt Christiani libertate in Christo Iesu: Et Domini est terra & omnis plenitudo eius. Ergò licet piis singulis rebus uti cum gratiarum actione. Non sumus adstricti ad certum genus ciborum, neque ad certos dies festos, neque ad certam formam politiae, neque ad certum genus vestimentorum, neque ad certas ceremonias: sed omnia licent piis, scilicet in his rebus mediis. Nam si quis ferociter peccet contra decalogum, iam non est pius, sed impius contemptor Dei: cui omnia sunt immunda, tam mens, quam conscientia Titum: 1. Deinde, etsi Christiano in rebus mediis omnia licent. Conscientia enim eius per fidem in verbo libera est ab omnibus: tamen hac libertate in nullius fraudem vel detrimentum abuti debet. Non enim tantum nostri, sed etiam Ecclesiae & proximirationem habere debemus. Quare si intempestivus usus libertatis impediturus videtur aedificationem Ecclesiae, & pariturus scandalum proximo, potiùs de meo iure cedere debeo, et abstinere ab usu libertatis. Liber erat Paulus, & potuisset omittere Timothei circumcisionem: Sed quia censet expedire Ecclesiae ut circumcidatur, ne Iudaei ab eo abhorreant, circumcidit eum. Liber erat Paulus, & salarium petere potuit ab Ecclesiis, quas erudiebat: Abstinuit tamen, quia videbat hoc facere ad Ecclesiae aedificationem. Ita non tantum pii videre debent, quid ipsis bona conscientia liceat per se: sed etiam quid expediat, quid aedificet Ecclesiam, quid erudiat et confirmet fratrem in veritate. Nemo quaerat, quae sua sunt hoc est, nemo adfectibus et cupiditatibus suis indulgeat, sed singuli quaerant, quae sunt alterius: iuxta praeceptum. Diliges proximum tuum, sicutite ipsum.

## 10:25
Everything that is sold in the meat market, eat, judging nothing, for the sake of conscience: for the earth is the Lord's and all its fullness.

Paul strictly forbade that Christians should approach the sacrifices of idols, and that they should eat of things sacrificed to idols: lest they should become partakers of demons. Now it could happen that meat sacrificed to idols in temples might afterwards be carried into the meat market, and there be publicly sold. For thus Satan would desire to fill all the corners of the whole world with his filth by his idol-mania, so that he might contaminate everyone. Here, therefore, the weak could doubt what ought to be done. If the eating of foods which have been sacrificed to idols and demons so contaminates a man that it makes him a partaker of demons: and it cannot be certain to us whether the meats or breads which are sold in the meat market have been sacrificed to idols, therefore shall we be able to safely buy and eat nothing of food? Paul answers: Nay, everything that is sold in the meat market eat, without dispute or inquiry, whether it has been sacrificed or not sacrificed.

For the use of creatures is lawful for the pious: In the sacrifices of idols it is not lawful to eat of things sacrificed to idols: Because that fellowship in sacrifices approves the idols: And he brings reproach upon God. But since we have no commerce with idols, nor is the abuse and impiety of others established for us, all creatures are clean to us Christians. For the earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof. He proves by the testimony of scripture, taken from Psalm: 24., that all creatures are clean to Christians. The impious indeed contaminate creatures for themselves by their own impiety, so that they turn to their own destruction, but this has nothing to do with the pious: for creatures are not of the Devil, nor of impious men: But they are of our Lord Jesus Christ, who created heaven and earth, and all things that are in them. Since therefore all things are Christ's: And God has given all things with his son out of his goodness to the clean of heart, that is, to those believing in Christ by faith, nothing can be unclean or harmful, if it is received with thanksgiving. An idol is a most contaminated thing: But if money is minted from a golden idol, it will be lawful for a Christian to use it as clean money. How copious a doctrine this little verse contains, we show in the explanation of Psal: 24.

Latin:

Omne quod in macello venditur, comedite, nihil diiudicantes, propter conscientiam: Domini enim est terra & omnis plenitudo eius.

Severè prohibuit Paulus, ne Christiani ad sacrificia Idolorum accederent, & ne Idolothytis vescerentur: ne fierent participes daemoniorum. Iam fieri poterat, ut caro sacrificata Idolis in templis, postea ferreretur in macellum, & isthic publicè venderetur. Sic enim Satan sua idolomania cuperet omnes angulos totius mundi opplere suis sordibus, ut omnes contaminet. Hîc ergò dubitare poterant imbecilles, quid faciendum esset. Si esus ciborum, qui Idolis & daemoniis sacrificati sunt, adeò contaminat hominem, ut faciat eum participem daemoniorum: Et constare nobis non potest, an carnes velpanes, qui in macello venduntur, Idolis fuerint sacrificati, Ergò nihil ciborum tutò emere & comedere poterimus? Paulus respondet: Imò, omne quod venditur in macello comedite, sine disputatione vel inquisitione, sive sit sacrificatum, sive non sacrificatum.

Creaturarum enim usus licitus est piis: In sacrificiis idolorum vesci non licet idolothytis: Quia societas illa in sacrificiis adprobat idola: Et Deum adficit contumelia. Sed cum nihil commercii habemus cum idolis, nec constat nobis de aliorum abusu & impietate, creaturae omnes nobis Christianis sunt mundae. Domini enim est terra & plenitudo eius. Probat testimonio scripturae, ex Psalm: 24. desumpto omnes creaturas mundas esse Christianis. Impii quidem sua impietate sibi contaminant creaturas, ita ut ipsis cedant in perniciem, sed nihil hoc ad pios: creaturae enim non sunt Diaboli, neque impiorum hominum: Sed sunt Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui condidit coelum & terram, & omnia quae in eis sunt. Cum ergò omnia sint Christi: Et Deus omnia cum filio pro sua bonitate dederit mundis corde, hoc est, fide in Christum credentibus, nihil potest esse immundum aut noxium, si cum gratiarum actione percipiatur. Idolum res est contaminatissima: Sed si ex aureo idolo confletur moneta, Christiano licebit ea, ut pecunia munda, uti. Quam copiosam doctrinam contineat hic versiculus, ostendimus in explicatione, Psal: 24.

## 10:27-28
If any of the unbelievers invites you, and you wish to go, eat everything that is set before you, asking no questions for conscience' sake: but if anyone says to you, this is offered in sacrifice to idols, do not eat, for the sake of him who pointed it out, and for the sake of conscience. For the earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof.

Again he proposes another case about which he instructs the Corinthians, if any unbelieving relative or friend invites you to a dinner and a feast: And it pleases you to be present at the banquet of friends, I do not forbid it: For it is permitted to take food even with openly impious people who are not part of the Church. And at a banquet there is no need to inquire which things have been sacrificed to idols, and which have not. A banquet is an external and civil matter and does not pertain to the worship of idols. Therefore you may eat of every kind of food that is set before you; for the earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof. All things are Jesus Christ's: And we are the servants of this omnipotent Lord: It is permitted therefore for us to use and enjoy the things of our Lord. But if indeed some Christian is present at the banquet, and he points out that this or that is an idol-sacrifice, then do not eat of it so that you may spare his conscience. For he could be offended by your example, and since he has not yet grasped the doctrine concerning Christian liberty, his conscience being in doubt could imitate your example, and eat of the idol-sacrifice, with a grave wound to his conscience. For to him who judges something to be unclean, to him it is unclean. Rom. 14. Thus although it would be permitted for you to eat of the idol-sacrifice at a banquet, without any inquiry and judgment: Nevertheless lest you wound the conscience of the weak Christian, who has indicated that this or that is an idol-offering, you must abstain. Thus Paul teaches clearly when there is a need for the confession of the divine name against the worship of idols: And how widely extends the liberty into which the Son of God has placed us: And how liberty is to be used.

Latin:

Si quis autem infidelium invitaverit vos, & vultis accedere, omne quod vobis adponitur edite, nihil disputantes propter conscientiam: si quis verò dixerit vobis, hoc est idolothyton, ne edatis, propter eum qui indicavit, & propter conscientiam. Domini enim est terra & plenitudo eius.

Rursus alium proponit casum de quo erudit Corinthios, si quis infidelium cognatus vel amicus invitaverit vos ad coenam & prandium: Et placet vobis inter esse convivio amicorum, non prohibeo: Licet enim cibum capere etiam cum palam impiis qui non sunt pars Ecclesiae. Et in convivio nihil opus est inquirere quae sint idolis sacrificata, quae non sint. Convivium est res externa & civilis nec pertinet ad cultum idolorum. Itaque vescaris omnigenere ciborum, qui apponuntur vobis; Domini enim est terra & plenitudo eius. Omnia sunt Iesu Christi: Et nos huius omnipotentis domini servi sumus: Licet ergo nobis uti & frui rebus domini nostri. Quod si verò Christianus aliquis interfuerit convivio, isque indicaverit hoc vel illud esse idolothyton, tum ne comedas de eo ut eius parcas conscientiae. Posset enim offendituo exemplo, & cum ille nondum percepit doctrinam de libertate Christiana conscientia dubit ante posset tuum imitari exemplum, & vesci idolothyto, cum gravi vulnere conscientiae. Nam qui iudicat aliquid immundum esse, ei est immundum. Roma: 14. Ita quamquam tibi liceret vesci idolothyto in convivio, sine omni inquisitione & diiudicatione: Tamen ne infirmi Christiani, qui indicavit hoc vel illud esse Idolothyton, conscientiam vulneres, abstinendum est tibi. Ita Paulus praeclarè docet, quando opus sit confessione nominis divini, contra idolorum cultus: Et quàm latè pateat libertas, in quam nos filius Dei collocavit: Et quomodo utendum sit libertate.

## 10:29-30
Conscience, I say, not your own, but another's: For why is my liberty judged by another's conscience? If, however, I become a participant through grace, why am I blasphemed for that for which I give thanks.

Because he had said that one must abstain from the eating of an indicated idol-offering on account of conscience, lest the pious take this as if a scruple could be cast into our own consciences by the indication of others: He adds an exposition, that he is speaking about the conscience of another, which is to be spared: And he adds the necessary doctrine, that our conscience ought not to depend upon the judgment of others. You must abstain, he says, from the idol-offering, not on account of your own conscience, which is free in the Lord, whose is the whole earth: But on account of the conscience of another, lest it, because it is weak, be scandalized by your example.

Why, he says, is my liberty judged by another's conscience? As if he were to say: Our conscience and liberty ought not to depend upon the judgment of another's conscience, but upon the word of God, which shows us liberty in Christ. The judgment of another's conscience can neither wound nor heal my conscience. It is enough for me that I acknowledge the benefit of Christ and have a certain word, whatever others may judge concerning me.

If, he says, I partake by grace: He adds another argument, that he ought not to be condemned by the weak because he has used his liberty and enjoys the benefits of God. By grace, he says, I partake. This is, I understand the benefit of God, and I know that foods of every kind are given to us by the grace of God: And I also eat with thanksgiving proceeding from faith: Therefore the weak person, who sees me eating without judgment and inquiry, ought not to judge nor condemn my conscience.

Latin:

Conscientiam dico non propriam, sed alterius: Cur enim libertas mea iudicatur, ab alterius conscientia? Si autem per gratiam particeps fio, quare blasphemor in eo, pro quo ego gratias ago.

Quia dixerat, propter conscientiam abstinendum esse ab esu indicati Idolothyti, ne pii hoc sic acciperent, ac si nostrae conscientiae aliorum indicatione scrupulus iniici possit: Addit expositionem, se loqui de alterius conscientia, cui sit parcendum: Et addit necessariam doctrinam, quòd nostra conscientia non debeat pendere ab aliorum iudicio. Abstinere inquit, debes ab idolothyto, non propter tuam conscientiam, quae libera est in domino, cuius est tota terra: Sed propter conscientiam alterius, ne ea, quia infirma est exemplo scandalizetur.

Cur inquit, libertas mea ab alterius conscientia iudicatur? Quasi dicat: Conscientia & libertas nostra non debet pendere à iudicio alterius conscientiae: Sed à verbo Dei, quod ostendit nobis libertatem in Christo. Alterius conscientiae iudicium meam conscientiam, nec vulner are, nec sanare potest. Mihi satis est, me agnoscere Christi beneficium, & habere certum verbum, quidquid alii de me iudicaverint.

Si inquit, ego per gratiam participo: Aliud addit argumentum, non se debere damnari ab infirmo, quod libertate sua sit usus, & fruatur beneficiis Dei. Per gratiam inquit participo. Hoc est, ego intelligo Dei beneficium, & scio nobis per gratiam Dei dari omnis generis cibos: Atque ego etiam vescor cum gratiarum actione profectae ex fide: Itaque infirmus, qui videt me vescentem sine diiudicatione & inquisitione, non debet iudicare, nec damnare meam conscientiam.

## 10:31
Whether therefore you eat, or you drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God: be not an offense, neither to the Jews, nor to the Greeks, nor to the Church of God: even as I also, (I do this) that I may please all men in all things in all things I may please: not seeking my own advantage, but that which may profit many, that they may be saved.

This is the conclusion of the whole treatise concerning the use of liberty, which doctrine he has expounded in three chapters. This, he says, is the sum of all, that not only in food and drink, but in every action and endeavor of life, you should direct all things to the glory of God, and the utility of your neighbor: that no one should study his own advantage: nor offer scandal to any man, but should always look to the edification of the Church of Jesus Christ. A most ample and truly most useful precept: And a most certain norm, according to which the conscience can test itself in every action. For cases are numberless and infinite, and it is not possible that defined sentences be handed down concerning individual cases. This rule, therefore, is handed down for the whole of life, and for all actions. That all things must be done for the glory of God, and for the utility of the Church, and of the neighbor. The word of God teaches what yields to the glory of God: so also the word of God and reason teach what is conducive to the neighbor. It is not, therefore, difficult for the truly pious man, even in an obscure case, to know what needs to be done: let only all hypocrisy be absent: and let Christ also be seriously invoked, that He may rule us by His Spirit.

Latin:

Sive igitur editis, sive bibitis, sive quid facitis, omnia ad gloriam Dei facite: ne sitis offendiculo, neque Iudaeis, neque Graecis, neque Ecclesiae Dei: quemad modum & ego, (hoc ago) ut omnibus in omnibus gratificer: non quaerens meum commodum, sed quod multis prodesse possit, ut salventur.

Conclusio est totius tractatus de usu libertatis, quam doctrinam tribus capitibus exposuit. Haec summa est inquit omnium, ut non tantum in cibo & potu, sed in omni actione & conatu vitae, omnia dirigatis ad gloriam Dei, & utilitatem proximi: ne quis suo commodo studeat: neque ulli homini scandalum praebeat, sed semper spectet Ecclesiae Iesu Christi aedificationem. Amplissimum sanè & utilissimum praeceptum: Et norma certissima, iuxta quam in omni actione sese probare potest conscientia. Casus enim innumeri, & infiniti sunt, & fieri non potest, ut de singulis casibus definitae tradantur sententiae. Haec igitur regula traditur totius vitae, & omnium actionum. Omnia ad gloriam Dei facienda esse, & ad utilitatem Ecclesiae, & proximi. Verbum Dei docet, quid cedat ad gloriam Dei: Sic etiam verbum Dei & ratio docent, quid conducat proximo. Non igitur difficile est verè pio etiam in ob curo casu scire, quid facto opus sit: absit tantum omnis hypocrisis: & seriò etiam invocetur Christus, ut nos suo Spiritu regat.

## 10:31 Places of Doctrine
Places of Doctrine.

1. That the title of the Church, external society with the children of God, and the external use of the sacraments and of the benefits of God, neither constitutes the children of God, nor makes us immune from the punishments which the word of God threatens against those sinning against the law of God.

2. That always in the Church of Jesus Christ the evil, such as hypocrites and Epicureans, are mixed with the good and the holy.

3. Concerning the divine miracles by which the doctrine of Moses was confirmed.

4. Concerning the eternal divinity of Jesus Christ and his perpetual presence in the Church. Paul interprets Moses in Exodus and the following books, and testifies that Jesus Christ is that Lord Jehovah who spoke with Moses, who ruled and defended the people of Israel, and performed stupendous miracles through Moses. Therefore Jesus Christ is the eternal and omnipotent God, who is perpetually present to his Church.

5. Concerning the severity of God, by which he is accustomed to take notice of idolaters.

6. Concerning the justice of God, by which he is accustomed to punish fornicators.

7. That God is not to be tempted: since many and excellent men who tempted God out of impatience, and murmured against him, were most severely punished and cast off by God.

8. The entire holy scripture for our use must be adapted: for the examples of the justice of God exhort us to avoid sins: the examples of the mercy of God ought to arouse faith and hope in us.

9. That presumption and confidence of mind must be avoided by all the pious, and that help must always be sought in the fear of God, so that we may be confirmed in faith by the Holy Spirit. For many great men, who began well, have fallen shamefully and have fallen away from the grace of God.

10. A huge consolation, that God does not allow us to be tempted beyond our strength, but provides strength through the Holy Spirit, so that we may be able to endure them.

11. That the Church of Jesus Christ has the right and power of judging concerning the doctrines of all who teach in the Church. Since indeed the Apostle himself submits his own doctrine to the judgment of the Church.

12. That in the most holy supper of Jesus Christ the true and substantial body, and the true and substantial blood of our Lord Jesus Christ is truly and substantially present: which is received by the mouth not only by the worthy and truly pious, for the confirmation of faith, but also by the unworthy, hypocrites, and the impious, like Judas, when they approach the table of the Lord, unto judgment.

13. How Christian liberty is to be used: namely, in such a way that we always study the glory of God, the edification of the Church, and the utility of our neighbor, rather than our own advantage.

20. That the liberty of our conscience does not depend upon the judgment of another, but upon the word of God, which reveals to us the benefits of Christ.

Latin:

Loci Doctrinae.

1. Quòd titulus Ecclesiae, externa societas cum filiis Dei, & externus usus sacramentorum, & beneficiorum Dei, nec constituat filios Dei, neque faciat nos immunes à poenis, quas verbum Dei minatur, contra legem Dei peccantibus.

2. Quòd semper in Ecclesia Iesu Christi mali, ut hypocritae & Epiurei, sint admixti bonis & sanctis.

3. De miraculis divinis, quibus confirmata est doctrina Mosis.

4. De aeterna divinitate Iesu Christi, & perpetua eius praesentia in Ecclesia. Paulus interpretatur Mosen in Exodo & sequentibus libris, & testatur Iesum Christum esse illum dominum Iehova, qui locutus sit cum Mose, qui rexerit & defenderit populum Israel, & stupenda miracula per Mosem ediderit. Ergò Iesus Christus est aeternus & omnipotens Deus, qui perpetuò adest suae Ecclesiae.

5. De severitate Dei, qua solet animadvertere in Idolatras.

6. De Iustitia Dei, qua solet punire scortatores.

7. Quòd non sit tentandus Deus: siquidem multi & excellentes viri qui tentaruna Deum, ex impatientia, & murmurarunt contra eum, gravissimè à Deo puniti & abiecti sunt.

8. Universam sacram scripturam ad nostrum usum esse accommodandam: nam exempla iustitiae Dei nos hortantur, ut vitemus peccata: Exempla misericordiae Dei fidem & spem in nobis exuscitare debent.

9. Omnibus piis cavendam esse prae sumptionem, & confidentiam animi, & semper in timore Dei petendum auxilium, ut Spiritu sancto in fide confirmemur. Nam multi magni viri, qui bene coeperunt, turpiter lapsi sunt, & gratia Dei excidrunt.

10. Ingens consolatio, quòd Deus non sinat nos tentari super vires, sed vires praebeat per Spiritum sanctum, ut eas suffere possimus.

11. Quòd Ecclesia Iesu Christi habeat ius & potestatem iudicandi, de doctrinis omnium docentium in Ecclesia. Siquidem ipse Apostolus subiicit suam doctrinam iudicio Ecclesiae.

12. Quòd in sacrosancta Iesu Christi coena verè & substantialiter praesens sit verum & substantiale corpus, & verus & substantialis sanguis domini nostri Iesu Christi: qui non solum à dignis, & verè piis, ad confirmationem fidei, sed etiam ab indignis, hypocritis & impiis, ut Iuda, cùm accedunt ad mensam domini, ore percipiatur ad iudicium.

13. Quomodo libertate Christiana sit utendum: nimirum ita, ut semper gloriae Dei, aedificationi Ecclesiae, et utilitati proximi potiùs studeamus, quàm nostro commodo.

20. Quòd conscientiae nostrae libertas non pendeat ab alterius iudicio, sed à verbo Dei, quod nobis Christi beneficia patefacit.

## 11:1 Argument
CHAPTER XI.

As the whole Epistle, so also this chapter contains both doctrine and reproofs. There are, however, two principal parts of the chapter. In the first part he praises the Corinthians because they studiously imitate and retain the doctrine and rites commended to them by Paul: and he exhorts them to persevere in that study. He censures them, however, because they sin in external discipline, in that they permit women to pray with head uncovered in the assembly of the faithful: but that men should pray with head covered. He teaches them, therefore, what is fitting for decency, and what nature itself teaches. The other part of the chapter is a discourse concerning the Lord's Supper, and its administration. Here he reproves first the abuse in the Corinthian Church: that they received the Eucharist confusedly, without fear of God, and intemperately: Then he delivers the institution of the Lord's Supper, and exhorts that individuals examine themselves, before they approach the sacred supper: lest they eat the body of the Lord unto judgment: he also warns that on account of this carelessness many in the Church are chastised with diseases: and finally he exhorts the whole Church to serious repentance.

Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ: Now I praise you, brethren, that ye remember me in all things, and keep the traditions, as I delivered them to you.

In the eighth, ninth, and tenth chapters, the Apostle Paul often proposed his own example to the teachers and to the Corinthian Church, from which they might know how they ought to use Christian liberty. But lest they might doubt whether they pleased God in all things by imitating Paul, he leads them to Christ himself. When you imitate me, he says, you do not imitate me only, but Christ himself, whom I always have in my sight, so that I may direct all my counsels and actions to his example. Christ did not seek his own advantages, but studied only the glory of God and the salvation of the Church: Thus it also behooves us to refer all our counsels and efforts to this end. He then commends the Church, because it well remembered the doctrine and rites which the Apostle Paul delivered to them. For although vices and abuses had crept into the Church: Yet they had not cast off the profession of Apostolic doctrine, nor did they ferociously change the institutions of Paul. Therefore, he commends those things which were right, so that they may continue in them: He censures and amends those things which had need of amendment: And thus he shows that he does not [act] out of hatred or desire of vengeance, but with fatherly love, and with an Apostolic Spirit, he chastised the Corinthians with such a severe speech. He also promises himself that by this commendation the Corinthians will be docile in other matters.

What Paul says, that the Corinthians hold the traditions and institutions, the papists transfer to their own invention, by which they establish two parts of the word of God, namely, written doctrine and unwritten tradition: And then they contend that we are bound with no less religion to unwritten traditions than to the doctrine comprised in the writings of the prophets and Apostles. If this were granted to them, then indeed they would be both very liberal and bold in establishing Apostolic traditions. For there is no idolatry so foul among the papists, no ceremony so futile and inept, no abuse of the sacraments so hideous, no dogma so blasphemous, and finally no worship so impious that is not covered by this veil: that it is, forsooth, an Apostolic tradition, although this can be proven by the testimony of no man: it must therefore be known that Paul by no means intends that uncertain traditions of the elders should be equaled to the word of God. Nay, elsewhere he warns that we should beware of the traditions of men. Colos: 2. Lest that impose upon you according to the tradition of men. But he speaks of traditions which they had certainly received from Paul, either in person or through Epistles.

First, therefore, when it is a matter of traditions, it must be seen whether they are expressly contained in the writings of the Apostles. For if this is discovered by you, one must acquiesce without any ambiguity to the Apostolic tradition: for the command of God is immovable, to which all men are bound to obey: Hear him: Likewise, he who hears you, hears me.

Next, if a tradition is not expressed in the Apostolic writings, it must be seen whether it conflicts with the word of God. For if this can be taught, nothing is more certain than that the tradition did not proceed from the Apostles. For it is a crime to think that the Apostles instituted rites conflicting with the express word of God. Therefore, whose testimonies of the fathers soever are brought forward into the midst, where a tradition disagrees with the writings of the Prophets and Apostles, it is to be rejected and removed without any hesitation. For Holy Scripture is the most straight and most certain norm of all religion, of all articles of faith, of all controversies of rites and worships: And it was piously and gravely said by Cyprian: It is adulterous, it is impious, it is sacrilegious, whatsoever is instituted by human madness, so that the divine disposition is violated. lib: 1. Epist: 8.

Thirdly, if any tradition is preached under the title of Apostolic authority, and it is neither expressly contained in the Apostolic writings, nor does it conflict with the express word of God, then we can certainly determine that it is not to be numbered among the articles of faith, nor even to be necessary for salvation. For all articles of faith, and whatever is necessary to be known for salvation, is explicitly and fully set forth in the Holy Scripture of the Old and New Testament. Therefore, tradition, which is not contained in the Apostolic writings, nor conflicts with them, is to be reckoned among the Adiaphora, or indifferent things. Nor indeed is a tradition to be embraced immediately, which is sold under the title of Apostolic institution: But certain and firm testimonies of antiquity and of approved authors must be sought. Next, it must be seen whether errors conflicting with the express word of God are attached to the Adiaphorous rites: When we discover this, we ought to reject them without hesitation, according to the command of Paul. If anyone shall have taught another Gospel, let him be anathema. In this place, therefore, Paul speaks of those traditions which he commended to the whole Church in his written Epistles, which pertain to faith and morals.

Latin:

CAPUT XI.

Ut tota Epistola, ita & hoc caput, cùm doctrinam, tùm reprehensiones, continet. Sunt autem duae praecipuae partes capitis. Priore parte laudat Corinthios, quòd doctrinam et ritus à Paulo illis commendatos studiosè imitentur, & retineant: & hortatur ut in eo studio pergant: Taxat autem quòd peccent in externa disciplina, eò quòd permittant foeminis orare nudo capite in coetu fidelium: Viri verò orent capite tecto. Docet ergò eos quid congruat honestati, & quid ipsa natura doceat. Altera pars capitis est concio de coena dominica, & eius administratione. Hîc reprehendit primùm abusum in Ecclesia Corinthiaca: quòd confusè, sine timore Dei, & bene poti Eucharistiam acciperent: Deinde tradit institutionem coenae dominicae, & hortatur ut singuli sese explorent, priusquam ad sacram coenam accedant: ne ad iudicium corpus domini edant: monet etiam ob hanc securitatem multos in Ecclesia morbis castigari: & tandem hortatur totam Ecclesiam ad seriam paenitentiam.

Imitatores mei estote, quemadmodum & ego Christi: Laudo autem vos fratres, quòd omnia mea memoria tenetis, & quemadmodum tradidi vobis, traditiones observatis.

In octavo, nono, & decimo capitibus saepè proposuit suum exemplum Apostolus Paulus doctoribus, & Ecclesiae Corinthiacae, ex quo scire possent quomodo uti debeant Christiana libertate. Ne autem dubitare possent, num in omnibus placerent Deo imitando Paulum ad Christum ipsum deducit ipsos. Cum me imitamini inquit, non me tantum, sed ipsum Christum imitamini, quem ego semper in conspectu habeo, ut ad ipsius exemplum omnia mea consilia, & actiones dirigam. Christus non quaesivit sua commoda, sed tantum gloriae Dei, & saluti Ecclesiae studuit: Sic & nos decet huc referre omnia nostra consilia & conatus. Commendat deinde Ecclesiam, quòd probè meminerit doctrinae, et rituum, quos tradidit eis Apostolus Paulus. Etsi enim irrepserant vitia & abusus in Ecclesiam: Non tamen abiecerant doctrinae Apostolicae professionem, nec mutabant ferociter Pauli instituta. Quae ergò recta erant commendat, ut in iis pergant: Quae emendatione opus habebant, taxat & emendat: Atque ita ostendit, se non ex odio vel cupiditate vindictae, sed amore paterno, & Apostolico Spiritu tam severa oratione castigasse Corinthios. Pollicetur etiam sibi hac commendatione Corinthios fore in caeteris dociles.

Quod Paulus dicit Corinthios tenere traditiones & instituta, hoc pontificii transferunt ad suum figmentum, quo duas statuunt partes verbi Dei, nimirum doctrinam scriptam, & traditionem non scriptam: Ac Deinde contendunt non minore religione ad traditiones non scriptas, nos obligatos esse, atque ad doctrinam, in scriptis prophetarum & Apostolorum comprehensam. Hoc si illis concederetur, tum sanè admodum essent & liberales & audaces in statuendis traditionibus Apostolicis. Nulla enim tam foeda Idolomania apud pontificios, nulla tam futilis & inepta ceremonia, nullus tam teter sacramentorum abusus, nullum tam blasphemum dogma, nullus denique tam impius cultus est qui non tegatur hoc velamine: Esse nimirum traditionem Apostolicam, licet hoc nullius hominis testimonio probari possit: sciendum est igitur, Paulum ne qua quam hoc velle quod incertae traditiones maiorum verbo Dei sint aequandae. Imò alibi monet, ut traditiones hominum caveamus. Colos: 2. Secundum traditionem hominum ne illa vobis imponat. Sed de traditionibus loquitur, quas vel coram, vel per Epistolas certò à Paulo acceperant.

Primùm ergò cùm de traditionibus agitur, videndum est, num expressè in scriptis Apostolorum contineantur. Hoc enim si tibi deprehensum est, sine omni ambiguitate acquiescendum est Apostolicae traditioni: immotum enim mandatum Dei est, cui omnes homines parere tenentur: Hunc audite: Item, qui vos audit, me audit.

Deinde, si non exprimatur traditio in scriptis Apostolicis, videndum est, num ea pugnet cum verbo Dei. Hoc enim si doceri potest, nihil est certius, quàm traditionem non esse profectam ab Apostolis. Nefas enim est cogitare, quòd Apostoli instituerint ritus cum expresso Dei verbo pugnantes. Quorumque igitur patrum testimonia proferantur in medium, ubi traditio discrepat à scriptis Prophetarum & Apostolorum, sine omni haesitatione reiicienda & tollenda est. Sacra enim scriptura norma est rectissima & certissima totius religionis, omnium articulorum fidei, omnium controversiarum rituum et cultuum: Et piè ac graviter à Cypriano dictum est: Adulterum est, impium est, sacrilegum est, quodcunque humano furore instituitur, ut divina violetur dispositio. lib: 1. Epist: 8.

Tertiò, si qua traditio sub titulo Apostolicae authoritatis praedicetur, neque ea expressè continetur in scriptis Apostolicis: Neque etiam pugnat cum expresso Dei verbo, tum certò statuere possumus, eam inter fidei articulos non esse numerandam, neque etiam ad salutem necessariam esse. Omnes enim fidei articuli, & quidquid ad salutem necessarium est cognitu, disertè & plene in sacra scriptura veteris & novi testamenti est expositum. Traditio igitur, quae Apostolicis scriptis non continetur, neque cum iis pugnat, inter Adiaphora, seu res medias recensenda est. Nec verò statim amplectenda est traditio, quae venditatur titulo Apostolicae institutionis: Sed certa & firma testimonia antiquitatis & probatorum authorum inquirenda sunt. Deinde videndum est, num ritibus Adiaphoris adfingantur errores cum expresso Dei verbo pugnantes: Quod cum deprehendimus, sine dubitatione eas reiicere debemus, iuxta praeceptum Pauli. Si quis aliud Evangelion docuerit, sit anathema. Hoc ergò loco Paulus de iis traditionibus loquitur, quas scriptis Epistolis toti Ecclesiae commendavit, quae ad fidem & mores pertinent.

## 11:3-5
But I want you to know, that the head of every man is Christ: but the head of the woman is the man: the head of Christ, God. Every man praying or having the Prophets with something on his head, brings reproach upon his head. But every woman praying or Prophesying: with her head not veiled, dishonors her head. For that is just the same as if she

Latin:

Volo autem vos scire, quòd omnis viri caput Christus est: Caput autem mulieris vir: Caput Christi, Deus. Omnis vir orans seu Prophetas habens aliquid in capite, probro adficit caput suum. Omnis verò mulier orans aut Prophetans: non velato capite, dehonestat caput suum. Nam id perinde est, ac si rasa

## 11:6
were shaven. For if the woman is not covered, let her also be shorn. But if it is shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her be covered.

It is likely that the Corinthian women, as in a wealthy city full of lasciviousness, behaved too licentiously in the public assembly of the saints, and that some prayed with heads uncovered in the public gathering. The Apostle censures and corrects this lascivious custom, and teaches that women ought to pray with covered heads: but men with heads uncovered. And he adds reasons for this precept of his:

The first is because Christ is the head of the man: but the man is the head of the woman. Therefore, the man ought to profess his liberty and dominion with an uncovered head, which he possesses in Christ: the woman ought to profess with a covering that she is under her husband. Christ is indeed the head of the whole Church, as much of holy women as of reborn men, and He provides life and Spirit to all His members. And in Christ Jesus there is neither male nor female: the male does not have a prerogative over the female, so that he is rather saved: But here Paul speaks of the peculiar order by which God ordained that men should bear the ministry of teaching, and obtain the primacy, and preside with authority over their spouses. God, he says, is the head of Christ: for Christ in the flesh received the primacy and the office of high priest from the eternal Father; and therefore He refers all things Christ to the glory of the eternal Father. The doctrine, he says, which you hear, is not mine, but his who sent me. Christ is the head of the man: that is, Christ has entrusted the ministry to the man: he has constituted him a prince in the family, and has adorned him with this glory, that in ministry and government he may represent Christ the Lord, therefore he ought to refer all things to the glory of Christ: and with head uncovered profess that he is free in Christ. The man is the head of the woman: that is, the woman both is from the man and has glory and honor from her husband: for the wife shines with the rays of her husband: therefore with covered head she ought to profess that she is under the power of her husband, and that she owes modesty and reverence to her husband.

Paul takes the second reason from common sense and the light of nature: Reason itself naturally warns that it is shameful if a woman is shorn or shaved: because nature itself has adorned women with hair, and it is foul to the sight if a woman is seen with a shorn or shaved head: But for a woman to be seen with a bare head is just as if she were shorn or shaved. Therefore nature itself teaches what is becoming and honest. Therefore when a woman prays in a public assembly, let her cover her head, and modestly acknowledge that she is under the power of her husband.

Latin:

esset. Etenim si non velatur mulier, etiam tondeatur. Quod si turpe est mulieri tonderi aut radi, veletur.

Verisimile est, mulieres Corinthiacas, ut in opulenta & lasciviae plena urbe, nimis licenter se gessisse in publico coetu sanctorum, & quasdam nudo capite orasse in publico congressu, Hunc lascivum morem taxat, & corrigit Apostolus, & docet mulieres debere velato capite orare: viros autem aperto capite. Et huius sui praecepti addit rationes:

Prima est, quia Christus sit caput viri: vir autem sit caput mulieris. Ergò vir nudo capite libertatem suam, et dominium profiteri debet, quod possidet in Christo: Mulier tegmine profiteri debet, quod sit sub marito. Est quidem Christus caput totius Ecclesiae, tam mulierum sanctarum, quàm virorum renatorum, & omnibus suis membris praebet vitam & Spiritum.
