Et in Christo Iesu neque est mas, neque foemina: mas non habet praerogativam prae muliere, ut potius salvetur: Verum hîc Paulus loquitur de peculiari ordine, quo Deus instituit, ut virigerant docendi ministerium, & obtineant principatum, & authoritate praesint coniugibus. Deus inquit est caput Christi: Christus enim in carne principatum, & munus summi pontificis à patre aeterno accepit; atque ideò omnia refert Christus ad gloriam patris aeterni. Doctrina inquit quam auditis, non est mea, sed eius qui memisit. Christus est caput viri: hoc est, Christus commendavit viro ministerium: constituit eum principem in familia, & hac gloria eum ornavit, ut in ministerio & gubernatione repraesentet Christum dominum, omnia igitur ad gloriam Christi referre debet: & capite aperto profiteri, quod sit liber in Christo. Vir est caput mulieris: hoc est, mulier & est à viro & gloriam & honorem à marito habet: uxor enim coruscat radiis mariti: velato igitur capite profiteri debet, quod sit sub mariti potestate, & quòd verecundiam, & reverentiam debeat marito.

Secundam rationem sumit Paulus à sensu communi, & luce naturae: Ipsa ratio naturalis admonet, turpe esse, si radatur vel tondeatur foemina: quia ipsa natura ornavit mulieres coma, & foedum aspectu est si conspiciatur mulier raso vel tonso capite: Sed capite nudo conspici mulierem, perinde est, ac si tondeatur vel radatur. Ergò ipsa natura docet, quid sit decorum & honestum. Mulier ergo cum orat in publico coetu, velet caput suum, & verecundè agnoscat, se sub potestate mariti esse.

## 11:7-12
A man indeed ought not to cover his head: being the image and glory of God. But the woman is the glory of the man. For the man is not from the woman, but the woman from the man. Nor was the man created for the woman, but the woman for the man. Therefore, she ought to have power, that is, a veil, upon her head, because of the angels.

The same is the argument, which he posited above, concerning the excellence and eminence of the husband in marriage. God has so ordained, that although each sex is created to the image and glory of God: nevertheless the man obtains the primacy in the family, and is as it were a certain king in his own home, who acts in the place of God and Christ in the family. It is fitting therefore for the man as lord in his own family to represent Christ the Lord with covered head. For he is the image and glory of God. This is by his duty and office and primacy over his family, he reflects Christ, and is an ornament of God, who created him and established him as lord. It is not said here concerning the spiritual image, to which male and female is created, which is restored through the Holy Spirit, as much in the female as in the male: but concerning the order of sex, and the glory of the ministry, and Ecclesiastical polity. The woman is the glory of the man: That is, she is a distinguished ornament and crown of the man: for it is a great glory of the man, that God has joined such a companion of life to him. Solomon Proverb: 12. pronounces concerning a diligent wife, that she is the crown of her husband:

But here the Holy Spirit pronounces concerning the whole sex, and looks back to the history of creation. Most heathen writers, especially Euripides, treat this sex with great insult: but they are insulting toward God, the author of the sex, and ungrateful toward their parents, from whom they drew their origin. The Holy Spirit, however, is accustomed in Holy Scripture to adorn the works of God with various praises. Then the Apostle proves the preeminence of the man with two arguments, that is, because the woman was taken from the man. God, says the Scripture, took a rib from the side of Adam, and fashioned the woman. And Adam says, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh, therefore she shall be called woman. Gen: 2. The other is, because the woman was created for the sake of the man, and not the man for the sake of the woman. For when a helper was not found that was before Adam, God said, It is not good for man to be alone, I will make him a helper that is before him. Therefore, in order the man is prior, and in preeminence superior. Therefore, the woman ought to signify by a covering that she is under the power of the man. Then the Apostle adds a third reason why women ought to cover their head with a shawl or veil in a public assembly, namely on account of the angels, who, since they are constant guardians of the pious, and especially delight in public gatherings in which the word of God is preached, and God is worshipped with true invocation and thanksgiving, are vehemently offended by the wantonness of women and the foul custom, from which nature itself shrinks.

Nevertheless neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in the Lord: For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman: but all things of God.

Paul adds limits to his opinion, in what sense he wishes these things to be accepted, lest anyone abuse the opinion of the Apostle. As if he were to say: I do not say these things so that men may proudly despise their wives, or exalt themselves, or think that they have a prerogative in obtaining salvation: But only that a decent and convenient order of discipline and of Ecclesiastical polity may be observed. Outside of this rank, women as well as men are creatures of God, and pertain to the promise concerning the inheritance of eternal life. Otherwise, he says, neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in the Lord. That is, neither sex could exist and beget without the other. Therefore, they ought to show mutual benevolence and love toward one another. Let the man piously consider that he was born of a woman and that by the ordination of God a helper was created for him: and therefore let him show honor to this sex: let the woman piously consider that she was created from the man and for the sake of the man, and by the ordination of God is subject to her husband: Wherefore let her with a ready mind subject herself to him and show reverence. The Apostle adds in the Lord: By which particle he signifies this prudence and

moderation and virtue are provided only by those who are members of Jesus Christ and are led by the Holy Spirit. For impious men, if they can do without wives, treat the sex with insult: if they cannot do without them, they are tyrants to their spouses and are angry at the necessity of nature: Whence the heathens said, A wife is a necessary evil. Conversely, women, if they are not pious, either wish to dominate their husbands with the order disturbed, or they obey their husbands with an unwilling mind: Because they do not acknowledge the will of the Lord. Therefore Paul admonishes pious spouses, that in the fear of the Lord they may look to the author of the human race, who created male and female, and submit themselves to his will and ordinance.

Judge among yourselves, whether it is proper that a woman should pray to God unveiled: Does not even nature itself teach you, that a man, if he nourishes his hair, brings disgrace upon himself, but a woman if she nourishes her hair, it is an honor to her: Because hair is given to her for a covering.

He repeats the argument which he took from the judgment of nature. Nature itself teaches that the sex must be distinguished, and that hair is both a covering and an ornament for women. Therefore do not oppose nature. Doctrine of the Gospel does not extinguish or delete the remnants of natural judgment, but rather restores and rekindles the light of nature that had been obscured. And it adds a new heavenly light, which was unknown to the whole of reason.

Latin:

Vir quidem non debet velare caput: imago & gloria Dei existens. Mulier autem gloria viri. Non enim vir est ex muliere, sed mulier ex viro. Neque conditus est vir propter mulierem, sed mulier propter virum. Quapropter debet potestatem, id est, velamen habere in capite, propter angelos.

Idem argumentum est, quod supra posuit, de excellentia et eminentia mariti in coniugio. Ita ordinavit Deus, ut quanquam uterque sexus ad imaginem et gloriam Dei sit conditus: tamen vir principatum obtineat in familia, et tanquam rex quidam sit domi suae, qui vices Dei & Christi agat in familia. Decet ergò virum ut dominum in familia sua de tecto capite Christum dominum repraesentare. Nam imago & gloria est Dei. Hoc est munere et officio et principatu suo super familiam suam, refert Christum, & est ornamentum Dei, qui condidit eum & constituit eum dominum. Non hîc dicitur de imagine spirituali, ad quam mas & foemina est conditus, quae per Spiritum sanctum, tam in foemina quàm in mare restituitur: sed de ordine sexus, & gloria ministerii, & politia Ecclesiastica. Mulier est gloria viri: Id est, insigne ornamentum & corona est viri: magna enim gloria est viri, quòd talem vitae sociam adumxit et Deus. Salomon Proverb: 12. de munere sedula pronunciat, quòd sit corona mariti:

sed hîc Spiritus sanctus de toto sexu pronunciat, & ad historiam creationis respicit. Ethnici scriptores plerique, inprimis Eurypides, magna contumelia hunc sexum adficiunt: sed contumeliosi sunt in Deum authorem sexus, & ingrati in parentes, ex quibus ortum duxerunt. Spiritus sanctius verò in sacra scriptura variis encomiis opera Dei ornare solet. Duobus deinde argumentis probat Apostolus viri eminentiam, Id est, Quia mulier ex viro sit desumpta. Sumpsit, inquit scriptura, Deus costam è latere Adae, & fabricavit mulierem. Et Adam inquit. Hoc nunc est os ex ossibus meis, & caro de carne mea, propterea virago vocabitur. Gen: 2. Alterum est, quia mulier propter virum est condita, & non vir propter mulierem. Cùm enim non inveniretur adiutorium, quod coram Adam esset, dixit Deus, non esse bonum homini esse soli, faciam et auditorium, quod coram eo sit. Ordine igitur prior est vir, & eminentia superior. Ergo mulier tegumento significare debet, quod sit sub potestate viri. Addit deinde Apostolus rationem tertiam, cur mulieres peplo, vel velamine tegere caput debeant in publico caetu, nimirum propter angelos, qui cùm sint adsidui custodes piorum, et inprimis delectentur publicis congressibus, in quibus praedicatur Dei verbum, et Deus vera invocatione et gratiarum actione colitur, vehementer offenduntur mulierum lascivia et foeda consuetudine, à qua ipsa natura abhorret.

Caeterum neque vir absque muliere neque mulier absque viro in domino: Quemadmodum enim mulier ex viro: Ita & vir per mulierem: Omnia autem ex Deo.

Paulus limites addit suae sententiae, quo sensu haec accipi velit, ne quis Apostoli sententia abutatur. Quasi dicat: Non haec eo dico ut viri super bè contemnant uxores, aut sese efferant, aut se praerogativam habere existiment in adipiscenda salute: Sed tantum ut decens & conveniens ordo disciplinae, & politiae Ecclesiasticae observetur. Extra hunc gradum tam mulieres quam viri & creaturae sunt Dei, & ad promissionem de vitae aeternae haereditate pertinent. Alioquin inquit, neque vir absque muliere, neque mulier absque viro in domino. Id est, neuter sexus absque altero existere, & gignere posset. Itaque mutuam inter se benevolentiam & amorem exhibere debent. Vir piè cogitet se ex muliere natum esse & Dei ordinatione sibi adiutorium conditum esse: ideoque huic sexui exhibeat honorem: mulier piè cogitet se ex viro & propter virum conditam esse, & Dei ordinatione marito subiectam: Quare prompto animo sese ei subiiciat & reverentiam praestet. Addit Apostolus in domino: Qua particula significat hanc prudentiam &

moderationem & virtutem tantùm ab iis praestari, qui sunt membra Iesu Christi, & ducuntur Spiritu sancto. Nam viri impii, si uxoribus carere possunt, contumelia adficiunt sexum: Sicarere nequeunt tyranni sunt coniugum, & necessitati naturae irascuntur: Unde Ethnici dixerunt, Uxor est necessarium malum. Vicissim mulieres, si non sint piae, aut ordine turbato viris dominari volunt, aut invito animo parent maritis: Quia voluntatem domini non agnoscunt. Monet ergò Paulus pios coniuges, ut intimore domini ad authorem generis humani, qui masculum & foeminam condidit, respiciant, et eius voluntatiet ordinationi sese subiiciant.

Inter vos ipsos iudicate, num decorum sit, ut mulier non velata oret Deum: Annon & ipsa natura docet vos, quòd vir, si comam nutriat, seipsum probro adficiat, mulier autem si comam nutriat, est illi honori: Quia coma pro velamine data est ei.

Repetit argumentum, quod sumpsit àiudicio naturae. Ipsa natura docet distinguendun esse sexum, & comam esse & velamen & ornamentum mulierum. Non ergò repugnetis naturae. Doctrina enim Evangelii non extinguit aut delet reliquias naturalis iudicii, sed potius lumen naturae obscuratum restituit & rursus accendit. Et addit novum coeleste lumen, quod toti rationi fuit incognitum.

## 11:16
But, if anyone seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the Churches of God.

Lest the Corinthians oppose their sophisms and subtle disputations with Greek custom, just as if they were brawling about philosophical matters, Paul breaks off the disputation and warns that one must abstain from contention. He says, I have neither the leisure, nor does my custom allow me to brawl with contentious men. Nor do the Churches of God have this custom, that they should litigate without end after the manner of contentious men, but the Church, when it hears either clear testimonies of Holy Scripture or weighty and pious reasons, placidly acquiesces, and does not further make trouble for either the teachers or itself. Thus I wish that, with contentions omitted, you may acquiesce in this pious and weighty opinion.

Latin:

Caeterùm, si quis videtur contentiosus esse, nos huiusmodi consuetudinem non habemus, neque Ecclesiae Dei.

Ne Corinthii Graeca consuetudine opponant sua sophismata & argutas disputationes, perinde ac si de Philosophicis rebus rixarentur, abrumpit Paulus disputationem, & monet à contentione abstinendum esse. Mihi inquit nec ocium est, neque mea consuetudo fert ut rixer cum hominibus contentiosis. Neque Ecclesiae Dei hanc consuetudinem habent, ut more contentiosorum hominum sine fine litigent, sed Ecclesia cùm audit vel clara sacrae scripturae testimonia, vel graves & pias rationes placidè acquiescit, neque amplius vel doctoribus vel sibi ipsi facessit negocium. Ita volo, ut omissis contentionibus in hac pia & gravi sententia acquiescatis.

## 11:16 The Second Part of This Chapter
THE SECOND PART OF THIS CHAPTER.

But in giving this charge I do not praise you, because you come together not for the better, but for the worse. For first of all, when you come together in the Church, I hear that there are divisions among you: And in part I believe it. For there must be sects among you, that those who are approved may be made manifest among you.

In this second part of the chapter, the Apostle again censures and corrects another abuse which had crept into the Corinthian Church. For some had turned the Lord's Supper into profane feastings and drinking bouts, and were fostering divisions among themselves, and the richer ones were indulging in luxuries in the Church, and were putting the poor to shame, and thus many were receiving the body and blood of Christ unto judgment. Therefore, the Apostle gravely censures this abuse, exhorts the Church to true repentance and the fear of the Lord: And by repeating the institution and doctrine of the Lord's Supper, he restores its true and salutary use.

That the Apostle confesses that there are divisions in the Corinthian Church, which had been founded by the Apostles, this agrees with the Lord's parable concerning the enemy, who at night, while men were sleeping, sows tares in the Lord's field. Wherefore, one must both watch and pray against this enemy.

And by the testimony of the Apostle and the parable of Christ, the Donatists are refuted, who imagine and require a Church of such a kind in which the evil are not mixed with the good, nor do any dissensions exist. Since Christ expressly says, let both grow until the harvest, at the time of the harvest God will command his angels to gather the tares and cast them into the fire, which shall not be extinguished.

The saying of Paul, There must be heresies, is not to be understood in such a way that the will of God or fate is the cause of heresies or sects: For the sentence must always be kept in view, You are not a God who wills iniquity. Psalm 5. Likewise, These are the things that I hate, says the Lord: Zach: 8. But that in this corrupt nature of men, and while the tyranny of Satan lasts in the world, it cannot be otherwise than that heresies and sects arise. For Satan, burning with horrible hatred of Christ and the saving truth, with tireless zeal instigates and inflames light, restless, and ambitious minds so that they may sow false dogmas and be the authors of new sects: That he may afflict Christ with insult, inflict wounds upon the Church, and hinder the salvation of many men.

Nor do all who join themselves to the Church by a confession of doctrine seriously perform penance, nor do they assiduously call upon God in Spirit and in truth, but many live securely, they are slaves of empty glory, or they are devoted to their belly, and they feign religion with hypocrisy. Since these causes exist, namely the hatred and fury of Satan against the truth, and the fickleness, and the ambition and impiety of many men, it cannot happen otherwise in the world than that sects and heresies arise. Yet the attempt of Satan does not succeed: For neither is the truth oppressed by heresies, nor is the Church utterly destroyed: Which is what Satan uniquely seeks. Rather, God knows how to use this evil for His own glory and the utility of the Church: for through these very heresies, those who are approved and firm in sincere piety become conspicuous, while they oppose themselves bravely to false dogmas, and persist constantly in the truth: Heresies also, once arisen, provide an occasion for more ardently imploring the help of the Holy Spirit, that He may lead us into all truth, and that He may repress the horrendous blasphemies of the fanatics: They are also an occasion for studying the scriptures with greater zeal, for inquiring into the truth, and for more attentively weighing the individual testimonies of the Holy Spirit.

The Church reaps this abundant fruit from heresies through the admirable governance and most wise disposition of God, who can use even the worst things for His own glory. Nevertheless, God also abominates heresies and punishes them with the most grave punishments: And the Church detests them from the heart, as the foulest works of Satan. When, therefore, the pious observe that sects arise in the Church, let them not be troubled, as if the Church were about to perish, nor let them desert the Church on account of the tares, but let them themselves take pains that they may be wheat, and both learn the truth and pray to the Lord so much the more fervently.

Latin:

SECUNDA PARS HUIUS CAPITIS.

Hoc autem praecipiens non laudo, quòd non in melius, sed deterius convenitis. Primum enim convenientibus vobis in Ecclesia, audio esse dissidia: Et ex parte credo. Oportet enim sectas in vobis esse, ut qui probati sunt manifesti fiant inter vos.

In hac secunda parte capitis rursus alium abusum, qui irrepserat in Ecclesiam Corinthiacam taxat & emendat Apostolus. Coenam enim dominicam converterant aliqui in prophanas comessationes & compotationes & inter sese dissidia fovebant, & ditiores deliciabantur in Ecclesia, & pudefacie bant pauperes, atque ita ad iudicium plerique accipiebant corpus & sanguinem Christi. Graviter igitur taxat Apostolus hunc abusum, hortatur Ecclesiam ad veram poenitentiam & timorem domini: Et repetendo institutionem & doctrinam coenae dominicae, restituit verum & salutarem eius usum.

Quòd fatetur Apostolus in Ecclesia Corinthiaca, quae ab Apostolis fundata erat, esse dissidia, congruit hoc cum parabola dominica de hoste, qui noctu dormientibus hominibus, serit zizania in agro domini. Quare contra hunc hostem & vigilandum & orandum est.

Et Apostoli testimonio & parabola Christi refutantur Donatistae, qui eiusmodi fingunt & requirunt Ecclesiam, in qua mali non sint admixti bonis, nec ulla existant dissidia. Cùm Christus disertè dicat, sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem, tempore messis mandabit Deus angelis suis, ut colligant zizania, & coniiciant ea in ignem, qui non extinguetur.

Dictum Pauli. Oportet esse haereses, non est ita intelligendum, quòd Dei voluntas, seu fatum sit causa haeresium seu sectarum: Semper enim in conspectu habenda est sententia. Non Deus volens iniquitatem tu es. Psalm 5. Item, Haec sunt quae odi, dicit dominus: Zach: 8. Sed quòd in hac corrupta hominum natura, & durante tyrannide Satanae in mundo fieri aliter non possit, quàm ut exoriantur haereses & sectae. Satan enim ardens horribili odio Christi & salutaris veritatis indefesso studio instigat & accendit levia, inquieta & ambitiosa ingenia, ut serant falsa dogmata, & novarum sectarum authores sint: Ut Christum contumeliae adficiat, vulnera infligat Ecclesiae, & multorum hominum salutem impediat.

Nec omnes, qui se adiungunt. Ecclesiae confessione doctrinae seriò agunt poenitentiam, nec adsiduè in Spiritu & veritate invocunt Deum, sed multi vivunt securè, sunt mancipia inanis gloriae, aut student ventri, & hypocrisi simulant religionem. Hae causae, cùm existant, nimirum odium & furor Satanae adversus veritatem, et levitas, et ambitio & impietas multorum hominum, fieri aliter in mundo non potest quin exoriantur sectae & haereses. Nec tamen conatus Satanae succedit: Nec enim veritas opprimitur haeresibus, neque Ecclesia funditus deletur: Quod unicè quaerit Satanas. Quin Deus hoc malo utinovit ad suam gloriam & utilitatem Ecclesiae: per ipsas enim haereses probati & in syncera pietate firmi fiunt conspicui, dum se fortiter falsis dogmatibus opponunt, & constanter in veritate persistunt: Haereses etiam ex ortae praebent occasionem ardentius implorandi auxilium Spiritus sancti, ut ducat nos in omnem veritatem, & ut reprimat horrendas blasphemias fanaticorum: Sunt etiam occasio maiore studio scrutandi scripturas, inquirendi veritatem, & attentius perpendendi singula testimonia Spiritus sancti.

Hunc uberem fructum admiranda gubernatione & sapientissima dispositione Dei, qui etiam pessimis uti potest ad suam gloriam, percipit Ecclesia exhaeresibus. Nihilominus & Deus abominatur haereses & gravissimis suppliciis punit eas: Et Ecclesia ex animo detestatur eas, ut opera foedissima Satanae. Quando ergò pii animadvertunt exoriri in Ecclesia sectas, ne turbentur, quasi pereundum sit Ecclesiae, nec propter zizania deserant Ecclesiam, sed ipsi dent operam, ut sint triticum, & tanto ardentiùs & discant veritatem, & orent dominum.

## 11:20-22
When therefore you come together in one place, it is not to eat the Lord's supper. For every one taketh before other his own supper in eating: and one is hungry, and another is drunken. What? have you not houses to eat and to drink in? Or despise you the church of God, and shame them that have not (food?) What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you in this? I praise you not.

Here now he approaches more closely to the abuse of the Lord's supper, which he determined to censure. Because the Corinthians were celebrating the Lord's supper with great carelessness, undoubtedly not one or two only, but many sins concurred. It was a grave crime that they were converting the Lord's supper, in which the body and blood of Jesus Christ was distributed, into feastings and drinkings. It was a grave sin that they were defrauding the poor in the public supper: It was a grave sin that they were despising the Church of Jesus Christ and might put the poorer to shame. Without doubt, some were also corrupting the doctrine itself: For those who got drunk at the supper did not believe that the blessed bread was the true body of Jesus Christ: And that the wine was his true blood. Therefore, the Apostle censures these grave and enormous abuses in ecclesiastical doctrine and discipline, and teaches that one must approach the holy communion reverently, soberly, and in the fear of God: And that this Lord's supper must be accurately distinguished from other banquets. In the primitive Church, it was the custom that as often as the pious gathered, the wealthier would bring gifts with them, bread, wine, and other kinds of food, and after they had heard the sermon and sung Psalms, they would prepare a banquet to refresh the poor, and then the Lord's supper was also distributed; Tertullian describes this custom of the ancient Church in his Apologeticus. The Corinthians, however, corrupted this custom: For having neglected the poor and removed them from themselves, they celebrated banquets and drank before the Church, unmindful both of brotherly love and of true repentance. Therefore, this abuse of the Lord's supper was worthy of grave reprehension.

The best method, however, for correcting the errors, and abuses, and depraved morals of the Church, is that which is done through the repetition and explanation of the doctrine handed down by Christ, and through serious exhortation to repentance.

For the foundation of the Church is the sound and incorrupt doctrine concerning Jesus Christ. Therefore, Paul repeats and explains here the doctrine concerning the Lord's Supper: and then he exhorts the Corinthians to serious repentance. So that we may understand Paul's sermon more fully, and weigh his individual sayings more attentively, I will explain the whole article concerning the Lord's Supper, as much as the Lord will grant through His Spirit, in order.

Latin:

Convenientibus ergò vobis in unum, non est dominicam coenam edere. Unusquisque enim propriam coenam sumit edendo: Et alius quidem esurit, alius verò est ebrius. Annon domos habetis ad edendum & bibendum? Num Ecclesiam Dei contemnitis? Et pudefacitis eos, qui non habent (cibum?) Quid vobis dicam? Laudabo vos in hoc? Non laudo.

Hic iam propius accedit ad abusum coenae domini, quem taxare constituit. Quia Corinthii magna securitate celebrabant coenam domini, haud dubiè non unum aut duo tantum, sed multa concurrerunt peccata. Grave scelus fuit, quòd coenam domini, in qua distribuebatur corpus & sanquis Iesu Christi, convertebant in comessationes & potationes. Grave peccatum erat, quòd pauperes defraudabant in coena publica: Grave peccatum fuit, quòd contemnerent Ecclesiam Iesu Christi & pauperiores pudefacerent. Haud dubiè etiam ipsam doctrinam corrumpebant aliqui: Nam qui sese in coena inebriarunt, ii non crediderunt panem benedictum esse verum corpus Iesu Christi: Et vinum esse verum sanguinem ipsius. Hos ergò graves & enormes abusus in doctrina & disciplina Ecclesiastica taxat Apostolus, & docet reverenter, sobriè & in timore Dei accedendum esse ad sacram synaxin: Et hanc coenam Dominicam accuratè distinguendam esse ab aliis conviviis. In primitiva Ecclesia consuetudo fuit ut quoties convenirent pii, ditiores munera secum adferrent, panem, vinum, & alia ciborum genera, & postquam concionem audiverant & Psalmos cantaverant, convivium instruebant ad reficiendos pauperes, deinde & coena domini distribuebatur, hanc morem veteris Ecclesiae Tertullia: in Apologetico describit. Corinthii autem corruperunt hanc consuetudinem: Pauperibus enim neglectis & à se remotis, convivia celebrarunt, & coram Ecclesia potarunt, immemores & fraternae dilectionis & verae poenitentiae. Gravi igitur reprehensione dignus fuit. iste abusus coenae domini.

Optima autem ratio est emendandi errores, & abusus & pravos mores Ecclesiae, quae fit per repetitionem & explicationem doctrinae à Christo traditae, & per seriam adhortationem ad poenitentiam.

Fundamentum enim Ecclesiae est sana & incorrupta, doctrina de Iesu Christo. Paulus igitur repetit & explicat hîc doctrinam de coena domini: & deinde hortatur Corinthios ad seriam poenitentiam. Ut ergò Pauli concionen plenius intelligamus, & singula eius dicta attentius expendamus, totum articulum de coena domini, quantum dominus per Spiritum suum dabit, ordine explicabo.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper
CONCERNING THE LORD'S SUPPER.

Latin:

DE COENA DOMINI.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper: Chapter I. Concerning the Appellations
CHAPTER I. Concerning the Appellations.

Since the Lord's Supper is named by various appellations in the Church, it is to be observed which appellations the Holy Spirit Himself has used, and which were customary in the ancient Church, and whence they were born.

I. The Holy Spirit in 1 Cor. 11 calls it the Lord's Supper δεῖπνον κυριακὸν, because it was instituted by the Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and in it the Lord Jesus Christ Himself is truly present and distributes His Body and blood: which must be accurately distinguished from all other suppers. Thus also τράπεζαν κυριόν Paul names it, as that which is not a common table for refreshing the Body: But which the Lord Jesus Christ himself instructed for fostering the salvation of our soul.

2. The disciples of the Apostles then called it ἐυχαριστίαν thanksgiving; because the Evangelists say, Christ ἐυχαριστήσας broke: That is, Christ by giving thanks consecrated this Bread & Wine: And we in the use of the supper ought to give thanks to God for the redemption of the Church, which was made through the death of the son of God. Thus Irenaeus says: The Eucharist consists of two things, earthly & heavenly. lib: 5. And Tertullian: de Coro: militis. The Sacrament of the Eucharist, both in the time of the meal and to all, was commanded by the Lord, even before the dawn gatherings, nor do we take it from the hand of others than those presiding.

3. Thus also they called it synaxis from the congregation of the faithful. For Paul also says: when you come together. Chrysost: to: 3. in acta Apost: Homil: 18. For prayers are made for you perpetually, and praises & Synaxes, and the oblation on each Lord's day. And Epiphanius says that the Churches have this custom from the Apostles, that they celebrate Synaxes on the fourth day, the sixth, and the Lord's day. pag: 465. συνάξεις δὲ ἐπιτελούμεναι ταχθεῖσαι εἰσίν ἀπότῶν ἀποστόλων τετράδι, καί προσαββάτῳ καί κυριακῇ.

4. Fourthly, it was customary for the Greeks to call the administration of the Lord's Supper λειτουργίαν, taking the occasion from the passage Acts 13 λειτουργούντων ἀυτῶν τῷ κυρὶῳ. As they were ministering to the Lord and fasting. Where Luke speaks of the whole ministry: While the Church was both praying, and hearing the word, and using the Lord's Supper, and fasting. For the word λειτουργία, does not signify a sacrifice, but a public ministry, in which sense it is used by Paul 2 Corinthians 9. Therefore, they transferred it also to the public administration of the Lord's Supper. Ignatius: Epistle 2 Λειτουργοῦντες ἀυτῷ λειτουργιαν καθαρὰν καὶ ἄμωμον. Item. Canon 28 of the Apostles: If any Bishop, or Presbyter, or Deacon, having been justly deposed for manifest crimes, shall have dared to touch the ministry previously entrusted to him, let this man be altogether cut off from the Church. Therefore, λειτουργία, does not properly signify the Lord's Supper, but the whole administration of the Lord's Supper: Namely, the public duty of teaching, prayers, thanksgiving, and the distribution of the Supper.

Fifthly, the ancients also named it Ἀγάπην, namely on account of the offices of love: Because the richer ones brought gifts, by which they relieved the poverty of the poor. Whence Tertullian says in his Apologeticus: Our supper shows its reason from its name.

That which is ἀγαπὴ among the Greeks is called love: At whatever expense it may stand, it is a gain to make an expenditure in the name of piety: Since indeed we also assist the needy with that refreshment. Therefore this appellation does not only embrace the Lord's supper, but the offices of charity, which were performed at the same time in the administration of the supper.

Sixthly, the Greeks often call the Lord's supper προσφοράν καὶ θυσίαν, which the Latins, having imitated, named oblation and sacrifice. The causes, however, of this appellation are: First, because the rich offered breads, and wine, and other things, by which the poor were fed and assisted: Second, because Eucharistic sacrifices, thanksgiving, invocation, the preaching of the divine name, confession, and the offices of brotherly love were offered to God in place of the typical sacrifices. Therefore, not the supper itself properly, but the offices of piety, which were performed by the pious in the use of the supper, were so called. Can: Apost: 8. If any Bishop προσφορᾶς γενομένης shall not have communicated, let him explain the cause. Thus also Irenaeus says: lib: 4. Ca: 32. Christ, having confessed the cup to be his own blood of the new testament, taught a new oblation. But because the papists so deprave this appellation that they pretend the Lord's supper to be ἱλαστικόν a sacrifice, in which the Body and blood of Jesus Christ are offered to God for the remission of sins, it is necessary to be known, that this was not the mind of the fathers, but that they understood it concerning the Eucharistic sacrifice, and spoke not of offering the body and blood of Christ, but of the works of the pious, namely of invocation, thanksgiving, confession, and similar duties, which Paul calls λογικήν λατρέιαν and Peter calls θυσιαν πνευματικὴν. Thus Irenaeus clearly says. In the incense John in the Apocalypse says there are the prayers of the saints.

Seventh: Some writers call it κοινωνίαν, καὶ φρίκτα μυστήρια, as Basil, in the oration: On Baptism. Also μυσταγωγίαν καὶ ἱερουργίαν, as Nazianzen. Τελέτην θείαν συνάξεως Also, Τελέτην τελέτων, as Dionysius. τελέτην ἀπορρητον as Synesius. A mystical blessing, as Cyril. δόχην a banquet, as Dionysius. But these appellations are so general that they can also befit other sacred rites and ceremonies.

Eighth. The Latins called it the Mass, concerning the origin of which word, since there are conjectures rather than interpretations, the simplest of all is that this name was born from the dismissal of the people after the sacred rites were performed: since the minister was accustomed to say: Go, it is dismissed: just as it was also customary in the Greek Church to say Τοῖς. λαοῖς ἄφεσις ἔστω That is, everyone is now dismissed to their own affairs.

No designation departs further from the designation which the Holy Spirit has used than the term Mass. And because the papal idolaters understand by this designation the blasphemous offering of the body and blood of Jesus Christ for the living and the dead, it would be entirely beneficial for this profane word to be abolished in the purified Church, which has nothing in common with the idolatrous and blasphemous sacrifice of the Mass of the papists. Or if anyone wishes to use this word at all, let him at the same time show that he is not speaking of the idolatrous worship of the Popish Mass. It would also have been desirable that the ancients had not called the Lord's Supper either an offering or a sacrifice, so that an occasion would not have been given to the error concerning the offering of the body of Christ in the Supper to appease the wrath of God.

The other designations of the ancient Church, although they are more general, can nevertheless be piously used, especially if declarations consistent with the word of God are added, and those agreeing with the confession of pious antiquity. But it will be safest of all to retain in the Church the designation which the Holy Spirit has bestowed upon this sacrament.

Latin:

CAPUT I. De Appellationibus.

Cum coena domini variis adpellationibus in Ecclesia nominetur, observandum est, quas appellationes ipse Spiritus sanctus usurpaverit, & quae in veteri Ecclesia usitatae fuerint, & unde natae sint.

I. Spiritus sanctus 1. Cor. 11. vocat coenam Dominicam δεῖπνον κυριακὸν, quia sit ab ipso Domino Iesu Christo instituta, & in ea ipse Dominus Iesus Christus sit verè praesens & suum Corpus & sangumem distribuat: quae accuratè ab omnibus aliis coenis distinguenda, est. Sic & τράπεζαν κυριόν nominat Paulus, ut quae non sit communis mensa ad reficiendum Corpus: Sed quam ipse Dominus Iesus Christus instruxit ad fovendam animae nostrae salutem.

2. Discipuli deinde Apostolorum vocarunt ἐυχαριστίαν gratiarum actionem; quia Evangelistae dicunt, Christus ἐυχαριστήσας fregit: Id est, Christus gratias agendo consecravit hunc Panem & Vinum: Et nos in usu coenae Deogratias agere debemus pro redemptione Ecclesiae, quae per mortem filii Dei facta est. Sic Ireneus inquit: Eucharistia constat duabus rebus terrena & caelesti. lib: 5. Et Tertullia: de Coro: militis. Eucharistiae Sacramentum & in tempore victus & omnibus mandatum à Domino, etiam ante Lucanis caetibus, nec de aliorum manu quam praesidentum sumimus.

3. Sic & synaxin à congregatione fidelium vocarunt. Nam & Paulus inquit: convenientibus vobis. Chrysost: to: 3. in acta Apost: Homil: 18. Nam & preces propter te per petuae fiunt, et laudes & Synaxes, & oblatio per singulos dies dominicos. Et Epiphanius dicit Ecclesias ab Apostolis hanc habere consuetudinem, ut Synaxes celebrent seria quarta, sexta, & die dominico. pag: 465. συνάξεις δὲ ἐπιτελούμεναι ταχθεῖσαι εἰσίν ἀπότῶν ἀποστόλων τετράδι, καί προσαββάτῳ καί κυριακῇ.

4. Quartò graecis usitatum fuit administrationem coenae domini adpellari λειτουργίαν sumpta occasione ex loco Acto: 13.λειτουργούντων ἀυτῶν τῷ κυρὶῳ. Ministrantibus ipsis Domino & ieiunantibus. Ubi Lucas de toto ministerio loquitur: Dum Ecclesia & preces faceret, & verbum audiret, & coena Domini uteretur, & ieiunaret. Vox enim λειτουργία, non significat sacrificium, sed publicum ministerium, quo sensu à Paulo usurpatur 2. Corinth. 9. Transtulerunt igitur etiam ad publicam coenae domini administrationem. Ignat: Epistola. 2. Λειτουργοῦντες ἀυτῷ λειτουργιαν καθαρὰν καὶ ἄμωμον. Item. Cano: 28. Apostol: Si quis Episcopus, vel Presbyter, vel Diaconus iucté depositus propter manifesta scelera, ausus fuerit ministerium attrectare antea sibi commendatum, hic prorsus excindatur ab Ecclesia. Non ergò propriè coenam domini significat λειτουργία, sed totam administrationem coenae domini: Nimirum publicum munus docendi, preces, gratiarum actionem & distributionem coenae.

Quintò, veteres & Ἀγάπην nominarunt, nimirum propter officia ditectionis: Quia ditiores dona conferebant, quibus pauperum inopiam subdevahant. Unde Tertullianus in Apologetico inquit. Coena nostra de nomine rationem suam ostendit.

Vocatur ἀγαπὴ id, quod dilectio penes graecos est: Quantiscunque sumptibus constet, lucrum est pietatis nomine facere sumptum: Siquidem inopes quoque isto refrigerio iuvamus. Haec ergò appellatio non tantum coenam domini complectitur, sed officia caritatis, quae simul in administratione coenae praestabantur.

Sextò Graeci saepè προσφοράν καὶ θυσίαν adpellant coenam domini, quòd Latini imitati, nominarunt oblationem & sacrificium. Causae autem sunt huius adpellationis: Prima, quòd divites offerebant panes, & vinum, & alia, quibus cibabantur & iuvabantur pauperes: Altera, quòd Deo offerebantur sacrificia Eucharistica, gratiarum actio, invocatio, praedicatio nominis divini, confessio, & officia fraternae dilectionis, loco sacrificiorum typicorum. Non igitur ipsa coena propriè, sed officia pietatis, quae in usu coenae praestahantur à piis sic vocabantur. Can: Apost: 8. Si quis Episcopus προσφορᾶς γενομένης non communicaverit, causam exponat. Sic & Ireneus dicit: lib: 4. Ca: 32. Christus calicem confessus suum esse sanguinem novi testamenti, novam docuit oblationem. Quia verò pontificii hanc appellationem ita depravant, ut fingant caenam domini esse ἱλαστικόν sacrificium, in quo Corpus & sanguis Iesu Christi Deo offerantur pro remissione peccatorum, sciri necesse est, non fuisse hanc patrum mentem, sed eos de Eucharistico sacrificio intellixisse, & locutos esse, non de offerendo corpore & sanguine Christi, sed de operious piorum, videlicet de invocatione, gratiarum actione, confessione & similibus officiis, quae Paulus λογικήν λατρέιαν Petrus θυσιαν πνευματικὴν appellant. Sic Ireneus clarè dicit. In censa Ioannes in Apocalypsi dicit esse orationes sanctorum.

Septimò: Aliqui scriptores κοινωνίαν, καὶ φρίκτα μυστήρια appellant, ut Basilius, in orat: De Baptismate. Item μυσταγωγίαν καὶ ἱερουργίαν ut Nazanzenus. Τελέτην θείαν συνάξεως Item, Τελέτην τελέτων ut Dionysius. τελέτην ἀπορρητον ut Synesius. Mysticam benedictionem ut Cyrillus. δόχην convivium, ut Dionysius. Sed hae appellationes ita generales sunt, ut etiam aliis ritibus & ceremoniis sacris convenire possint:

Octavò. Latini Missam appellarunt, de cuius vocabuli origine, cùm variae sint coniecturae potius quàm interpretationes, tum omnium simplicissima est, quòd nomen hoc natum sit ex dimissione populi peractis sacris: Siquidem minister dicere solitus est: Ite missa est: Quemadmodum & in graeca Ecclesia usitatum fuit dicere. Τοῖς λαοῖς ἄφεσις ἔστω Id est, quisque iam ad propria dimittitur.

Nulla adpellatio longiùs recedit ab adpellatione, qua Spiritus sanctus est usus, quàm vocabulum Missae. Ac quia pontificii idolatrae hac appellatione intelligunt blasphemam oblationem corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi pro vivis & mortuis, prodesset prorsus aboleri hanc profanam vocem in Ecclesia repurgata, quae cum idolatrico & blasphemo pontificiorum sacrificio missae nihil commune habet. Aut si quis hac voce omninò uti velit is simul ostendat se non loqui de idolatrico cultu missae Papisticae. Optandum etiam esset veteres ipsam coenam domini, nec oblationem, nec sacrificium adpellasse, ita errori de oblatione corporis Christi in coena ad placandam iram Dei non fuisset data occasio.

Caeterae adpellationes veteris Ecclesiae, licet sint generaliores, tamen pie usurpari possunt, praesertim si declarationes congruentes cum verbo Dei addantur, & consentientes confessioni piae antiquitatis. Omnium autem tutissimum erit retinere in Ecclesia adpellationem, quam Spiritus sanctus huic sacramento indidit.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper: Chapter II. Concerning the Author of the Most Holy Supper
CHAPTER II. Concerning the Author of the Most Holy Supper.

Although it is most well-known to all in the Church that not some Apostle or prophet, but the only-begotten and omnipotent son of God our lord Jesus Christ, who is the redeemer and sole guardian of his Church, and now sits at the right hand of the eternal father, is the author of this most holy supper: and that he commanded it to be used by all; nevertheless there are many and grave reasons why it is necessary that this member of doctrine be repeated from time to time and inculcated in everyone. For it is the safest and strongest foundation of the nature of faith, that the omnipotent and eternal God, whose wisdom is immense and who is truth itself, has delivered those things which seem incredible and impossible to reason. Nor can all the weapons and sophistries of fanatical men attacking in various ways the sound doctrine concerning the supper of the lord be more validly repressed and blunted, than if we oppose to them the divine authority of Jesus Christ, who instituted the holy supper. With horrible audacity and impudence indeed Satan confesses in his decrees, by which he has defiled and lacerated the supper of the lord, that Jesus Christ the son of God is the author of this supper, yet he nevertheless, and as he himself speaks, this notwithstanding, defines and establishes the contrary, and snatches away the other part, namely the use of the chalice, from the common people. But all men, in whom there is even a spark of sound judgment and of the fear of the Lord, are compelled to shudder when they hear that Satan in his Council of Constance dared to contradict such great authority. Nothing also is more effective for moving minds to the pious and frequent use of the most holy supper than the inculcation of such an author, who is the creator and preserver of all creatures in the world. Therefore, let that which Paul inculcates with the most grave weight of words always be in sight. I, he says, received from the Lord that which I also delivered to you. For Jesus Christ in that night in which he was betrayed took bread: etc. Therefore, what the Lord commanded and instituted, a good servant should not change. For it is repugnant to nature for a servant to change the law of his master. And the most grave voice of Cyprian deservedly has a place here. It is impious, erroneous, and sacrilegious, whatever is instituted by human fury, so that the divine disposition may be violated. Then, against all the deceptions of those who attempt to call into doubt the truth of the words of the supper, let us fortify ourselves in such a way that we may think it to be a horrendous crime to doubt the certainty of the words of the only-begotten Son of God, who is truth itself and God of immense wisdom.

Let a pious mind also seriously weigh the circumstances in the fear of God, namely that Jesus Christ in the last supper, when he was about to enter the most difficult struggle of all and to wrestle with the wrath of God and the whole kingdom of sin and his own blood for the world's life, bequeathed this treasure to us by testament, and demonstrated his immense love to us by the institution of this supper: And that he testified that the blessed bread and wine are his body and blood: And distributed them to the disciples to be eaten, and expressly commanded that the Church should use this supper of his until his glorious return from the heavens: All of which are expressed in the words of the institution of the supper.

Latin:

CAPUT II. De Authore Sacrosanctae Coenae.

Etsi omnibus in Ecclesia notissimùm sit non aliquem Apostolum vel prophetam, sed ipsum unigenitum & omnipotentem filium Dei dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, qui est redemptor & custos unicus suae Ecclesiae, ac nunc sedet ad dextram aeterni patris, esse authorem huius sacrosanctae coenae: eamque mandârit omnibus usurpandam; tamen multae & graves causae sunt, cur necesse sit, subinde repeti hoc membrum doctrinae & singulis inculcari. Tutissimùm enim & fortissimùm fidei naturae fundamentum est, quòd omnipotens & aeternus Deus, cuius immensa est sapientia & qui est ipsissima veritas, ea tradidit, quae rationi incredibilia & impossibilia videntur. Neque validius omnia tela & sophismata fanaticorum hominum impugnantium variis modis sanam doctrinam de coena domini, reprimi & retundi possunt, quam si authoritatem divinam Iesu Christi, qui sacram coenam instituit, eis opponamus. Horribili quidem audacia & impudentia Satan fatetur in suis decretis, quibus faedavit, & laceravit coenam domini, Iesum Christum filium Dei esse authorem huius coenae, se tamen nihilominus, & ut ipse loquitur, hoc tamen non obstante, definire & statuere contrarium, & alteram partem videlicet usum calicis plebi eripere. Verum omnes homines, in quibus velscint illa est sani iudicii, & timoris domini cohorrescere coguntur, cùm audiunt Satanam in suo conciliabulo Constantiensi ausum fuisse tantae authoritati contradicere. Nihil etiam efficacius est ad permovendos animos ad pium & crebrum usum sacrosanctae coenae, atque inculcatio tanti authoris, qui est conditor & conservator omnium creaturarum in mundo. Semper igitur in conspectu sit, quod gravissimo verborum pondere inculcat Paulus. Ego inquit à Domino accepi, quod et tradidi vobis. Nam Iesus Christus in ea nocte, in qua traditus est, accepit Panem: &c. Quòd ergò Dominus mandavit et instituit, bonus servus non mutet. Naturae enim repugnat servum mutare legem domini sui. Et gravissima Cypriani vox meritò hîc locum habet. Impium, erroneum, sacrilegum est, quidquid humano furore instituitur, ut divina violetur dispositio. Deinde adversus omnes praestigias eorum, qui veritatem verborum coenae in dubium vocare conantur, sic nos muniamus, ut cogitemus horrendum scelus esse, dubitare de certitudine verborum unigeniti filii Dei, qui est ipsissima veritas & immensae sapientiae Deus.

Circumstantias quoque pius animus seriò seriò in timore Dei expendat, quòd nimirum Iesus Christus in ultima caena, cùm agonem omnium difficilimum esset ingressurus & luctaturus cum ira Dei & toto regno peccati & sanguinem suum pro mundi vita effusurus hunc thesaurum testamento nobis legaverit, & immensum suum amorem huius coenae institutione nobis demonstraverit: Et quòd panem & vinum benedictum corpus & sanguinem suum esse testatus sit: Et discipulis vescendum distribuerit, ac disertè mandaverit, ut Ecclesia hanc suam coenam usurparet usque ad gloriosum ipsius reditum de coelis: Quae omnia in verbis institutionis coenae exprimuntur.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper: Chapter III. Definition of the Lord's Supper
CHAPTER III. Definition of the Lord's Supper.

The Lord's Supper is a sacred action instituted by the Son of God himself, our Lord Jesus Christ, in the New Testament on that night in which he was betrayed, in which under the blessed bread and wine he truly exhibits his true and substantial Body to be eaten, and his true blood to be drunk, to all of us who use this sacred supper according to his institution, as a testimony and pledge that he delivered his Body for us, and shed his blood for the remission of our sins, and that he wishes to dwell in us and sustain us for eternal life, and that he applies all the benefits of his kingdom to each of us and works salvation in us.

That the Lord's Supper is an action, Paul testifies when he says, As often as you do this, you shall announce the death of the Lord: it is most sacred, because it was instituted by the Son of God, and in it the most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ is distributed, and through it God works salvation in us, confirming faith and raising us up with consolation: That this action was instituted by the Son of God our Lord Jesus Christ, in the last supper, the Evangelists and Paul testify. In that night, says Paul, in which he was betrayed. That in this action under blessed bread and wine, the true and substantial body and true blood of Jesus Christ is given to those eating, is the principal question, which is now controverted in this member of doctrine in the Church. Therefore in its own place both a sound confession concerning this matter will be set forth and will be confirmed by solid arguments. Here it is enough to be taught by these words of Christ: Take, eat, this is my body, Item, drink from this all, this cup is the new testament in my blood: that the body and blood of Jesus Christ is distributed to those eating under bread and wine, therefore it is added, lest anyone should imagine transubstantiation, as if bread were changed or trans-elemented into the substance of the body of Christ, and consecrated wine into the substance of the blood of Christ, as the scholastics rave.

Paul after consecration names the bread:

As often as you shall eat this bread, you shall announce the death of the Lord. Therefore, there is no annihilation of the substance of the bread with only the accidents remaining: but the substance of the bread itself also remains: yet at the same time He exhibits to us in and with the bread His true body to be eaten, and in and with the wine His blood to be drunk. Nor do we mean anything else, when we say that the body of the Lord is distributed under the bread, than what Christ says, that the blessed bread is the body of Christ, and that all who eat the blessed bread become participants of the body of Jesus Christ. For Paul says that this blessed bread is the communion, that is, the participation of the body of Jesus Christ, since there is one bread, and we all participate of one bread.

That this sacred supper was instituted to this end, that it might be a testimony and a pledge that Christ delivered His body for us and shed His blood for the remission of our sins, is evident from the very words of Christ. This is the blood of the new Testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. Do this, as often as you shall do it, in remembrance of me. And just as Paul says of circumcision that it was given to Abraham as a seal of the righteousness of faith, and Peter calls Baptism ἐπορώτημα a stipulation of a good conscience before God: so it is rightly said of the Sacrament of the body and blood, that it is a pledge or a seal, by which is sealed the faith apprehending the remission of sins obtained for us by the passion and death of Jesus Christ. But that through this holy supper Christ applies to individual believers the benefits of his kingdom and works salvation in them, the words of the institution teach: Take, he says, Eat: By which voice he addresses individual persons approaching the table of the Lord, and commands individuals to apply to themselves this immense benefit, which by his death appeased the wrath of the eternal Father and merited for us righteousness and eternal life. That he also works salvation through the holy supper, nourishes and confirms faith, increases consolation, imparts life, gives the Holy Spirit, and makes us members of his body, is manifest from the saying of Paul. The Gospel is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth. The holy supper of the Lord is a great part of the Gospel, inasmuch as it shows the passion and death of Christ, and offers the promise concerning the gratuitous remission of sins. Thus the individual parts of the definition placed above rely upon the express word of God. And this our definition agrees entirely with the description of Luther in the Catechism, which holds as follows: The Sacrament of the altar is the true body and true blood of our Lord Jesus Christ under bread and wine, instituted by Christ himself for us Christians to eat and to drink. We have only added the end and effect in the definition.

Latin:

CAPUT III. Definitio Coenae Domini.

Coena domini est sacra actio ab ipso filio Dei domino nostro Iesu Christo, in novo testamento in ea nocte, in qua traditus est, instituta, in qua sub pane & vino benedictis verè exhibet verum & substantiale Corpus suum manducandum, & verum sangumem suum bibendum, nobis omnibus, qui iuxta ipsius institutionem hac sacra coena utimur, in testimonium & pignis, quòd Corpus suum pro nobis tradiderit, & sanguinem suum in remissionem nostrorum peccatorum effuderit, quodque in nobis habitare & ad vitam aeteram nos sustentare velit & ut omnia regni sui beneficia nobis singulis adplicet & salutem in nobis operetur.

Quòd coena domini sit actio, testatur Paulus tùm inquit, Quotiescunque hoc feceritis, mortem domini annunciabitis: sacratissima est, quia à filio Dei instituta est, & in ea distribuitur sanctissimum corpus, & sanguis domini nostri Iesu Christi, & per eam operatur Deus in nobis salutem confirmans fidem, & erigens nos consolatione: Actionem hanc institutam esse à filio Dei domino nostro Iesu Christo, in ultima coena, Evangelistae & Paulus testantur. In ea nocte, inquit Paulus, in qua traditus est. Quòd in hac actione sub pane & vino benedicto, verum & substantiale corpus & verus sanguis Iesu Christi detur vescentibus, precipua est quaestio, quae nunc in hoc doctrinae membro controvertitur in Ecclesia. Ideò suo loco & sana confessio hac de re exponetur & solidis argumentis confirmabitur. Hîc satis est doceri hoc verbis Christi: Accipite, edite, hoc est corpus meum, Item, bibite ex hoc omnes, hic calix est novum testamentum in meo sanguine: sub pane & vino distribui corpus & sanguinem Iesu Christi vescentibus, idcircò additur, ne quis fingat trans substantiationem, quasi panis in substantiam corporis Christi, et vinum consecratum in substantiam sanguinis Christi mutaretur, vel transelementaretur, ut scholastici delirant.

Paulus post consecrationem nominat panem:

Quotiescunque comederitis hunc panem, mortem domini annunciabitis. Non fit igitur annihilatio substantiae panis manentibus tantum accidentibus: sed ipsa quoque substantia panis manet: simul autem exhibet nobis in & cum pane verum suum corpus manducandum, & in & cum vino sanguinem suum bibendum. Nec aliud volumus, cùm dicimus sub pane distribui corpus domimini, quàm quòd Christus dicit panem benedictum esse corpus Christi, & omnes, qui manducant benedictum panem, participes fieri corporis Iesu Christi. Pauli enim hunc panem benedictum dicit esse communicationem, hoc est, participationem corporis Iesu Christi, siquidem unus sit panis, & de uno pane omnes participemus.

In hunc finem sacram hanc coenam institutam esse, ut sit testimonium & pignus, quòd Christus corpus suum pro nobis tradiderit & sanguinem suum in remissionem nostrorum peccatorum effuderit, ex ipsis verbis Christi patet. Hic est sanguis novi Testamenti, qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. Hoc facite, quotiescunque feceritis in mei commemorationem. Et sicuti Paulus dicit de circumcisione fuisse eam datam Abrahae in sigillum iustitiae fidei, & Petrus Baptismum adpellat ἐπορώτημα stipulationem bonae conscientiae coram Deo: ita rectè de Sacramento corporis & sanguinis dicitur, quòd sit pignus sive sigillum, quo obsignatur fides adprehendens remissionem peccatorum impetratam nobis passione & morte Iesu Christi. Quòd verò per hanc sacram coenam singulis credentibus adplicet Christus regni sui beneficia & salutem in eis operetur, docent verba institutionis: Accipite, inquit, Commedite: Qua voce singulas personas ad mensam domini accedentes alloquitur, & iubet singulos sibi adplicare hoc immensum beneficium, quod morte sua aeterni patris iram placavit & iustitiam & vitam aeternam nobis meruit. Quod etiam per satram coenam salutem operetur, alat & confirmet fidem, augeat consolationem, impertiat vitam, donet Spiritum sanctum, & faciat nos membra sui corporis, ex dicto Pauli manifestum est. Evangelion est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti. Sacra coena domini magna pars est Evangelii, siquidem ostendit passionem & mortem Christi, & offert promissionem de gratuita remissione pectatorum. Ita singulae partes definitionis supra positae nituntur ex presso Dei verbo. Ac prorsus congruit haec nostra definitio cum descriptione Lutheri in Catechismo, quae sic habet: Sacramentum altaris est verum corpus & verus sanguis domini nostri Iesu Christi sub pane & vino, nobis Christianis ad manducandum & bibendum, ab ipso Christo institutum. Nos tantum finem & effectum in definitione adiecimus.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper: Chapter IV. Concerning the True Presence of the Body and Blood of Jesus Christ in the Supp
CHAPTER IV. Concerning the True Presence of the Body and Blood of Jesus Christ In the Supper of the Lord.

Although the clarity of the words of Christ is so great that it is to be lamented that at any time there has ever been doubt in the Church concerning this matter: Whether the body of Jesus Christ is truly distributed in the holy supper: Yet since in this our age a most serious struggle has been stirred up in the Church, and the consciences of many are anxiously inquiring after the truth concerning this controversy, it is necessary for the Church to be instructed concerning this matter, and for the controversy to be explained clearly: And this, since it has been done hitherto by many with pious zeal and with great fruit, and our own little books concerning this part of doctrine are also publicly extant: Then it is necessary to repeat and inculcate the truth from time to time, so that the youth may be confirmed in it, and the deceits of the fanatics may be refuted. Thus, therefore, let the pious mind determine according to the clear words of Jesus Christ, that in the supper of the Lord, which is administered on earth according to the institution of the Son of God, the true and substantial body of Jesus Christ, which hung for us on the cross, is truly and substantially present, distributed, and eaten: And that the true and substantial blood of Jesus Christ, which flowed from his wounds and for the remission of our sins, is truly and substantially present, distributed, and taken by the mouth, and is poured out. For Christ explicitly says, Take, eat, this is my body, which is given for you; And this is my blood, which is poured out for you for the remission of sins. Although, therefore, we cannot comprehend with the sharpness of human intellect how bread is the body of Christ, and wine is the blood of Christ: nor can we understand how Christ gives his body to us to be eaten: yet since we know him to be truthful and omnipotent, we owe him this reverence and obedience, that we do not doubt that we in the holy Supper eat the true body of Christ according to his own word and drink his blood. Far be the calumny and sycophancy, which least of all befit those who are studious of the truth: And by which Satan acts to obscure the truth: we have shown our opinion plainly and clearly.

1. We do not invent transubstantiation, ἢμεταβολὴν τοῦ ἄρτου ἐις τὸ σῶμα χριστοῦ: That is, the change of bread into the body of Christ: So that only the accidents of bread, taste, color, size, and the like remain, with the substance abolished. We know and confess that this figment of the scholastics has no testimony in sacred scripture: but that it was devised by fanatical men without any foundation of sacred scripture. Christ does not say this bread I transmute into my body; but this is my body: And Paul says. The bread is the communion of the body of Christ: Therefore Christ distributes bread, and at the same time by this means exhibits to us his body to be eaten. And Paul very often names the Eucharist itself bread. Whoever shall eat this bread unworthily, is guilty of the body of Christ: Let a man prove himself and so let him eat of this bread. The substance of the bread therefore remains, which also retains its own properties. And at the same time with the bread, the body of Christ is given to us to be eaten by mouth, in a mysterious, heavenly, and to us inscrutable manner. For God can perform greater and more admirable things than we understand.

Some excuse the word μεταβολῆς, which is found among writers, as if it were not to be taken concerning papal transubstantiation, but concerning such a change, by which the common use of bread has been changed into a sacred use, so that it may be a Symbol of the body of Christ. But since the papists do not understand this word otherwise than concerning the annihilation of substance, transelementation, and transubstantiation, as they themselves speak, it is safer and better that the word μεταβολῆς be exploded from the Church in this doctrine. And thus I openly testify before God, that I utterly abhor the Papistic error concerning the transubstantiation of bread into the body, and of wine into the blood of Christ, and utterly reject and condemn the Tridentine canon 2. Session 3, concerning the Eucharist. On the contrary, however, I confess that in the Lord's Supper the substance of bread and wine remains. And I rely upon the testimonies of the Apostle Paul, which I cited above.

2. Nor do we imagine any consubstantiation, as if two substances were mixed together: for we confess that we are ignorant of the mode of the presence of the body of Christ: Bread is present in a physical mode: But the body of Jesus Christ in a mysterious and heavenly mode. Therefore, a consubstantiation of two most diverse things, earthly and heavenly, cannot exist. The power of God is infinite, circumscribed by no limits, which we cannot investigate with our senses. We do not doubt, therefore, that He can exhibit and truly does exhibit His body to us with and in the bread, since He said, take, eat, this is my body.

3. It is also a mere calumny that the enemies of the Lord's Supper, the Calvinists, object to our churches a local inclusion of the body in the bread, and what they themselves call impanation. Both Luther of holy memory and we who follow the doctrine of Luther have often testified that we by no means establish such a presence that locally includes the body of the Lord in the bread. For we ingenuously profess that we are ignorant of the mode of the presence, urging only this, that the words of Jesus Christ are most true, and that the consecrated bread is the very body of Jesus Christ. With pious antiquity we humbly say, it is His to know, it is ours to believe.

4. Thus also we have never imagined a personal union of the bread and the body of Christ: these are the virulent calumnies of fanatics, which have never entered our minds. We only confess and acknowledge that the human flesh of Christ is united λόγω hypostatically: And we know this to be the closest of all unions, by which God has joined Himself to a creature: The Son of God does not join Himself so closely even to blessed men or angels, so that He becomes one person with them: who therefore would be so delirious as to imagine that the bread and the body of Christ are united in the Lord's Supper by a personal union? When the theologians of our side warn that the phrase is unusual, just as many others are unusual, such as the Word was made flesh, God is man, the dove seen by John was the Holy Spirit, they do not mean by this that the nature of the union is the same: By no means: but just as those phrases placed above neither conform to the rules of the arts, nor are they figurative: But are theological phrases divinely revealed, just as the things themselves are divine, which exceed the grasp of human intellect: so also this phrase the bread of blessing is the body of Jesus Christ, is neither customary, nor figurative, but entirely new, theological, divinely revealed, as it speaks of a mystery entirely unknown to human reason. From this it can be gathered how impudent is the calumny of the Calvinists, who accuse our theologians, as if they might imagine that the bread and the body of Christ are united by a personal union.

5. It is of the same artifice that they object against our Churches ἀρτολατρίαν. For we do not teach that the bread of the Supper is to be invoked, but to be eaten, just as Christ instituted. We confess that Jesus Christ, God and man, is to be invoked both at the right hand of God and in the holy Supper, and in Baptism, and everywhere and always, but we do not invoke the blessed bread, for bread is not God, but is and remains a creature. It is a medium by which the Son of God exhibits and distributes to us his body to be eaten. If anyone objects that bread is the body of Christ: but the body of Christ is to be adored. Therefore, the blessed bread is also to be adored, to this we respond. Since there are different predications in the argument, regular and unusual, there is no connection of the propositions. Bread is not the body of Christ in such a way that it becomes the same thing as the body of the Lord, nor is it one person with the body of the Lord. But it is a communication, that is, a medium by which Christ imparts to us his body to be eaten. Therefore, it is not necessary that all the properties which are attributed to the body of Christ be immediately attributed to the bread: the body of Christ was crucified for us, but the bread was not: the body of Christ was born of the Virgin Mary, but the bread was not: the body of Christ sits at the right hand of the Father, but religion forbids affirming that of the bread: the body of Christ with the Word, to whom it is united, is to be adored. But the bread is not adored by the pious and those who understand the Holy Scripture. One must approach the Holy Supper with all reverence and modesty, in which the eternal Son of God himself is present and distributes his most holy body to us: but it is a sin to invoke a creature distinct from the person of the Son of God: The whole Trinity is present in the action of baptism: And yet no one except an idolater adores the water of baptism; Since all the pious in the Spirit adore the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit in Baptism.

6. We also reject the figment of the papists concerning the durable dwelling of the body of Christ in the bread outside the use instituted by Christ. For Christ gave his body to be eaten in the bread, and his blood to be drunk in the wine, he did not wish it to be adored, carried around, stored away, or enclosed. Therefore, when the blessed bread is not eaten according to the institution of the Son of God, it is not the body of the Lord. And it is a horrible idolatry when the papists carry around, or display, or store away the consecrated bread as if it were the body of Christ, and command it to be adored. For the rule, rightly understood, is true. Nothing has the nature of a Sacrament outside the use instituted by Christ.

7. We also testify that we abhor Capernaitic eating. For we do not feel that the flesh of Christ is to be torn into parts, or given as food in a bodily manner: But we confess the manner to be unknown to us, heavenly, secret, Spiritual, and known to Christ alone: we break the bread, we chew it, and we feed upon it as natural food: But the body of Jesus Christ truly present is heavenly food, sustaining our soul unto eternal life. Therefore, we eat this heavenly food in a heavenly manner unknown to us, without any breaking of the body of Christ: The body of Christ is not altered in this supper, but rather it alters us, so that we may be made members of the head, Christ. Since the Calvinists are not ignorant that we are entirely alien to the profane imaginations of the Capernaites, and yet they do not cease to ascribe such figments to our confession, there is no reason for them to doubt that they will one day render serious accounts to God for these slanders.

8. Nor do we assert such a ubiquity of the body of Christ as the Calvinists invent for the sake of their lust for lying: Namely, that the body of Christ is in every piece of wood, stone, blade of grass, and individual creature. What need is there for these foreign opinions in declaring the doctrine concerning the supper of the Lord? The question concerning the Supper of the Lord is what the blessed bread and blessed wine are, and whether the true and substantial body and true blood of our Lord Jesus Christ are truly present in this supper.

We utterly abhor the prodigious opinions concerning the infinite extension of the human nature of Christ, which the Calvinists imagine. But we do not doubt that the true body of Jesus Christ is truly present everywhere, wherever the Lord's Supper is administered: and here there is no need to invent an extension or a Calvinian ubiquity. Jesus Christ, by his omnipotence, above the laws of nature and above every grasp of human ingenuity, can bring it about that his true body is truly present in all places in which the Lord's Supper is administered, and wherever the pious are gathered. The body of Christ can be present both in the heavens at the right hand of God and on earth according to the express word of God. And thus in the sacred Supper of the Lord we profess, according to the words of Christ, that the blessed bread is the true body of Christ, and the blessed wine is the true blood of Christ: which body and which blood is perceived not only by faith, spiritually by the pious and those believing the word of God, but by all who approach the table of the Lord, as much by hypocrites and those lacking faith as by the pious and faithful, orally, corporally, or really: with this distinction, that the unworthy and hypocrites take to themselves the body of the Lord for judgment: but the pious, and those embracing the promise of the Gospel with true faith, for the confirmation of their salvation, the increase of life, and the sealing of their eternal inheritance: And of this pious and true confession of ours we hold these as the immovable foundations and infallible arguments.

I. ARGUMENT. From the Testimony and Declaration of Jesus Christ.

The controversy is concerning the meaning of these words, (This is my body) whether they are to be taken simply, as they sound, that the blessed bread is the true and substantial body of our Lord Jesus Christ: or indeed figuratively, that the bread is a symbol of the absent body of Christ. But who will be for us in the whole world a more certain and more trustworthy interpreter than the only-begotten Son of God our Lord Jesus Christ: who is the eternal truth, and in whom all the treasures of wisdom are hidden? In whom dwells the fullness of the divinity? Who is the author of the most holy supper? Who understood his own words best of all, and is the teacher and governor, and redeemer and guardian of the whole Church? To this great majesty not only men, but also angels are compelled to yield, and all the pious most readily yield.

Let us hear therefore how Jesus Christ settles the controversy: For he did not set forth these words of his nakedly without any interpretation. Take, this is my body: But that he might forestall the corruptions of the Calvinists and of all fanatical men and lies, he soon added the declaration: This is my body (he says) which is given for you. If the Son of God himself were now dwelling on earth among men, and it were now permitted to us to question him face to face, as it was once permitted to the Apostles, what more would he answer us than that the blessed bread is his body, which he gave for us? And with this declaration obtained, what more would a man endowed with sound judgment, and a mind fearing the Lord, desire? All who are rightly instructed in the Catechism understand that the body was given for us, namely not a symbol of the body, not a figure, not the mystical body, namely the Church. But the true and substantial body of Jesus Christ, which was born of the Virgin Mary, and which hung on the cross for our sins. No one can deny this unless he is an enemy of the entire religion. What doubt, therefore, still remains concerning the meaning of the words of Christ? Christ says of the blessed bread, this is my body, and he adds what kind of body this is, namely the true one, which is given for us. Why, therefore, do the Calvinists, the sworn enemies of the Lord's Supper, not apply faith to the omnipotent God? The interpretation and figment of Calvin and other fanatical men concerning a figurative locution fights diametrically against the declaration of the Son of God, the author of the most holy Supper. For if, according to Oecolampadius or Calvin, you say, Bread is a symbol of the body: can the declaration of Christ be attached by any reasoning? Is the bread a sign or symbol of the body of Christ, which symbol was delivered into death for us? Who without great sacrilege can say that only a sign or symbol and not the true body of Jesus Christ was delivered into death for our sins? If the word (Body) in the words of the supper only signifies a symbol, or a sign of an absent body, shall we therefore believe that only a symbol or sign was delivered for us? Do you see, reader, that the Calvinists ferociously contradict the clearest and most open truth of Jesus Christ? Thus also the Son of God added a clear declaration to the word (blood). This is my blood, not figurative or allegorical, But which is shed for you for the remission of sins. No one is so unlearned in the Church that he does not know that no other blood was shed for our sins than the true and substantial one, which flowed from the wounds of Jesus Christ. Since therefore Christ testifies concerning the blessed wine, that it is that blood which was shed for us, is it not of horrible audacity so to deprave and twist the words of the Son of God, that the word blood in the words of the Lord's supper signifies only a symbol or sign of an absent blood?

Even if an angel from heaven were to affirm in the supper of the Lord that the true body and true blood are not distributed to us, but only a symbol or sign of an absent body, it would be ours not to have faith in it, but to acquiesce constantly to the most open declaration of Jesus Christ, the only-begotten and omnipotent Son of God, who is more certain to us than all the angels in heaven.

The Calvinists assert nothing solid against this most valid argument. For the fact that they say, if the bread is the body of Christ: therefore the bread was crucified for us. And if the relative prayer is to be referred to the body, then also to the bread: And thus it will follow, that the bread was delivered for us: is a futile evasion. For it is not necessary on account of this sacramental union to attribute to the bread all things which are attributed to the body of Christ. For they are not one either by nature, or by person, or by perpetual connection: but only by sacrament, that is, so that the bread may be the medium by which the body of Jesus Christ is given to us in the Holy Supper. What the bread was by its own nature, the Apostles saw. But because Christ reveals the mystery that the bread is his body, he adds a declaration, lest they themselves imagine a metaphor or an allegory, that it is that body which he delivers for us into death. Another evasion then is, that the Calvinists say those words, which is delivered for you, speak only of the fruit of the passion, and not of the substance of the Lord's Supper, but a pious mind easily understands how impudent this cavil is.

For, in the first place, these words treat of the very substance of the Lord's Supper. For it is a relative clause, which refers to the preceding word 'body,' and explains that this bread is the body, namely that body which is delivered for us. Then also those words speak of the fruit of the passion of Christ, that namely Jesus Christ delivered his body into death for our sins, by his death appeased the wrath of God, and merited for us righteousness and life. They also admonish that the very eating of the body of Christ in the Supper of the Lord ought to nourish and confirm our faith, by which we determine that God is appeased toward us. And doctrine otherwise, and consolation most ample and inexhaustible, is contained in the very few words, 'which is delivered for you.' But to deny that, besides the doctrine concerning the fruit, they also speak of the substance of the Lord's Supper and most clearly demonstrate that the true and substantial body of Jesus Christ is given to us in the sacred Supper, is of manifest impiety. Therefore, with both hands, nay with the whole heart, let pious minds hold fast and defend this most clear declaration of the Son of God, which is clearer than the midday sun, and let them not suffer it to be obscured, or removed, or twisted elsewhere by the Calvinists. But let them simply urge both the authority of the Son of God sublime, and the clarity of the words of the supper. If the Calvinists object that this opinion is full of absurdity, we respond that it is not a wonder if mysteries revealed by God seem absurd to reason. The doctrine of Christ concerning the regeneration of man seemed most absurd to Nicodemus: and yet it was most true. The omnipotent Son of God understands divine mysteries more correctly than blind human reason. Let us therefore learn the truth from Him; and let us know that He is able to speak correctly and harmoniously, nor let anyone dare to correct the tongue of the omnipotent God.

We embrace the sum of this argument in a few words thus.

The interpretation of Jesus Christ the Son of God is the most certain of all.

But Jesus Christ interprets the words of the supper (this is my body) in such a way that (Body) signifies not a symbol, but the essential body of Christ, namely, that which was delivered into death for us.

Therefore in the words of the supper the term (body) does not signify a symbol, but the true and essential body of Christ, which was delivered into death for us.

Item.

The body which was delivered into death for us is the true and essential body of Christ.

Christ, declaring the words of the supper (this is my body), testifies that the bread is that body which was delivered for us.
