Therefore, according to the most certain interpretation of the Son of God, the blessed bread is the true and substantial body of Jesus Christ.

Item.

No other blood was shed for the remission of our sins than the true and substantial blood of Jesus Christ.

Jesus Christ, declaring the words of the supper, testifies that the blessed wine is that blood which was shed for the remission of our sins.

Therefore, the blessed wine in the sacred supper is the true and substantial blood of Jesus Christ.

II. ARGUMENT. From the property of the New Testament.

The words of Christ must be most diligently weighed by us, because he calls the blessed wine in the sacred supper the blood of the New Testament, and the New Testament in his blood.

For nothing is more certain than that he wished to place a distinction between the blood of the Old Testament and the New Testament. For as the epistle to the Hebrews Chapter 9. from Chapter 24 of Exodus he proves, there was also the blood of the old testament, namely, the blood of the Burnt Offering, with which the people were sprinkled, Moses saying: Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord has made with you.

From this blood of the old testament, he wished to distinguish this blood, which he distributes to us in the holy supper. Therefore Matthew and Mark say that Christ used this form. This is my blood of the new Testament. Luke and Paul report that Christ said. This cup is the new Testament in my blood. The individual words show the mind of Christ. For when he says, this is my blood, he shows that he is not speaking of the blood of Burnt Offerings, or of the old testament, which was only a figure and Type of the blood of Christ, but of his own proper and substantial blood, which he was about to pour out for the life of the world. But for the sake of greater certainty and declaration he added. This is my blood of the new testament, so that without any doubt it might be established that he himself was speaking of his natural and substantial blood. For to all who hold the first rudiments of true religion, it is most well known that the blood of the new testament is none other than the true and essential blood of our lord Jesus Christ, by which salvation was obtained for the world. For upon this blood God made a new covenant with us, and

He made a new testament, because he wishes to remit sins to us freely and to grant eternal life. This new testament is also confirmed by this blood. Whence scripture attributes all the benefits of the new testament to this precious blood. 1. John 1. The blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin. Coloss: 1. Through which son we have redemption through his blood, namely the remission of sins. Heb: 9. How much more shall the blood of Jesus Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself blameless to God, purify your consciences from dead works, to serve the living God. And for this reason he is the mediator of the new testament. Item, Christ entered not by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood once into the holy places, having obtained eternal redemption. Heb: 13. May the God of peace, who brought us back from the dead to the great shepherd of the sheep, in the blood of the eternal testament our Lord Jesus, make you fit and ready for every good work. It is expressly said here that the blood of the new and eternal testament is none other than the true blood of Jesus Christ, which flowed from the wounds and side of Jesus Christ, and satisfied God for our sins. Since therefore Christ the son of God testifies that the blessed wine, which he distributes in the holy supper, is his blood of the new testament: who can any longer doubt that the wine is the true, natural, and substantial blood of Jesus Christ blessed. A pious mind rightly shudders, hearing the petulance and rashness of the human intellect, which dares to call into doubt such clear words of Christ.

First, Christ says: This is my blood: this ought to have been enough for us, so that we might understand it only as the true and substantial blood of Jesus Christ.

Secondly, he adds: This is my blood of the new testament: here he removes every doubt, and shows that his words cannot be understood otherwise than of his own blood, by which he redeemed the human race.

Thirdly, he adds an even clearer declaration: This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for you for the remission of sins. Here, indeed, Christ set forth his words with such clarity that, without the gravest sin, a doubt cannot be admitted into the mind as to whether Christ truly offers us his true and substantial blood in the sacred supper. To this now is added what, with Luke and Paul reporting, Christ said: This cup is the new testament in my blood. For this form of words also demonstrates the presence of the true blood of Christ in the sacred supper. For if the true blood of Christ were not distributed in the sacred supper, the cup of blessing, it could by no means be called the new testament. For a type or symbol, or sign is not the new testament, but all figures pertain to the old testament. Since therefore Christ names the cup of blessing the new testament, and adds the cause of this naming (in my blood) as if he were to say, I therefore call the cup of blessing the new testament, because it contains my blood, by which the new testament is established, it is necessary that not only wine, as a sign of absent blood, but also true and substantial blood be distributed in the cup.

That the Calvinists cavil here that the blood of the new testament and the new testament itself are not one and the same: I indeed confess that they can be distinguished. For the new testament is the very promise of God, by which he binds himself to us to remit sins. But the blood of the new testament is the natural Blood itself, which flowed from the wounds of Jesus Christ. In this place, however, because Christ adds, the new testament in my Blood, the sense is entirely the same.

For because the blood of Christ merits for us the remission of sins, at the same time it embraces the new testament itself, that is, the remission of sins, whence also Christ soon adds, which is shed for you for the remission of sins. Here you hear both the promise of the Gospel and the blood of Christ. Thus, when the cup is called the new testament in the blood of Christ: The very promise of the Gospel concerning the gratuitous remission of sins is shown to us in the holy supper, just as the promise is expressly set forth, and at the same time the very blood of Jesus Christ is offered to us. That Beza and Zwingli cavil here that the blood of Christ confirms the new Testament only insofar as it was shed, is both putrid and impious. Not only at that moment, in which the blood of Christ was shed, was it the blood of the new Testament, but from then on, from the revelation of the first promise, even unto eternity. The blood of Christ is the blood of the new Testament: for this merit of the shedding of blood, and of the death of Christ, perpetually endures and is valid. Many centuries before the incarnation of the son of God, the Prophet Zechariah names the blood of Christ the blood of the new covenant or new Testament: You, he says, in the blood of the covenant will lead forth your prisoners from the pit, in which there is no water. To pour out mists upon this argument, the Calvinists sweat greatly, to demonstrate that the old as well as the new Testament is one in substance, because both were struck in Christ, and offer the remission of sins and eternal goods. So that in whatever way they may obtain their figments, they do not fear to contradict the manifest holy scripture. Not only the ancient Ecclesiastical writers, And in the first place, Augustine teaches that there are two diverse testaments, which differ from one another in their whole substance, but also the Holy Spirit, whose doctrine it is a sin to call into doubt, expressly affirms that there are two, and those diverse, testaments. Jeremiah in a long discourse teaches that the new testament differs entirely and in its whole species from the old. Not according to the covenant which I made with your fathers, will I make a covenant with you, but I will strike a new covenant with you: And the author of the Epistle to the Hebrews teaches at length that the new Testament is founded upon better promises. And the Apostle Paul most clearly says. These are two Testaments, Galat: 4. To contradict this so manifest truth and so sublime authority is a matter of great impiety and detestable petulance. And so our argument remains unmoved, namely, that in the cup of blessing the true and substantial blood of Jesus Christ the Son of God is distributed, since Christ calls the blessed wine his blood of the new Testament. Let the studious and pious reader also attend to how accurately the Holy Spirit has blocked all cracks for sophistry and for inventing tropes, for if anyone strives to place a figure or Metaphor or Metonymy in the word (blood), the phrase new Testament does not permit it. For the symbol or sign of the blood of Christ is not is the new testament. Again, if anyone should attempt to place a figure in the word testament, the word Blood does not permit this. For it cannot be said, the cup is a figure of the new testament in the blood of Christ. For who without insult to Christ would affirm that the blood of Christ is a figure of the new testament. Therefore, the Holy Spirit has most firmly fortified the sound opinion concerning the presence of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ in the holy supper, so that it cannot be overturned by any sophistry. We gather the summary of this our argumentation briefly thus.

There is no other blood of the new testament than the true, natural, and essential blood of Jesus Christ:

But Christ confesses the blessed wine to be his blood of the new testament.

Therefore, by the testimony of the most weighty Son of God, the blessed wine in the Lord's supper is the true and substantial blood of our Lord Jesus Christ.

III. ARGUMENT. From the Testimony of the Apostle Paul.

These arguments are most firm and most plain; which we have taken from the very words of Jesus Christ, by which he instituted the most holy supper. But not less firm and plain is that which the testimony and declaration of the Apostle Paul provides for us. 1 Corinthians 10, when he says: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? And the bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? First, as regards the word κοινωνίας, that is, of communion. Although the Zwinglians fought for a long time that it signifies only a common right, or society: yet at length, convinced by the perspicuity and truth of the matter, Calvin and his followers are forced to admit that the word (communion) in this passage of Paul signifies participation. For Paul himself explicitly explains himself: For we all, he says, participate of one bread, Μετέχομεν.. Therefore, to Paul, κοινωνεῖν, that is, to communicate, and Μετέχειν, that is, to participate, are one and the same. But this is still disputed, whether Paul is speaking of a spiritual communion or participation, which happens through faith, or indeed of a sacramental one, that is, a bodily one, which happens by the mouth of the body. And in what sense he said that the blessed bread is a participation of the body of Christ. Now if anyone attends to the whole series of Paul's discourse, he will easily discover that Paul is not speaking of a spiritual communion of the body of Christ, which happens by faith alone in Christ: but of a sacramental, that is, a bodily one, by which the worthy and the unworthy communicate in the body and blood of Jesus Christ.

For the scope of the Pauline argumentation shows this. Paul wishes to deter the Corinthians from idolatry and the communion of Gentile sacrifices: And he does this by an argument taken from the communication of the body of Christ in the holy supper.

No one, he says, can simultaneously with fruit participate in the body and blood of Christ, and communicate at the table of Idols: But Christians in the Eucharist communicate in the body and blood of Christ: Therefore Christians ought to abstain from things sacrificed to idols and flee all sacrifices of the Gentiles and all Idolatry. Either the sacrifices of Idols must be fled by you, Or you must abstain entirely from the table of the Lord and the participation of the body of Christ: Lest besides other most grave sins you make yourselves guilty of the body and blood of Christ: Since therefore Paul attempts to deter the secure and impenitent from the participation of the body of Christ, it is certain that he is not speaking of spiritual and salutary communication. For this can harm no one. And those who used this in faith did not need that severe castigation of Paul. For in those in whom true faith shone, they undoubtedly fled Idols. Therefore he speaks of the corporal or Sacramental perception of the body of Christ, by which he wishes Christians to be admonished that they should abstain from things sacrificed to idols, lest they become guilty of the body of Christ.

Then when he says the bread is the communication of the body of Christ, he teaches quite openly that he is speaking about sacramental or corporal participation: for if he had wished for spiritual communication to be understood, he would rather have named faith or the Spirit. For by faith we eat the flesh of Christ spiritually, and the Spirit makes us members of the body of Christ. But Paul names neither faith nor the Spirit, but says that the blessed bread is the communication of the body of Christ: of which blessed bread not only the pious and faithful, but also many unworthy persons and hypocrites partake. It is manifest, therefore, that he is speaking of the corporal participation of the body of Christ, which is common to the worthy and the unworthy and occurs by the taking of the bread. For if not all who eat of that bread were to become partakers of the body of Christ, but only those performing penance and endowed with saving faith, certainly the bread could not be called the communication of the body of Christ. For many who would take the bread, such as hypocrites, would not become partakers of the body of Christ. This reasoning is evident. Not only those performing penance, but also hypocrites and the unworthy eat the blessed bread in the Supper: But hypocrites and the unworthy do not communicate in the body of Christ spiritually. Therefore the bread is not a spiritual communication of the body of Christ, but a sacramental one, that is, a corporal one, in which the true body of Christ is present and is received by the mouth. From the proof also, which Paul brings forward The mind of the Apostle shines forth, for thus he shows that the bread is the communion of the body of Christ. Because there is one bread, and we being many are one body in the Church, and we all partake of one bread. If from the fact that we all partake of one blessed bread, it follows according to the Apostle's argument that the blessed bread is the communion of the body of Christ, it is necessary that all, as many as use the supper of the Lord, become partakers of the body of Christ: But if all, as many as approach the table of the Lord, become partakers of the body of Christ, therefore it is necessary that Paul does not understand a spiritual communion. For the unworthy, the unfaithful, and hypocrites are clearly devoid of that; But a Sacramental or corporal one. That the blessed bread is the true and substantial body of Jesus Christ, which all who use the sacred supper of the Lord eat with the mouth of the body. The example also, which he takes from the Jewish sacrifices, shows the same opinion. For those who were partakers of the altar, and at the same time ate of the same sacrifice, were not all equally faithful; But they had this in common, that they all became partakers of the same sacrifice, so also these who approach the table of the Lord have this in common, that they eat the body and drink the blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, although they are not all endowed with faith, nor do they have spiritual communion with Christ. We have therefore demonstrated quite evidently that Paul, when he says, The bread is the communication of the body of Christ, to speak of this Sacramental, that is, corporal communication or participation of the body of Christ, and clearly to mean the same thing as Christ. This is my body, that is to say, the Bread is the true and substantial body of Christ, and as many as eat of this bread, these communicate in the body of Jesus Christ. In the same sense he also says the cup is the communication of the blood of Jesus Christ: That is, that it is the very true blood of Jesus Christ which is communicated to all who drink from this cup. The words of Paul are most plain: The bread is the communication of the body of Christ, thus the Calvinists twist it, The bread is that by which fellowship is made with the body of Christ: And then they interpret the fellowship as spiritual, by which we are members of the body of Christ. But who does not see that this violent exposition of the words of Paul does not stand? For the bread is not that by which we are made members of the body of Christ: For many participate in the bread who do not become members of Christ, nor are they vivified by His Spirit. And scripture teaches that through faith we are inserted into the body of Christ, and through the Holy Spirit. How therefore is the bread that by which a spiritual fellowship is made with the body of Christ? Nor does Paul speak of the mystical or allegorical body of Christ, that is, of the Church, but of His substantial body. And why does the term of fellowship please more than that of participation and communication, which is much clearer? Therefore, rather through the words of Christ, from which Paul took his phrase Let us interpret Paul. The bread is the communication of the body of Christ, that is, the bread is the true and substantial body of Jesus Christ, which is communicated to all who eat in the sacred supper. Others invent a figure in the word ( κοινωνιάς ) of communication, as if the mind of Paul were: The bread is a sign or symbol of the communication of the body of Christ. Here we do not undeservedly first wonder at and even detest the levity and petulance of the Calvinists, who establish their tropes sometimes in the word of the body, sometimes in the word of the Testament, sometimes in the word κοινωνιάς . And thus they have no certain place on which to fix their foot. Such slipperiness is a certain indication of an uncertain and fluctuating conscience. Furthermore, what kind of opinion is that, the bread is a symbol of the communication of the body of Christ? Bread can in some way represent the body, and wine the blood, through a Metaphor, but bread is not a sign or symbol of the spiritual eating or participation of the body of Christ. If Paul had wished to say this, which the Calvinists invent, he ought to have named not the bread, but the external eating of the bread. The pious therefore notice that the expositions of the Calvinists are twisted and violent, inasmuch as they attribute foreign and monstrous opinions to Paul. Regarding what the Calvinists object to the words of Paul:

You cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of demons: you cannot be made partakers of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons; and from this they attempt to infer that the unworthy are not made partakers of the body of Christ, and from there they also gather further that Paul is speaking of a spiritual communication, this is easily refuted. For Paul does not deny that the unworthy, hypocrites, and the secure, who while wishing to be Christians, polluted themselves with idolatry, are made partakers of the body of Christ: for he expressly testifies to that in Chapter 11, where he affirms that they become guilty of the body and blood of Christ by the very eating, because they do not discern, nor judge the body of the Lord. But he teaches and warns that no one can communicate at the table of demons, and at the same time with fruit and salvation be made a partaker of the body and blood of Christ: Therefore he wishes them to abstain either from things sacrificed to idols, and every communion of idols, or from the table of the Lord, lest they provoke the most grave wrath of God upon themselves by a most foul crime, namely, the contempt of the body. Whence he adds: Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? are we stronger than he? by which rebuke he reproves the rashness of those who, having spurned the admonitions of the Apostles, boldly approached the supper of the Lord, and nevertheless were present at the sacrifices of idols and demons. If there had been no danger, and no injury had been done to the body of Christ by those secure ones and idolaters, not with such severity would he have repelled them from the use of the Lord's supper, who were still contaminating themselves with idols. It is certain, therefore, that Paul asserts that the blessed bread in the sacred supper is the true and essential body of Jesus Christ: It is certain that Paul speaks of a corporal communication, when he says that the bread of blessing is the communication of the body of Christ. It is certain that Paul testifies that all, as many as eat of this bread, become participants of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, whether they be worthy, that is, faithful and endowed with the Spirit of God: Or whether they be unworthy, hypocrites, secure, and devoid of faith. We embrace Paul's argumentation thus in a few words:

That which is a participation or communication of the body of Christ, with it the body of Christ must necessarily be truly exhibited.

But the bread of blessing is the communication of the body of Christ.

Therefore, with the blessed bread, the body of Jesus Christ is truly exhibited.

Item.

That which is a participation of the body of Jesus Christ, that is the true and essential body of Christ:

But the blessed bread is a participation of the body of Christ:

Therefore the blessed bread is the true and essential body of Christ.

Item.

All who eat that which is a participation of the body of Christ, it is necessary for them to become participants of the body of Christ.

But many hypocrites and unworthy persons eat the blessed bread, which, with Paul as witness, is the communion of the body of Christ.

Therefore many hypocrites become participants of the body of Christ.

Item.

No thing can be called a participation of the body of Christ, unless that which, taken and used according to the command of Christ, makes us participants of the body itself.

The blessed bread, with Paul as witness, is a participation of the body of Christ.

Therefore the blessed bread, taken according to the institution of Christ, makes us who eat at the supper participants of His body.

IV. ARGUMENT. From the Eating of the Unworthy.

But if we were to eat the flesh of Christ only spiritually through faith, as the Calvinists contend, and in the sacred supper were only to perceive the power and efficacy of the absent body of Christ, and if the blessed bread were only a symbol of the body of Christ, carried up into heaven and placed far from us, it would be entirely necessary to establish that the unworthy, the secure, the hypocrites, and those lacking saving faith are by no means made participants of the body and blood of the Lord. For the unworthy and those alien to faith do not at all perceive the power and efficacy of the body of Christ: They are not freed from sin, they are not vivified by the Spirit of Christ, but they remain in death and stick under the wrath of God, excluded from all communication of the benefits of Christ: He who does not believe in the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him, but Paul clearly teaches that not only the faithful, but also the unworthy and the secure are made participants of the body of Christ in the sacred supper of the Lord. For with a severe sentence the Apostle Paul affirms that those who eat of this bread unworthily become guilty of the body of Christ. He calls those who do not prove themselves to eat unworthily of this bread, that is, those who without repentance, without true contrition and faith, rashly and boldly run to the table of the Lord: These he says become guilty of the body and blood of Christ. But this most grave guilt is not contracted unless an injury is inflicted upon the body and blood of Christ: Now if the body and blood of Christ are absent, and the unworthy eat and drink only bread and wine, how do they become guilty of the body and blood of Jesus Christ? It is frivolous, what the Calvinists they say. He who treats the image or the command of an emperor with contumely is held to be contumelious toward the emperor himself. Thus, he who abuses the symbol of the body of Christ is said to be contumelious toward Christ himself. For the Apostle does not only say this, that he who eats unworthily has in a certain way done injury to Christ himself, but that he has become guilty of the body and blood of Christ. Now, he is prosecuted as guilty of some thing who has treated that very thing with contumely or wickedly. And indeed, Paul testifies that this guilt is contracted by the unworthy by the very act of eating: he says, he eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord. He who by eating the bread unworthily and by drinking the blessed wine unworthily becomes guilty of the body of Christ, and eats and drinks judgment to himself, it is necessary that he, by eating and drinking, does injury and contumely not only to the bread and wine, but to the body and blood of Christ himself. Which the Apostle indicates with a most clear voice, not discerning the body of the Lord, as if he were to say, because he does not distinguish the body and blood of Christ in the sacred supper from common food and drink, he holds the blessed bread and wine as if they were not the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, he becomes guilty of the body and blood of the Lord, and provokes against himself the judgment and wrath of God. Why would Paul burden the conscience of those who approach the table of the Lord unworthily with such an atrocious sentence, if there were not truly present body and blood of Jesus Christ in the Lord's Supper? How can the body of Christ in the Lord's Supper be discerned from other foods, by which we sustain our bodily life, since it is not present, but is very far away from the earth, in the most remote heaven? The Apostle does not say that a sacred thing is to be discerned from a profane one, he does not say that a symbol or sign of the body is to be discerned from common bread: But that the body of the Lord is to be discerned from other food. It is manifest therefore that the unworthy also eat the body of Jesus Christ in the sacred supper, although to their judgment.

But with this demonstrated, that the unworthy eat the body of the Lord, and drink his blood in the sacred supper: just as we have proven from the testimonies of Paul: it is most evidently gathered, that in the Lord's supper the flesh of Christ is not only eaten spiritually through faith: But also corporally, that the body of the Lord is taken with the mouth of the body along with the bread, and that the blessed bread is the true and substantial body of the Lord. For the unworthy and hypocrites do not eat the flesh of Christ spiritually through faith: for they are utterly destitute of faith and are devoid of the Spirit of Christ: Nor do they perceive the power and efficacy of the body of Christ, but rather they eat judgment to themselves, excluded from all the benefits of the kingdom of Christ: And yet they eat the body of Christ, and drink his blood unworthily, as Paul testifies, it is necessary therefore, that not only is the efficacy of the body of Christ distributed spiritually in the sacred supper, but also that the true and substantial body of Christ is present in the sacred supper, and is given with the blessed bread to all who use the sacred supper.

The firmness and evidence of this argument is so great that it can be shaken by no sophistry, and obscured by no cavils. Several times the Calvinists have made an incursion into this argument, but immediately repressed by the splendor of the truth, they have recoiled. First, they seek escapes in the word unworthily. They contend that Paul is not speaking of hypocrites and those lacking saving faith: But of the weak and those approaching the supper of the Lord negligently: Who are not entirely alien from all faith, but yet do not sufficiently prove themselves, and do not approach with sufficient reverence to receive the body of the Lord. These, they say, become guilty of the body of the Lord, and eat judgment to themselves. Here now let the pious and God-fearing mind consider what Satan seeks through such a violent depravation of the words of Paul. If Paul calls those unworthy who are endowed with weak or meager faith, and who approach the table of the Lord less reverently, will not a most pernicious scruple be injected into the minds of all the pious? Will they not make mere poison for the soul out of the most wholesome medicine?

Who of us, however great the light and strength of faith with which he is endowed, is there who does not feel his own weakness in the struggle?

Who among us dares to boast that he approaches the receiving of the body of Jesus Christ with sufficient reverence? Who among us does not lament both his own weakness and unworthiness? Now if the weak eat unworthily of that bread: therefore it will have to be established for all of us, as often as we approach the table of the Lord, that we become guilty of the body and blood of Jesus Christ: I shudder with my whole heart, as often as I think of that virulent cavil. Therefore we all eat judgment to ourselves, even we, who seriously perform penance, grieve that God has been offended by our sins, and also truly believe in the Son of God the mediator and embrace the Gospel: for we must confess that there is a huge weakness of faith in us: And according to Calvin's interpretation, the weak eat unworthily of the blessed bread: This is, forsooth, to console the consciences of the weak. Does the fault seem light to you, to become guilty of the body and blood of Jesus Christ? Would it not be better to abstain altogether from the use of the Eucharist, than to bind the conscience with the most grave guilt, even if you are not altogether lacking in faith? And who will ever make us certain that we use the supper of the Lord with fruit and for salvation? Since we cannot know whether we are endowed with sufficiently firm faith, and whether we approach the table of the Lord worthily? Since we must always confess that our faith is more languid than it ought to be, and that we are surrounded by manifold weakness. Where, therefore, this cavil of Calvin concerning the unworthy tends, is not obscure to the sensible reader. For he takes away entirely every fruit which we ought to have perceived from the use of the Eucharist, namely, that our languid faith might be confirmed and nourished, and he renders the most necessary consolation uncertain to us. Let us therefore detest with our whole heart this pernicious depravation of the words of Paul. Paul calls the unworthy the impenitent, the secure, who do not examine themselves, nor embrace the promise of grace with sincere faith, but remain in sins against conscience, and nevertheless approach the table of the Lord through hypocrisy. For Paul opposes to one another those who eat of this bread unworthily, and those who examine themselves. For he says, If anyone eats of this bread unworthily, he becomes guilty of the body of Jesus Christ. But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of this bread. Him who has examined himself, namely with true repentance, who grieves from the heart that he has offended God by his sins, and seriously assents to the Gospel, the Apostle does not say becomes guilty of the body of Christ, but with confidence he commands him to approach the table of the Lord, whether he be endowed with small or great faith. Therefore he understands by the unworthy the hypocrites and the secure, who are devoid of the motions of repentance, and yet approach the table of the Lord.

He has fabricated a new distinction of the unworthy Eberus [introduces a distinction] previously unknown to the Church. Namely, that some are unworthy hypocrites, unbelievers, secure, impenitent, who eat the body of Christ in the holy supper unto judgment: but others are unworthy, being ἀθεούς, merely profane, Ecebolites, utterly impious, Epicureans, who either are ignorant of the whole of religion, or utterly despise it: these he says do not receive the body of the Lord, even if the words of Christ sound toward them, Take, eat, this is my body, because they are not members of the Church. This distinction is both new, and dangerous, and contrary to the words of Paul. For Paul expressly pronounces concerning all who eat unworthily, that they become guilty of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, and that they eat judgment to themselves, in that they do not discern the body of the Lord. Now, by the testimony of Eberus himself, the Apostle would not have brought such an atrocious sentence concerning those who eat unworthily, unless he had thought that the unworthy eat the body itself, and drink the blood of Jesus Christ. Therefore, since it cannot be said of atheists, Ecebolites, and clearly impious Epicureans using the Eucharist, that they do not become guilty of the body and blood of Christ, and that they do not eat and drink judgment to themselves, it is necessary to confess that atheists, Ecebolites, and clearly Epicureans eat the body and drink the blood of Christ, just as hypocrites, the secure, and unfaithful Christians do.

Or it will have to be demonstrated that those who sin less, namely by security and impenitence, become guilty of the body of Christ while they use the Eucharist: But those who sin more gravely and are altogether atheists, mockers of religion and manifest enemies of God, do not become guilty of the body and blood of Christ, nor do they eat and drink judgment to themselves, even if they approach the sacred supper among other Christians. And since according to the Apostle Paul the unworthy eat and drink judgment to themselves for this very reason, that they do not discern the Lord's body, I would like to know how atheists, apostates, the merely profane, and contemners of all piety discern the Lord's body more than the secure, the impenitent, and hypocrites? And upon what foundation of Scripture, finally, does this distinction of the unworthy rest? Certainly the Holy Spirit pronounces all to be enemies of God, liable to divine wrath, and subject to death and the tyranny of Satan, as many as do not seriously perform penance, nor believe the Gospel. He who does not believe in the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him, John 3.

He who does not have the Spirit of Christ, this one is not His, Rom. 8. Whether he be a hypocrite, or secure, or an idolater, or an atheist, or an apostate, and merely profane. Some sins are indeed graver than others.

But all who are alien to the true motions of repentance are sinners of one kind, namely, bound by mortal sins, removed from the benefit of the kingdom of Christ. We therefore reject and explode that new and false distinction of the unworthy, and we say with Paul: all who approach the table of the Lord without true repentance eat the body and drink the blood of Christ without salutary fruit unto judgment.

Calvin very insolently feigned that the body of the Lord is indeed offered in the holy supper to hypocrites, the secure, and the unworthy, but is repelled and rejected by the impious by that very security and diffidence. This is truly to contradict the Apostle Paul to his face. For he expressly says, He who eats and drinks unworthily, eats and drinks judgment to himself, in that he does not discern the body of the Lord. If the impious man summons judgment to himself by the very eating, and by the very eating does not discern the body of the Lord. Therefore he does not repel it by his diffidence, but receives the body of the Lord with his mouth. For sacraments do not depend on the dignity or indignity of those receiving, but on the truth of the words of Jesus Christ. In the word (judgment) the Calvinists also seek the cracks of sophisms, through which they may slip away. For they interpret it concerning corporal punishments and temporal chastisement, not concerning the wrath of God and eternal condemnation. But this escape is also sought in vain. For from the whole discourse of Paul it is manifest that he threatens the wrath of God, present and eternal punishments, to those who receive unworthily. Those who approach the table of the Lord without examination are secure and impenitent. But the impenitent deserve not only temporal chastisements, but also judgment and eternal death. And those who are proven guilty by the Spirit of God of the body and Blood of Jesus Christ, these certainly have no part in the kingdom of Christ, but are liable to eternal damnation. For to those to whom the consolation of Paul pertains: There is no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus: Roma: 8. Likewise, of Christ: He who believes in the Son is not judged, are by no means to be terrified by this sad thunderbolt, that they become guilty of the body and Blood of Christ. Therefore, what Paul says, that those who receive the Eucharist unworthily eat and drink judgment to themselves, is to be understood not only of temporal chastisement, but of the most grave wrath of God, and eternal damnation, unless the secure person, hypocrite, and atheist has returned to God with true repentance, and has obtained forgiveness of sins by faith. Therefore, our argument taken from the eating of the impious is firm, namely, because Paul testifies that the unworthy, that is, the secure, hypocrites, atheists, apostates, and clearly impious, when they approach the table of the Lord, eat the body of the Lord, and drink his blood, it is most evident that in the sacred supper the true body and true Blood of Jesus Christ are truly present; and

that the blessed bread is the true and substantial body, and the blessed wine is the true and substantial Blood of Jesus Christ, which the worthy and the unworthy alike receive with their mouth, the former unto salvation, the latter unto judgment. We shall comprise our argumentation in syllogisms.

He who in the holy supper becomes guilty of the body and Blood of Jesus Christ, it is necessary for him, in the supper itself, to inflict injury upon the present body and Blood of Jesus Christ.

But those who unworthily take the blessed bread and wine become guilty of the body and Blood of Jesus Christ.

Therefore, those who unworthily take the blessed bread and wine, in the holy supper, inflict insult and injury upon the present body and Blood of Jesus Christ.

Another.

He who in the holy supper of the Lord eats and drinks judgment to himself, in that he does not discern the body of the Lord, truly eats the body of the Lord.

But he who unworthily eats the blessed bread, eats judgment to himself, in that he does not discern the body of the Lord.

Therefore, he who unworthily eats the blessed bread, truly eats the body of the Lord.

Another.

That which in the sacred supper must be distinguished from common food by the very eating and use, that must necessarily be present.

But the body of Jesus Christ in the sacred supper must be distinguished from common food by the very eating.

Therefore, it is necessary that the body of Jesus Christ be truly present in the sacred supper.

Another.

He who does not distinguish the body of Jesus Christ from other foods by the very eating, he undoubtedly eats the body of the Lord as other food.

But hypocrites and the secure do not distinguish the body of the Lord by the very eating of the Eucharist.

Therefore, hypocrites and the secure eat the body of the Lord as other food.

Another.

Blessed bread is therefore called the participation of the body of the Lord, because all, as many as eat that bread, become participants of the body of the Lord.

But many hypocrites, atheists, Epicureans, turncoats, clearly impious and profane persons eat the blessed bread in the sacred supper.

Therefore many hypocritical atheists, the secure, the impenitent, Epicureans, Ecebolians, and the plainly impious, become partakers of the body and blood of Christ.

These are the foundations of our opinion and confession concerning the presence of the body and blood of Jesus Christ in the sacred supper, which we have not taken from the arguments or speculations of human reason, nor have we sought them from far-fetched or violently twisted testimonies of scripture, nor do they lean upon the authority of learned and famous men in the Church: but they have been brought here from the very seat of the doctrine concerning the supper of the Lord. We have urged only the most plain words of Jesus Christ, the most clear interpretation of Christ, and the most lucid testimonies of Paul. And from the very text of the Holy Spirit, in which He instructs the Church concerning the supper of the Lord, we have demonstrated that this is the most true mind of the Holy Spirit, that the body and blood of Jesus Christ are truly and substantially present in the sacred supper: and that the blessed bread is the true and substantial body of Jesus Christ, and the blessed wine is the true and substantial blood of Jesus Christ, which body and which blood of Christ the worthy eat and drink unto salvation and the confirmation of faith: but the unworthy eat and drink unto judgment. Therefore we beseech the Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, our mediator and redeemer, and the author of the most holy supper with all our heart, that He may increase faith in us through the Holy Spirit, and mercifully confirm us in this certain, clear, and solid confession of the truth, Amen.

Latin:

CAPUT IIII. De Vera Praesentia Corporis & Sanguinis Iesu Christi In Coena Domini.

Etsi tanta est verborum Christi perspicuitas, ut dolendum sit, ullo unquam tempore hac de re in Ecclesia dubitatum esse: Num verè corpus Iesu Christi in sacra coena distribueretur: Tamen cùm hoc nostro seculo certamen gravissimum motum sit in Ecclesia, & multorum conscientiae de hac controversia anxiè inquirant veritatem, necesse est Ecclesiam hac de re erudiri, & controversiam perspicuè explicari: Idque cùm à multis hactenus pio studio & magno cum fructu factum sit, & nostri etiam libelli de hac parte doctrinae publicè extent: Tum subinde repetere & inculcare veritatem oportet, ut iuventus in ea confirmetur, & prestigiae fanaticorum refellantur. Sic ergò pia mens statuat iuxta perspicua Iesu Christi verba, quòd in coena domini, quae in terris iuxta filii Dei institutionem administratur, verè & substantialiter adsit, distribuatur & manducetur verum & substantiale corpus Iesu Christi, quod in cruce pro nobis pependit: Et quòd verè & substantialiter adsit, distribuatur & ore sumatur verus & substantialis sanguis Iesu Christi, qui ex vulneribus ipsius effluxit & in remissionem nostrorum peccatorum est effusus. Nam Christus disertè dicit Accipite, Commedite, hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis traditur; Et hic est sanguis meus, qui pro vobis in remissionem peccatorum effunditur. Etsi igitur acie humani ingenii comprehendere non possumus, quomodo panis sit corpus Christi, & vinum sit sanguis Christi: nec intelligere possumus, quomodo Christus corpus suum nobis det manducandum: tamen cùm sciamus eum veracem & omnipotentem esse, hanc reverentiam & obedientiam ei debemus, ut non dubitemus nos in sacra Coena verum Christi corpus iuxta ipsius verbum manducare & ipsius bibere sanguinem. Absit procul calumnia et Sycophantia, quae studiosos veritatis minimè decent: Et quibus Satan hoc agit ut obscuret veritatem: sententiam nostram planè & perspicuè ostendimus.

1. Non fingimus transsubstantiationem, ἢμεταβολὴν τοῦ ἄρτου ἐις τὸ σῶμα χριστοῦ: Id est, mutationem panis in corpus Christi: Ita ut tantum accidentia panis, sapor, color, magnitudo & similia remaneant, abolita substantia. Scimus & fatemur, hoc figmentum scholasticorum nullum habere testimonium in sacra scriptura: sed à fanaticis hominibus sine omni fundamento sacrae scripturae excogitatum esse. Non dicit Christus hunc panem in corpus meum transmuto; sed hoc est corpus meum: Et Paulus dicit. Panis est communicatio corporis Christi: Ergò panem distribuit Christus, et simul hoc medio exhibet nobis corpus suum manducandum. Et Paulus saepissimè ipsam Eucharistiam nominat panem. Qui ederit panem hunc indignè, reus est corporis Christi: Probet homo seipsum & sic de hoc pane edat. Manet igitur substantia panis, quae suas etiam proprietates retinet. Et simul cum pane datur nobis corpus Christi ore manducandum, arcano, coelesti & nobis inscrutabili modo. Deus enim maiora & admirabiliora praestare potest, quàm nos intelligimus.

Excusant aliqui vocem μεταβολῆς, quae apud scriptores reperitur, quasi ea non sit accipienda de pontificia transsubstantiatione, sed de eiusmodi mutatione, qua communis usus panis mutatus sit in sacrum usum, ut sit Symbolum corporis Christi. Verùm cùm pontificii hanc vocem non aliter intelligant, quàm de annihilatione substantiae, transelementatione et transsubstantiatione, ut ipsi loquuntur, tutius & melius est vocem μεταβολῆς in hac doctrina explodi ex Ecclesia. Atque ita palàm coram Deo testor, me prorsus abhorrere à Papistico errore de transsubstantiatione panis in corpus, & vini in sanguinem Christi, & prorsus reiicere & damnare canonem Tridentinum 2. Sess: 3. de Eucharistia. Contrà verò fateor in sacra coena domini manere substantiam panis & vini. Ac nitor testimoniis Apostoli Pauli, quae supra citavi

2. Neque nos imaginamur ullam consubstantiationem, quasi duae substantiae inter se mixtae essent: fatemur enim nos ignorare modum praesentiae corporis Christi: Panis physico modo adest: Sed corpus Iesu Christi arcano & coelesti modo. Ergò consubstantiatio duarum diversissimarum rerum, terrenae, & coelestis esse non potest. Infinita est Dei potentia nullis circum scripta limitibus, quam nostris sensibus pervestigare non possumus. Non ergò dubitamus, quin cum et in pane possit nobis exhibere & verè exhibeat suum corpus cùm ille dixerit accipite, edite, hoc est corpus meum.

3. Mera etiam calumnia est, quòd coenae domini hostes Calvinistae obiiciunt nostris Ecclesiis localem inclusionem corporis in pane, & ut ipsi vocant impanationem. Et Lutherus sanctae memoriae & nos Lutheri doctrinam sequentes, saepe testati sumus nequaquam nos talem statuere praesentiam, quae corpus domini localiter includat in panem. Modum enim praesentiae nos ignorare ingenuè profitemur, hoc solum urgentes, verissima esse Iesu Christi verba, et panem consecratum esse ipsissimum Iesu Christi corpus. Cum pia antiquitate humiliter dicimus ipsius est nosce, nostrum est credere.

4. Sic etiam nunquam finximus unionem personalem panis & corporis Christi: fanaticorum hae sunt virulentae calumniae, quae nobis nunquam in mentem venerunt. Tantum humanam Christi carnem cum λόγω hypostaticos unitam esse fatemur & agnoscimus: Et scimus hanc esse omnium arctissimam unionem, qua Deus se creaturae coniunxit: Ne beatis quidem hominibus vel angelis tàm arctè se coniungit filius Dei, ut una cum ipsis fiat persona: quis igitur adeò deliret, ut imaginaretur panem & corpus Christi uniri in coena domini personali unione? Cùm nostrae partis Theologi admonent phrasin esse inusitatam, sicuti et aliae plures sunt ininusiatae, ut verbum caro factum est, Deus est homo, columba visa à Iohanne fuit Spiritus sanctus, non hoc volunt, quòd eadem sit ratio unionis: Nequaquam: sed sicuti phrases ille supra positae, neque ad regulas congruunt artium, nec sunt figuratae: Sed sunt phrases theologicae divinitus patefactae, sicuti & res sunt divinae, quae captum humani ingenii excedunt: sic & haec phrasis panis benedictionis est corpus Iesu Christi, nec usitata, nec figurata est, sed prorsus nova, theologica, divinitus patefacta, utpote de mysterio loquens prorsus ignoto humanae rationi. Hinc colligi potest, quàm sit impudens Calvinistarum calumnia, qui nostros Theologos insimulant, quasi fingerent personali unione uniri panem & corpus Christa.

5. Eiusdem artis est, quòd obiiciunt nostris Ecclesiis ἀρτολατρίαν. Nos enim non docemus panem coenae esse invocandum, sed manducandum, sicuti Christus instituit. Iesum Christum Deum & hominem, & in dextera Dei & in sacra coena, & in Baptismo & ubique & semper invocandum esse fatemur, sed panem benedictum non invocamus, panis enim non est Deus, Sed est & manet creatura. Medium est, quo filius Dei exhibet & distribuit nobis suum corpus manducandum. Si quis obiiciat panem esse corpus Christi: Sed corpus Christi esse adorandum. Ergò & panem benedictum esse adorandum, huic respondemus. Cùm diversae sint praedicationes in argumento, regularis & inusitata, nulla est connexio propositionum. Panis non ita est corpus Christi, ut fit idem, quod corpus domini, nec sit una persona cum corpore domini. Sed est communicatio, hoc est, medium, quo Christus impertit nobis manducandum suum corpus. Non igitur necesse est mox tribui pani omnes proprietates, quae tribuuntur corpori Christi: Corpus Christi pro nobis est crucifixum, sed panis non: Corpus Christi natum est ex Maria virgine, Sed panis non: corpus Christi sedet ad dexteram patris, Sed id de pane adfirmare, religio vetat: corpus Christi cum Logo, cui unitum est adorandum est. Sed panis non adoratur à piis & sacram scripturam intelligentibus. Cum omni reverentia et modestia accedendum est ad sacram coenam, in qua ipse aeternus filius Dei est praesens & suum corpus sanctissimum nobis distribuit: sed creaturam distinctam à persona filii Dei invocare nefas est: Tota trinitas in actione baptismi est praesens: Et tamen aquam baptismi nemo nisi idolatra adorat; Cùm omnes pii in Spiritu adorent patrem & filium, & Spiritum sanctum in Baptismo.

6. Reiicimus etiam figmentum pontificiorum de durabili mansione corporis Christi in pane extra usum à Christo institutum. Christus enim dedit corpus suum manducandum in pane, et sanguinem suum in vino bibendum, non voluit adorari, circumferri, reponi, includi. Quando ergò panis benedictus non manducatur iuxta filii Dei institutionem, non est corpus domini. Et horribilis Idolatria est, quando pontificii panem consecratum circumferunt, vel ostentant vel reponunt tanquam corpus Christi, & iubent adorari. Vera enim est regula rectè intellecta. Nihil habet rationem Sacramenti extra usum à Christo institutum.

7. A Capernaitica quoque manducatione nos abhorrere testamur. Non enim sentimus carnem Christi in partes scindi, aut modo corporali dari in cibum: Sed fatemur modum nobis esse incognitum, coelestem, arcanum, Spiritualem & soli Christo notum: panem conterimus dentimus et vescimur eo ut cibo naturali: Sed corpus Iesu Christi verè praesens coelestis est esca, animam nostram sustentans in vitam aeternam. Hanc ergò escam coelestem coelesti et nobis incognito modo manducamus, sine omni comminutione corporis Christi: Non corpus Christi in hac coena alteratur, sed nos potius alterat, ut efficiamur membra capitis Christi. Cùm non ignorent Calvinistae nos prorsus alienos esse à prophanis Capernaitarum, imaginationibus & tamen non cessent eiusmodi figmenta nostrae adscribere confessioni, non est quòd dubitent se aliquando de istis calumniis graves rationes Deo reddituros esse.

8. Neque nos eiusmodi adserimus ubiquitatem corporis Christi, qualem Calvinistae pro sua mentiendi libidine comminiscuntur: Quòd nimirum corpus Christi sit in omni ligno, lapide, gramine, & singulis creaturis. Quid opus est his peregrinis opinionibus in declaranda doctrina de coena domini? De coena Domini est quaestio, quid sit panis benedictus, & vinum benedictum, & num verè adsit in hac coena verum & substantiale corpus, et verus sanguis domini nostri Iesu Christi.

A prodigiosis opinionibus de infinita extensione humanae naturae Christi, quam imaginantur Calvinistae, prorsus abhorremus. At non dubitamus, Verum corpus Iesu Christi passim verè esse praesens, ubicunque coena domini administratur: ac hîc nihil opus est fingere extensionem aut Calvinianam ubiquitatem. Iesus Christus pro sua omnipotentia supra naturae leges, & supra omnem captum humani ingenii efficere potest, ut verum suum corpus in omnibus locis, in quibus coena Domini administratur, & ubicunque pii congregati sunt, verè sit praesens. Corpus Christi & in coelis ad dexteram Dei & in terris praesens esse potest iuxta expressum Dei verbum. Atque ita in sacra Caena domini profitemur iuxta verba Christi, panem benedictum esse verum corpus Christi, & vinum benedictum esse verum sanguinem Christi: quod corpus & qui sanguis non tantum fide, spiritualiter à piis & verbo Dei credentibus, sed ab omnibus, qui ad mensam domini accedunt, tàm ab hypocritis & fide carentibus, quàm à piis & fidelibus ore corporaliter seu realiter percipitur: hoc discrimine, quòd indigni & hypocritae sumant sibi ad iudicium corpus domini: Pii verò & promissionem Evangelii vera fide amplectentes, ad salutis suae confirmationem vitae augmentum, & obsignationem haereditatis aeternae: Atque huius piae & verae confessionis nostrae haec immota habemus fundamenta, & infallibilia argumenta.

I. ARGUMENTUM. A Testimonio & Declaratione Iesu Christ.

Controversia est de sensu horum verborum, (Hoc est corpus meum) an simpliciter accipienda sint, ut sonant, quòd panis benedictus sit verumet substantiale corpus domini nostri Iesu Christi: an verò figuratè, quòd panis sit symbolum absentis corporis Christi. Quis verò erit nobis in toto orbe terrarum certior & magis fide dignus interpres, quam Unigenitus filius Dei dominus noster Iesus Christus: qui est aeterna veritas, & in quo omnes thesauri sapientiae reconditi sunt? in quo habitat plenitudo divinitatis? qui est author sacrosanctae coena? qui sua verba omnium optimè intellexit, & totius Ecclesiae & doctor & gubernator, & redemptor & custos est? Huic tantae maiestati non solùm homines, sed & angeli cedere coguntur, & omnes pii promptissimè cedunt.

Audiamus ergò quomodo Iesus Christus dirimat controversiam: Non enim nudè sine omni interpretatione posuit haec sua verba. Accipite, hoc est corpus meum: Sed ut anteverteret Calvinistarum & omnium fanaticorum hominum corruptelas & mendacia, adiecit mox declarationem: Hoc est corpus meum (inquit) quod pro vobis traditur. Si iam ipse filius Dei in terris versaretur inter homines, Et nobis nunc liceret ipsum coràm interrogare, ut olim licuit Apostolis, quid amplius responderet nobis quam panem benedictum esse suum corpus, quod pro nobis tradiderit? & hac impetrata declaratione, quid sano iudicio praeditus homo, & mens timens dominum amplius desideraret? Omnes rectè instituti in Catechesi intelligunt, quod corpus pro nobis sit traditum, videlicet non symbolum corporis, non figura, non mysticum corpus videlicet Ecclesia. Sed verum & substantiale corpus Iesu Christi, quod natum est ex maria virgine, & quod in cruce pependit pro nostris peccatis. Hoc nemo nisi universae religionis hostis inficiari potest. Quae ergò dubitatio adhuc de sensu verborum Christi relinquitur? Christus inquit de pane benedicto, hoc est corpus meum, et addit quale sit hoc corpus, videlicet verum, quod pro nobis traditum est. Cur ergò Calvinistae hostes coenae domini iurati non adhibent fidem omnipotenti Deo? Calvini & aliorum fanaticorum hominum interpretatio et figmentum de figurata locutione ex diametro pugnat cum declaratione filii Dei authoris sacrosanctae coenae. Si enim iuxta Oecolampadium vel Calvinum dicas, Panis est symbolum corporis: an ulla ratione attexi potest Christi declaratio? panis est signum vel symbolum corporis Christi, quod symbolum pro nobis in mortem est traditum? Quis sine grandi sacrilegio dicere potest tantùm signum vel symbolum & non verum corpus Iesu Christi pro nostris peccatis in mortem esse traditum? Si vocabulum (Corpus) in verbis coenae tantum significat symbolum, vel signum absentis corporis, ergò ne symbolum vel signum tantum pro nobis traditum esse credemus? Vides lector, quòd Calvinistae clarissimae et apertissimae veritati Iesu Christi ferociter contradicant? Sic & vocabulo (sanguinis) perspicuam addidit filius Dei declarationem. Hoc est sanguis meus, non figuratus aut allegoricus, Sed qui pro vobis in remissionem peccatorum effunditur. Nemo tàm rudis est in Ecclesia, quin sciat non alium sanguinem pro nostris peccatis effusum esse, quàm verum & substantialem, qui effluxit è vulneribus Iesu Christi. Cùm ergò Christus de vino benedicto testetur, quòd sit ille sanguis, qui pro nobis effusus est, an non horribilis audaciae est ita de pravare & contorquere filii Dei verba, quod vocabulum sanguinis in verbis coenae Domini tantum symbolum vel signum absentis sanguinis significet?

Etiamsi angelus de coelo adfirmaret in coenae domini non verum corpus, nec verum sanguinem nobis distribui, sed tantum symbolum seu signum absentis corporis, nostrum esset, ei non habere fidem, sed constanter acquiescere apertissimae declarationi Iesu Christi unigeniti & omnipotentis filii Dei, qui omnibus angelis in coelo nobis est certior.

Nihil solidi adserunt Calvinistae contra hoc validissimum argumentum. Nam quòd dicunt, si panis est corpus Christi: ergò panis pro nobis est crucifixus. Et si oratio relativa ad corpus est referenda, tum etiam ad panem: Et sic sequetur, panem esse pro nobis traditum: futile effugium est. Non enim necesse est propter hanc sacramentalem unionem, omnia tribuere pani, quae corpori Christi tribuuntur. Non enim unum sunt vel natura, vel persona, vel per petua connexione: sed tantum sacramento, hoc est, ut panis sit medium, quo detur nobis corpus Iesu Christi in Sacra coena. Quid panis sua natura esset, videbant Apostoli. Sed quia Christus mysterium revelat panem esse corpus suum, addit declarationem, ne ipsi metaphoram velallegoriam imaginarentur, esse illud corpus, quod pro nobis tradat in mortem. Aliud deinde effugium est, quòd Calvinistae dicunt verba illa, quod pro vobis traditur tantum de fructu passionis loqui, & non de substantia coenae Domini, sed quàm impudens sit haec cavillatio pius animus facilè intelligit.

Primùm enim de ipsa substantia coenae domini agunt ista verba. Relativa enim oratio est, quae refertur ad praecedentem vocem corpus, et exponit quod corpus sit iste panis, nimirum illud corpus, quod pro nobis est traditum. Deinde etiam verba illa de fructu passionis Christi loquuntur, quòd nimirum Iesus Christus pro nostris peccatis corpus suum in mortem tradiderit, morte sua iram Dei placaverit, & iustitiam ac vitam nobis meruerit. Monent etiam quod ipsa manducatio corporis Christi in coena Domini fidem nostram, qua statuimus Deum nobis placatum esse, alere & confirmare debeat. Et doctrina aliâs & consolatio amplissima & inexhausta, continetur in verbis paucissimis, quod pro vobis traditur: At negare quod praeter doctrinam de fructu non etiam de substantia coenae domini loquantur & clarissimè demonstrant, quod verum & sabstantiale corpus Iesu Christi in sacra coena nobis detur, manifestae impietatis est. Utraque igitur manu, imò toto pectore retineant & tueantur pii animi hanc clarissimam filii Dei declarationem, quae sole meridiano clarior est, neque patiantur eam à Calvinistis vel obscurari, vel semoveri, vel aliò torqueri. Sed simpliciter urgeant & authoritatem filii Dei sublimen, & verborum coenae perspicuitatem. Si obiiciant Calvinistae plenam absurditatis esse hanc sententiam, respondemus non esse mirum, si mysteria divinitus patefacta videantur rationi absurda. Doctrina Christi de regeneratione hominis, Nicodemo videbatur absurdissima: et tamen verissimaerat. Omnipotens filius Dei divina mysteria rectius intelligit, quàm caeca ratio humana. Ab illo igitur discamus veritatem; et sciamus eum rectè, & concinnè loqui posse, nec audeat quisquam omnipotentis Dei linguam corrigere.

Summam huius argumenti sic paucis complectimur.

Omnium certissima est interpretatio Iesu Christi Filii Dei.

Sed Iesus Christus sic interpretatur verba coenae (hoc est corpus meum) quod (Corpus) significet non symbolum, sed essentiale corpus Christi, nimirum, quod pro nobis in mortem est traditum.

Ergò in verbis coenae vocabulum (corpus) non symbolum significat, sed verum & essentiale corpus Christi, quod pro nobis in mortem est traditum.

Item.

Corpus quod pro nobis in mortem est traditum, est verum & essentiale corpus Christi.

Christus declarans veroa coenae (hoc est corpus meum) testatur panem id corpus esse, quod pro nobis est traditum.

Ergo iuxta certissimam filii Dei interpretationem panis benedictus est verum & substantiale corpus Iesu Christi.

Item.

Non alius sanguis effusus est in remissionem nostrorum peccatorum, quàm verus & substantialis sanguis Iesu Christi.

Iesus Christus declarans verba coenae, testatur vinum benedictum esse eum sanguinem, qui in remissionem nostrorum peccatorum est effusus.

Ergò vinum benedictum in sacra coena est verus & substantialis sanguis Iesu Christi.

II. ARGUMENTUM. A proprietate Novi Testamenti.

Diligentissimè nobis expendenda sunt verba Christi, quòd vinum benedictum in sacra coenae adpellat sanguinem novi Testamenti, & novum Testamentum in suo sanguine.

Nihil enim certius est, quàm quòd discrimen ponere voluerit inter sanguinem veteris testamenti & novi testamenti. Nam ut epistola ad hebraeos Cap: 9. ex 24. Cap: Exodi: probat, fuit & sanguis veteris testamenti, nimirum, sanguis Holocausti, quo populus adspergebatur, dicente Mose: En sanguis faederis, quod pepigit dominus vobiscum.

Ab hoc sanguine veteris testamenti, hunc sanguinem, quem nobis distribuit in sacra coena distinguere voluit. Ideò Mathaeus & Marcus dicunt hac forma Christum usum esse. Hic est meus sanguis novi Testamenti. Lucas & Paulus referunt Christum dixisse. Hic calix est novum Testamentum in meo sanguine. Singulae voces ostendunt mentem Christi. Nam cùm dicit, hic est meus sanguis, ostendit se non loqui de sanguine Holocaustorum, vel veteris testamenti, qui tantùm erat figura et Typus sanguinis Christi, sed de suo proprio & substantiali sanguine, quem effusurus erat pro mundi vita. Verùm maioris certitudinis & declarationis gratia addidit. Hic est meus sanguis novi testamenti, ut sine omni dubitatione constaret ipsum loqui de suo naturali & substantiali sanguine. Omnibus enim, qui prima rudimenta verae religionis tenent, notissimum est sanguinem novi testamenti, nullum esse altum, quam verum & essentialem sanguinem domini nostri Iesu Christi, quo parta est salus mundo. Super hoc enim sanguine pepigit nobiscum Deus novum foedus, &

novum fecit testamentum, quòd gratis velit nobis remittere peccata & vitam donare aeternam. Hoc etiam sanguine confirmatum est novum testamentum. Unde scriptura omnia beneficia novi testamenti huic praecioso sanguini tribuit. 1. Ioan: 1. Sanguis Ie su Christi mundat nos ab omni peccato. Coloss: 1. per quem filium habemus redemptionem per ipsius sanguinem, nimirum remissionem peccatorum. Heb: 9. Quantò magis sanguis Iesu Christi, qui per Spiritum aeternum obtulit seipsum irreprehensibilem Deo, purificabit conscientias vestras, à mortuis operibus, ut serviatis Deo viventi. Ac propterea novi testamenti mediator est. Item, Christus non per sanguinem hircorum & vitulorum, sed per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel in sancta aeterna redemptione inventa. Heb: 13. Deus pacis, qui reducit nos ex mortuis ad pastorem ovium magnum, in sanguine testamenti aeterni dominum nostrum Iesum, faciat vos idoneos & promptos ad omne opus bonum. Disertè hîc dicitur novi & aeterni testamenti sanguinem non esse alium, quam verum sanguinem Iesu Christi, qui ex vulneribus & latere Iesu Christi effluxit, & pro nostris peccatis Deo satisfecit. Cùm ergò Christus filius Dei testetur vinum benedictum, quod in sacra coena distribuit, esse suum sanguinem novi testamenti: quis amplius dubitare potest, vinum benedictum esse verum, naturalem & substantialem sanguinem Iesu Christi. Pius animus meritò cohorrescit, audiens petulantiam & temeritatem humani ingenii, quod audet tàm perspicua Christi verba in dubium vocare.

Primùm Christus inquit. Hic est meus sanguis: hoc nobis satis esse debuisset, ut tantum de vero & substantiali sanguine Iesu Christi intelligeremus.

Secundò addit, Hic est sanguis meus novi testamenti: hîc omnem aufert dubitationem, et ostendit non posse aliter intelligi sua verba, quam de suo sanguine, quo genus humanum redemit.

Tertiò adhuc clariorem addit declarationem. Hic est sanguis meus novi testamenti, qui pro vobis in remissionem peccatorum effunditur. Hîc sanè tanta perspicuitate verba sua exposuit Christus, ut sine gravissimo peccato non possit in animum admitti dubitatio, an Christus in sacra coenà verè exhibeat nobis verum & substantialem suum sanguinem. Huc iam accedit, quod Luca & Paulo referentibus Christus dixit. Hic calix est novum testamentum in meo sanguine. Nam & haec forma verborum demonstrat praesentiam veri sanguinis Christi in sacra coena. Si enim verus Christi sanguis non distribueretur in sacra coena calix benedictionis, nulla ratione dici posset novum testamentum. Typus enim vel symbolum, vel signum non est novum testamentum, sed figurae omnes ad vetus testamentum pertinent. Cùm ergò Christus calicem benedictionis nominet novum testamentum, & causam huius adpellationis addat (in meo sanguine) quasi dicat, ideò adpello calicem benedictionis novum testamentum, quod contineat meum sanguinem, quo stabilitur novum testamentum, necesse est non solum vinum, tanquam absentis sanguinis signum, sed etiam verum & substantialem sanguinem in calice distribui.

Quòd cavillantur hîc Calvinistae non esse unum & idem sanguinem novi testamenti & ipsum novum testamentum: fateor quidem distingui posse. Nam novum testamentum est ipsa promissio Dei, qua se nobis obstringit ad remittendum peccata. Sanguis verò novi testamenti est ipse naturalis Sanguis, qui è vulneribus Iesu Christi effluxit. Hoc autem loco, quia Christus addit, novum testamentum in meo Sanguine, prorsus idem est sensus.

Quia enim sanguis Christi meretur nobis remissionem peccatorum, simulipsum novum testamentum, id est, remissionem peccatorum complectitur, unde & Christus mox subiicit, qui pro vobis in remissionem peccatorum effunditur. Hîe & promissionem Evangelii & sanguinem Christi audis. Sic cùm calix dicitur novum testamentum in sanguine Christi: Ipsa promissio Evangelii de gratuita remissione peccatorum nobis in sacra coena ostenditur, sicuti expressè promissio ponitur, & simul ipse sanguis Iesu Christi offertur nobis. Quòd Beza & Cinglius hîc cavillantur sanguinem Christi ea tenus confirmare novum Testamentum, quatenus est effusus, & putidum & impium est. Non tantum illo momento, quo effusus est sanguis Christi, fuit sanguis novi Testamenti, sed inde usque à patefactione primae promissionis, usque in aeternum. Sanguis Christi est sanguis novi Testamenti: hoc enim meritum effusionis sanguinis, & mortis Christi per petuò durat & valet. Multis seculis ante incarnationem filii Dei Propheta Zacharias nominat Christi sanguinem, sanguinem novi foederis seu novi Testamenti: Tu inquit in sanguine foederis educes vinctos tuos de lacu, in quo non est aqua. Ut nebulas effundant huic argumento Calvinistae valdè sudant, ut demonstrent substantia unum esse tàm vetus quàm novum Testamentum, quia utrumque ictum sit in Christo, & offerat remissionem peccatorum & aeterna bona. Ita ut quoquo modo sua obtineant figmenta, non verentur manifestae sacrae scripturae contradicere. Non tantum veteres Ecclesiastici scriptores, & in primis Augustinus docent duo esse diversa testamanta, quae tota substantia inter se dissideant, sed etiam Spiritus sanctus, cuius doctrinam in dubium vocare nefas est, disertè adfirmat duo esse, eaque diversa testamenta. Ieremias prolixa concione docet novum testamentum prorsus, & tota specie differre à vetere. Non secundum foedus, quod pepigi cum patribus vestris, foedus inibo vobiscum, sed novum foedus feriam vobiscum: Et author Epistolae ad Hebraeos multis docet novum Testamentum super melioribus promissionibus conditum esse. Et Apostolus Paulus apertissimè dicit. Haec sunt duo Testamenta, Galat: 4. Huic tam manifestae veritati & tam sublimi authoritati contradicere magnae impietatis & detestandae petulantiae est. Manetitaque immotum nostrum argumentum, nimirum, quod in calice benedictionis distribuatur verus & substantialis sanguis Iesu Christi filii Dei, siquidem Christus vinum benedictum adpellat suum sanguinem novi Testamenti. Attendat etiam studiosus & pius lector, quàm accuratè Spiritus sanctus omnes rimas sophisticandi, & tropos comminiscendi obstruxerit, si quis enim in voce (sanguinis) collocare figuram vel Metaphoram vel Metonymiam nititur, non permittit vox novum Testamentum. Symbolum enim seu signum sanguinis Christi non est novum testamentum. Rursus si quis in voce testamenti ponere figuram tentaverit, non permittit hoc vox Sanguinis. Non enim dici potest, calix est figura novi testamenti in sanguine Christi. Quis enim sine contumelia Christi adfirmaret sanguinem Christi esse figuram novi testamenti. Firmissime igitur munivit Spiritus sanctus sanam sententiam de praesontia corporis & sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi in sacra coena, ita ut nulla sophistica convelli queat. Summam huius nostrae argumentationis sic breviter colligimus.

Non est alius sanguis novi testamenti, quàm verus, naturalis & essentialis sanguis Iesu Christi:

At Christus fatetur vinum benedictum esse sanguinem suum novi testamenti.

Ergo teste gravissimo filio Dei, vinum benedictum in coena domini, est verus et substantialis sanguis domini nostri Iesu Christi.

III. ARGUMENTUM. A Testimonio Apostoli Pauli.

Firmissima & planissima sunt haec argumenta; quae ex ipsis verbis Iesu Christi, quibus sacrosanctam coenam instituit, desumpsimus. Sed non minus firmum & planum est, quod nobis suppeditat Apostoli Pauli testimonium & declaratio. 1. Corinth: 10. cum inquit. Calix benedictionis, quem benedicimus, an non est communicatio sanguinis Christi? Et panis quem frangimus, an non est communicatio corporis Christi? Primum quod ad vocem κοινωνίας Id est, communicationis attinet. Etsi Zwingliani diu pugnarunt eam tantum commune ius, vel societatem significare: tamen tandem rei perspicuitate & veritate convictus Calvinus & eius asseclae fateri coguntur, Vocem (communicationem) in hoc Pauli loco significare participationem. Ipse enim Paulus sese disertè exponit: Omnes enim inquit ex uno pane participamus, Μετέχομεν. Ergo Paulo unum & idem est κοινωνεῖν Id est, communicare et Μετέχειν Id est, participare. Hoc vero adhuc controvertitur, num Paulus de communicatione seu participatione Spirituali, quae fit per fidem, an vero de sacramentali, hoc est, corporali, quae sit ore corporis loquatur. Et quo sensis dixerit. Panem bene dictum esse participationem corporis Christi. Iam si quis attendat ad totam seriem orationis Paulinae, is facile deprehendet, Paulum non loqui de Spirituali communicatione corporis Christi, quae fit sola fide in Christum: sed de sacramentali hoc est corpor ali, qua digni & indigniare communicant corpore et sanguini Iesu Christi.

Id enim scopus paulinae argumentationis ostendit. Paulus deterrere vult Corinthios ab idolatria & communione Ethnicorum sacrificiorum: Idque facit argumento sumpto à communicatione corporis Christi in sacra coena.

Nemo inquit potest simul cum fructu participare corpori & sanguini Christi, & communicare mensae Idolorum: Sed Christiani in Eucharistia communicant corpori et sanguini Christi: Ergò Christiani ab Idolothytis abstinere et omnia sacrificia Ethnicorum et omnem Idolotriam fugere debent. Aut sacrificia Idolorum fugienda sunt vobis, Aut à mensa domini & participatione corporis Christi prorsus abstinendum: Ne praeter alia gravissima peccata reos vos faciatis corporis & sanguinis Christi: Cum ergò Paulus deterrere conetur securos, & impoenitentes à participatione corporis Christi, certum est eum non loqui de spirituali & salutari communicatione. Haec enim nemini obesse potest. Et qui hanc usurpabant in fide, non indigebant illa severa castigatione Pauli. In quibus enim vera lucebat fides, illi haud dubiè fugiebant Idola. De corporali igitur seu Sacramentali perceptione corporis Christi loquitur, qua admoneri vult Christianos ut ab Idolothytis abstineant, ne fiant rei corporis Christi.

Deinde cum dicat panis est communicatio corporis Christi, satis apertè docet, quod de Sacramentali vel corporali participatione loquatur: si enim spiritualem communicationem intelligi voluisset, potius fidem, vel Spiritum nominasset. Fide enim spiritualiter manducamus carnem Christi, & Spiritus facit nos membra corporis Christi. Paulus verò nec fidem nec Spiritum nominat, sed dicit, Panem benedictum esse communicationem corporis Christi: De quo pane benedicto non solum pii & fideles, sed etiam multi indigni et hypocritae participant. Manifestum est igitur eum loqui de corporali participatione corporis Christi, quae dignis & indignis communis est & fit sumptione panis. Si enim non omnes, qui de pane isto edunt participes fierent corporis Christi, sed tantum poenitentiam agentes, & salvifica fide praediti, certè panis non posset dici communicatio corporis Christi. Multi enim qui panem sumerent, ut hypocritae, non fierent participes corporis Christi. Evidens est haec ratiocinatio. Non tantum agentes poenitentiam, sed etiam hypocritae & indigni edunt in coena panem benedictum: Sed hypocritae & indigni non communicant corpori Christi spiritualiter. Ergò panis non est spiritualis communicatio corporis Christi, sed Sacramentalis, id est, corporalis, in qua verum corpus Christi prae ens est & ore accipitur. Ex probatione etiam, quam Paulus adducit mens Apostoli elucet, sic enim ostendit, panem esse communicitionem corporis Christi. Quia unus est panis, & unum corpus multi sumus in Ecclesia, & omnes ex uno pane participamus. Si ex eo quod omnes ex uno pane benedicto participamus, sequitur iuxta Apostoli argumentationem, panem benedictum esse communicationem corporis Christi, necesse est omnes quot quot ut untur coena domini participes fieri corporis Christi: Si verò omnes quot quot ad mensam domini accedunt participes fiunt corporis Christi ergo necesse est Paulum non intelligere spiritualem communicationem. Nam eius planè expertes sunt indigni, infideles & hypocritae; Sed Sacramentalem seu corporalem. Quod panis benedictus sit verum & substantiale corpus Iesu Christi, quod ore corporis manducant omnes, qui sacra coena domini ut untur. Exemplum etiam, quod sumit à sacrificiis Iudaicis, eandem sententiam ostendit. Qui enim participes erant altaris, & simul de eodem sacrificio vescebantur, non omnes pariter fideles erant; Sed hoc habebant commune, quod eiusdem sacrificii omnes fiebant participes, sic et hi qui ad mensam domini accedunt, hoc commune habent, quod edunt corpus & bibunt sanguinem domini nostri Iesu Christi, licet fide non omnes sint praediti, nec spiritualem cum Christo communionem habeant. Satis ergo evidenter demonstravimus Paulum, cum dicit, Panis est communicatio corporis Christi, de Sacramentali hoc est corporali communicatione seu participatione corporis Christi loqui, & plane idem velle quod Christus. Hoc est meum corpus, nimirum Panis est verum & substantiale corpus Christi, & quotquot de hoc pane edunt, hi communicant corpori Iesu Christi. Eodem sensuetiam dicit calicem esse communicationem sanguinis Iesu Christi: Hoc est, esse ipsum verum sangumem Iesu Christi qui communicatur omnibus bibentibus ex hoc calice, Verba Pauli planissima: Panis est communicatio corporis Christi, sic contorquent Calvinistae, Panis est id, quo fit societas cum corpore Christi: Ac deinde societatem interpretantur spiritualem, qua sumus membra corporis Christi. Quis vero non videt hanc violentam expositionem verborum Pauli non consisteres Panis enim non est id, quo efficimur membra corporis Christi: Multi enim participant de pane, qui non fiunt membra Christi, nec vivisicatur Spiritu ipsius. Et scriptura docet per fidem nos inseri corpori Christi, et per Spiritum sanctum. Quomodo ergo panis est id, quo sit Spirituatis societas cum corpore Christi? Nec Pauli loquitur de corpore Christi mystico seu allegorico, hoc est, de Ecclesia, sed de substantiali suo corpore. Et cur magis placet vocabutum societatis, quam participationis & communicationis, quod multò est clarius? Potius ergò per Christi verba, ex quibus Paulus suam phrasin desumpsit interpretemur Paulum. Panis est communicatio corporis Christi, id est, panis est verum & substantiale corpus Iesu Christi, quod omnibus in sacra coena vescentibus communicatur. Alii figuram fingunt in voce ( κοινωνιάς) communicationis, quasi mens Pauli esset. Panis est signum vel symbolum communicationis corporis Christi. Hîc non immeritò primùm miramur atque etiam detestamur levitatem & petulantiam Calvinistarum, qui aliâs in voce corporis, aliâs in voce Testamenti, aliâs in voce κοινωνιάς statuunt suos tropos. Atque ita certum locum non habent, in quo fingant pedem. Tanta lubricitas certum est indicium incertae & fluctuantis conscientiae. Deinde qualis nam illa est sententia, panis est symbolum communicationis corporis Christi? Panis corpus, & vinum sanguinem aliquomodo repraesentare per Metaphoram potest, sed panis non est signum vel symbolum spiritualis manducationis seu participationis corporis Christi. Si hoc, quod Calviniste fingunt, voluisset dicere Paulus, non panem, sed manducationem panis externam nominare debuisset. Animadvertunt ergò pii contortas & violentas esse Calvinistarum expositiones, siquidem peregrinas & monstrosas sententias Paulo adfingunt. Quòd Calvinistae obiiciunt verba Pauli:

Non potestis bibere calicem domini, & calicem daemoniorum: non potestis mensae domini fieri participes & mensae daemoniorum; & hinc inferre conantur indignos non participes fieri corporis Christi, atque inde etiam amplius colligunt, Paulum loqui de Spirituali communicatione, facilè refellitur. Paulus enim non negat indignos, hypocritas & securos, qui cùm Christiani esse vellent, Idolatria sese polluebant, participes fieri corporis Christi: Id enim Cap: 11. disertè testatur, ubi adfirmat eos fieri reos corporis et sanguinis Christi ipso esu, quòd non discernant, nec diiudicent corpus domini. Sed hoc docet & monet non posse quem quam communicare mensae demoniorum, & simul cum fructu & salute participem fieri corporis & sanguinis Christi: Itaque vel ab Idolothytis, & omni communione Idolorum aut à mensa domini eos vult abstinere, ne gravissimam Dei iram scelere teterrimo, nimirum, contemptu corporis in sese provocent. Unde subiicit: Nunquid provocabimus Dominum, num fortiores ipso sumus? qua increpatione reprehendit temeritatem eorum, qui spretis Apostolorum admonitionibus, audacter ad coenam domini accedebant, et nihilominus intererant sacrificiis Idolorum & daemoniorum. Si nihil fuisset periculi, neque iniuria facta fuisset corpori Christi, à securis illis & Idolatris, non tanta saevitate illos repulisset ab usu coenae domini, qui se adhuc Idolis contaminabant. Constat ergò Paulum ad serere, quòd panis benedictus in sacra coena sit verum & essentiale corpus Iesu Christi: Constat Paulum de communicatione corporali ioqui, cùm dicit, panem benedictionis esse communicationem corporis Christi.
