The ascension of Christ to the heavens, therefore, does not only signify a physical change of place, and the translation of the body of Christ to higher places: But it signifies much more the translation of Christ from this perishing world to heavenly blessedness, and the sight of God, it signifies his exaltation in the kingdom, and the glorification of the flesh of Jesus Christ, thus Peter, Act: 3. says. Jesus Christ has occupied heaven until the time in which all things shall be restored. This is, the Lord Jesus Christ has been constituted of the heavens, so that he may rule in heaven and on earth. And Christ most clearly of all explains what it is to ascend to the heavens, namely to leave this world and to ascend to the Father. I, he says, leave this world and go to the Father, Item, I ascend to my Father and your Father, to My God and your God. Therefore, to be in the heavens is to enjoy the sight of the eternal Father and eternal blessedness. But whether in this eternal and spiritual heaven there are circumscribed places and distinct times, according to the elements and infirmities of this world, that indeed cannot be defined by us. With God, says Peter, a thousand years are as one day. And those things which the eye does not see, nor the ear has heard, nor have ascended into the heart of man, those things God has prepared for those who love him.

What madness, therefore, it is to argue from the doctrine of physics, concerning the spaces and distance of places, about the presence or absence of the glorious body of Jesus Christ, which has laid aside the elements of this world, has been exalted in the kingdom, has been lifted up above all the heavens, and sits at the right hand of the majesty of God? Why do we not rather conclude thus, as undoubtedly all the pious and orthodox conclude, that Jesus Christ not only as to his divinity, but also as to his humanity, ascended into the heavens, occupied heaven, was lifted up above all the heavens, was exalted in the kingdom, and was constituted Lord of the entire creation of angels and men. Therefore, since concerning the bread and wine of blessing he said, this is my body, this is my blood, it is most certain that the glory and power of Jesus Christ is so great that he is able to perform those things which he promised, and his true body and his true blood to exhibit to us in the Sacred Supper with bread and wine.

The article also concerning the session of Jesus Christ at the right hand of the eternal Father is not to be understood in such a way that we imagine some sublime seat or throne, placed at the right hand of God, in which the Son of God, Jesus Christ, clothed in a robe, sits, just as King Solomon commands a seat to be placed at his right hand for his mother Bathsheba: But to sit at the right hand of God signifies to obtain sovereignty over every creature in heaven and on earth, to be adored by angels and men, and with equal wisdom, power, glory, authority, honor, majesty, and right to govern the entire world and to have all things in his power. For the Holy Spirit testifies in many places that this is the force and meaning of this article. The Son of God himself, by his very passion, thus explained this article.

From this time now the Son of God will be sitting at the right hand of the power of God. To sit at the right hand of power, what else is it than to be endowed with equal power and strength with God? Paul in Eph: 1 says: God raised Jesus from the dead and placed him at his right hand in the heavenly places above every principality, and power, and dominion, and above every name that is named, not only in this, but also in the future age, and He gave all things under His feet. 1. Pet: 3. Through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who is at the right hand of God, having entered heaven, with angels and powers and virtues being subjected to Him. Here the Apostles Paul and Peter explain clearly, that to sit at the right hand of God signifies to obtain the principate over angels and men, and over the universal creature, and to have all things in His hand. This truly is to be omnipotent: this is to rule over all creatures with equal power, wisdom, and glory with God. Thus to Heb: 1. upholding all things by the word of His power, having made purification of His sins by Himself, He sat down at the right hand of the majesty on high, to sit at the right hand of the majesty is to reign with equal majesty with God. Just as Luther and Philippus, in the explanation of Psal: 110 say in the clearest words. To sit at the right hand of the Father is to reign with equal power with God. And Philippus adds that this explanation is placed by Paul Eph: 1. and Heb: 1. Now therefore the pious mind easily sees from this article concerning the session of Christ at the right hand that the presence of the body of Christ in the sacred supper is by no means overturned. For what madness would it be to wish to argue thus? Jesus Christ reigns with equal power, glory, and majesty over all creatures, and all things are subjected to His feet, therefore although He said concerning the blessed bread, this is, my body, yet he cannot offer us his body to be eaten in the holy supper. No one is so stupid as not to see that the best consequence is gathered thus instead. Christ sits at the right hand of the Father, that is, he reigns with equal power and majesty over angels and men and over every creature. Therefore it is very easy for him to perform what he promised, namely that his true body should be present in the holy supper, wherever it is administered according to his institution.

V. Objection.

Christ says John 6 The flesh profiteth nothing: it is the Spirit that quickeneth.

Therefore Christ does not give his flesh to be eaten in the holy supper.

Response:

As in other sophisms, by which the Calvinists attack the presence of the body of Jesus Christ, so especially in this objection they betray their impiety and profane thoughts concerning the flesh of Jesus Christ. For what pious soul is not kindled with just indignation, when it hears the enemies of the testament of Christ dare even that saying John 6 to bring forward to remove the presence of the flesh of Christ from the Supper? If even a crumb of piety and love toward Christ were in the Calvinists: would not shame deter them, lest they speak so contumeliously about the flesh of Christ? We answer therefore to those profane and impious disputants. Christ in that saying did not speak of his holy flesh, but of our flesh corrupted by sin. For although as to the substance of body and soul the flesh of Christ is of the same species as is ours: yet there is a huge difference between his flesh and ours. For ours is polluted by sin, liable to death and subject to the tyranny of Satan, it lacks spirit and life, it is not fit for the kingdom of God, but destined for eternal torments, unless it be regenerated. But the flesh of Jesus Christ was conceived of the Holy Spirit, born without sin, filled with the Holy Spirit, united λόγῳ to the eternal Son of God, made life-giving, and adorable to angels and men, the price for the life of the world, which provides salvation to the whole Church. What impiety therefore? what stupor? what madness is it to assert that the flesh of Jesus Christ profits nothing? Is there no utility of that flesh, which appeases the wrath of God, provides salvation to the world, vivifies our dead bodies, and merits for us eternal blessedness? Does that flesh profit nothing, which by personal union λόγῳ is united to the eternal, and now sits at the right hand of God? Let the Calvinists therefore at some time be ashamed of such great impiety.

The universal Church of Christ calls upon the precious Blood of Jesus Christ, as that by which our salvation is obtained: and the Church holds the body of Jesus Christ as the most precious treasure of all and to be preferred before the whole world. We therefore consider it a crime to understand those words (the flesh profiteth nothing) concerning the flesh of Jesus Christ.

But concerning our own corrupt flesh, infected by sin, Christ most truly said: The flesh profiteth nothing: that is, whatever proceeds from the flesh, your carnal thoughts, your carnal prudence, and your carnal senses are not fit for grasping the kingdom of God. You are not yet reborn, not yet illuminated by the holy Spirit: therefore you do not perceive my words, which are Spirit. But you dream carnally that it is necessary for my flesh to be divided into pieces, and thus to be eaten by you: these carnal imaginations of yours profit nothing, they neither take away death nor restore life. It is the Spirit that quickeneth, namely the holy Spirit, whom the Son of God imparts through faith: he kindles the true understanding of the words of Christ, illuminates the mind, and restores life. Therefore this saying of Christ is not to be twisted toward the flesh of Jesus Christ.

And in the whole sermon of Christ John 6 concerning the eating of the flesh of Christ, nothing is treated concerning the Lord's Supper, which was instituted a whole year after this communication: But concerning the faith, by which the benefits of the mediator are to be apprehended. They are, he says. And his whole sermon is metaphorical: taken from the sermons of the Prophets Isaiah, who compare the kingdom of Christ to a most sumptuous banquet: and David, who compare the gifts of the Holy Spirit to a most well-furnished table by allegory. He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood, has eternal life, and remains in me, This is, he who truly believes the promise of the Gospel, offering the remission of sins and eternal life on account of my death, he will live on account of me. Thus Christ and the Prophets compare faith to eating; since the anxiety of an evil conscience is not unlike hunger. And this spiritual eating must also be used entirely in the sacred supper. But besides it, the son of God Jesus Christ instituted a peculiar eating of his flesh, so that in the sacred supper he exhibits to us in the bread his body to be eaten, and in the wine his blood to be drunk. Concerning this Sacramental perception of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, which is common to the pious and the hypocrites approaching the supper, since nothing is said in the 6th Chapter of John: The Calvinists act impudently because they [say] these sayings nothing Those things pertaining to this, even with the insult to the flesh of Christ, they violently twist to attack the presence of the body of Christ in the sacred supper.

VI. Objection.

Christ says, John 12. You have the poor always with you, but me you do not have always. Likewise, the angels announcing the resurrection of Christ say, Matt: 28. He has risen, he is not here. Likewise. John: 16. Again I leave the world and go to the Father.

Therefore the body of Jesus Christ is not truly present in the supper of the Lord.

Response:

Christ and the angels in these sayings speak of visible and bodily conversation with the Church. For after the Son of God performed and completed the work of our redemption, he rose from the dead and ascended to the heavens, and so he left the world, that henceforth he does not offer himself to be seen by our eyes and touched by our hands, as he had previously conversed with his disciples. John says, that which our hands have touched and which we have seen with our eyes, we announce to you the word of life: 1. John: 1.

Item, John 1. And he dwelt among us and we saw his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the father full of grace and truth. But after the resurrection he says to Mary: Do not touch me: For I have not yet ascended to the father, as if he were saying, You imagine for yourself a visible and bodily conversation, as I conversed visibly with you before my passion: But another reason now emerges. I ascend to the father so that your faith may be exercised and so that I may be wholly for the Church. From this, however, it does not follow that the body and blood of Jesus Christ are not in the holy supper. For the most wise and omnipotent God knows many ways by which he can exhibit the presence of his body and blood to us. And not only after he rose from the dead and entered into a new and heavenly life was he present to the Apostles in a different way than before his death, but even when he was still in the world, he could exhibit himself as present in various ways according to his immense wisdom and omnipotence, Luke 24. On the very day of the resurrection, he says to the Apostles: These are the words which I spoke to you, when I was still with you.

Not only is he truly present to the Apostles with his body and divinity, but he also exhibits his body to be handled by hands and to be looked upon by eyes: And yet he says, These things I was speaking to you, when I was among you, just as if he is not now in the world among the Apostles. Thus he is at once among the Apostles and is seen by the Apostles, and at the same time he is not among the Apostles: in his substance he is truly present and is seen, but he is not present to the Apostles in that manner in which he was previously among them; he is no longer mortal, he is not subject to the elements of this world, he no longer needs food, drink, sleep, rest: It is not necessary for him to be seen: He is not bound by the laws of this world, but he now lives a blessed, new, spiritual life, devoid of death and every infirmity. Therefore, to leave the world signifies for Christ, through death and resurrection, to lay aside the conditions of this world and to live a heavenly life. However, this glory and blessedness of Christ does not hinder at all that Christ should be truly present to his Church, and offer his body to us to be eaten and his blood to be drunk in the sacred supper. For the same Christ, who said: You have the poor always with you, but me you do not have always, said also: Where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I in the midst of them. Matthaei 18. Likewise, I am with you all days even to the consummation of the age. Nor indeed does he speak only of the presence of his divine nature, but of his whole person.

Visibly therefore and corporally and according to the conditions and laws of this world, Christ is not with us, we do not know Christ according to the flesh. But invisibly, in a heavenly manner, Spiritually, and by that reason which is known to Him, He is truly, really, and substantially present in the Church, and truly, really, and substantially exhibits in the blessed bread His body to be eaten and His blood in the blessed wine to be drunk. For He Himself said: Eat, this is my body: Drink all of this, this chalice is the new testament in my blood.

VII. Objection.

The reason is the same for all sacraments, as much in the old as in the new testament.

But the sacraments of the old testament are only figures of other things, which they signify.

Therefore also the sacrament of the body and Blood of Jesus Christ is only a sign of the absent body and Blood of Jesus Christ.

Response:

The major premise of the argument is simply false, nor can it be demonstrated by any testimony of holy scripture.

For there is a great dissimilarity and variety between the sacraments of the Old and New Testaments. And although they agree in the efficient and final cause, yet they clearly differ in the material and formal cause. And first, there is a great variety and similarity of the sacraments of the Old Testament. The cloud under which the Israelites were baptized. The water flowing from the rock, which the Israelites drank. The manna, which fell from heaven, the ashes of the red heifer by whose sprinkling the people were expiated, were indeed figures, which signified the presence of God, and reminded the Israelites of the promise: but they were not a sealing of the righteousness of faith as circumcision was. And what is to be determined concerning individual sacraments in the Old Testament, that must be sought from those places in which they are instituted by divine command. What is to be believed concerning circumcision in the Church, is taught not by some common rule of the sacraments, but by the express word of God Gen. 17. Chapter. Thus what is to be thought concerning the Paschal Lamb must be sought from the 12th Chapter of Exodus. Thus how the sacraments of the New Testament are to be understood cannot be sought from elsewhere than from the words of institution. Matthew 26. We read what Christ pronounces concerning his holy supper. From these words, therefore, this is my body: And this is my blood, it must be determined what we perceive in the holy supper, one must not dream of some common rule, which relies on no testimony of scripture at all, to which the words of Christ are to be bent. Matth: 28. & Marci 16. Christ teaches what he wishes us to believe concerning the Sacrament of Baptism, which is, of course, that it is a washing of regeneration and of the cleansing of sins. Therefore, the figment concerning a common rule, according to which all Sacraments are to be understood, must be exploded. Indeed, holy scripture does not even acknowledge the appellation of Sacrament, so that it might call the supper of the Lord a Sacrament: How therefore can it be determined from a common rule concerning the Sacraments what is to be thought concerning the presence of the body and blood of Jesus Christ in the holy supper? Augustine says that Sacraments are signs of those things which they signify. That can be extended to all types and figures, and finally to all allegories. As Abraham sacrificing his son is a Sacrament of God the Father, who did not spare his own son, but gave him for us: but who is so rude in the Church that he does not see that there is a huge difference between such allegories and the testament of Jesus Christ, by which he bequeathed his body and blood to us?

VIII. Objection.

The promise of grace speaks only of spiritual communication with Christ: And it is perceived only by faith.

The words of the institution of the Lord's Supper pertain only to the promise of grace.

Therefore, in the Lord's Supper there is only a spiritual communication of the body of Christ, which is perceived only by faith.

Respond:

The discerning reader undoubtedly observes that the Calvinists do not seek arguments to prove their opinion from the clear words of Jesus Christ, by which He instituted the holy Supper: But they clearly remove them from sight: Because the most brilliant light of truth dazzles their eyes. The Calvinists, however, manufacture new dogmas, which are destitute of every support of the divine word, and then they accommodate the figments of their opinions concerning the Lord's Supper to this Lesbian rule. We therefore demand of the Calvinists that they demonstrate to us by clear sayings of Scripture this rule, that the promises of grace speak only of the spiritual communication of Christ and spiritual gifts. For since this is a new dogma in the Church, we are bound by no religion to assent to it, unless it be demonstrated by clear sayings of Holy Scripture.

We indeed read in the word of God, that not only spiritual goods and the spiritual communication of the flesh of Christ are promised to the Church by God, but also that many corporal things are brought forth and given by the immense mercy of God, not only to the worthy but also to the unworthy. Manna, the heavenly food, and water drawn from the hardest rock, happened to the people of Israel out of the mere grace of God, and yet they were corporal goods. For the reason that Paul calls it spiritual food and drink, he does so because that food and drink was created miraculously and by divine omnipotence against the order of nature; otherwise it was a truly corporal thing, which nourished the bodies not only of the faithful but also of the unfaithful. It was a promise of grace that a son was to be born to Abraham from Sarah, and that Abraham was to be the heir of the world. But did this promise encompass only spiritual goods and spiritual communication with Christ? By no means. Isaac the son and the whole most numerous posterity of Abraham was a corporal thing. The Jews had true flesh and true blood. And the possession of the land and the whole kingdom of Israel, and all the riches of David, of Solomon, and of all the Jews, flowed as from a fountain from the gratuitous promise which was made to Abraham, that he was to be the heir of the world. And who will be so insane as to say that these were only spiritual goods? The very incarnation of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, and his dwelling among men, his miracles, healings, and good deeds flowed from the promise of grace alone, not from the law. And yet it cannot be denied that these were immense bodily benefits: That the Messiah exhibited himself to be seen and touched in the body, that he visibly instructed his disciples in his presence, that he healed the sick, cleansed the lepers, and fed a great multitude of men with bread and fish. It is manifest, therefore, that the promises of grace do not speak only of a spiritual communion with Christ. Cyril does not hesitate to profess that, besides a spiritual one, we also have a bodily communion with the flesh of Christ, and he demonstrates it from the institution of the Lord's Supper.

In 15. Capit: Ioan: We do not deny that we are joined to Christ spiritually by right faith and sincere charity, but that we have no communion with him according to the flesh, that we utterly deny, and we say that it is altogether alien to the divine scriptures. Or does he perhaps think that the power of the mystical blessing is unknown to us? For when it happens in us, does it not also cause Christ to dwell in us corporally through the communion of the flesh of Christ?

And in Chapter 17. For the Son is united to us corporally through the mystical blessing as a man, but spiritually, as God, by the grace of his Spirit restoring our Spirit to a new life and to the participation of the divine nature. Here Cyril explicitly mentions both the Spiritual and the corporal communication of Christ. Therefore, the opinion of the Calvinists is false, by which they pretend that the promise of grace speaks only of Spiritual goods.

As for what they add, that the promise of grace is perceived only through faith, this is indeed most true: For Paul rightly says, Without faith the promise is void. Roma. 4. And Habakkuk says, The just shall live by his faith. From this, however, it does not follow that the truth of divine promises depends upon the faith of men. Nay, Paul says, let God be true, but every man a liar. This is, even if no man believed God, nevertheless the truth of the divine promise would stand for all eternity. Through the Prophet Isaiah, God promised that it would come to pass that a virgin would conceive, and bear a son, and call his name Immanuel. Ahaz and a great multitude of the Jews did not have faith in this promise, but did God retract or abolish His promise on account of their disbelief? By no means. Nay, in truth Jesus Christ Immanuel was born of the virgin Mary and was made man. God had promised that it would come to pass that Jesus Christ would rise from death. None of the Apostles believed this; For they were all ignorant of scripture. Yet the Son of God rose again on the third day, according to the scriptures. Therefore, the truth of divine promises does not depend on the faith of men, but on the infallible certainty of the divine word; indeed, the spiritual fruit from the promise of grace cannot be perceived except through faith. For the just man lives by his faith. But those things which God promises He will exhibit, or will bring about, those are exhibited and stand firm, whether men believe or do not believe. Thus, when Christ affirms that He exhibits His body to be eaten and His blood to be drunk in the Holy Supper, He truly performs it, whether men believe it or do not believe it: however, no one perceives the spiritual fruit of the Eucharist except he who is endowed with faith.

IX. Objection.

Paul, 1 Corinthians 10, speaks of such a communion by which we are all made one body. But the impious are not one body with us.

Therefore, Paul is not speaking of a bodily communion, of which even the unworthy, the impious, and hypocrites become participants.

Response:

I deny the minor premise. For when Paul says, We being many are one body, he does not embrace only the faithful, who are the living members of the body of Christ, but also the unfaithful, the impious, and the hypocrites, who enjoy the external society of the saints. One body signifies one assembly bound together among themselves by certain laws and ceremonies, a Church associated by a common confession and the use of the sacraments. Of this Church, which Paul compares to a human body, there are diverse citizens, some good, some evil: some holy, some not holy: of this body, I say, there are diverse members, some living, some dead, which do not receive either life or the Spirit from the head. Eli, Phineas, and Ahitob are members of the body, which is the Church, and they perform the priesthood among the people of God: but because they are without repentance and faith, they are dead members. Ananias and Sapphira, and Nicolaus are members of the body, which is the Church, but because they simulate piety by hypocrisy, and are alien to the motions of repentance and faith, they are dead members, which at length were cut off by the sword of the divine word. If anyone now should cavil, that it is absurd if it is said that the body of Christ has dead members; the answer is ready and plain. When we speak of the essential body of Jesus Christ, in no way are dead members to be attributed to Christ, for Christ is life entirely, and in him is life is, and gives life to all things. But when we speak of the allegorical or metaphorical body of Christ, which is the Church, it cannot be denied that there are diverse members of this body, some living, others dead, just as Christ, depicting the Church in another similitude, says that some are good fish, others bad. For it is manifest that the Church is considered in two ways in Holy Scripture. For at one time the Church is described as it is in the sight of God, who is the searcher of hearts. Considered in this way, this temple of God consists only of living and precious stones. For God counts only the holy, and those endowed with saving faith, to His elect Church, to which He is about to give eternal life. But at another time the Church is described insofar as it falls under our sight and judgment. By this reasoning we call the Church all those who hear the word of God, and by public confession and the use of the sacraments, join themselves to the head of the Church. And of this assembly of those professing the Gospel, Paul says that it is one body, namely, bound together among themselves by external profession and the use of the sacraments as by a bond. He does not, however, treat of the spiritual communion by which the holy and the faithful become together partakers of the life and all the benefits of Christ. For from the fact that all partake of one bread, he proves the communion. But it cannot be denied that many hypocrites, alien from faith and devoid of of true piety, they do indeed partake of the blessed bread: But they by no means perceive the spiritual fruit of the flesh of Jesus Christ, nay rather, they eat judgment unto themselves. Therefore, it is evidently concluded from this that Paul is not speaking only of the spiritual communion of the body of Christ, when he says: The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

X. Objection.

Paul speaks of such a communion which cannot stand with the communion of demons, for he says, you cannot at the same time partake of the table of the Lord and the table of the Devils.

That corporal or that Sacramental communion, which you assert, can stand with the communion of Devils.

Therefore Paul did not speak of such a corporal or Sacramental communion of the flesh of Christ, which you assert, but of a spiritual one.

Response:

What Paul says, you cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of the Demons: You cannot be partakers of the table of the Lord and the table of the Demons; It must be understood with a saving fruit. For those who participate in the table of demons and contaminate themselves with idolatry, these receive the Eucharist unto judgment. For by the society of Gentile sacrifices they show that they do not yet truly believe the word, nor burn with the zeal of piety, even if they were to approach the table of the Lord. The principal scope of this whole severe castigation was that the Apostle, by the mention of the Eucharist, might deter the Corinthians from the society of Gentile sacrifices, in which they were contaminated by idolatry. And the Apostle wishes that the Corinthians abstain entirely from the idolatrous sacrifices of the Gentiles, or not participate in the table of the Lord, lest they summon a more grievous judgment upon themselves. Therefore, he does not deny that the Corinthians can be made participants of both the table of the Lord and the table of demons: Indeed, because this abuse had prevailed among some, for that reason he rebukes them: And he teaches that it cannot be done with saving fruit. Therefore he adds, What? Shall we provoke the Lord? Are we stronger than he? Paul also testifies that there are some who drink the cup of the Lord unworthily. Therefore he admits that some can be made participants of both the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons, in the sacrifices of idols, but not with saving fruit.

XI. Objection.

Sacraments outside the use instituted by Christ are not sacraments.

But the ungodly depart entirely from the use instituted by Christ, since they neither confirm nor nourish their faith with the Eucharist.

Therefore, for the ungodly, the blessed bread is not a sacrament.

Respond:

There are snares in the rule concerning the sacraments, and especially in the phrase (outside the use). The rule is true, that nothing has the nature of a sacrament outside the use instituted by Christ. When the water of baptism is transferred to the magical consecrations of fountains, herbs, or animals, it does not have the nature of Baptism: when bells are baptized, it is in no way Baptism. For here the entire action instituted by Christ is perverted. When the blessed bread is reserved, or carried about and adored, or offered for the living and the dead, it is not a Sacrament, but a horrible profanation of the Lord's Supper, for one departs entirely from the use instituted by Christ. In this sense, therefore, the rule is true, that nothing has the nature of a sacrament outside the use instituted by Christ. But the Calvinists and sacramentarians play with sophistries; they do not understand by 'use' the action itself which Christ instituted, but the faith by which one perceives the fruit of the Eucharist. and applies to itself the benefits of the mediator. Therefore, if you understand the rule concerning this use of faith, it is false. For the truth of the sacraments depends neither on the dignity nor on the indignity of those receiving them, but on the infallible certainty of the divine word.

XII. Objection.

The body of Jesus Christ is always full of the Holy Spirit and is life-giving.

But the ungodly do not receive the Holy Spirit, nor are they made alive.

Therefore, they do not receive the body of Jesus Christ either.

Response:

To the major premise, which stands in need of explanation. The body of Jesus Christ in itself is always full of the Holy Spirit and is life-giving: but how, to whom, and by what means it imparts the Holy Spirit, and communicates the life, righteousness, and salvation obtained by its death, is to be learned not from the darkness of human reason, but from the express word of God. For this testifies that Christ, who is our salvation, righteousness, life, sanctification, and redemption through the promise of the Gospel, [is given] only to those who seriously turn to God and by true faith embrace the gratuitous promise to communicate and impart his benefits, the remission of sins, righteousness, the Holy Spirit, life, and eternal salvation, according to the saying. This is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the son and believes in him may have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day. Here Christ explicitly teaches to whom and through what medium he wishes to communicate his goods, life, and Spirit, namely, to believers. And he warns that he wishes to work in believers unto salvation. And indeed Christ acts most freely, not by any necessity of nature, he is always instructed with the force and power of vivifying; but it is not necessary for him to vivify, when he does not wish to. Moreover, he does not wish to vivify those, nor bestow upon them the Holy Spirit, whom he observes to persist in sins against conscience, and to be alien from faith, such as are Epicureans and hypocrites, whence are the sayings. He who does not believe in the son is already judged. Item, He who does not believe in the son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon the fallen. Therefore, as Paul says concerning the Gospel of Jesus Christ, that to believers it is an odor of life unto life: but to the impious it is an odor of death unto death: not by his own fault but by the fault of the impious. Thus also the body of Christ, always existing in itself as vivifying, endows those endowed with faith and those assenting to the word, both with Spirit and with life: but those alien from faith and serious repentance, it leaves to death and damnation. adjudges. The Holy Spirit, because He is everywhere and fills all things, is even in the impious: but by a universal presence, not by a mode of sanctification, or by the spiritual action of God.

XIII. Objection.

Jesus Christ instituted His holy supper only for the faithful: and only to believers does He promise and exhibit His goods.

But the impious, hypocrites, and Epicureans are not faithful, nor are they disciples, but enemies of Christ.

Therefore Christ neither promised nor exhibits His body to the impious.

Response:

The major premise is false. Our Lord Jesus Christ instituted the holy gathering for His whole Church, in which there are certainly always good and bad, and He commands all who have given their name to Christ to use this holy supper. The spiritual goods, indeed, which are contained in the promise, such as the remission of sins, righteousness, life, salvation, the Holy Spirit, only these they receive, who apply the promise to themselves by true faith and acquiesce in the word. But other innumerable goods, both spiritual and corporal, in which however justice and eternal life do not consist, also happen to the impious and hypocrites in the society of the Church. The impious hear the word of God, they hear the prophecies of the Prophets and Apostles, they see the miracles of Christ, which was a great glory; many impious in the Church are adorned with the singular gift of prophesying, of performing miracles, of healing the sick, of interpreting the holy scripture by the gift of wisdom and eloquence. The impious enjoy peace, victories, the protection of the Church. And there are innumerable goods which the impious and hypocrites enjoy in the society of the Church. Judas the traitor enjoys an immense good; he is a domestic and assiduous hearer of the sermons of Jesus Christ, with his own eyes he sees the stupendous miracles of Christ, he is constituted an Apostle, he is adorned with great gifts of the holy spirit, of preaching the Gospel, and of casting out demons. And yet he is impious, he lacks faith, and does not become a participant in the spiritual goods of Christ. Balaam is impious and an enchanter; and yet he was adorned by God with the distinguished gift of prophesying. Scripture celebrates the excellent wisdom which shone in Achitophel: when nevertheless he was a hypocrite and an enemy of the innocent David. Ahab persists in his impiety and impenitence. And yet God reveals to him an illustrious promise. On the Messiah, who is to be born of a virgin. God bestows countless goods, both spiritual and bodily, not only upon the pious and faithful, but even upon the impious and hypocrites; but God does not bestow eternal life and the Holy Spirit upon the unfaithful. Thus Christ also bestows His body and Blood upon hypocrites and the unworthy: But He does not impart righteousness and salvation to them.

XIV. Objection.

It is not good to take the bread of the children and cast it to the dogs.

The body and blood of Jesus Christ is the bread of the children of God.

Therefore it is not good to give the body of Jesus Christ to hypocrites and the unfaithful, whom Christ calls dogs.

Response:

I concede the whole argument. When hypocrites, Epicureans, Atheists, and the impenitent are known to the pastor or minister of the Church, they are to be entirely warded off from the supper of the Lord, and the body of Jesus Christ is by no means to be distributed to them. For the command of Christ is, do not give what is holy to the dogs. From this, however, it does not follow, when hypocrites, atheists, and Epicureans approach the sacred supper and either impose upon the pastor by hypocrisy, or the pastor, for fear of danger, does not perform his office, that the impious and unworthy receive nothing except bread and wine. As hypocrisy and distrust in beasts does not change the Sacrament, so neither does the negligence and impiety of the pastor. The truth of the Sacraments depends on the word and institution of the Son of God. The pastor certainly sins most gravely by distributing the body and blood to a secure and impenitent man, whom he knows to persist in impiety: Nevertheless, the blessed bread which the hypocrite and atheist receives is the true body, and the blessed wine which the impious man drinks in the synaxis is the true blood.

XV. Objection.

Christ says, John 6. He who eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, has eternal life and remains in me and I in him.

But hypocrites, the unworthy and the secure, do not receive eternal life, nor do they remain in Christ.

Therefore hypocrites, the secure and the unworthy, do not eat the flesh of Christ.

Response:

Christ John 6. does not speak of the Lord's Supper, which was instituted a whole year after that sermon. But he uses figurative speech and treats of the spiritual eating of the body of Christ, which happens by faith in the promised mediator. Concerning this Spiritual eating, if you understand the conclusion, I concede the whole argument. For it is most true that the unworthy, the secure, and the hypocrites neither eat the flesh of Christ Spiritually, nor become partakers of the life of Christ. But if you understand the conclusion concerning the corporal or sacramental participation of the body of Christ, since the major premise of the argument speaks of the Spiritual, everyone sees that there are four terms in the argument and that what is usually said is that the brooms are scattered. For the sacred scripture speaks distinctly of a twofold eating of the body of Christ. One is Spiritual or figurative, which happens as often as we apprehend by true faith the promise concerning the Mediator, and apply to ourselves his benefits offered in the word. For our conscience labors under a most sad hunger, oppressed by the wrath of God; but it is fed and refreshed by the passion and death of Jesus Christ the mediator. Hence it is that Isaiah says. Come to the waters, buy and drink without silver, procure food and eat: Ies: 55. In this way also the fathers in the old testament, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, David, Elijah, ate the flesh of Christ Spiritually, that is, they believed in the Messiah, and by this faith sustained themselves against the power of death and Satan. Of this eating Christ speaks Ioannis 6. He who shall eat my flesh, and drink my blood has eternal life. And Augustine said concerning this eating: Believe and you have eaten. But the other is corporal, or Sacramental, which the Son of God therefore instituted in the new testament, so that through it the spiritual eating of the flesh of Christ might be confirmed. This is the true reception of the body and blood of Jesus Christ under the blessed bread and wine, which eating is indeed done with the corporal mouth, but it is not done in a corporal or sensible manner. For in an arcane and heavenly manner the Son of God Jesus Christ offers us his body to be eaten and his blood to be drunk. Because therefore the spiritual eating of the body of Christ could even then take place when it was not yet born: For the fathers Noah, Abraham, Moses, David also spiritually ate the flesh of Christ: And it can take place by faith, even outside the supper, when we do not receive the Eucharist, and it is done only by the pious, in whom true faith shines, putting on Christ; Therefore it is distinguished from the corporal, which is done only in the sacred supper, when we eat the blessed bread, and it is common at the same time to the faithful and to hypocrites or Epicureans and atheists, who approach the table of the Lord unworthily among the pious. And these are the principal objections by which the Calvinists and Zwinglians attack the presence of the body and blood of Jesus Christ in the sacred supper. Which, since they lean upon no foundation of sacred scripture, but are ropes made of sand connected, should by no means so move pious minds that they drive them away from the clear and indubitable word of the omnipotent God.

Latin:

CAPUT V. Refutatio Obiectionum, Quibus Calvinistae Oppugnant Praesentiam Corporis Iesu Christi.

Prima & potissima cura piae mentis esse debet, ut sanam & perspicuam sententiam de singulis religionis controversiis ex verbo Dei hauriat, eamque indubiis verbi divini testimoniis probè muniat: Quam deinde constanter tueri debet, qualescunque etiam obiiciantur cavillationes: fidei enim syncerae proprium est, varios sustinere insultus Satanae, mundi, rationis, & tamen à verbo Dei claro non dimoveri.

Altera deinde cura piae mentis esse debet, ut sedulò inquirat, quomodo adversariorum cavillationes perspicuè dilui, & falsitas earum monstrari possit. Multum enim in fide confirmamur, cùm depraehendimus antagonistarum opiniones, nullo certo fundamento inniti. Et in ipsa seria veritatis inquisitione, subinde maius lumen accendit Spiritus sanctus.

Post quam igitur piam & sanam doctrinam, de praesentia corporis & Sanguinis Iesu Christi, perspicuis & infallibilibus sacrae scripturae demonstrationibus probavimus atque munivimus: Accedemus nunc ad refutationem sophismatum, quibus Calvinistae & eorum adseclae nostram confessionem labefactare conantur. Etsi enim omnes cavillationes, quae à Zwinglio, Calvino et omnibus eiusdem farine hominibus adferri solent, perspicuè, nervosè et validè sint refutatae, adeò, ut impudentia Calvinistarum, qui eiusmodi protritas naenias in Ecclesiam reducere audent, odio digna sit, tamen, quia Satan non desistit pusillos Christi istis sophismatibus turbare, & veritatem Ecclesiae obfuscare, necesse est nos repetere refutationes nostras, & perspicuam veritatem praestigiis & sophismatibus opponere.

I. Obiectio Calvinistarum.

Impossibile est, ut verum & naturale corpus humanum, simul & semel sit in diversis, vel pluribus locis.

At Christus sedens ad dexteram patris, habet verum & naturale corpus, constans carne, sanguine & ossibus.

Ergò impossibile est, ut verum & naturale corpus Iesu Christi in omnibus locis, in quibus sacra coena administratur in terris, verè et substantialiter sit praesens.

Respond:

Primùm ad maiorem. Cùm in hoc argumento quaeratur, non quid homini vel creaturae, sed quid unigenito & omnipotenti filio Dei Iesu Christo sit possibile, non solum falsa, sed etiam impia, sacrilega, & blasphema est maior propositio. Fides enim nostra sic habet: Apud Deum omnia sunt possibilia, Et quod apud homines est impossibile, hoc possibile est apud Deum: Et nihil est impossibile apud Deum. Unde et primus articulus fidei nostrae, fundamentum nostrae religionis, sic dicit. Credo in Deum creatorem coeliet terrae. Huic immoto fundamento fidei nostrae cum impia sententia in argumento contradicat, ab omnibus piis explodi, & pro blasphema haberi debet. Nihil adhuc dico de proprietatibus aut praerogativis humanae naturae Iesu Christi: hac dere suo loco, iuvante Deo, agam. Maior argumenti omnipotentiam Dei vocat in dubium: num Deus facere possit, ut verum & naturale corpus humanum, simul & semel sic in diversis, & pluribus locis. Hîc disertè adfirmo, Eum, qui negat Deum id praestare posse, nihil ab homine Ethnico differre, ut qui praecipuum fundamentum totius religionis Christianae et omnis pietatis evertit.

Quae enim vel mica verae religionis residuà erit, si statuemus ea, quae legibus naturae repugnare videntur, ne Deo quidem esse possibilia? Quae potest esse spes nostra, non solum contra mortem & infernum, qui videntur nobis invicti hostes, sed in ulla necessitate? ubi secundae causae nos deserunt, si non credemus apud Deum omnia esse possibilia? An quisquam nostrum vel incarnationem filii, vel resurrectionem mortuorum certò credere poterit, everso hoc axiomate. Quod apud Deum omnia sint possibilia? Attendant ergò piae mentes, quid Satan per Calvinistas quaerat, nimirum, totius religionis & fidei extirpationem.

Paulò verecundiores inter Calvinistas, statim hîc resiliunt, & quaeruntur transponi hîc statum disputationis. Non enim de omnipotentia Dei, sed de voluntate eius esse quaestionem. His respondeo: si tantùm de voluntate & non de omnipotentia eius est quaestio, cur ergò à vobis tale contexitur argumentum? Certè nexus argumenti esse debet. Quod fieri non possit, (& ut aliqui loquuntur ex Calvinistis) Ne Deus quidem facere possit, ut unum & naturale corpus sit in diversis & multis locis. Annon hoc est derogare omnipotentiae Dei? quam si conceditis, saltem sermone simulato: Ergò explodite vestram argumentationem. Maiore enim propositione eversa, quae est σύνεχον argumenti, totum concidit. Alii verò impudentiores, ut Beza & Petrus Martyr, non dubitant palàm suum Ethnicismum profiteri: sine omni enim verecundia scribunt, & loquuntur in Ecclesia, Universalem illam propositionem, quae adfirmat, Apud Deum omnia esse possibilia, restringendam esse. Hoc sanè est filio Dei Iesu Christo in os contradicere. Et huius modi blasphemiae ab illis proficiscuntur, qui se antistites Ecclesiae profitentur.

Ad speciem deinde descendunt Beza & Martyr, & claris verbis ponunt, ne Deo quidem possibile esse efficere, ut unum corpus habeat veri corporis rationem, & tamen sit in diversis & pluribus locis. Et huc alia adducunt, quae à Deo fieri non possint: ut quod Hieronymus non sine blasphemia dixit. Deus cùm omnia possit, tamen virginem post ruinam suscitare non potest; Item Triangulus non potest fieri quadrangulus. Et ut declinent aliquomodo invidiam blasphemiae, praetexunt haec non esse signa imbecillitatis, sed potius omnipotentiae. Annon igitur manifestum est, Calvinistas non de voluntate Dei, sed de ipsius omnipotentia disputare? Repetimus igitur nostram confessionem, & dicimus blasphemam esse maiorem propositionem. Deus enim cùm omnia possit, non solùm possibile, sed & facile illi est efficere, ut cùm ipse vult unum corpus sit in diversis & pluribus locis, & nihilominus retinat veri corporis rationem. Nec verò tantùm possibile est Deo, efficere, ut Christi glorio sum corpus in diversis locis: Verùmetiam si volet efficere, potest ut Pauli, Eliae vel alterius hominis corpus simul & semel sit in diversis & pluribus locis Qui enim verbo suo coelum & terram ex nihil condidit, et leges totius naturae instituit, an ei quicquam esset impossibile? Constanter igitur sine omni restrictione retinemus Axioma. Omnia esse possibilia apud Deum: Et prorsus nullum verbum apud Deum esse impossibile. Blasphemam sententiam Hieronymi, quod Deus virginem post lapsum restituere non possit, nihil moramur: Plus fidei habemus Iesaiae: Qui promittit fore, ut etiamsi peccata nostra fuerint ut coccinum, tamen nivè candidiores reddamur. Certè Rahab, Bersabea, Magdalena, quae post lapsum poenitentiam egerunt, & in mediatorem crediderunt, multis virginibus mundiores erunt in futuro seculo. Et quae fatalis necessitas impediret Deum, quò minùs triangulum ex quadrangulo facere posset, si vellet?

Impietatem igitur suam Ethnicam produnt Calviniste, cùm talia in medium adferunt exempla. Peccare vel mentiri non potest Deus, quia voluntatem suam in verbo suo sit exposuit, quòd irascatur peccato & mendacio.

Nuspiam autem exposuit Deus, quòd nolit efficere, ut unum corpus sit in diversis locis. Blaphemia est igitur dicere, quòd ne Deus quidem efficere possit, ut unum corpus sit in diversis locis.

Cùm ergò maior in argumento non subsistat, corruit sponte totum figmentum cavillationis.

Non est quòd clamitent Calvinistae, ineptam nos texere consequentiam. Deus potest hoc vel illud facere: Ergò facit. Nos enim nequaquam sic argumentamur. Effugia sunt ista usitata Calvinistis. Hoc solum hîc demonstramus, Deo non esse impossibile, efficere, ut unum corpus sit in diversis & pluribus locis. Quod, cùm hic obtinemus, satis est nobis: tum enim concidit prorsus obiectio Calvinistarum, qua nostram confessionem impugnarunt ab impossibilitate. Quòd Dei voluntas sit, ut corpus Christi in coena sacra, ubicunque illa in terris administratur, verè sit praesens, non ex Dei omnipotentia, sed expresso Dei verbo, quod suprà in confirmationem nostrae sententiae perspicuè, & sine omni obscuritate monstravimus, probamus. Itaque calumnia est, quòd obiiciunt Calvinistae nos à Dei potentia ad voluntatem eius argumentam; Perinde ac si quis sic colligeret, potuisset Deus hominem condere volatilem: Ergò talem condidit. Imò verò nos sigillatim & Dei voluntatem, & eius potentiam ex ipsius verbo demonstramus.

Voluntas eius manifesta est ex verbis institutionis coenae: omnipotentia eius constat ex creatione omnium rerum & testimonio Christi. Apud Deum omnia sunt possibilia. Matth: 19. Si quis plenè ponat maiorem propositionem, is mox deprehendet eius falsitatem & impietatem: sic enim ponenda erat. Impossibile est apud Deum, ut unum corpus naturale & finitum, simul & semel sit in pluribus locis. Quis verò pius animus non statim exhorreat & execretur impietatem eius propositionis?

In hoc argumento disputari etiam solet, de proprietatibus & praerogativis humanae naturae Iesu Christi. Verùm, quia eversa maiore propsitione, quae debebat esse σύνεχον argumenti, tota argumenti structura corruit, & evanescit, non miscebo hanc disputationem. Nihil enim opus est longiore sermone, postquam protritum & conculcatum est sophisma. Palàm & ingenuè concedimus minorem, eamque ad serimus atque defendimus contra Eutychianos. Dicimus Iesum Christum filium Dei sedentem ad dexteram aeterni patris, habere verum naturale & finitum corpus, quod constat carne, sangume, ossibus, & retinet omnes suas proprietates essentiales. At hinc non sequitur, quòd corpus eius non possit esse praesens in Sacra coena, ubicunque illa in terris administratur: Immo ta enim regula est, nullam admittens restrictionem. Quod apud Deum omnia sint possibilia. Matt: 19. Quare cùm omnipotens filius Dei dixit. Hic panis benedictus est meum corpus: Certò credere debemus, quòd naturale corpus Iesu Christi, verè sit praesens, ubicunque coena sacra iuxta Christi institutionem celebratur.

II. Obiectio.

Essentialis proprietas est veri & naturalis corporis humani, in uno tantum & non in multis locis esse simul & semel.

Iesus Christus sedens ad dexteram aeterni patris, habet verum & naturale corpus.

Ergò essentialis proprietatis est corporis Christi, iam ad dextram Dei sedentis, in uno tantùm loco esse & non in multis.

Respond:

Maior non est vera. Nam esse in loco, non est essentialis proprietas humani corporis, sed accidentalis. Non est enim de ipsa substantia corporis. Essentiales seu substantiales proprietates corporis humani sunt, esse finitum, esse conditum, habere carnem, sanguinem, ossa, membra, caput, epar, venas. At in loco vel tempore esse, non est de essentia corporis. Secundò, Esse in loco, est quidem proprietas corporis humani, secundum elementa & infirmitates huius mundi: Quis verò impediet aut prohibebit Deum, ne si velit eximat aliquod corpus huius mundi legibus & elementis? Corporis humani proprietas est, comburi in igne, mergim aqua, cibo per multos dies subtracto mori: Et tamen divina virtus fecit, ut trium sociorum Danielis corpora in fornace ardente non comburerentur: ut Petrus corpore suo ambularet in mari: ut Moses & Elias sine cibo 40. dies viverent. Distinguendum est igitur inter naturae huius leges, & omnipotentiam Dei, quae nullis limitibus circumscripta, nec ad ullas naturae leges alligata est.

Etsi igitur huius mundi leges postulant, ut unum corpus sit uno alique loco, hae tamen mundi leges verbum Dei infringere non possunt, quòd adfirmat corpus Iesu Christi passim adesse, ubicunque sacra coena domini iuxta Christi institutionem administratur. Qui legibus naturae subiiciunt Deum, illos necesse est inficiari omnia miraculosa facta Dei, de quib? testatur: sacra scriptura: neque hi ullam possunt sperare salutem contra peccatum et mortem: Semper igitur in conspectu sit certissimam fidei nostrae fundamentum. Apud Deum omnia sunt possibilia. Quando ergò Deus pronunciat ac revelat aliquid, universae naturae leges eius omnipotentiae cedere coguntur.

III. Obiecto.

Caro Iesu Christi nostrae carni per omnia est similis absque peccato: Heb: 2.

At nostra caro non potest esse in multis locis, sed tantum est in uno loco.

Ergò & caro Christi tantum est in uno loco, nec potest esse ubicunque coena administratur.

Respond:

In hoc argumento aliquid dicendum nobis est, de proprietatibus et praerogativis humanae naturae Iesu Christi, idque adiuvante Spiritu Dei.

Primùm perspicùè & constanter profitemur Iesum Christum ad sumpsisse veram & naturalem carnem humanam per omnia nobis similem absque peccato: Habitu inventus est ut homo, forma servi accepta, Phili: 2. Fatemur etiam in Iesu Christo duas naturas, divinam, quae ab aeterno est, & humanam, quae ex virgine Maria nata est, non confusas neque permixtas, sed unione hypostatica unitas esse, servata cuiusque naturae essentiali proprietate. Eatemur etiam Christum tempore humiliationis, omnes infirmitates humanae carnis suscepisse absque peccato. Praeterea adfirmamus Christum sedentem ad dexteram aeterni patris retinere in omni aeternitate veram humanam carnem, cum suis essentialibus proprietabus, quibus ab essentia divina discernitur. Haec certa sunt ex testimonio Ph: 2. Ph: 3.Heb: 2.Luc: 24. Videte & palpate: Nam Spiritus carnem & ossa non habet: per omnia igitur similis est caro Christi nostrae carni, quod ad substantiae veritatem, & essentiales proprietates attinet. Hîc verò iàm quaeritur, an non Christus etiam tempore humiliationis citra carnis suae abolitionem, ea praestare potuerit corpore suo, quae excederent omnes naturae leges. Deinde quaeritur, an non sublimes praerogativas habuerit humana natura Christi prae omnium hominum carne, & propter unionem personalem cum divina natura λόγου: Et propter exaltationem eius in regno & sessionem eius ad dexteram Dei. Praeterea quaeritur, an non corpus Christi, postquam transiit ex hoc mundo ad patrem in vitam alteram, elementa & infirmitates huius seculi deposuerit citra abolitionem humanae carnis. Haec ubi iuxta Dei verbum explicata fuerint, liquidò constabit sophisma adversariorum, nihil habere virium ad impugnandam nostram confessionem, de vera praesentia corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi in sacra coena.

Ad primam ergò quaestionem quod attinet, manifestè testatur Evangelica historia, Christum etiam tempore humilitationis multa fecisse corpore suo, citra eius abolitionem, quae nostris corporibus imitari non possumus, & excedunt huius mundi non solùm leges, sed & captum: Tactu sanavit aegrotos: Voce suscitavit mortuos: 40. diebus & noctibus ieiunavit: Pedibus ambulavit in mari: Virginitate matris illaesa natus est in mundum. Etsi igitur, quo ad substantiam naturae attinet, videlicet, animae & corporis, carnis, sanguinis, ossium, &c. Nostrae carni est similis: Tamen nostra natura, quod ad virtutes, proprietates & praerogativas, non est similis per omnia carni Christi: Quare cùm sacra scriptura aliquid adseverat de carne Christi, non debemus ex nostra carne iudicium facere, num fieri id potuerit, nec ne; Sed verbo Dei omnipotentis & veracis in omni simplicitate & obedientia adsentiri.

Adhaec propter sublimem & ineffabilem unionem hypostaticam carnis Christi, eum λόγῳ aeterno Deo, multas excellentes praerogativas possidet caro Christi, quae reliquorum hominum corporibus sine idolatria & sacrilegio tribui nec potest nec debet. Fatemur quidem aperte nos sublime & arcanum mysterium incarnationis filii Dei, seu unionis personalis duarum naturarum in Christo in hac vita neque exhaurire, neque penitus perspicere posse. Neque nos ex unione personali colligimus, aut exaequationem utriusque naturae, aut alterius abolitionem, vel in alteram naturam transmutationem, vel commixtionem. Imò iuxta verbum Dei credimus, utramque naturam manere & retinere proprietates suas essentiales in omni aeternitate sine omni confusione aut divulsione. Λόγος est & manet Deus aeternus, humana natura est, & manet creatura in aeternum. Quas verò praerogativas, virtutes, & eminentias tribuit Spiritus sanctus humanae naturae Iesu Christi, propter unionem hypostaticam, eas nemo sine sacrilegio & blasphemia illi naturae Christi derogare potest. Non quidem licet nobis nostro arbitrio fingere, vel attribuere carni Christi proprietates aut gloriam. Sed intra verbi divini cancellos manendum nobis est, & hoc solum & credendum & adseverandum, quod expressa vox divina de carae Christi testatur.

De praerogativis humanae naturae Iesu Christi.

Prima ergò gloria & praerogativa carnis Iesu Christi est, quod universam Dei iram totius mundi peccatis accensam & sustinuit, & superavit, & placavit: Quod nulli homini, atque adeò nulli creaturae erat possibile. David inquit, si iniquitates observaveris Domine, Domine quis sustinebit: Universum genus humanum succumberet, si Deus totam suam iram in illud effunderet. Unde inquit, Non accendam totum aestum irae meae: Quia Deus ego sum, & non homo. Christus verò carne sua totam patris iram sustinuit. Eamque sua obedientia sedavit. Sudavit quidem sanguinem in hoc agone, & in summas angustias redactus fuit, non tamen succubuit huic oneri, sed victor gloriosus adparuit. Hanc verò virtutem & gloriam non habuit ex sese, eùm enim creatura esset, non potuisset, si sola fuisset, totam iram Dei, sustinere. Habet autem eam ex unione personali cum λόγῳ omnipotente, qui cum sibi propriam fecerit banecarnem, hoc immensum robur ei praebuit, ut ardentissimam patris iram & totam legis maledictionem superare ac vincere posset. Non enim putandum est solum naturam divinam sustinuisse & placasse iram aeterni patris. Sed tota persona Christi, Deus et homo secundum utramque naturam subiit hoc onus, et contulit in nos hoc immensum beneficium. Non potuisset autem humana natura id praestare, nisi à λόγῳ in personae unitatem adsumpta, et divino robore instructa fuisset. Hîc Paulus inquit 2. Corin: 5. Deus erat in Christo, mundum reconcilians sibi, non imputans ipsis peccata ipsorum. Et Ephes: 2. Ut reconciliaret utrosque in uno corpore Deo per crucem, interficiens inimicitiam in ipso. Rom: 5. Si enim, cùm hostes essemus, reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem filii sui, multò magis nunc reconciliati, salvabimur vita ipsius.

Haec testimonia Spiritus sancti disertè testantur, quod reconciliatio nostra cum Deo, non tantum per divinam naturam Christi, sed etiam per carnem Christi sit facta. Ac diligenter observandum est, quod Apostolus loquens de gloria & beneficio reconciliationis, non tantum loquitur in concreto, hoc est, per vocabula, quae totam personam significent, sed etiam in abstracto, hoc est, per vocabula, quae unam naturam, videlicet, carnem humanam significant. Dicit enim Christum in corpore suo reconciliasse mundum Deo. Excellit igitur caro Christi omnium hominum carnem, eminentissima hac praerogativa.

II. Secunda gloria & praerogativa carnis Christi est, quod deleat, abluat & auferat peccata ex nostra natura, & tribuat atque etiam efficiat in nobis iustitiam. Divinum planè opus est, auferre & delere peccata, & reddere atque accendere iustitiam spiritualem atque aeternam. Ego, Ego sum, inquit, Iehova, Iesa: 43. Qui deleo peccata & iniquitates vestras tanquam nubem. Propter me propter me faciam ne blasphemer. Non ergò potuisset natura humana velsola vel ex sese id efficere.

Quia verò divinae naturae unita est, hanc vim & gloriam accepit, ut & peccata abluat, & iustitiam tribuat. Non enim sola divina natura aufert peccata, & accendit iusticiam: sed etiam naturae humanae hoc ingens beneficium acceptum ferre debemus. Sacra scriptura enim Spiritus sancti ore prolata hanc gloriam tribuit carni & Sanguini Iesu Christi. 1. Ioan: 1. Sanguis Iesu Christi mundat nos ab omni peccato. Heb: 9. Si enim sanguis taurorum & hircorum & cinis vaccae aspergens immundos, sanctificabat ad carnis mundiciem: quantò magis Sanguis Christi, qui per Spiritum aeternum seipsum obtulit irreprehensibilem Deo, mundabit conscientias vestras à mortuis operibus, ad serviendum Deo viventi? Et Ro: 3. Iustificati gratis ipsius gratia, per redemptionem, quae in Iesu Christo facta est, quem proposuit propiciatorium, per fidem in sanguine ipsius. Ro: 5. Multò igitur magis iustificati in sanguine ipsius, servabimur per ipsum ab ira. Eph: 1. in quo Christo habemus redemptionem per Sanguinem ipsius, remissionem peccatorum. Haec perspicua & clara Spiritus sancti testimonia, ostendunt Carnem & sanguinem Iesu Christi hanc excellentiam & praerogativam habere, quod deleat & auferat peccata à nobis, & tribuat nobis mundiciem & iustitiam coram Deo. Non quidem ex sese, sed virtute quam accepit à λόγῳ, à quo in unam personam est adsumpta. Ac rursus observent hîc pii, quod Apostoli non solùm in concreto loquuntur, Christum hominem delere peccata, & conferre iustitiam, sed etiam in abstracto, hoc est, per vocabula, quae naturam humanam significant. Dicunt enim, Sanguis Iesu Christi mundat nos ab omni peccato: Sanguis Iesu Christi iustificat nos coram Deo. Hae sunt locutiones non in concreto, sed in abstracto, hoc est, quae disertè de humana Christi carne & sanguine loquuntur. Haec ergo divina maiestas & vis delendi peccata, & tribuendi iustitiam Spiritualem carni Iesu Christi, a λόγῳ communicata est.

III. Tertia praerogativa est, quòd caro Christi auferat mortem ex nostra natura & restituat vitam Spiritualem & aeternam: quae rursus divina est proprietas, vis & gloria. Nullus enim creaturae tanta est vis, ut mortem in homine possit destruere, & abolere, & vitam ei restituere spiritualem & aeternam. Creationis enim opus est vivificare, ut loram rex Israel testatur. Num Deus ego sum, ut possim interficere & vivificare. Et Hanna inquit, Deus deducit ad inferos & reducit, morti tradit & vivificat. At sacra scriptura spiritus sancti disertè adfirmat Carni Christi inesse hanc vim, ut tollat mortem ex nostra natura, & largiatur atque efficiat vitam sempiternam. Sic enim Christus inquit: Ioan: 6. Ego sum panis vivus, qui de coelo descendit: si quis edit ex hoc pane, vivet in aeternum: Et panis, quem ego dabo, caro mea est, quam do pro mundi vita. Item, Amen, Amen dico vobis, nisi comederitis carnem filii hominis, & biberitis ipsius sanguinem, non habetis vitam in nobis. Qui edit carnem meam, & bibit meum sanguinem, habet vitam aeternam, & ego resuscitabo eum in novissimo die. Caro enim mea verè est cibus, & sanguis meus verè est potus. Quod posset hîc dici planius de praerogativa eminentissima carnis Christi? quod nimirum divinam vim & maiestatem habeat vivificandi homines. Non enim tantum de merito, sed etiam de efficacia, adplicatione & communicatione loquitur: Nec tantum divinitati suae attribuit vim vivificandi, sed de carne sua pronunciat, quod communicet hominibus vitam aeternam: neque tantum in concreto adfirmat filium hominis vivificare alios: sed in abstracto carni suae hanc adscribit gloriam, quòd habeat vim vivificandi: quae gloria extra Christum nefas est ulli creaturae adscribere. Hinc est, quod Cyrillus & tota synodus Ephesina de carne Christi pronunciat.

Si quis non confitetur carnem Christi esse vivificam, propterea, quòd propria facta est verbi, quòd omnia vivificare potest, sit anathema. Et lib: 4. cap: 14. Quoniam igitur salvatoris caro verbo Dei, quod naturaliter vita est coniuncta, vivifica effecta est: quàndo eam comedimus, tunc vitam habemus in nobis, illi coniuncti, qua vita effecta est.

Et Theodoretus Dialo: 2. pag: 69. Corpus Christi nominamus divinum, vivificum, dominicum, docentes non esse commune alicuius hominis corpus: sed Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui est Deus & homo.

Haec admodum illustris est praerogativa carnis Christi, siquidem divinae maiestatis & potentiae est, vivificare homines mortuos, & quidem aeternam communicare vitam. Nec verò tantùm ita communicata est haec gloria & maiestas homini Christo, ut tantum liceat in concreto adfirmare hominem Christum praeditum esse potentia vivificandi: Sed etiam in abstracto, loquuntur & scriptura & sancti patres carnem Iesu Christi esse vivificam.

Unde manifestissimum est diversa esse genera communicationis & idiomatum & maiestatis. Nam quaedam idiomata sic communicantur naturae alteri, ut non liceat in abstracto, sed tantum in concreto ista efferre. Ut cùm rectè dicatur Deus est passus, mortuus, crucifixus: Deus esurivit: Item, Homo Christus est ab aeterno, Homo Christus est Deus, Homo Christus condidit coelum & terram. Non tamen fas est dicere, Divinitas est passa, mortua, crucifixa. Divinitas esurivit: Item, Humanitas Christi est ab aeterno, Humanitas Christi est deitas, Humanitas Christi condidit coelum & terram. Hae enim phrases veram naturarum in Christo distinctionem confunderent, & Eutychianismum reducerent. Aliud verò genus communicationis est, cum divina natura λόγῳ. sic impertit divinam suam vim, gloriam, maiestatem, proprietatem, carni adsumptae, ut non solum liceat in concreto, verumetiam in abstracto ista enunciare, ut quod λόγος, qui vivificat omnia & vim vivificandi possidet ab aeterno, ita impertit carni suae hanc vim & maiestatem, ut liceat nobis secundum sacram scripturam dicere. Caro Iesu Christi est vivifica. Corpus Iesu Christi est vivificum & confert mundo salutem. Horribilis igitur caecitas, impietas, & inscitia est velle carnis Christi proprietates ex reliquorum corporum humanorum infirmitate metiri: Et carnem Christi sua spoliare gloria & maiestate, qua illam λόγος in personali adsumptione exornavit.

IIII: Quarta praerogativa est, quòd humana Christi natura frangit & destruit totum Satanae & inferni regnum: Quod certè nullus alioquin homo purus praestare potuisset. Est enim horribilis Satanae potentia & quidem tanta ut scriptura vocet eum dominum mundi, & Deum huius seculi. Et ingens multitudo est immundorum Spirituum. Atque ideò mediatorem nostrum oportebat esse Deum omnipotentem, ut superior esset Satana, & certam vos spem victoriae contra tam immanem tyrannum haberemus. Superavit autem Christus Satanam, & contrivit totum serpentis caput, non solùm ut Deus, verumetiam ut homo. Nam λόγος omnipotens hoc ingens robur contulit carni suae adsumptae à se in unitatem personae, ut praevaleat Satanae, & destruat omnia opera eius. Unde in prima promissione dicitur. Semen mulieris conteret caput serpentis. Quasi dicat scriptura verae caro humana franget totam Satanae potentiam, & liber abit genus humanum. Non quidem sola, neque ex sese caro contrivit caput serpentis: Sed caro Iesu Christi personaliter unita deitati λόγου, et divinum robur à λόγῳ accipiens, fuit victor Satanae, & destruxit eius tyrannidem. Quod etiam in promissionibus significacum est. 2. Samuel: 7: Excitabo semen tuum post te, quod egredietur de utero tuo, & firmabo regnum eius. Humanam Christi carnem nominat semen Davidis. Quod promittit firmum fore regnum huius seminis, ostendit carnem Christi victricem fore Satanae, & inferni & omnium hostium nostrorum. Item, Psalm 132. De fructu ventris tui, olio tuo imponam. Ergò caro Christi licet vera sit caro, tamen obtinet praerogativam, quae nullius hominis corpori in toto terrarum orbe tribui potest.

V. Quinta gloria & praerogativa est, quod caro Iesu Christi, simul cum divinitate effundit in credentes Spiritum sanctum, & sanctificat eos. Haec tanta gloria est, ut sine impietate non possit ea ulli creaturae attribut. Cum enim Spiritus sanctus sit aeternus Deus & dominus omnium creaturarum, non mittitur, nec datur ab ulla creatura. Humana autem natura ad umpta à λόγῳ ad hanc gloriam & maiestatem evecta est, ut simul cum divinitate Christi impertiat donum Spiritus sancti fide libus. Ut enim sanguine suo meruit nobis hoc donum: Ita & facultatem & gloriam accepit Spiritum impertiendi. Christus ex morte resuscitatus adflat Apostolos suos & dicit. Accipite Spiritum sanctum.

Cum hoc suo halitu manante ex pectore eius sanctissimo verè dedit Spiritum sanctum, & testatum fecit humanam suam naturam hac praerogativa praeditam esse, impertiendi Spiritum sanctum fidelibus. Unde & Petrus. Act: 2. inquit: Postquam dextera Dei exaltatus est & promissionem Spiritus accepit à Patre, effudit illud, quod videtis. Quia loquitur de exaltatione Christi, certum est quod eius humanam naturam significet. Divina enim exaltata non est, sed ab aeterno fuit in sublimi maiestate. Humana autem natura perfecto opere nostrae redemptionis adscendit ad coelos, & ad dexteram aeterni patris collocata est. Hanc naturam humanam in Christo exaltatam dextera Dei, dicit Apostolus Petrus accepisse promissionem Spiritus, hoc est, promissum Spiritum sanctum à patre, eumque visibili specie effudisse in Apostolos. Ac sanè Christus ipse fatetur, nisi iverit ad patrem, id est, nisi sanguinem suum effuderit pro mundo, & per mortem ad patrem transiverit, non venturum esse Spiritum sanctum: Si verò iverit tum se missurum eum. Docet igitur & se morte sua impetrasse nobis & meruisse Spiritum sanctum, Et humanam suam naturam hanc gloriam possidere, ut impertiat Spiritum sanctum fidelibus. Non quidem procedit Spiritus sanctus de carne vel humana Christi natura. Spiritus sanctus enim est ab aeterno omnipotens Deus: Humana verò natura Christi est & manet creatura in utero Mariae virginis condita à Spiritu sancto atque à tota Trimtate. Mittitur autem & donatur ab humana Christi natura à λόγῳ in personae unitatatem adsumpta. Quod & Ioannes Baptista innuit: Cùm inquit: Ego Baptizo vos aqua: Post me autem venit qui prior me est, is Baptizabit vos igne & Spiritu sancto.

VI. Sexta praerogativa carnis Christi, quod est Caput totius Ecclesiae, passim per totum terrarumorbem dispersae, quae omnibus aetatibus ministerio verbi colligitur, quod fovet, sustentat, custodit, regit, conservat, & tuetur singula membra & omnia in omnibus adimplet atque efficit. Haec quoque gloria & proprietas nulli creaturae convenit. Nullius Apostolus Propheta toti Ecclesiae, & singulis membris adesse potest: Nullus etiam angelus singulis piis opem ferre, omnia pericula depellere, in omni necessitate succurrere potest. Christi autem humanitas, quia unita est Logo unione personali, & quia constituta est caput totius Ecclesiae, omnibus membris sui corporis adest, singulos pios fovet suo Spiritu, sustentat, regit, defendit, arcet omnia pericula, suppeditat omnia necessaria. Praesentes & in sua manu habet omnes creaturas, & implet omnia. Sic enim amplissima & dulcissima eius habet promissio: Ubicunque duo aut tres congregati sunt in nomine meo, in medio ipsorum sum, Matth: 18. Et Matth: ult: Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consumationem seculi.

Etsi autem hae promissiones sint in concreto enunciatae, siquidem inquit: Ego Christus Deus & homo ero vobiscum: Tamen fingendum non est, quod tantum divinitatis suae praesentia nobis promiserit, sed totius personae, atque etiam carnis suae, licet eam externis sensibus non comprehendimus. Ac ne de carnis eius praesentia dubitaremus, sacro sanctam coenam instituit, in qua cum pane dat nobis corpus suum manducandum & eam vino benedictum sanguinem suum bibendum, tanquam evidentissimam & infallibile argumentum, quod perpetuò adsit suae Ecclesiae totus Christus, Deus & homo. Et Paulus Eph: 1 & 4. Cum testatur Christum omnia implere & de humana eius natura significanter loquitur & veram eius in tota Ecclesia praesentia demonstrat. Sic enim inquit, Omnia subiecit pedibus eius, & ipsum dedit caput super omnia Ecclesiae, quae est corpus eius, plenitudo eius, qui omnia in omnibus implet. De carne Christi loqui Apostolum manifestum est: Quia dicit Deus excitavit Iesum à mortuis & collocavit eum in dextera sua. Nemo autem adeò imperitus est, ut putet divinitatem à mortuis esse resuscitatam. Addit Paulus ut gloriam coelestem Iesu Christi de scribat, omnia subiecit pedibus eius. Ergò omnes creaturae etiam humanae naturae Christi resuscitatae à mortuis sunt praesentes & subiectae. Et quia caput est totius Ecclesiae, necesse est eam praesentem adesse singulis membris. Praeterea inquit eum omnia in omnibus adimplere, hoc est, Christum non tantum operari in omnibus fidelibus sed etiam in iis praesentem esse ac habitare, & salutem aeternam impertiri, sic & quarto Cap: inquit: Qui descendit, idem & adscendit, supra omnes coelos, ut omnia impleret. Paulum de natura humana λόγῳ adsumpta loqui, nemo negare potest. Divinitas enim, nec descendit, nec adscendit. Adfirmat autem Apostolus hunc Christum, qui supra omnes coelos adscendit omnia adimplere, nec tantum de eius operatione velefficacia loquitur, sed ipsius praesentia. Ideò inquit adscendit supra omnes coelos ut omnia impleret. Quomodo haec fieri possint ut humana Christi natura, quae finita est, omnia impleat, nostris ingeniis comprehendere non possumus: Sicut nec de divinitate capere aut intelligere possumus, quomodo ea impleat omnia, nulla enim moles, nulla extensio hic imaginanda est. Quia verò Spiritus sanctus haec mysteria in Ecclesia per Apostolos patefecit, omninò et adsentiri debemus.

VII. Septima praerogativa humanae naturae Christi est, quod est omniscia, omnia videt & novit, & intelligit gemitus cordium nostrorum. Paulus enim expresse inquit omnes thesauros sapientiae & cognitionis in Christo reconditos esse Coloss. 1. Non solum divinitati λόγου, sed Christo toti personae tribuitur, quod omnes sapientiae thesauri in ipso sint reconditi. Et discipuli post coenae institutionem loquentes cum domino inquiunt. Ecce nunc apertè loqueris & proverbium nullum dicis, nunc scimus te scire omnia, nec opus esse tibi, ut quis te interroget. Non solum divinitati tribuunt hanc gloriam omniscientiae, exclusa carne Christi, sed huic Iesu Christo homini hanc gloriam dant, quod sciat omnia. Item, Ioan: 21. Cùm tertiò rogatus esset Petrus, respondet, Iesu Domine, tu omnia nosti: tu scis quod amem te. Loquitur Petrus cum Christo, quem coram videt humana carne indutum, & à mortuis resuscitatum, & diserte adfirmat hunc hominem Iesum omnia scire, tam futura, quàm praesentia. Neque refellit hoc Iesus, sed adprobat piam eius confessionem. Ac cùm Ecclesia carnem Christi simul cum λόγῳ adoret & in omni necessitate invocet, necesse est ei omniscientiam et scrutationem cordium nostrorum tribuere: alioqui invocatio esset irrita. Frustra enim invocatur, qui nostros gemitus & necessitates ignorat, quas saepe ne exponere quidem possumus. Quod vero in Luca dicitur Iesus crescebat aetate & sapientia, non derogat humanae Christi naturae omniscientiam. Nam Spiritus sanctus in eo loco ostendit, quod Christus omnes infirmitates carnis absque peccato ad sumpserit. Non statim perfectus vir natus est, sed parvulus infans: Et tamen erat Deus omnipotens. Non ostendit statim divinam suam sapientiam in infantia, sed paulatim magis magisque fulsit hoc lumen divinae sapientiae in ipso, ut doceret se verum esse hominem per omnia similem nobis absque peccato. Paulus dicit, Christum iudicaturum etiam arcanas cordium cogitationes, in die adventus sui: At certum est non solum divinam, sed & humanam Christi naturam iudicaturam vivos & mortuos, sicuti Christus testatur. Pater omne iudicium filio dedit: proptera quod est filius hominis Ioan: 5. Necesse est igitur Christum etiam secundum humanitatem introspicere omnium hominum corda, gemitus, consilia, cogitationes et desideria. Scriptura quidem in concreto loquitur, cum Christo omnium rerum scientiam tribuit: sed non obscure simul ostendit etiam in abstracto, hoc est, per vocabula, quae humanam naturam significant hanc praerogativam & gloriam rectè enunciare. Secundum humanam enim naturam iudicabit omnium hominum cogitationes & adfectus: Ergò & secundum humanam naturam videt & intelligit omnia.

VIII. Octava praerogativa est, quod humana Christi natura unita λόγῳ accepit omnem potestatem in coelo & in terra, ac verè est omnipotens, quae gloria & maiestas alioqui soli & omnipotenti Deo competit. Etsi magna est potentia angelorum & spirituum in coelo: nullius tamen angeli infinita est potestas. At Iesus Christus secundum humanitatem, quae verbo est unita, accepit hanc gloriam & maiestatem, ut omnia illisubiecta sint, quod sacra scriptura in multis locis testatur. Matth. ult; inquit Christus. Data est mihi omnis potestas in coelo & interra. Omnis potestas certe immensa et infinita est potentia. Hanc non accepit in tempore secundum divinam suam essentiam: sed λόγος possedit eam ab omni aeternitate. Squidem eiusdem essentiae & potentiae est cum patre ab omni aeternitate, secundum humanitatem autem non perpetuo hanc obtinuit gloriam, sed data illi est in tempore. Ac omnia quae sacra scriptura dicit Christum in tempore accepisse, humanae eius naturae collata esse intelligendum est. Humana ergo natura accepit omnem potestatem. Ioannes Baptista inquit. Pater diligit filium & omnia dedit in manus eius. Ioan: 3. Non tantum divinitati, sed & humanae Christi naturae omnia dedit pater. Sic & Psal: 8. Sivisti cum paulisper indigere Deo, sed gloria & honore coronasti eum: omnia subiecisti sub pedibus eius, oves, boves & pecora campi. Manifestum est prophetam non loqui tantum de natura divina Christi, cui pater omnia subiecit: Sed etiam de carne Christi. Nam dicit Christum paulisper fuisse desertum à Deo: Hoc certè de carne Christi intelligi necesse est, mox addit gloria & honore coronasti eum: Et omnia subiecisti sub pedibus eius. Ergò & humanae Christi carni omnia sunt subiecta. Certè Christus etiam iuxta humanitatem est custos & defensor suae Ecclesiae in omnibus locis & omnibus temporibus, & in omni periculo & necessitate. Quomodo poterit autem Christus secundum humanitatem omnia depellere pericula, ex omnibus nos eripere necessitatibus contra omnes tueri hostes, & omnia largiri bona, si non est omnipotens etiam iuxta humanitatem? Sanè gubernatio, defensio, & custodia totius Ecclesiae omnipotentiam requirit. Iesus Christus non tontum secundum divinitatem, sed etiam iuxta humanitatem iudicaturus est universum mundum: Quod sanè sine omnipotentia fieri non potest. Qui enim non introspicit omnium hominum consilia, cogitationes, gemitus, fidem veram ab hypocrisi potest discernere, nec omnes creaturas in suae habet potestate, quomodo is totum mundam & omnes animas iudicare, & iudicii sui sententiam, quae in omni aeternitate valitura est, exequi potest? Paulus dicit Christum resuscitatum ex morte, constitutum esse super omne nomen, quod nominari potest, non solum in hoc sed & in futuro seculo: Quis ergò nomen & gloriam omnipotentiae derogare humanae Christi naturae audebit? Veteres Ecclesiae scriptores ex his ipsis fontibus sacrae scripturae non dubitarunt in abstracto carni Christi tribuere omnipotentiam.
