Moreover, this salutary proof consists in true and serious repentance or conversion to God: of which there are two parts. The former is contrition and sorrow for committed sins: truly and without hypocrisy you ought to acknowledge yourself to bear an unclean nature, which is entirely at variance with the divine law: And that you are contaminated with infinite sins, by which you have provoked the wrath of God and have deserved punishments of every kind and eternal damnation. You ought to dread seriously the severe judgment of God: And with a true groan of the heart to grieve that you have provoked the wrath of the most holy God: And from the soul to detest sin. This movement of the heart God requires in the promise. As I live, I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he may be converted and live. Item, be converted to me and I will be converted to you. The other part of conversion is faith or trust in the mediator, by which we embrace the promise of grace, and we determine that we have the remission of sins and are reconciled to God through the death of the son of God Jesus Christ, and are gifted freely with the Holy Spirit and eternal life, according to those sayings: To him all the Prophets bear witness that all who believe in him receive the remission of sins in his name: Acto: 10 He who believes in this Jesus is just. Act: 14. Item, He who believes in the son, has eternal life. Therefore, he who by this faith or trust raises himself in the terrors of a conscience recognizing its own baseness and fearing the judgment of God, he is truly reconciled, and thus can worthily approach the table of the Lord. He who believes in the son, says Christ, is not judged. Item, He who sees the son and believes in him, who sent me, shall not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life. Therefore, there is no reason for him who is endowed with faith to fear that he eats and drinks judgment to himself. But with this faith, sins that devastate the conscience are never joined; which Paul names the works of the flesh, when men indulge the affections of the flesh and fulfill them in deed. Paul says: Fight the good fight, keeping faith and a good conscience. Likewise, the sum of the commandment is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and faith unfeigned. These sayings testify that those who labor with an evil conscience and retain the will and purpose of sinning are destitute of true faith. For faith is a movement of the soul resisting the sorrow which we conceive on account of sin committed. Therefore, he who does not truly grieve for sin, but persists in it and proceeds securely, cannot have faith. Faith, says Bernard, is a consolation; he does not need consolation who rejoices when he has done evil and exults in the worst things. Therefore, the purpose of sinning must be utterly cast away: Sins are not to be excused: Nor is the judgment of God to be mocked, so that you acknowledge some sins and defend others, but you ought to acknowledge and cast away all sins which are accused by divine law and are manifest to your conscience from the word of God. Practicing usury, fostering hatreds, unjustly possessing the property of others, against conscience, errors fighting against the word of God pertinaciously defending after admonition, indulging in drinking bouts and lusts, without any doubt is devoid of true contrition and sincere faith. Therefore if such a one approaches the Eucharist, he eats and drinks judgment to himself.

Let no one therefore flatter himself in his sins, but let each one examine and test himself according to the law of God, whether he bears a conscience burdened with mortal sins: Which if he has noticed, let him immediately cast them away, and seriously do penance for them and return into favor with God. For whatever our sins may have been, if we approach God seriously in the true fear of God, and in confidence of the mediator, we obtain forgiveness, and are deemed by God worthy to eat the body and drink the blood of Jesus Christ. If your sins shall have been as scarlet, they shall become white as snow. Isa: 1. Item: Where sin abounded, there grace did superabound; Rom: 5. Item: Come to me all you who labor and are burdened, I will refresh you: Matt: 11. Although those who are seriously doing penance, and grasping with confidence all the benefits of the mediator, feel that great weakness, impure motions, trembling of faith, much security, and doubts remain in them: They ought not however on that account to determine that they are unworthy of the Eucharist. For the Lord has taken up the weak; Nor can we all infirmities in this life lay aside. And therefore this holy supper was instituted, so that God might succor our infirmity, increase His gifts in us, and daily sanctify us more and more. Therefore, in order that we may worthily receive the body and blood of Christ in the holy supper, it is sufficient for this if we are free from sins that devastate the conscience: Let us flee security and diffidence: But let us be instructed with a true, not feigned, confidence, leaning upon the merit and promise of the Mediator.

Latin:

CAPUT VII. Quomodo Christiani Sese Probare & Praeparare Debeant, Ad Salutarem Sumptionem Coenae Domini.

Haec magni momenti quaestio est, fulmen enim est tristissimum, quod Paulus dicit indignè manducantes de hoc pane, & indignè bibentes de hoc calice reos fieri corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi. Ac ostendit Deum gravissimas poenas infligere illis qui securè & sine probatione sui accedunt ad mensam domini. Itaque omnes seriò adhortatur, ut sese probent sive explorent & sic de hoc pane edant, & de hoc calice bibant. Salutaris autem haec probatio consistit in vera & seria poenitentia seu conversione ad Deum: Cuius duae sunt partes. Prior est contritio et dolor de admissis peccatis: Verè & sine hypocrisi agnoscere debes te immundam gerere naturam, quae tota discrepat à lege divina: Et te infinitis peccatis contaminatum esse, quibus iram Dei provocasti & omnis generis supplicia & aeternam damnationem es meritus. Expavescere debes seriò severum Dei iudicium: Et vero gemitu cordis dolere quod sanctissimi Dei iram provocaveris: Ac ex animo detestari peccatum. Hunc motum cordis requirit Deus in promissione. Vivo ego nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat. Item, convertimini ad me & ego convertar ad vos. Altera pars conversionis est fides seu fiducia in mediatorem, qua amplectimur promissionem gratiae, & statuimus nos habere remissionem, peccatorum et esse reconciliatos Deo per mortem filii Dei Iesu Christi, ac donari gratis Spiritu sancto & vita aeterna, iuxta illa dicta: Huic omnes Prophetae testimonium perhibent accipere omnes remissionem peccatorum in nomine ipsius quotquot credunt in eum: Acto: 10 In hunc Iesum qui credit iustus est. Act: 14. Item, Qui credit in filium, habet vitam aeternam. Hac ergò fide seu fiducia, qui sese erigit in pavoribus conscientiae agnoscentis suam turpitudinem & metuentis iudicium Dei, is verè reconciliatus est, atque ita dignè accedere potest admensam Domini. Qui credit in filium inquit Christus, non iudicatur. Item, Qui videt filium & credit in eum, qui misit me, in iudicium non veniet, sed à morte in vitam transivit. Non est ergò quod metuat is, qui fide est praeditus, ne sibi edat & bibat iudicium. Cum hac verò fide nunquam coniuncta sunt peccata vastantia conscientiam; Quae Paulus nominat opera carnis, cum homines adfectibus carnis indulgent & eos opere complent. Paulus inquit: Milita bonam militiam servans fidem & bonam conscientiam. Item, summa mandati est dilectio ex puro corde conscientia bona & fide non simulata. Haec dicta testantur, eos qui mala conscientia laborant & retinent voluntatem & propositum peccandi destitui vera fide. Nam fides est motus animi repugnans dolori, quem propter admissum peccatum concipimus. Is ergò qui non verè dolet de peccato, sed in eo persistit & securè pergit, fidem habere non potest. Fides, inquit Bernhardus, solatium est, non eget ille solatio qui laetatur cum malefecerit & exultat in rebus pessimis. Prorsus igitur abiiciendum est propositum peccandi: Non sunt excusanda peccata: Nec illudendum est iudicio Dei, ita ut alia agnoscas peccata, alia defendas, sed omnia peccata quae divina lege accusantur & conscientiae tuae ex verbo Dei manifesta sunt agnoscere & abiicere debes. Usuras exercens, odia fovens, res alienas iniustè possidens, contra conscientiam, errores pugnantes cum verbo Dei pertinaciter defendens post admonitionem, potationibus & libidinibus indulgens, citra omnem dubitationem est expers verae contritionis & fidei syncerae. Itaque si talis accesserit ad Eucharistiam, edit & bibit sibi iudicium.

Nemo ergo blandiatur sibi in suis peccatis, sed quisque se examinet & probet iuxta legem Dei, num gerat conscientiam gravatam peccatis mortalibus: Quae si animadverterit statim abiiciat ea, & seriò de iis poenitentiam agat & cum Deo redeat ingratiam. Qualiacunque enim fuerint peccata nostra si seriò in vero timore Dei, & fiducia mediatoris accedimus ad Deum, impetramus condonationem, & censemur à Deo digni ad manducandum corpus & bibendum sanguinem Iesu Christi. Si peccata vestra fuerint veluti coccinum, quasi nix dealbescent. Ies: 1. Item: Ubi abundavit peccatum, ibi super abundavit gratia; Rom: 5. Item: Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis & onerati estis ego reficiam vos: Matth: 11. Esti verò seriò poenitentiam agentes, & fiducia adprehendentes omnia mediatoris beneficia, sentiunt in se magnam restare imbecillitatem, impuros motus, trepidationem fidei, multum securitatis, & dubitationum: Non tamen propterea statuere debent se indignos esse Eucharistia. Infirmos enim dominus adsumpsit; Nec possumus omnes infirmitates in hac vita deponere. Atque ideò instituta est haec sacra coena, ut nostrae infirmitati succurrat Deus, dona sua in nobis augeat & quotidie nos magis magisque sanctificet. Ut ergò dignè percipiamus corpus & sanguinem Christi in sacra coenae, adhoc sufficit si immunes simus à peccatis vastantibus conscientiam: Fugiamus securitatem & diffidentiam: Instructi autem simus vera non simulata fiducia, nitente Mediatoris merito & promissione.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper: Chapter VIII
CHAPTER VIII.

Who are to be admitted to the holy communion, and who are to be warded off from it.

It is not placed in the judgment of any man to either distribute or deny the body and blood of Jesus Christ to any man. For it is not the benefit of a man, whether a monarch or an apostle, but of the omnipotent and only-begotten Son of God. Therefore, it is to be distributed according to His own command and will. Christ, however, offers consolation and all the benefits of His kingdom to those who labor and thirst for salvation. Come, He says, to Me all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you. He repels, however, from Himself all who are secure, impenitent, and in sins rushing against conscience. Depart, he says, from me all you who work iniquity Matth: 7. according to this will of Christ, therefore, the Lord's Supper is to be distributed, and the whole ministry of the Gospel is to be administered. Therefore, to all who show signs of true repentance, acknowledge themselves to be sinners according to the law, and give a confession of their faith that they acquiesce in the promise of the Gospel, the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ is to be distributed, without any respect of persons. Drink from this all, says Christ: Christ entices and calls to himself all who thirst for salvation. We are all one body, says Paul: and we all partake of one body. It is not for the pastor or minister of the Church to judge who are endowed with sincere faith and who simulate faith. For God alone is the searcher of hearts. It ought to be enough for the pastor that he notices signs of repentance and hears a pious confession from him who is about to approach the holy synaxis. But those whom he discovers to be impenitent, secure, and atheists, such as those who either stubbornly defend errors conflicting with the foundation of the faith, or petulantly persist in manifest crimes, or proudly excuse their sins, or insult and heap abuse upon the ministry of the Gospel in mockery, them he must exclude from the communion of the Lord's Supper without any deliberation and hesitation. it is owed. For the command of Christ is expressed, do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not cast your pearls before swine. Matth: 7. Item, Do not bear the yoke with unbelievers. For what communication has light with darkness? What agreement has Christ with Belial? What part has the faithful with the infidel? Take away the evil, he says, from among yourselves. 2. Cor: 6. Item, Do not communicate with the sins of others. 1. Timoth: 5. These sayings testify that a pastor sins most gravely against the command of Christ, and provokes the severe wrath of God upon himself, who knowingly and willingly imparts the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ to a man, of whose impenitence and crimes he is certainly aware against his conscience. Ezech: 13. God says. Woe to you Prophets who kill the souls which you ought not to give to death, and give life to the souls to whom you ought not to promise life: who afflict the heart of the just with a lie, and strengthen the hands of the wicked so that he does not turn back from his evil way.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Qui admittendi sint ad sacram synaxin, qui verò ab ea arcendi.

Non est in ullius hominis arbitrio positum, ut vel distribuat vel deneget ulli hominum corpus & Sanguinem Iesu Christi. Non enim hominis vel Monarchae vel Apostoli, sed omnipotentis & unigeniti filii Dei beneficium est. Itaque iuxta ipsius mandatum & voluntatem distribuendum est. Offert autem Christus consolationem & omnia regni sui beneficia laborantibus & sitientibus salutem. Venite inquit ad me omnes qui laboratis & onerati estis, ego reficiam vos. Repellit vetò à se omnes securos, impoenitentes & in peccata contra conscientiam ruentes. Discedite inquit à me omnes qui operamini iniquitatem Matth: 7. iuxta hanc ergò Christi voluntatem distribuenda est coena Domini, & totum ministerium Evangelii administrandum. Omnibus ergò qui signa ostendunt verae poenitentiae, agnoscunt se esse peccatores iuxta legem: edunt & fidei suae confessionem quod acquiescant in promissione Evangelii, distribuendum est corpus & Sanguis Domini nostri Iesu Christi, sine omni respectu personarum. Bibite ex hoc omnes inquit Christus: Omnes salutem sitientes allicit & ad se vocat Christus. Omnes inquit Paulus unum corpus sumus: & omnes de uno corpore participamus. Qui syncera fide sint praediti, qui verò simulent fidem, pastoris aut ministri Ecclesiae non est diiudicare. Nam solus Deus est scrutator cordium. Satis esse debet pastori, quod signa poenitentiae animadvertit & piam audit confessionem ab eo qui ad sacram synaxin est accessurus. Quos verò deprehendit impoenitentes, securos & Atheos, ut qui vel errores pugnantes cum fundamento fidei pertinaciter defendunt, vel in manifestis sceleribus petulanter pergunt, vel peccata sua superbè excusant, vel ministerio Evangelii per ludibrium insultant & convitia faciunt, eos sine omni deliberatione & dubitatione à communicatione coenae Domini arcere debet. Expressum est enim Christi mandatum, nolite sanctum dare canibus, & ne proiicite margaritas ante porcos. Matth: 7. Item, Nolite iugum ducere cum infidelibus. Quae enim communicatio est Luci cum tenebris? Quae convenientia Christi & Belial? Quam partem habet fidelis cum infideli? Auferte malum inquit ex vobis ipsis. 2. Cor: 6. Item, Ne communices alienis peccatis. 1. Timoth: 5. Haec dicta testantur pastorem gravissimè delinquere contra mandatum Christi, & severam Dei iram in se provocare, qui sciens & volens impertit corpus & sanguinem Domini nostri Iesu Christi homini, de cuius impoenitentia & sceleribus contra conscientiane certò illi constat. Ezech: 13. Deus inquit. Vae vobis Prophetis qui interficitis animas, quas neci dare non debebatis, & vivificatis animas, quibus vitam promittere non debebatis: qui moerore adficitis cor iusti mendacio, & roboratis manus impii quo minus revertatur à via sua mala.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper: Chapter IX
CHAPTER IX.

Causes which ought to move the pious, so that they frequently use the supper of the Lord.

I. It is not an indifferent matter, which is permitted to our own judgment, so that it is permitted to us with impunity either to use the Lord's Supper, or to abstain from it. Indeed, our Lord Jesus Christ strictly commanded that all who have given their name to Christ, and expect salvation from Him, should frequently partake of the Lord's Supper. Take, eat (He says), As often as you do this, do it in remembrance of me, Drink from this all of you: As often as you do this you will proclaim the death of the Lord. Therefore, they sin most gravely and provoke the wrath of God against themselves, who neglect the use of the Lord's Supper. For they contumaciously oppose themselves to the sublime command of the Son of God, and proudly despise the most wholesome means by which Christ wills to work salvation in us, and to increase the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

The second cause is the dignity of the sacrament, and the magnitude of the treasure which is offered to us in the sacred supper. Among all creatures that are in heaven and on earth, there is nothing more excellent, nothing more precious than the most holy body and Blood of Jesus Christ, which body was conceived of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin Mary, λόγῳ joined to the eternal God by personal union, and placed at the right hand of the eternal Father in sublime majesty above all creatures. By this body and Blood of Christ, salvation was obtained for the world: In this body dwells the fullness of the divinity. When, therefore, the Son of God bestows upon us His body and His Blood in the sacred supper, He bestows upon us a greater and more excellent good, than if He were to give us heaven and earth. And indeed He bestows upon us things to eat and to drink, so that He Himself may dwell in us, impart life to us, make us temples of the Holy Spirit, and unite us most closely with God. And by this huge pledge He makes it testified to us that all our sins have been forgiven us, that the eternal Father has been reconciled to us, and that all the benefits of His kingdom have been sealed for us. Therefore it was fitting for us to seek this immense treasure with huge desire, to receive it when offered with a most ready mind, and to use it frequently.

The third cause is our huge weakness and inevitable necessity. The only-begotten Son of God, Jesus Christ, procured salvation for the whole world by the shedding of His Blood; He appeased the wrath of the Father, He took away the curse of the law: He broke the empire of Satan and of death: and He merited for us the kingdom of heaven. And these goods He most liberally offers to us in the word: which the divine majesty even establishes with an oath. But our hearts are so narrow and prone to flight, that we do not even apply sufficiently firm faith to God as He swears. From time to time doubts recur concerning the will of God toward us: from time to time we grow faint in temptations. And at a light moment of human events we are cast down from the step of faith. Nor does Satan cease to construct snares for us, so that he may snatch from us the shield of faith. For this reason, we are in every way in need of this salutary medicine of the soul, that is to say, the body and blood of Jesus Christ, so that our weak hearts may be fortified, and our faith strengthened, so that we may be able to receive the various assaults of Satan, and overcome the enemy.

Fourth. Nor is the utility of this immense good only one, but they are manifold. First, the utility is great, because it brings with it the remission of sins. For he who receives the blood of Christ by faith, certainly receives the remission of sins: For the blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin. Then it seals for us the promise of grace and renders the conscience tranquil. Thirdly, it applies to us individually all the benefits of the mediator: Fourthly, Christ vivifies and sanctifies us with his body: and increases in us his spiritual gifts, the knowledge of God, fear, trust, joy, patience, desire for eternal life, constancy, zeal, and the like. Fifthly, it joins us most closely with Christ: Inasmuch as he dwells in us and we in him. Sixthly, it fortifies us against all the snares and darts of Satan. Seventhly, it shows us the certain hope of the resurrection of our bodies. These manifold utilities ought to inflame us, so that we may frequently and with ardent desire make use of the supper of the Lord.

Fifth cause, that we may publicly declare our confession, of which Church we are citizens: And that we may not by our example invite others to the frequent use of the Lord's Supper.

Sixth. That we may avoid the most grave punishments, which God is accustomed to send upon those who proudly and contumaciously despise the use of the Lord's Supper. For God threatens most grave punishments to the despisers of the most holy ministry and sacraments. Because you have rejected knowledge (He says in Hosea) I also will reject you: Item: Because I called, and no one listened, I also will laugh in your calamity. Prov: 1. Item: God will send a famine, not of bread, but of hearing the word of God. Item: God will send the efficacy of error, that they may believe a lie, that all may be judged who do not believe the truth. And sacred scripture is full of such threats, which denounce the horrible wrath of God to the despisers of the ministry and Sacraments. And very many examples of the wrath of God are almost daily before our eyes. For the despisers of the Lord's Supper are punished with blindness and madness, they are delivered into a reprobate mind, so that they repeatedly heap up sins, their impenitent heart is hardened, and at length when in the agony of death they seek consolation through the Lord's Supper, they are suddenly overwhelmed by the judgment of God, so that they can neither perform repentance nor enjoy the most salutary medicine of the Lord's Supper.

Latin:

CAPUT IX.

Causae quae pios movere debent, ut crebrò usurpent coenam Domini.

I. Non est res media, quae nostro arbitrio permissa sit, ut nobis impunè liceat vel uti coena Domini, vel ab ea abstinere. Quin severè mandavit Dominus noster Iesus Christus, ut singuli qui nomen dederunt Christo, et ab ipso salutem expectant frequenter usurpent coenam Domini. Accipite, edite (inquit) Quotiescunque hoc feceritis, in meam commemorationem facite, Bibite ex hoc omnes: Quotiescunque hoc feceritis mortem Domini annunciabitis. Gravissimè igitur peccant & iram Dei adversus ipsos provocant, qui negligunt usum coenae Domini. Contumaciter enim sese opponunt sublimi mandato filii Dei, & superbè aspernantur media saluberrima, quibus Christus salutem in nobis operari, & dona Spiritus sancti augere vult.

Secunda causa est dignitas sacramenti, & magnitudo thesauri, qui nobis in sacra coena offertur. Inter omnes creaturas quae sunt in coelo & in terra nihil est praestabilius, nihil preciosius quam sanctissimum corpus & Sanguis Iesu Christi, quod corpus de Spiritu sancto in utero virginis Mariae conceptum, λόγῳ aeterno Deo, unione personali copulatum, & ad dexteram aeterni patris in sublimi maiestate supra omnes creaturas collocatum est. Hoc corpore & Sanguine Christi, parta est mundo salus: In hoc corpore habitat plenitudo divinitatis. Cùm ergò filius Dei in sacra coena largitur nobis suum corpus & suum Sanguinem, maius et praestabilius bonum nobis largitur, quam si coelum & terram nobis donaret. Et quitem ad manducandum & bibendum largitur nobis, ut ipse in nobis habitet, impertiat nobis vitam, faciat nos templa Spiritus sancti, & arctissimè cum Deo copulet. Atque hoc ingenti pignore testatum nobis facit, omnia nostra peccata nobis condonata, patrem aeternum nobis reconciliatum, & omnia regni sui beneficia nobis obsignata esse. Itaque decebat nos ingenti desiderio hunc immensum thesaurum expetere, oblatum promptissimo animo suscipere, & crebrò usurpare.

Tertia causa est ingens nostra imbecillitas & inevitabilis necessitas. Unigenitus Dei filius Iesus Christus universo mundo peperit salutem effusione sui Sanguinis; placavit iram patris, sustulit legis maledictionem: fregit Satanae & mortis imperium: & promeruit nobis regnum coelorum. Atque haec bona liberalissimè offert nobis in verbo: quod etiam iureiurando divina maiestas stabilit. Verùm adeo angusta & ad sugam prona sunt nostra pectora, ut ne quidem Deo iuranti satis firmam fidem adhibeamus. Subinde recurrunt dubitationes de Dei erga nos voluntate: subinde langue scimus in tentationibus. Et levi momento humanorum eventuum de gradu fidei deiicimur. Nec desinit Satanas nobis struere: insidias ut eripiat nobis scutum fidei. Hac ergò satutare medicina animae, nimirum corpore & sanguine Iesu Christi, omninò indigemus ut muniantur nostra infirma pectora, & roboretur nostra fides, ut varios Satanae insultus excipere, & hostem superare possimus.

Quarta. Nec tantum una est huius immensi boni utilitas, sed multiplices sunt. Primùm magna est utilitas, quod adfert secum remissionem peccatorum. Qui enim sanguinem Christi fide percipit, accipit certò remissionem peccatorum: Sanguis enim Iesu Christi abluit nos ab omni peccato. Deinde obsignat nobis promissionem gratiae & reddit tranquillam conscientiam. Tertiò adplicat nobis singulis omnia beneficia mediatoris: Quartò Christus corpore suo nos vivificat & sanctificat: & auget in nobis dona sua spiritualia, agnitionem Dei, timorem, fiduciam, laeticiam, patientiam, desiderium vitae aeternae, constantiam, zelum, & similia. Quintò arctissimè coniungit nos cum Christo: Siquidem in nobis habitat & nos in ipso. Sextò munit nos contra omnes insidias et telas Satane. Septimò ostendit nobis certam spem resurrectionis nostrorum corporum. Hae multiplices utilitates nos accendere debent, ut crebrò & ardenti desiderio usurpemus coenam domini.

Quinta causa, ut edamus publicè nostram confessionem, cuius Ecclesiae cives simus: Utque nonostro exemplo alios ad frequentem usum coenae domini invitemus.

Sexta. Ut vitemus poenas gravissimas, quas Deus immittere solet iis, qui coenae domini usum superbè & contumaciter contemnunt. Minatur enim Deus supplicia gravissima contemptoribus sacrosancti ministerii & sacramentorum. Quia scientiam repulisti (inquit in Osea) et ego repellam te: Item: Quia clamabam, & nemo audiebat, ridebo & ego in calamitate vestra. Prover:1. Item: Immittet Deus famem non panis, sed audiendi verbi Dei. Item: Immittet Deus efficaciam erroris, ut credant mendacio, ut iudicentur omnes qui non credunt veritati. Et plena est sacra scriptura talium comminationum, quae contemptoribus ministerii & Sacramentorum horribilem Dei iram denunciant. Ac plurima exempla irae Dei quotidie fere sunt ante oculos. Contemptores enim coenae domini puniuntur caecitate & amentia, traduntur in reprobum sensum, ut subindè cumulent peccata, obduratur cor illorum impoenitens, & tandem cum in agone mortis expetunt consolationem per coenam domini, subitò obruuntur iudicio Dei, ut nec poenitentiam agere nec saluberrima medicina coenae domini frui possint.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper: Chapter X
CHAPTER X.

What fruits ought to follow the salutary reception of the Lord's Supper.

Since the Son of God therefore instituted his most holy supper, that through it he might confirm and increase faith in us, impart his Spirit and life to us, and most closely unite us, sanctified, to God, every effort must be made that we may testify and demonstrate by the true fruits of faith and the Spirit that this heavenly and spiritual medicine has been efficacious in us. First, therefore, a joyful act of thanksgiving ought to follow the salutary use of the Eucharist, by which we may celebrate the immense mercy and goodness of God with as much strength as we can, and make manifest before the world what huge goods the eternal Father has conferred upon us through the death of his only-begotten Son: from what miseries he has freed us, and to what blessedness he has gratuitously transferred us. Next, the mind must be excited to true joy in God, so clement and beneficent. By assiduous invocation and imploration of divine aid we ought to testify that nothing in the whole world is dearer to us than those spiritual benefits which the Son of God procured for us by his death and sealed for us in his holy supper. On individual days and moments we must recall to ourselves by how great a pledge God has sealed our faith, by what bond He has bound Himself to us, so that in this way we may nourish, cherish, and excite our faith. True love and fear of God must also grow in us, so that we may refer all things to His glory, who has bestowed such immense gifts upon us, the unworthy, and has given us all things with His only-begotten Son.

Then, a lively and constant confession of the divine name must shine in us. For after He has confirmed us with His Body and Blood, that the eternal Father has received us into grace and has appointed us heirs of eternal life and of all heavenly goods, it is most equitable that we prefer this supreme benefactor to all things of this life and to all creatures in heaven and on earth: and, having disregarded all dangers and adversities, we should vindicate the glory of Jesus Christ before the world and bear witness to the eternal truth, according to the saying: I believed, therefore I have spoken. Likewise, therefore, let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God always through Him, that is, the fruit of lips confessing His name. He who drinks the Blood of Jesus Christ, which He shed for our sins, must be of a ready mind to shed his own blood for the glory of Jesus Christ and His truth, when we are called to this by God.

Thirdly, reverence and love ought to be kindled in us toward the sacrosanct ministry of the Gospel, and the use of the Sacraments. Because by the benefit of the ministry of the Gospel we are made partakers of such great goods, we ought to hold it reverently, to give thanks to God with an ardent heart for the light of his word, and the legitimate use of the Sacraments, to invoke God assiduously, that he may preserve these such great goods for us, also to exercise piety in ourselves by the frequent use of the Lord's supper, to testify openly that we value this Treasure highly, and to invite others to true piety: as much as is also in us, to assist the preservation of the evangelical ministry with labors, and studies, and resources.

Fourthly, true and unfeigned love of neighbor ought to follow the use of the Eucharist. For we are fed with the body and blood of Christ for this reason, that the Holy Spirit may work in us and kindle virtues of every kind. The Holy Spirit is alien to all spite, envy, hatred, enmity, and anger. He glues together hearts, however, with an unfeigned bond of mutual love. God is love, says John. He who abides in love, abides in God. And Christ says, by this it will be known that you are my disciples, if you have loved one another. And the sacred supper itself is a covenant of mutual union and brotherly love, since indeed we are fed and given to drink in this, that we may all be one body, just as we all partake of one bread, and we all drink from one cup.

Fifth, we must take care that we do not inflict any ignominy or insult upon our bodies. Therefore, we must flee with all zeal from drunkenness and forbidden lusts of every kind, by which the bodies of men are dishonored and the horrible wrath of God is provoked: For through the supper of the Lord our bodies have been made temples of Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit: Therefore, we must live soberly, temperately, modestly, and chastely: Lest by the contamination of our bodies we grieve the Holy Spirit within us and drive Jesus Christ away from us.

Sixth, we must guard our mouth and lips, as those which have been sanctified by the body and blood of Jesus Christ, lest they be polluted by false doctrine, or blasphemy, or lying, or calumnies, or filthiness of speech. And in sum, a pious mind must seriously strive for justice and truth and all virtues and duties which are demanded of us in the decalogue; And by its piety toward God and men demonstrate that it has approached the table of the Lord in true faith, and has received the body and blood of the Lord with salutary fruit.

Latin:

CAPUT X.

Qui fructus sequi debeant salutarem sumptionem coenae Domini.

Cum ideò instituerit filius Dei sacro sanctam suam caenam, ut per eam fidem in nobis confirmet & augeat, Spiritum suum & vitam nobis impertiat, nosque sanctificatos Deo arctissime coniungat, omnino danda est opera ut veris fructibus fidei et Spiritus testemur atque demonstremus, efficacem in nobis fuisse coelestem & Spiritualem hanc medicinam. Primùm ergò salutarem Eucharistiae usurpationem sequi debet laeta gratiarum actio, quo immensam Dei misericordiam & bonitatem quantis possimus viribus celebremus & coram mundo palam faciamus, quam ingentia bona pater aeternus per mortem sui unigeniti filii in nos contulerit: ex quantis miseriis nos liberaverit, & ad quantam beatitudinem gratuitò nos transtulerit. Subinde excitanda est mens ad veram laeticiam in Deo, tam clementi & benefico. Adsidua invocatione & imploratione auxilii divini testari debemus, nihil nobis carius esse in toto orbe, Spiritualibus illis beneficiis, quae nobis filius Dei sua morte peperit & sacra sua coena nobis obsignavit. Singulis diebus & momentis in memoriam nobis revocare debemus, quanto pignore Deus fidem nostram obsignaverit, quali vinculo se nobis obstrinxerit, ut ita alamus, foveamus & excitemus fidem. Crescere etiam in nobis debet, vera Dei dilectio & timor, ut omnia ad ipsius gloriam reseramus, qui tam immensa dona in nos indignos contulit & cum filio suo unigenito omnia nobis dedit.

Deinde alacris & constans nominis divini confessio in nobis lucere debet. Postquam enim corpore & Sanguine suo nos confirmavit, quod pater aeternas nos in gratiam receperit, & haeredes vitae aeternae & omnium caelestium bonorum constituerit, aequissimum est, ut hunc benefactorem summum omnibus rebus huius vitae, omnibusque creaturis in coelo & in terra praeferamus: ac post habitis omnibus periculis & adversitatibus vindicemus coram mundo gloriam Iesu Christi, & veritati aeternae demus testimonium, iuxta dictum. Credidi propter quod locutus sum. Item, per ipsum igitur offeramus hostiam laudis semper Deo, hoc est, fructum labiorum confitentium nomini eius. Qui bibit Sanguinem Iesu Christi, quem ille pro peccatis nostris effudit, is prompto animo esse debet ad effundendum suum Sanguinem pro gloria Iesu Christi & ipsius veritate, cum ad hoc à Deo vocamur.

Tertiò, reverentia & amor in nobis accendi debet erga sacrosanctum ministerium Evangelii, & usum Sacramentorum. Quia beneficio ministerii Evangelii tantorum bonorum efficimur participes, reverenter id habere debemus, ardenti pectore Deo gratias agere pro luce sui verbi, & legitimo Sacramentorum usu, adsiduè Deum invocare, ut haec tanta bona nobis conservet, Etiam crebro coenae domini usu in nobis exercere pietatem, palàm testari, quod plurimi hunc Thesaurum faciamus, & alios ad veram pietatem invitare: Quantum etiam in nobis est & laboribus, & studiis & facultatibus ministerii Evangelici conservationem adiuvare.

Quartò, vera & non simulata proximi dilectio sequi debet usum Eucharistiae. Ideò enim cibamur corpore & sanguine Christi, ut Spiritus sanctus in nobis operetur & omnis generis virtutes accendat. Ab omni livore, invidia, odio, inimicitia, & ira alienus est Spiritus sanctus. Conglutinat autem pectora non simulato vinculo amoris mutui. Deus dilectio est, inquit Ioannes. Qui manet in dilectione, manet in Deo. Et Christus inquit in hoc cognoscetur quod discipuli mei sitis, si vos invicem dilexeritis. Et ipsa sacra coena foedus est mutuae coniunctionis & amoris fraterni, siquidem in hoc cibamur & potamur, ut omnes unum simus corpus, quemadmodum de uno pane omnes participamus, & ex uno calice bibimus omnes.

Quintò, Cavere debemus ne corpora nostri ulla ignominia vel contumelia adficiamus. Itaque temulentiam, & omnis generis libidines prohibitas, quibus corpora hominum dehonestantur & horribilis Dei ira provocatur, omni studio fugere debemus: Per coenam enim domini corpora nostra facta sunt templa Iesu Christi & Spiritus sancti: Idcirco sobriè, temperanter, pudicè & castè vivendum est: Ne contaminatione nostrorum corporum Spiritum sanctum in nobis contristemus & Iesum Christum à nobis abigamus.

Sextò, os & labia nostra ut quae corpore & sanguine Iesu Christi sunt sanctificata, custodire debemus, ne falsa doctrina, aut blassphemia, aut mendacio, aut calumniis aut spurcitie sermonis, polluantur. Et in summa iustitiae & veritati & omnibus virtutibus & officiis, quae à nobis in decalogo flagitantur, pia mens serio studere debet; Et pietate sua erga Deum et homines demonstrare, quod in vera fide ad mensam domini accesserit, & cum fructu salutari corpus & sanguinem domini perceperit.

## 11:22 Concerning the Lord's Supper: Chapter XI
CHAPTER XI.

What are the principal abuses and profanations of the Lord's Supper among the Papists.

No voice can sufficiently lament and set forth the audacity and monstrous insolence with which the Roman Antichrist has profaned the most holy Supper of the Lord. Nor is there any doubt that the world suffers grave punishments on account of the horrible insult which is inflicted upon the most holy Supper of the Lord in the papacy. Satan has in a way established the profanation of the Lord's Supper as the foundation of the entire kingdom of Antichrist, but now I shall note only four horrendous abuses.

1. The first is that, contrary to the express institution of Christ, they have mutilated the Lord's Supper, and they grant the body and blood of Christ to be distributed only to priests and clerics: but they snatch the blood of Jesus Christ away from the laity. This sacrilege fights against the express institution of Jesus Christ and against his own command, Drink of this all of you. Therefore, there is no doubt that this sacrilegious change of the Sacrament, which the Tridentine synod stubbornly retains, has proceeded from Satan himself.

2. The second profanation is that they have transformed the Lord's Supper into a sacrifice, and they feign themselves to offer to God the Father the body and blood of Jesus Christ in the mass for the sins of the human race, for the living and the dead. This horrible and detestable blasphemy not only fights against the institution of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, but also against the entire Holy Scripture: And it affects Jesus Christ with extreme insult: Who did not institute His holy supper for this purpose, that His body might be offered again as a victim to God for the sins of the world, but that it might be eaten by us for the confirmation of our faith. What else do the blasphemous little sacrificers do when they assert that they offer the body of Jesus Christ to God the Father, than that which, as much as is in them, they crucify Jesus Christ again, now sitting with glory at the right hand of the eternal Father, burden Him with the sins of the whole world, and establish Him as a curse before God. For this signifies being a victim for sins. What more hideous blasphemy, therefore, could be devised by Satan? Holy Scripture says concerning ἱλαστιχῷ sacrifice, that He was offered once, and by a single oblation found eternal redemption. Heb. 9. But by His own blood He entered once into the holy places, having found eternal redemption. Item, but now once in the end of the ages, He has appeared for the abolition of sin by His own sacrifice. Item: Heb: 10. By a single oblation He has perfected forever those who are sanctified.

These clear testimonies teach that Jesus Christ, the Lamb of God, was offered once to appease the wrath of God and to abolish the sins of the world, which was done on the cross. Therefore, it is an invention of Satan that they have imagined that the body and blood of Jesus Christ must be offered in the mass for the sins of the world, for the living and the dead. It is also a horrible and detestable blasphemy that they imagine that that work, which the little priest offers, bread and wine, merits the remission of sins and appeases the wrath of God, and is of no less merit and efficacy than the bloody sacrifice of the Son of God, which was accomplished on the altar of the cross. There are almost infinite profanations of the Lord's Supper among the papists, which arise from the idolatrous sacrifice of the mass. For they imagine that by the oblation of the body and blood of Christ they merit and obtain not only spiritual goods, but also corporal ones: victory in war, happiness in hunting, success in trade, liberation from diseases, the repression of storms, the fertility of fields, and the like. Therefore, all the pious ought to flee the sacrifice of the mass, which is performed among the papists, as an extreme idolatry and blasphemy.

3. The third profanation is that they have imagined the transubstantiation of bread into the body and of wine into the blood of Christ, with only the accidents of bread and wine remaining. We have refuted this error above.

And we show that he fights against the testimony of Paul. Who even after the consecration calls the Eucharist bread.

4. The fourth profanation is that the papists manufacture an idol out of the consecrated bread, inasmuch as they store it, carry it about in processions, and command it to be adored. Which idolatry fights against the institution of the Son of God, who gave us blessed bread to eat and blessed wine to drink, but did not command it to be adored. For bread is not God: But it is and remains a creature, and it is a medium through which Christ exhibits his body to us to be eaten. Concerning adoration, the rule is unmoved and most plain. You shall adore the Lord your God and him only shall you serve. Therefore to you now, Jesus Christ, Son of God, Redeemer and Savior of the whole Church, I give thanks with my whole heart for this huge benefit, that by your Holy Spirit you have preserved your most holy supper in the Church, and have defended the true opinion concerning it against the illusions of all heretics, and have kept us in the acknowledgment of the truth by your Holy Spirit. With true groaning we pray you that you may repress the fanatical errors of the Zwinglians and Calvinists, and restrain the blasphemies of the fury of the Epicureans, and vindicate your holy name; but us, who attribute to you the praise of truth and omnipotence and depend on you alone, protect clemently, may you illuminate with your Holy Spirit, confirm in saving truth, console in all dangers, and by your immense goodness cause that through faith we may obtain the inheritance of eternal life, and may we celebrate with praises the eternal Father, you, and the Holy Spirit for all eternity, Amen.

Latin:

CAPUT XI.

Qui sint praecipui abusus & prophanationes coenae Domini apud Pontificios.

Nulla voce satis deplorari & exponi potest audacia & immanis petulantia, qua Romanus Antichristus prophanavit sacrosanctam coenam Domini. Nec dubium est quin orbis graves det poenas, propter horribilem contumeliam, quae in papatu sacrosanctae coenae domini infertur, Fundamentum quodammodo totius regni Antichristi constituit Satanas prophanationem coenae domini, nunc verò tantum quatuor horrendos abusus notabo.

1. Primus est, quod contra expressam Christi institutionem mutilarunt coenam domini, & tantum sacerdotibus & clericis concedunt corpus & sanguinem Christi distribui: Laicis verò eripiunt sanguinem Iesu Christi: Hoc sacrilegium pugnat cum expressa institutione Iesu Christi & cum ipsius mandato, Bibite ex hoc omnes. Nihil igitur dubitandum est hanc sacrilegam mutationem Sacramenti, quam blasphemam synodus Tridentina mordicus retinet ab ipso Satana profectam esse.

2. Secunda prophanatio est, quod coenam domini transformarunt in sacrificium, & fingunt se offerre in missa Deo patri corpus & sanguinem Iesu Christi pro peccatis generis humani, pro vivis & mortuis. Haec horribilis & detestanda blasphemia non solùm pugnat cum institutione filii Dei Iesu Christi, verumetiam cum universa sacra scriptura: Et extrema contumelia adficit Iesum Christum: Qui sacram suam coenam, non hoc fine instituit ut suum corpus tanquam victima denuò offerretur Deo pro peccatis mundi, sed ut à nobis manducaretur in confirmationem nostrae fidei. Quid aliud faciunt blasphemi sacrificuli cum adserunt se offerre Deo patri corpus Iesu Christi, quam quod Iesum Christum nunc cum gloria sedentem ad dexteram aeterni patris rursus quantum in se est crucifigunt, onerant totius mundi peccatis, & statuunt maledictum coram Deo. Hoc enim significat esse victimam pro peccacatis. Quae ergò tetrior blasphemia posset à Satana excogitari? Sacra scriptura de ἱλαστιχῷ sacrificio inquit, quod semel oblatus sit, & unica oblatione aeternam redemptionem invenerit. Heb. 9. per proprium autem sanguinem semel ingressus est in sancta aeterna redemptione inventa. Item, nunc autem semel in fine seculorum, ad abolitionem peccati per proprium sacrificium adparuit. Item: Heb: 10. Unica oblatione consumavit in perpetuum qui sanctificantur.

Haec perspicua testimonia docent sufficere ad placandam iram Dei, & abolenda peccata mundi, semel oblatum esse Iesum Christum agnum Dei, quod in cruce factum est. Satanae ergò inventum est, quod finxit corpus & sanguinem Iesu Christi in missa offerenda esse pro peccatis mundi, pro vivis & mortuis. Horribilis etiam & detestanda blasphemia est, quod fingunt opus illud, quod sacrificulus offert panem et vinum mereri remissionem peccatorum, & placare iram Dei, ac non minoris esse meriti & efficaciae, atque cruentum sacrificium filii Dei, quod in ara crucis peractum est. Propemodum sunt infinitae prophanationes coenae domini apud pontificios, quae ex idolatrico sacrificio missae oriuntur. Fingunt enim se oblatione corporis & sanguinis Christi mereri & impetrare non tantum spiritualia bona, verumetiam corporalia, victoriam in bello, felicitatem in venatione, successum in mercatura, liberationem ex morbis, repressionem tempestatum, fertilitatem agrotum & similia. Omnes igitur pii sacrificium missae, quod fit apud pontificios, ut extremam idolatriam & blasphemiam fugere debent.

3. Tertia prophanatio est, quod finxerunt transsubstantiationem panis in corpus & vini in sanguinem Christi, manentibus tantum accidentibus panis & vini. Hunc errorem supra refutavimus:

Et ostendimus eum pugnare cum testimonio Pauli. Qui etiam post consecrationem Eucharistiam nominat panem.

4. Quarta prophanatio est, quod pontificii ex pane consecrato idolum fabricant, siquidem reponunt, circumferunt in pompis, & iubent adorari. Quae idolatria pugnat cum institutione filii Dei, qui nobis panem benedictum ad manducandum & vinum benedictum ad bibendum dedit, non autem iussit adorari. Panis enim non est Deus: Sed est & manet creatura, Et est medium per quod Christus exhibet nobis corpus suum manducandum. De adoratione immota & planissima est regula. Dominum Deum tuum adorabis et illi soli servies. Tibi ergò nunc Iesu Christe fili Dei redemptor & salvator totius Ecclesiae toto pectore gratias ago, pro hoc ingenti beneficio, quod Spiritu tuo sancto Sacrosanctam tuam coenam in Ecclesia conservasti, & veram de ea sententiam contra omnium haereticorum praestigias defendisti, & nos Spiritu tuo sancto in agnitione veritatis custodivisti. Vero gemitu te precamur ut Zwinglianorum & Calvinistarum fanaticos errores reprimas, & Epicureorum furoris blasphemias coerceas, & sanctum nomen tuum vindices; Nos verò, qui tibi laudem veritatis & omnipotentiae tribuimus & à te solo pendemus, clementer protegas, Spiritu tuo sancto illumines, in salutari veritate confirmes, in omnibus periculis consoleris, & pro tua bonitate immensa facias, ut per fidem vitae aeternae haereditatem adipiscamur, & aeternum patrem, te & Spiritum sanctum ad omnem perpetuitatem laudibus celebremus, Amen.

## 11:23-25
For I received from the Lord that which I also delivered to you. For the Lord Jesus, in the night in which he was betrayed, took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, Take, eat, this is my body, which is broken for you, Do this in my remembrance: In like manner also the cup, after he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood. Do this as often as you drink in my remembrance.

The Apostle Paul here relates how the Lord's supper was instituted by the Son of God, Jesus Christ. For it is the best refutation of errors and the best amendment of abuses which have crept into the Church, when one recurs to the first institution and the author himself, the Son of God, is shown.

But first it must be diligently observed here, that the Apostle Paul testifies that he did not learn this rite from other Apostles, who were present at the last supper, nor from the Evangelists, but received it from our Lord Jesus Christ himself. For Paul was caught up into the third heaven, and with his own eyes saw the Lord Jesus resurrected from death, as he testifies several times. Therefore, we ought to apply no less faith to this description of the Lord's supper than if the Son of God, Jesus Christ himself, had handed down this form to us. And so that we may admit no doubt about the truth of the words of the supper, and so that we may rouse ourselves to the frequent use of the holy supper, we must always look back to this author full of majesty, Jesus Christ. Christ, after his resurrection from death and ascension into heaven, handing down to Paul the form of the holy supper, uses the same form of words which the Evangelists also used. It is not permitted, therefore, for a man to invent interpretations according to the capacity of human wit: But the very form of Christ's words must be retained, that the blessed bread in the holy supper is the body of Jesus Christ. Nor is the supper itself to be administered otherwise than the Son of God himself instituted, and the Apostle Paul reported.

Secondly, what is distributed to us in the holy supper, the words of Christ expressly teach, namely not only bread and wine, but the true and essential body and Blood of Jesus Christ. For Christ does not pronounce nakedly, This is my body: but he adds a declaration and interpretation. This is my body, which is broken for you, or as the Evangelists report, which is given for you. Likewise this is my Blood, which is poured out for you for the remission of sins, but there is no other body broken for us and given into death, except the essential body of Jesus Christ: nor is there any other Blood poured out for the remission of our sins than the natural Blood of Jesus Christ, which flowed from the veins and side of Christ. Therefore, with every handle for doubting completely removed, the blessed bread in the supper of the Lord is the essential body of Jesus Christ which hung on the cross: and the blessed wine is the essential Blood of Jesus Christ.

The phrase of Paul. Which is broken for you is referred to the body of Christ itself. For it agrees with the phrase of Luke, which is given for you. For for our sins the body of Christ was broken and given and crucified on the cross. And when it is added concerning the cup, this is my Blood, which is poured out for you for the remission of sins: it is certain that Christ wished to declare in the same way concerning the body of which he was speaking. And when he says is broken for you, he explains the cause of his death; that he delivers his body into death for our sins, and for our salvation. Therefore this proper and native meaning must be retained. When Paul says τόν ἄρτον ὃν κλῶμεν: the bread which we break: he is speaking of the distribution of the bread and of the body of Christ in the supper. If anyone wishes the word (is broken) to be understood concerning the distribution of the body in the supper, I do not fight it, provided the truth of the body of Christ present in the supper is not denied. Because Carlstadt and other fanatical men have argued thus. Yet in the supper of the Lord the body of Christ is neither broken nor crucified: therefore neither is the bread the true body of Christ, and it is foolish and inept. For Christ declares of which body he is speaking, not the mystical, but his own proper one, which at that time of the sacrifice he offered for us into death. Concerning the cup, although there is some diversity in the words of the Evangelists and of Paul, yet the entirely same meaning emerges. Matthew and Mark say. This is the Blood of the new testament, which is shed for you for the remission of sins. Paul and Luke say. This cup is the new testament in my Blood, the meaning is. That the blessed wine in the cup is the true Blood of Jesus Christ, by which the new testament is established, and which for the remission of our sins is poured out. Therefore this demonstration is most valid. There is no other Blood of the new testament than the true and natural Blood of Jesus Christ. But the Son of God testifies that the blessed wine in the holy supper is his blood of the new testament. Therefore the blessed wine in the holy supper is the true and essential Blood of Jesus Christ.

Thirdly, the entire fruit of the passion and death of Jesus Christ is delivered in these words. Which is broken for you. Item, which is poured out for you for the remission of sins. For by these words the Son of God Jesus Christ our Lord testifies that he underwent death for the sake of our salvation, so that by his death and the shedding of Blood he might pay for our sins, appease the wrath of God, abolish the curse of the law, and procure for us new life and righteousness. Therefore all our salvation consists in the Blood of Jesus Christ. For by his stripes we are healed. And he himself is the lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world.

Fourthly, the words of Christ teach for what end he instituted this his sublime supper, namely that he might preserve in us a perpetual memory of his passion and death, confirm our faith, and apply the benefits of his kingdom to each of us.

Therefore he adds: Do this in remembrance of me, as if he were saying, for this reason I institute this supper, for this reason I distribute to you my body and my blood, that I may from time to time bring back to your memory that I have shed my blood for your sins, and that by this pledge I may seal for you this most ample consolation, and apply it to each one. For just as the general promise of the Gospel offers to all the remission of sins and eternal life on account of the mediator: So the supper of the Lord applies and seals the benefits of the kingdom of Christ to each one approaching the table of the Lord. To you who are eating, Christ offers his body, which he delivered into death for you. To you who are drinking from the cup of the Lord, Christ bestows his Blood, which he shed for the remission of your sins. Therefore the utility of the Eucharist is immense, and every pious person ought to use the table of the Lord most frequently.

Latin:

Ego enim à Domino, accepi quod & tradidi vobis. Nam Dominus Iesus, in ea nocte, in qua traditus est, accepit panem, & cùm gratias egisset, fregit & dixit, Accipite, edite, hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur, Hoc facite in meam recordationem: Similiter & calicem, postquam coenasset, dicens, Hic calix novum testamentum est in meo sanguine. Hoc facite quotiescunque biberitis in meam recordationem.

Apostolus Paulus hic refert, quomodo caena domini à filio Dei Iesu Christo sit instituta. Optima enim est & errorum refutatio & abusuum qui in Ecclesiam irrepserunt emendatio, cum recurritur adprimam institutionem & monstratur author ipse filius Dei.

Primum autem diligenter hîc observandum est, quod Apostolus Paulus testatur se non ab aliis Apostolis, qui ultimae coenae interfuerunt, nec ab Evangelistis hunc ritum didicisse, sed ab ipso domino nostro Iesu Christo accepisse. Raptus enim fuit Paulus in tertium coelum, & oculis suis vidit Dominum Iesum ex morte resuscitatum, ut aliquoties testatur. Ergò huic descriptioni coenae domini non minorem fidem adhibere debemus, quam si ipse filius Dei Iesus Christus nobis hanc formam tradidisset. Ac ut nullam admittamus dubitationem de veritate verborum coenae, & ut ad crebam sacrae coenae usurpationem nos excitemus, semper ad hunc authorem plenum maiestatis Iesum Christum respicere debemus. Christus post resurrectionem ex morte & adscensionem in coelum tradens Paulo formam sacrae coenae, eadem forma verborum utitur, quam & Evangelistae usurparunt. Non igitur licet homini fingere interpretationes pro humani ingenii captu: Sed ipsa forma verborum Christi retinenda est, quod panis benedictus in sacra coena sit corpus Iesu Christi. Nec aliter ipsa coena administranda est, quam ipse filius Dei instituit, & Paulus Apostolus retulit.

Secundò quid nobis in sacra coena distribuatur, expresse docent verba Christi, nimirum non tantum panis & vinum, sed verum & essentiale corpus & Sanguis Iesu Christi. Christus enim non pronunciat nude, Hoc est corpus meum: sed addit declarationem & interpretationem. Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis frangitur, vel ut Evangelistae referunt, quod pro vobis traditur. Item hic est Sanguis meus, qui pro vobis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum, sed non est aliud corpus pro nobis fractum & in mortem traditum, nisi essentiale corpus Iesu Christi: nec est alius Sanguis effusus in remissionem nostrorum peccatorum quam naturalis Sanguis Iesu Christi, qui fluxit ex venis & latere Christi. Ergò omni ansa dubitandi penitus sublata, panis benedictus in coena Domini est essentiale corpus Iesu Christi quod in cruce pependit: & vinum benedictum est essentialis Sanguis Iesu Christi.

Phrasis Pauli. Quod pro vobis frangitur ad ipsum corpus Christi refertur. Congruit enim cum phrasi Lucae, quod pro vobis traditur. Pro nostris enim peccatis corpus Christi in cruce fractum & traditum & crucifixum est. Et cum de calice addatur, hic est Sanguis meus, qui pro vobis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum: certum est, Christum eodem modo declarare voluisse de quo corpore loqueretur. Et cum dicit pro vobis frangitur, causam mortis suae exponit; quod pro peccatis nostris, & propter salutem nostram tradat corpus suum in mortem. Haec ergò propria & nativa significatio retinenda est. Cùm Paulus dicit τόν ἄρτον ὃν κλῶμεν: panis quem frangimus: de distributione panis & corporis Christi in coena loquitur. Si quis vocem (frangitur) de distributione corporis in coena vult intelligi, non pugno, modo veritas corporis Christi in coena praesentis non negetur. Quod Carolstadius & alii fanatici homines sic argumentati sunt. Tamen in coena Domini non frangitur nec crucifigitur corpus Christi: ergò nec panis est verum corpus Christi, & stolidum & ineptum est. Christus enim declarat, de quo corpore loquatur, non mystico, sed proprio suo, quod tum tempore sacrificii obtulit pro nobis in mortem. De calice etsi quaedam diversitas est in verbis Evangelistarum et Pauli, tamen prorsus eadem emergit sententia. Mattheus & Marcus inquiunt. Hic est Sanguis novi testamenti, qui pro vobis in remissionem peccatorum effunditur. Paulus & Lucas dicunt. Hic calix est novum testamentum in meo Sanguine, sententia est. Vinum benedictum in calice esse verum Sanguinem Iesu Christi, quo stabilitum est novum testamentum, & qui in remissionem nostrorum peccatorum est effusus. Est ergò validissima haec demonstratio. Non est alius Sanguis novi testamenti, quàm verus & naturalis Sanguis Iesu Christi. Sed filius Dei testatur vinum benedictum in sacra coena esse sanguinem suum novi testamenti. Ergò vinum benedictum in sacra coena est verus & essentialis Sanguis Iesu Christi.

Tertiò, universus fructus passionis & mortis Iesu Christi traditur in his verbis. Quod pro vobis frangitur. Item, qui pro vobis in remissionem peccatorum effunditur. His enim verbis testatur filius Dei Iesus Christus Dominus noster, quod propter nostram salutem subierit mortem, ut sua morte & Sanguinis effusione pro nostris solveret peccatis, placaret iram Dei, aboleret legis maledictionem, & novam vitam & iustitiam nobis compararet. Omnis ergò salus nostra consistit in Sanguine Iesu Christi. Nam livore eius sanati sumus. Et ipse est agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi.

Quartò docent verba Christi, quo fine instituerit hanc suam sublimem coenam, nimirum ut memoriam passionis & mortis suae in nobis perpetuam conservaret, fidem nostram confirmaret, & sui regni beneficia nobis singulis adplicaret.

Idcirco addit: Hoc facite in mei recordationem, quasi dicat, ideo instituo hanc coenam, ideò distribuo vobis meum corpus & meum sauguinem, ut subindè redigam vobis in memoriam, me pro vestris peccatis effudisse sanguinem, utque hoc pignore obsignem vobis amplissimam hanc consolationem, & singulis eam adplicem. Ut enim generalis promissio Evangelii omnibus offert remissionem peccatorum & vitam aeternam propter mediatorem: Ita coena Domini singulis ad mensam Domini accedentibus adplicat & obsignat beneficia regni Christi. Tibi manducanti offert Christus suum corpus, quod pro te tradidit in mortem. Tibi bibenti ex calice Domini largitur Christus suum Sanguinem, quem in remissionem tuorum peccatorum effudit. Immensa ergò utilitas est Eucharistiae, et singuli pii creberrime mensa Domini uti debent.

## 11:26-27
For as often as you shall eat this bread, and drink this cup, you shall announce the death of the Lord, until he comes.

After Paul explained with what words our Lord Jesus Christ his holy supper he established and adds a precept that this supper should be repeated often in the Church, and frequently used by all the pious.

As often, he says, as you shall eat this bread. Therefore Christ did not only do this with his Apostles, but he also wishes us to imitate him, and to eat his body under the blessed bread: and to drink his blood under the blessed wine. For he addresses the Corinthians and the whole Church here. Nor is it a matter of indifference to use the supper of the Lord or to abstain: But God through the Apostle severely commands that we should often use this supper. Therefore they sin gravely against God, who rarely approach the table of the Lord. Let the reader also observe here, that in the primitive Church the blood of Jesus Christ was distributed to the laity as well as to the priests, and the supper of the Lord was administered without mutilation. For Paul writes to the whole Corinthian Church, and commands that individuals should often both eat the body of the Lord, and drink from the cup of the Lord. Therefore the sacrilegious Roman pontiffs are to be detested, because they snatched the blood of Christ from the people. Furthermore, the Apostle Paul commands that in the very use of the supper we should announce the death of the Lord. He does not wish the administration of the supper to be a mute spectacle, which is carried out in deep silence: But a public confession ought to resound concerning Jesus Christ crucified and resurrected: So that by this public voice the Church may be gathered and our faith may be stirred up and confirmed.

Until he comes First, he teaches how long this rite is to endure in the Church: Namely, until the coming of the Son of God in the clouds, until the final day, on which God is to adorn His Church with eternal glory. Therefore, no other form of the Church, no other Sacraments are to be expected in this world. Next, these words contain a sweet promise, that the Church will never perish in this world, however much it may be attacked by tyrants and heretics, but that there will perpetually be some assembly on earth which, with true confidence, worships the mediator and nourishes and stabilizes its faith by the use of the Lord's Supper according to the promise. I am with you always, even unto the end of the world. He also hands down here an article of faith concerning the glorious coming of Jesus Christ in the clouds for the universal judgment of the whole world: That this glorious coming and joyful day is now at the doors is evident not only from many signs, but it is also rightly gathered from the fact that in these last times the doctrine concerning the Lord's Supper is most gravely attacked by heretical Sacramentarians, and this Epicurean error is making great gains in many kingdoms.

Wherefore whoever eats this bread, and drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily, he is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

Because the Apostle Paul noticed that the Corinthians were approaching the table of the Lord with great security, just as if they were approaching ordinary feasts, he not only repeats the institution of the supper, but also adds a most grave warning, and warns those who approach the table of the Lord securely and without movements of repentance, that they become guilty of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, which, since it is a most grave fault, which God is accustomed to punish with atrocious punishment, each one must be vigilant, so that in the fear of the Lord and true faith they may partake of the body and blood of Jesus Christ. Here Paul explicitly refutes the figment of the papists concerning the transelementation, or annihilation, or transubstantiation of bread into the body of God. For he calls the blessed bread, bread. For the substance of the bread truly remains. And yet it is the true body of Christ, because it is the medium through which Christ offers his body to us to be eaten. To eat the blessed bread unworthily is not only to receive the bread of the Lord less reverently: But it is to eat the bread of the Eucharist and to drink the cup of the Lord securely, without true contrition, without trust resting in the mediator, and with sins devastating the conscience, just as if it were common food and drink, and thus they did not discern the body of the Lord from common bread. Judas the traitor received the body of the Lord unworthily. But those who bring serious repentance and apply true faith to the words of Christ receive it worthily. To be guilty of the body and blood of Jesus Christ is to sustain the guilt of the body of Christ affected by injury and insult. He who eats the bread of the Eucharist unworthily and securely, says Paul, sustains guilt by the judgment of God, because he has insulted and injured the very body of Jesus Christ, just as the Jews, striking the face of Jesus Christ with blows, affected his most holy body with atrocious insult. Here, therefore, it is again most evidently demonstrated that there is a true presence of the body of Jesus Christ in the Holy Supper. For no one becomes guilty of the body and blood of Christ unless he affects the body and blood of Christ with injury; since, therefore, Paul testifies that those who eat this bread and drink from this cup unworthily become guilty of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, it is necessary that they affect the body and blood of Christ with injury, and that by the very eating and drinking. Whence also a little later he says: He who eats and drinks unworthily, eats and drinks judgment to himself. If the body of Jesus Christ were not present in the Supper, those receiving the bread of the Eucharist unworthily would neither affect the body of Christ itself with insult by the very eating, nor would they bind themselves with such a sad state of guilt.

Latin:

Quotiescunque enim ederitis hunc panem, & calicem hunc biberitis, mortem Domini annunciabitis, donec veniat.

Postquam exposuit Paulus, quibus verbis dominus noster Iesus Christus sacram suam coenam instituerit addit praeceptum quod saepè in Ecclesia iteranda sit haec coena, & ab omnibus piis crebrò usurpanda.

Quotiescunque inquit hunc panem ederitis) Non ergò tantum cum suis Apostolis hoc egit Christus, verumetiam vult nos imitari, & corpus ipsius sub pane benedicto manducare: & sanguinem eius sub vino benedicto bibere. Corinthios enim & totam Ecclesiam hîc alloquitur. Nec est adiaphoron quiddam uti coena domini vel abstinere: Sed Deus per Apostolum severè mandat, ut saepè hac coena utamur. Peccant igitur graviter in Deum, qui raro ad mensam domini accedunt. Observet hic etiam lector, quod in primitiva Ecclesia tàm laicis, quàm sacerdotibus distributus sit sanguis Iesu Christi, coena domini sine mutilatione sit administrata. Paulus enim scribit toti Ecclesiae Corinthiacae, & iubet ut singuli crebrò & corpus domini edant, & de calice domini bibant. Detestandi igitur sunt sacrilegi, pontifices Romani, quod sanguinem Christi eripuerunt populo. Praeterea iubet Apostolus Paulus ut in ipso coenae usu mortem domini annunciemus. Coenae administrationem non vult esse mutum spectaculum, quod alto silentio peragatur: Sed publica confessio sonare debet de Iesu Christo crucifixo & resuscitato: Ut hac publica voce & colligatur Ecclesia & excitetur & confirmetur nostra fides

Donec veniat) Primum docet quamdiu duraturus sit hic ritus in Ecclesia: Nimirum usque ad adventum filii Dei in nubibus, ad extremum usque diem, quo Deus Ecclesiam suam aeterna gloria est ornaturus. Non ergò alia Ecclesia forma, non alia Sacramenta sunt expectanda in hoc mundo. Deinde dulcem promissionem continent haec verba, nunquam interituram Ecclesiam in hoc mundo, quantumvis ea oppugnetur à tyrannis & haereticis, sed perpetuò sore in terris aliquem coetum, qui vera fiducia colat mediatorem & usu coenae domini alat & stabiliat suam fidem iuxta promissionem. Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consumationem seculi. Articulum quoque fidei hic tradit de glorioso adventu Iesu Christi in nubibus ad universale iudicium totius mundi: Quem gloriosum adventum & laetum diem nunc prae foribus esse cum ex multis indiciis pateat, tùm inde etiam recte colligitur, quod his postremis temporibus doctrina de caena domini gravissimè ab haereticis Sacramentariis oppugnatur, & hic Epicureus error magna sumit in multis regnis incrementa.

Quamobrem qui manducat panem hunc, & bibit calicem domini indignè, reus est corporis & sanguinis Domini.

Quia animadvertit Apostolus Paulus Corinthios magna securitate accedere ad mensam domini, perinde ac si ad usitatas epulas accederent, non solùm repetit institutionem coenae, verumetiam gravissimam addit comminationem, & monet eos, qui secure & sine motibus poenitentiae ad mensam domini accedunt, fieri reos corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi, quae cum sit culpa gravissima, quam Deus atroci supplicio punire solet, advigilandum est singulis, ut in timore domini & vera fide participent de corpore & sanguine Iesu Christi. Hic disertè refellit Paulus figmentum pontificiorum de transelementatione, vel annihilatione, vel transsubstantiatione panis in corpus Dei. Panem enim benedictum nominat panem. Verè enim manet substantia panis. Et tamen est corpus Christi verum, quia est medium per quod Christus corpus suum praebet nobis manducandum. Indignè edere panem benedictum, non est tantum minus reverenter accipere panem domini: Sed est secure, sine vera contritione, sine fiducia acquiescente in mediatore, & cum peccatis conscientiam vastantibus manducare panem Eucharistiae & bibere poculum domini, perinde ac si communis esset cibus & potus, atque ita corpus domini à communi pane non discernere. Iudas proditor indignè sumpsit corpus domini. Digne autem sumunt, qui seriam adferunt poenitentiam & veram fidem adhibent verbis Christi. Reum esse corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi est culpam sustinere iniuria et contumelia adfecti corporis Christi. Qui indigne & secure edit panem Eucharistiae, is, inquit Paulus, culpam sustinet iudicio Dei, quod contumelio se mactarit & iniuria adfecerit ipsum corpus Iesu Christi, sicuti Iudaei colaphis caedentes faciem Iesu Christi, atroci contumelia sanctissimum eius corpus adfecerunt. Hîc ergò rursus evidentissimè demonstratur vera praesentia corporis Iesu Christi in Sacra coena. Nemo enim reus fit corporis & sanguinis Christi, nisi qui corpus & sanguinem Christi adficit iniuria, cum ergò Paulus testetur indigne manducantes hunc panem et de hoc calice bibentes reos fieri corporis et sanguinis Iesu Christi, necesse est eos iniurta adficere corpus & sanguinem Christi, idque ipso esu & potu. Unde & paulo post dicit. Qui edit & bibit indigne, iudicium sibi edit & bibit. Si corpus Iesu Christi in coena praesens non esset, indigne sumentes panem Eucharistiae, nec contumelia adficerent ipso esu ipsum Christi corpus, nec tam tristi reatu sese abstringerent.

## 11:28
But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of this bread, and drink of this cup.

Because an unworthy and careless reception merits the most grievous wrath of God, and atrocious punishments, therefore he diligently exhorts the Corinthians that they should approach the table of the Lord in the fear of God, and first examine themselves. This examination, however, which the Apostle demands, is done through serious repentance, when a man first acknowledges his sins, fears the wrath of God, grieves that he has offended God, seriously detests idolatry, errors, crimes, and sins of every kind, which are accused in the word of God: And thus he shakes off carnal security. Then, indeed, he raises himself up by true faith and confidence in the mediator Jesus Christ, he apprehends the promise of grace, and determines that he, on account of Christ the mediator, is reconciled to God and is an heir of life. Whoever discovers in himself these movements of repentance, true contrition, and faith not feigned, he certainly can and ought to determine that he worthily perceives the body and blood of Jesus Christ. Not indeed is a man worthy of himself to perceive the body and blood of Jesus Christ, however much faith he may be endowed with, but all worthiness comes to him from the immense mercy of Him who in His son valued us as worthy of heavenly and spiritual goods. And the Son of God himself, just as all other things, so also offers and gives his body and blood freely out of his mere liberality and goodness to us to be eaten and drunk. Effort must therefore be made that we bring true faith to the synaxis: And that we cast away all sins devastating the conscience, and resist the depraved affections of the flesh. For he who indulges the affections of the flesh, loosens the reins to desires and proceeds in crimes against the conscience, he both lacks true faith, and if he thus approaches the table of the Lord without self-examination, he eats the body of Christ unworthily, and becomes guilty of the body and blood of Christ. Whence also Paul repeats and explains more clearly the prior threat.

For he who eats and drinks unworthily, eats and drinks judgment to himself: While he does not discern the body of the Lord.

We have said above what it is to eat and drink unworthily, namely to bring carnal security and an impenitent heart to the use of the Lord's supper, to be without contrition and true trust in the mediator, such a one, he says, eats and drinks judgment to himself. Lest anyone suspect that this secure man only affects Christ with insult by impenitence and diffidence, Paul testifies clearly that this guilt of the body of Christ is contracted by the very eating. He eats and drinks judgment to himself. It is necessary, therefore, that the body and blood of Christ be truly present in the bread and wine, and that both be received even by the unworthy, that is, by atheists, Epicureans, and hypocrites. Paul, however, also adds the cause of the fault and the guilt. While he does not discern the body of the Lord. On account of this cause alone the unworthy eater contracts guilt to himself, because he takes the blessed bread, which is the body of the Lord, for common bread, and does not discern the holy body of the Lord from the remaining foods. From which it is again evident that the unworthy eat the body of the Lord to judgment, for how could the body of the Lord be discerned from other foods in the sacred supper if it were not truly present? Nor would the blessed bread be the true Body of Christ. Let us therefore hold with firm assent this opinion of Paul, that even those who unworthily eat the blessed bread, eat the body of Jesus Christ, but to judgment and become guilty of the body of Christ. Therefore let us apply every diligence that we may test ourselves, and bring true motions of repentance to the sacred communion.

For this cause many among you are weak and sick, and a good part sleep. For if we would judge ourselves, we would not be judged

Latin:

Probet autem seipsum homo & sic de hoc pane edat, & de hoc calice bibat.

Quia indigna & secura sumptio meretur gravissimam Dei iram, & poenas atroces, idcirco diligenter hortatur Corinthios, ut in timore Dei ad mensam domini accedant, & sese prius probent. Haec autem probatio quam Apostolus flagitat, fit per seriam poenitentiam, cum homo primum agnoscit sua peccata, metuit iram Dei, dolet se offendisse Deum, serio detestatur idolatriam, errores, scelera et omnis generis peccata, quae accusantur in verbo Dei: Atque ita carnalem securitatem excutit. Deinde verò erigit sese vera fide atque fiducia in mediatorem Iesum Christum, adprehendit promissionem gratiae, & statuit se propter Christum mediatorem esse reconciliatum Deo & esse haeredem vitae. Qui hosce poenitentiae motus veram contritionem & fidem non simulatam in se deprehendit, is certò statuere & debet & potest, quod digne percipiat corpus & sanguinem Iesu Christi. Non quidem per se dignus est homo percipiendi corpus et sanguinem Iesu Christi, quantavis fide sit praeditus, sed omnis dignitas provenit ei ex immensa misericordia, qui in filio suo dignos nos aestimavit coelestium & spiritualium bonorum. Et ipse filius Dei ut caetera omnia, ita & corpus & sanguinem suum gratis ex mera sua liberalitate & bonitate offert & donat nobis manducandum & bibendum. Danda igitur est opera, ut veram fidem ad synaxin adseramus: Utque abiiciamus omnia peccata vastantia conscientiam, & repugnemus pravis carnis adfectibus. Qui enim indulget adfectibus carnis, laxat frena cupiditatibus & pergit in sceleribus contra conscientiam, is & vera fide caret, & si ita sine probatione sui ipsius ad mensam domini accedit, indigne sumit corpus Christi, & sit reus corporis & sanguinis Christi. Unde & Paulus repetit & clarius exponit priorem comminationem.

Qui enim indignè edit & bibit, iudicium sibi edit & bibit: Dum non discernit corpus domini.

Diximus suora quid sit indigne edere & bibere, nimirum carnalem securitatem & cor impoenitens adferre ad usum coenae domini, esse sine contritione & vera fiducia in mediatorem, talis inquit, edit & bibit sibi iudicium. Ne quis suspicetùr securum istum hominem tantum impoenitentia & diffidentia adficere Christum contumelia, disertè testatur Paulus reatum istum corporis Christi contrahi ipso esu. Edit & bibit sibi iudicium. Necesse est igitur verè praesens esse corpus & sanguinem Christi in pane & vino, & utrumque sumi etiam ab indignis, hoc est, atheis, Epicureis & hypocritis. Paulus verò etiam addit causam culpae & reatus. Dum non discernit corpus domini. Propter hanc causam tantum reatum contrahit sibi indigne manducans, quod panem benedictum, qui est corpus domini habet pro communi pane, non discernit corpus domini sauctum à reliquis cibis. Ex quo rursus patet indignos manducare corpus domini ad iudicium, quomodo enim in coena sacra corpus domini discerni posset ab aliis cibis, si non esset verè praesens? Nec panis benedictus esset verum Christi Corpus. Firmo igitur adsensu teneamus hanc Pauli sententiam, quod etiam indigne manducantes panem benedictum, edant corpus Iesu Christi, sed ad iudicium & rei fiant corporis Christi. Idcirco omnem diligentiam adhibeamus ut nos ipsos probemus, & veros poenitentiae motus ad sacram synaxin adferamus.
