Propterea multi inter vos sunt infirmi & aegroti, & bona pars dormit. Si enim nos ipsos iudicaremus, non iudicaremur

## 11:32
by the Lord. But when we are judged, we are chastened by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with this world.

The frequency of punishments, which God inflicts for this reason, demonstrates the gravity of the sin and the magnitude of the guilt which they commit by their security and unworthy reception. Because you Corinthians, says Paul, do not perform repentance seriously, but live securely and profane the supper of the Lord, therefore God sends various diseases upon you, and chastises you harshly, so that he may recall you to serious repentance. The life of many was shorter, for the reason that they provoked the wrath of God by their security. For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged by the Lord. This is: If we were seriously to dread the wrath of God, we would seriously perform repentance, we would shake off security, and in the true fear of God and trust in the mediator we would seek the mitigation of punishments, and the divine blessing, without doubt God would grant us both a longer and a happier life, and would more temper his wrath. For by repentance he not only forgives sins, and imputes righteousness, but also softens temporal chastisements, and does good in many ways. To Manasseh performing repentance, God mitigates the punishment and frees him from prison.

God spares the Ninevites as they perform penance and changes His sentence regarding the destruction of the city. Although God still harshly punishes David, who had returned to God with true penance, with exile and various calamities, He nevertheless dealt much better with him than if he had persisted in that impiety of his. Therefore, Paul here exhorts all Christians to penance, and to those performing penance he promises the mitigation of calamities, according to the promise Joel 2. Thus says the Lord. Turn to me with all your heart, in weeping, in fasting. Rend your heart and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, for He is beneficent, merciful, long-suffering, and of great goodness: who is led to penance over evil.

Papist writers wickedly corrupt this notable passage of Paul while they violently twist it toward their own feigned satisfactions. For what Paul says, If we would judge ourselves, they interpret thus: if we voluntarily undertake punishments, such as fastings, χαμεινιὰς, ἀγρυπνείας, if we enter a monastery, if we go on pilgrimage armored to holy places, if we lacerate our own body with rods, or whatever the conscience-tormenting little priest may have enjoined, then we satisfy God for sins and become immune from eternal punishments.

But nothing of these things came into the mind of the Apostle Paul. Nowhere does Paul teach that God is satisfied for sins by our punishments. For the death of the only Son of God, Jesus Christ, is the satisfaction for our sins, according to the saying: By his stripes we are healed. Ies: 53. Nor does Paul command that we afflict our bodies, but rather that we take care of the body and offer it its own honor; Christ says, the affliction of the day is sufficient: God has imposed enough miseries upon this wretched nature. It is enough if we patiently bear the calamities imposed by God. Therefore, to judge oneself is to acknowledge one's sins and to deplore them, to fear the wrath of God, and to grieve seriously that we have offended God, and with a suppliant voice and groaning to seek pardon from God.

But when we are judged, we are chastened by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with this world.

By Apostolic custom he mingles sweet consolation with threats and severe punishments: for he shows with what counsel and end God chastens his Church, namely not that he may destroy and soon cast it away into perdition, but that he may recall it to repentance, lest together with the secure world it may fall into eternal destruction. The world proclaims itself to be blessed, when it is permitted to live securely without hardships and calamities. But Paul warns that there is nothing more dangerous than that temporal security. For thus the world proceeds in wickedness, does not think about repentance, despises the judgment of God, only gapes after the pleasures of this life, and at length, oppressed by the judgment of God, is submerged into eternal damnation. But for this reason He chastises the pious with various diseases, hardships, exiles, and great calamities, so that He may bend their minds to repentance, may reveal His judgment to them, may shake off their carnal security, and may arouse in them a petition for the remission of sins and a desire for eternal life. Therefore, the calamities and miseries of the pious yield to them for good. First, let the reader observe here the distinction between the hardships of the pious and the calamities of the world. The hardships of the pious are fatherly chastisements, which yield to them for salvation, which are both mitigated by God, and at length are entirely taken away from them. But the calamities of the world are just punishments, and signs of the wrath of God, and the beginning of eternal damnation. Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and the Lord will deliver them out of them all. He keeps all their bones, not one of them shall be broken. But evil shall slay the wicked. Psal: 34. Then also the cause of the calamities Let the Church learn here. Therefore the Church is exercised by miseries so that it may perform penance, seriously seek the remission of sins, lest it imitate the security of the world, but fear the judgment of God, and avoid sins.

Latin:

à Domino. Cùm autem iudicamur, à domino corripimur, ne cum hoc mundo damnemur.

Gravitatem peccati & culpae magnitudinem, quam committunt securitate sua & indigna sumptione demonstrat frequentia poenarum, quas Deus propterea infligit. Quia vos Corinthii, inquit Paulus, non serio agitis poenitentiam, sed vivitis secure & prophanatis coenam Domini, idcirco Deus varios morbos vobis immittit, & duriter castigat, ut vos ad seriam poenitentiam revocet. Multorum vita fuit brevior, eo quod securitate iram Dei provocarunt Si enim nos iudicaremus, non iudicaremur à domino. Hoc est: Si serio expavesceremus iram Dei, ferio ageremus poenitentiam, excuteremus securitatem, & in vero timore Dei & fiducia mediatoris peteremus poenarum mitigationem, & divinam benedictionem bauà dubiè & longiorem & beatiorem vitam nobis largiretur Deus, & magis temperaret suam iram. A gentibus enim poenitentiam non solum condonat peccata, & imputat iustitiam, verumetiam lenit temporales castigationes, & multis modis benefacit. Manassae agenti poenitentiam, mitigat Deus poenam & liberat eum ex carcere.

Ninivitis agentibus poenitentiam parcit Deus & mutat suam sententiam de delenda urbe. Etsi Deus Davidem, qui vera poenitentia ad Deum redierat duriter adhuc castigat exilio & variis calamitatibus, tamen multo melius egit cum ipso, quam si in impietate sua illa perstitisset. Hortatur ergò hîc Paulus omnes Christianos ad poenitentiam, & poenitentiam agentibus promittit calamitatum mitigationem, iuxta promissionem Ioel 2. Sic dicit Dominus. Convertimini ad me in toto corde vestro, in fletu, in ieiunio. Scindite cor vestrum & non vestimenta vestra, & convertimini ad Dominum Deum vestrum, quia beneficus est, misericors, longanimis & multae bonitatis: qui poenitentia ducitur super malo.

Hunc insignem locum Pauli flagiciose depravant pontificii scriptores: dum eum ad ementitas suas satisfactiones violenter contorquent. Quod enim Paulus dicit. Si nos ipsos iudicaremus, illi sic interpretantur, si nos sponte suscipiamus castigationes, ut ieiunia, χαμεινιὰς, ἀγρυπνείας, si ingrediamur monasterium, si peregrinemur cataphracti ad loca sancta, si virgis proprium corpus laceremus, aut quidquid conscientiae carnifex sacrificulus iniunxerit, tum nos satisfacere Deo pro peccatis, & fieri immunes à poenis aeternis.

Verúm Apostolo Paulo nihil horum venit in mentem. Nuspiam docet Paulus nostris castigationibus satisfieri Deo pro peccatis. Solius enim filii Dei Iesu Christi mors satisfactio est pro nostris peccatis, iuxta dictum. Livore ipsius sanati sumus. Ies: 53. Nec iubet Paulus, ut corpora nostra adfligamus, sed potius ut corporis curam agamus & ei suum praebeamus honorem, sufficit inquit Christus diei adflictio sua: satis miseriarum Deus imposuit huic miserae naturae. Satis est si à Deo impositas calamitates patienter feramus. Sese igitur iudicare est, sua peccata agnoscere & deplorare iram Dei extimescere, & serio dolere, quod Deum offenderimus, & supplici voce & gemitu veniam à Deo petere.

Cùm autem iudicamur, à Domino corripimur, ne cum hoc mundo damnemur.

Consuetudine Apostolica comminationibus & severis castigationibus immiscet dulcem consolationem: ostendit enim quo consilio & fine castiget suam Ecclesiam Deus, nimirum non ut perdat & mox abiiciat in interitum, sed ut revocet eam ad poenitentiam, ne unà cum securo mundo ruat in perpetuum exitium. Mundus praedicat se beatum esse, cum licet ei secure vivere sine aerumnis & calamitatibus. Sed Paulus monet ista temporali securitate nihil esse periculosius. Sic enim mundus pergit in sceleribus, non cogitat de poenitentia, contemnit iudicium Dei, tantum inhiat huius vitae voluptatibus & tandem oppressus iudicio Dei, mergitur in aeternam damnationem. Pios autem ideò castigat variis morbis, aerumnis, exiliis, & magnis calamitatibus, ut flectat eorum animos ad poenitentiam, patefaciat eis suum iudicium, excutiat eis securitatem carnalem, exuscitet in eis petitionem remissionis peccatorum & desiderium vitae aeternae. Ergò calamitates & miseriae piorum cedunt ipsis in bonam. Primùm observet hic lector discrimen inter aerumnas piorum, & calamitates mundi. Piorum aerumnae sunt paternae castigationes, quae ipsis cedunt in salutem, quae & mitigantur à Deo, & tandem penitus auferuntur ab ipsis. At mundi calamitates sunt Iusta supplicia, & signa irae Dei, & initium aeternae damnationis. Multae tribulationes iustorum, & de omnibus hîc liberabit eos dominus. Custodit omnia ossa eorum, unum ex his non conteretur. Impium verò interficiet malum. Psal: 34. Deinde & causam calamitatum Ecclesiae hic discat. Ideò exerceri Ecclesiana miseriis ut agat poenitentiam, serio petat remissionem peccatorum, ne imitetur mundi securitatem, sed metuat Dei iudicium, & vitet peccata.

## 11:33-34
Wherefore my brethren, when you come together to eat, wait for one another. If any man hunger, let him eat at home; that you come not together unto judgment: and the rest I will set in order when I come.

He concludes the passage concerning the Lord's Supper and repeats the admonition, that they may come together in the fear of the Lord to celebrate the Eucharist, lest by their security they summon upon themselves judgment and punishment. That which he promises he will set in order the rest when he comes, the Papists, the depravers of Scripture, transfer to their own fictitious traditions.

As if the Apostle Paul had delivered many more things to the Churches, which are necessary to be known for salvation. Which, however, he did not commit to writing. But they do an injury to the Pauline words. For those things which are necessary to be known for salvation, he has consigned to his epistles. And in the Epistle to the Romans, Galatians, and Ephesians, the whole body of Christian doctrine is complex. But here he treats of indifferent things, and of certain external rites and customs, of the order of readings and sermons, of the manner of convening the assembly, and of the order of distributing the supper. As when some new Church is to be instituted in that place where before the worship of idols and foul confusion flourished, there is need of some prudent Pastor who may arrange individual things, where and when it is to be convened, in what order and manner sermons are to be held and Psalms sung, and the supper is to be distributed. The Corinthians, as men ingenious and proud, undoubtedly contended among themselves; one approved this order, another prescribed that. Paul therefore promises that he will come and will rightly arrange all things in the Church, namely concerning the instituting of meetings, concerning the order of readings, concerning the collection of alms, concerning having care of the poor, and similar indifferent things, in which salvation does not consist, for whether those things are arranged in this or that way, provided they are done in order and decently, it is the same.

Latin:

Quare fratres mei, quando convenitis ad edendum vos invicem expectate. Si autem quis esurit domi edat, ne ad iudicium conveniatis: reliqua cùm venero disponam.

Concludit locum de coena domini & repetit commonefactionem, ut in timore domini conveniant ad celebrandam Eucharistiam, ne sibi accersant sua securitate iudicium & poenam. Quod promittit se reliqua dispositurum cum venerit, pontificii scripturae depravatores ad suas commentitias traditiones transferunt.

Quasi Paulus Apostolus multo plura tradiderit Ecclesiis, quae ad salutem cognitu sint necessaria. Quae tamen literis non mandarit. Verum iniuriam faciunt verbis paulinis. Ea enim, quae ad salutem cognitu necessaria sunt, suis epistolis consignavit. Et in Epistola ad Rom: Galatas & Ephesios, totum doctrinae Christianae corpus est complexus. De adiaphoris verò hic agit, & externis quibusdam ritibus & consuetudinibus, de ordine lectionum & concionum, de modo convocandi coetum, & distribuendi ordine coenam. Ut cum nova aliqua Ecclesia instituenda est in eo loco, ubi antea viguit idolorum cultus, et foeda confusio prudente aliquo Pastore opus est, qui singula disponat, ubi & quando sit conveniendum, quo ordine & modo & conciones habendae & Psalmi canendi, & coena sit distribuenda, Corinthii ut homines ingeniosi et superbi, haud dubiè inter se certabant, alius hunc probabat ordinem, alius istum praescribebat. Paulus ergò promittit, se venturum & omnia rectè dispositurum in Ecclesia, nimirum de instituendis congressibus, de ordine lectionum, de collectione Eleemosynarum, de habenda cura pauperum, et similibus adiaphoris, in quibus non consistit salus, sive enim ista vel hoc vel illo modo disponantur, modo ordine & decenter fiant, perinde est.

## 11:34 Places of Doctrine
Places of Doctrine.

1. Concerning the traditions of the Apostles: Which are not to be sought from elsewhere than from the Apostolic writings. For those things which they delivered by mouth to the Churches, those they also committed to letters, and left monuments to the Churches, so that they might have certain foundations of faith. Those things which are peddled by the papists as Apostolic traditions, and either do not have testimonies of sacred scripture, or are diametrically opposed to it: are to be held as most impudent lies.

2. Concerning the order, which God instituted in the Church and the whole human race, that Christ is the head of the man, that is, of the whole Church. For all governors and ministers of the Church have all dignity, help, and wisdom from Christ. But the man is the head of the woman. For the woman has all dignity and splendor from the man: to whom she owes obedience and reverence according to the ordinance of God.

3. That the customs of the Church ought to be modest and honest: Women ought to be adorned with a veiled head, so that they may testify that they acknowledge their husbands as lords.

3. Concerning the presence of angels in the Church.

4. That the doctrine of Christ does not abolish the judgment of nature, which makes a distinction between honorable and shameful things, but rather confirms and illuminates it.

5. That the Churches of God do not have the custom of contending and litigating without end about things that are open and known by nature. Therefore, he shows himself to be a stranger to the Church of Christ, who is eager for unnecessary contentions.

6. That heresies and scandals arise in the Church of Christ: and that God permits this to happen to this end, that those who are approved and firm in the faith may become more conspicuous.

7. Concerning the abuses of the Lord's Supper, which crept into the Corinthian Church. The secure and hypocrites did not believe that the blessed bread was the true and substantial body of Jesus Christ. But they held it for common bread: And they approached the Supper of the Lord without repentance, and in the public assemblies of the Church they invited themselves liberally to cups.

8. Doctrine concerning the institution of the Lord's Supper.

9. Concerning the causes of the calamities and miseries of the Church. With what counsel God afflicts his own, namely, that they may not be condemned with this world.

Latin:

Loci Doctrinae.

1. De traditionibus Apostolorum: Quae non sunt aliunde petendae, quam ex scriptis Apostolicis. Quae enim ore tradiderunt Ecclesiis, ea etiam literis mandarunt, & monumenta reliquerunt Ecclesiis, ut certa haberent fidei fundamenta. Quae à pontificiis, pro traditionibus Apostolicis venditantur, & vel sacrae scripturae testimonia non habent, vel ei ex diametro adversantur: pro impudentissimis mendaciis sunt habenda.

2. De ordine, quem Deus in Ecclesia & toto genere humano instituit, ut Christus sit caput viri, hoc est, totius Ecclesiae. Omnes enim gubernatores & ministri Ecclesiae omnem dignitatem, auxilium & sapientiam à Christo habent. Vir autem est caput mulieris. Omnem enim dignitatem & splendorem habet mulier à viro: Cui obedientiam & reverentiam iuxta Dei ordinationem debet.

3. Quod mores Ecclesiae verecundi & honenesti esse debent: Mulieres velato capite ornari debent, ut testentur se maritos agnoscere dominos.

3. De praesentia angelorum in Ecclesia.

4. Quod doctrina Christi non aboleat iudicium naturae, quod facit discrimen honestorum & turpium, sed potius confirmet illud atque illustret.

5. Quod Ecclesiae Dei non habeant consuetudinem sine fine contendendi & litigandi de rebus apertis & natura notis. Alienum ergo se esse ostendit ab Ecclesia Christi, qui studet contentionibus non necessariis.

6. Quòd in Ecclesia Christi exoriantur haereses & scandala: quodque Deus id fieri permittat hoc fine ut probati & firmi in fide fiant conspectiores.

7. De abusibus coenae dominicae, qui irrepserunt in Ecclesiam Corinthiacam. Non crediderunt securi & hypocritae, panem benedictum esse verum & substantiale corpus Iesu Christi. Sed pro communi pane habuerunt: Et sine poenitentia ad coenam Domini accesserunt, & in publicis Ecclesiae congressibus largiter sese poculis invitarunt.

8. Doctrina de institutione coenae Domini.

9. De causis calamitatum & miseriarum Ecclesiae. Quo consilio suos adfligat Deus nimirum, ne cum hoc mundo damnentur.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII.

In this chapter the Apostle Paul teaches the Corinthian Church what is to be thought concerning spiritual gifts, from whom they proceed, to what end they are given to the pious, what kind of distinctions of gifts there are in the Church, how they are to be used for the illustration of the glory of God and the edification of the Church of Christ as they must be used. For the Corinthians, after they had embraced the doctrine of the Apostles, and were baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, through the laying on of the hands of the Apostles, they were adorned with the visible outpouring of the Holy Spirit and instructed with excellent spiritual gifts: so that they both spoke in various tongues, uttered prophecies, explained the holy scripture, and performed miracles. But with these gifts, certain of the Corinthians exalted themselves, especially the false apostles; they endeavored to show off their knowledge of languages in assemblies, they sought popular favor with eloquence, they began to grow proud in their gifts, and to despise others in comparison to themselves, and they affected the highest ranks in the ministry so that they might stand out above others; just as if the Holy Spirit had established a field of vain glory, and had given His gifts for the purpose of suppressing and despising others. Therefore, the Apostle Paul gravely censures this great error and foul abuse of gifts by the Spirit in this place. And he teaches that they are conferred by God upon the pious for a far different purpose, namely, that they may serve the glory of God, build up and adorn the Church, and benefit individuals in the Church. Pride, emulation, contempt for those of lower status, and envy ought to be far removed from pious men, who are citizens in the kingdom of Christ.

And that he may obtain piety and modesty from his Corinthians in the use of the gifts, four most grave reasons he uses. First, he recalls to their memory what sort of people they were before their conversion and illumination, that at that time they were destitute of all knowledge of God, and had defiled themselves with foul idolatry. Therefore, they ought not now to plume themselves. Second, he shows the author of the gifts, namely, not our free will, not the sharpness of our wit or the excellence of our nature: But the eternal God the Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit. It is right, therefore, that we use the gifts that have proceeded from God for the glory of God. Third, he teaches that we Christians are members of one body, from which he teaches us to strive with no rivalry, to labor with no envy toward one another, but rather to promote the common salvation of the whole body, to assist the common advantage and honor. Fourth, he explains what degrees and what distinctions both of offices and of gifts God has placed in the Church, that in one place he has placed Apostles, in another prophets, in another teachers in the Church. Therefore, each one ought to be content with his own place and gift and to take pains that he may adorn his station and prove his faith to God and the Church. This doctrine and admonition is necessary in the extreme. For the pride of teachers, who have preferred themselves to others on account of their gifts, has often troubled the Church of Christ, as has rivalry, envy, and the affectation of a higher degree in the ministry. Samosatenus While he prides himself on the gifts of eloquence and talent, and despises the rest, he has inflicted a grave wound upon the Church. Arius aspires to the Alexandrian Episcopate: and when he sees another preferred before him, he feigns a new kind of doctrine so that he may become famous. Nestorius, relying on his loquacity and rank, undertakes the patronage of error, and wickedly tears the Church apart. John of Antioch envies the gifts of Cyril, Bishop of Alexandria, to whom he was equal neither in erudition, nor in piety, nor in zeal, nor in φιλοπονίᾳ,, nor in constancy: therefore he deforms him before the Emperors and the Ephesian synod. And at all times these plagues have most gravely afflicted the Church; therefore this admonition of the Apostle must often be repeated.

Latin:

CAPUT XII.

In hoc capite Apostolus Paulus docet Ecclesiam Corinthiacam, quid de spiritualibus donis sit sentiendum, à quo illa proficiscantur, in quem finem dentur piis, qualia sint discrimina donorum in Ecclesia, quomodo iis ad gloriae Dei illustrationem & Ecclesiae Christi aedificationem sit utendum. Corinthii enim postquam doctrinam Apostolorum sunt amplexi, & in nomine Iesu Christi baptizati per impositionem manuum Apostolorum Spiritus sancti visibili effusione ornati sunt & excellentibus donis spiritualibus instructi: ita ut & variis linguis loquerentur, vaticinia ederent, sacram scripturam explicarent, & miracula ederent. His verò donis quidam ex Corinthiis sese efferebant in primis pseudoapostoli, noticiam linguarum conabantur ostentare in congressibus, eloquentia quaerebant auram popularem, superbire incipiebant in donis, & alios prae se contemnere, & summos gradus in ministerio adfectabant ut super alios eminerent; perinde ac si Spiritus sanctus gloriae inanis campum instituisset, & dona sua dedisset ad premendos & contemnendos alios. Hunc ergò grandem errorem & tetrum abusum donorum, Spiritus graviter hoc loco taxat Apostolus Paulus. Et docet longè alio consilio ea conferri à Deo piis, nimirum, ut servtant gloriae Dei, aedificent atque ornent Ecclesiam, & singulis in Ecclesia prosint. Superbiam, aemulationem, contemptum inferiorum, invidiam procul oportere abesse à piis hominibus, qui cives sunt in regno Christi.

Utque à suis Corinthiis obtineat pietatem & modestiam in usurpatione donorum, quatuor gravissimis rationibus utitur. Primùm revocat illis in memoriam, quales fuerint ante conversionem & illuminationem, quod tum omni cognitione Dei destituti fuerint, & foeda Idolatria sese contaminaverint. Ideò nunc cristas sumere non debent. Secundo ostendit authorem donorum, nimirum non liberum nostrum arbitrium, non ingenii nostri acumen aut praestantiam naturae: Sed aeternum Deum patrem, Iesum Christum, & Spiritum sanctum. Aequum est igitur ut donis à Deo profectis ad Dei gloriam utamur. Tertio docet nos Christianos unius corporis membra esse, unde doceat nos nulla certare aemulatione, nulla laborare invidia invicem, sed potius communem totius corporis salutem promovere, commodum atque decus commune adiuvare. Quartò exponit, quos gradus & quae discrimina cum officiorum tum donorum posuit Deus in Ecclesia, quod alio loco Apostolos, alio prophetas, alio doctores in Ecclesia posuerit. Unumquemque igitur suo loco & dono debere contentum esse & id operam dare, ut suam stationem ornet & fidem suam Deo & Ecclesiae probet. Haec ad modum necessaria est doctrina & commonefactio. Saepe enim turbavit Ecclesiam Christi, superbia doctorum, qui se propter dona praetulerunt aliis, Item aemulatio, invidia, adfectatio altioris gradus in ministerio. Samosatenus dum donis facundiae & ingenii superbit, & reliquos contemnit, grave vulnus inflixit Ecclesiae. Arrius adfectat Episcopatum Alexandrinum: et cum alterum sibi praeferri videt, fingit novum genus doctrinae ut inclarescat. Nestorius fretus sua loquacitate & gradu erroris patrocinium suscipit, & sceleratè scindit Ecclesiam. Ioannes Antiochenus invidet donis Cyrilli Alexandrini Episcopi, cui nec eruditione, nec pietate, nec zelo, nec φιλοπονίᾳ, nec constantia par erat: deformat ergò ipsum apud Imperatores & synodum Ephesinam. Atque omnibus temporibus hae pestes gravissimè adflixerunt Ecclesiam, saepe igitur haec Apostoli commonefactio repetenda est.

## 12:1-3
Concerning spiritual things however, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant. You know that when you were Gentiles, you were led away to mute idols, just as you were being led. Therefore I make it known to you, that no one of those who speaks in the Spirit of God says Jesus is anathema. And no one can say Lord Jesus, except in the Holy Spirit.

It is the command of Paul, that the Corinthians or anyone in the Church should not be proud of their gifts, or abuse them to emulation, envy, and contentions, which tend toward the destruction of the Church, but rather that individuals might contribute their gifts to the illustration of the glory of Christ and the edification of the Church. The first argument is taken from a comparison of the blindness, ignorance, and most miserable condition of the Corinthians under paganism before their conversion, with that illustrious light, knowledge, wisdom, and gifts with which they were adorned when converted to God. For the old condition of man, and that a most miserable one, deservedly admonishes them of modesty. The miserable state of the Gentiles and of all men who are ignorant of God and are aliens from the kingdom of Christ cannot be explained by any speech. For they live in horrendous darkness, they contaminate themselves with horrible idolomania; the Gentiles worshipped fever, pallor, Bellona, Priapus, Boreas, cats, and crocodiles as divinities. They committed most foul crimes in their sacred rites, by which they attempted to appease the divinities; they slaughtered human victims. In no necessity did they have firm consolation, they did not understand the benefits of the mediator, and at length with gnashing they were plunged into eternal destruction. Thus in the papacy also we were ignorant of the true God, and were led by errors; one worshipped Anna, another Catherine, another Paul, another the three kings, another the consecrated bread. Since He has led us out of such great darkness God by the ministry of the word and through the illumination of the Holy Spirit, it always behooves us to be mindful of this so great a benefit, and with modesty and true humility to declare our gratitude toward God. For he who exalts himself because of gifts, he has forgotten what sort of person he was before. But because he is about to speak next concerning the distinction of spiritual gifts in the Church, he first distinguishes the pious from the impious, and treats of a general gift, which ought to be in all the pious. It is not necessary that all the pious be instructed with similar or the same gifts: it is not necessary that Timothy be instructed with equal eloquence and knowledge of the mysteries of God as the Apostle Paul or as the prophet Isaiah. This, however, is necessary, that all the pious be illuminated and led by the Holy Spirit. For he who does not have the Spirit of Christ, is not his. Romo 8. Item, But because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his son into your hearts, crying abba father Galat: 4. But whether anyone is ruled by the Holy Spirit, this can be known by a most evident argument, if anyone loves Jesus Christ and confesses his name.

No one, he says, speaking by the Spirit of God, says Jesus is anathema. Therefore, whoever either openly or secretly curses the son of God Jesus Christ, he ought to determine for certain that he is a stranger to the Holy Spirit, and is led by the spirit of lying. Christ Jesus for the Holy Spirit always glorifies. Not only Arians, Photinians, but all the impious, who defile or persecute the doctrine of Christ, call him anathema: And by that very fact they testify by what Spirit they are ruled.

And no one, he says, can call Jesus Lord, except by the Holy Spirit. Paul warns that it is a spiritual light by which we recognize Jesus Christ to be the eternal and omnipotent Lord. Reason and Philosophy by no means teach this; indeed, they boldly contradict this doctrine. It cannot happen, therefore, that anyone should believe in Jesus Christ and in faith call him Lord, unless he has received this light from the Holy Spirit and has been confirmed. Paul is not speaking of a feigned confession of the name of Christ, such as many hypocrites utter when out of danger; of whom Christ says: Not everyone who says to me Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven: But of a confession which proceeds from true faith, and which invokes Jesus as Lord and creator of heaven and earth in every necessity. And the conscience of each one can determine whether he truly from the heart, or indeed feignedly, calls Jesus Lord: and from this he can determine whether he is illuminated and ruled by the Holy Spirit. For he does not teach this only so that we may be able to make a judgment about others, but primarily he instructs us how to examine ourselves so that we may be able to know whether we are of the number of the saints and citizens of the kingdom of Christ. Judgment is not always to be made from excellent gifts. You are not on that account a stranger to the kingdom of Christ and the benefits of the mediator, because you do not possess various languages, because you are not the equal of Chrysostom in eloquence of speech, because you do not raise the dead, as the Apostle Peter did. But if you truly confess Jesus Christ in faith as Lord and almighty God, it is certain that you are an heir of eternal life, and that you are led by the Holy Spirit, whether you are adorned with great or small gifts. Again, it can happen that someone may have the remarkable gifts of various languages, of singular eloquence, of prudence, of miracles: and yet say anathema to the Son of God, be secure, impenitent, a hypocrite, an atheist, despise the benefits of the mediator; it is certain that this man is not led by the Spirit of God, nor has a part in the kingdom of God, as Achitophel was famous for the gift of both wisdom and eloquence: But by his impiety he showed that he did not believe in the Messiah. Balaam was endowed with the gift of prophesying: and yet he did not obtain salvation: because he was impenitent. To this, therefore, one must look first of all, that one may truly love and confess Jesus Christ as Lord, from which he can determine that he is ruled by the Spirit of God and is a son of God. This opinion of Paul overturns the presumption of free will; for if no one in faith and truly He can call Jesus Lord, except in the Holy Spirit. Therefore there is no power of free will in spiritual matters: Therefore man cannot strive of himself toward the kingdom of heaven. For without the acknowledgment of Jesus Christ no salvation can happen to any man. Shamefully therefore do the Synergists and all patrons of free will err, who attribute to the will not reborn by the Holy Spirit the power or any little faculty of applying itself to grace or of assenting or of agreeing to the word. To call Jesus anathema is either openly to curse Christ as Decius, Diocletian, Julian, Crescens Celsus, Lucian, and their likes did, or to treat Christ with contumely by false and blasphemous doctrine. The Roman Pontiffs, while they call themselves Vicars of Christ, and deny that they can err, and condemn and persecute the doctrine concerning Christ the mediator, call Jesus anathema. The monks trust in their own works in the sight of God, they call Jesus anathema. The popish mass-priests, while they say in the blasphemous mass that they offer Christ for the living and the dead, call Jesus anathema. All the impious also, who remain without repentance, and securely contemn the benefits of the mediator, or laugh at the doctrine of the Church, call Jesus anathema in their heart, whatever they may profess with their mouth, or simulate by their external life. On the contrary, to call Jesus Lord is not only to think rightly concerning the person of Jesus Christ, that he is true man and eternal God, but also to understand his benefits and to embrace them by faith, and to place hope in this Lord of the world, and to assent to the universal doctrine of Jesus Christ. The Calvinists, because they call into doubt the words of Jesus Christ by which he instituted the holy supper, do not call Jesus Lord: for they do not offer him the obedience of faith. Luther, however, calls Jesus Lord: because in all his writings he breathes nothing but Jesus Christ crucified and resurrected and sitting at the right hand of the eternal Father.

Latin:

De spiritualibus autem fratres, nolo vos ignorare. Scitis quod quando gentes eratis, ad muta Idola currebatis pro ut ducebamini. Propterea notum vobis facio, quod nemo eorum, qui in Spiritu Dei loquitur, dicit Iesum anathema. Et nemo potest dicere dominum Iesum, nisi in Spiritu sancto.

Praeceptum Pauli est, ne Corinthii vel quispiam in Ecclesia superbiat suis donis, aut iis abutatur ad aemulationem, invidiam, contentiones, quae vergunt ad destructionem Ecclesia, sed potius ut singuli dona sua conferant ad illustrationem gloriae Christi & aedificationem Ecclesiae. Primùm argumentum sumit à collatione coecitatis, ignorantiae, & miserrimae conditionis Corinthiorum sub gentilismo ante conversionem, cum praeclara illa luce, agnitione, sapientia & donis, quibus conversi ad Deum ornati sunt. Vetus enim conditio hominis, eaque, miserrima merito eos modestiae admonet. Nulla oratione exponi potest miser status gentilium & omnium hominum, qui Deum ignorant, & à regno Christi alieni sunt. In horrendis enim tenebris vivunt, horribili Idolomania sese contaminant, Gentes febrim, pallorem, Bellonam, Priapum, Boream, feles & crocodilos, pro numinibus adorarunt. Foedissima scelera in sacris patrarunt, quibus numina placare conati sunt, mactarunt hostias humanas. In nulla necessitate firmam habuerunt consolationem, non intellexerunt beneficia mediatoris, & tandem cum fremitu demersae sunt in aeternum exitium. Sic in papatu quoque Deum verum ignorabamus, & erroribus ducebamur, alius Annam, alius Catharinam, alius Paulum, alius tres reges, alius panem consecratum adorabat. Ex tantis tenebris cum nos eduxerit Deus ministerio verbi & per illuminationem Spiritus sancti, semper decet nos esse memores huius tanti beneficii, & modestia & humilitate vera nostram erga Deum declarare gratitudinem. Qui enim effert sese donis, ille oblitus est qualis antea fuerit. Quia verò deinceps de discrimine donorum spiriritualium in Ecclesia dicturus est, primum discernit pios ab impiis, & de generali dono agit, quod in omnibus piis esse oportet. Non necesse est omnes pios similibus aut eisdem donis esse instructos: non necesse est Timotheum pari eloquentia & cognitione mysteriorum Dei instructum esse, cum Apostolo Paulo aut cum propheta Esaia. Hoc autem necesse est, ut omnes pii à Spiritu sancto illuminentur et ducantur. Qui enim Spiritum Christi non habet, non est eius. Romo 8. Item, Quia autem filii estis, misit Deus Spiritum filii sui in corda vestra, clamentem abba pater Galat: 4. An verò quis Spiritu sancto regatur, hoc evidentissimo argumento cognosci potest, si quis Christum Iesum diligat & nomen eius confiteatur.

Nullus inquit per Spiritum Dei loquens, dicit Iesum anathema. Ergò quicunque filio Dei Iesu Christo aut aperte aut clam maledicit, is certo statuere debet, quod à Spiritu sancto alienus sit, & à Spiritu mendacii ducatur. Christum Iesum enim semper glorificat Spiritus sanctus. Non tantum Arriam, Photiniani, sed omnes impii, qui conspurcant aut persequuntur doctrinam Christi, anathema eum dicunt: Et eo ipso testantur à quo Spiritu regantur.

Et nemo inquit potest Iesum vocare dominum, nisi per Spiritum sanctum. Monet Paulus spiritualem esse lucem, qua agnoscimus Iesum Christum esse aeternum & omnipotentem dominum. Ratio & Philosophia nequaquam hoc docent, imò audacter isti doctrinae contradicunt. Fieri ergò non potest, ut quis in Iesum Christum credat et in fide Dominum eum vocet, nisi à Spiritu sancto hanc lucem perceperit, et confirmatus fuerit. Non loquitur Paulus de simulata confessione nominis Christi, qualem multi hypocritae extra periculum edunt; de quibus Christus dicit. Non omnis, qui dicit mihi Domine Domine, intrabit in regnum coelorum: Sed de confessione, quae ex vera fide proficiscitur, et quae Iesum ut Dominum et conditorem coeli et terre in omni necessitate invocat. Ac uniuscuiusque conscientia statuere potest, num verè ex animo, an verò simulatè Iesum vocet Dominum: & hinc se statuere potest, num Spiritu sancto illuminetur & regatur. Non enim hoc solum docet, quomodo de aliis iudicium facere possimus, sed inprimis erudit nos, quomodo nos ipsos explorare possimus, num simus è numero sanctorum & civium regni Christi. Ex donis excellentibus non semper est faciendum iudicium. Non propterea alienus es à regno Christi & beneficiis mediatoris, quod non tenes varias linguas, quod facundia sermonis non es par Chrysostomo, quod non resuscitas mortuos, ut Apostolus Petrus fecit. Sed si Iesum Christum verè in fide fateris Dominum & Deum omnipotentem, certum est te esse haeredem vitae aeternae, & te duci Spiritu sancto, sive magnis, sive parvis donis sis ornatus. Rusus fieri potest, ut quis praeclara habeat dona variarum linguarum, eloquentiae singularis, prudentiae, miraculorum: & tamen anathema dicat filio Dei, sit securus, impoenitens, hypocrita, atheos, contemnat beneficia mediatoris, hunc certum est non duci Spiritu Dei, nec habere partem in regno Dei, ut Achitophel & dono sapientiae & eloquentiae clarus erat: Sed impietate sua ostendit quod in Messiam non credidit. Bileam praeditus suit dono vaticinandi: & tamen salutem non est adeptus: quia fuit impoenitens. Huc ergò inprimis respiciendum est, ut quis verè Iesum Christum Dominum diligat & confiteatur, unde statuere potest, quod Spiritu Dei regatur & sit filius Dei. Haec Pauli sententia evertit liberi arbitrii praesumptionem; Si enim nemo in fide & verè Iesum potest vocare dominum, nisi in Spiritu sancto. Ergò nulla est vis liberi arbitrii in spiritualibus: Ergò homo ex sese ad regnum coelorum contendere non potest. Nam sine agnitione Iesu Christi nulla satus ulli homini contingere potest. Turpiter igitur errant Synergistae & omnes liberi arbitrii patroni, qui voluntati non renatae per Spiritum sanctum tribuunt vim vel facultatulam aliquam adplicandi sese ad gratiam vel adsentiendi vel annuendi verbo. Iesum dicere anathema, est vel palàm maledicere Christo ut Decius, Diocletianus, Iulianus, Crescens Celsus, Lucianus, & similes fecerunt, vel falsa & blaspema doctrina Christum contumelia adficere. Pontifices Romani dum se Vicarios Christi adpellant, & se errare posse negant, & doctrinam de mediatore Christo damnant & persequuntur, anathema dicunt Iesum. Monachidum suis operibus confidunt in conspectu Dei, anathema dicunt Iesum. Sacrificuli pontificii dum in blasphema missa dicunt se offerre Christum pro vivis & mortuis, anathema dicunt Iesum. Omnes etiam impii, qui manent sine poenitentia, & secure contemnunt beneficia mediatoris, aut rident doctrinam Ecclesiae, Anathema dicunt Iesum in corde, quidquid ore profiteantur, vel simulent externa vita. Contrà, Iesum vocare dominum est non solum rectè sentire de personae Iesu Christi, quod sit verus homo et aeternus Deus, verùmetiam eius beneficia intelligere & fide amplecti, & spem in istum Dominum mundi collocare, & universae doctrinae Iesu Christi adsentiri. Calvinistae quia verba Iesu Christi, quibus sacram coenam instituit, vocant in dubium, non vocant Iesum dominum: non enim praestant ei obedientiam fidei. Lutherus verò vocat Iesum Dominum: quia in omnibus suis scriptis nihil spirat, nisi Iesum Christum crucifixum & resuscitatum & sedentem ad dexteram aeterni patris.

## 12:4-7
There are divisions of gifts, but the same Spirit. And there are divisions of ministries, but the same Lord. And there are divisions of operations, but the same God, who works all things in all, but to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit, as it is expedient.

This second is the reason, taken from the efficient cause of spiritual gifts, and from the final cause: By which he proves that one must not be proud in gifts, that no one is to be envied on account of gifts, that no struggles, no contentions about gifts are to be stirred up, but rather that effort is to be given by individuals, so that with the gifts bestowed by God they are used for the glory of God and the edification of the Church. The common gift, which is necessary for each person for salvation, namely, the acknowledgment of Jesus Christ and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, has been bestowed upon each pious person. For without this gift, salvation could not be established for a man, but the remaining gifts, in which our salvation does not consist, but which contribute to building up and adorning the Church, it is not necessary that they be equal in each person. For the very diversity of the gifts bears witness to the immense wisdom of the Spirit. For it is not to be thought that, just as spiritual gifts are dissimilar and diverse, so also are the Holy Spirits multiple and diverse. But one and the same is the Holy Spirit, who distributes such diverse gifts; thus also, if there are many and diverse offices in the Church—for one is an Apostle, another a Prophet, another a Teacher, another a Bishop, another a Pastor, another a Deacon, another a Tutor, another a Governor—nevertheless, there is only one Lord, who presides over all ministers and is about to demand an account of the performed duty from each one; thus, although the operations or powers are various, as Peter raises the dead and kills Ananias with a word; Paul heals the sick, casts off the viper clinging to his hand, strikes Elymas with blindness; Jonathan with his armor-bearer turns a whole army to flight: nevertheless, there are not many gods, but one is God, who works all things in all. Since, therefore, all spiritual gifts Since they proceed from one Holy Spirit, who dwells in the individual hearts of the pious, dissensions, schisms, or contentions are not to be stirred up by those gifts, lest we be ungrateful and contumelious toward the author, but rather each individual ought to contribute his own gifts to the common utility of the whole Church. Paul was instructed in eloquence, Agabus in the gift of prophesying, Apollos in singular knowledge of scripture, Peter in the gift of performing miracles. And yet these individual gifts had proceeded from one Holy Spirit. Therefore, they ought to be contributed to one end, namely, to the edification of the Church.

A notable testimony of the Apostle Paul, by which he demonstrates the distinction of persons in the divinity, and confirms the omnipotence and eternity both of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, and of the Holy Spirit. For since the Apostle testifies that all spiritual gifts, of whatever kind they are in all the saints, proceed from one and the same Holy Spirit, it is necessary that his wisdom and power be immense, for the understanding of holy scripture, the light of faith, constancy in the cross, peace of conscience, strength of soul, eloquence, the gift of prophesying, the faculty of healing the sick, and of raising the dead, the wisdom of governing assemblies, hope and joy in God: And similar gifts cannot be effected or given by any creature. And the Spirit who dwells in the individual hearts of the pious wherever they are and makes gifts, and rules them, is eternal and omnipotent, since indeed to be everywhere is a property befitting the divine nature. Rightly, therefore, the Church of Christ adores the Holy Spirit as eternal and omnipotent God: in whose name it has been baptized. Thus also Paul demonstrates the divinity of Jesus Christ, by this very fact, that he confesses all ministries or offices to be from Christ, and he himself is the Lord of all Apostles, Prophets, Evangelists, Bishops, Doctors, Pastors, and ministers of the Church. For the wisdom and power of no angel is so great that he could preside over the whole Church in the entire world, teach, rule, and protect all Apostles, Prophets, Pastors, and ministers, and govern the universal Church. Also, no angel is the lord of all ministries. For ministries in the Church were not produced and instituted by an angel, but by Jesus Christ. Whence Paul to Ephe: 4. He ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things: And he gave some Apostles, some Prophets, some Evangelists, some Pastors and Doctors, that the saints might be instructed for the ministry, for the edification of the body of Christ: Therefore let Pastors and ministers know that they serve this Lord Jesus Christ in the ministry: Let them know that they will render an account to this Lord: Let them know that they are helped and defended by this Lord Jesus Christ against the insults of the world and of Satan. He also shows the distinction of persons in the divinity. from the offices. The eternal Father is the first person of the divinity, the author and defender of the kingdom of Christ, who gave the Son to us, and pours out the Holy Spirit, and works all virtues in individuals. For all things are from him, He founded heaven and earth, he sustains all things: He bestows all gifts: And he attributes powers and efficacy to individual things: The Son is the second person of the divinity, the Lord of all ministries and of the whole Church, as one who redeemed the Church with his own blood, and was constituted by the Father as head of the Church over all things, and both institutes, and governs, and protects all ministries in the Church. The Holy Spirit is the third person of the divinity, which is sent by the Father and the Son into the hearts of believers so that it may regenerate, sanctify, and spiritually adorn them with various gifts. Therefore, there is not only one person or συναληφή as the blasphemous Sabellius, seduced by Artemon, raved: But there are three distinct persons, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, of the same essence, glory, and majesty.

That which says God works all things in all, must not be twisted toward the crimes of the wicked, as if those also proceeded from God, for the immovable sentence must always be before our eyes. You are not a God willing iniquity Psalm 5. And Hosea 13. Destruction is from you, O Israel: In me alone is your salvation. Likewise, when the Devil speaks a lie, He speaks from his own, John 8. Therefore, the things of God, which are just, right, and salutary, and which agree with the will of God, the Apostle speaks.

To each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit, as it is profitable: Paul explains with what purpose God distributes diverse gifts to the saints, namely, that individual members might be for the use and ornament of the Church; He did not bestow all things upon one, lest there be no use for the remaining members. And God most rightly understands of all things which gifts are expedient for us, and what our shoulders can bear. Therefore, let each one be content with his own measure, which God has attributed to him by most wise counsel.

Latin:

Divisiones donorum sunt, sed idem Spiritus. Et divisiones ministeriorum sunt, sed idem dominus. Et divisiones operationum sunt, sed idem Deus, qui operatur omnia in omnibus, unicuique verò datur manifestatio Spiritus, quatenus expedit.

Secunda haec est ratio, sumpta à causa efficiente donorum spiritualium, et à causa finali: Qua probat non esse superbiendum in donis, nemini esse invidendum propter dona, nulla certamina, nullas contentiones de donis movendas esse, sed potius singulis operam dandam esse, ut donis à Deo collatis utantur ad gloriam Dei & aedificationem Ecclesiae. Commune donum, quod singulis ad salutem est necessarium, videlicet, agnitio Iesu Christi, & effusio Spiritus sancti, singulis piis collatum est, Nam sine hoc dono non posset constare homini salus, sed reliqua dona in quibus non consistit nostra salus, sed quae faciunt ad aedificandam et exornandam Ecclesiam, non est necesse ut sint paria in singulis. Ipsa enim diversitas donorum testimonium dicit de immensa sapientia Spiritus. Non enim existimandum est, ut dissimilia & diversa sunt dona spiritualia, ita & multiplices & diversos esse Spiritus sanctos. Sed unus & idem est Spiritus sanctus, qui tam diversa dona distribuit, sic et si multa & diversa sint officia in Ecclesia, alius enim est Apostolus, alius Propheta, alius Doctor, alius Episcopus, alius Pastor, alius Diaconus, alius Paedagogus, alius Gubernator: tamen unus tantum est dominus, qui omnibus praeest ministris & à singulis rationem gesti muneris posciturus, sic licet variae sint operationes, seu virtutes, ut Petrus resuscitat mortuos, et verbo interficit Ananiam: Paul; sanat agrotos, abiicit viperam adhaerentem manui, Elymam percutit caecitate: Ionatham cum armigero totum exercitum vertit in fugam: tamen non sunt multi dii, sed unus est Deus, qui omnia in omnibus operatur. Cum ergò omnia dona spiritualia ab uno Spiritu sancto, qui in singulis piorum cordibus habitat proficiscantur, non sunt excitanda dissidia, schismata, aut contentiones illis donis, ne in authorem ingrati & contumeliosi simus, sed potius singuli sua dona ad communem totius Ecclesiae utilitatem conferre debent. Paulus eloquentia fuit instructus, Agabus dono vaticinandi, Apollo singulari cognitione scripturae, Petrus dono edendi miracula. Et tamen singula haec dona ab uno Spiritu sancto profecta erant. Ad unum ergò finem, nimirum, ad Ecclesiae aedificationem conferri debent.

Insigne testimonium Apostoli Pauli, quo demonstrat discrimen personarum indivinitate, & confirmat omnipotentiam & aeternitatem cùm filii Dei Iesu Christi, tùm Spiritus sancti. Cum enim testetur Apostolus omnia dona spiritualia, qualiacunque sunt in omnibus sanctis, ab uno eodemque Spiritu sancto proficisci, necesse est eius esse immensam sapientiam & potentiam, nam intellectus sacrae scripturae, lumen fidei, constantia in cruce, pax conscientiae, robur animi, eloquentia, donum vaticinandi, facultas sanandi aegrotos, & suscitandi mortuos, sapientia gubernandi caetus, spes & laeticia in Deo: Et similia dona non possunt ab ulla creatura effici aut dari. Et Spiritus qui in singulis piorum cordibus ubicunque locorum ea sunt, habitat & dona efficit, & regit ea, aeternus atque omnipotens est, siquidem ubique esse proprietas est divinae naturae conveniens. Rectè igitur Ecclesia Christi Spiritum sanctum ut aeternum & omnipotentem Deum adorat: In cuius nomine baptizata est. Sic & Iesu Christi divinitatem demonstrat Paulus, hoc ipso, quod fatetur omnia ministeria seu officia esse à Christo, & ipse est omnium Apostolorum, Prophetarum, Evangelistarum, Episcoporum, Doctorum, Pastorum & ministrorum Ecclesiae Dominus. Nullius enim angelitanta est sapientia & potentia, ut toti Ecclesiae in universo mundo praeesse, omnes Apostolos, Prophetas, Pastores & ministros docere, regere & tueri, & universam Ecclesiam gubernare possit. Nullus etiam angelus est dominus omnium ministeriorum. Non enim ab angelo, sed à Iesu Christo & parta et instituta sunt ministeria in Ecclesia. Unde Paulus ad Ephe: 4. Adscendit super omnes coelos, ut omnia impleret: Et ipse dedit alios Apostolos, alios Prophetas, alios Evangelistas, alios Pastores et Doctores, ut sancti instructi essent ad ministerium, ad aedificationem corporis Christi: Sciant ergò Pastores & ministri, se huic domino Iesu Christo in ministerio servire: Sciant se huic domino reddituros rationem: Sciant se iuvari atque defendi ab hoc domino Iesu Christo contra insultus mundi & Satanae. Discrimen etiam monstrat personarum in divinitate ab officiis. Pater aeternus est prima persona divinitatis, author & defensor regni Christi, qui filium nobis dedit, & Spiritum sanctum effundit, & omnes virtutes in singulis operatur. Omnia enim ab ipso sunt, Ipse condidit coelum & terram, omnia sustentat: Ipse largitur omnia dona: Et singulis rebus vires & efficaciam tribuit: Filius est secunda persona divinitatis, Dominus omnium ministeriorum & lotius Ecclesiae, ut qui suo sanguine Ecclesiam redemit, & à patre constitutus est caput Ecclesiae super omnia, ac omnia ministeria in Ecclesia & instituit, & gubernat & tuetur. Spiritus sanctus est tertia persona divinitatis, quae mittitur à patre & filio in corda credentium ut ea regeneret, sanctificet & variis donis spirituasiter exornet. Non ergò tantum una est persona vel συναληφή ut blasphemus Sabellius ab Artemone seductus deliravit: Sed tres sunt distinctae personae, pater, filius & Spiritus sanctus, eiusdem essentiae, gloriae & maiestatis.

Quod dicit Deum operari omnia in omnibus, non ad scelera impiorum contorquendum est, quasi & illa à Deo proficiscantur, semper enim in conspectu nobis esse debet immota sententia. Non Deus volens iniquitatem tu es Psalm 5. Et Oseae. 13. Perditio ex te est Israel: In me tantum salus tua. Item Diabolus quando mendacium loquitur, ex proprio loquitur, Ioan: 8. Dei is ergò, quae iusta, recta & salutariae sunt & cum voluntate Dei congruunt, loquitur Apostolus.

Unicuique data est manifestatio Spiritus, quatenus conducit: Quo consilio Deus diversa dona partiatur sanctis exponit Paulus, nimirum, ut singula membra usui essent Ecclesiae & ornamento, non contulit uni omnia, ne reliquorum membrorum nullus esset usus. Et Deus omnium rectissimè intelligit, quae dona nobis expediant, quid humeri nostri ferre possint. Quisque ergò sua mensura contentus sit, quam Deus sapientissimo consilio ei attribuit.

## 12:8-10
To one indeed is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom: to another the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit: to another faith, in the same Spirit: to another the gifts of healing in the same Spirit: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.

Paul enumerates the various kinds of spiritual gifts with which the Church is adorned, so that he may show that equal gifts do not shine in individuals. The word of wisdom is the ability to teach the people the doctrine concerning God, concerning the creation and fall of the human race, concerning the benefits of the mediator, concerning faith, concerning the gathering of the Church, concerning the final judgment and eternal life, just as Isaiah, Jeremiah, David, Paul, Peter, John the Baptist, and Athanasius were endowed with the word of wisdom, and with singular eloquence and dexterity explained the mysteries of the doctrine of Christ, in which the highest wisdom is contained.

The word of knowledge, or science, is the ability to set forth plans prudently conceived, just as Hushai, the friend of David, is not only prudent but also eloquent, so that he can conveniently set forth and adorn his plan, and persuade both the king and the counselors. David employed prudence in that he did not kill Shimei the reviler, and he repressed the untimely zeal of Abishai: for thus he commended himself to Israel, and showed that he was not desirous of vengeance, but that he gave pardon to deserters, and he taught that his new kingdom, as it were, should begin not from the shedding of blood, but rather from the very example of clemency. Paul employed prudence in that he circumcised Timothy. He did not circumcise Titus. Ambrose employed prudence in that he did not wish to dispute with the Arians, the Emperor taking upon himself the role of judge, who did not understand the foundations of religion, and depended upon a mother infected with heresy. Thus it was a matter of prudence that he fasted on the Sabbath at Rome: at Milan he did not fast on the Sabbath.

Other faith: He speaks here of a special faith, by which either miracles are performed, or horrendous and huge temptations are overcome, or singular benefits are obtained from God. For the general faith by which we apprehend the promise of the Gospel concerning the free remission of sins to be granted on account of the Mediator Jesus Christ is given to all and each by the Holy Spirit, just as Benjamin lives by his faith before God, as do Abraham, or Elijah, or David. But that special faith by which either miracles are performed or great things are accomplished is not in all. There was a special faith in David that he trusted in the Lord that he would be the victor over Goliath, and he attacks such a braggart, at whose sight the whole army of the Israelites was trembling. There was a special faith in Elisha raising the dead boy, whom Gehazi could not raise. By a special faith Isaiah obtained from the Lord that the shadow of the sun would go back 10 degrees. And Joshua commanded the sun and the moon to stand in the middle of the sky for the whole day.

The Apostle uses those particles indifferently by the Spirit, according to the Spirit, in the Spirit: for it signifies that the same Holy Spirit is the author and bestower of all gifts, even the most diverse.

To another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit: That the Apostles were instructed by Christ through the Holy Spirit with the gift of healing the sick is evident from the Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles. The Apostle Paul healed the father of Publius, suffering from fevers and dysentery, by the laying on of hands. Act: 28.

To another the working of miracles: that is, most efficacious powers or virtues; there was an admirable force and power in the Apostle Peter, who by a word killed Ananias and Sapphira: It was an efficacious operation that Paul struck Elymas the sorcerer blind with a word. It was an efficacious operation that Ambrose drove the scribe of Stilicho into a fury by the word of excommunication.

To another prophecy: To the Apostles, the term prophecy does not signify only the prediction of future things: but in general the office of teaching the Gospel and explaining the Holy Scripture, as in Chapter 14. He who prophesies speaks to men for edification, exhortation, and consolation.

Therefore, the term Prophecy is used in two ways in Holy Scripture: at times for prediction, as Agabus predicted the famine. Athanasius predicted the death of Julian, which he foretold; in other places it signifies the faculty of preaching to the people about God and eternal life. Others [call it] the discernment of spirits. This gift is distinguished and very necessary in the Church: yet it is not granted to all. It is not the lot of all pious men, even if they understand the truth, have a zeal for fleeing errors, and are ruled by the Holy Spirit, to immediately detect fanatical spirits and to understand their illusions and snares. For Satan transforms himself into an angel of light. How great a blasphemy Arius attempted to introduce into the Church, Alexander and Athanasius judged more correctly than many other Bishops. Cyril judged the fanatical spirit of Nestorius much more correctly than either John of Antioch or Theodoret. Flavian and Eusebius, Bishop of Dorylaeum, were endowed with the gift of discerning the fanatical spirit of Eutyches.

Luther of holy memory: He was instructed with the distinguished gift of discerning spirits, he immediately detected the error of Carlstadt, Zwingli, Oecolampadius, Muntzer, Schwenckfeld, and the Anabaptists of Münster: That Luther detected and revealed to the world the Roman Antichrist, was a gift of discerning spirits. How many Doctors of the Church and princes in all of Germany did Jacob Andreae deceive with his fascination, by which he attempted to lead them to the confusion of Christ and Belial, and to the very Epicureanism into the Church? Yet the Holy Spirit had His own, who would both detect the deceit, and resist his impious machination, and warn the Church. Since this distinguished gift is most needed by the Church of Christ, so that the machinations of Satan may be pointed out to the little ones of Christ and be beaten back, God must be ardently invoked, that He may always adorn some in the Church with this illustrious gift of the Holy Spirit.

To others, kinds of tongues: The Apostles, by the benefit of the Holy Spirit, spoke in various tongues. Jerome in the Church was famous for his knowledge of the Hebrew, Greek, and Latin language, and he rendered useful service to the Church with his versions.

To others, the interpretation of tongues: Even if some do not speak in various tongues, yet they know how to interpret them. Luther did not speak either Hebrew or Greek: And yet he interpreted the Hebrew writings of the Prophets, and the Greek [writings] of the Apostles, most significantly and most clearly, and he surpassed in the propriety of his version all the interpreters of the Bibles who were before him.

But all these things one and the same Spirit works, distributing to each one individually just as He wills.

He now shows the author, effector, and distributor of the commemorated gifts with which the Church of Jesus Christ is adorned. Even though the gifts are diverse, he says: yet there are not many Holy Spirits: but one and the same is the Holy Spirit, namely, the third person of the divinity proceeding from the Father and the Son. Here the Holy Spirit effects and creates all those gifts, so manifold in the Church, and adorns each one according to his good pleasure. Therefore, one must not be proud in the gifts, nor abuse them, but the author, the Holy Spirit, must be acknowledged, and the gifts must be used submissively for the illustration of his glory and the edification of the Church. This is a most bright and most evident testimony concerning the eternal divinity and omnipotence of the Holy Spirit. For the glory or majesty of no creature is so great that it could effect and bestow all those most excellent gifts which shine in the universal Church of God. Wisdom, the strength of faith, the ability to perform miracles, the gift of healing the sick, and of predicting future things proceed immediately from God himself. Since, therefore, Paul testifies that the Holy Spirit is the effector of all spiritual gifts in the universal Church and in individual members, it is necessary that he be the eternal and omnipotent God, of the same essence and majesty with the eternal Father and the Son.

Paul also teaches that the Holy Spirit is the Lord of such excellent gifts and of the whole Church, as one who according to his own good pleasure and will distributes individual gifts in the Church; to attribute such great glory and majesty, according to one's own will, of adorning and ruling the individual members of the Church, to either an angel, or a man, or a Prophet, or an Apostle would be idolatry.

Latin:

Huic quidem per Spiritum datus est sermo sapientiae: Alii datus est sermo cognitionis, secundum eundem Spiritum: Alii verò fides, in eodem Spiritu: Alii dona curationum in eodem Spiritu: Alii operationes virtutum, alii Prophetia, alii diiudicatio Spirituum, alii verò genera linguarum, alii interpretatio linguarum.

Varias species donorum spiritualium, quibus exornata est Ecclesia recenset Paulus utostendat, non in singulis paria dona lucere. Sermo sapientiae est facultas docendi populum doctrinam de Deo, de creatione & lapsu generis humani, de beneficiis mediatoris, de fide, de collectione Ecclesiae, de extremo iudicio & vita aeterna, ut Iesaias, Ieremias, David, Paulus, Petrus, Ioan: Baptista, Athanasius, praediti fuerunt sermone sapientiae, singulari facundia & dexteritate explicarunt mysteria doctrinae Christi, quibus summa sapientia continetur.

Sermo cognitionis, seu scientiae est facultas exponendi consilia prudenter cogitata, ut Chusai amicus Davidis non solum prudens est, sed etiam facundus, ita ut consilium suum commode exponere & ornare, & regem & consiliaros persuadere possit. Prudentiam adhibuit David, quod non interfecit Semei conviciatorem, & repressit intempestivum zelum Abisai: Sic enim commendabat se Israeli, & ostendebat se non esse cupidum vindictae, sed se veniom dare desertoribus, Et docebat novum quasi regnum non ab effusione sanguinis, sed potius ab ipso exemplo clementiae ordiri. Prudentiam adhibuit Pavius, quod Timotheum circumcidit. Titum non circum cidit. Prudentiam adhibuit Ambrosius, quod noluit disputare cum Arrianis Imperatore sumente sibi iudicis partes, qui fundamenta religionis non intelligebat, & à matre infecta haeresi pendebat. Sic prudentiae erat quod Romae ieiunavit Sabbatho: Mediolani non ieiunavit Sabbatho.

Alii fides: De speciali fide hîc loquitur, qua vel miraculaeduntur, vel horrendae, & ingentes tentationes superantur, vel singularia beneficia à Deo obtinentur. Generalis enim fides qua adprehendimus promissionem Evangelii de gratuita remissione peccatorum donanda propter Mediatorem Iesum Christum omnibus & singulis datur per Spiritum sanctum, tam Beniamin vivit sua fide coram Deo, quam Abraham, vel Elias, vel David. At specialis illa fides qua vel miracula eduntur, velres magnae geruntur non est in omnibus. Specialis fides fuit in Davide quod confidit Domino se fore victorem Goliath, & talem thrasonem adoritur, ad cuius conspectum totus exercitus Israelitarum contremiscebat. Specialis fides fuit in Eliseo resuscitante puerum extinctum, quem Gehasi resuscitare non poterat. Speciali fide Iesaias impetravit à domino ut umbra solis 10. gradibus retrocederet. Et Iosua iussit solem & lunam stare in medio coeli totum diem.

Indifferenter usurpat Apostolus illas particulas per Spiritum, secundum Spiritum, in Spiritu: significat enim eundem Spiritum sanctum omnium etiam diversissimorum donorum esse authorem & largitorem.

Alii dona sanationum in eodem Spiritu: Dono sanandi aegrotos Apostolos a Christo per Spiritum sanctum instructos fuisse patet ex Evangeilo & actis Apostolorum. Paulus Apostolus patrem Publii laborantem sebribus & dysenteria sanavit impositione manuum. Act: 28.

Alii operationes virtutum: hoc est efficacissimae vires seu virtutes, admiranda vis & potentia fuit in Apostolo Petro, qui verbo interfecit Ananiam & Sapphiram: Efficax operatio fuit, quod Paulus Elymam magum verbo excoecavit. Efficax operatio fuit quod Ambrosius scribam Stilliconis excommunicationis verbo adegit in furorem.

Alii prophetia: Apostolis vocabulum prophetia non significat tantum praedictionem rerum futurarum: sed in genere munus docendi Evangelion & explicandi sacram scripturam, ut Cap: 14. Qui prophetat hominibus loquitur, ad aedificationem, exhortationem & consolationem.

Dupliciter igitur vocabulum Prophetiae usurpatur in Sacra scriptura: alias pro praedictione ut Agabus famem praedixit. Athanasius Iuliani interitum praedixit, alias significat facultatem concionandi ad populum de Deo & vita aeterna. Alii diiudicationes Spirituum. Insigne est hoc donum & valde necessarium in Ecclesia: Nec tamen omnibus conceditur. Non omnium piorum est, etiamsi intelligant veritatem, habeant studium fugiendi errores, & regantur à Spiritu sancto, mox deprehendere fanaticos Spiritus, & illorum praestigias & insidias intelligere. Satan enim se transformat in angelum lucis. Quantam blasphemiam Arrius in Ecclesiam invehere conaretur, Alexander & Athanasius rectius iudicabant, quam multi alii Episcopi. Cyrillus multò rectius iudicavit Spiritum fanaticum Nestorii, quàm vel Ioannes Antiochenus vel Theodoretus. Flavianus & Eusebius Dorilei Episcopus, dono praediti fuerunt diiudicandi fanaticum Spiritum Eutychetis.

Lutherus sanctae me: Insigni dono diiudicandi Spiritus instructus fuit, mox deprehendit Carolstadii, Zwinglii, Oecolanipadii, Muntzeri, Schwenckfeldii, Monasteriensium anabaptistarum errorem: Quod Luthe: deprehendit et orbi revelavit Antichristum Romanum, fuit donum diiudicandi Spiritus. Quam multis Doctoribus Ecclesiae & principibus in tota Germania imposuit fascino suo Iacobus Andreae, quo ad confusionem Christi & Belial, & ipsissimum Epicureismum in Ecclesiam inducere conabatur? Habuit tamen Spiritus sanctus suos, qui & dolum deprehenderent, & impiae eius machinationi resisterent & Ecclesiam monerent. Hoc insigni dono cum maximè opus sit Ecclesiae Christi, ut pusillis Christi machinationes Satanae indicari & retundi possint, ardenter invocandus est Deus, ut semper aliquos in Ecclesia exornet hoc illustri dono Spiritus sancti.

Alii genera linguarum: Apostoli beneficio Spiritus sancti locuti sunt variis linguis. Hieronymus in Ecclesia, clarus fuit cognitione Hebraicae, graecae & latinae linguae, & utilem operam suis versionibus navavit Ecclesiae.

Alii interpretatio linguarum: Etsi aliqui non loquantur variis linguis, tamen eas norunt interpretari. Lutherus nec Hebraicè nec Graecè loquebatur: Et tamen Hebraica scripta Prophetarum, & Graeca Apostolorum significantissime & planissime est interpretatus, & vicit proprietate versionis omnes interpretes Bibliorum, qui ante ipsum fuerunt.

Haec verò omnia operatur unus & idem Spiritus, distribuens unicuique sigillatim quemadmodum vult.

Commemoratorum donorum, quibus exornata est Ecclesia Iesu Christi, authorem, effectorem & distributorem nunc ostendit. Etiamsi diversa sint dona inquit: non tamen multi sunt Spiritus sancti: sed unus & idem est Spiritus sanctus, nimirum, tertia persona divinitatis procedens à patre & filio. Hîc Spiritus sanctus efficit & creat omnia illa dona tam multiplicia in Ecclesia, & unumquemque exornat pro suo beneplacito. Non igitur in donis superbiendum, aut iis abutendum est, sed author Spiritus sanctus est agnoscendus, et donis ad illius gloriae illustrationem & Ecclesiae aedificationem submissè utendum. Luculentissimum & evidentissimum hoc est testimonium de aeterna divinitate & omnipotentia Spiritus sanctus. Nullius enim creaturae tanta est gloria vel maiestas, ut efficere & largiri posset omnia illa dona excellentissima, quae lucent in universa Ecclesia Dei. Sapientia, robur fidei, facultas edendi miracula, donum sanandi aegrotos, & praedicendi futura immediate ab ipso Deo proficiscuntur. Cùm ergò Paulus testetur Spiritum sanctum esse effectorem omnium donorum spiritualium in universa Ecclesia, & in singulis membris necesse est esse aeternum & omnipotentem Deum, eiusdem essentiae & maiestatis cum aeterno patre & filio.

Docet etiam Paulus Spiritum sanctum esse Dominum talium excellentium donorum & totius Ecclesiae, ut qui pro suo beneplacito & arbitrio distribuit singula dona in Ecclesia, tantam gloriam & maiestatem pro suo arbitrio ornandi & regendi singula membra Ecclesiae vel angelo, vel homini, vel Prophetae, vel Apostolo tribuere idolatria esset.

## 12:12-20
For as the body is one, and has many members: and all the members of the one body, whereas they are many, are one body, so also is Christ. For in one Spirit were we all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free. And we have all been made to drink into one Spirit.

This is the third argument, by which the Apostle Paul teaches that one should not strive for rivalries and contentions in the Church, nor be proud of gifts: But with all zeal and effort, unity is to be fostered, and the gifts granted by the Holy Spirit are to be used for the salvation and edification of the whole Church as something to be used. It is taken from the likeness of the human body. The universal Church, which is gathered in all times and in all places by the ministry of the Gospel, is one body, whose head is Jesus Christ, God and man. For as many of us as believe in Jesus Christ are made children of God and members of Jesus Christ; we are grafted into the body of Christ through Baptism, and through the sacred supper we are endowed with the one Spirit of Christ. Therefore, just as the members of one body contribute their common efforts with equal zeal to protect and preserve the health of the whole body, there is no rivalry here, no envy, no dissension. So too it ought to be in the Church, which is the mystical body of Christ. Those who have put on Christ ought to be most alien to all rivalry, envy, dissension, and contention, and ought to apply themselves entirely to this: that they may preserve and protect the health of the whole body of the Church.

Let the pious reader observe in this place the testimony concerning the final cause and efficacy of Baptism and the Lord's supper: Paul says that in one Spirit we have all been baptized into one body. Therefore, Baptism was instituted by God for this end, that through it we might be made members of the body of Christ, be washed from sin, be regenerated through the holy Spirit, and be constituted heirs of eternal life, just as it is said elsewhere. As many as in Jesus Christ have been baptized, you have put on Jesus. Item, Rom: 6. Do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? Therefore we were buried with him through Baptism into death, that just as Christ rose from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also should walk in newness of life.

Baptism is therefore not only an external sign that we are citizens of the Church, but it is a medium through which God works salvation in us, and the Holy Spirit regenerates us into life. In the same way he also pronounces concerning the supper of the Lord: We have been made to drink into one Spirit, as if he were saying, For this end the Son of God instituted his most holy supper, and gives to all to eat his body, and to drink his blood, that he may impart his Holy Spirit to us, and by this bond may glue us to himself as members of one body.

The supper of the Lord is therefore not only an external sign, which may admonish us concerning the passion and death of Christ, but it is also a medium and instrument through which the Son of God imparts his Spirit to us, bestows life, nourishes and confirms our faith, and seals to us the inheritance of eternal life.

For the body is not one a member, but many: if the foot should say, because I am not the hand, therefore I am not of the body, shall it therefore not be of the body? And if the ear should say, because I am not the eye, therefore I am not of the body, shall it therefore not be of the body? If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing remain? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be? But now God has placed the members, each one of them in the body, just as He willed. If therefore all were one member, where would the body be? But now indeed there are many members, yet one body. Moreover, the eye cannot say to the hand, I do not need you, or again the head to the feet, I have no need of you. Nay, much more the members of the body, which seem to be weak, are necessary: and those which seem to be less honorable of the body, upon these we bestow more abundant honor, and our less decent parts have greater comeliness they have. But those which are comely, have no need. But God hath tempered the body together, giving to that which lacked the more abundant honour, that there might be no schism in the body. But that the members should have the same care one for another: And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it: or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it. Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.

Paul himself has explained the individual parts of the similitude and the instituted comparison copiously and at length, and therefore there is no need for a longer declaration. But this is the sum of the whole comparison, just as God has established and tempered the diverse members in the human body with wonderful wisdom: So also, for his admirable wisdom and goodness, he has adorned the citizens of the Church with diverse gifts, wherefore just as there are no rivalries, no contentions, no schisms among the members of one body: So also among Christians there ought to be no schism, no rivalry. The Bishop is as it were the eye of the Church: The ministers of the word are as the beautiful feet of those who evangelize peace.

A Bishop cannot say that he does not need the work of a minister of the word. And God confers such excellent gifts upon the lower citizens of His Church, that all may be an ornament to the body. Therefore, is not one member solicitous for another in the body: And when one is harmed, do all suffer and are affected together? Such συμπάθεια ought to be among Christians, they ought to envy no one either a higher degree of dignity, or more excellent gifts: But to consider that God has established individuals in their own place: And that no one among the little ones of Christ is of such an abject lot, who does not serve the glory of God, and bear fruit for the Lord. Therefore, we ought to despise no one: But rather, when an injury is inflicted upon one Christian, we ought all to grieve: When glory and honor befall one, we ought all to rejoice. If such consensus and concord should exist in all the members of the body of Christ, then there will be no place for contentions and dissensions.

Latin:

Quemadmodum enim corpus unum est, & membra habet multa: omnia autem membra unius corporis, cum multa sint unum sunt corpus, sic & Christus. Nam in uno Spiritu nos omnes in unum corpus Baptizati sumus, sive Iudaei, sive Graeci, sive servi, sive liberi. Et omnes in unum Spiritum potati sumus.

Tertium hoc est argumentum, quo Apostolus Paulus docet, non esse studendum aemulationibus & contentionibus in Ecclesia, nec superbiendum donis: Sed omni studio & conatu fovendam coniunctionem & donis à Spiritu sancto concessis ad totius Ecclesiae salutem & aedificationem esse utendum. Sumptum à similitudine humani corporis. Universa Ecclesia quae omnibus temporibus & omnibus locis ministerio Evangelii colligitur est unum corpus, cuius caput est Iesus Christus Deus & homo. Quot quot enim in Iesum Christum credimus, efficimur filii Dei & membra Iesu Christi, per Baptismum inserimur corpori Christi: & per sacram coenam uno donamur Spiritu Christi.
