And falling on his face, he will worship God, who revealed himself by such illustrious testimonies in the Church: and he will confess that God is truly present in the Church: but that the idols of the Gentiles are nothing: Here a huge fruit, namely, the refutation of idols, the illustration of the glory of God, the conversion of the infidels, the confirmation of the faithful is born from the Prophecy and explanation of the holy scripture. It is therefore much more profitable to study the gift of Prophecy, than to show off the knowledge of foreign languages.

Latin:

Fratres, ne sitis pueri sensibus: sed malitia pueri sitis: sensibus verò sitis perfecti.

Commonefactionem interspergit de usu donorum: quae non pueriliter, nec ineptè ostentanda, sed sapienter sint usurpanda. Ne sitis pueri sensi huius: quasi dicat, ne adeò deliretis, ne adeò pueriles togitationes in animum admittatis, ut existimetis in eo consistere religionem, & Christianorum felicitatem, si modò liceat vobis sine omni fructu dona Spiritus ostentare. Etiam communis sensus intelligit, ineptum esse ostentare peregrinam linguam inter eos, qui eius ignari sunt. Vosergò illuminati per spiritum sanctum, plus sapere debebatis aliis homnibus, qui sunt extra Ecclesiam. Malicia sitis pueri: Id est, in rebus malis & prohibitis, estote simplices & ignari: non adfectate acumen aut solertiam in malis artibus aut dolis, sed sensibus estote perfecti, Hoc est, semper proficite in sapientia & agnitione voluntatis Dei: veram, spiritualem & perfectam sapientiam, quoad eius fieri potest, comparate vobis. Perfectum hîc non significat omnibus numeris absolutum, sed quod syncerum, rectum, & solidum est: & opponitur ei, quod corruptum, simulatum, falsatum, & mutilum est: sapientia carnis imperfecta & adulterata est stulitia & errore: sed sapientia Spiritus est perfecta, licet in piis subinde crescat. Mens ergò Pauli est sapienter utendum esse donis spiritualibus: non ad inanem ostentationem, non ut ad plausus populi captemus, quemadmodum stolidae gentes ineptire solent: sed ad illustrationem gloriae Dei: & aedificationem Ecclesiae. Sic enim solida comparatur gloria, non solùm in mundo, sed in omni aeternitate duratura, cùm omnia ad gloriam Dei referimus. Verissima enim & amplissima est promissio: Glorificantes me, glorificabo.

In lege scriptum est, alienis linguis, & labiis alienis loquar populo huic: & ne sic quidem audient me, dicit Dominus. Itaque linguae signi vice sunt, non iis, qui credunt, sed incredulis: contrà Prophetia non incredulis, sed credentibus.

Sextum est hoc argumentum sumptum à causae finali, & effectibus donorum, cùm linguarum, tum Prophetiae. Ea quae fidelibus à Deo ordinata sunt, praestantiora sunt, quàm quae sunt in signum & prodigium data infidelibus. At peregrinae linguae datae sunt in signum non fidelibus, sed infidelibus. Ergò praestabilius donum est Prophetia, quae fideles aedificat, quàm peregrinarum linguarum donum: potius igitur Prophetiae studendum est.

Quòd peregrinae linguae in signum datae sint infidelibus, probat Paulus testimonio Iesaiae Prophetae, ex Cap: 28. Ubi Propheta primùm graviter accusat caecitatem, errores, & stuporem populi Iudaici: Halluciati sunt in vino, errarunt in sicera: Sacerdos & Propheta aberrarunt: omnes mensae plenae sunt vomitu: Id est, Populus planè defecit à veritate Dei: plenus, & planè ebrius est erroribus, & superstitionibus, nunc in hanc, nunc in illam im pingit idolatriam more ebriorum: Prophetae & Sacerdotes, ut Pharisaei & Sadducaei, mensas, quas instruere debebant, optimis ferculis verbi divini & concionibus, de beneficiis mediatoris, quibus conscientiae miserorum refici possent, replent vomitu, impiis dogmatibus, humanis traditionibus, superstitionibus, idolomaniis, et carnificinis conscientiarum. Quem ergò docebit scientiam? ablactatos à lacte, & avulsos ab uberibus, quasi dicat, Cùm Iudaei cum suis Pharisaeis & scribis fastidiant doctrinam. Evangelii, eò, quòd sint ebrii erroribus & traditionibus hominum: nec audire velint, neque Christum neque Apostolos: quò igitur vertet se Deus? Oportet ut aliqua sit Ecclesia, & Christus habeat discipulos? quos ergò docebunt Christus & Apostoli? Ablactatos à lacte & avulsos ab uberibus, Id est, Iudaeos exules, quos Deus castigavit exiliis, & longo tempore avulsit ab uberibus Propheticae doctrinae:

item, gentes, quas Deus ablactavit à lacte Evangelii, & avulsit ab uberibus ministerii: quemadmodum in die Pentecostes factum est: ubi Deus docuit scientiam Iudaeos, proselytos, & gentiles, qui ex omnibus nationibus venerant Hierosolymam. Qui enim vàriis aerumnis castigati sunt, & sitiunt veritatem & iustitiam, hi sunt idonei ad percipiendam doctrinam.

Addit deinde aliam causam, cur Deus Iudaeos percussurus sit caecitate, & gentibus revelaturus Evangelion, nimirum, quia non tantum ebrii sunt erroribus, sed etiam saninis excipiunt altissimi Dei veritatem, & saluberrimas Christi & Apostolorum conciones. Praeceptum ad praeceptum: expectatio ad expectationem: paululum bîc, paululum isthic, Mimesi recitat verba impiorum Iudaeorum, Pharisaeorum & scribarum, quasi dicerent: nihil adferunt Prophetae, nisi unum praeceptum post aliud: subinde inculcant eadem praecepta: semper iubent expectare: et inani spe lactant homines. Iam iam venturam esse promissionem Messiae: sed merae sunt praestigiae, dicere volunt. Ideò melius est, ut edamus & bibamus: & nihil curemus conciones Prophetarum: sic Iudaei illudebant Christo: cùm dicebant. Quis potest eum audire: insanus est: Daemonium habet: Minatur ergò Deus impiis &

blasphemis Iudaeis irridentibus verbum Dei, hic verbis, quae citat Paulus. Certè labiis blaesis & lingua alia loquetur dominus ad populum istum. Hoc est, dominus vicissim subsannabit illos blasphematores, efficiet, ut Apostoli per Spiritum sanctum peregrinis & variis linguis utantur Hierosolymis, & praedicent ingentia Dei beneficia & opera, quo stupendo miraculo impii Iudaei magis excaecabuntur, & Pharisaei in furorem redigentur: gentibus verò & Iudaeis conversis, & proselytis, revelabuntur mysteria regni Iesu Christi. Ex hac ergò comminatione Prophetae manifestum est, donum variarum linguarum in signum datum esse non fidelibus, sed incredulis, subsannatoribus, hypocritis, & blasphemis.

Cum ergò iram suam ostendat Deus, quando nobis loquitur lingua peregrina & nobis ignota: valdè ineptum & stolidum est, eo ipso velle in Ecclesia superbire, tanquam dono excellenti, quo Deus punit & excaecat incredulos & blasphemos. Ergò si quis ostentet in Ecclesia linguae peregrinae scientiam, quam non interpretatur, is demonstrat se invidere Ecclesiae lucem veritatis, & se gaudere inscitia piorum. Et hîc causae considerandae sunt, cur donum linguarum dederit Deus Ecclesiae.

1. Prima, ut sit testimonium praesentiae Dei & Spiritus sancti in Ecclesia: Dei enim praeclarum & admirandum beneficium & donum est, uno momento instruere homines variarum linguarum cognitione.

2. Secunda, ut Deus vindicaret hoc prodigio maliciam, superbiam & sarcasmos, quibus populus Iudaicus illudebat Christi & Apostolorum doctrinae: magis enim caecitate & amentia cerdis percussit eos dominus, postquam Apostoli peregrinis lingis sunt usi.

3. Tertia, ut tantò citiùs doctrina Evangelii in varias gentes, quae diversissimis linguis utuntur, propagari possit.

4. Quarta, ut esset testimonium, doctrinam Evangelii de beneficiis mediatoris non tantum ad populum Israel, sed etiam ad alias gentes pertinere: Hoc in loco Paulus praecipuè urget secundam causam, quae, in concione Prophetae Iesaiae extat. Prophetia non incredulis, sed credentibus: Id est, donum explicandi sacram scripturam, tantum ad Ecclesiam pertinet, & servit aedificationi.

Ergò si convenerit Ecclesia tota simul & omnes linguis loquantur:

ingrediantur autem indocti aut increduli: nonne dicent vos insanire? Quod si omnes Prophetent, ingrediatur autem incredulus aut indoctus, coarguitur ab omnibus, diiudicatur ab omnibus: Et sic occulta cordis eius manifesta fiunt: atque ita procidens in faciem, adorabit Deum, praedicans, quòd Deus revera in vobis sit.

Septimum argumentum à testimonio & iudicio infidelium, si omnes utamini peregrina lingua in Ecclesia, infideles dicent vos insanire; quorsum enim attinet aërem inaniter verberare, & edere sonos in publico, quos nemo intelligit. Hanc amentiam etiam ratio ridet. Cur ergò vos Corinthii, qui Spiritu Dei illuminati estis, hanc stultitiam non videtis & indicatis?

Si verò Prophetetis omnes: Id est, si singull vestrum instructi sint dono explicandi sacram scripturam, & tradendi doctrinam de Deo & vita aeterna, tum incredulus coarguetur & diiudicabitur ab omnibus. Hoc est, convincetur in corde suo se in errore esse; In Ecclesia verò magnam fulgere lucem. Si incredulus aliquis accedat ad conciones & congressus piorum, & audiat hymnum vel precationem lingua peregrina, inde non convertitur, nec aedificatur, potius deridet barbarum sonum. At si audiat plures in concionibus explicantes doctrinam de Deo, de lege, de lapsu generis humani, de causa mortis & calamitatum, de beneficiis mediatoris, de bonis operibus, de Ecclesia, de vita aeterna: audiat graviter & ex fundamentis refelli idola, taxari libidines, & scelera, vocarihomines ad poenitentiam, proponi comminationes & exempla irae divinae, explicari amplissimas promissiones, convincitur et redarguitur in corde suo saniorem esse doctrinam in Ecclesia, quàm apud Ethnicos, qui foedis libidinibus & scleribus sese polluunt, tetra idola comminiscuntur, in horrendis tenebris errorum & blasphemiarum versantur, & tandem omni consolatione destituti, desperabundi ruunt in exitium.

Ac si Deus converterit incredulum suo Spiritu in concione, ut verbum Dei non abit absque fructu, tum sponte revelabit occultas cogitationes cordis sui, fatebitur se evidentia rei convictum esse. Detestabitur idola, quae hactenus coluit, admirabitur tenebras in quibus anteà cum aliis Ethnicis vixit; abiiciet scelera, quibus antea se polluebat: Et procidens in faciem, adorabit Deum, qui se tam illustribus testimoniis patefecit in Ecclesia: & fatebitur Deum verè in Ecclesia praesentem esse: Gentium verò idola nihil esse: Hic ingens fructus, nimirum, refutatio idolorum, illustratio gloriae Dei, conversio infidelium, confirmatio fidelium nascitur ex Prophetia & explicatione sacrae scripturae. Multò igitur conducibilius est studere dono Prophetiae, quàm peregrinarum linguarum cognitionem ostentare.

## 14:26-28
What then is it brothers? whenever you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a doctrine, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation: let all things be done for edification, whether one speaks in a tongue, let it be done by two, or at most three: and that by turns, and let one interpret. But if there is no interpreter, let him be silent in the Church: but let him speak to himself and to God.

The conclusion is of this long discourse, in which he proved by 7 Arguments that the gift of Prophecy is more necessary, more excellent and more useful to the Church, than the gift of various languages. and now he teaches the Corinthians in what order and by what method they ought to use and rightly arrange the various gifts with which God has adorned His Church. From this passage it is manifest what the custom was in the primitive Church. As often as the Church assembled, some sentence from the Prophetic writings was proposed, and one or another delivered an exposition to the rest of the multitude: If anyone approached instructed with the gift of preaching, a place was given to him. Thus Christ, Luke 4, asks for the book, reads a pericope from Isaiah, and shows that this prophecy has been fulfilled: thus Acts 13, after it had been read in Moses and the Prophets, the rulers of the Synagogue sent to Paul, whether he wished to propose any doctrine or consolation to the people. This was the custom in the ancient Church. Paul therefore warns the Corinthians that they themselves also should keep order in their gatherings, lest they mix shouts confusedly: if anyone has either a Psalm, or a tongue, or a doctrine, or a revelation: let him bring it forth into the midst in such a way that he may edify the Church, not that he may ineptly display his own gift without the fruit of others. If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be done by two, or at most three, and in turn. This is, if anyone attempts to bring forth Prophetic sermons, and indeed in the Hebrew as a foreign idiom, only to two or at most Let this be permitted to three, and by turns. And let one person interpret. Once the sentence has been read from the writings of the Prophets according to the Hebrew truth, let the interpretation be added immediately, so that the Church may be edified. But if an interpreter is not present, let a foreign language not be brought into the midst, for the Church receives no fruit from it, since it does not understand it. Yet, lest he who possesses a foreign language think that this gift is useless, he can speak those things to himself and to God in that language, and stir himself up to invocation, thanksgiving, hope, and patience: but the Church of God is not to be wearied by an unknown language without interpretation.

Latin:

Quid igitur est fratres? quoties convenitis, unusquisque vestrum canticum habet, doctrinam habet, linguam habet revelationem habet, interpretationem habet: omnia ad aedificationem fiant, sive lingua quis loquitur, fiat per duos, aut ad summum tres: idque per vices, & unus interpretetur. Quod si non sit interpres, taceat in Ecclesia: caeterum sibi ipsi loquatur & Deo.

Conclusio est prolixae huius concionis, in quae 7. Argumentis probavit donum Prophetiae esse magis necessarium, praestantius & utilius Ecclesiae, quàm donum variarum linguarum: & nunc docet Corinthios, quo ordine & qua ratione varia dona, quibus Deus suam Ecclesiam ornavit usurpare & rectè collocare debent. Ex hoc loco manifestumest, qualis fuerit consuetudo in primitiva Ecclesia. Quoties Eccle: conveniebat, proponebatur aliqua sententia ex scriptis Propheticis, et unus atque alter expositionem tradebant reliquae multitudini: Si quis accedebat dono concionandi instructus, huic dabatur locus. Sic Christus, Luc: 4 poscit librum, legit pericopen ex Iesaia, & ostendit vaticinium hoc impletum esse: sic Actorum 13. Postquam lectum esset in Moise & Prophetis, miserunt principes Synagogae ad Paulum, num quam doctrinam vel consolationem populo proponere vellet. Haec fuit consuetudo in veteri Ecclesia. Corinthios igitur monet Paulus, ut & ipsi ordinem in suis congressibus servent, ne confuse misceant clamores: si quis habet vel Psalmum, vel linguam, vel doctrinam, vel revelationem: sic conferat in medium, ut aedificet Ecclesiam, non ut suum donum ineptè sine fructu aliorum ostentet. Si quis loquitur lingua, fiat per duos, vel ad summum tres, & alternatim. Hoc est, si quis adferre conatur Propheticas conciones, & quidem Hebraico ut peregrino idiomate, tantum duobus vel ad summum tribus hoc permittatur, & per vices. Et unus aliquis interpretetur. Lecta sententia ex Prophetarum scriptis secundum Hebraicam veritatem, mox addatur interpretatio, ut Ecclesia aedificari possit. Quod si non adsit interpres, peregrina lingua non adferatur in medium, ex ea enim Ecclesia nullum percipit fructum, cùm eam non intelligit. Ne tamen is, qui linguam peregrinam tenet, putet donum hoc esse inutile, potest ille sibi & Deo ista lingua loqui, & seipsum excitare ad invocationem, gratiarum actionem, spem & patientiam: sed Ecclesia Dei ignota lingua sine interpretatione fatiganda non est.

## 14:29
Let two or three prophets speak: and let the others judge.

Paul proceeds to teach in what order all things ought to be carried out in public assemblies: and first of all, he establishes those things which belong to the ministry of the word. Not all are instructed with the gift of preaching to the people and explaining the articles of faith: therefore he does not permit individuals to teach or shout in the public assembly of the Church: Let, he says, two or three prophets speak: He wishes two or three prophets to be chosen and appointed by the Church, that is, preachers and heralds of the word.

This testimony is therefore clear and evident, that the Church of Jesus Christ has the power and authority of choosing, calling, and appointing Prophets, Pastors, Doctors, and heralds of the word, who may teach the people about God and eternal life. This authority does not depend upon the political magistrate: nor is the right of calling ministers of the Gospel granted to Bishops alone: But the Holy Spirit instructs the Church of Christ with this great authority. The political magistrate converted to the faith indeed acts piously if, when the people are either ignorant or negligent of their right in calling suitable ministers, he promotes the kingdom of Christ, and undertakes the care of the people, and calls pious Pastors for the benefit of the Church: but it is not to be thought that this power resides with the political magistrate alone: and that when he is negligent or persecuting the truth of the Gospel, it is not permitted for the Church to call Pastors and to entrust to them the office of teaching: For in this place the Holy Spirit expressly attributes this right to the Church without any mention being made of the political Magistrate. And since Jesus Christ the son of God has delivered the keys of the kingdom of heaven to his Church, no pious person can doubt that Christ has given to his Church the power of calling and appointing faithful Pastors and Bishops.

Hence therefore let the Church of Christ learn its right in calling ministers: And let the faithful ministers of the word seek hence firm consolation, that they may be certain in conscience that they have been legitimately and by God called, when they have been appointed by the authority of the Church as heralds of the word. This is a great consolation in the most grave dangers and difficulties, to know that you are in the station into which the Son of God himself has placed you through his Church. For hence you can conceive a certain hope of the presence, help, and defense of Christ. Paul also here prohibits that anyone should break forth to teach in public without a calling: for it is a grave thunderbolt: which exists in Jeremiah. They ran and I did not send them. Therefore, by the consent of the Church, two or three are to be appointed, according to the necessity of the assembly, to whom the duty of teaching and explaining the holy scripture is to be committed. And Paul wishes a distinction to be observed between the Prophets, That is, Pastors and Doctors in the Church, and between the hearers, whom he wishes to judge concerning the sermons of the Prophets.

Let the others judge: Paul does not grant to Prophets or preachers that they should bring forth any dreams, or figments of opinions, or fables into the midst, or that they should twist the holy scripture according to their own will, and accommodate it to the inventions of human minds: but he wishes those things to be proposed which do not fear to undergo the judgment of the Church of God, which is the seat and pillar of truth, and the dwelling of the Holy Spirit. Therefore Paul established judgment in the Church: and he wishes individual dogmas to be examined, whether they are ἀνάλογα of faith. Here, let it be observed above all that by Apostolic testimony the judgment concerning the doctrine of Pastors is deferred to the whole Church and to individual hearers. For it is in the interest of all that sound and uncorrupted doctrine be proposed; it must be attended to by individuals, lest they be infected by false doctrine. Whence also Christ says: Beware of false prophets: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees. And John says in his Epistle: Test the Spirits, whether they are from God. The Roman Antichrist with horrible audacity claims for himself and his councils and Bishops the right of judging concerning the controversies of religion, and wishes to be exempt from all judgment. This is a manifest mark of the Antichrist. Paul does not wish the ministers of the Church to be ἀνυπευθύνους superior to all judgment, but subjects them to the examination of the hearers, and wishes the Spirits and doctrine to be tested, whether they are from God. The pontiffs also contend, just as civil judgments pertain only to the civil magistrate: so the judgment concerning doctrine pertains only to Bishops and Ecclesiastical persons: and they wish secular princes and the common people to stand by the judgment of the Bishops without any examination in matters of religion. Paul refutes this most unjust and most dangerous tyranny here: and he attributes to individual pious persons, as much to laymen as to clerics, the right and power of judging concerning the doctrine of pastors. Let two or three prophets speak: let the others (he says), that is to say the hearers, and the whole Church judge. For in the final judgment each one is going to render an account for himself, whether they have believed the Gospel of Jesus Christ rightly or otherwise. If a blind man leads a blind man, both fall into the pit, says the Holy Spirit. It is not therefore safe to have faith in all teachers without examination. For there are many false prophets, who come in sheep's clothing. And Satan can transform himself into an angel of light.

Let pious minds therefore vindicate and defend with all their strength this right of theirs, which the Son of God has granted to them: let them know that this is a great glory, that it is permitted to pious persons to judge concerning the doctrine, sermons, and decrees of any teacher, or Bishop, or of an entire council: let them also know that this right cannot be neglected without the greatest danger to souls. Nor is there any reason for anyone to object that the judgment concerning the highest matters of faith cannot be entrusted to the unskilled. For the Church of Jesus Christ is not unskilled: pious minds, which have learned the Catechism, hold the articles of faith, have exercises of repentance, and of invocation, and are illuminated and led by the Holy Spirit into all truth, are not to be condemned for ignorance. often some pious person placed in an obscure position judges better concerning some serious controversy than a Bishop of great name or a celebrated doctor in the Church. For the gifts of the Holy Spirit are not tied to sublime places or celebrated persons: And all pious people ought to understand the articles of faith. They can despise the empty subtleties of idle or fanatical men.

Let this right therefore remain to individual pious people, that it is permitted to each one to make a judgment and to examine by the rule of the divine word all the dogmas of any Bishops or councils whatsoever: just as Paul also says, you can all prophesy one by one, That is, to state an opinion concerning doctrine: so that all may learn, and all may receive consolation. This liberty granted to pious people by Christ does not overturn the judgments of synods, nor does it produce confusion and infinite license to embrace what one pleases and to repudiate what displeases. For God has entrusted the care and custody of incorrupt doctrine both to the elders and to the more experienced: As Actorum 15. the Apostles and elders were gathered, that they might consider this cause.

And Paul commands the Bishops: Attend to yourselves and to the whole flock. for I know that savage wolves will come. Let there be, therefore, the judgments of synods: let Bishops and elders, pious men of proven faith, skilled in the struggles of the Church, learned in the sacred letters, not ignorant of the Prophetic and Apostolic speech, come together: let them consider the controversies that have been stirred up: let them weigh the foundations of the dogma: and let them show what agrees with the Prophetic and Apostolic doctrine: what dissents from it. But let this Synod not take upon itself a praetorian or royal authority: as if its sentence were valid on account of its position and authority: let it not think itself to be ἀνυπεύθυνον, but let it subject its sentence to the examination of the pious: and let it show the foundations of its decree from clear testimonies of the divine word, to which it is necessary to assent, and in which pious minds can safely rest. For Christ has not granted to the pious an infinite license either to reject what displeases our palate, or to approve what pleases our wit: but He has placed for them certain boundaries of judging. Where it is established that the doctrine of the Pastor, or the decree of a council, agrees with the Prophetic and Apostolic writings, and rests upon clear and indubitable testimonies of the Holy Spirit, then it is necessary to assent without any exception, or further inquiry. Here has place, He who hears you, hears me: He who rejects you, rejects me. Item, if anyone the Church refuses to hear, let him be to you as a Gentile. But where the foundation of a doctrine or of a proposed opinion is not demonstrated in the Prophetic and Apostolic writings, it is not only permitted to subject the controversy to ἐπέχειν, and examination, but it is also necessary. But if a new dogma or decree of a council conflicts with the doctrine of the Apostles, the pious have a command: if anyone has taught another Gospel than I, Paul, have taught, even if he were an angel from heaven, let him be anathema. This most grave and necessary doctrine must be considered in the saying of Paul (let the others judge).

Latin:

Prophetae duo aut tres loquantur: caeteri diiudicent.

Pergit Paulus docere, quo ordine omnia in publicis congressibus peragi debeant: & inprimis ea, quae sunt ministerii verbi, constituit. Non omnes instructi sunt dono concionandi ad populum, & explicandi articulos fidei: Non ergò permittit singulis, ut doceant vel vociferentur in publico Ecclesiae congressa: Prophetae, inquit, duo aut tres loquantur: Vult ab Ecclesia eligi & constitui duos aut tres Prophetas, id est, concionatores & precones verbi.

Est ergo hoc testimonium perspicuum & evidens, quod Ecclesia Iesu Christi habeat potestatem, & authoritatem eligendi, vocandi, & constituendi Prophetas, Pastores, Doctores, & praecones verbi, qui populum doceant de Deo & vita aeterna. Non pendet haec authoritas à politico magistratu: neque solis Episcopis concessum est ius vocandi ministros Evangelii: Sed Spiritus sanctus Ecclesiam Christi hac tanta authoritate instruit. Piè quidem facit magistratus politicus ad fidem conversus si populo vel ignorante vel negligente ius suum in vocandis idoneis ministris, promovet regnum Christi, & curam populi suscipit, & in Ecclesiae commodum vocat pios Pastores: sed non est putandum penes solum magistratum politicum hanc residere potestatem: & eo negligente vel persequente veritatem Evangelii, non licere Ecclesiae, Pastores vocare & illi munus docendi mandare: Hoc enim in loco Spiritus sanctus disertè tribuit hoc ius Ecclesiae non facta ulla mentione politici Magistratus. Et cùm Iesus Christus filius Dei, claves regni coelorum tradiderit Ecclesiae suae, nemo pius dubitare potest Christum Ecclesiae suae dedisse petestatem vocandi & constituendi fideles Pastores & Episcopos.

Hinc ergò Ecclesia Christi discat ius suum in vocandis ministris: Et fideles verbi ministri petant hinc firmam consolationem, ut certi sint in conscientia se legittimè & à Deo vocatos esse, quando authoritate Ecclesiae constituti sunt verbi praecones. Magna haec consolatio est in gravissimis periculis & difficultatibus, scire quod sis in statione, in quam te ipse filius Dei per Ecclesiam suam collocavit. Hinc enim spem certam concipere potes, de praesentia, auxilio & defensione Christi. Paulus etiam hîc prohibet, ne quis sine vocatione prorumpat ad docendum in publico: fulmen enim grave est: quod apud Ieremiam extat. Currebant & non mittebam eos, De consensu igitur Ecclesiae constituendi sunt, duo vel tres, pro necessitate caetus, quibus munus docendi & explicandi sacram scripturam est committendum. Et vult Paulus discrimen observari inter Prophetas, Id est, Paltores & Doctores in Ecclesia & inter auditores, quos vult iudicare de Prophetarum concionibus.

Caeteri diiudicent: Non concedit Paulus Prophetis vel concionatoribus ut quaevis somnia, vel figmenta opinionum, vel fabulas proserant in medium, vel sacram scripturam pro suo arbitrio contorqueant, & ad commenta humanorum ingeniorum accommodent: sed ea vult proponi, quae non verentur subire iudicium Ecclesiae Dei, quae est sedes, & columna veritatis, & domicilium Spiritus sancti. Constituit ergò Paulus iudicium in Ecclesia: & vult singula dogmata examinari, num sint ἀνάλογα fidei. Hîc inprimis observetur Apostolico testimonio iudicium de doctrina Pastorum, deferri toti Ecclesiae & singulis auditoribus. Interest enim omnium, ut sana & incorrupta proponatur doctrina; singulis attendendum est, ne falsa doctrina inficiantur. Unde & Christus dicit: Cavete vobis à pseudoprophetis: Cavete vobis à fermento Phariseorum. Et Ioannes inquit in Epistola: Probate Spiritus, utrum ex Deo sint. Romanus Antichristus horribili audacia vendicat sibi & suis conciliis & Episcopis ius iudicandi de controver iis religionis, & omni iudicio vult esse exemptus. Haec manifesta nota est. Antichristi. Paulus non vult ministros Ecclesiae esse ἀνυπευθύνους omni iudicio superiores, sed subiicit eos examini auditorum, & vult probari Spiritus & doctrinam, utrum ex Deo sint. Contendunt etiam pontificii, sicuti iudicia civilia tantum ad magistratum pertinent civilem: sic iudicium de doctrina tantum ad Episcopos & personas Ecclesiasticas pertinere: & volunt principes seculares & plebem sine omni examine stare iudicio Episcoporum in causis religionis. Hanc iniquissimam & periculosissimam tyrannidem refutat hîc Paulus: & tribuit singulis piis, tam laicis, quàm clericis ius & potestatem iudicandi de doctrina pastorum. Prophetae duo aut tres loquantur: caeteri (inquit) nimirum auditores, & tota Ecclesia diiudicent. Nam in extremo iudicio quisque pro se redditurus est rationem, num rectè an secus, crediderint Evangelio Iesu Christi. Si caecus caecum ducat, ambo cadunt in foveam, inquit, Spiritus sanctus. Non igitur tutum est sine examinè fidem habere omnibus doctoribus. Multi enim sunt pseudoprophetae, qui veniunt in vestimentis ovium. Et Satanas potest se transformare in angelum lucis.

Vindicent ergò & totis viribus tueantur piae mentes hoc ius suum, quod illis filius Dei concessit: sciant hanc magna me esse gloriam, quod licet piis iudicare de cuiusvis doctoris, vel Episcopi, vel totius concilii doctrina, concionibus & decretis: sciant etiam hoc ius sine summo periculo animarum negligi non posse. Nec est quod obiiciat aliquis, imperitis non posse committi iudicium de summis rebus fidei. Ecclesia enim Iesu Christi imperita non est: piae mentes, quae didicerunt Catechesin, tenent articulos fidei, habent exercitia paenitentiae, & invocationis, illuminantur & ducuntur à Spiritae sancto in omnem veritatem, imperitiae non sunt condemnandae: saepè pius aliquis obscuro loco positus, melius iudicat de gravi aliqua controversia, quàm magni nominis Episcopus vel celebris doctor in Ecclesia. Dona enim Spiritus sancti ad sublimia loca, vel personas celebres alligata non sunt: Et omnes pii articulos fidei intelligere debent. Inanes subtilitates ociosorum aut fanaticorum hominum contemnere possunt.

Maneat ergò hoc ius singulis piis, quod licet unicuique indicium facere & ad regulam verbi divini examinare omnia dogmata quorumcunque Episcoporum vel conciliorum: sicut et Paulus dicit, potestis omnes singulatim Prophetare, Id est, sententiam de doctrina dicere: ut omnes discant, & omnes consolationem percipiant. Haec libertas concessa piis à Christo, non evertit iudicia synodorum, nec parit confusionem & infinitam licentiam amplectendi, quod libet & repudiandi quod displicet. Nam & senionibus & peritioribus commisit Deus curam & custodiam incorruptae doctrinae: Ut Actorum 15. congregati sunt Apostoli & seniores, ut considerarent hanc causam.

Et Paulus Episcopis mandat: Attendite vobisipsis & universo gregi: scio enim venturos saevos lupos. Sint ergo synodorum iudicia: conveniant Episcopi & seniores homines pii probatae fidei, periti certaminum Ecclesiae, eruditi in sacris literis, non ignari sermonis Prophetici & Apostolici: considerent motas controversias: expendant fundamenta dogmatis: & ostendant quid congruat cum doctrina Prophetica & Apostolica: quid ab ea dissideat. Verùm haec Synodus non sumat sibi authoritatem praetoriam vel regiam: quasi valeat sententia eius propter locum & authoritatem: non existimet se esse ἀνυπεύθυνον, sed subiiciat suam sententiam examini piorum: & ostendat fundamenta sui decreti ex perspicuis verbi divinite stimoniis, quibus nec esse est adsentiri, & quibus piae mentes tutò acquiescere possunt. Non enim infinitam licentiam vel repudiandi, quod nostro palato displicet, vel adprobandi, quod arridet nostro ingenio, concessit Christus piis: sed certas illis posuit iudicandi metas. Ubi constat doctrinam Pastoris, vel decretum concilii congruere cum scriptis Propheticis & Apostolicis, & niti perspicuis & indubiis Spiritus sancti testimoniis, tum adientiri necesse est sine omni exceptione, vel ulteriore inquisitione. Hic locum habet, Qui vos audit, me audit: Qui vos spernit, me spernit. Item, si quis Ecclesiam audire noluerit, sit tibi velut Ethnicus. Ubi verò non demonstratur fundamentum doctrinae vel sententiae propositae in scriptis Propheticis & Apostolicis, non solùm licet ἐπέχειν, & examini subiicere controversiam, sed etiam necessarium est. Quod si novum dogma vel decretum concilii pugnet cum doctrina Apostolorum, mandatum habent pii: si quis aliud Evangelion docuerit, quàm ego Paulus docui, etiam si angelus fuerit de coelo, sit anathema. Haec gravissima & necessaria doctrina in Pauli dicto (caeteri, diiudicent) consideranda est.

## 14:30
If indeed it has been revealed to another sitting by, let the first be silent.

There is a great diversity of gifts in the Church; in one there is more light, in another less: nor are all the mysteries of the Spirit understood at once: nor does God give all things to one. Nor is the Holy Spirit bound to a place, or to a rank, or to a person: He freely distributes His heavenly gifts, often bestowing greater light in spiritual matters upon someone placed in the lowest rank than upon a Bishop of supreme dignity: often He gives to a youth or a boy a more illustrious knowledge of Christ and His kingdom than to a wise man. This grace of the Holy Spirit and divine counsel must therefore be acknowledged and received with a grateful mind through whomever God reveals His will to us. Those who are placed in a higher rank in the Church should not exercise tyranny, should not wish to be heard alone, should not pertinaciously defend their own opinions where they have brought forward something less conveniently: If anyone placed in a lower position in the Church understands some passage of scripture more correctly and better through the illumination of the Holy Spirit, let a place for speaking be given to him: let it not shame however celebrated a doctor of the Church to learn the truth resting upon the clear testimony of sacred scripture, even from the lowest Christian, or even a boy. It did not shame Paul, such a great doctor, to learn from Ananias of Damascus. It did not shame the prophet Nathan to retract his opinion concerning the building of the Jerusalem temple. It did not shame Moses to borrow prophecies from the prophet, and even the impious Balaam: for the authority of revelations and doctrines depends not on the person of the minister, but on the Holy Spirit. Therefore, Paul forbids here that anyone should exercise tyranny in the Church: he forbids that anyone should blurt out whatever they please, as if they were superior to all judgment: he forbids that we should despise the word of God on account of the vileness of a person. He requires even of the highest Bishops that they should of their own accord yield to those who bring forward something better and more agreeable to sacred scripture, even if they are of the lowest rank. Eusebius, Bishop of Dorylaeum, thought more correctly concerning the two natures in Christ, than Abbot Eutyches: but because Eutyches was a rich and powerful Abbot, and Eusebius a poor Bishop, Eutyches thinks it unworthy of his person to yield to a poorer man: and he prefers to disturb the whole Church with a new dogma. Malchion, moderator of the School of Antioch, and Presbyter, felt more rightly concerning the divinity of λόγου Jesus Christ, than the Bishop of Antioch, Paul of Samosata: but Paul, puffed up with pride, thinks it unworthy of the person of a Bishop to learn from a presbyter. Therefore, he would rather disturb the whole Church with his own obstinacy by an impious and nefarious dogma, which he himself devised: therefore this precept of Paul is highly necessary.

Latin:

Si verò alii revelatum fuerit sedenti, taceat prior.

Magna donorum diversitas est in Ecclesia, in alio plus, in alio minus lucis est: nec statim omnia intelliguntur mysteria Spiritus: nec uni omnia dat Deus. Nec Spiritus sanctus vel loco, vel gradui, vel personae est alligatus: liberè partitur sua coelestia dona, saepè maius lumen tribuit in rebus spiritualibus alicui in infimo gradu posito, quàm supremae dignitatis Episcopo: saepè iuveni vel puero dat illustriorem noticiam Christi & regni eius, quàm sapienti sem. Haec igitur Spiritus sancti gratia & divinum concilium agnoscendum, & grata mente accipiendum est, per quoscunque Deus revelat nobis suam voluntatem. Qui altiore gradu in Ecclesia collocati sunt, non exerceant tyrannidem, non velint soli audiri, non pertinaciter defendant suas sententias, ubi quid minus commodè protulerunt in medium: Si quis inferiore loco positus in Ecclesia, locum aliquem scripturae rectius & melius intelligit per illuminationem Spiritus sancti, detur huic dicendi locus: non pudeat quantumvis celebrem doctorem Ecclesiae, vel ab infimo Christiano, vel etiam puero discere veritatem nitentem perspicuo sacrae scripturae testimonio. Non puduit Paulum tantum doctorem discere ab Anania Damasceno. Non puduit Nathan Prophetam retractare suarn sententiam de aedificando templo Hierosolymitano. Non puduit Moisen mutuari vaticinia à Propheta, quaro & impio Bileam: non enim à persona ministri, sed à Spiritu sancto pendet authoritas revelationum & doctrinarum. Prohibet ergo hic Paulus, ne quis tyrannidem in Ecclesia exerceat: prohibet ne quis effutiat quidlibet, acsi omni iudicio esset superior: prohibet ne Det verbum propter per onae vilitatem contemnamus. Requirit à summis etiam Episcopis, ut sponte sua cedant etiam insimis aliquid melius, & sacrae scripturae magis consentaneum adferentibus. Eusebius Dorilaei Episcopus rectius sentiebat de duabus naturis in Christo, quàm Abbas Eutyches: sed quia Eutyches dives & potens erat Abbas, Eusebius pauper Episcopus, Eutyches putat indignum esse sua persona, cedere pauperiori: & mavult novo dogmate universam turbare Ecclesiam. Malchion moderator Scholae Antiochenae, & Presbyter rectius sensit de divinitate λόγου Iesu Christi, quàm Episcopus Antiochenus Paulus Samosatenus: sed Paulus inflatus superbia, putat indignum esse persona Episcopi, discere à presbytero. Potius ergò sua pertinacia universam turbat Ecclesiam impio & nefario dogmate, quod ipse excogitavit: summè igitur necessarium est hoc praeceptum Pauli.

## 14:31
For you can one by one all prophesy, that all may learn, and all may receive consolation.

Lest anyone in the Church should be able to complain that a place for speaking is not given to him, when nevertheless he is instructed in doctrine, consolation, or exhortation: because only two or three Prophets are appointed, Paul excepts that he excludes no one: whomever the Holy Spirit has adorned with the faculty of speaking, so that he may be able to instruct the Church of Christ, or to admonish concerning error, or to console, or to exhort to piety, even if he is a public minister of the word is not, yet when necessity and use demand it, a place for speaking must be granted to him, at least so that they do not burst forth to speak at an inopportune time, so that they do not interrupt in the course of the speech, but keep the ordered sequence. for foul is the confusion, which is described in the verse. Νόμαδες: Ακούει δε ὀυδὲις, ὀυδέν οὐδένος. That is, no one hears another. When Paul says, you can all Prophesy, he understands all who boast that they are equipped with the faculty of speaking. For it is manifest that individual pious men are not suitable for speaking.

Here, however, a serious question is now raised, if the power of speaking and teaching is to be granted to all in the Church, what need is there therefore to appoint certain ministers? Against whom therefore is the sad thunderbolt threatened? They ran and I did not send them, Iere: 23.

I answer: First, the Church of God is entirely in need of certain Pastors and ministers, who may be the guardians and heralds of doctrine: who may be entirely occupied with the study of learning, may assiduously propose the doctrine concerning God to the people, and may distribute the Sacraments: For not all pious men can be free for this matter: political governors are occupied with civil business: the father of a family is occupied in educating his offspring and caring for his household. The sad thunderbolt, They ran and I did not send them, strikes those who without a calling invade either by force or by fraud ministries, and those who bring false doctrine, under the title of the divine word bring forth the dreams and figments of their own hearts, they lie about heavenly revelations, they do not serve Christ but their own greed. God did not send these men, but they run of their own accord. Thus Thomas Muntzer, Nicolaus Pelargus of Zwickau, John of Leiden the King of Münster, David Joris, and similar Anabaptists ran of their own accord, not sent by God. Ten years ago at Heidelberg there was a certain Belgian, Justus Velsius, Doctor of Medicine; this man wanted to be considered a Prophet, when he was circulating the ravings of Origen, and contending that a man in this life could be without sin: he even attempted to teach in public, when he had not learned the articles of the faith. This man was not sent: and yet he was running. Therefore let the rule be held: Do not be ἀλλοτριεπίσκοποι: Study this, that you may do your own things. And Christ says: I did not come of myself. Let no one by his own audacity, or confidence of wit, invade the public office of teaching, but let each one await a calling.

However, the opinion of Paul does not conflict with this rule, by which he grants to individuals in the Church a place for speaking: for he speaks of certain cases. When something has been divinely revealed to some private person, when someone sitting in a lower place understands some passage of scripture more correctly than the Pastor: when occur. of the controversy, and also the opinion of the Church must be heard: when a confession is to be published: When the ministers of the Church and pastors applaud a false opinion. In these and similar cases, a place is deservedly given to individual pious persons to speak, and to succor the laboring truth: it has been gravely said.

Κοινὴ γὰρ χρείω: κοινοί δε τε μῦθοι ἔασσι. This is.

That which touches all, ought to be approved by all.

And thus Paul shows here a remarkable consolation to those who, although they are not in the public ministry, are nevertheless compelled either by writing or by voice to instruct the Church. For Paul here grants to individual pious persons a place to speak, and to instruct the Church, when the need demands. You can all prophesy one by one: Therefore if any assembly is destitute of suitable ministers, it is permitted even to a private person understanding the articles of faith, and equipped with the faculty of speaking, to teach others. Therefore if error is spread in the Church, it is permitted even to a private person and one not called to the ministry, either by writing or by voice to refute the error, to show the truth in the word, to warn the Church and to publish his own confession. Therefore it is also permitted to a private person or layman to state an opinion in a synod, and to refute erring bishops. And a simple layman bringing forward Holy Scripture is to be believed more than a universal council establishing decrees without the foundations of Scripture. With this saying of Paul agrees the sentence at Coloss: 3. Let the word of Christ dwell among you abundantly with all wisdom, and teach and admonish one another. Here Paul grants to individual pious persons the faculty of teaching a neighbor about religion and exhorting to piety, yet in such a way that order is preserved, the ministry is not disturbed, false doctrine is not sown, disturbances are not excited, factions are not nourished, and men are not led away from the public ministry. God also enjoins fathers of families that they should instruct their children and family in piety, as Psalm 77 establishes, He set up testimonies in Jacob, and placed a law in Israel, and commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their sons. And Paul says Ephes: 6. Bring up your children in the discipline and doctrine of the Lord. This method of instructing children, however, ought by no means to lead them away from the public ministry, but much more to excite them to frequent public sermons.

That all may learn, and that all may receive consolation: He shows for what end he grants a place of speaking to individuals, and what he ought to regard who desires to set forth his opinion in public: vain ostentation is not to be affected, nor is public tranquility to be disturbed. rightly established dogmas must not be torn up: one must not study subtleties, of which there is no use: contentions about unnecessary matters must not be stirred up: but prayer must be instituted and directed to this end, that all may learn and all may receive consolation: no one is to be left in error or doubt: no one is to be defrauded of necessary consolation, whether Bishop, or Pastor, or layman, he is in need of instruction, admonition, consolation, let individuals help, adorn, and promote the Church according to their strength, and with that gift which they have received from God. O thrice and four times blessed is the Church, if both Bishops and Pastors, as well as hearers, would obey this most wholesome precept of Paul.

And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets. For God is not the (author) of confusion, but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints.

This is a preoccupation. For lest anyone might be able to pretend that he cannot contain himself from bringing forth into the midst the doctrine or revelation which he has, Paul anticipates him, and teaches that it is the impulse of fanatical men when someone cannot be silent and bursts forth to speak at an unseasonable time. The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets. That is, the ministers, who are led by the Spirit of God, do not exceed their authority, do not cease to be in control of themselves, and are not like fanatics, who are driven by frenzies so that they cannot restrain themselves from shouting: just as the heathens describe the frenzies of their own seers.

Such is not the manner of the prophets in the Church: where the prophets are both endowed with a sound mind and deliver the oracles of the most high God with great moderation and gravity. Therefore, when men pretend that they are so driven by the spirit that they cannot be silent, and disturb the order in the Church of God with unseasonable shouting, Paul warns that this is a sign of a fanatic spirit. Others explain these words of Paul in this way, The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets, that is, true and wholesome prophets are not burdened to subject their gifts and doctrines to the college of prophets and teachers to be examined according to the analogy of faith. Both interpretations are suitable.

Paul adds the reason: For God is not the author of confusion. Therefore, He does not fill His prophets with frenzies, as the impure spirit does: He does not command His own to disturb peace and order in the Church: He does not approve of the tyranny of those who wish to be superior to every judgment. the obstinacy of those who, having been convicted by the truth of the matter, are unwilling to depart from their conceived opinion, is not pleasing. God is the author of peace and concord: therefore those spirits who disturb peace without cause, who create tumults in the Church without necessity, who confound order, are not from God. The reason is different when the very salvation of the Church imposes upon us the necessity of contending for the truth. For when we notice that war is being brought against the truth, the pursuit of peace and concord would be most untimely; then the saying of Christ has place: I came not to send peace upon the earth, but a sword and fire.

Accursed be the love, peace, and sacred concord: Which violates the holy dogmas of Christ of God.

As also in all the Churches: That is to say, it is observed. Those things which he prescribed to the Corinthians, he says are observed in all the Churches of the saints. For it is the same Spirit who presides over all the Churches: it is therefore most equitable that you also, Corinthians, should give place to my admonitions, lest your assembly appear unlike the remaining Churches of the saints.

Let your women keep silence in the Churches: for it is not permitted to them to speak, but that they be subject. as also the law says: but if they wish to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home: for it is shameful for women to speak in the Church.

Thus far he has established the ministry, and the judgments and the order of sermons in public assemblies, and he has instructed the men: now he adds a precept concerning women, and he forbids that women be permitted to preach in public. For Scripture pronounces that the woman is under the power of the man Gene: 3. under your husband shall be your desire, and he shall rule over you. Because the woman sinned first, and seduced the man, therefore God imposed this punishment upon her, that she should perpetually be under the power of the man. Since therefore speaking in public is a great part of government, the Holy Spirit teaches that it does not befit the Church of God that they should give women the power of preaching in public, lest they seem to hand over to them any part of government. At home, however, it is permitted to them both to learn from their husbands, and to instruct their children in piety, it is also permitted to them to utter a confession: Hannah the mother of Samuel, testified to her faith by an act of thanksgiving, and proposed her example to the Church. Deborah the Prophetess reveals the command of God, judges and instructs Israel, but at her own home, just as a mother instructs her children. she does not go out into public to preach: she indeed follows the army with Barak as leader when he urges it: but she abstains from preaching in public. Huldah the Prophetess also gives responses and explains the oracles of God in her own home: she does not preach in the Church.

In the New Testament, Mary the mother of the Lord delivers a notable confession concerning the immense mercy of God toward her, and the exhibition of the Messiah: but within private walls in the presence of Elizabeth, and Zechariah, and the remaining relatives. In this way it is permitted for holy matrons to instruct their children and their family in their own home, to lift up and console the sick and those wasting away with grief with the word of God within private walls: and when necessity demands, to deliver a pious confession, and to refute false opinions. And Paul speaks of this case. 1. Corinth: 11: Every woman praying or prophesying with head uncovered, shames her head: clearly, when she prophesies within private walls in the presence of children or relatives, that is, she delivers the word of God, exhorts her own to piety, instructs and consoles others. In the public assembly of the pious, however, they ought to abstain from preaching, lest they seem to assume authority over husbands against scripture.

Did the word of God go out from you

Latin:

Potestis enim singulatim omnes Prophetare, ut omnes discant, & omnes consolationem accipiant.

Ne quis in Ecclesia conqueri posset sibi non dari locum dicendi, cùm tamen doctrina, consolatione, vel exhortatione sit instructus: quia tantum duo vel tres Prophetae sint constituti, excipit Paulus se neminem excludere: quemcunque ornaverit Spiritus sanctus facultate dicendi, ita ut Ecclesiam Christi possit erudire, vel de errore admonere, vel consolari, vel ad pietatem exhortari, etiam si publicus minister verbi non sit, tamen cùm necessitas & usus vostulat, locum dicendi illi tribuendum esse, saltem ne intempestivè prorumpant ad dicendum, ne interpellent in cur su orationis, sed iussum ordinem servent: foeda enim est confusio, quae in versu describitur. Νόμαδες: Ακούει δε ὀυδὲις, ὀυδέν οὐδένος. Id est, nemo alterum audit. Cûm Paulus dicit, potestis omnes Prophetare, omnes intelligit, qui dicendi facultate se instructos esse gloriantur. Nam singulos pios ad dicendum non esse idoneos, manifestum est.

Hîc verò iam gravis movetur quaestio, si omnibus in Ecclesia potestas dicendi & docendi facienda est, quid igitur opus est certos constituere ministros? quibus ergò minatur triste fulmen? Currebant & non mittebam eos, Iere: 23.

Respondeo: Primùm omninò certis Pastoribus & ministris indiget Ecclesia Dei, qui sint doctrinae custodes & praecones: qui toti sint occupati studio discendi doctrinam Ecclesiae adsiduè proponant populo doctrinam de Deo, & distribuant Sacramenta: Non enim omnes pii huic rei vacare possunt: politici gubernatores occupantur civilibus negociis: pater familias in educanda sobole et curandare familiari est occupatus. Triste fulmen, Currebant & non mittebam eos, eos ferit, qui sine vocatione vel vi vel fraude invadunt ministeria, quique falsam adferunt doctrinam, sub titulo verbi divini suorum cordium somnia, & figmenta proferurt, mentiuntur revelationes coelestes, non serviunt Christo sed suae cupiditati. Hos non misit Deus, sed illi sponte sua currunt. Sic Thomas Muntzerus, Nicolaus Pelargus Cygneus, Ioannes Leiden Rex Monasteriensis, David Georgius, & similes Anabaptistae cucurrerunt sponte, non missi à Deo. Ante decennium Heidelbergae Belga quidam erat Iustus Velsius Medicinae Doctor, hic Propheta haberi volebat, cùm origenis deliria circumferret, & contenderet hominem in hac vita posse esse sine peccato: In publico etiam docere conabatur: cùm ille articulos fidei non didicisset. Hic non erat missus: & tamen currebat. Regula itaque teneatur: Ne sitis ἀλλοτριεπίσκοποι: Hoc studete, ut propria agatis. Et Christus inquit: Ego à me ipso non veni. Nemo propria audacia, vel confidentia ingenii invadat publicum docendi munus, sed quisque expectet vocationem.

Non autem pugnat cum hac regula sententia Pauli, qua singulis in Ecclesia concedit locum dicendi: De certis enim casibus loquitur. Cùm alicui privato quid divinitus sit revelatum, cùm quis inferiore loco sedens rectius intelligit locum aliquem scripturae, quàm Pastor: cùm incidunt controversiae, & Ecclesiae quoque sententiae est audienda: cùm edenda est confessio: Cùm ministri Ecclesiae & pastores ad plaudunt falsae sententiae. In his & similibus casibus singulis piis meritò datur locus dicendi, & succurrendi laboranti veritati: graviter dictum est.

Κοινὴ γὰρ χρείω: κοινοί δε τε μῦθοι ἔασσι. Hoc est.

Quod omnes tangit, ab omnibus debet adprobari.

Atque ita insignem hîc monstrat Paulus consolationem iis, qui cùm in publico ministerio non sunt, tamen vel scripto vel voce coguntur erudire Ecclesiam. Paulus enim hîc singulis piis concedit locum dicendi, & erudiendi Ecclesiam, cùm usus postulat. Potestis sigillatim omnes Prophetare: Ergò si quis coetus destituatur idoneis ministris, etiam privato intelligenti articulos fidei, & instructo facultate dicendi, licet docere alios. Ergò si error spargatur in Ecclesia, etiam privato & non vocato ad ministerium licet vel scripto vel voce refutare errorem, monstrare veritatem in verbo, monere Ecclesiam & edere suam confessionem. Ergò & privato seu laico, licet in synodo dicere sententiam, & refelleri Episcopos errantes. Et simplici laico sacram scripturam adferenti plus est credendum, quàm universali concilio sine scripturae fundamentis decreta condenti. Cum hoc dicto Pauli congruit sententia ad Coloss: 3. Sermo Christi habitet inter vos abundè cum omni sapientia, & docete & commonefacite vos mutuò. Hic Paulus singnlis piis concedit facultatem docendi proximum de religione & exhortandi ad pietatem, ita tamen ut ordo servetur, non turbetur ministerium, non seratur falsa doctrina, non excitentur turbae, non alantur factiones, non abducantur homines à ministerio publico. Patribus familias etiam iniungit Deus, ut liberos & familiam erudiant in pietate, ut Psalmus 77 statuit testimonia in Iacob, & legem posuit in Israel, & praecepit patribus nostris, ut notam faciant ea filiis suis. Et Paulus inquit Ephes: 6. Educate filios in disciplina & doctrina domini. Haec autem ratio instituendi liberos nequaquam eos à publico, ministerio abducere, sed multò magis ad frequentandas publicas conciones excitare debet.

Ut omnes discant, & ut omnes consolationem accipiant: Ostendit quo fine concedat singulis dicendi locum, & quid is respicere debeat, qui sententiam suam exponere cupit in publico: non adfectanda est inanis ostentatio, non turbanba est publica tranquillitas: non convellenda sunt rectè constituta dogmata: non studendum subtilitatibus, quarum nullus est usus: non movendae sunt certamina de rebus non necessariis: sed huc instituenda & dirigenda est oratiout omnes discant & omnes consolationem accipiant: nemo relinquendus est in errore, vel dubitatione: nemo de fraudandus est necessaria consolatione, sine Episcopus, sive Pastor, sive idiota, indiget institutione, commonefactione, consolatione, singuli iuvent, ornent, promoveant Ecclesiam pro viribus, & eo dono, quod à Deo acceperunt. O ter quaterque beatam Ecclesiam, si tam Episcopi & Pastores, quàm auditores huic saluberrimo Pauli praecepto parerent.

Et Spiritus Prophetarum Prophetis subiiciuntur. Deus enim non est (author) confusionis, sed pacis, sicuti in omnibus Ecclesiis sanctorum.

Praeoccupatio est. Ne enim posset quis praetendere, non posse se continere, quin proferat in medium quam habet doctrinam vel revelationem, antevertit Paulus, & docet fanaticorum hominum impetus esse, cum quis tacere non potest & intempistivè ad dicendum prorumpit. Spiritus Prophetarum subiecti sunt Prophetis. Id est, Ministri, qui Spiritu Dei aguntur, non excedunt sua potestate, non desistunt esse sui compotes, non sunt similes fanaticis, qui agitantur furoribus, ita ut se continere à clamoribus non possint: quemadmodum Ethnici furores suorum vatum describunt

Non est talis ratio Prophetarum in Ecclesia: Ubi Prophetae & sana mente sunt praediti, & cum magna moderatione & gravitate edunt altissimi Dei or acula. Cùm ergò fingunt homines se adeò impelli à spiritu, ut tacere non possint, & intempestivis clamoribus ordinem in Ecclesia Dei turbant, id esse indicium monet Paulus, fanatici Spiritus. Alii sic exponunt haec Pauli verba, Spiritus Prophetarum subiecti sunt Prophetis, ld est, veri & salutares Prophetae non gravantur sua dona & dogmata collegio Prophetarum & docentium, subiicere examinanda iuxta analogiam fidei. Utraque sententia est commoda.

Rationem addit Paulus: Quia Deus non sit author confusionis. Non ergò replet Prophetas suos furoribus, ut impurus Spiritu fatit: non iubet suos turbare pacem & ordinem in Ecclesia: non probat tyrannidem eorum, qui omni iudicio superiores esse volunt: non delectatur pertinacia eorum, qui convicti rei veritate à sua concepta opinione discedere nolunt. Deus est author pacis & concordiae: Illi ergò Spiritus, qui sine causa turbant pacem, qui tumultuantur in Ecclesia sine necessitate, qui confundunt ordinem, non sunt à Deo. Alia ratio est cùm ipsa salus Ecclesiae im ponit nobis necessitatem certandi pro veritate. Cùm enim animadvertimus bellum inferri veritati, admodum intempestivum esset studium pacis & concordiae, tum locum habet Christi dictum: Non veni mittere pacem in terram, sed gladium & ignem.

Sit maledictus amor, pax, & concordia sacra:Quae violat Christi dogmata sancta Dei.

Quemadmodum & in omnibus Ecclesiis: Scilicet observatur. Ea quae Corinthiis praeseripsit, dicit observari in omnibus Ecclesiis sanctorum. Idem enim est Spiritus, qui omnibus praeest Ecclesiis: aequissimum est igitur, ut & vos Corinthii locum detis meis admonitionibus, ne caetus vester adpareat dissimilis reliquis Ecclesiis sanctorum.

Mulieres vestrae in Ecclesiis sileant: non enim conceditur ipsis, ut loquantur, sed ut subditae sint: quemadmodum & lex dicit: si quid verò discere volunt, domi proprios maritos interrogent: turpe enim est, mulieres in Ecclesia loqui.

Hactenus constituit ministerium, & iudiciae & ordinem concionum in publicis congressibus, & viros erudivit: nunc addit praeceptum de mulieribus, Et vetat ne mulieribus permittatur concionari in publico. Scriptura enim pronunciat mulierem esse sub potestate viri Gene: 3.sub viro tuo erit concupiscentia tua, & ipse dominabitur tibi. Quia mulier primum peccavit, & virum seduxit, Idcircò hanc poenam imposuit ei Deus, ut perpetuò sit sub potestate viri. Cûm ergò oratio in publico sit magna pars gubernationis, docet Spiritus sanctus non decere Ecclesiam Dei, ut mulieribus potestatem faciant concionandi in publico, ne viáeantur illis tradere aliquam partem gubernationis. Domi verò licet illis & discere â maritis, et instituere liberos in pietate, licet etiam eis edere confessionem: Hanna mater Samuelis, gratiarum actione fidem suam testata est, & suum exemplum proposuit Ecclesiae. Debora Prophetissa revelat Dei mandatum, iudicat & erudit Israelem, sed domi suae, sicuti mater erudit liberos: non prodit ipsa in publicum ad concionandum: sequitur quidem exercitum Barack duce id urgente: sed à concionibus in publico abstinet. Hulda etiam Prophetissa domi suae dat responsa & exponit oracula Dei: non concionatur in Ecclesia.

In novo testamento, Maria mater domini insignem edit confessionem de immensa Dei misericordia erga se, & exhibitione Messiae: sed intra privatos parietes apud Elizabetham, & Zachariam, & reliquos cognatos. Hoc modo licet sanctis matronis domi suae liberos & familiam suam erudire, intra privatos parietes aegrotos & moerore tabescentes verbo Dei erigere & consolari: & cùm necessitas postulat piam edere confessionem, & falsas sententias refellere. Et de hoc casu loquitur Paulus. 1. Corinth: 11: Omnis mulier orans aut Prophetans detecto capite, pudefacit caput suum: nimirum, cùm intra privatos parietes apud liberos vel cognatos Prophetat, hoc est, verbum Dei tradit, hortatur suos ad pietatem, erudit & consolatur alios. In publico autem congressu piorum à concionibus abstinere debent, ne videantur sibi imperium in maritos contra scripturam sumere.

An à vobis sermo Dei profectus

## 14:37
is it? or did it come to you alone? If anyone thinks himself to be a Prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things I write to you are the commandments of the Lord. But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant. Therefore, brethren, desire to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak with tongues.

He attaches at the end a sharp rebuke, so that he may restrain those who are more fierce and more stubbornly defending their opinions, and bend them toward modesty. Without a doubt, the Apostle perceives that the Corinthians are suffering from the vice of pride, and the lust for contention, and stubbornness. Therefore, he uses a sharper castigation, so that he may recall them to a sounder mind. He wants them to remember that they were Gentiles, and received the doctrine of the Gospel from others, namely, from the Jews and the Apostles: it is therefore right that they should allow themselves to be instructed, and receive the laws of piety, not prescribe them to others. The Corinthians are not the only Church of God: they ought therefore to see what honorable customs are observed in the other Churches of the saints as well. And so that he may remove from them every doubt as to whether they ought to obey his warnings or not: he adds that the things he has proposed are the commandments of the Lord, and that this can be understood by those who are spiritual: which If anyone stubbornly opposes himself, it is a certain sign that he is a stranger to the spirit and despises the commandments of the Lord. If anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant: Paul here drives away from himself those who dispute without end: As there are certain contentious and morose dispositions, which never allow themselves to be satisfied, they continually raise new questions, continually bring forward new glosses, continually devise new evasions: but they despise and do not consider the solid foundations which are shown to them. Paul commands that such incurable people be left and despised. Let such people (he says) be farewell, who make no end of disputing and inquiring: There is no reason why we should be moved by the stubbornness and petulance of such men: for they do not seriously inquire after the truth, but rather they insist on ignorance on purpose and delight in darkness. In vain, therefore, would we weary ourselves for their sake. He concludes at last that the gift of Prophecy, as the most useful of all and most necessary for the Church, is to be sought above all, and that one must strive for it with great zeal: but the gift of tongues is neither to be despised, nor hindered, nor envied in anyone, but is to be held in value in its own place.

Let all things be done decently & in order.

Because in these three chapters 12. 13 & 14 he instructed the Church concerning spiritual gifts, he showed their use, he instituted the ministry, he handed down the order of readings, explanations, and prayers. he warned with what modesty and in what order sentences are to be spoken in the public assembly of the Church: he gave precepts to men and women, he concludes this whole passage with this notable rule. That all things in the Church ought to be done decently and in order. But those things are done decently and in order, which first agree with the word of God: Then, which agree with the right judgment of reason, that is, which are done gravely and honestly. And here the Holy Spirit grants to the Church of God the power of ordaining some rites, which may contribute to edification, serve order, and be an ornament to the Church.

Latin:

est? vel ad vos solos pervenit? si quis videtur sibi Propheta esse aut spiritualis, cognoscat, quae scribo vobis, quia sunt mandata domini. Si quis verò ignorat, ignoret. Quamobrem fratres cum zelo studete, ut Prophetis, & linguis loqui ne prohibeatis.

Annectit in fine acrem obiurgationem, ut ferociores & pertinacius defendentes suas opiniones compescat & ad modestiam flectat. Haud dubiè animadvertit Apostolus Corinthios & superbiae vicio, & libidine contendendi, & pertinacia laborare. Itaque acerbiore castigatione utitur, ut eos ad mentem saniorem revocet. Vult eos recordari, quodgentiles fuerint, & Evangelii doctrinam ab aliis, nimirum, à Iudaeis & Apostolis acceperunt: per igitur est, ut se erudiri patiantur, & leges pietatis accipiant, non praescribant aliis. Non soli Corinthii sunt Ecclesia Dei: videre ergò debent, quae honestae consuetudines in aliis quoque Ecclesiis sanctorum seri entur. Utque eximat ipsis omnem dubitationem, num parere monitis debeant, nec ne: subiicit mandata Domini esse, quae proposuit, & hoc intelligi posse ab iis, qui spirituales sint: quod si quis pertinaciter se opposuerit, certum esse indicium, quod alienus sit a spiritu & praecepta Domini contemnat. Si quis ignorat, ignoret: Abigit hîc à se Paulus sine fine disceptantes: Ut sunt quaedam contentiosa & morosa ingenia, quae nunquam patiuntur sibi satisfieri, subinde movent novas quaestiones, subinde novas adferunt glossas, subinde nova excogitant effugia: solida verò fundamenta, quae ipsis monstrantur, contemnunt & non considerant. Huiusmodi insanabiles iubet Paulus relinqui & contemni. Valeant (inquit) tales, qui nullum disceptandi et inquirendi finem faciunt: Non est quod moveamur talium hominum pertinacia & petulantia: non enim seriò inquirunt veritatem, imò data opera insistunt inscitiae & delectantur tenebris. Frustrà igitur ipsorum causa nos fatigaremus. Concludit tandem donum Prophetiae, ut omnium utilissimum & maximè necessarium Ecclesiae, inprimis expetendum, & magno studio ad id nitendum esse: donum verò linguarum, nec contemnendum, nec impediendum, nec invidendum cuiquam, sed suo loco in precio habendum.

Omnia decenter & ordine fiant.

Quia his tribus capitibus 12. 13 & 14 instituit Ecclesiam de donis spiritualibus, monstravit eorum usum, constituit ministerium, tradidit ordinem lectionum explicationum, & precationum: monuit qua modestia & quo ordine dicendae sint sententiae in publico congressu Ecclesiae: dedit praecepta viris & mulieribus, concludit totum hunc locum insigni hac regula. Omnia in Ecclesia oportere decenter & ordine fieri. Decenter autem & ordine fiunt, quae primùm congruunt cum verbo Dei: Deinde, quae congruunt cum recto rationis iudicio, hoc est, quae graviter & honestè fiunt. Atque hîc Spiritus sanctus tribuit Ecclesiae Dei potestatem ritus aliquos ordinandi, quae faciant ad aedificationem, serviant ordini, & sint ornamento Ecclesiae.

## 14:37 Places of Doctrine
Places of Doctrine.

1. The first is concerning the gift of Prophecy, that it is more excellent and more useful than the gift of tongues, for the reason that it edifies the Church more. And therefore all who are instructed with the faculty of speaking ought to aspire most to this gift: so that the Church may be edified with so much more fortunate success.

2. Concerning the gift of tongues, which in its own place is to be held in value and made much of: but without fruit to the Church it is not to be displayed vainly in public.

3. That all things are to be directed to the edification of the Church, and that this ought to be the goal of all gifts.

4. That prayers are to be recited in the Church of God in the vernacular and known language, so that the people may be able to say Amen.

5. Concerning the triple kind of sermons; 1. Doctrine is proposed to the people concerning all articles of faith: to this kind belongs the exposition of sacred scripture: Item the refutation of errors. 2. Exhortation, to this kind belong sermons of repentance, serious rebukes of crimes, threats of punishments, commendations of virtues, and promises of rewards. 3. Consolations.

6. Concerning the causes why the gift of tongues was given to the world. We indicated this above in 4.

7. That the Church of Jesus Christ has the right and power of calling pastors and ministers of the Gospel.

8. That the judgment concerning the doctrine of Bishops, pastors, councils, and any teachers whatsoever is in the hands of the Church: and that it is free for every pious person to inquire into the doctrine of his pastor, and to submit the decrees of councils to examination.

9. That he who is superior in rank or office ought to yield his opinion to an inferior who interprets scripture more correctly.

10. That with order being preserved, and the ministry of the Gospel retaining its own dignity and use, it is permitted for individual pious persons in the Church to express an opinion concerning doctrine, to publish a confession, to instruct others, to confirm the doubting, and to refute blasphemies.

11. That the spirits of the Prophets are subject to the Prophets.

12. That it is not to be permitted for women to preach in the public assembly of the Church.

13. That all things are to be performed decently and in order in the Church.

14. That it is permitted for the Church of God to institute external rites and an order of readings: provided that all things are done decently and in order, and that an opinion of worship, or of necessity, or of merit is not attached to the rites.

Latin:

Loci Doctrinae.

1. Primus est de dono Prophetiae, quod sit praestantius & utilius dono linguarum, eò quòd magis aedificet Ecclesiam Ideòque omnes, qui facultate dicendi instructi sunt, maximè ad hoc donum adspirare debere: ut tanto feliciore successu Ecclesia aedificetur.

2. De dono linguarum, quod suo loco in precio habendum & magni faciendum est: sed absque fructu Ecclesiae in publico non est ostentandum inaniter.

3. Omina ad aedificationem Ecclesiae dirigenda esse, & hunc oportere scopum esse omnium donorum.

4. In Ecclesia Dei vernacula & nota lingua precationes recitandas esse, ut populus possit Amen dicere.

5. De triplici genere concionum; 1. Doctrina proponitur populo de omnibus articulis fidei: ad hoc genus pertinet expositio sacrae scripturae: Item refutatio errorum. 2. Exhortatio, ad hoc genus pertinent conciones poenitentiae, graves reprehensiones scelerum, comminationes poenarum, commendationes virtutum, & promissiones praemiorum. 3. Consolationes.

6. De causis, cur donum linguarum mundo sit datum. suprà 4. indicavimus.

7. Quòd Ecclesia Iesu Christi habeat ius & potestatem vocandi pastores, & ministros Evangelii.

8. Quòd iudicium de doctrina Episcoporum, pastorum, conciliorum, & quorumcunque doctorum sit penes Ecclesiam: & quòd unicuique pio liberum sit inquirere in pastoris sui doctrinam, & conciliorum decreta examini subiicere.

9. Quod is, qui gradu vel munere est superior, cedere debeat de sententia inferiori rectius scripturam interpretanti.

10. Quòd ordine servato, & ministerio Evangelii sua manente dignitate & usu, singulis piis in Ecclesia liceat dicere sententiam de doctrina, edere confessionem, erudire alios, confirmare dubitantes, & refutare blasphemias.

11. Quòd Spiritus Prophetarum sint subiecti Prophetis.

12. Mulieribus permittendum non esse, ut in publico congressu Ecclesiae concionentur.

13. Omnia decenter & ordine in Ecclesia peragenda esse.

14. Ecclesiae Dei licere instituere ritus externos & lectionum ordinem: modò omnia decenter & ordine fiant, & non attexatur ritibus opinio cultus, aut necessitatis, aut meriti.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV.

This whole chapter is a lengthy and distinguished explanation of the article concerning the resurrection of the dead unto judgment and eternal life: which is the sole scope of the entire Christian religion. Fanatical men had disturbed the Corinthians, who had contended that the resurrection of the dead had already been accomplished and fulfilled through regeneration, by which we were made alive with Christ in the Spirit: Nor were they to be understood as the sermons of the Prophets, of Christ, and of the Apostles concerning the resurrection of bodies, and the other life to be in the future after this life. but that after the death of the body all things are finished, and it itself as well. And thus these tricksters have overturned from the foundations the entire religion of Christ. Therefore, Paul institutes here a just refutation of this blasphemous and Epicurean error. He teaches that Christ Jesus truly rose from the dead, and that we together with our bodies shall truly rise again, and that Christ, with death and sin abolished, shall reign in the heavens with blessed men, and that we shall live with Christ for all eternity and shall enjoy heavenly glory. This is the sum of this long sermon.

The whole sermon of Paul can be conveniently divided into 8 members.

1. The member is the Exordium, in which he recalls to the memory of the Corinthians the Gospel which he had taught among them, shows its efficacy, and binds the Church to this doctrine.

2. In the second he places the foundation of the article concerning the resurrection of the dead, namely, the Resurrection of Jesus Christ: and he proves it with many arguments.

3. The third is the proposition concerning the universal resurrection of the dead, and the proof of this article.

4. The fourth contains a comparison of Adam and Christ, of death and life.

5. The fifth contains a comparison of the kingdom of Christ in this life, with his kingdom, which he is to have in the other life in all eternity.

6. It treats of the manner of the resurrection of bodies: of the diversity of glory, which is to shine in the blessed: and of the circumstances.

7. In the seventh member he teaches the cause of human death, and the office of the divine law.

8. Lastly, he gives thanks to God for the victory of Christ, by which he overcame the empire of death and sin: and he raises up the pious with this consolation, that our labors and struggles in this life do not depart without fruit, but have a copious reward stored up in the heavens.

Latin:

CAPUT XV.

Totum hoc caput prolixa & insignis est explicatio articuli de resurrectione mortuorum ad iudicium & vitam aeternam: Qui est totius Christianae religionis unicus scopus. Turbaverant Corinthios homines fanatici, qui contenderant peractam & impletam iam esse mortuorum resurrectionem per regenerationem, quae essemus vivificati cum Christo in Spiritu: Nec intelligendas esse conciones Prophetarum, Christi, & Apostolorum de resurrectione corporum, & vita altera post hanc vitam futura: sed post mortem corporis omnia finiri & ipsam. Atque ita è fundamentis everterunt isti praestigiatores universam religionem Christi. Paulus ergò iustam hîc instituit refatationem huius blasphemi & Epicurei erroris. Docet Christum Iesum verè à mortuis resurrexisse, & nos unà cum corporibus verè resurrecturos, & Christum abolita morte & peccato in coelis cum beatis hominibus regnaturum, & nos in omni aeternitate cum Christo victuros & coelesti gloria fruituros esse. Haec est summa huius prolixae concionis.

Tota concio Pauli in 8. membra commodè dividi potest.

1. Membrum est Exordium, in quo Corinthiis revocat in memoriam Evangelion, quod apud eos docuerit, ostendit eius efficaciam, & ad hanc doctrinam alligat Ecclesiam.

2. In secundo fundamentum ponit articuli de resurrectione mortuorum, nimirum, Resurrectionem Iesu Christi: eamque probat multis argumentis.

3. Tertium est propositio de universali resurrectione mortuorum, & huius articuli probatio.

4. Quartum continet collationem Adae & Christi, mortis & vitae.

5. Quintum continet collationem regni Christi in hac vita, cum regno eius, quod habiturus est in altera vita in omni aeternitate.

6. Agit de modo resurrectionis corporum: de diversitate gloriae, quae fulsura est in beatis: & de circumstantiis.

7. In septimo membro docet causam mortis humanae, & officum legis divinae.

8. Postremò, Gratias agit Deo pro victoria Christi, qua mortis & peccati imperium devicit: & erigit pios hac consolatione, quòd nostri labores & certamina in hac vita non abeant absque fructu, sed habeant mercedem copiosam repositam in coelis.

## 15:1-2
Notum vobis I make known to you, brethren, the Gospel, which I preached to you, which also you have received, and in which you stand, by which also you have salvation: in what manner I preached to you, if you hold fast, unless you have believed in vain.

Paul, about to refute those who denied the resurrection of the dead, and about to illustrate this article, leads the Corinthians to the first source & the immovable foundation of all articles of faith: namely, to the Gospel concerning Jesus Christ, which God announced to the world through the Prophets & Apostles.
