For this is the unique foundation of all our salvation: as Paul clearly teaches, no other foundation can be laid besides that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ. 1 Corinthians 3. Nor is there any more convenient, nor any more valid reason for refuting corruptions of every kind, than if we oppose to them the Gospel of Jesus Christ revealed to the world through the Prophets & Apostles. And thus Paul hands down to us a norm, both for confirming our faith, and for refuting the deceits of errors. For he binds the universal Church to this Gospel, and wishes all dogmas to be examined according to this Gospel, which Paul taught.

That which he says, I make known to you the Gospel, which I have evangelized, shows that it is not enough for sound doctrine to have been proposed once in the Church, and for articles to have been correctly explained: but on account of the sloth and negligence of men: and also on account of the snares of Satan, who from time to time scatters tares among the wheat, it is necessary that doctrine be repeated from time to time, and articles be recalled to memory, and confirmed by testimonies of scripture: so that the pious may constantly persist in the acknowledged faith: Paul says, do not neglect the gift which was given to you through prophecy. He also signifies that he does not strive for this, that he should repeatedly bring forth new sermons, and serve the curiosity of the common people with new opinions: but that he always repeats and inculcates the same doctrine concerning Jesus Christ; and that he devotes himself entirely to this one thing, that he may instill the sound faith of Jesus Christ into his listeners.

The Gospel here signifies not any one article, but the whole doctrine of the Prophets and Apostles concerning Jesus Christ, which Paul had faithfully proposed to the Corinthians: The chief sum of which is this, that Jesus Christ according to the scriptures died for our sins, and according to the scriptures rose again from the dead on the third day for our justification. This is the chief head of the whole religion, to be guarded with the greatest diligence.

Which also you have received, in which also you stand: Paul bears witness to the Corinthian Church, that it had eagerly received the Gospel concerning Jesus Christ, and had constantly retained it. From that doctrine, therefore, which it received from Paul, it can make a judgment concerning the errors of fanatical men and false Apostles. He indicates that the Corinthians would incur the mark of great levity and inconstancy, if they allowed themselves to be led away from that doctrine of the Gospel, which they received by faith, and have hitherto constantly defended spurning the sarcasms of the nations, various dangers, and the insults of Satan. For the knowledge of the Gospel is not retained and constantly defended without a struggle. Since, therefore, the Corinthians not only received the Gospel, but have also persisted in it thus far constantly, it would be unworthy for them now to fall away from it, and to follow empty illusions.

By which also you obtain salvation: This, indeed, is the most serious exhortation of all, by which he stirs them up so that they may constantly persist in the acknowledgment of the truth, since indeed through this Gospel, which they have received, they have obtained salvation: for they have been reconciled to God through faith in Christ: they have been freed from the power of Satan: they have obtained peace of conscience: they have been gifted with the Holy Spirit: and they have been constituted heirs of eternal life: And from this salvation already acquired, which was sealed in their own conscience, they could certainly determine that they had learned the true and saving Gospel of Jesus Christ from the Apostle Paul. Therefore, they ought not to desert the doctrine whose saving efficacy they had already experienced: it also signifies that this true and eternal doctrine of the Gospel cannot be cast aside without the danger of eternal salvation.

This argument is therefore most serious for retaining the Corinthians in the acknowledged truth. And let an illustrious testimony be observed here concerning the saving efficacy of the Gospel. Through this Gospel, which Paul announced to the Corinthians, he says that they have obtained salvation. The preaching of the Gospel is therefore not merely an exercise of the external man, as the Schwenckfeldians rave: but as Paul says, the Gospel is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth. Rom: 1. My word, says the Lord of Hosts, shall not return unto me void: but it shall prosper in everything for which I sent it: just as the rain does not return to heaven without fruit, but makes the earth fruitful. Iesa: 55. God has established this medium and instrument, through which He wills to impart to men in this life light, righteousness, and life, namely the preaching of the Gospel. Paul says, after that in the wisdom of God, the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. 1. Corinth: 1. Let us therefore reverently hold the ministry of the word. Let us certainly determine that this is the highest treasure on earth, the knowledge of the Gospel of Jesus Christ: let us constantly defend the purity of the doctrine of the Gospel, inasmuch as our salvation is contained by it.

If you hold fast, unless you have believed in vain: In order to rouse the more sleepy, he intersperses a very sharp admonition: You must pay attention to what and how I have taught the Gospel, what is the sum of the whole Gospel, what is the foundation of our faith, which is the scope of all religion. For unless you have paid attention, you have believed in vain, and you are going to be deprived of every fruit of faith, namely, eternal salvation. Therefore, let us each apply ourselves so that we may thoroughly learn the very foundations of our faith, and persist constantly in the acknowledged doctrine of the Gospel against any illusions of errors whatsoever.

Latin:

Notum vobis facio, fratres, Evangelium, quod annunciavi vobis, quod & suscepistis, in quo & statis, per quod & salutem habetis: quo pacto annunciarim vobis, si tenetis, nisi frustra credidistis.

Paulus refutaturus eos, qui resurrectionem mortuorum negabant, & articulum hunc illustraturus, deducit Corinthios ad primum fontem & immotum fundamentum omnium articulorum fidei: nempe ad Evangelion de Iesu Christo, quod Deus mundo per Prophetas & Apostolos annunciavit. Hoc enim unicum est omnis salutis nostrae fundamentum: ut Paulus disertè docet, fundamentum aliud poni non potest praeter id, quod positum est, quod est Iesus Christus. 1. Corinth; 3. Nec est alia commodior, nec validior ratio refutandi omnis generis corruptelas, quàm si eis Evangelion Iesu Christi per Prophetas & Apostolos mundo revelatum opponamus. Atque ita normam tradit nobis Paulus, & confirmandi nostram fidem, & refellendi praestigias errorum. Universam enim Ecclesiam ad hoc Evangelion alligat, & omnia dogmata iuxta hoc Evangelion, quod Paulus docuit, vult examinari.

Quod dicit notum vobis facio Evangelion, quod Evangelizavi, ostendit non esse satis semel sanam doctrinam in Ecclesia esse propositam, & articulos rectè explicatos: sed propter hominum oscitantiam & negligentiam: tum propter insidias Satanae, qui subinde zizania spargit inter triticum, subinde repeti oportere doctrinam, & articulos revocari in memoriam, & testimoniis scripturae confirmari: ut pii constanter in agnita fide persistant: Paulus inquit, ne negligas donum, quod tibi datum est per prophetiam. Significat etiam se non hoc studere, ut subinde novas adferat conciones, & novis sententiis curiositati vulgi inserviat: sed se eandem semper repetere & inculcare doctrinam de Iesu Christo; & huic uni rei se totum incumbere, ut sanam fidem Iesu Christi instillet suis auditoribus.

Evangelion hîc significat non unum aliquem articulum, sed totam Prophetarum & Apostolorum doctrinam de Iesu Christo, quam Paulus Corinthiis fideliter proposuerat: Cuius summa haec est praecipua, quòd Iesus Christus secundum scripturas mortuus sit pro nostris peccatis, & secundum scripturas resurrexerit à mortuis tertia die ad nostram iustitiam. Hoc est caput praecipuum universae religionis, summa diligentia custodiendum.

Quod & accepistis, in quo & statis: Testimonium tribuit Paulus Ecclesiae Corinthiacae, quòd Evangelion de Iesu Christo avidè susceperit, ac constanter retinuerit, Ex ea igitur doctrina, quam percepit ex Paulo, iudicium de erroribus fanaticorum hominum & falsorum Apostolorum facere potest. Indicat Corinthios magnae levitatis & inconstantiae notam incursuros, si passi fuerint se abduci ab illa Evangelii doctrina, quam fide susceperunt, & huc usque constanter defenderunt spretis gentium sarcasmis, variis periculis, & insultibus Satanae. Non enim sine certamine noticia Evangelii retinetur, & constanter defenditur. Cùm ergò non tantum susceperint Corinthii Evangelion, sed etiam perstiterint in eo hactenus constanter, indignum esset eos nunc deficere abeo, & sequi inanes praestigias.

Per quod & salutem consequimini: Haec verò omnium gravissima est exhortatio, qua illos excitat, ut constanter in agnitione veritatis persistant, siquidem per hoc Evangelion, quod susceperunt, salutem consecuti sint: reconciliati enim sunt Deo per fidem in Christum: liberati sunt à potestate Satanae: adepti sunt conscientiae pacem: donati sunt Spiritu sancto: & constituti sunt vitae aeternae haeredes: Atque ex hac iam comparata salute, quae in conscientia ipsorum obsignata erat, certò statuere poterant, se verum & salvificum Evangelion Iesu Christi ab Apostolo Paulo didicisse. Non igitur deserere debent doctrinam, cuius salutarem efficaciam iam erant experti: significat etiam sine salutis aeternae periculo non posse abiici hanc veram & aeternam Evangelii doctrinam.

Gravissimum est igitur hoc argumentum ad retinendos Corinthios in agnita veritate. Et illustre testimonium hîc observetur de salutari efficacia Evangelii. Per hoc Evangelion, quod Paulus annunciavit Corinthiis, dicit eos salutem consecutos esse. Non est igitur tantum externi hominis exercitium praedicatio Evangelii, ut Schwenckfeldiani delirant: sed ut Paulus inquit, Evangelium est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti. Rom: 1. Verbum meum, inquit Dominus Zebaoth, non redibit ad me vacuum: sed prospere expediet omne, ad quod misero illud: sicuti pluvia non revertitur in coelum sine fructu, sed foecundat terram. Iesa: 55. Constituit Deus hoc medium & organon, per quod velit hominibus in hac vita impertiri lucem, iustitiam & vitam, nimirum praedicationem Evangelii. Paulus inquit, postquam in sapientia Dei, mundus non cognovit Deum per sapientiam, placuit Deo per stultam praedicationem salvos facere credentes. 1. Corinth: 1. Reverenter ergò ministerium verbi habeamus. Certò statuamus hunc summum esse in terris Thesaurum, noticiam Evangelii Iesu Christi: constanter tueamur puritatem doctrinae Evangelii, utpote qua nostra continetur salus.

Si tenetis, nisi frustrà credidistis:Ut somnolentiores excitet, valde acrem interspergit commonefactionem: Attendendum est vobis, quid & quomodo docuerim Evangelion, quae sit summa totius Evangelii, quod sit fundamentum nostrae fidei, qui est scopus universae religionis. Nisi enim attenderitis, frustra credidistis, & omni fructu fidei, nimirum, aeterna salute carituri estis. Singuli ergò operam demus, ut ipsa fidei nostrae fundamenta probè addiscamus, & in agnita Evangelii doctrina constanter adversus quasvis errorum praestigias persistamus.

## 15:3-4
For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures, and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures.

The sum and foundation of our entire religion is that our Lord Jesus Christ died for our sins, and rose again for our justification. Upon this foundation rests every consolation, every salvation, and our hope. From this also flows that highest consolation concerning the resurrection of the dead and the future glory of eternal life. Rightly, therefore, does Paul begin from this the refutation of the Epicurean error, which denied the resurrection of the dead. For with this foundation thoroughly fortified, that Jesus Christ is the son of God and died for the sins of the world, and rose again for our justification, it is necessary that blasphemous Sadduceeism or Epicureanism, and all heresies, collapse. Therefore, let this noble and highest head of our religion be perpetually in our sight. Because Jesus Christ the Son of God died and was buried for our sins: it is certain by the judgment of the law and the justice of God that satisfaction has been made for us; it is certain that the kingdom of Satan and sin has been overturned: it is certain that the wrath of God has been appeased, and that by the merit of Jesus Christ righteousness has been obtained for us before God: Because Jesus Christ also did not remain in death, but by the power of God rose again from the dead on the third day, and entered into a new and heavenly life, it is necessary that the empire of death has been destroyed: it is necessary that the human race was not created only for the miseries of this life: it is necessary that an eternal and heavenly life remains after this life; it is necessary that the faithful do not hope in Christ only in this life: it is necessary that our bodies, which are inserted into Christ through faith, do not remain perpetually in the dust of death, but at some time rise again to life, so that they may perceive the fruit of their faith, and live with Christ forever. These most ample consolations necessarily follow from that Gospel, that Jesus Christ died for our sins and

he rose again on the third day. Rightly, therefore, Paul repeated, and placed at the head of the refutation of Sadduceeism this sum and foundation of our religion: he proves and fortifies this chief citadel of our religion, first by sacred scripture. Christ, he says, died according to the scripture, and rose again according to the scripture: This is the firmest demonstration of all for our religion: for God cannot lie. Therefore, greater faith must be applied to sacred scripture than to the experience of the whole world. The Corinthians held in recent memory the testimonies of scripture concerning the death and resurrection of Christ: Therefore Paul omits them here: However, they ought to be most well-known to the pious, especially Psalm 22. and Isaiah 53.

And that he was seen by Cephas, then by the twelve, then he was seen by more than five hundred brethren at one time: of whom the greater part are still alive, but some of them have fallen asleep. Then he was seen by James: then by all the Apostles, last of all he was seen also by me as by one born out of due time.

He proves the resurrection of Christ with testimonies of the most grave authority, inasmuch as Christ resurrected was seen by the Apostles, who had seen him hanging on the cross and expiring. Paul does not recite all the testimonies of the resurrection of Christ: but only certain principal ones: let the others also be known to the pious, so that they may fortify our faith.

On the very day of the resurrection he gave himself to be seen five times. First he appeared to Mary Magdalene in the garden. John 20. Mark 16. Secondly to the other women, who had come to anoint the Lord: Matthew 28. Thirdly he appeared to Peter. Luke 24. And Paul makes mention of this history here. Fourthly he appeared to Cleopas and Nathanael going into Emmaus. Luke 24. Fifthly towards the evening of the day of the Resurrection he appeared to the disciples gathered together: Luke 24. Mark 16. and John 20. and the Apostle Paul makes mention of this history again here. Sixthly Christ appeared to the Apostles and Thomas gathered together on the eighth day after the resurrection. John 20. He adds then more testimonies of the resurrection of Christ, which are most worthy of observation. For he says that Christ Jesus resurrected from the dead was seen at one time by more than five hundred brethren. This is the seventh appearance of Christ. When this appearance happened, it is not expressed. I think, however, that it was the one of which makes mention. Matthew Chap: 28. That which happened on the mountain of Galilee: where, by the command of Christ and the angels, the Apostles were gathered after the feast of the Passover had been completed, and without doubt with them many disciples of Christ and the Apostles: Paul mentions this notable history here, as the most evident and most certain testimony of the resurrected Christ: for a great part of the disciples, who had been ἄυτοπται,, was still surviving and could testify with a living voice that they had seen Christ. Eighth, Christ appeared at the Sea of Tiberias to Simon Peter, Thomas, Nathanael, the sons of Zebedee, and two others of the Apostles, which appearance is described John: 21. Ninth, as Paul testifies here, Christ was seen by James, who was called the brother of the Lord, for the reason that he was born of the sister of Mary, the aunt of Christ, who was the first Bishop of the Church of Jerusalem. But where and when this appearance happened, it is not written. Tenth, Christ appeared to all the Apostles, as Paul testifies here, namely on the day of the ascension of the Lord near Bethany on the Mount of Olives. Luke: 24.Acts: 1. Where in the sight of the Apostles and many disciples Christ ascended into heaven.

These appearances are described in the history of the Evangelists, so that, confirmed by these testimonies, we may certainly establish that Jesus Christ truly was raised from the dead, and now reigns at the right hand of the eternal Father. Without doubt, Christ offered himself to be seen quite often after his resurrection from the dead, since Luke Acts 1 testifies that Jesus Christ, after he rose from the dead, conversed with the Apostles for 40 days, and spoke about the kingdom of God: but because those narrations of so many appearances were sufficient to create faith, therefore they omitted the rest. Paul, however, testifies that Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, was seen by him also: and as much as can be gathered from various places, Paul saw the Lord several times. For on the journey, when he was proceeding to Damascus, he saw the Lord Jesus, as Ananias testifies. And he speaks of this revelation here. Then, being in the temple of Jerusalem, in an ecstasy he saw the Lord JESUS, commanding that he should depart. Furthermore, he saw the Lord Jesus in the Jerusalem barracks. Acts 23 There is no doubt that he also saw the Lord Jesus when caught up into the third Heaven, and into paradise, of which revelation he makes mention, 2 Cor. 12. Deservedly, therefore, faith is held in Paul as a witness ἀυτοπτῇ. Considering the magnitude of the benefit with which the Son of God, Jesus Christ, affected him, who gave himself to be seen by Paul many times after his resurrection and ascension into Heaven, and him to the Apostles he made him equal: at the same time he also confesses his own unworthiness, so that the mercy and clemency of God toward him might be all the more illustrious.

To me as to one born out of due time Christ appeared: As if he were to say, I was not chosen to the Apostleship together with the other Apostles, I was not present at the sermons and miracles of Christ, I was not regenerated by the word before the death of Christ, like the other Apostles, who saw Christ for 40 days: but after the ascension I was as it were ἐκτρωμα, a foul mass, lacking life, and devoid of light: I was not reborn of the Spirit, I did not know Christ, I was destitute of all life and righteousness, I was a most foul mass in the sight of God: inasmuch as I persecuted the Church of God. Yet so great and so immense was the mercy of God toward me, that He not only imparted life to me, received me into favor, and regenerated me as a son of God, but also gave the resurrected Christ Jesus to be seen by me, and appointed me an Apostle.

Latin:

Tradidi enim vobis inprimis quod & acceperam: quod Christus mortuis est pro peccatis nostris secundum scripturas, & quod sepultus sit, & quod resurrexit tertia die secundum scripturas.

Universae nostrae religionis summa & fundamentum est, quòd dominus noster Iesus Christus pro nostris peccatis mortuus est, & resurrexit propter nostram iustitiam. Huic fundamento innititur omnis consolatio, omnis salus & spes nostra. Hinc etiam manat summa illa consolatio de resurrectione mortuorum & de futura vitae aeternae gloriae. Rectè igitur Paulus hinc orditur Epicurei erroris, qui resurrectionem mortuorum negabat, refutationem. Hoc enim fundamento probè munito, quòd Iesus Christus filius Dei & mortuus sit propter peccata mundi, & resurrexit propter nostram iustitiam, Et blasphemum Sadduceismum seu Epicureismum, & universas haereses collabi necesse est. Sit ergò nobis perpetuò in conspectu hoc nobile & summum caput nostrae religionis. Quia Iesus Christus filius Dei mortuus & sepultus est pro peccatis nostris: certum est iudicio legis, & iustitiae Dei satisfactum esse pro nobis; certum est Satanae & peccati regnum esse eversum: certum est iram Dei placatam esse, & meritò Iesu Christi iustitiam coram Deo nobis impetratam esse: Quia etiam Iesus Christus non mansit in morte, sed virtute Dei tertia die resurrexit à mortuis, & novam ac caelestem vitam est ingressus, necesse est imperium mortis destructum esse: necesse est genus humanum non tantum ad huius vitae miserias conditum esse: necesse est aeternam & coelestem vitam post hanc vitam restare; necesse est fideles non tantum in hac vita sperare in Christum: necesse est corpora nostra, quae per fidem Christo inseruntur, non manere perpetuo in pulvere mortis, sed aliquando resurgere ad vitam, ut fidei suae fructum percipiant, & cum Christo in aeternum vivant. Hae amplissimae consolationes necessariò sequuntur ex illo Evangelio, quòd Iesus Christus pro nostris peccatis est mortuus &

tertia die resurrexit. Rectè ergò Paulus repetiit, & in capite refutationis Sadduceismi posuit hanc religionis nostrae summam & fundamentum: probat autem & munit hanc arcem nostrae religionis praecipuam, primùm sacrae scriptura. Christus inquit, mortuus est secundum scripturam, & resurrexit secundum scripturam: Haec omnium firmissima est demonstratio nostrae religionis: Deus enim mentiri non potest. Itaque maior fides sacrae scripturae adhibenda est, quam universi mundi experientiae. Recenti memoria tenebant Corinthii testimonia scripturae de morte & resurrectione Christi: Itaque Paulus ea hîc omittit: Debent autem piis quàm notissima esse, inprimis Psalm 22. & Iesa: 53.

Et quòd conspectus est Cephae, deinde duodecim, deinde conspectus est plusquàm quingentis fratribus una vice: quorum maior pars adhuc est in vita, quidam verò ex illis obdormierunt. Deinde conspectus est Iacobo: deinde omnibus Apostolis, postremò omnium conspectus est & mihi tanquam abortivo.

Resurrectionem Christi probat gravissimae authoritatis testimoniis, siquidem Christus resuscitatus visus sit Apostolis, qui eum viderant in cruce pendere atque expirare. Non recitat Paulus omnia testimonia resurrectionis Christi: sed tantum praecipua quaedam: sint autem & caetera nota piis, ut fidem nostram muniant.

Ipso die resurrectionis quinquies se conspiciendum dedit. Primùm apparuit Mariae Magdalenae in horto. Ioan: 20.Marci: 16. Secundò reliquis mulieribus, quae venerant ad ungendum dominum: Matth: 28. Tertio adparuit Petro. Lucae: 24. Atque huius historiae hîc meminit Paulus. Quartò apparuit Cleophae & Nathanaeli euntibus in Emaus. Luc: 24. Quintò sub resperam diei Resurrectionis apparuit discipulis congregatis: Luc: 24.Marci: 16. & Ioan. 20. atque huius historiae rursus hîc meminit Apostolus Paulus. Sextò apparuit Christus Apostolis & Thomae congregatis octavo die post resurrectionem. Ioan: 20. Addit deinde plurae tesimonia resuscitari Christi, quae observatu sunt dignissima. Dicit enim Christum Iesum resuscitatum a mortuis una vice plusquam quingentis fratribus visum esse. Haec septima est adparitio Christi. Quando haec adparitio contigerit, non ex primitur. Existimo autem eam fuisse, cuius meminit Mattheus Cap: 28. Quae in monte Galileae facta est: ubi ex mandato Christi & angelorum Apostoli peracto festo pascatos congregati fuerunt, ac sine dubio cum ipsis multi discipuli Christi & Apostolorum: huius insignis historiae meminit hîc Paulus, tanquam testimonii evidentissimi & angustissimi resuscitati Christi: magna enim pars discipulorum, qui fuerant ἄυτοπται, adhuc superstes erat viva voce testari poterat se vidisse Christum. Octavò apparuit Christus ad mare Tiberiadis Simoni Petro, Thomae, Nathanaëli, filiis Zebedaei, & duobus aliis ex Apostolis, quae apparitio describitur Ioan: 21. Nonò, ut hic testatur Paulus, visus est Christus Iacobo, qui dictus fuit frater domini, eò quod ex sorore Mariae matertera Christi natus esset, qui primus fuit Episcopus Ecclesiae Hierosolymitanae. Ubi autem & quando haec adparitio contigerit, non scribitur. Decimò, omnibus Apostolis adparuit Christus, ut hic testatur Paulus, nimirum in die adscensionis domini prope Bethaniam in monte Olivarum. Luc: 24.Acto: 1. Ubi in conspectu Apostolorum & multorum discipulorum Christus in caelum adscendit.

Hae adparitiones describuntur in historia Evangelistarum, ut his confirmati testimoniis certò statuamus Iesum Christum verè à mortuis resuscitatum esse, et iam regnare ad dexteram aeterni patris. Haud dubié saepius se conspiciendum praebuit Christus post resurrectionem à mortuis, siquidem Lucas Acto. 1. testatur Iesum Christum, post quam à mortuis resurrexit, 40. diebus conversatum esse cum Apostolis, & de regno Dei locutum esse: sed quia istae narrationes tot adparitionum sufficiebant ad faciendam fidem: Ideò reliquas omiserunt. Paulus verò testatur & sibi visum esse Iesum Christum, à mortuis resuscitatum: ac quantum ex variis locis colligere licet Paulus aliquoties vidit Dominum. Nam in itinere, cùm Domascum pergeret, vidit Dominum Iesum, ut Anonias testatur. Et de hac revelatione hîc loquitur. Deinde in templo Hierosolomitano existens, in ecstasi vidit Dominum IESUM, praecipientem ut egrederetur. Vidit praeterea dominum Iesum in castris Hierosolymitanis. Acto. 23. Non dubium est, quin etiam viderit Dominum Iesum raptus in tertium Coelum, & in paradysum cuius revelationis meminit, 2. Corinth. 12. Meritò igitur Paulo tanquam testi ἀυτοπτῇ fides habetur. Considerans Paulus magnitudinem beneficii, quo eum filius Dei Iesus Christus & adfecit, qui se Paulo multoties post resurrectionem & ascensionem in Coelos conspiciendum dedit, eumque Apostolis parem fecit: simul & indignitatem suam fatetur, ut tantò illustrior sit Dei misericordia & clementia erga ipsum.

Mihi tanquam abortivo visus est Christus: Quasi dicat, Ego non sum unà cum aliis Apostolis electus ad Apostolatum, non interfui concionibus & miraculis Christi, non sum regeneratus verbo ante Christi mortem, ut caeteri Apostoli, qui Christum viderunt 40. diebus: sed post adscensionem veluti ἐκτρωμα eram, massa foeda, carens vita, & expers lucis: non eram renatus ex Spiritu, non noveram Christum, destituebar omni vita & iustitia, foedissima massa eram in conspectu Dei: siquidem persequebar Ecclesiam Dei. Tanta autem & tam immensa fuit Dei erga me misericordia, ut non solùm vitam mihi impertiverit, me in gratiam receperit, & in filium Dei regeneraverit, sed etiam Christum Iesum resuscitatum à mortuis mihi conspiciendum dederit, & Apostolum constituerit.

## 15:9-10
For I am the least among the Apostles, who am not worthy to be called an Apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God. But by the grace of God I am what I am: and His grace in me (bestowed) was not in vain: but I labored more abundantly than the others: yet not I, but the grace of God, which was with me.

He further commemorates his own dignity, so that he may amplify and illustrate all the more the beneficence and mercy of God, who bestowed such a greatness of gifts upon him. This is indeed a most evident argument, and a most brilliant testimony that the mercy of God is immense toward unworthy and miserable sinners, since He not only converted a cruel and vehement persecutor of the Church to the faith, and received him into grace, but also adorned him with such a greatness of gifts that he is numbered among the Apostles of Jesus Christ. Therefore, those whom the consciousness of great offenses terrifies and attempts to drive to despair, let them always gaze upon this illustrious example of the mercy of God.

By the grace of God, he says, I am what I am: Everything, he says, that I am and have, I am and have not from myself, but from the immense mercy of God.

And His grace in me was not in vain: Lest the false apostles hold the Apostleship of Paul in contempt, he shows that the gifts which were bestowed upon him did not exist without fruit: for many churches he instructed and laudably established: and the doctrine of the Gospel, which he spread most widely. That he says he labored more than the other Apostles, he does not contend with emulation against the remaining Apostles of Jesus Christ, but he commends his ministry, and shows that God grants a happy success to his labors: the Apostles labored with great faith in the vineyard of the Lord, each according to his own measure, but Paul was superior to all: He spread the seed of the divine word into many nations; Paul traveled through a great part of Asia and Europe, so that he might convert many nations to the faith, Paul sustained most grave struggles, he underwent very many dangers, just as he narrates in the 2nd Epistle to the Corinthians: His Epistles also now instruct the Churches of God in the whole world more than the monuments of the remaining Apostles. Therefore the boasting of Paul is true: in which he looks rather to the fruit of his labors and of his ministry, than to his own praise. And therefore he repeats. But not I, but the grace of God, which was with me: Lest anyone should suspect him to be desirous of vain glory, and lest he should provide an opportunity for sophistry to the proud patrons of free will, he wishes nothing to be attributed to himself in such great success of his labors, but all things to be ascribed to the grace of the Holy Spirit. For it is God, who supplies to us spirit, wisdom, strength of body and mind, the office, the occasions, efficacy, prosperous success, protection, and everything. Therefore, everything is of God, and nothing is ours.

Latin:

Ego enim sum minimus inter Apostolos, qui non sum dignus, qui vocer Apostolus, eò quòd persecutus sum Ecclesiam Dei. Gratia verò Dei sum, quod sum: & gratia ipsius in me (collata) non fuit inanis: sed copiosius laboravi, quàm caeteri: non ego autem, sed gratia Dei, quae mihi adfuit.

Commemorat amplius suam in dignitatem, ut amplificet atque illustret tantò magis beneficentiam et misericordiam Dei, qui tantam donorum amplitudinem contulit in ipsum. Evidentissimum sanè est hoc argumentum, & testimonium luculentissimum immensam esse Dei misericordiam erga indignos & miseros peccatores, siquidem saevum & vehementem Ecclesiae persecutorem non solùm convertit ad fidem, & recepit ingratiam, sed etiam tanta donorum amplitudine exornavit, ut Apostolis Iesu Christi annumeretur. Quos ergo delictorum magnorum conscientia terret & ad desperationem adigere conatur, hi semper hoc illustre misericordiae Dei exemplum intueantur.

Gratia Dei inquit sum, quod sum: Totum inquit, quod sum & habeo, non ex me, sed immensa Dei misericordia & sum & habeo.

Et gratia Dei in me non fuit inanis: Ne Pseudoapostoli contemptim habeant Apostolatum Pauli, ostendit dona, quae ipsi collata sunt, non absque fructu extitisse: multas enim Ecclesias erudivit & laudabiliter constituit: & doctrinam Evangelii, quam latissimè sparsit. Quòd dicit se plus caeteris Apostolis laborasse, non certat aemulatione cum reliquis, Apostolis Iesu Christi, sed commendat suum ministerium, & ostendit Deum largiri laboribus eius felicem successum: Apostoli magna fide laborarunt in vinea domini, quisque pro sua mensura, sed Paulus omnibus fuit superior: In multas gentes sparsit semen verbi divini; magnam partem Asiae & Europae peragravit Paulus, ut multas gentes ad fidem converteret, gravissima sustinuit Paulus certamina, plurima subiit pericula, quemadmodum narrat in 2. Epistola ad Corinth: Ipsius etiam Epistolae nunc magis erudiunt Ecclesias Dei in universo orbe, quàm reliquorum Apostolorum monumenta. Vera est igitur gloriatio Pauli: in qua potius fructum suorum laborum & sui ministerii respicit, quàm suam laudem. Ideoque repetit. Non ego autem, sed gratia Dei, quae mihi adfuit: Ne quis suspicaretur eum inanis gloriae essem cupidum, & ne superbis patronis liberi arbitrii ansam sophisticandi praeberet, nihil sibi vult tribui in tanto successu suorum laborum, sed omnia adscribi gratiae Spiritus, sancti. Deus enim est, qui nobis suppeditat spiritum, sapientiam, robur corporis & animi, munus, occasiones, efficaciam, successum prosperum, protectionem & omnia. Totum ergò Dei est, & nihil est nostrum.

## 15:11
Whether therefore I, or they: so we preach, and so you believed.

He warns the Corinthians, lest on account of the diversity of ministers and gifts they should think the dogmas of the Gospel to be diverse. For there is one heavenly truth, by which our salvation is contained, whether it be preached by a Prophet, by an Apostle, by an Angel, or by a Bishop: whether the herald of truth be instructed with the highest or with mediocre gifts, he is compelled to sound the same doctrine of the Gospel. For the Gospel was not invented or devised by men or Angels: but God alone made known His will concerning the salvation of men and the gathering of the Church through His Son. It is not permitted for any Angel to change this. Therefore Paul says, if an Angel from heaven should teach another Gospel, let him be anathema. Therefore, one must always look not to the diversity of gifts in ministers: but to the eternal God, the author of the most holy Gospel.

Latin:

Sive igitur ego, sive illi: ita praedicamus, & ita credidistis.

Monet Corinthios, ne propter ministrorum & donorum diversitatem arbitrentur diversa esse dogmata Evangelii. Una est enim coelestis veritas, qua salus nostra continetur, sive ea à Propheta, ab Apostolo, ab Angelo, vel ab Episcopo praedicetur: sive praeco veritatis summis sive mediocribus donis sit instructus, eandem doctrinam Evangelii sonare cogitur. Non enim ab hominibus vel Angelis inventum aut excogitatum est Evangelion: sed solus Deus suam voluntatem de salute hominum & collectione Ecclesiae per filium patefecit. Hanc non licet ulli Angelo mutare. Ideò Paulus inquit, si Angelus de coelo aliud Evangelion docuerit, sit anathema. Non ergò ad diversitatem donorum in ministris: sed ad authorem sacro sancti Evangelii Deum aeternum semper est respiciendum.

## 15:12-23
If however Christ is preached, that He has been raised from the dead, how some among you say, that there is no resurrection of the dead:

This is the principal proposition of this 15th Chapter, fortified by a most firm argument, taken from the efficient cause, which he premised: it is a false, he says, dogma, which some among you assert, that there is no resurrection of the dead: for Jesus Christ truly rose from the dead, as was demonstrated above. The Apostle shows here what was the occasion for him writing this chapter: namely, the Sadduceeism of certain ones, who, although they wished to be considered not only Christians, but also Apostles of Christ: nevertheless openly taught that there is no resurrection of the dead: just as the Sadducees also had openly taught among the people of God. Without doubt others depicted this error in different ways: Some simply affirmed that souls together with bodies are extinguished, and that man after death differs in nothing from a brute animal: others imagined that souls indeed are survivors for some time, after they are released from bodies: but that bodies do not rise again. But whatever the scripture might testify concerning the resurrection of the dead, that was to be understood concerning spiritual vivification and regeneration through Baptism, and the whole ministry; as when Paul the persecutor of the Church is converted to God through the Holy Spirit, he is regenerated and is vivified, that he may walk in newness of life, having been raised from the dead. However they may have depicted the error, this was the sum, that after the death of the body all things are finished, and that no other life remains after this life. From this let the pious reader estimate how immense is the power of Satan, who, while Jesus Christ the Son of God was teaching the world, dared through his Sadducees to bring forth so impudent a dogma in the Church of God? And at that very time, when the Son of God by his resurrection from the dead most evidently demonstrated the entire religion, and indeed the article concerning the resurrection of the dead: at which many were still surviving who had beheld Jesus Christ raised from the dead: at which most of the Apostles were still instructing the Church: at which through the Apostles and other heralds of the Gospel many dead were being recalled to life: yet he dared openly and publicly through false apostles to dispute against the doctrine concerning the resurrection of the dead. It is not therefore a wonder in this delirious old age of the world that profane Sadduceeism prevails: and that men slip into security. But let us fortify our breasts so much the more diligently against these furies of the Sadducees and Epicureans: and let us fix in our minds this irrefutable demonstration, which Paul here supplies to us. Christ, he says, He rose from the dead: Therefore it is most certain that there is a resurrection of the dead, and indeed of human bodies. The consequence holds from the efficient cause to the proper effect. The resurrection of Christ is the efficient cause of our resurrection: but Jesus Christ truly rose. Therefore it is necessary that we also rise. As Christ did not die for himself, but for us: so neither did he rise for himself, but for us. Not only the divinity of Christ, devoid of death, lives from eternity into all eternity, but also his humanity, immune from every stain of sin, could have lived in all eternity: had he not undergone death for the sake of our salvation. Since therefore Christ both died and rose for us and for our salvation: it is necessary that we, who believe in Christ, become participants of his death and resurrection. It is necessary that the fruit of his resurrection, by which he broke the power of death, be communicated to us: It is necessary that we be made conformable to the image of his glory. And since we are members of the body of Christ, but Christ, as the Head of the Church, rose from the dead with his body, it is necessary that we, as members of Christ, rise from death with our bodies. This is a most certain demonstration, which can be weakened by no Sophistry, For if God had wished to leave us in death, and to be entirely devoid of future life, it would not have concerned the son of God to to send a mediator from heaven, it was not necessary for Christ to undergo death, nor was there any reason why Christ should descend to the underworld and rise again on the third day. And the whole work of the redemption of the human race would have been undertaken in vain. Since therefore Jesus Christ the Son of God has truly risen from the dead, it is necessary that we also rise, so that we may perceive the fruit of his passion and resurrection.

If indeed there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ risen.

The same is the argument from the connection of causes and effects. If there is no resurrection of the dead, it is necessary that it be denied that Christ also has risen: for with every effect and every final cause removed, it is necessary that the efficient cause also be denied. For to what end was there a need for the Son of God to die and rise on the third day, if he wished to free the human race from the power of death? If he wished to communicate eternal life to the faithful? And if the resurrection of the dead is denied in general, it must be entirely denied that Christ also has risen from the dead. For he is the leader and head of all who rise from the dead. He made for us a way through death into eternal life: he broke the power of death and the prison of hell: on account of this mediator the dead receive life. But if therefore the resurrection of the dead is denied, the resurrection of Jesus Christ the mediator is altogether overturned.

If however Christ has not risen, then our preaching is vain, and your faith is also vain: And we are found to be false witnesses of God, since we testify against God, that he raised him whom he did not raise, if indeed the dead do not rise: for if the dead do not rise, neither has Christ risen.

He gathers absurdities, which necessarily follow from this false and impious dogma, so that he may thus demonstrate its vanity and falsity. For hypotheses from which absurd and false things follow, must necessarily be false, because from the true nothing follows except the true. Nothing is more absurd than that the entire preaching of the Apostles is vain, and without any fruit. It is one of the greatest benefits, which God out of his immense goodness confers upon the human race, that he instituted the ministry of the Gospel in the human race, raised up, and adorned the Apostles with illustrious gifts, so that they might explain to the world the benefits of the mediator, and show the way to eternal life: this is the highest Treasure of the human race, namely, the preaching of the Gospel, through which we obtain the true knowledge of God, are called to repentance, are regenerated to eternal life, are gifted with the Holy Spirit, and from which in every necessity we draw most efficacious consolations of every kind. To call this most wholesome and salvific preaching, than which there is nothing in the world more precious, nor more necessary, empty, is the height of absurdity and impiety, overturning the entire sacred scripture. Thus it would be the height of absurdity to say that your faith is empty. For through faith you have been freed from idol-mania and Ethnic furies, and have arrived at the acknowledgment of the true God: through faith you have been reconciled to God, you have obtained the remission of all sins, you have been snatched from the power of darkness, and the tyranny of Satan: you have a tranquil conscience: you have been gifted with the Holy Spirit: you have been adorned with distinguished and manifold gifts: you perceive firm consolation in every tribulation: you have free access daily to the throne of God: and you hold a certain hope of the inheritance of eternal life: This faith, therefore, whose such distinguished fruits and effects you have experienced in your heart, and daily To attempt to say that it is empty and void is truly the height of absurdity and madness. But these absurdities necessarily follow, if Christ has not risen from the dead. For this is the head and foundation of the entire preaching of the Gospel: which being overturned, it is necessary that all the articles of faith collapse. For thus Christ shows the sum and cause of the preaching of the Gospel, Luke 24 thus it behooved Christ to suffer, and to die, and to rise again, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name. Upon this foundation also our whole faith rests: by which we both determine that God is reconciled to us, and we hope for eternal life: namely, because Jesus Christ satisfied for our sins by his death: and by his resurrection broke the power of death, and obtained for us righteousness and everlasting life. Since therefore these absurdities, which necessarily follow from the opinion (that Christ has not risen), are in no way to be conceded, it is manifest that the dogma which denies that Christ has risen from the dead is false. Then he attaches another absurdity. From thence it would follow that we the Apostles are false witnesses, who spread manifest lies about God. Since indeed we testify in the world, that God raised Jesus Christ from the dead, when according to the impious dogma Christ has not risen from the dead. It is horrible. moreover, to think that the Apostles of Jesus Christ are accused of false testimony. For it is the same as if someone were to accuse the Holy Spirit of lying: for the Holy Spirit testifies in the world through the mouths of the Apostles concerning the resurrection of Christ, but the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of truth, who cannot lie. Therefore, the Apostles are witnesses greater than any exception: and it is a crime to call their testimony into doubt: Therefore, it remains firm and immovable that Jesus Christ rose from the dead, just as the Apostles testify concerning God, and it follows that there is a resurrection of the dead, which flows from the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

If however Christ has not risen, your faith is vain: you are still in your sins: Therefore also those who sleep in Christ have perished: if in this life only we hope in Christ, we are the most miserable of all men.

He repeats, inculcates, and exaggerates the absurdities which follow from the impious dogma by which the resurrection of the dead and of Christ is denied. For this is by far the most serious argument, which cannot be sufficiently explained by any speech. For if there is no resurrection of the dead, then the entire of Christians Religion is overturned from its foundations: all articles of faith collapse entirely: and all the consolations which exist in the word of God vanish. Paul therefore cannot sufficiently detest the impiety and profanity of this sacrilegious dogma: and in order to deter all the thoughts of the pious from it, he shows that by this error the whole of religion is destroyed. Vain, he says, is your faith: This is, in vain do you believe in God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit: in vain do you embrace the doctrine of the Apostles: in vain do you perform penance: in vain do you struggle against sin, death, and Satan: in vain do you sustain yourselves with divine promises: in vain do you receive baptism: in vain do you partake of the supper of the Lord: in vain do you hope for the benefits and glory of the kingdom of Jesus Christ. For all these things tend to this, that you, reconciled to God through faith, might be resurrected from death, and enjoy eternal blessedness. Truly therefore your faith is vain, he says, if there is no resurrection of the dead. You are still in your sins. To be in sins signifies here for Paul, not to be reconciled to God: to be pressed by the curse of the law: to be guilty before the judgment of God: to feel the horrible burden of sin, and to be under the tyranny of Satan and to be destined for eternal torments on account of sin. Nothing sadder than this misery can be said or thought. But it follows from that dogma, by which The resurrection of the dead is denied. For if the dead do not rise, then Christ has not risen either. If Christ has not risen, therefore He did not exist as the victor over sin and Satan: therefore He was not the true Messiah: since Scripture promised that the Messiah would rise again. Therefore He did not free you from sin and death. It is necessary, therefore, that you still remain in your sins, which is the extreme calamity, if the dead do not rise. Even those who sleep in Christ have perished: The Corinthians had heard a distinguished consolation from Christ, that those who had fallen asleep in Christ would be blessed: Since eternal life and glory awaited them. Now he says, if you take up this sacrilegious error of the Sadducees, all hope for you perishes concerning their blessedness, who have happily fallen asleep in CHRIST JESUS: Indeed he says, not only does hope for you perish concerning the blessedness of the dead, but also the entire religion of Christians will be condemned to extreme madness. For there is no kind of men or sect in the world that undergoes such hatreds, such varied dangers, such calamities, and such dire punishments on account of religion as we Christians: just as the history of the Church, and especially of the Apostles and martyrs, shows: the world can bear sects, errors, blasphemies, and crimes of every kind, at least it cannot bear Christians: The truth of Christ seriously professing, he hates extremely, he detests the Apostles themselves as καθάρματα καὶ περιψήματα. Isaiah was cut with iron: Jeremiah was overwhelmed with stones in Egypt: Paul was beheaded: Polycarp was burned by fire: Ignatius was torn apart by wild beasts; Blandina was placed upon a glowing iron seat: And the world raged against Christians with such madness, that both tyrants and executioners were exhausted, both in devising new punishments and in torturing Christians. Now if there is no resurrection of the dead, nor does any blessedness remain after this life, certainly Christians are the most miserable and most calamitous, and even the most foolish of all men, who ought to be both the wisest and the happiest of all men, for the reason that they alone are illuminated by the light of the divine word, are guided by the leading of the Holy Spirit, alone practice the true worship of God, and are cherished by the clemency of God before all the peoples of the whole world. Since therefore it cannot be that these, whom God embraces with the highest love, in whom God himself dwells as in his own temple, whom he adorns with illustrious testimonies, because they are pleasing to him, to whom he has given most ample promises concerning perpetual happiness, and a copious reward for their labors, are the most miserable of all men. Therefore it is necessary that another life remains and that the dead will rise again, so that God, in accordance with his promises may He fulfill the truth, which He deferred to His saints in this life, in the resurrection of the dead and the other life. And thus Paul teaches here that by this plan the pious are exercised in this life by calamities of every kind, and often have sad ends, so that the very punishments of the innocent may be an illustrious testimony of the future resurrection of the dead, and of the future life. God from heaven testified that the Prophet Isaiah was a faithful minister of the most high God: since through him He brought forth stupendous miracles: And yet He permits him to be sawn asunder: It is necessary therefore that another life remains, in which Isaiah is to be blessed, and in reality to possess that which was promised to him in the word of God (Blessed are all who trust in Him): since in this life he did not attain the promised blessedness.

Now indeed Christ has risen from the dead, the firstfruits of those who sleep.

After he has aggravated and inculcated the absurdities which follow from the nefarious dogma of the Sadducees, he now places an adversative, and repeats the chief foundation of the doctrine concerning the resurrection of the dead, which he demonstrated above with clear testimonies, and also from the preceding arguments gathers and concludes: as if he were saying, All sane people, and those who have even an ounce of piety, are compelled to confess that those horrendous absurdities which I mentioned above must in no way be conceded, unless someone wishes to utterly overturn the entire religion. Therefore, it remains firm and immovable that Jesus Christ truly rose from the dead: and that there is a resurrection of the dead: For Christ is the firstfruits of those who have been raised from the dead. Therefore, the fullness of the Church is to follow from the dead. Christ has gone before the Church as a leader, and has made a way through death to eternal life: the Church of the faithful is to follow Christ: just as Micah predicted. The breaker will go up before them, they will break out and pass through the gate, and will go out through it, and their king will pass before them, and the Lord at the head of them:

For since by man came death, and by man came the resurrection of the dead: For as in Adam all die: so also in Christ shall all be made alive. But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits: afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.

This is the fourth member of this sermon, in which both the source, of death and of resurrection, he demonstrates and compares among themselves; and thus he teaches that Christ did not rise from the dead for himself alone, but for us, and that our resurrection flows from the resurrection of Christ. Through man, he says, death entered into the world, as if he were to say. When Adam fell into sin and death, he did not die alone: but he dragged his entire posterity into death and condemnation: For when he was the root of the entire human race, when he despoiled himself of life and justice, he cast all his posterity into death. Christ, however, the other Adam, and the new root of the elect Church, both preserved life and merited it for all the faithful. Rightly, therefore, our resurrection is gathered from the resurrection of Christ. Paul treats this comparison of Adam and Christ more lengthily, Rom: 5. In this place it is enough for him to have shown both the first cause of death and the first cause of resurrection. Whence the consequence is manifest, because Christ has risen, it is certain that we also shall rise from the dead: because Christ is the second Adam: and he sustains the person of the whole human race: in the place of all men he underwent death: and by his resurrection he merited and prepared life for all. It is to be observed in this place that there is a clear testimony concerning the cause of human death, and concerning original sin. Man was not in his first creation before the fall subject to death: nor was the flux of matter subsequently rushing to other forms, is the cause of human death: Nor does man die rashly or by chance: but through one man came death, and in Adam we all die: That is, the sin or disobedience of Adam brought death into the world: For God had threatened him: On whatever day you eat from that tree, you shall die the death. When Adam transgressed this commandment of God, he cast both himself and all his posterity into death. Therefore, let us always look upon this cause of human death: namely sin, at which God is rightly angry: And let us know that no other remedy against death can be found, except the obedience and resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ. For here is the second Adam, to whom as the second, God entrusted the entire salvation, righteousness, and life of the whole human race: The doctrine also concerning original sin must be sought from here. For Paul teaches that all men are dead in Adam. Therefore, Adam did not only harm himself by his fall: as the Pelagians rave: Therefore, human nature did not remain intact after Adam's fall: but the whole was infected by sin and destroyed by death. For after Adam sinned against God by disobedience, and according to the threat fell into death, he could not beget anything from himself, except that which was subject to death. For nature is depraved and by the Spirit lacking, does not produce from itself something whole. Whence Christ says, Whatever is born of the flesh, is flesh: That is, whatever is procreated from a corrupt nature, infected with sin, subject to death, devoid of the Spirit, and destined for damnation; that is necessarily corrupt, infected with sin, subject to death, devoid of the Spirit, and destined for damnation. Hence those most sorrowful sayings concerning the corruption of the whole human nature: They are become corrupt and abominable: All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable: There is none that doeth good, no not one Psal: 14. Item: We were all by nature the children of wrath. Eph: 2. Item, The mind of the flesh is death and enmity against God. Item, 1. Cor: 2. The natural man perceiveth not the things that are of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him. This is the reason, because in Adam we are all dead. For in the loins of Adam was the whole human race, as a tree in the seed. Therefore, just as Adam through sin lost righteousness, life, and the Spirit, so by the sin of Adam the whole human race was despoiled of righteousness, life, and the Spirit. Nor could anyone recover life, and righteousness, and the Spirit, unless the Son of God descended from heaven, assumed human flesh, and by his merit and efficacy vivified us and endowed us with the Holy Spirit. As many, therefore, as are vivified, are vivified through our Lord are made alive by Jesus Christ, established by God as mediator, God and man.

Here, therefore, let the doctrine be repeated concerning the office and benefits of the mediator Jesus Christ: and that Jesus Christ is mediator according to both natures. For Paul here expressly affirms that through one man the resurrection of the dead exists: Hence it is also evident that all men who are ignorant of the mediator Jesus Christ, or do not believe in him, remain in death, as John also testifies: He who does not believe in the Son, the wrath of God remains upon him. Ioan: 3. Each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then those who will be Christ's at his coming, Subsequently he inculcates the prerogative and preeminence of Christ: just as, Coloss: 1. Paul names him προτότοκον ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν: the beginning and the firstborn from the dead, that in all things he might have the preeminence. For he wishes the fountain of our resurrection to be always in our sight. If anyone should object that Enoch and Elijah were translated alive into heaven: and that Moses was resurrected before Christ: it must be answered: that this was done by the merit and virtue of the Son of God the mediator, in whom they believed. For the death and resurrection of Christ, defined at a certain time, extends itself to all times. Nor let anyone wonder that our bodies rot in the sepulchers: since Christ's flesh [did not see] corruption has not seen. Paul teaches that this order has been established by God, so that Christ may hold the first place in all things, and be the firstborn from the dead: then that we individually, who in this life believe in Christ, may be resurrected at his glorious coming.

Latin:

Si autem Christus praedicatur, quòd ex mortuis resuscitatus sit, quomodo dicunt quidam inter vos, quòd non sit resurrectio mortuorum:

Haec principalis est pro positio huius 15 Capitis, munita argumento firmissimo, sumpto à causa efficiente, quod praemisit: falsum est inquit, dogma, quod aliqui adserunt inter vos non esse resurrectionem mortuorum: Iesus Christus enim verè à mortuis resurrexit, ut suprà demonstratum est. Ostendit hîc Apostolus, quae fuerit occasio ipsi scribendi hoc caput: nimirum Sadduceismus quorundam, qui cùm non solum Christiani perhiberi vellent, sed & Apostoli Christi: tamen palàm docebant non esse resurrectionem mortuorum: quemadmodum & Sadducai palàm in populo Dei docuerant. Haud dubiè alii aliter hunc errorem pinxerunt: Alii simpliciter adfirmarunt animas unà cum corporibus extingui, & hominem post mortem nihil differre à bruto animali: alii finxerunt animas quidem aliquandiu esse superstites, post quam corporibus soluti sunt: sed corpora non resurgere. Quid quid verò de resurrectione mortuorum scriptura testaretur, id intelligendum esse de spirituali vivificatione & regeneratione per Baptismum, & totum ministerium; ut cùm Paulus persecutor Ecclesiae convertitur ad Deum per Spiritum sanctum, regeneratur & vivificatur, ut in novitate vitae ambulet, resuscitatus est à mortuis. Quomodocunque autem pinxerunt errorem, haec fuit summa, post mortem corporis omnia finiri, & non restare aliam vitam post hanc vitam. Hinc aestimet pius lector, quàm immanis sit potentia Satanae qui Iesu Christo filio Dei docente orbem ausus est per suos Sadduceos, tam impudens dogma proferre in Ecclesia Dei? & eo ipso tempore, quo filius Dei sua resurrectione ex mortuis universam religionem, & quidem articulum de mortuorum resurrectione evidentissimè demonstravit: quo multi adhuc superstites erant, qui Iesum Christum resuscitatum à mortuis conspexerant: quo plerique Apostoli adhuc erudiebant Ecclesiam: quo per Apostolos & alios praecones Evangelii multi mortui in vitam revocabantur: ausus est tamen palàm & publicè per pseudoapostolos disputare contra doctrinam de resurrectione mortuorum. Non igitur mirum est in hac delira mundi senecta, prophanum Sadduceismum invalescere: & homines prolabi in securitatem. Nos verò tantò diligentius muniamus nostra pectora contra hos furores Sadducaeorum & Epicureorum: & animis nostris infigamus demonstrationem hanc irrefutabilem, quam hic suppeditat nobis Paulus. Christus inquit, resurrexit à mortuis: Ergò certissimum est, quod sit resurrectio mortuorum, & quidem corporum humanorum. Valet consequentia à causa efficiente ad proprium effectum. Christi resurrectio est efficiens causa nostrae resurrectionis: sed Iesus Christus verè resurrexit. Ergò necesse est & nos resurgere. Christus ut sibi non est mortuus, sed nobis: ita nec sibire surrexit, sed nobis. Non solùm divinitas Christi expers mortis, ab aeterno in omnem aeternitatem vivit, sed & humanitas eius immunis ab omni labe peccati, in omni aeternitate vivere potuisset: nisi nostrae salutis causa mortem subiisset. Cùm ergò Christus pro nobis & in nostram salutem & mortuus sit & resurrexerit: necesse est nos, qui in Christum credimus, mortis & resurrectionis eius, fieri participes. Necesse est fructum resurrectionis eius, qua fregit potentiam mortis, nobis communicari: Necesse est nos conformes fieri imagini gloriae ipsius. Cùmque membra simus corporis Christi, Christus autem, ut Caput Ecclesiae, corpore suo resurrexerit à mortuis, necesse est nos, ut membra Christi, corporibus à morte resurgere. Haec est certissima demonstratio, quae nulla Sophistic labefactari potest, Si enim Deus voluisset nos relinquere in morte, & futurae vitae prorsus expertes esse, nihil attinebat filium Dei de coelo mittere mediatorem, non erat necesse Christum subire mortem, nulla etiam causa erat, cur Christus ad inferos descenderet & tertia die resargeret. Ac totum opus redemptionis generis humani frustrà susceptum fuisset. Cùm ergò Iesus Christus filius Dei verè a mortuis resurrexerit, necesse est & nos resurgere, ut fructum passionis & resurrectionis eius percipiamus.

Si verò resurrectio mortuorum non est, neque Christus resurrexit.

Idem est argumentum à connexione causarum & effectuum. Si nulla est resurrectio mortuorum, necesse est negari & Christum resurrexisse: Sublato enim omni effectu, & omni causa finali, etiam efficientem negari necesse est. Quorsum enim opus erat filium Dei mori & tertia die resurgere, si volebat genus humanum à potestate mortis liberare? Sinolebat fidelibus aeternam vitam communicare? Et Si in universum negatur resurrectio mortuorum, omninò negadum est & Christum à mortuis resurrexisse. Hic enim dux & caput est omnium, qui à mortuis resurgunt. Hic nobis viam fecit per mortem in vitam aeternam: Hic fregit potentiam mortis & carcerem inferni: propter hunc mediatorem mortui recipiunt vitam. Quod si ergò negetur resurrectio mortuorum, omninò & Iesu Christi mediatoris resurrectio evertitur.

Si verò Christus non resurrexit, inanis igitur est praedicatio nostra, inanis verò est & fides vestra: Et nos reperimur esse falsi testes Dei, siquidem contra Deum testificamur, quòd excitavit, quem non excitavit, stquidem mortui non resurgunt: si enim mortui non resurgunt, neque Christus resurrexit.

Absurda colligit, quae ex falso & impio isto dogmate necessariò sequuntur, ut ita vanitatem et falsitatem eius demonstret. Hypotheses enim ex quibus absurda & falsa sequuntur, falsas esse necesse est, Eò quòd ex vero nil nisi verum sequitur. Nihil magis absurdum est, quàm universam praedicationem Apostolorum esse inanem, & absque omni fructu. Unum est de summis beneficiis, quae Deus ex immensa bonitate confert in genus humanum, quod ministerium Evangelii instituit ingenere humano, excitavit, & illustribus donis ornavit Apostolos, ut mundo explicarent beneficia mediatoris, & monstrarent viam ad vitam aeternam: summus hic Thesaurus est generis humani, nimirum, praedicatio Evangelii, per quam adipiscimur veram Dei noticiam, vocamur ad poenitentiam, regeneramur ad vitam aeternam, donamur Spiritu sancto, & ex qua in omni necessitate omnis generis efficacissimas consolationes haurimus. Hanc igitur saluberrimam, & salvificam praedicationem, qua nihil est in mundo preciosius, nec magis necessarium, inanem dicere, summa est absurditas & impietas, universam sacram scripturam evertens. Sic summa esset absurditas dicere, quòd inanis sit fides vestra. Per fidem enim liberati estis ab idolomania & furoribus Ethnicis, & pervenistis in agnitionem veri Dei: per fidem reconciliati estis Deo, impetrastis remissionem omnium peccatorum, erepti estis ex potestate tenebrarum, & tyrannide Satanae: tranquillam habetis conscientiam: donati estis Spiritu sancto: exornati estis insignibus et multiplicibus donis: percipitis in omni tribulatione firmam consolationem: liberum accessum quotidie habetis ad thronum Dei: & spem certam tenetis de vitae aeternae haereditate: Hanc igitur fidem, cuius tam insignes fructus & effectus in corde experti estis, & quotidie experimini dicere inanem & irritam extrema sanè est absurditas & dementia. Necessariò autem sequuntur haec absurda, Si Christus non resurrexit à mortuis. Hoc enim est caput, & fundamentum universae praedicationis Evangelii: quo everso, omnes fidei articulos collabi necesse est. Sic enim Christus summam & causam praedicationis Evangelii monstrat, sic opertebat Christum pati, & mori & resurgere, & praedicari in nomine ipsius poenitentiam & remissionem peccatorum. Huic etiam fundamento omnis nostra fides innititur: qua & Deum nobis reconciliatum esse statuimus, & vitam aeternam speramus: nimirum quòd Iesus Christus morte su pro nostris peccatis satisfecerit: & sua resurrectione mortis potentiam fregerit, & iustitiam & vitam sempiternam nobis impetraverit. Cum ergò nullo modo haec absurda, quae ex sententia (quod Christus non resurrexerit) necessariò sequuntur, sint concedenda, manifestum est falsum esse dogma, quod negat Christum resurrexisse à mortuis. Aliud deinde absurdum attexit. Inde sequeretur nos Apostolos esse falsos testes, qui manifesta mendacia spargerent de Deo. Siquidem in mundo testamur, quòd Deus Iesum Christum à mortuis resuscitaverit, cùm iuxta impium dogma Christus à mortuis non resurrexerit. Horrendum est autem cogitatu Apostolos Iesu Christi falsi testimonii insimulari. Idem enim ac si quis Spiritum sanctum accuset mendacii: Spiritus sanctus enim per ora Apostolorum de resurrectione Christi testatur in mundo, Spiritus sanctus autem est Spiritus veritatis, qui mentiri non potest. Ergo omni exceptione maiores sunt testes Apostoli: & nefas est ipsorum testimonium in dubium vocare: Manet ergò firmum & immotum, quod Iesus Christus à mortuis resurrexit, quemadmodum Apostoli de Deo testantur, & sequitur esse resurrectionem mortuorum, quae ex resurrectione Iesu Christi promanat.

Si verò Christus non resurrexit, vana est fides vestra: adhuc estis in peccatis vestris: Ergò & hi, qui in Christo dormiunt, perierunt: si in hac vita tantum speramus in Christum, miserrimi sumus omnium hominum.

Absurda, quae sequuntur ex impio dogmate, quo negatur resurrectio mortuorum & Christi, repetit, inculcat & exaggerat. Est enim hoc argumentum longè gravissimum, quod nulla oratione satis exponi potest. Si enim nulla est resurrectio mortuorum, tum universa Christianorum religio ex fundamentis evertitur: concidunt prorsus omnes articuli fidei: & universae consolationes, quae extant in verbo Dei, evanescunt. Paulus igitur impietatem & prophanitatem sacrilegi dogmatis non potest satis detestari: & ut omnes piorum cogitationes inde deterreat, ostendit isto errore universam deleri religionem. Vana est, inquit, fides vestra: Hoc est, frustrà creditis in Deum patrem, filium & Spiritum sanctum: frustrà amplectimini doctrinam Apostolorum: frustrà agitis poenitentiam: frustrà luctamini contra peccatum, mortem & Satanam: frustrà sustentatis vos promissionibus divinis: frustrà suscipitis baptismum frustrà sumitis coenam domini: frustrà speratis beneficia & gloriam regni Iesu Christi. Haec enim omnia eò tendunt, ut neconciliati Deo per fidem resuscitemini ex morte, & aeterna beatitudine fruamini. Verè igitur vana est fides vestra inquit, si nulla est mortuorum resurrectio. Adhuc estis in peccatis vestris. In peccatis esse, significat hîc Paulo, non esse reconciliatum Deo: premi maledictione legis: esse reum coram iudicio Dei: sentire horrendum onus peccati, & esse sub tyrannide Satanae ac destinatum esse ad aeternos cruciatus propter peccatum. Hac miseria nihil tristius dici, nec cogitari potest. Ea autem sequitur ex illo dogmate, quo negatur resurrectio mortuorum. Si enim mortui non resurgunt, nec Christus resurrexit. Si Christus non resurrexit, ergò non extitit victor peccati et Satanae: ergò non fuit verus Messias: siquidem scriptura promisit Messiam resurrecturum. Ergò non liberavit vos à peccato & morte. Necesse est igitur vos adhuc in vestris haerere peccatis, quae extrema est calamitas, si mortui non resurgunt. Etiam qui dormiunt in Christo perierunt: Audierant Corinthii insignem consolationem à Christo, quòd, qui in Christo obdormivissent, beati essent: Siquidem illos aeterna maneret vita & gloria. Iam inquit, si sacrilegum istum errorem Sadduceorum suscipitis, perit vobis omnis spes de beatitudine eorum, quin CHRISTO IESU feliciter obdormiverunt: Imo inquit, non solùm perit vobis spes de beatitudine mortuorum, sed etiam universa Christianorum religio extremae condemnabitur dementiae. Nullum est enim genus hominum vel secta in mundo, quae tanta odia, tam varia pericula, tantas calamitates, & tam dira subeat supplicia propter religionem atque nos Christiani: quomadmodum historia Ecclesiae, & inprimis Apostolorum & martyrum ostendit: mundus omnis generis sectas, errores, blasphemias & scelera ferre potest, saltem Christianos ferre non potest: Veritatem Christi seriò profitentes, extremè odit, ipsos Apostolos tanquam καθάρματα καὶ περιψήματα detestatur. Iesaias ferra dissectus est: Ieremias lapidibus in Aegypto obrutus: Paulus capite truncatus: Polycarpus igne combustus: Ignatius à feris dilaniatus; Blandina ferreae sedi candenti imposita: Tantaque rabie saeviit mundus in Christianos, ut defatigati sint & tyrranni & carnifices, & excogitando nova supplicia & excruciando Christianos. Iam si nulla est resurrectio mortuorum, nec ulla restat beatitudo post hanc vitam, certè omnium hominum miserrimi & calamitosissimi, atque etiam stultissimierunt Christiani, quos oportebat omnium hominum esse cùm sapientissimos, tùm felicissimos, eò quòd soli luce verbi divini illustrantur, ductu Spiritus sancti reguntur, soli verum Dei cultum exercent, & clementia Dei prae omnibus populis totius orbis foventur. Cùm ergò fieri non possit, ut hi, quos Deus summo amore complectitur, in quibus ipse Deus tanquam in templo suo habitat, quos illustribus testimoniis ornat, quòd placeant ipsi, quibus amplissimas dedit promissiones de perpetua felicitate, & copiosa laborum mercede, sint omnium hominum miserrimi. Ergò necessè est restare aliam vitam et mortuos resurrecturos, ut Deus pro suarum promissionum veritatem, quam distulit sanctis suis in hac vita, in resurrectione mortuorum & vita altera impleat. Atque ita docet hîc Paulus hoc consilio pios in hac vita omnis generis calamitatibus exerceri, & sepè tristes habere exitus, ut ipsa innocentum supplicia illustre sint testimonium futurae resurrectionis mortuorum, & futurae vitae. Deus de coelo testatus est Iesaiam Prophetam fidelem esse altissimi Dei ministrum: siquidem per eum stupenda edidit miracula: Et tamen permittit eum ferra dissecari: Necesse est igitur alteram restare vitam, in qua Iesaias futurus est beatus, & reipsa possessurus, quod illi in verbo Dei (Beati omnes, qui confidunt in eo) promissum est: siquidem in hac vita promissam beatitudinem non est consecutus.

Nunc verò Christus resurrexit à mortuis, primitiae eorum, qui dormiunt.

Postquam absurda, quae ex nefario dogmate Sadduceorum sequuntur, ex aggeravit atque inculcavit, adversativam nunc ponit, & praecipuum fundamentum doctrinae de resurrectione mortuorum, quod suprà luculentis testimoniis demonstravit, repetit, atque etiam ex praecedentibus argumentis colligit & concludit: quasi dicat, Omnes sani, & qui vel unciam pietatis habent, fateri coguntur, nullo modo ista horrenda absurda, quae suprà commemoravi, concedenda esse, nisi quis penitus universam religionemevertere velit. Firmum ergò et immotum manet, quòd Iesus Christus verè à mortuis resurrexerit: & quòd sit mortuorum resurrectio: Primitiae enim resuscitatorum ex mortuis est Christus. Ergò plenitudo Ecclesiae ex mortuis secutura est. Christus veluti dux praeivit Ecclesiae, & viam fecit per mortem ad vitam aeternam: Ecclesia fidelium Christum secutura est: quemadmodum Micheas praedixit. Adscendet perruptor ante eas, erumpent & transibunt per portam, exibuntque per eam, rexque eorum ante eas transibit, & dominus in capite earum:

Postquàm enim per hominem mors, & per hominem resurrectio mortuorum: Quemadmodum enim in Adam omnes moriuntur: sic & in Christo omnes vivificantur. Unusquisque verò in proprio ordine: Primitiae Christus: deinde, qui sunt Christi in adventu ipsius.

Quartum hoc est membrum huius concionis, in qua utrumque fontem, & mortis & resurrectionis, et monstrat & inter se confert; atque ita docet Christum non sibi soli resurrexisse à mortuis, sed nobis, & ex Christi resurrectione nostram manare resurrectionem. Per hominem inquit, mors intravit in mundum, quasi dicat. Cùm Adam in peccatum & mortem prolapsus est, non ille solus est mortuus: sed universam posteritatem protraxit ille in mortem et damnationem: Cùm enim ille radix esset universi generis humani, ubi se spoliavit vita & iustitia, omnem posteritatem in mortem coniecit. Christus verò alter Adam, & nova radix electae Ecclesiae, & servavit vitam & promeruit eam omnibus fidelibus. Rectè ergò ex resurrectione Christi, nostra colligitur resurrectio. Prolixius tractat hanc collationem Adae & Christi Paulus, Rom: 5. Hoc loco satis illi est monstrasse, & primam causam mortis, & primam causam resurrectionis. Unde consequentia manifesta est, quia Christus resurrexit, certum est et nos resurrecturos à mortuis: quia Christus est secundus Adam: et totius generis humani personam sustinet: loco omnium hominum subiit mortem: & sua resurrectione omnibus meruit et paravit vitam. Observandum est hoc loco clarum testimonium de causa mortis humanae, & de peccato originis. Non fuit homo in prima creatione ante lapsum subiectus morti: neque fluxus materiae susubinde ruentis ad alias formas, causa est mortis humanae: Nec temerè aut casu moritur homo: sed per unum hominem venit mors, & in Adam omnes morimur: Hoc est, peccatum seu inobedientia Adae mortem invexit in mundum: Deus enim comminatus ei fuerat: Quacunque die comederis de arbore ista, morte morieris. Hoc praeceptum Dei, cùm transiret Adam & se & universam posteritatem praecipitavit in mortem. Hanc ergò causam mortis humanae semper intueamur: nimirum peccatum, cui iure irascitur Deus: Ac sciamus aliud remedium contra mortem inveniri non posse, nisi obedientiam & resurrectionem domini nostri Iesu Christi. Hîc enim secundus est Adam, cui secundo Deus universam salutem, iustitiam & vitam totius generis humani credidit: Doctrina etiam de peccato originis hinc petenda est. Docet enim Paulus omnes homines in Adam mortuos esse. Ergò nòn tantum sibi nocuit Adam suo lapsu: ut Pelagiani delirant: Ergò natura humana non mansit integra post Adae lapsum: sed universa infecta est peccato & morte destructa. Adam enim postquam inobedientia peccavit contra Deum, et iuxta comminationem in mortem est prolapsus, non potuit ex sese gignere quidquam, nisi quod morti esset obnoxium. Natura enim depravata & Spiritu carens, non producit ex se integrum quiddam. Unde Christus inquit, Quidquid ex carne natum est, caro est: Hoc est, quidquid ex natura corrupta, peccato infecta, morti obnoxia, Spiritus experte, & ad damnationem destinata procreatur; id necesse est esse corruptum, peccato in fectum, morti obnoxium, Spiritus expers, & ad damnationem destinatum. Hinc illa sunt tristissima dicta de corruptione totius humanae naturae: Corrupti & abominabiles facti sunt: Omnes declinaverunt, & inutiles facti sunt: Non est, qui faciat bonum, ne unus quidem Psal: 14. Item: Eramus omnes natura filii irae. Eph: 2. Item, Sensus carnis est mors & inimicitia adversus Deum. Item, 1. Cor: 2. Animalis homo non percipit ea, quae sunt Spiritus Dei: stultitia enim sunt ei. Ratio haec est, quia in Adam omnes mortui sumus. In lumbis enim Adae totum erat genus humanum, ut arbor in semine. Ut igitur Adam per peccatum iustitiam, vitam, & Spiritum amisit, ita peccato Adae totum genus humanum iustitia, vita & Spiritu spoliatum est. Nec potuit quisquam vitam, & iustitiam & Spiritum recuperare, nisi filius Dei descenderet de coelo, humanam carnem adsumeret, & suo merito & efficacia nos vivificaret & Spiritu sancto donaret. Quotquot ergò vivificantur, per dominum nostrum Iesum Christum vivificantur, Deum & hominem constitutum à Deo mediatorem.

Hîc ergò doctrina repetatur de officio & beneficiis mediatoris Iesu Christi: & quòd Iesus Christus secundum utramque naturam sit mediator. Paulus enim disertè hîc adfirmat per unum hominem existere resurrectionem mortuorum: Hinc etiam patet omnes homines, qui sunt ignari mediatoris Iesu Christi, aut non credunt in ipsum, manere in morte, ut et Ioannes testatur: Qui non credit in filium, ira Dei manet super ipsum. Ioan: 3.Quisque in proprio ordine: primitiae Christus, deinde qui Christi erunt in adventu ipsius, Subinde inculcat praerogativam et praeeminentiam Christi: quemadmodum, Coloss: 1. Paulus nominat eum προτότοκον ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν: principium & primogenitum ex mortuis, ut in omnibus primas teneat. Vult enim fontem nostrae resurrectionis nobis semper in conspectu esse. Si quis obiiciat Enoch & Eliam vivos translatos esse in coelum: & Moisen ante Christum esse resuscitatum: respondendum est: id factum esse merito & virtute filii Dei mediatoris, in quem crediderunt. Mors enim & resurrectio Christi certo tempore definita, ad omnia se extendit tempora. Ne etiam quis miretur, quod nostra corpora in sepulchris putrescant: cùm Christi caro corruptionem non viderit. Paulus docet hunc ordinem à Deo constitutum esse, ut Christus teneat primas in omnibus, & sit primogenitus ex mortuis: deinde ut nos singuli, qui in hac vita credimus in Christum, in ipsius glorioso adventu resuscitemur.

## 15:24-28
Afterwards the end when he shall have delivered the kingdom to God and the Father, when he shall have abolished all principality and all power and virtue. For he must reign, until he has put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. For he has subjected all things under his feet. But when he says that all things are subjected, it is clear that he is excepted, who subjected all things to him. But when all things shall be subjected to him, then the son himself also shall be subjected to him, who subjected all things to him, that God may be all in all.

This is the fifth member of this chapter, in which he compares the form of the kingdom of Christ, which he bears in this life, with the form of the kingdom which he is to have in the other life, after all his enemies shall have been defeated.
